abstract: Aiming at velocity/height tracking control and attitude stabilization for the longitudinal flight of cruise vehicle, the research of intelligent flight control method is carried out by combining the backstepping control theory and the deep reinforcement learning method. Firstly, the longitudinal flight control system of the vehicle is decomposed into velocity and height subsystems, and the control law is designed based on backstepping control theory. Then, aiming at the problems that the selection of the multiple control gains will directly affect the control performance of the closed-loop system and the adjustment process of control gains is cumbersome, the twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm (TD3) will be adopted to train the cruise vehicle, so that it can determine the control gains online according to the current flight states. The numerical simulation results show that, the proposed intelligent flight control method can guarantee the high-precision tracking with respect to height and velocity commands, and also realize the attitude stability of cruise vehicle.

Author Keywords: twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm (TD3)

articleTitle: Non-Singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control with Super-Twisting ESO for Spacecraft Formation Flying Systems
abstract: In this article, we analyze how spacecraft formation can save more fuel and achieve more accurate relative position motion in the configuration control under the influence of external disturbances and perturbations. A non-singular fast terminal sliding mode controller(NFTSMC) combined with Super-Twisting extended state observer(STESO) is proposed for disturbance rejection control of spacecraft formation configuration. In this paper, we will establish the kinematics model of spacecraft relative motion, and linearize this model. Then, the convergence of STESO and the stability of the combination of NFTSMC and STESO are analyzed respectively. Finally, sufficient numerical simulations will be provided to verify the feasibility of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Centralized Multi-Robot Collaborative LiDAR SLAM Utilizing Loop Closure Selection
abstract: Multi-robot systems have attracted much attention due to their high efficiency and robustness. Multi-robot Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is the cornerstone of collaboration, such that each robot can localize and build a map of the workspace. One of the key challenges of this problem lies in utilizing the shared information between robots adequately so that the system can retain the correct information and reject the outliers. Here we propose a centralized multi-robot collaborative LiDAR SLAM framework for robots, each only equipped with a 2D LiDAR without the need for additional sensors. With each robot able to run simple LiDAR odometry onboard, a central server with greater computational capacity collects the information from robots, optimizes their poses globally, and updates their poses through communication. For a large number of loop closures in multi-robot SLAM systems, it is catastrophic to build wrong data associations between pose nodes in the global factor graph. We resort to a loop closure selection method to ensure the correctness and consistency of global optimization. Throughout the verification process on the real Automated Mobile Robot (AMR) platform, the framework exhibits better performance on localization and mapping.

articleTitle: The LSTM-PER-TD3 Algorithm for Deep Reinforcement Learning in Continuous Control Tasks
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning has shown great potential in the field of robot control, but it still faces challenges in continuous control tasks. Traditional reinforcement learning algorithms perform poorly when dealing with high-dimensional state spaces and continuous action spaces, resulting in low learning efficiency and degraded performance. To solve this issue, we propose a novel reinforcement learning algorithm named LSTM-PER-TD3 (LPT3), which combines Long Short-Term Memory networks (LSTM), prioritized experience replay (PER), and Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient algorithm (TD3). The LPT3 algorithm utilizes LSTM networks to process sequential state information and combines PER and TD3 methods to achieve efficient continuous control. It is capable of learning accurate policies in high-dimensional state spaces, improving learning efficiency and performance through experience replay and policy evaluation. We evaluate the LPT3 algorithm on several standard continuous control tasks and compare it with traditional reinforcement learning algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of LPT3 in terms of learning efficiency and performance. Compared to traditional algorithms, LPT3 converges faster and achieves higher control accuracy, effectively addressing the challenges in continuous control tasks.

articleTitle: Research on vehicle routing problem based on improved dragonfly algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the low carrying rate and high fuel consumption cost of vehicle routing optimization, a vehicle routing model with time window is constructed. An improved dragonfly algorithm integrated with random learning strategy is designed and applied to solve the problem. The real-value calculation form of the five behaviors of the original dragonfly algorithm is changed into random learning target position pairs and applied to vehicle routing problem with time windows. By comparing the results with those of other three algorithms, the effectiveness and feasibility of improved effective dragon algorithm are further verified, which can reasonably allocate logistics capacity and human resources, and realize the cost reduction and efficiency increase of enterprise business.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Robust Control of Nonlinear Delay Systems via Different Power Hamiltonian Functions
abstract: The study examines the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> control problem of nonlinear time-delay systems (NTDSs) at a predetermined period. We design suitable Lyapunov functions and Hamiltonian functions that have various powers to apply to Hamiltonian systems involving outside disturbances and delay phenomena. Next, in order to guarantee that the NTDS stabilizes within one predeter-mined period and possess greater resistance against disturbances, a predefined-time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> control strategy is introduced. Finally, a case serves to confirm the correctness of our findings.

articleTitle: Small Vehicle Recognition Based on Attention Mechanism and Feature Fusion
abstract: This paper proposes an improved method combining the attention mechanism and feature fusion on the basis of YOLOv5. We firstly introduce CA attention mechanism in the network, which simultaneously considers the attention in channel dimension and spatial dimension; feature fusion adopts ASFF fusion mechanism, which solves the inconsistency problem inside the feature pyramid by learning the connection between different feature maps; finally, Focal Loss function is introduced during the training time. Based on the improved YOLOv5, the accuracy in identifying small vehicle targets is improved by 4.92%, and the processing speed of a single image is improved by 30.34%, which effectively enhances the processing accuracy and speed of small vehicle targets.

articleTitle: Organic Rankine Cycle Performance Analysis Based on WGCNA
abstract: Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) system operates with gas-liquid two-phase coexistence, resulting in complex and variable working conditions, along with intricate coupling relationships between parameters. The comprehension of the extent to which certain parameters impact the performance of the system is of paramount significance. In this paper, we propose to identify key parameters affecting the overall system efficiency using Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA). Initially, a dynamic simulation model of the ORC system is developed on the Simulink platform based on its working principles. Subsequently, the WGCNA network is constructed, and it is employed to examine the operational parameters of several components inside the ORC system. The identification of important parameters that exert a substantial influence on both the overall efficiency and mechanical power has been effectively accomplished. The aforementioned findings elucidate the fundamental variables that influence the performance of the system and offer significant perspectives for enhancing and optimizing the system's overall efficacy.

articleTitle: An Improved Artificial Potential Field Method for Formation Control and Obstacle Avoidance of the Multi-Agents Systems
abstract: Obstacle avoidance is a significant research content in multi-agents formation control. The obstacle avoidance of multi-agents systems is investigated in this paper, and an improved artificial potential field method (IAPF) is proposed to avoid unknown obstacles in multi-agent formation. Aiming at improving the efficiency of formation avoidance and solving the non-reachable and local minima problems, the dynamic sub-target algorithm is proposed. The proposed method enables the multi-agent system (MASs) to avoid obstacles smoothly and quickly and complete formation tasks in complex environments by tracking dynamic sub-target as well, in which the position and motion direction of adjacent agents are taken into account in the selection of a sub-target for the formation efficiency. In addition, a variable potential field range is defined to ensure the safety of the formation. Finally, several simulation results verify the superiority and effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Perceptual Image Hash for Fine-Grained Tampering Detection
abstract: Perceptual image hash is one of the effective technologies for image content authentication. In this study, we propose a lightweight perceptual image hash method for tampering detection and tampering localization. In the proposed method, we extract global features, layout features and local color features from image to generate compact hash code, then we present an image tampering detection and localization algorithm using the hash code. The proposed method can be used to detect the shape and location of tampering image regions with higher precision. Plenty of experimental results show that the proposed method is provided with pixel-level detection accuracy and stronger robustness to tolerating content-preserving manipulations and geometric distortion.

articleTitle: Tips on Multibody System Modeling with Loop Constraints
abstract: It is well known that for constrained multibody system, cutting off the loop is an efficient way for modeling, and several methods have been proposed. In this paper, several tips are proposed to provide another choice for both constrained dynamic model and reduced control model. Its main advantage is that no special treatment is needed for loop constraint, while unknown constraint forces are still eliminated. The explanation and numerical simulations are presented to valid accuracy of proposed tips.

articleTitle: Research on Urban Safety Monitoring and Early Warning Strategy for Coupling Scenarios of Natural Disaster and Accident Disaster
abstract: With the rapid development of urbanization in contemporary Chinese society, security risks also gather in cities, which puts forward higher requirements for the resilience of cities to tolerate and resist risks, and for capabilities of monitoring and early warning as well as emergency disposal. On the basis of introducing the research background and significance, the paper first analyzes the current situation of urban safety development at home and abroad, and then analyzes the main challenges faced by urban safety development, mainly pointing out the shortcomings in the fields of planning system, monitoring and early warning, and emergency treatment. On this basis, from the two aspects of urban infrastructure construction and operation management, the paper puts forward several countermeasures and suggestions to promote urban safety development with the building of smart resilient cities as a breakthrough, including implementing dynamic assessment of urban security risks and strengthening top-level planning for urban security management as well as other suggestions.

articleTitle: A Feature Extraction Method for Soft Fault Diagnosis of DC/DC Converters Using Wavelet Analysis and Gramian Angular Field
abstract: DC/DC converter is the key component of power supply system, its safety and reliability ensure the stable operation of the system. Under various environmental stresses, the parameters of the converter gradually deviate from their initial values as the running time increases. When the parameters exceed a certain threshold, the system will suffer from soft faults. This paper presents a novel feature extraction method for soft fault diagnosis of DC/DC converters using wavelet analysis (WA) and gramian angular field (GAF). The degradation index is the ripple of output voltage, After the correlation time-frequency features are extracted by WA, the correlation features are cross-fused by GAF method. On the basis of fusion features, K-nearest neighbor (KNN) network is established for soft fault detection and location. Since no additional hardware or signal injection is required, the entire application process is low in cost and complexity. Simulation and experimental results show the proposed method has a good diagnosis effect on various soft faults.

articleTitle: Ash Accumulation Prediction in Coal-Fired Power Plant Boilers Based on GWO-VMD-BiLSTM
abstract: The presence of soot in coal-fired power plant boilers has long been recognized as a significant factor leading to reduced heat transfer efficiency and compromised safety. A precise and scientific prediction of ash fouling on the heat transfer surface plays a crucial role in developing effective strategies for soot-blowing, thereby improving energy efficiency. To tackle the challenges associated with fluctuation and randomness in predicting ash fouling, we propose an innovative approach integrating the Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm, The implementation of Variational Modal Decomposition (VMD) and Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) neural network is undertaken. Initially, the Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm is employed to automatically ascertain the crucial parameters of VMD, thereby aiding in the decomposition of the original time series. Subsequently, GWO-VMD is employed to obtain the Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs), forming the basis for constructing prediction models using Bi-LSTM. Each IMF corresponds to a sub-series whereby a distinct Bi-LSTM model is created. In the end, the projected values of each sub-series are combined to produce the ultimate prediction outcomes. By comparing our proposed model with three alternative models, we demonstrate that our model achieves the highest accuracy in predicting the cleanliness factor sequences, thus confirming its credibility and precision.

articleTitle: Video based Gesture Recognition Method using Two-Stream 3D-ConvNet Network for Coal Mine Emergency Rescue Robot
abstract: The complexity and danger associated with underground coal mining operations constantly threats the miners' safety. Remote-controlled robot with man-in-loop can assist the emergency rescue. Thus, human gesture recognition is one of the most important issues. This paper proposes a method for recognizing emergency rescue gestures based on video understanding. First, the routine emergency rescue gestures of coal miners are decomposed, and a video dataset of underground emergency rescue gestures containing 9 gestures are constructed. Then a method based on the Two-Stream 3D-ConvNet network model is designed to complete gesture recognition. Feature extraction in the model adopts the method of calculating video optical flow information. The comparative experiments show that the model improves the recognition accuracy compared with 3D ConvNet and other methods on the constructed dataset, and verifies that the model has a better classification ability for the self-collected video dataset of mine emergency rescue gestures.

articleTitle: Error Prediction of Springback in Bending Process Based on GA-BPNN for Accurate Forming Angle
abstract: The issue of springback in sheet metal bending has always been of great concern in industrial applications. To reduce its influence on forming angle in bending process., a prediction model based on GA-BPNN (Genetic Algorithm-Backpropagation Neural Network) was proposed and optimized. To train the network., the finite element method was introduced to construct the dataset. Then the parameters in the neural network were determined., and a 5-dimensional input improved model considering material classification was adopted to further improve the prediction accuracy. The experimental results showed that the maximum errors of forming angle reduced from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.45^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.4^{\circ}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.15^{\circ}$</tex> by applying different models.

articleTitle: Game Theory-Based Vehicle Lane Change Collaboration Strategy in Connected Vehicle Environment
abstract: Vehicle lane changing is one of the main causes of traffic congestion and traffic safety. In view of the existing problems, a vehicle lane change decision model based on game theory is proposed in the connected vehicle environment, and the predicted gain function is constructed. Then, the weight coefficients of the gain function are designed by using Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) hierarchical analysis, and the optimal strategy of vehicle lane change is obtained by solving the equilibrium solution of the game model combining the right-of-way information and the game decision model. Finally, the simulation results show that the game decision model can improve the driving speed of lane change vehicles, enhance the operation efficiency, and then increase the road capacity.

articleTitle: Cloud Manufacturing Task Scheduling Under Machinery Breakdown Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Task scheduling is one of the major research issues in cloud manufacturing. At present, most studies choose heuristic algorithms to solve task scheduling problems. However, cloud manufacturing environment is highly complex, and dynamic events can easily affect the execution of scheduling scheme. Heuristic algorithms are difficult to satisfy requirements of dynamic scheduling. In recent years, deep reinforcement learning has been applied to many fields. In this paper, a deep reinforcement learning algorithm named as Long Short Term Memory-Double Deep Q-Network (LSTM-DoubleDQN) is designed to solve the scheduling problem in cloud manufacturing, and the rescheduling method under machinery breakdown is also explored. The results show that the convergence speed of LSTM-DoubleDQN is faster than Deep Q-Network (DQN), Long Short Term Memory-Deep Q-Network (LSTM-DQN) and Double Deep Q-network (DoubleDQN). The QoS of scheduling scheme of LSTM-DoubleDQN is better, which is more suitable for solving the scheduling problem in cloud manufacturing. The effectiveness of rescheduling method is also verified.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Graph Convolutional Point Cloud Registration Method Combining Global Attention
abstract: In order to solve the problems of low efficiency and high requirements on the initial position of aligned point clouds encountered by the traditional ICP (Iterative Closest Point) registration algorithm in the registration of large point cloud models, this paper proposes a point cloud registration algorithm based on the global attention mechanism and dynamic graph convolutional network. The algorithm enhances the spatial connection between point cloud pairs by introducing a global attention mechanism to enhance the extraction of key features in point clouds and integrating this mechanism in DGCNN (Dynamic Graph Convolutional Neural Network) feature extraction networks. In addition, the algorithm uses a similarity-based soft connection instead of the traditional hard connection for point cloud point pair matching, resulting in faster processing speed and higher registration accuracy. Experimental results show that the algorithm exhibits higher robustness and registration accuracy in large point cloud models, demonstrating the effectiveness of the global attention mechanism in the point cloud registration task.

articleTitle: Digital Drive Method of Coriolis Mass Flowmeter Based on Tracking Vibration Attenuation
abstract: A new digital drive method is proposed to solve the problem that ordinary digital drive method cannot accurately track the natural frequency change of tube. After analyzing the source of tracking error of tube natural frequency, the method uses amplitude to monitor the natural frequency of tube and updates the driving frequency by estimating the attenuation signal frequency after vibration stop. Experiments show that the proposed digital drive method can timely adjust the synthetic signal parameters when the natural frequency of the tube changes, improve the tracking accuracy of the digital driving natural frequency, and make the driving system perform better; At 65 °C, compared to ordinary digital drives, the measurement accuracy of the Coriolis mass flowmeter using the new digital drive method has improved by 37.87%.

articleTitle: Cross-spectral Proximity Detection and Tracking of Underwater Suspicious Targets
abstract: Intelligent visual tracking is a hot research topic in the field of computer vision, which not only has high scientific research value but also has broad application prospects. The development speed of aerial or ground vision tracking systems is fast, and the relevant technology is also becoming more and more perfect. They play an important role in the detection and tracking of suspicious vehicles and pedestrians in the field of security. However, the visual detection and tracking of underwater suspicious targets face the great challenge of weak observation and low light images, and related research is still immature. This paper proposes a cross-spectral proximity detection and tracking method based on the latest Segment Anything model, and verifies the effectiveness of the method in low light pool experiments.

articleTitle: A Watermark Detection Method for Approximate Replay Attacks Based on State Compensation
abstract: Approximate replay attacks are a form of attacks obtained by parameter selection of the generalized replay attack model, which seriously threatens the security of cyber-physical system (CPS). To address the detection problem of approximate replay attacks, this paper proposes a watermark detection method based on state compensation. The adverse effect of the watermark signal added in the control channel on the system state estimation can be eliminated completely by the designed state compensation structure with an auxiliary estimator. Simulation experimental results show that the detection method proposed in this paper can effectively detect approximate replay attacks.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Turbulence Phase Correction Using Digital Micro-Mirror Devices Based on Binary Off-Axis Holography
abstract: We propose a phase correction technique for atmospheric turbulence based on a digital micromirror device using binary off-axis holography to compensate for the distortion of the beam occurring in atmospheric turbulence. Simulations verify the phase distortion correction of the beam under different turbulence conditions, such as strong, medium, and weak, and the results indicate that the phase correction technique proposed in this paper can effectively compensate for atmospheric turbulence under all turbulence conditions.

articleTitle: Prediction of Traffic Flow Density and Velocity Based on Kalman Filter Fusion of The Non-Local Gas-Kinetic Model and Convolution Neural Networks-Long-Short Term Memory Model
abstract: The integrated perception, planning, and control of intelligent transportation system has become a research hotspot in academia. In this context, the safe running of an intelligent vehicle highly depends on the accurate prediction of its driving environment and working conditions. Traffic flow parameters represent the macro characteristics of an intelligent vehicle driving environment. Accurate prediction of traffic flow parameters is beneficial to improve the accuracy of trajectory prediction of vehicles in the surrounding environment. As two kinds of traffic flow parameter prediction models: the macroscopic traffic flow model and the data-based learning model have their own characteristics. To fully take advantage of these two models, our work proposes a study of the macroscopic traffic flow model based on a nonlocal gas-kinetic (GKT) and a deep learning model based on convolutional neural networks-long short term memory. Real data sets US-101 and PeMS are used respectively to predict traffic flow density and velocity. Finally, the Kalman filter is employed to fuse the results of the two models. The experiment shows that the prediction accuracy of traffic flow density and velocity can be improved as compared with the Macroscopic traffic flow model and the data-based learning model.

articleTitle: Attentional Graph Neural Network for 3D Multi-Object Tracking
abstract: 3D Multi-Object Tracking technology is significantly important in many applications such as autonomous driving, robotics and visual surveillance. In recent years, Graph Neural Networks has been introduced into MOT and impressive progress has been made. However, most methods do not take into account the differences in importance of nodes within the neighborhood when updating node features, leading to a lack of description capabilities for local details. In this paper, while modeling the temporal-spatial relationship between objects, we introduce graph attention into GNN network in the message passing module to better aggregate intra-frame node information. Extensive experiments show that our method achieves competitive results on the nuScenes and KITTI datasets, which demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Knowledge Distillation on Multiple Experts for Long-Tailed Recognition
abstract: Deep learning-based image recognition encounters a great challenge since the real-world data always exhibits long-tailed distribution, that is, a few categories contain most of the examples while the rest categories have very few ones. Imbalanced distribution makes it difficult for models to achieve expected recognition performance. The works proposed to tackle this problem main focus on two strategies: re-balancing and ensemble learning. In this paper, we propose a new ensemble method: Multi-Expert Distillation for Long-tailed Recognition (MED), which consists of two training phases. Specifically, we first design a Multi-Expert Network containing multiple experts, each of which is trained in a particular domain. In this case, the whole task is split into several sub-tasks. On top of that, we perform knowledge distillation training to transfer knowledge from Multi-Expert Network to a unified student network to ensemble the experts so that the student can recognize all the categories. Besides, we construct a weight module to control the impact of each expert on the student to maximize the effectiveness of knowledge transfer. We conduct extensive experiments on three benchmarks and the results show that our proposed MED achieves compelling performance with notable improvements.

articleTitle: Secondary Frequency Regulation Strategy of Multi-agent Virtual Power Plant Based on Scenery Storage
abstract: The increasingly mature related technologies of multi-agent system (MAS) and virtual power plant (VPP) provide new ideas for supporting the automatic generation control (AGC) demand of the bulk power grid. In this paper, a multi-agent VPP hierarchical control strategy based on scenery storage is proposed. The upper layer is responsible for receiving the AGC requirements of the grid and using grey wolf optimizer (GWO) to solve the optimization target and output power's reference value. In order to improve the accuracy of GWO, the population members of the algorithm are optimized, the linear convergence factor is replaced, and the Levy flight strategy is adopted. After the iteration of the algorithm, the random step size is used to search the current range in a small range. The lower layer constructs the corresponding model prediction control (MPC) model based on the state space equations of wind turbine, photovoltaic and energy storage system. The output value of the upper layer is used as a reference for predictive tracking to ensure that the output power can track the reference value shortly. The simulation results show that the hierarchical control strategy based on MAS can quickly and accurately respond to AGC demand and maximize economic benefits, and the improved GWO performance is better than GWO.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Swarm Control for UAVs in Static and Dynamic Multi-Obstacle Environments
abstract: In this paper, a reinforcement learning-based method for controlling the swarm of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in complex environments with static and dynamic obstacles has been presented. The method in this paper utilizes double deep Q-network (DDQN) algorithm to train the action of virtual leader in UAV swarm, which enables the UAVs to effectively navigate through complex environments while avoiding collisions. Besides, the artificial potential field method is also applied on each individual UAV to deal with emergency. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is evaluated by simulations in complex scenario.

articleTitle: DANF: Dual-Flow Aggregation Network for Curtain Wall Frame Real-Time Segmentation
abstract: The precise positioning of curtain wall frames is a crucial step for the automated installation of curtain walls. This paper proposes a network (DANF) with a dual-flow aggregation structure to achieve semantic segmentation of curtain wall frames. We constructed a dataset (CWF) for the segmentation of curtain wall frames and analyzed the characteristics of both the curtain wall frames and the background environment. Our proposed network architecture combines the strengths of transformers for semantic information extraction and CNNs for high-resolution feature extraction. Moreover, we introduced a dual-flow aggregation module to effectively fuse the features derived from transformers and CNNs. The experimental results on the CWF dataset validate the powerful performance of our method.

articleTitle: Vessel Collision Risk in Meeting Area Based on Traffic Conflict Technique
abstract: In order to reduce the collision risk of mega-ships and improve the navigation safety in meeting area, an approach for evaluating the collision risk of large vessels in the vessel meeting area is proposed. This proposal is based on vessel traffic conflict technique, and the rationality of the expansion of the meeting area is evaluated. In accordance with the AIS data, the traffic flow and vessel traffic conflict situation in the vessel meeting area are analyzed. The traffic conflict rate and traffic conflict points should be taken as the evaluation index of the collision risk in the vessel meeting area. The anchorage near the meeting area should be considered as well. Using K-Modes clustering and traffic hub complexity index is to evaluate the collision risk of the vessel meeting area. Taking Zhujiang River estuary and Hong Kong port water area as examples, the paper puts forward suggestions for modification of the vessel meeting area so as to meet actual demands of Zhujiang River estuary for large vessels meeting with the insufficient capacity situation. This paper not only make some suggestions, but also provides a reference for channel design and scientific formulation of vessel traffic management measures.

articleTitle: A Contour-Based Instance Segmentation Method for Copper Tube
abstract: Image segmentation is an essential prerequisite task for the defect detection approach. To improve the performance of defect detection in copper tube welding areas, a contour-based instance segmentation method is presented in this study. The proposed method is a coarse-to-fine process and it can be divided in two stages. Firstly, the coarse contour of welding areas is generated by learnable initial contour proposal architecture. Different from existed approaches, the proposed architecture applied the inner center replace the bounding box center for the center point prediction to ensure the center point falls inside the contour. Moreover, a label sampling strategy based on Douglas Peucker (DP) algorithm is proposed to enhance the performance of corner points sampling and a normalized corner attention loss function is proposed to reduce the learning difficulty. Secondly, an coarse contour deformation framework based on the multi-scale vertex feature fusion and low-level feature enhancement Deep Snake modules is organized to optimize the coarse contour obtained by first stage. The experimental results show that our method has achieved certain improvements in both segmentation accuracy and segmentation speed compared to the baseline method on both SBD benchmark and the copper tube dataset.

articleTitle: Learning to Simulate Labelled Datasets with an Image-Level Content Consistent Graph Constraint
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the explosive growth of data annotation due to the deep learning algorithm's thirst for labelled datasets. To ease the workload of data annotation, researchers begin to concentrate on automatic dataset generation, i.e. dataset synthesis via virtual engine like Unity. However, the large domain gap between the target and simulated images hinders the great potential of these methods. In this paper, we propose a novel method to simulate labelled datasets under an image-level content consistent graph constraint. A detection model is applied to extract the semantic content of target and simulated images, and the corresponding scene graphs are constructed to compare the differences between them. This method not only utilizes the high-dimensional features of the images to reduce the content gap between target and simulated datasets, but also reserves the differentiability of the whole learning pipeline. As a result, we are able to automatically simualte labelled datasts in an end-to-end manner, and the models trained on the simulated datasets behave the best against existing methods.

articleTitle: Research on Traceability Method of Gas Leak for Emergency Auxiliary Support
abstract: In the field of environmental emergency, sudden gas leaks cause great harm to the economy and society. In recent years, gas leaks have occurred frequently, and the problem of locating the source of air pollution is mainly divided into two steps: dispersion and traceability. However, the application of mechanism modeling or data-driven modeling methods for dispersion prediction is difficult to meet computational efficiency and prediction accuracy. Conventional source estimation methods also have the disadvantage of local optima in tracing pollution sources. In this paper, we propose a gaussian-machine learning model for gas dispersion prediction using gaussian features as inputs, and the improved particle swarm optimization algorithm that takes into account globally search and optimization. Predicted concentration is utilized as the input of the traceability model. Results demonstrate that this method have better performance on estimating leak location and concentration.

articleTitle: Visual SLAM Algorithm Based on YOLOv5 in Dynamic Scenario
abstract: Aiming at the problem of inaccurate pose estimation caused by dynamic feature points produced by dynamic objects during the operation of traditional SLAM system, a visual SLAM algorithm based on YOLOv5 is proposed to identify environmental images, distinguish dynamic objects in the scene and eliminate their dynamic feature points, and then use the remaining static feature points to perform oppositional geometric constraints. Finally determine the pose transformation matrix to improve the accuracy of the system. In this paper, the published TUM dataset is used to carry out experiments, and the results show that the algorithm adopted in this paper improves the relative positioning results of SLAM system in common dynamic situations, and reduces the mean of the median range of relative position error (RPE) in the monocular mode of the original ORB-SLAM3 by 91.53%. Effectively improve the positioning accuracy of the system.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning and Visual Guidance of a UAV under Field of View Constraint of Camera
abstract: When conducting visual landing, UAVs need to ensure the reasonableness of their flight trajectory and be under specific constraints on velocity and acceleration. Furthermore, to prevent the failure of the visual system, the cooperative target used for visual detection must always remain within the camera's field of view. In this paper, we first propose a PID controller-based IBVS guidance method. Then, a trajectory planning method based on the properties of Bezier curves and the tau coupling strategy is designed to satisfy the constraints on UAV velocity, acceleration, and camera field of view. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through simulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Resonant DC-DC Converter with Wide Voltage Gain
abstract: A novel resonant DC-DC converter is proposed in this article. By adding a capacitor to form a notch network, a zero voltage gain point is introduced into the voltage gain curve. The control strategy adopts traditional variable frequency control, and the system has good soft-switching characteristics and a wide voltage gain range. The structure, working mode, and the influence of parameters on the circuit characteristics are discussed. Finally, a 1-kW prototype is simulated and the results is given. The converter achieves an output voltage of 400V under the range of input voltage is 200-600V.

articleTitle: Links and Differences Among Wilkinson Iteration Refinement, Newton Iteration, and Zhang Neural Dynamics for Linear Equation System Solving
abstract: Solving linear equation system is not only a very important topic in theoretical research, but also a practical issue often encountered in engineering. This paper introduces the use of Wilkinson iteration refinement, Newton iteration, and Zhang neural dynamics (ZND) models to solve linear equation system. Links and differences among Wilkinson iteration refinement, Newton iteration, and ZND models in solving static linear equation system are found. Besides, the angles of arrival (AoA) positioning technique is utilized. The AoA technique is combined with the above models as an application of solving linear equation system. Through the numerical solving processes of static and time-varying equation system, links and differences among the above three methods are shown further.

articleTitle: State of Charge Estimation for the Lithium Battery Based on the IGWO-EKF Algorithm
abstract: The Extended Kalman Filtering (EKF) algorithm is the mainstream algorithm for State of charge (SOC) estimation. The uncertainty noise covariance matrix can slow down the EKF algorithm's correction of state variables, and even make the filtering process unstable or divergent, thereby reducing the accuracy of SOC estimation. Here, an improved Extended Kalman Filter algorithm with improved Grey Wolf Optimization is developed to address the above issue. Firstly, a first-order Thevenin lithium battery model is established to identify the battery parameters. Secondly, the Grey Wolf Optimization algorithm is improved and it is used to optimize the random noise covariance matrix of EKF. Finally, under different working conditions, the Simulation and battery test platform are built under different working conditions to demonstrate the validity of proposed algorithm, and the proposed algorithm can decrease SOC estimation error by 1%.

articleTitle: Multiple Fading Factors Extended Kalman Filter Based on Mahalanobis Distance for Robot Localization Under Measurement Abnormality
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of mobile robot positional estimation with robot localization under measurement abnormality. In order to improve the accuracy of position estimation without increasing the computational complexity, multiple fading factors extended Kalman filter based on Mahalanobis distance is proposed. The criterion of measurement abnormality is constructed based on the Mahalanobis distance of the innovation vector and the hypothesis testing method. A multiple fading factors matrix is constructed to provide different fading rates for different measurement data channels by combining the scalar fading factor and the innovation covariance, which realizes the adaptive adjustment of the statistical characteristics of measurement noise. Simulation results under two typical measurement abnormality scenarios verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Global Integrated Correction Algorithm for Marine Rotational Modulation Inertial Navigation Under Normal Vector Position Model
abstract: In order to suppress the navigation error accumulated over time in the polar marine inertial navigation system, the research group proposed a comprehensive correction algorithm based on the n-vector position model. In order to improve the global adaptability of the comprehensive correction algorithm, the algorithm is improved: 1 The adaptive conditions of the comprehensive correction algorithm are derived, and the adaptive range of the algorithm is further defined, that is, the comprehensive correction can be carried out only when the failure point is avoided. The effectiveness of the adaptive conditions is verified by using the simulation data. 2 The positioning accuracy of the algorithm can be improved by using the position reset method of the position reference signal at the failure point. Based on these two improvements, the comprehensive correction can be adapted globally.

articleTitle: Viscosity Measurement System Based On FreeRTOS Embedded Operating System
abstract: To address the limitations of traditional viscosity measurement methods, such as low intelligence and lack of remote control capabilities, this study presents a novel viscosity measurement and control system based on the FreeRTOS embedded real-time operating system. The proposed system partitions the viscosity measurement process into multiple tasks and schedules them in parallel using the FreeRTOS kernel. This architecture offers high operational efficiency, robust function expandability, and superior real-time performance compared to conventional embedded systems. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves high accuracy and stability in various viscosity measurement functions.

articleTitle: Intelligent Design of Complex Products Based on Extraction and Reconstruction of Key Dimensions
abstract: Complex products are characterized by many parts, complex assembly relationships, and a large number of part dimensions, etc. When there is a serialization demand or a change in the structural dimensions of the product, designers need to modify and reassemble each part one by one, which results in a large amount of workload and a high error rate. This paper presents an intelligent design approach for the above problems. First, the assembly relationship and size association logic of complex products are analyzed. Then, the key dimensions of complex products are characterized and extracted using the form of matrix and network diagram. Finally, the dimension data flow propagation model is constructed, and the functional relationship is established. Based on this approach, the secondary development of SolidWorks software with VB programming language is applied to establish the adaptive design platform for product dimensions modification. The dimension-driven adaptive design can improve the design efficiency of complex products with size modification. In this paper, the feasibility of both the theoretical method and software platform is verified by the intelligent design of the transition roller bed in an automotive coating line.

articleTitle: Reconfiguration Scheme Design of DRDES based on Simulated Annealing Algorithm
abstract: A dynamic reconfigurable discrete event system (DRDES) could change its configuration at runtime according to volatile internal/external execution environment. Under the premise that the target configuration is known, how to change the active configuration step by step without a system halt guaranteed by global performance indicators, is a hot topic in the research area of DRDESs. This work takes a low orbit satellite communication network system as an application example of DRDESs, where configurations are modeled by undirected graphs and the global performance indicator is the average invulnerability. After comparing the initial and the target configurations, the set of reconfiguration events are obtained and the simulated annealing algorithm is applied to find an adequate reconfiguration scheme that is a reconfiguration event sequence. The simulation results show that the algorithm can find an appropriate reconfiguration scheme efficiently such that the required maximum average invulnerability of the low orbit satellite communication network during dynamic reconfiguration is guaranteed.

articleTitle: Rotating Object Detection for Aerial Images Based on Improved YOLOv5
abstract: For the problem of low accuracy and ignoring target directionality in aerial object detection, a rotating object detection algorithm for aerial images based on improved YOLOv5s is proposed. Firstly, angles are processed using CSL to transform angle regression prediction into angle classification prediction, which solves the periodicity of angular and the exchangeability of edges, and improves detection accuracy. Secondly, the ability of the model to extract important features is enhanced by fusing an attention mechanism module. Finally, the NWD loss function is introduced to optimize the CIoU, mitigating the sensitivity of the IoU to small object position deviations and improving the robustness and generalization of the model. The experiment uses the DOTA dataset released by Wuhan University, and the result show that the improved YOLOv5 network model improved the mAP from 72.57% to 76.60 compared to the original network, demonstrating better performance in aerial images object detection by the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Modeling and Heuristic Solutions for Storage Scheduling of Steel Plates in Steel Logistics Park
abstract: Steel plates are highly customized according to different customer demands. In this case, the outbound date, the specifications of the steel plates and the distribution of stacks must be simultaneously considered when the steel plates are stored in the yard. Improper storage of steel plates significantly increases the number of shuffles during outbound operations. To overcome the challenge, we propose an efficient steel plate storage scheme based on the actual scenario of existing steel plate distribution in the yard. Firstly, a model for steel plate storage scheduling is established to minimize the number of extra blocking plates. Then, three heuristic algorithms are designed to solve the problem. Comparative experiments are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The experimental results show that the proposed method can sufficiently improve the efficiency of steel plates scheduling.

articleTitle: Path Curvature Based Variable Weight Multi-Constraint MPC for Smart Vehicle Trajectory Tracking Control
abstract: In order to balance the accuracy and stability of trajectory tracking for intelligent driving vehicles under the com-plex working conditions, this study proposes trajectory tracking control strategy based on path curvature variable weight model predictive control. model predictive control is established with front wheel steering angle and front wheel speed as control variables, using real-time lateral displacement error, longitudinal displacement error and azimuth error as inputs, and setting control volume constraints, control volume increment constraints and friction circle constraints. Based on changes in road curvature, the weight of the model predictive control objective function is optimised online, and the influence of the weight matrix on trajectory tracking accuracy and stability is coordinated. Based on Simulink, a vehicle kinematic model and control strategy were established to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy through simulation experiments. The results show that compared with linear time-varying model predictive control, the proposed variable weight control based on path curvature can reduce the maximum tracking displacement error by 65.70 %; and reduce the trajectory tracking mean square error by 55.06%. The maximum speed which satisfy the control tracking accuracy of not less than 0.3m can be increased by 20.69 %; The maximum speed which satisfy the control tracking accuracy of not less than 0.1m can be increased by 46.67%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Scheduling Efficiency of Steel Logistics Parks by Optimized Storage Distribution
abstract: The efficient management of storage has become a critical determinant of operational efficiency due to the growing and diverse demand for steel logistics parks. However, the current storage methods consistently result in significant imbalances in the loading of steel products and operating times across multiple yards. To address this challenge, we propose optimizing the distribution of steel products based on demand levels and retrieval efficiency. Firstly, we present an optimization problem that employs demand-driven storage principles to formulate the scheduling of steel product storage. Then, we introduce a novel algorithm called the Adaptive Preferred Evolutionary Heuristic (APEH) to tackle this problem. The results from our experiments indicate that this model effectively enhances the storage structure, and the proposed algorithm consistently yields optimal solutions within a reasonable timeframe.

articleTitle: Sample Selection Algorithm Based on Graph Centrality Weighted Anomaly Score
abstract: Selecting representative samples is very important to establish an accurate calibration model. When faced with data sets with different characteristics and a large number of samples, selecting representative samples effectively can save costs. To enhance the generality of this method and the representativeness of samples, a sample selection method is proposed, which takes the degree of anomaly as the evaluation standard and classifies samples according to the degree of anomaly. In this method, the anomaly scores corresponding to different detection methods are weighted to get a comprehensive evaluation. The weighting process of detecting method weights is used to describe their importance ratio, and a method to obtain weights by the centrality of graphs is proposed.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Integrated Energy System with Hydrogen Considering Gas Flow Dynamics
abstract: To increase renewable energy penetration, surplus renewable energy can be used to electrolyze water to produce hydrogen. Hydrogen can be blended with natural gas to facilitate low-cost, large-scale, and long-distance deliveries through the existing natural gas pipelines. To accurately model and schedule the integrated energy system with hydrogen, this paper develops an optimal scheduling approach considering gas flow dynamics. The scheduling problem of the integrated energy system with hydrogen is formulated as a time-domain mixed-integer problem with gas flow dynamics modeled using partial differential equations to guarantee the security of pipelines. The scheduling model also employs binary variables to represent the on/off states of devices, such as electrolyzers. By transforming time-domain partial differential equations into frequency-domain linear equations using a generalized phasor method, the problem is converted into a hybrid time-and-frequency domain mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) problem. The problem can be conveniently solved by commercial solvers and preserves the modeling accuracy of gas flow dynamics and the resulting security of pipelines. Numerical testing results demonstrate the modeling accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Spine Labeling Algorithm Based on IMAA-Unet
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is one of the commonly used inspection methods in clinical imaging diagnosis of human spinal diseases. Rapid and accurate localization and segmentation of vertebrae are helpful to the clinical diagnosis and treatment of spinal diseases. In this paper, according to Nash equilibrium principle, the training data is selectively augmented to obtain more comprehensive training data. Combine traditional Unet network with InceptionV2, Attention Gate, Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling to reduce contextual information loss. Then, the Merge module is added to enable the network to learn context features more fully. During marking and positioning, the vertebral body label is set to the coccygeal vertebra (S), the rest of the vertebral body, and the non-vertebral body. Then, the image data is used for training and the recognition model is generated. When it is necessary to mark and locate the spine, the image is recognized according to the trained spine recognition model, and the spatial position information between the recognized vertebrae is calculated. Based on the identification and positioning of coccygeal vertebra, the labeling and positioning of other vertebral bodies are completed. Compared with the results of traditional Unet and Unet++, the algorithm used in this paper has better recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Fine-Grained Vehicle Recognition Based on Deep Learning
abstract: This paper aims to solve the problem of low precision of fine grain identification in intelligent traffic and community security. Based on B-CNN, this paper proposes a fusion bilinear neural network model for fine-grained vehicle recognition. The image is input into the network, the double feature extractor New-Xception extracts the features of the image, and introduces the self-attention mechanism module to improve the overall performance of the network, improve the original pooling part, extract different attributes of the same location, and make comprehensive discrimination. Compared with other network models of the same class, the fusion model has obvious advantages in accuracy. It performs well on Stanford Cars, an open data set of Stanford University, with an accuracy rate of 94.6%, which verifies that the model is competent for the task of fine-grained vehicle recognition.

articleTitle: Tracking Control of Unmanned Surface Vessels Based on Fully Actuated System Approaches
abstract: Considering the complication and high requirements of controller design in unmanned surface vessels (USVs) from the perspective of under-actuated model, this paper investigates the tracking control of USVs in terms of fully actuated system approaches (FASA). We firstly propose a high-order fully actuated (HOFA) model of USV for path tracking. Then, using the idea and method of FASA controller design, a control law is proposed to make the closed-loop system obtain the dynamic characteristics we expect and decouple it into two linear systems, which can be achieved with simple and easy computation. The proposed USV path tracking control law achieves global asymptotic stability without continuous angular and forward velocity excitations. The effectiveness of this method is verified through MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: Almost Disturbance Decoupling for A Class of Underactuated Nonlinear Systems with Unknown Disturbances by Backstepping
abstract: In response to the lack of backstepping technology and almost disturbance decoupling (ADD) method in the under-actuated field, this paper proposes a new ADD controller design strategy for a class of underactuated nonlinear systems with unknown disturbances by using backstepping technology. Firstly, an error system is formed via a special state feedback, which is based on a partial differential equation (PDE). It can be deter-mined that this process is essentially the backstepping technique. Then, a novel error transformation is developed for the non-strict feedback problem of the formed error system. An ADD controller for the error system is designed by backstepping technology. Finally, the stability and ADD problem of the proposed strategy are verified according to converse Lyapunov theorem. The inertia wheel pendulum (IWP) with external matched disturbances is utilized to explain the effectiveness of the proposed strategy. From the simulation results, it can be seen that the proposed scheme possesses excellent control performance compared to previous underactuated control methods.

articleTitle: Degraded Image Semantic Segmentation Using Intra-image and Inter-image Contrastive Learning
abstract: Image degradation increases the difficulty of semantic segmentation, leading to the decreased accuracy. The gap of feature distribution between degraded images and clear images becomes a burden for accurate semantic segmentation. To solve this problem, we propose a contrastive learning method for degraded image semantic segmentation which is parallel to the semantic decoder of semantic segmentation network to utilize both intra-image and inter-image contrastive learning for feature representation. The former forces pixel embeddings and region embeddings belonging to the same semantic class to be more similar than the embeddings belonging to the different classes, while the latter utilizes memory banks to enhance the diversity of positive and negative samples. As a result, the intra-image and inter-image contrastive learning is able to effectively utilize multiple pixels, multiple regions, even multiple images to augment the degraded features and learn a more general representation of degraded features. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance on various benchmarks, including Cityscapes, ADE20K, FoggyDriving and our synthetic datasets. The code and synthetic datasets are open-sourced on Github: https://github.com/cocolord/degraded_image_seg.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Integrated Energy Systems in Hydrogen-containing Parks Considering Dynamic Energy Efficiency
abstract: Taking full account of the complexity of energy supply equipment and load demand of the integrated energy system of the park, to promote the absorption of offshore wind power and reduce the operating cost of the park, this paper proposes a hydrogen-containing park energy cascade optimization method considering the dynamic energy efficiency model. First of all, in order to make the energy structure reasonably and make full use, the comprehensive energy system framework used by energy steps is established. Secondly, considering the operation efficiency of the equipment is affected by the load rate, environment and other related factors, in order to make the energy equipment flexibly respond to the load change, the dynamic efficiency model of the equipment is established. Finally, the optimal scheduling model is developed with the objective of minimizing the operational costs of the system, and its effectiveness and rationality are validated through simulation examples.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Multi-Metric Fusion Learning
abstract: Deep learning-based bearing fault diagnosis methods have achieved good results in recent years. However, most of them depend heavily on massive labeled data and are not available for the situations under limited labeled samples. To alleviate the problem, this paper proposes a few-shot bearing fault diagnosis model based on multi-metric fusion learning, which is suitable for the inadequate data and variable conditions. The proposed model introduces Manhattan distance (Ll metric) and Euclidean distance (L2 metric) to measure the feature similarities of the support and test signals which are extracted by a Siamese network architecture. By adopting the maximum fusion strategy, these two measurement representations are fused together and the fault diagnosis is performed accordingly. Various experiments on the two publicly available datasets, CWRU and JNU, demonstrate that the proposed method not only achieves better diagnostic performance with limited labeled samples, but also has good transfer capability between different conditions.

articleTitle: Neural Architecture Search Method Based on Improved Monte Carlo Tree Search
abstract: With the continuous development of deep learning technology, various deep neural networks have been proposed to solve various problems, but the artificial design of neural network architecture requires certain professional knowledge and experience. The emergence of neural architecture search provides an automated solution for network architecture design. Current neural architecture search methods have a huge computational problem, and further research is needed to improve sample efficiency and network evaluation cost to obtain better results. In this paper, a neural architecture search method based on improved Monte Carlo Tree Search(MCTS) is proposed. The upper confidence interval (UCT) strategy of the tree is replaced by the RAVE strategy combining UCT strategy and AMAF strategy, and the absolute pruning strategy is added to better guide the search trajectory, speed up the convergence of the search tree and improve the accuracy of the results. By comparing the improved algorithm with the original tree search on the benchmark dataset, the feasibility of applying the improved algorithm to the neural network architecture search is proved, and the search process is accelerated.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control for a Compound Helicopter During Transitional Period
abstract: Compound helicopters exhibit a range of flight modes, which necessitates a transitional period to complete mode transitions. This transition period presents challenges, including manipulation redundancy and external disturbances. To address these issues, we initially develop a flight dynamics model for the compound helicopter. Subsequently, we develop a strategy for manipulating the transitional period by assigning weight coefficients to redundant manipulation mechanisms, taking into account the constraint of manipulation efficiency. Next, we employ the Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) theory to design ADRC controllers. These controllers, along with the module for assigning weight coefficients, form the ADRC control system. Lastly, we construct a simulation model and perform a comprehensive comparative analysis to verify the anti-disturbance capability of the ADRC controllers and assess the feasibility of the manipulation strategy. The simulation results clearly demonstrate that the ARDC controllers effectively track commands without any steady-state error, maintain stable control despite external disturbances, and ensure continuous and smooth changes in control variables within a reasonable range. Consequently, these outcomes validate the feasibility of the manipulation strategy.

articleTitle: Voxel Transformer with Shifted Windows for 3D Object Detection
abstract: Recent three-dimensional object detection methods are typically classified into point-based and voxel-based categories based on the processing method of raw point clouds. Voxel-based methods, which convert the point clouds to voxels to reduce computational load, often suffer from the geometric information loss and limited detection accuracy. In this paper, we propose a novel single-stage and voxel-based 3D object detection algorithm (VWTr) using Voxel Feature Encoder to extract features and Transformer Backbone with shifted windows to enhance the capability of feature extraction, which achieves a balance between accuracy and speed. The Transformer Backbone with shifted windows can help the network efficiently concentrate on global information and make up for the geometric information loss arose from the voxelization operation of the voxel feature encoder. To this end, we design a feature aggregation operation to enhance the network's representation capability. Relevant experiments on KITTI have demonstrated that our method has respectively reached 84.11%, 75.18%, 69.53% AP on three difficulty levels of KITTI car test set, which is superior to PointPillars algorithm,

articleTitle: Bipartite Synchronization of Multiplex Networks With Cooperative- Antagonistic Interactions
abstract: The bipartite synchronization (Bi-Syn) for multiplex networks with cooperative-antagonistic interactions is investigated. The interaction topology is described by multiple weighted and signed digraphs, and the single digraph can be structurally unbalanced and not strongly connected. With rearranging variables' order technique, we derive some sufficient conditions for exponential Bi-Syn with/without pinning control, whose validity is illustrated by two numerical examples.

articleTitle: Structural Innovation and Control System Design of Intelligent Linear Stroke Electric Actuator
abstract: The electric actuator holds significant importance within the process industry. Its fundamental operation involves the conversion of input signals into a linear displacement to drive regulating mechanism actions. This paper focus on enhancing the mechanical structure through the innovative modules such as the manual-automatic switching module, the compact main transmission mechanism, and efficient limit module. The developed intelligent control system enables functionalities like positive and negative effect setting, manual and automatic switching, and fault status display. Additionally, the integrated sensor facilitates real-time data acquisition and characteristic curve display software, fostering effective human-computer interaction. Finally, the actuator's strength and control precision undergo validation through fatigue experiments and vibration experiments.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning Method for the Weapon Target Assignment Problem with Unknown Hit Rate
abstract: The weapon target assignment problem is a combinatorial optimization problem that aims to assign multiple weapons to multiple targets to achieve optimal operational effectiveness. In previous studies, all methods for weapon target assignment problem are based on the assumption that the probabilities of successful interception are all known. In this paper, we take into consideration the situations where the probabilities of successful interception are unknown. We modify the mathematical model of the static weapon target assignment (SWTA) problem and decomposes it as a Markov decision process so as to apply deep reinforcement learning for this problem. Two sets of computational experiments are conducted, and the results show that the proposed reinforcement learning method has validity and generalization ability for the SWTA problem.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Feedback ILC Design for Batch Processes via Two-Dimensional System Theory
abstract: This study investigates a novel data-driven feedback iterative learning control algorithm under the two-dimensional system framework for batch processes. A set of linear two-dimensional models obtained from plant data by the dynamic linearization technique provides the information required to adjust the parameters of the presented control algorithm. The convergence of the data-driven control approach is derived by a rigorous analysis based on two-dimensional system theory such that the tracking error converges asymptotically along both time-axis and iteration-axis. A simulation example is presented to verify the validity of the researched scheme.

articleTitle: Hybrid Energy Storage Control Method For DC Microgrid Based On Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient
abstract: This research offers a deep reinforcement learning-based optimal control technique for a DC microgrid hybrid energy storage system (HESS) to increase system stability in the face of uncertainty in renewable energy generation and load volatility. First, the hybrid energy storage system is modeled and analyzed, and the voltage dynamic characteristics of the DC bus and current inner-loop tracking characteristics are investigated; a framework of the input/output-based deep reinforcement learning algorithm for the hybrid energy storage system's inner-loop is provided; and the reward function and neural network are designed to achieve optimal control of the hybrid energy storage system's DC/DC converter is provided. Finally, the suggested control strategy is compared to the PI double-loop control by modeling real-world scenarios of abrupt changes in renewable energy power and load power in the MATLAB/Simulink simulation program, and the effectiveness of the proposed control approach is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Petri Net Modelling and Motion Analysis of the Football Robot System
abstract: The football robotics competition has become one of the typical systems used in multi-robot research to study robot control, artificial intelligence and task allocation. The design of a football robot is a more integrated research module including robot design, visual information processing, and robot motion control. In this paper, a monocular global camera is used on the vision acquisition module to capture information within the football field in real time. Edge detection and feature point extraction are performed on the images after color recognition processing to obtain the position coordinates of the key elements of the football field, the football and the robot, thus significantly reducing the amount of information required for image processing. In addition to this, this paper builds Petri network models for different role robots to achieve different motion state control and analyses the temporal error of the robot's motion. The image processing approach and Petri net modelling used in this paper provide research directions for future indoor multi-robot localization approaches and task allocation.

articleTitle: Open-Circuit Fault Diagnosis for Grid-tied T-Type Inverters Using an LSTM Autoencoder
abstract: Grid-tied T-type inverters are widely used in photovoltaic power (PV), Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and other power conversion applications. However, their transistors are fragile and prone to open-circuit faults that can lead to power loss or system crashes. An open-circuit fault diagnosis method for grid-tied T-type converters is proposed based on the long short-term memory (LSTM) autoencoder. At first, the autoencoder extracts latent feature vectors automatically from the three-phase current series, and a low-dimensional feature is obtained. Then, the feature vectors are represented as the multivariate Gaussian distribution, and their distribution features are calculated. Finally, in the stage of online diagnosis, the latent features of real-time signals are extracted by only the encoder and used to measure the latent distance between the signals and the fault categories to realize fault diagnosis. The distance measurement ensures the accuracy of diagnosis instead of directly outputting fault categories by the learning model. Experiment results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: HingeSR: Using Hinges for Degraded Image Restoration and Super-Resolution
abstract: Single-image super-resolution (SISR) has been a fundamental task for various vision applications. In practice, the captured images are inevitable to be degraded due to the instability of image sensors, processors, and transmission or storage medium, and the degradation is fatal for most SISR methods which are experts in processing clean inputs. In this work, we proposed HingeSR, a dual-branch network for Degraded-image super-resolution (DegSR), which contains one Context U-Branch for Restoration and the other Pixel-Mapping Branch for Super-Resolution. Between them, hinge modules are utilized to fusion those features from two different domains. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method improves both quantitative and qualitative performance when compared with the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Event-Triggered Weighted Consensus of Multiagent System
abstract: This paper addresses fixed-time event-triggered weighted consensus problem for first-order multiagent system (MAS). First, event-triggered condition is designed and fixed-time event-triggered weighted consensus control is developed, which overcomes the difficulty brought by nonlinearity of fixed-time control protocol and intermittent communication and avoids continuous communication and monitoring. Next, the dynamics of weighted value under event-triggered environment is analyzed. Then, fixed-time convergence of the consensus error is analyzed and consensus time bound is derived. Finally, non-zeno behavior is analyzed and the result shows the developed control algorithm excludes zeno behavior. The developed algorithm is applied to active power and reactive power sharing among distributed generators (DGs) and numerical simulation validates its effectiveness.

articleTitle: An Improved PSO-SA-ML Algorithm for Longitudinal Aerodynamic Parameter Identification of the Aircraft
abstract: Aerodynamic parameter identification is one of the effective methods to obtain aerodynamic parameters of aircraft. Aiming at the problems that the maximum likelihood (ML) method is susceptible to the initial value, and the basic particle swarm optimization (PSO) is easy to precocious convergence. An improved PSO-SA-ML algorithm is proposed to identify aerodynamic parameters of the aircraft in this paper. The PSO algorithm is integrated with the maximum likelihood algorithm, and the adaptive inertia weight is added to improve it. Mean-while, the Metropolis criterion of the simulated annealing (SA) algorithm is introduced. The simulation results prove that the proposed improved PSO-SA - ML algorithm has the possibility of accepting poor solutions, enhances the optimization ability, and improves the convergence speed compared with basic PSO algorithm.

articleTitle: Anchor-Free Spatio-Temporal Attention Pyramid Network for Object Detection in Driving Scenes
abstract: In driving scenarios, perception and motion prediction are important guarantees for the safe and stable operation of autonomous vehicles. In recent years, an increasing number of studies have directly used raw point cloud data as input for perception and motion prediction. In this paper, we propose a new anchor-free spatio -temporal attention pyramid network that enhances the network's perception ability of driving scene objects by obtaining multiscale spatio -temporal contextual information, while substantially improving the accuracy of object detection in the network on the basis of ensuring the effectiveness of motion prediction. Experimental results on the nuScenes dataset show that our method significantly outperforms all state-of-the-art LiDAR-based networks in terms of perception.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Remote Sensing Image Classification Based on Class Centroid Alignment
abstract: Deep learning algorithms based on data-driven approaches have shown remarkable success in remote sensing image classification. Nevertheless, these methods often assume that the training data and test data adhere to the same distribution, which is not always the case in real-world scenarios. To address the constraints of unsupervised learning in land classification for remote sensing images and facilitate the automated annotation of land at a large scale across different sensors, this paper proposes a novel technique known as centroid alignment-based conditional domain confusion. This method aligns the class feature centroids of the source and target domains, leveraging category information in the conditional domain discriminator to enhance discriminative capabilities and achieve cross-domain distribution alignment at the class level. The proposed method is evaluated on the MRSSC2.0 dataset by conducting comprehensive experimental analysis. The results substantiate the efficacy of the proposed method in mitigating the domain shift in data distribution and enhancing the classification accuracy of cross-sensor high-resolution remote sensing images.

articleTitle: Roadside Bird's Eye View Perception Algorithm for Vehicle Tracking under Vehicle-Road Collaboration
abstract: Roadside perception is a crucial research area in the domain of intelligent vehicle-road collaboration. It aims to enhance collaboration between vehicles and the environment perception system while improving perception coverage and accuracy. This paper proposes a two-stage perception and localization algorithm utilizing a bird's eye view from roadside sensing units. The algorithm utilizes an object detection approach rooted in deep learning, which is then followed by a coordinate transformation and correction algorithm. The coordinate transformation is a fusion of the camera imaging principle and inverse perspective mapping. By taking these steps, we can localize human-vehicle objects and construct a car-following model for vehicle-road cooperation using a leader-follower approach. Experimental tests are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for perceiving targets and localizing unmanned vehicles following human movement. The results demonstrate that the lightweight bird's eye perception algorithm implemented through roadside sensing units can provide essential perception and location for autonomous vehicle car-following behaviors. This algorithm holds significant potential applications in intelligent parking, obstacle avoidance for car-following vehicles, and inspection of unmanned vehicles.

articleTitle: Water Quality Index Forecasting via Transformers: A Comparative Experimental Study
abstract: Water quality index (WQI) forecasting plays a crucial role in water resource management and water pollution control. It can provide early warnings and facilitate proactive prevention measures. This paper focuses on the task of long-term WQI forecasting utilizing transformer models. We first provide a brief overview of the basic Transformer and its seven improved models, namely Reformer, Informer, Autoformer, Pyraformer, FEDformer, Crossformer, and PatchTST. Based on this survey, we conduct a comparative experimental study by applying these eight transformer models to forecast WQI for two national monitoring river sections. The experimental results reveal that the PatchTST and Crossformer models outperform other models across almost all future forecasting window sizes, including very long-term settings.
