Abnormalities or faults in the laminar cooling are unavoidable, and the mechanical and physical performance of the strip steel will be affected if they can't be handled in time. Considering these characteristics such as the spatial distribution of the strip temperature and the variable environmental conditions, a fault tolerant control scheme with boundary feedback is proposed for the laminar cooling of the hot-rolled strip steel, which is usually described by heat conduction models with hyperbolic partial differential equations. Firstly, laminar cooling process is divided into several subsystems and the dynamic descriptions of them with time-space coupled can be obtained; Then, for the faultfree case, stabilizing boundary feedback controllers is established based on backstepping approach with the characteristic of interconnection between subsystems; Next, the solvability conditions are characterized to maintain the stability of the faulty systems, and the fault tolerant control strategies are provided by the output feedback regulator; Finally, an experiment is conducted to demonstrate the practical application effects by a real laminar cooling process data.

articleTitle: Lightweight 3D Object Detection Based on Bridging Structure
abstract: The study of 3D object detection based on deep learning has increasingly grown in importance in the realm of autonomous driving technology. In this study, we developed a lightweight 3D object detection model based on bridge structure while maintaining the model's accuracy. The model has a much smaller number of parameters. The SGE attention mechanism and the cross-attention mechanism module are first integrated into a backbone network that enhances the lightweight CNN's global semantic information. Second, the loss of target details is prevented thanks to a new bridging structure. Finally, the model's parameter count is decreased using the weight fusion recovery training-based model pruning technique. According to the experimental findings, the model's calculation amount is decreased by 50% while its detection accuracy is raised by 1% to 2%.

articleTitle: GO-LIO: Lidar-IMU SLAM Algorithm Based on Ground Optimization
abstract: To address the drift problem of existing Simultaneous Localization And Mapping (SLAM) algorithms in the vertical Z-axis direction during autonomous navigation of unmanned vehicles in urban road scenarios, this paper proposes GO-LIO: a robust algorithm based on ground optimization with tightly coupled Lidar and IMU. The algorithm is divided into three main parts: distortion removal, ground optimization, and loop closure detection. To address the problem of insufficient constraints in the Z-axis direction, correction is performed using residuals constructed from ground distances. To address the problem of error accumulation caused by low-quality ground estimation in ground constraints, a fitting detection method is employed to verify the authenticity of the fitted ground. To address the issues of continuity and consistency in large-scale mapping, a loop closure detection method is employed to perform secondary correction of errors in the Z-axis direction. The experimental results indicate that this method exhibits excellent robustness in urban road scenes. Compared to ALOAM and FAST-LIO2 algorithms, it achieves a 17.5% and 33.1% improvement in Z-axis accuracy on the KITTI seq 00, respectively. Under the highly challenging dataset collected by ourselves, it was improved by 6.7% compared with FAST-LIO2.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Flamingo Algorithm and Application for Compression Spring Design
abstract: The Flamingo Search Algorithm (FSA) is a new swarm intelligence optimization algorithm proposed in 2021. It has a unique search mechanism and mathematical model. However, when handling complex optimization problems, it has defects such as low convergence accuracy, low stability, and easy fall into local optimization. Given these shortcomings, a Flamingo algorithm with the adaptive and lens learning strategy (LILAFSA) is proposed. First of all, the population is initialized with the theory of good point set. Secondly, a nonlinear adaptive factor is added to balance the exploration and production capabilities of the algorithm. Then, the reverse learning strategy of convex lens imaging is introduced to improve the diversity of the population in the later stage. At the same time, the water wave dynamic adaptive factor is added to the attacker's location update to enhance the ability of jumping out of the local optimum. Finally, six benchmark test functions are used to test the ability of the improved algorithm and apply it to mechanical design optimization problems. The experimental results show that FSA has good performance in engineering design optimization problems.

articleTitle: Multi-Granularity Feature Fusion Network for Dynamic Sequential Facial Expression Recognition
abstract: Dynamic sequential facial expression images can effectively reflect the essence of dynamic process of facial expression, and it is easy to eliminate the influence of various interference factors existing in static facial expression images. However, most previous studies only recognize static facial expression images, ignoring the facial expressions change is a dynamic and continuous process. To address these issues, this work proposes a network based on multi-granularity feature fusion for dynamic sequential facial expression recognition. The proposed network firstly extracts 68 facial landmarks of each frame in the sequence, and then calculates two types of offset distances of different frame’ s facial landmarks in the sequence. One is the offset distances of landmarks between each frame and the first frame. Another is the offset distances of landmarks between two adjacent frames. These distances are served as the coarse-granularity feature of the facial expression sequence. Meanwhile, the facial features of single image in the sequence are used as the fine-granularity feature of the facial expression sequence. Finally a dual channel neural network model is built to learn muti-granularity features for predicting facial expression. Compared with the experimental results of mainstream facial expression recognition methods on the CK+ and Oulu-CASIA datasets, this method has improved the accuracy by 1.21% and 3.34% respectively.

articleTitle: Research on Low Overlap 3D Point Cloud Reconstruction Algorithm Based on Kinect Camera
abstract: 3D reconstruction technology covers many fields and is getting closer and closer to public life. In this paper, a complete set of 3D object reconstruction processes based on the Kinect camera is designed by acquiring point cloud data from the Kinect camera and performing 3D reconstruction, in which the acquisition of point cloud data and point cloud registration are the two key problems that need to be solved to realize 3D reconstruction. This paper addresses these two issues. Firstly, the Kinect camera is selected to acquire the point cloud data, and the Kinect camera is calibrated. By analyzing the noise interference of the data acquired by the Kinect camera, it is decided to remove the noise by using the method of bilateral filtering. Secondly, the process of users acquiring point cloud data of target objects with the Kinect camera will be interfered with by various factors, which results in low overlap between 3D point clouds. Therefore, this paper proposes a second-order spatial metric point cloud registration algorithm based on FPFH features, which, compared with the traditional point cloud registration method, is able to have a good registration effect between different overlapping rates, and finally, all the point clouds are registered to the same coordinate system to complete the 3D reconstruction.

articleTitle: Research on Pseudorange Differential Relative Positioning Spoofing Method Based on Repeater
abstract: The spoofing problem of pseudorange differential relative positioning is researched in this paper, and the pseudorange differential relative positioning spoofing method based on repeater is designed. Firstly, the feasibility of spoofing rover station in relative differential positioning systems is analyzed and demonstrated. The constraint on the precise offset positioning results is obtained, and then the repeater spoofing scheme is used to deceive. The delay of each channel is dynamically manipulated by calculating the spoofing parameters of each channel to achieve precise positional offset spoofing of the pseudorange differential relative positioning system terminal. Finally, the simulation experiment is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the method. The study has some theoretical and practical value, as it enhances the spoofing attack capability of attackers.

articleTitle: Fast Aerial Image Stitching Algorithm for UAV Based on Improved SURF
abstract: In order to address the realtime performance and robustness issues in UAV aerial image stitching, an improved SURF-based algorithm is proposed. This algorithm enhances the stitching process for UAV aerial images by first employing the Speeded-Up Robust Features SURF algorithm for rapid and robust feature point detection and localization. Subsequently, binary BRISK descriptors are used for feature description. In the feature matching phase, an initial coarse matching is performed using the Nearest-Neighbor Distance Ratio NNDR algorithm to filter out correct match pairs. Then, precise matching is achieved through the application of the PROSAC algorithm. Finally, a weighted fusion algorithm is employed for seamless image stitching. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in both matching efficiency and accuracy achieved by this algorithm. It serves as a robust and highly accurate solution with excellent stitching outcomes for UAV aerial image stitching.

articleTitle: A Variational Neural Network for Image Segmentation Based on Chan-Vese Model
abstract: The Chan-Vese model for image segmentation is a fundamental region-based model under variational level set framework with a lot of variants for different tasks. Although its solution schemes have been investigated systematically, the segmentation results depend heavily on hand crafted models and algorithms, especially annoying parameter tuning. The computational efficiency is a challenging problem also. Modern deep learning methods based on neural networks are excellent alternatives to deal with these problems, but there are also problems such as un-explanation, discontinuous boundaries, and noise sensitivity. In this paper, we propose a novel deep neural network framework for image segmentation based on algorithm unfolding of Chan-Vese model to inherit the merits of variational models and neural networks without their demerits. Firstly, the original Chan-Vese model is reformulated using a data term of multichannel images and a boundary length term via fields of experts. Secondly, the algorithms are designed based on the splitting method and alternating direction optimization to decompose the original minimization problem into some sub-optimization problems which can be solved iteratively or analytically. Finally, a supervised Chan-Vese network (CVN) is designed based on the corresponding relations of iterative algorithms and network layers, in which the convolutional kernels are designed based on convex combinations of discrete cosine transformation basis, activation functions are parametric soft thresholding formulas. Experiments based on ground truth datasets demonstrate the properties of CVN visually and the advantages of CVN over Chan-Vese model and other existing semantic segmentation networks.

articleTitle: Identification of Nonlinear Multi-Input Multi-Output Systems Based on Maximum Likelihood Principle
abstract: Identification of multi-input multi-output (MIMO) industrial system with block structure is helpful to analyze the dynamic characteristics of the system, and beneficial to design the controller based on the model and the operation monitoring. Based on the identification strategy, the model of MIMO Hammerstein structure has a unique advantage to fit the dynamic input and output data of the process. A parameterized identification algorithm without increasing the number of parameters to be identified is proposed based on the maximum likelihood principle (MLC). Compared with the conventional parameterized identification method, the proposed identification algorithm can effectively separate the coupled nonlinear static parameters from the system dynamic parameters, and reduce the compute calculation amount of the identification algorithm and the variance of parameter estimation error. Besides, an adaptive forgetting factor is also constructed to improve the convergence rate and stability. Finally, the superiority and advantage of the proposed algorithm is verified by a chemical process.

articleTitle: Ananlysis and Scheduling for Distributed Robust Production Lines with Bernoulli Machines and Sequence-dependent Setup Time
abstract: Driven by the increasing need of enterprises to meet the demands of multi-cooperation production, the distributed flow shop scheduling problem (DFSP) has emerged as a cutting-edge research topic in the field of flexible manufacturing. Because of the uncertainties in practical production environment of the distributed production lines, the processing efficiency of machines can be undetermined in different scenarios. In this paper, a robust model for DFSP with Bernoulli machines and sequence-dependent setup time is studied. Firstly, the robust model and the analysis of distributed production lines are formulated. Secondly, an improved genetic algorithm with linear rank selection and acceptance criterion is proposed, which has been empirically proven to effectively overcome the issue of being stuck in local optima. Finally, the result of the comparative experiments shows that the proposed improved genetic algorithm can solve the distributed flow shop scheduling problem with uncertain processing efficiency (UPE) and sequence-dependent setup time.

articleTitle: The Scheduling of Dual Pipeline Crude Oil: A Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: In this paper, a short-term scheduling method for refinery crude oil in dual pipelines based on deep reinforcement learning algorithm is proposed. First of all, the short-term scheduling problem of dual-pipeline crude oil in refinery is converted into the solution of pipeline operation sequence. PPO algorithm is then used to construct action value network to solve the model. After that, we introduce the specific design of a refinery's dual pipelines based on deep reinforcement learning aiming at minimizing the total cost consumption. Finally, the action value network model is trained by using actual data, and the results are compared with the scheduling scheme of the currently used intelligent optimization algorithms. Simulation results indicate the feasibility and optimization of the proposed method, and provide a new approach for the short-term scheduling of dual pipeline crude oil in refineries.

articleTitle: Vision-Based Urban Rail Vehicle Fault Detection Using Enhanced YOLO Framework
abstract: Urban rail transit systems serve as pivotal city transport modalities. However, conventional vehicle condition monitoring methodologies often fail to provide realtime respon-siveness, potentially giving rise to safety hazards. Predominant vehicle state detection research leans on data from TVDS and TEDS systems, engendering inconsistencies due to diverse vehicle types and data quality variations. This consequently impacts the optimal performance of existing algorithms in urban rail transit contexts, particularly in minor entity detection. To mitigate this, a novel vehicle state detection approach premised on YOLOv5 is presented in this study. A Coordinate Attention Mechanism (CA) is implemented to augment local detail extraction in vehicle status images. Additionally, the conventional Feature Pyramid Network(FPN) is supplanted with a Progressive Feature Pyramid Network(PFPN), facilitating superior multilevel feature fusion devoid of information degradation. On application of this model to an urban rail vehicle state dataset, noteworthy results, including an accuracy of 0.98, recall rate of 0.96, and mean average precision (MAP) of 0.983, are realized. Such outcomes illustrate excellent object detection performance, sans significant augmentation of the model's parameter size.

articleTitle: A Mill Load Identification Method Based on Deep Neural Network
abstract: Mill load identification is crucial for the grinding process. Accurate identification of mill load is beneficial for enhancing the overall production efficiency and ensuring safe operation throughout the entire grinding classification process. The internal conditions of the mill are complex and difficult to detect directly, so ore processing plants often identify mill load through grinding sound signals or mill vibration signals generated during the grinding process. Currently, most of the mill load identification methods based on grinding sound signal or mill vibration signals are realized by signal processing and traditional machine learning. However, these methods are difficult to fully extract the features of the signals and the identification effect needs to be improved. In this study, a mill load identification method based on deep neural network from grinding sound is proposed, which takes the Mel spectrogram of the grinding sound signal as input and uses the Resnet34 network as the base network. Combining with the temporal characteristics of spectrogram, a spatial attention mechanism is introduced in the network. And a soft thresholding mechanism based on spatial attention is proposed for the problem that the complex industrial environment makes the grinding sound signal contain a large amount of redundant information. In experimental comparison, the accuracy of the proposed method is 93.5%, which is 4.5% higher than the original Resnet34 and has faster convergence speed, which verifies the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: IOADA: An Optimal Automated Augmentation Algorithm for Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Deep learning has seen remarkable advancements in the field of automatic data augmentation, but its implementation in medical imaging remains constrained due to a predominant focus on natural images. To solve the problem of complex spatial information and high acquisition cost of medical images, we propose a differentiable automatic data augmentation framework based on Sinkhorn optimal transport and proximal updates(IOADA), which encompasses a specialized search space and leverages enhanced algorithms tailored specifically for complex medical images. Through our approach, the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) for retinal image segmentation increased by 2.18% and 3.78<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on two datasets. Additionally, the DSC scores on the SKIN, STS2D, and LIVER datasets all exceeded 90%, and the model significantly reduces the time costs involved. Furthermore, our approach demonstrates successful transferability to other medical image segmentation tasks. These findings underscore the potential of our method in enhancing medical image analysis by employing efficient and effective data augmentation techniques.

articleTitle: Deep Q-Network Based Inter-Station Tracking Control for Virtual Coupling Trains
abstract: Virtual Coupling (VC) is a technology based on vehicle-vehicle communication that allows multiple trains to operate as a virtually coupled train set (VCTS) without physical hook connections. The V CTS employs the relative distance braking mode to calculate a safe distance between trains, thereby significantly reducing the tracking interval. However, the risk of train collisions increases with smaller intervals. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a V CTS inter-station tracking control strategy based on relative distance braking mode to ensure safe distance between trains and decrease speed errors. Additionally, the paper utilizes the Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithm to achieve automatic control of the following trains. Finally, it is verified through experiments that the DQN algorithm can effectively control the operation of VCTS and has a certain limit to the interference, and the control performance is better than the existing control algorithm.

articleTitle: A Multi-Scale Defect Detection for Steel Surface Based on Improved Faster R-CNN
abstract: The accuracy of defect detection is increased by the improved Faster R-CNN detection algorithm, which addresses the issue of an extended target scale span and complex characteristics causing missed detection in steel surface defect detection. The algorithm introduces path aggregation network (PANet), which uses bottom-up path aggregation to combine shallow details and deep semantic information to better capture features on various dimensions. It also adapts the reconstruction of the anchor box size information to filter out the optimal proposal box for more accurate localization. The backbone network of the original Faster R-CNN is replaced with an improved ResNet50, which has more powerful feature extraction skill and makes the model more flexible. On the NEU-DET dataset, the improved algorithm's detection performance is contrasted with that of other detection algorithms. According to the results of the investigation, the Faster R-CNN with additions has an average detection rate of 63.7 frames per second (FPS) and a mean average precision (mAP) of 80.2%, which is 8.7 percentage points higher than that of the Faster R-CNN. The conclusion is that the boosted Faster R-CNN can enhance both the precision and localization information of multi-scale faulty targets.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Power Supply Potential of Microgrids Considering Uncertain Energy Output
abstract: To address the impact of uncertainty in clean energy output on the power supply potential of microgrids connected to large-scale clean energy, a method for evaluating the power supply potential of microgrids considering uncertain energy output is proposed. Firstly, a long and short term memory neural network is used to predict the wind power and photovoltaic output within the microgrid, and empirical modal decomposition and principal component analysis are used to reduce the data dimensionality of the neural network and improve the prediction accuracy.Based on the prediction results of the uncontrollable energy output, the risky standby power of the microgrid at different confidence levels is calculated based on the internal energy storage and load power consumption of the microgrid, and the external power supply potential of the microgrid at different confidence levels is derived. A microgrid system is selected for simulation to validate the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method can accurately assess the supply potential of the microgrid at different confidence levels.

articleTitle: Copyright Page
Cover Page
Table of Contents
GCE-YOLOv5s Based Surface Defect Detection Algorithm for Strip Steel
abstract: The detection of surface defects on the strip steel is an indispensable step in the production process. Aiming at the traditional strip steel inspection method exists slow detection speed, detection accuracy is not high and so on problems, proposed the GCE-YOLOvSs method which based on ameliorate YOLOvSs. First, we used the Ghost module instead of the ordinary convolution module to reduce the volume of parameters and computational complexity of the original network. Secondly, in order to increase the sensitivity of the original network to the information characterizing defects on the strip surface and to make it more accurate in localization, insert CA (Coordinated Attention) attention module into feature extraction network part. Finally, the bounding box loss is computed using the EIOU loss function, which allows the predicted box to move closer to the true box more quickly. The experimental outcomes demonstrate that the method achieves a mAP(Mean Average Precision) of 80.6% on the NEU-DET public dataset, surpassing the original network model by 3.3%. Additionally, there is a reduction of 47% and 48.7% in the parameter volume and computation, respectively, and the detection speed of 78 FPS (Frames Per Second) was achieved on a single GPU to satisfies the detection requirements.

articleTitle: A Rolling-Horizon Approach for Mitigation of Exhaust Emissions in Urban Traffic Networks
abstract: With the continuous and rapid increase in the number of motor vehicles in our country, vehicle exhaust emission pollution is one of the important sources of air pollution, so the prevention and control of motor vehicle exhaust pollution is becoming more and more severe. Aiming at the problem of vehicle exhaust emissions in the urban transportation networks, this paper proposes a predictive control method based on the Macroscopic Fundamental Diagram, which can not only reduce vehicle exhaust emissions, but also alleviate the congestion of the transportation network. According to the historical traffic data of the road network, we obtain the macroscopic fundamental diagram of the sub-road networks through the polynomial fitting method, and then construct the traffic dynamics model between multi-sub road networks on this basis. Then, a mixed pollutant emission model is constructed by using the relationship between the pollutant emission rate and the state of the vehicles in the road network. With the objective function of minimizing pollutant emissions, we design a model-based road network optimization control method, and simulate three different traffic scenarios. The results show that the proposed predictive control method can effectively alleviate the congestion of the road network and reduce the pollutant emissions of vehicles.

articleTitle: Formation Control of Leader-Following Multi-AGV with Communication Delay and Acceleration Disturbance
abstract: This paper explores the issue of multi-Automated Guided Vehicles formation control in special scenarios. The leader-following type of formation is adopted, take account of both the time delay in communication between AGVs and the disturbance caused by the acceleration of the leader AGV. In the first, a third-order kinematic model is established for the driving mode of the automated guided vehicles. Secondly, a composite controller consisting of an integral sliding mode controller and a feedback controller is designed. The feedback controller is used for the followers to track the leader AGV, the distinctive sliding surface of the sliding mode controller enables compensation for jerk. Thus, the effect of the acceleration disturbance from the leader is mitigated. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by Matlab/simulink simulation software.

articleTitle: Autonomous Unmanned Vehicle Based on SLAM
abstract: In the UAV distribution center, the use of unmanned vehicles as the UAV carrier platform can perfectly compensate for the short time that UAVs are in the air, while saving manpower and material resources, autonomously completing navigation and obstacle avoidance in known environments, and at the same time. With human-computer interaction function, it provides target tracking ability, which greatly facilitates the centralized and distributed management of UAVs.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Composite DC-DC Converter Structure for Battery SOC Balance System
abstract: Lithium batteries are widely used in electric vehicles (EVs) energy storage systems because of their long life and high energy density. This paper presents an active state-of charge (SOC) balancing system architecture for EVs utilizing isolated DC-DC power converters. The system consists of multiple battery cells connected in series and parallel with different DC-DC converters. By adjusting the duty cycle of each converter, not only the active SOC balancing of the battery can be realized, but also the continuous and stable power supply to both high-voltage and low-voltage loads can be provided simultaneously without additional power loss. In this paper, the working principle of this system architecture is described in detail, and a simulation model is built using Matlab/Simulink to verify the experiment.

articleTitle: Angles-Only Orbit Determination Method Based on Strong Tracking Extended Kalman Filter
abstract: For common GEO (Geostationary Orbit Satellite) service satellites, using cameras to orbit non-cooperative targets in space is of great significance for improving space survivability. Aiming at the problem that the distance of angles-only measurement is not observable, this article explains first the observability of maneuvering orbit determination, analyses the influence of maneuvering on observability, and gives the observability index function according to this. On this basis, the interior point method is used to solve the problem of optimal space maneuvering direction under the constraint conditions, considering the constraints of relative position and anti-collision based on the CW (Clohessy-Wiltshire) equation. Aiming at the problem that the unknown velocity pulse maneuvering of non-cooperative target will lead to the divergence of filtering results, a strong tracking extended Kalman filter is used to determine the orbit of the target. The simulation results show that the proposed orbit determination method can reach the orbit determination error within 1 km within a short time after the maneuver. Compared with other single-line Angle measurement methods, the proposed method has faster convergence, higher orbit determination accuracy and better stability.

articleTitle: A Casual-Based Operational Analysis Framework for Multi-UAV Systems
abstract: In the collaborative task scenario of heterogeneous Multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle(UAS) systems, there are many factors which affecting mission efficiency, and they form a network with potential casual relationship. How to effectively analyze the causal relationship between each factor and the mission efficiency indexes is of great significance for improving the system efficiency. Thus, an casual-based analysis framework is proposed to identify the critical factors affecting the operation efficiency. Based on the traditional correlation test method, the framework proposed a rule-based test method identifying meta casual relationships of the network. The framework is verified in experimental environment which shows that it has reference value in the operational efficiency research of multi-UAV systems and guide the deployment of UAV system.

articleTitle: Robust Monocular Visual Odometry with Point-Line Features in Low-texture Scenes
abstract: Traditional visual SLAM systems rely on tracking point features for camera pose estimation and environment map construction. However, these tasks remain challenging in low-texture scenes where the number of available features is limited. This paper proposes a novel visual odometry solution that incorporates both point and line features. To be robust in low-texture scenes, the proposed method develops the LSD algorithm to detect line features, which includes short lines rejection and line segments merging to improve the identification of line features. Validating our approach, we conduct experiments on the EuRoC and TUM datasets and compared our results with ORB-SLAM2 and PL-SLAM, which demonstrate that our method not only improves the quality of extracted line segments but also reduces the time consumption required for line segment tracking. Additionally, the visual odometry presented in this paper shows greater robustness in low-textuer environments.

articleTitle: Input-Output Finite-Time Stability of Nonlinear Descriptor Systems via Hamiltonian Function Method
abstract: The problem of the input-output finite-time stability (IO-FTS) of nonlinear Hamiltonian systems is tackled in this paper. Two types of disturbance inputs, which belong to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\infty}$</tex> are considered. This paper presents the sufficient condition on the basis of a dissipative Hamiltonian differential-algebraic system to study its stability with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\infty}$</tex> disturbance inputs. At last, an example of a nonlinear Hamiltonian system is given, and the performance of the simulation illustrates the effectiveness of studying the IO-FTS problem via the Hamiltonian function method.

articleTitle: Physics- Informed Neural Network Based Dynamic Estimation for Power Grid Using a Kuramoto-Like Model
abstract: Dynamic state estimation for power grid is an important task for power system monitoring and operation. In this paper, we build the power network dynamic model with the form of the Kuramoto model, and use the physics-informed neural network (PINN) to capture the dynamics of the power system. Physics-informed neural network is a new deep learning method that can incorporate the mathematical models describing power grid dynamics into network training to achieve high accurate estimation, while using less training data. We also verify the effectiveness by a simulation on a two generators-one machine power grid system.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Control Strategy Based on Integral Terminal Sliding Mode for Three-Level Neutral Point Clamped Converter
abstract: To improve the capability of current loop of the three-level neutral point clamped (3L-NPC) inverter, the integral terminal sliding mode control (ITSMC) for the current inner loop of the 3L-NPC inverter is proposed. Firstly, the math equation of the system is set up. Secondly, the sliding surface of ITSMC is designed. Due to the introduction of proposed strategy, this method can ensure that the error of converter current converges to 0 in a fixed time. Thirdly, the controller of ITSMC is designed based on Lyapunov function. Besides, the stability proof of the strategy is derived as well. In comparison with the traditional proportional-integral (PI) method, the convergence velocity of the converter current is greatly raised, and the anti-interference ability of 3L-NPC is also enhanced. Comparative simulations between PI controller and proposed ITSMC method are put forward to verify the effectiveness and merits of ITSMC strategy.

articleTitle: UneLRPt: A Light Network in Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: The fusion of U-Net and attention mechanism has emerged as a novel approach for medical image segmentation. However, the simple combination of U-Net and the Transformer can lead to model overloading and slow inference. Some studies have attempted to replace traditional convolutions with new blocks, such as depth-wise convolutions, to reduce the model's burden. Due to the presence of a large number of point-wise convolutions, the memory access of these networks is high, which actually further prolongs the inference time. In the field of clinical medicine, intelligent assistance for diagnosis is gradually becoming popular. For deployment on edge devices, it is crucial to build a lightweight and fast network while ensuring accuracy. To solve these problems, we propose a novel framework called UneLRPt. Based on the U-Net, it combines a multi-layer bottleneck with sliding windows, a channel mixing function and a partial convolution without point-wise convolution. We extensively test the UneLRPt on two public datasets involving two organs (breast and skin tissues) and two imaging modes (ultrasound and original images) on three devices. Compared to U-Net, UneLRPt decreases parameters and FLOPs by 97.308% and 86.619% respectively while only decreasing 0.013~0.059 in mean intersection over union and 0.043~0.06 in accuracy in two datasets, making contributions to intelligent diagnosis in clinical medicine.

articleTitle: Oil-Paper Insulation State Analysis Based on Subjective-Objective Comprehensive Assignment and Double-Basis Point Method
abstract: The accurate diagnosis of transformer oil-paper insulation state has important guiding significance for the formulation of maintenance strategy. In order to realize the objective scientific evaluation of the insulation state of oil-paper, a multi-feature comprehensive evaluation model of transformer oil-paper insulation state based on combined weight-double base point method is proposed. Firstly, based on the shortcomings of the single feature quantity evaluation, based on the existing time-domain dielectric spectrum data, multiple aging feature quantities are extracted from the recovery voltage polarization spectrum and the extended Debye equivalent circuit respectively, and a standard evaluation index system is established.Secondly, it proposes an index combination weighting model that takes into account the subjective experience of experts and objective differences in data, overcoming the shortcomings of the single weighting method. Finally, the closeness of the object to be evaluated and the ideal point of the standard state is calculated based on the double base point method, and the comprehensive evaluation result of the oil paper insulation state is obtained.The example verification shows that the evaluation model built in this paper can effectively and accurately diagnose the insulation state of the transformer, which can provide a new method for the evaluation of transformer oil-paper insulation state.

articleTitle: Cascaded Feedback Pyramid Network for Salient Object Detection base on Microorganism Image
abstract: Salient Object Detection (SOD) has made significant progress, thanks to the effectiveness of various feature aggregation strategies. Nevertheless, prevalent methods frequently combine low-level features with intricate details and high-level features carrying semantic information across a broad spectrum. This amalgamation introduces noise into the aggregated features, resulting in the generation of inaccurate saliency maps. However, when these methods are applied on microorganism images, they usually face numerous challenges due to the limited foreground-background contrast of microorganism images. To address these problems, a Cascaded Feedback Pyramid Network (CFP-Net) is designed. Specifically, multi-scale parallel convolution (MPC) is introduced to preprocess the features of the backbone network to obtain a larger perceptual field. The cross aggregation module (CAM) is designed to adaptively select complementary components from input features before feature fusion, effectively avoiding the introduction of excessive redundant information that might disrupt the original features. Furthermore, the pyramid feedback decoder (PFD) is designed, which adopts a multi-level feedback mechanism to introduce the progressively refined features from the CAM to the output of the original layers, complementing them and eliminating feature disparities. Experiments show that CFP-Net can accurately segment microbial regions and provide clear local details on the microorganism dataset, and our method can effectively improve the SOD performance on microorganism images.

articleTitle: A Location Selection Method for Infected Areas Material Distribution Based on SIR Model and GA-K - means Algorithm
abstract: The sudden outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic has had a serious impact on the health and daily life of people. The problem of determining where to put household goods during an epidemic is particularly important. This paper proposes a siting method for the distribution of supplies in disaster area relief missions. Firstly, a qualitative analysis of the SIR prediction model for infectious diseases is established, and it is learned that how subsistence supplies are distributed has a direct impact on the direction of the number of infected people in the disaster area. Secondly, the entropy weight is applied to comprehensively evaluate the reasonableness of the number of material drop-off points. The optimal number, location, and size of drop-off points are determined by the GA-K-means clustering algorithm. This algorithm resulted in a 22.88% reduction in the overall number of task drop-off points. The average contour coefficient is then used to find the number and location of large-scale material sorting sites. The siting method for drop-off points provides practical implications for the solution of material or personnel deployment problems during various natural disasters.

articleTitle: Safe Deep Learning-Based Offset-Free MPC for Green Hydrogen Injected PEMFC Systems
abstract: Safe and stable operation of a proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) system requires stringent control of oxygen excess ratio (OER). However, the OER regulation in PEMFC is challenging due to frequent fluctuations of current, various modeling nonlinearities, constrained manipulated variable, and real-time requirements. Offset-free model predictive control (MPC) provides a useful means for controlling systems with disturbances and constraints, but suffers from the heavy computational burden of repeatedly solving an optimization problem in real time. Such computational issue precludes the possibility of meeting the real-time requirements of PEMFC. In this paper, a PEMFC cathode gas supply model is firstly established. Next, we develop a safe deep learning-based offset-free MPC algorithm. Based on the nominal offset-free MPC, the proposed MPC not only reserves the ability of disturbance rejection, but also leverages deep neural networks for approximating the explicit solution to the MPC problem to greatly reduce online computational time. Furthermore, a gauge map is used to guarantee the satisfaction of safe constraints regarding compressor voltage. The simulation results show that the proposed MPC is an order of magnitude faster than the nominal offset-free MPC.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Localization Method of Multiple Infrared Cameras Based on Subpixel
abstract: This paper presents a novel three-dimensional localization method using multiple infrared cameras based on subpixel localization to overcome the low accuracy problem of traditional indoor space localization techniques. In this method, subpixel localization algorithms with the Harris operator are employed during camera calibration and localization experiments to replace traditional pixel localization algorithms in the two-dimensional image positioning stage. The Bundle Adjustment method is used to optimize the camera extrinsic parameters, while the collinearity equation and the least square method are applied to solve the spatial point coordinates. The feasibility of the proposed method is verified through experimental methods. The results show that the three-dimensional positioning system achieves millimeter-scale accuracy, surpassing that of pixel-level positioning algorithms.

articleTitle: Intelligent Decision-Making in Wargaming Environment: A Streamlined Coding Framework for Wargames
abstract: In recent years, the wargaming environment has attracted much attention from researchers in the field of intelligent decision technology. Its appeal stems mainly from challenging features such as imperfect information, asymmetric environments, and long-term decision-making in wargames. In this article, we devise a coding framework for a small-scale wargame and develop an intelligent inference system based on the proposed framework. Meanwhile, we conduct intelligent deduction experiments using this system and thoroughly analyze the results. Based on our findings, we reflected on the direction of research of intelligent decision-making technology in wargaming environments.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Decision Method for Microwave Photonic Radar Intermodulation in Intelligent Perception
abstract: In recent years, the rapid development and the advanced technology of China's high-speed railways have attracted worldwide attention. With the increasing scale of the construction of high-speed railways, the characteristics of significant climate differences and complex terrain along the high-speed railways become more prominent, and emergencies such as slope deformation, rockfall from cutting slopes, and perimeter intrusion occur more frequently. Therefore, the real-time monitoring of environmental changes surrounding high-speed railways is significant in achieving independent and efficient train operation control. However, existing train environmental detection methods are challenging to combine the advantages of high penetration, large range, and high-precision imaging, leaving risks and hidden dangers for train operation safety. This paper uses the three-way decision based on intuitionistic fuzzy reasoning as the adaptive decision-making method for microwave photonic radar intermodulation in intelligent perception. The method schedules train radar detection range, power, and band resources in complex weather and terrain reasonably. Besides, a correction function for radar detection power is proposed for complex scenarios to meet the imaging needs of railways.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Optimization Control of Industrial Label Printer Process Parameters
abstract: For industrial label printers, it is difficult to describe the dynamic characteristics between the long-term printing quality and the output of the control loop with a mathematical model, and the printing quality is easily affected by the lack of details of the ribbon or thermal label, which is difficult to detect online; through research data Based on the optimization idea of driving operation mode, a method of data-driven industrial label printer process parameter optimization control is proposed; this method establishes the model between the input parameters of the print head and the output print quality and print head temperature prediction by the method of neural network, and predicts Set the input parameters to obtain the expected print quality and print head temperature through the model, and then optimize the print quality and reduce the temperature rise as the goal to feedback and optimize the input parameters, iteratively obtain the best input that is as close to the optimal target as possible under the current print head temperature parameter. Through practical application, this method can indeed reduce the temperature rise of the print head, and on the premise of ensuring the printing quality, optimize the input parameters so that the temperature of the print head rises slowly, ensuring that the printing can last for a longer time.

articleTitle: Cooperative Differential Game-based Optimal Tracking Control of Modular Reconfigurable Robot with Actor-Critic-Identifier Structure
abstract: Based on the cooperative differential game, this paper proposes an optimal control for modular reconfigurable robot (MRR) systems. Describe the dynamical model of MRR in the form of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> joint subsystems, including interconnected dynamic coupling (IDC). Considering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> joint subsystems as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> players in a cooperative game, uncertainties such as IDC and unknown disturbances contained in the dynamic model are approximated by neural network (NN) identifier. An n-player cooperative game theory can be utilized to convert the tracking control issue of MRR into an optimal control task. Solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations for optimal control by adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) using actor-critic-identifier (ACI) structure. It is proved that the MRR system tracking error is uniformly ultimately bounded (UUB) by the Lyapunov theory. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: The Cyclic Dynamic Task Allocation Algorithm for Multi-UAV Air Combat
abstract: The aim of this paper is to allocate the tasks when the number of the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) changed in air combat. During the process of task allocation, how to minimize the consumption of UAVs needs to be considered. In order to solve this problem, a cyclic dynamic task allocation algorithm for multi-UAV is proposed. Firstly, the multi-UAV task allocation model is modeled. Secondly, the method of calculating the preference value is proposed. The preference list is calculated according to the preference value. Thirdly, the existing enemy UAVs in the battlefield are assigned as tasks to own UAVs based on the cyclic algorithm. Additionally, reassign the tasks when the number of the enemy UAVs changed. By conducting theoretical proofs and simulation experiments, this paper demonstrates that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce flight time and flight cost.

articleTitle: Design of Unmanned System Integrated Navigation Algorithm Simulation Demonstration System
abstract: In order to address the issues of poor demonstration effects and difficulties in analyzing algorithms effectiveness in real-time during the research process of navigation algorithms for unmanned systems, and to facilitate the design of navigation algorithms and improve the professionalism of their demonstrations, this paper proposes a method for designing an unmanned system integrated navigation simulation demonstration system. Firstly, the carrier motion simulation scene is designed based on the Gazebo simulation platform to generate the necessary navigation parameters in real-time. Secondly, a visual display interface is designed based on ROS and Qt, which displays the carrier's navigation parameters, motion trajectories, and other information in real-time by publishing and subscribing to related topics. In addition, the system has extensible functionality to support secondary development according to user needs. The system has been validated to have good demonstration effects and is helpful for the research and demonstration of navigation algorithms for unmanned systems.

articleTitle: Gesture Recognition Based on Millimeter-wave Radar with Multi-Parameter Fusion Network
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low information quantity of signal dimensional and low generalization ability in existing frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) millimeter radar-based dynamic hand gesture recognition methods, a three-dimension parameter dataset convolution neural network is proposed. First, radar signal was collected based on the application condition. Then, a data set for gesture recognition classification is constructed by performing time-frequency. Finally, a lightweight multi-branch CNN is proposed to feature extraction and fusion. The experiment results that the method can effectively detect and recognize 6 types hand gestures, and the recognition accuracy is 97.16%.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning Based On Continuous Decision Deep Reinforcement Learning for Stratospheric Airship
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of stratospheric airships which are greatly influenced by continuous wind fields, this paper proposes a trajectory planning method based on continuous deep reinforcement learning. Firstly, the state space, action space and reward function are designed. After that, the twin delay deep determined policy gradient algorithm based on time series is used the trajectory planning. The algorithm can be used to output actions under continuous space. The experimental results show that the algorithm is stable and efficient, and the feasibility and generalizability of the algorithm are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Structural Design of Clamping-Type Truss-Climbing Robot
abstract: A novel clamping-type climbing robot is proposed with the aim of achieving efficient climbing capabilities through biomimetic design and structural optimization. The primary application scenario involves truss structures, where the robot replaces manual climbing for tasks such as exploration, maintenance, and inspection of trusses. Inspired by the locomotion of the inchworm, the design introduces a clamping mechanism that emulates the inchworm's undulating motion and applies it to truss climbing tasks. The innovative clamping mechanism features V-shaped grippers equipped with a dual-layer cushioning structure to enhance friction and distribute forces. The robot's main body achieves multidimensional complex motions through five rotatable joints, resulting in significantly improved obstacle-surmounting abilities. Genetic algorithms are employed to optimize link lengths, yielding enhanced obstacle-surmounting performance within limited volume and force constraints. Finite element analysis and physical testing confirm the effectiveness of the optimization results and the rationality of the robot's structure.

articleTitle: TSC-BEV: Temporal-Spatial Feature Consistency 3D Object Detection
abstract: Multi-View 3D object detection plays an important role in autonomous driving. Many methods have designed temporal fusion modules to integrate BEV (Bird's Eye View) features from different time steps. However, they seldom consider how to guide the parameter updates in the temporal fusion module to achieve better performance. In this paper, we propose two kinds of loss named Temporal Feature Consistency Loss and Spatial Feature Consistency Loss. The Temporal Feature Consistency Loss emphasizes the relationship between features from the same obstacle at different time steps. It aims to ensure consistency in the representation of an obstacle across consecutive frames. On the other hand, Spatial Feature Consistency Loss focuses on the relationship among all obstacles of the same category. It enables the model to learn a shared common feature representation for obstacles belonging to the same category. Our method is evaluated on the nuScenes 3D object detection benchmark, achieving a performance of 52.1% NDS, with average translation error outperforming baseline by 2 points.

articleTitle: Super Resolution Reconstruction of MiniLED Based on Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: With the development of industrial detection technology, image super-resolution reconstruction is used as an effective data enhancement technique to provide the possibility of higher detection accuracy. This paper focuses on the image super-resolution in industrial detection scenarios, with the following two main contributions: 1) Constructing our own dataset in industrial detection specific scenarios. 2) Proposing EASRGAN, an image super-resolution reconstruction network, to effectively increase the accuracy of subsequent detection. Experimental results show that EASRGAN achieves excellent image super-resolution reconstruction, and the reconstructed image can increase the accuracy of the classification network by 2.83%.

articleTitle: Encrypted Traffic Classification Method Based on GSK and BiLSTM
abstract: As the global Internet moves towards full encryption, the significance of encrypted traffic classification is to provide an effective method to detect and monitor encrypted traffic in the network to detect and respond to potential security threats promptly. In addition, encrypted traffic classification can be used in areas such as network performance optimization, traffic management, and quality of service assurance. In this paper, we utilize the superior optimization-seeking capability of the GSK algorithm (human knowledge sharing algorithm) to optimize the initial learning rate, the maximum number of iterations, and the number of hidden layers of BiLSTM, and introduce an attention mechanism to assist in the classification of encrypted traffic. The model is classified using the Tor2016 dataset, and the experimental results show that the model classification accuracy reaches over 94%, showing high accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Event - Triggered Multirobot Cooperative Localization Based on Unscented Kalman Filter
abstract: This paper studies the multirobot cooperative localization problem under resource-constrained scenarios, such as the limited communication bandwidth and battery capacity. Multirobot cooperative localization heavily relies on inter-robot communication, and it is challenging to ensure high localization accuracy when the communication bandwidth is constrained. To deal with this issue, a new distributed event-triggered unscented Kalman filter cooperative localization (ETUKF CL) approach is proposed in this paper, where an event-triggered mechanism is introduced to reduce the communication and energy cost. The proposed algorithm significantly reduces communication resource consumption while maintaining high positioning accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed cooperative localization algorithm.

articleTitle: An Improved Method for the Foreign Object on the Power Line Detection Based on Sample Simulation
abstract: In the transmission line intelligent inspection object detection, the imbalance of defect categories results low detection rates for the few data categories in deep learning algorithm, such as the foreign objects on the power line, which causes short circuits and fires in the transmission line potentially. In this paper, a sample simulation method based on the 3D modeling and the generative adversarial network is proposed to generate foreign objects simulated samples. Compared with the result with the only ground truth samples as training dataset, the detection rate of the foreign objects category with the addition of the simulated samples in the training dataset increased from 74.70% to 81.22% based on the YoloV5 object detection model. The experiment results indicate that the samples simulation method benefits the power line defect detection in the intelligent inspection.

articleTitle: An Improved Hybrid Grey Wolf Optimizer for Multi-Agent Trajectory Planning in Complex Environment
abstract: This paper considers the problem that Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) has some defects in solving trajectory optimization problems. To solve this problem, this paper proposes the improved GWO algorithm based on GWO by the idea of linear differential decrement and dynamic exponential weighted average. Compared with other algorithms, this algorithm has more flexibility in position updating and finds the global optimal solution effectively. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the improved GWO algorithm in terms of search accuracy and running time.

articleTitle: Adaptive Backstepping Sliding Mode Control for Underwater Glider Trajectory Tracking Based on Nonlinear Disturbance Observer
abstract: An adaptive backstepping dynamic surface sliding mode controller based on nonlinear disturbance observer (NDOABSMC) is designed to track zigzag motion of underwater glider (UG). Firstly, a nonlinear disturbance observer is devised to observe ocean current. Then, the backstepping sliding mode control is used to devise motion attitude controller of UG to ensure that UG can track the target trajectory quickly. Additionally, the stability of UG's control system is analyzed. In the end, the proposed control strategy is compared with other approaches.

articleTitle: Initial Approach Segment Control for Out-of-Plane Capture Based on a Space Tether System
abstract: Study of the release of a tether from a base station spacecraft to a given rendezvous maneuver feasibility point for the out-of-plane capture of space debris by a space tether system. Considering the out-of-plane angle of the system, the pseudospectral method is used to plan the optimal trajectory of the initial approach section, and the effect of the initial state error on the initial approach segment trajectory is analyzed. In turn, the system model is controlled by segmental feedback using sliding mode control based on an adaptive convergence law to overcome the initial state error. The results show that initial approach section control can be achieved by adjusting the tether tension and the out-of-plane thrust on the capture mechanism, provided that the relevant constraints are met.

articleTitle: A Traffic Simulation Algorithm for Time-Trigger Flows in Asynchronous Time-Sensitive Networking
abstract: Asynchronous Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) is an efficient solution to confront exponentially growing data services because it can provide low latency network service without time synchronization in network nodes. However, the upper bound of the clock deviation is unknown and the actual operating status can not be obtained because each network device does not execute time synchronization in the asynchronous TSN. To this end, a traffic simulation algorithm for time-triggered flows in asynchronous time-sensitive networks is proposed. Firstly, the concept of the reference clock is introduced based on the difficulty analysis of the asynchronous TSN system. Secondly, the essence of simulation in an asynchronous TSN system is analyzed. And it is concluded that the simulation algorithm is a necessary and effective way to obtain the actual operating status. Then a traffic simulation algorithm based on the reference clock is proposed. The algorithm is implemented via two different test cases, where the scales of the cases are randomly generated. The test results show that the simulation algorithm proposed in this paper can analyze the specific operating conditions of the asynchronous TSN system. Consequently, it can be used to compare the quality of different arrangement results and can provide guidance for the arrangement of asynchronous TSN traffic.

articleTitle: Sequential Convex Programming for Reentry Trajectory with Piecewise Constant Bank Angle Profile Constraint
abstract: In this study, we present a sequential convex programming method for the reentry trajectory optimization problem with a piecewise constant bank angle profile constraint. Firstly, we design a piecewise constant bank angle profile that includes two free-time nodes to reserve maneuverability. Then, to handle the nondifferentiability of the profile at the piecewise points, the reentry problem is reformulated in a multiphase form so that the profile is differentiable in each phase. Finally, we convert the nonlinear multiphase problem into a sequence of convex subproblems by successive convexification. By iteratively solving these subproblems, a feasible solution to the original problem can be obtained. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in short, medium, and long downrange reentry scenarios.

articleTitle: Multiagent Pursuit-Evasion Game Control Based on Inter-Satellite Communication Link Attacked
abstract: In this paper, the resilient control strategy design of multi-agent pursuit-evasion game problem for a class of discrete-time linear time-invariant systems is studied. The communication link between the studied multi-pursuer systems is vulnerable to network attacks. This paper considers that the multi-pursuer inter-satellite link is attacked by false data injection. In the context of non-cooperative game, the control strategy of the pursuers is designed to tolerate false data injection attacks. First, an upper bound is derived from the cost function of each pursuer. Then, the upper bound is unilaterally minimized by iteratively solving a convex optimization problem, and then the resilient control strategy of each pursuer is obtained according to some coupled backward Riccati-like recursive solutions. And the evader is not affected by the cyber attack, so its control strategy can be obtained by minimizing its own cost function. Finally, a numerical example is given to verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A Novel Distributed Reinforcement Learning Training System for Network Congestion Control
abstract: Network communication is the foundation of various industries and the Internet. As the core of network communication, congestion control (CC) algorithms directly impact network quality. Traditional CC algorithms, such as CUBIC and BBR, are designed by experts. With the advancement of deep reinforcement learning (RL) technology, many researchers have designed reinforcement learning algorithms to achieve self-learning models. However, existing RL models are limited to generating training samples on a single machine, which restricts the training efficiency of the. Additionally, during the model training process, the lack of online analysis tools makes it difficult to analyze the training failures of the model. In this paper, we propose an RL-distributed training system for CC, which utilizes multiple machines to generate training samples. Furthermore, we have designed an online analysis kit to observe the model's control performance in real-time. In experiments, we successfully replicated Indigo using the distributed training system. The experimental results show the effectiveness of the system and the online analysis kit.

articleTitle: Robust Stability Analysis of a LCC-HVDC System Connected with Wind Farms
abstract: The small-signal stability of a line-commutated converter based high voltage direct current (LCC-HVDC) system connected with wind farms (WFs) is a challenging issue in modern power systems. Most of researches focus on the absolute stability based on different stability criteria, and it has not pay much attention yet to quantify the relative stability. This paper proposes a new stability index based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\nu$</tex>-gap metric, i.e. the robust stability margin, to quantify the relative stability of a LCC-HVDC system connected with WFs. We build a suitable multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) model of a LCC-HVDC system connected with WFs represented by transfer function matrix first. Then, the robust stability margin of the system is calculated based on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\nu$</tex>-gap metric. Moreover, according to the corresponding stability criterion, we present a method to easily calculate the stable region of control parameters in LCC-HVDC and WFs. Case studies based on the nonlinear model are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: False Data Injection Attacks Detection in Power Grid Based on Deep Learning Multi-Model Fusion
abstract: Aiming at FDIA in smart grid, this paper proposes a FDIA detection method for power grid set up on deep learning multi-model fusion. Firstly, two different Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) were used to form a double-branch structure to extract and learn the global and local spatial features of normal data and unnormal data in the smart grid respectively. Then, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network was used to extract and learn temporal features. Then, Multi-layer Perceptron (MLP) was used to further compress and extract features. Finally, the output of Softmax layer was used to determine whether there was unnormal data injection in the smart grid. The detection model was trained, verified and tested by IEEE14 and IEEE118 bus systems. The experimental shows that the proposed method can accurately detect false data in smart grid, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Generating Prompt-Based Adversarial Text Examples via Variable Neighborhood Search
abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) models are immensely vulnerable to adversarial text examples. Various word-level attacks have been proposed to modify input texts by carefully-picked substitute words via static or dynamic opti-mization algorithms. However, existing word-level attack methods usually ignore text fluency and semantic consistency for seeking a high attack success ratio, often resulting in unnatural adversarial text examples. In this paper, we propose to generate Prompt-based adversarial texts via Variable Neighborhood Search (P-VNS), which achieves a high attack success ratio while simulta-neously keeping text fluency and semantic similarity. Specifically, the well-designed prompt texts are constructed for input texts and the substitute words are obtained by mask-and-filling procedure under the effect of prompt texts, so the text fluency and semantic similarity can be enhanced. Additionally, the word modification priority is adaptively determined by employing the variable neighborhood search algorithm, yielding an improvement in the attack success ratio. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the P- VNS accomplishes the highest attack success ratio meanwhile preserving text fluency and semantic similarity. Besides, the pro-posed P- VNS also manifests effectiveness in adversarial training and transfer attack.

articleTitle: Local Adaptive Clustering Based Image Matching for Automatic Visual Identification
abstract: In industrial production, monitoring cameras are widely used to pay attention to the running status of equipments. With the development of computer vision, it is possible to use image features to recognize devices. In this paper, a vision-aided identification system is designed to realize real-time automatic labeling of equipments by image matching in surveillance videos. The ORB algorithm is used to extract the image features, and the GMS algorithm is used to eliminate the wrong matching points. Then, according to the clustering locality and template locality, a Local Adaptive Clustering (LAC) method is proposed to optimize the position of labels. Matching templates are segmented with the center of clusters, which improves the efficiency and stability of labels. Experimental results show that LAC significantly suppresses the drift of labels.

articleTitle: Attitude Tracking Control of Liquid- Filled Spacecraft Based on Internal Model
abstract: This paper studies the attitude tracking problem of liquid-filled spacecraft with time-varying inertial matrix and unmodeled input disturbances. First we establish the attitude error system of liquid-filled sapceraft based on quaternions. Aiming at the dynamic characters of the system, a linear time-varying internal model is designed. After we attach the internal model to the original system and get the augmented system, a dynamic high-gain controller is designed to ensure the input-to-state stability (ISS) property of the closed-loop system. Simulation verifies the robustness and accuracy of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: A Mask Anomaly Detection Method for Printed Circuit Board Defects
abstract: Defect inspection of printed circuit boards (PCBs) is a crucial task in the electronics manufacturing industry, as PCBs contain many components and complex characters. Most of the existing research on this topic relies on the PCB Defect dataset, which only covers six types of defects. However, the defects that occur in industrial production are diverse and variable. It is very challenging to accurately classify all possible defects and obtain a large number of defect training samples. To overcome these difficulties, we propose a novel PCB anomaly detection model called the mask anomaly detection method for printed circuit board defects (MADM-PCB), which is based on the principle of reconstruction error. This model can detect unlimited types of defects on PCBs and only requires positive samples for training, which are more abundant in industry. Moreover, to enhance the detection performance, we introduce Spatial-Shift-MLP (S2-MLP), which can strengthen the connection of adjacent semantics on the channel at low cost. We conduct experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Fish Feeding Control System Based on Visual Monitoring of Foraging Quantity in Fish Schools
abstract: Due to individual variations in foraging abilities, there is an uneven distribution of feed consumption among individuals within a fish school. To address this issue, a visual monitoring system is introduced to assess the foraging quantity of individual goldfish, and a precise feeding system is developed based on the differences in foraging quantity among different areas of the fish school. First, the foraging quantity of each individual in the fish school is determined by analyzing the fish school images collected during the feeding process. Then, the feeding amount for each area is determined based on the foraging quantity of individuals in that specific area. Finally, a PLC-controlled feeding system is employed to achieve precise feeding in different areas. Experimental results from a physical simulation system demonstrate that the developed system enables precise feed distribution based on the differences in individual foraging quantity within the fish school. This system will contribute to improving foraging efficiency in fish schools, thus providing a technological foundation for enhanced feed utilization and scientific aquaculture practices.

articleTitle: Mechanical and Electrical Parameter Estimation for PMSMs Considering Sensor Measurement Offset
abstract: Given the problem of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) driving, a multi-parameter estimation method for PMSM considering the influence of torque bias is proposed to improve the accuracy of motor torque estimation. Torque deviation is a factor that cannot be ignored in parameter estimation, which directly leads to the accuracy of electrical parameter estimation. To improve the accuracy of parameter estimation, this paper combines the dq-axis voltage equation, mechanical motion equation and electromagnetic torque equation to establish a decoupling estimation model considering the nonlinearity of the inverter, which effectively reduces the coupling effect between parameters and improves the calculation efficiency and the accuracy of parameters. It also processes a large number of redundant data to achieve accurate and efficient parameter estimation, especially suitable for machine testing applications.

articleTitle: ACR-ILPU: Internal Learning 3D Point Cloud Upsampling Network Using Attention Coordinate Refinement
abstract: The performance of conventional externally trained networks for point cloud upsampling is often influenced by the semantic range size of the training dataset, leading to limited capability in learning shapes at all levels. Consequently, the upsampling of complex shapes fails to preserve their original characteristics and generates an excessive number of dense point cloud outliers. To address these issues, we propose an internally learned method for point cloud upsampling, termed Internal learning 3D Point Cloud Upsampling Network using Attention Coordinate Refinement (ACR-ILPU). ACR-ILPU comprises three modules: an edge-aware generator, a discriminator, and attention-based coordinate refiners, which collectively facilitate the training and testing processes of the network. Notably, our approach eliminates the need for an external training dataset and solely relies on an input sparse point cloud for internal learning. To evaluate the effectiveness of ACR-ILPU, we conduct comprehensive qualitative and quantitative experiments using the PU1K dataset. The results demonstrate that ACR-ILPU significantly reduces training time while surpassing the performance of both externally trained and internally learned methods. Furthermore, ACR-ILPU exhibits promising results when applied to point clouds from the extensive KITTI autonomous driving dataset.

articleTitle: Hybrid Path Planning Based on Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm and Dynamic Window Approach
abstract: To address the drawbacks of the sparrow search algorithm (SSA), including poor initial solution quality, slow convergence, and drop into the local optimal condition easily, this work proposed an upgraded SSA to handle the hybrid path planning issue. First of all, the Tent chaotic mapping approach is employed to increase its diversity. Subsequently, the producers' locations are adjusted with the adaptive weight strategy, which balances for exploration and exploitation. At last, the locations of the scroungers are revised via the differential evolution algorithm (DE), which can enhance the algorithm's capacity to break out the local ideal situation. Furthermore, the upgraded SSA (TADSSA) is coupled with the dynamic window approach (DWA) to avoid obstructions and smooth the route. The proposed method is known as TADSSA-DWA. The proposed TADSSA-DWA and other state-of-the-art techniques are tried to the mobile robot's hybrid path planning independently in order to confirm its effectiveness. While compared to other classical algorithms, the experimental findings demonstrated that the proposed TADSSA-DWA increased the path smoothness by 69.05% and reduced the path length and turns by around 14.12% and 71.42%, respectively. Not noly can the proposed TADSSA-DWA shortens the length of the planned route, but also has capabilities of path smoothing and real-time obstacle avoidance.

articleTitle: Combinatorial Double Auction on Cloud Platform Considering User Budget and Logistics Cost
abstract: This paper primarily investigates the resource allocation problem in cloud manufacturing. Unlike other research institutes, the resources considered in this research are entity manufacturing resources, which possess a regional nature. In order to approach real-world scenarios, this study takes into account the budget constraints of buyers and examines the manufacturing combinations of buyers under these constraints. The paper models the allocation process of physical resources in cloud manufacturing through a bilateral combinatorial auction and establishes a combinatorial double auction mechanism that takes into consideration both budget constraints and logistics costs. Experimental results confirm that the matching success rate of the proposed scheme remains stable at over 60%, demonstrating its feasibility. Moreover, with the increase of cloud platform users, the stability and transaction rate of the mechanism also exhibit a corresponding increase.

articleTitle: Control System Based on STM32 2D Palletising Platform Driving Multiple Motors
abstract: The development of palletizing platforms has received widespread attention as the global logistics market is expanding and the improvement of logistics efficiency has become a common goal of governments and enterprises. More technologies have been improved based from low-bed type palletizing platforms to omnidirectional wheel palletizing platforms or logistics sorting devices. In the omnidirectional wheel part, the DC brush motor is more often used for driving, but at present, the STM32F103 microcontroller only provides a 4-channel timer with encoder mode in hardware. Therefore, in terms of hardware, only 4-channel motors with an encoder are provided, so the motor control system of the palletizing platform with omnidirectional wheels puts forward greater requirements, both to meet the control effect of more motor closed-loop, to improve the accuracy, and also to reduce the cost. Based on this, a hardware platform using multiple analogue switches, which can input 9 encoder data as well as output 18 PWM waveforms, and adopts incremental PID for closed-loop control is investigated based on the STM32F103 microcontroller.
