Compared with the simple experimental protocol (only positive point prompt mode involved) in the original SAM paper, we test its performance sufficiently on two X-ray prohibited datasets with a total of 37524 images, including 58304 instances in 16 categories, when categories, occlusion conditions, prompt modes and checkpoints vary. Moreover, we compared SAM's performance with other SOTA detection models and segmentation models. Our empirical study shows that though SAM has certain segmentation ability on X-ray images especially with prompts, the performance on irregular instances and complex overlapping conditions still wait to be improved due to the overlapping characteristics.

articleTitle: Shrimp Detection Method Based on Dense Unbiased Teacher
abstract: With the development of computer vision, agricultural technology is also moving towards intelligence. Deep learning-based object detection algorithms have gained widespread adoption in the shrimp farming industry, providing superior accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional machine learning algorithms. However, a large amount of labeled data are required in previous detector training procedures. In some intensive scenarios, labeling a single image can even take a few minutes, while model training requires hundreds or thousands of labeled data to obtain good performance. Therefore, we propose the Dense Unbiased Teacher (DUT) algorithm for shrimp detection in this work, an semi-supervised object detection (SS-OD) pipeline based on dense pseudo-labels, which can learn rich semantic information from unlabeled data more efficiently. Compared to the original Unbiased Teacher (UT) algorithm, our method can more efficiently utilize the supervision of the teacher model. We utilized the high-definition camera to capture shrimp image data and used this dataset to establish a Shrimp-SSOD benchmark for evaluating the performance of our model. The experimental results show that our method outperforms the original UT in all Shrimp-SSOD settings. Specifically, DUT achieves 2.21 mAP improvements compared to UT and 9.21 mAP improvements compared to the supervised baseline when using 50% of labeled data. It is worth noting that our method achieves comparable performance to fully supervised learning despite using only 50% labeled data, which means we can save half of the labeling time.

articleTitle: Vehicle Dimensional Measurement with RGB-D Camera
abstract: Vehicle dimensional measurement is crucial for road over-limit detection. As existing methods can not balance price, accuracy, and time complexity, we propose a low-cost, accurate, and real-time method for measuring vehicle dimensions using an RGB-D camera priced at 499 dollars. The proposed method builds the ground background model from a series of video frames and uses ground point cloud and lane information to self-calibrate the camera's extrinsic parameters. Subsequently, using the self-calibrated results, the vehicle point cloud in the current frame is transformed into the measurement coordinate system to facilitate accurate measurement. Finally, we measure the dimensions of the entire vehicle by combining the vehicle displacement, local width, and local height across multiple frames. By evaluating three different types of vehicles, the results show that the average error is less than 3.3% for length and less than 2% for width and height, indicating high accuracy. Furthermore, our method achieves real-time performance with each frame processed in less than 30 milliseconds.

articleTitle: VTAHMER: Vision-Text Alignment Based Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition
abstract: Handwritten mathematical expression recognition(HMER) has attracted considerable attention in pattern recognition community. However, it remains challenging due to distinct personal styles and qualities in real application. To this end, we propose an encoder-decoder method, namely VTAHMER, using scale attention and cross-modal learning in this paper. This method improves the efficiency and effectiveness of multi-scale mathematical expression symbol recognition by using an adaptive convolutional kernel weighting approach. In addition, the invariant features from both handwritten expression images and their corresponding labels represented by LaTeX form are learned respectively. Specifically, the image encoder with different kernel sizes merge attention information to accommodate varying receptive fields. We also design a text encoder for LaTeX formulas, contrastively learning them along with the image encoder. This cultivates the latent semantic information between vision and text domains, which is benefit to downstream recognition. Experimental results show our model achieves better recognition rates with 61.4%, 61.8% and 64.8% on CROHME 2014/2016/2019 datasets, respectively.

articleTitle: A Study on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm in Portfolio Optimization Problem
abstract: The PSO algorithm suffers from a singular population and a propensity to settle on a local optimal solution. We propose CPSO algorithm to enhance the diversity of the particle population and prevent local optima. The algorithm modifies the initialization process to ensure higher diversity and ergodicity of particles within the pre-stage. It employs non-linearly varying inertia weights and acceleration coefficients and introduces the Cauchy variational operator to increase population diversity and prevent particles from becoming trapped in local optima. According to the experimental findings, it shows that the CPSO algorithm has improved precision in terms of convergence and a faster rate of convergence for optimization problems of high complexity. It can achieve higher Sharpe ratios in the portfolio optimization problems.

articleTitle: An Automatic Code Generation Method Based on Directed Graph with Labels
abstract: Space TT&C system is in charge of the measurement and control of spacecraft and other TT&C objects. Due to the access of new target, the program of data processing needs to be developed incrementally. The TDRS software system is a Space TT&C system developed incrementally, which means that the basic functions are completed in the initial development and the software maintains continuous development to cope with the new target access. In this process, most of the software functions can be implemented by parameter configuration. However, the data processing function needs the software redevelopment. This paper presents an automatic code generation method based on directed graph with labels. This method guides the programmer to focus on the business logic modeling and generate the data processing code automatically. An example shows that this method can be applied in the TDRS system data processing and improve the software development efficiency and software quality remarkably.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous UAV Tracking Cooperative Control with Distributed Adaptive Consensus
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed adaptive heterogeneous UAV cluster cooperative control system, which designs the unmanned system as a multi-level architecture. A consensus control algorithm for linear systems and a control model for nonlinear systems are combined. Considering the cluster formation control protocol of both quadrotor and fixed-wing aircraft dynamics models, a nonlinear model predictive control and an adaptive LQR flight controller are presented. A consistent control trajectory generation algorithm considering the dynamic constraints of heterogeneous UAVs is proposed, and the conditions for the cooperative control layer to achieve consistent control are given. Finally, combined with model predictive control and linear quadratic regulatory control, the proposed heterogeneous UAV cluster control system is simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Research on Wind-Disturbance Suppression Control for Large Radio Telescope Servo System
abstract: Wind loads acting on a radio telescope antenna structure reduce the antenna's pointing accuracy and have become a serious problem with the high-accuracy pointing of a large aperture antenna. Research on compensation for wind-disturbance effect on the servo system to improve beam-pointing accuracy is very important. This paper analyzes the effect mechanism of wind disturbance on the antenna servo system and establishes a 4DOF model from the input current signal of the motor and wind-induced torque to angular displacements for the antenna azimuthal system. Then two double-loop active disturbance-suppression controllers based on disturbance observer-based control (DOBC) and active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) are designed, respectively. The validity and superiority of the proposed design scheme are verified on a 100m class antenna model. Compared with a PI controller designed by quantitative feedback theory (QFT), both active disturbance suppression schemes can obtain better dynamic response performance and rejection of external wind disturbances. In particular, compared with the robust PI controller, our simulations revealed that the maximum and RMS disturbance responses of the ADRC are reduced by half, and the response time is shortened by 20 seconds.

articleTitle: Research on Abnormal Lung Sound Recognition and Diagnosis Based on Improved CNN and Transfomer
abstract: Lung auscultation is one of the effective means to diagnose lung diseases. This study aims at the lung sounds of patients, and studies the diagnosis and recognition method of abnormal lung sounds in patients with lung diseases by combining convolutional neural network CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) and Transformer. In this study, a realtime lung sound acquisition system was designed, and the lung sound information was uploaded to the PC terminal by using the wireless WIFI module. Under the guidance of professional physicians, the collected lung sounds of patients were labeled to establish a feature data set (normal, light, common, and heavy). Secondly, based on the Butterworth filter Gaussian filter and the nonnegative matrix factorization method, the lung sound denoising was performed and the MFCC feature information of the lung sound was extracted. Finally, the lung sound auxiliary diagnosis model was designed to analyze the characteristics of lung sounds, and the patient's condition was diagnosed and evaluated. This paper proposes an SCBAM-CNN-Transformer classification model. After optimizing CNN by improving the channel attention mechanism CBAM, the improved CNN model is combined with Transformer. It combines the advantages of CNN spatial feature representation and Transformer sequence coding, forming a strong global feature perception and local feature extraction ability. The algorithm proposed in this paper has good robustness and generalization ability, and the recognition accuracy is 94.8 %. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can more effectively identify abnormal lung sounds and determine the infection level than other deep learning models.

articleTitle: Flexible Job-shop Scheduling Method Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: To minimize the makespan of flexible job-shop scheduling problem (F JSP), an end-to-end deep reinforcement learning algorithm (DRL) is proposed. Firstly, the complex constraints and information of F JSP are described by a dynamic heterogeneous graph, through which the process of F JSP can be transformed into a Markov decision process (MDP). Secondly, A two-stage heterogeneous graph neural network (HGNN) is designed to extract workshop state information, and a multilayer perceptron is utilized for end-to-end decision-making. Finally, the model is trained using the proximal policy optimization algorithm (PPO). To evaluate the performance and effectiveness of this algorithm, experiments were conducted on standard test sets and compared with other approximate solution algorithms. The experimental results highlight the superior performance of our algorithm over various priority dispatching rules (PDR) in terms of solution quality. Additionally, our algorithm achieves faster solving speeds compared to Meta-heuristics algorithms.

articleTitle: Analysis of Distributed Photovoltaic Grid Connection Acceptance Capacity Considering Joint Benefits
abstract: In response to the safety and economic impact of large-scale distributed photovoltaic grid connections on the distribution network, this paper proposes a distributed photovoltaic grid connection acceptance capacity model that maximizes the joint benefits of photovoltaic power plants and the distribution network while taking into account the constraints of grid-safe operation. Firstly, a brief description of the influence of distributed photovoltaic access on the distribution network was provided, followed by the presentation of a multi-objective optimization process for photovoltaic access to the distribution network. Then, taking into account electrical deviation, system loss, investment cost, and photovoltaic consumption ratio, a combined target distributed photovoltaic acceptance capability model was developed. Furthermore, the SSA sparrow search method was used to maximize the ideal position and maximum capacity of distributed photovoltaic access. Finally, the model's effectiveness was demonstrated by using distributed photovoltaic integration into the IEEE 33 node distribution network as an example, and the photovoltaic acceptance capacity at maximum joint benefit was obtained.

articleTitle: Identifying Tracking Motion Pattern in Rehabilitation Using Inverse Optimal Control
abstract: Rehabilitation training is essential for hemiplegia recovery and “tracking” is one of the most fundamental re-habilitation tasks. Nevertheless, the tracking motions between the patients are highly personalized. To maximize the treatment potency for each patient, it requires us to understand and model the patient's personalized tracking pattern during the rehabilitation training task. In this paper, we model the behaviour of a patient tracking a given reference signal by a linear quadratic optimal problem, while her control inputs are corrupted by signal-dependent noise. Since the parameters in the objective function stand for the trade-off between tracking error and control effort, they are interpreted as the “personalized” tracking motion pattern and the goal is to identify them based on the observed data. Such a problem is called Inverse Optimal Control (IOC). We first prove that the model structure is identifiable. Then we propose a statistically consistent IOC algorithm that handles multiplicative noise induced by muscle fluctuations. The performance of the objective function estimation is then illustrated by both numerical simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Research on the All-Wheel Steering Control Strategy for Multi-Axle Vehicles Based on Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control
abstract: All-wheel steering is an effective means to improve the high-speed handling stability and low-speed mobility flexibility of multi-axle vehicles, and the control strategy is a major factor affecting the steering characteristics. In view of the numerous nonlinearity (such as system coupling nonlinearity, tire nonlinearity), uncertainties (such as vehicle parameter uncertainty, modeling uncertainty, external disturbance, etc.), as well as the chattering phenomenon of steering system easily caused by traditional sliding mode control, this paper proposes a novel super-twisting sliding mode control strategy for all-wheel steering system of multi-axle vehicles. Firstly, a 11-DOF nonlinear uncertain dynamic model, nonlinear tire model, and random road surface model for the multi-axle vehicle are established. Secondly, an ideal reference model for the multi-axle vehicle is built by simultaneously considering the low-speed and high-speed steering performance. Thirdly, a continuous control law for the multi-axle vehicle is synthesized based on the super-twisting sliding mode control idea and the finite-time separation principle, which can overcome the effects of nonlinearity and uncertainty, suppress jitter phenomenon, and compel the system sates to converge in finite time. Finally, the finite-time stability of all-wheel steering system is systematically proven by using Lyapunov theory and finite time stability theory. The simulation results under three typical working conditions show that, in contrast to front axle steering control, proportional control and discontinuous switching sliding mode control, the designed controller posses faster convergence speed, and can improve the high-speed steering stability and low-speed steering mobility of multi-axle vehicles significantly.

articleTitle: A Single-Channel EEG Signal Based Sleep Staging with Global-Context-Modeling Feature Fusion
abstract: Sleep staging is important for the detection and treatment of sleep disorders. For sleep specialists, manual sleep stage scoring is a time-consuming task, which is also limited by inter-rater reliability. Therefore, it is important to implement automatic sleep staging. However, existing methods still face the challenges of poor feature quality and unbalanced classes. In this paper, we design a single-channel EEG signal based sleep staging method with more integrated feature fusion that employs global context modeling. To improve the feature quality, the proposed model utilizes global context network (GCNet) to implement feature fusion. The module improves feature quality by modeling input features globally through a self-attentive mechanism, which allows the model to capture long-term dependencies between features. The presence of the class imbalance problem makes the model perform poorly in minority classes. Therefore, the proposed model increases the focus of the model on minority classes of samples through gradient harmonizing mechanism (GHM), which improves the overall performance of the model. The proposed model achieves accuracy rates of 84.6% and 81.5% on two public data sets of Sleep-EDF-20 and Sleep-EDF -78, respectively, which is better than the state-of-the-art.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Based Sintering Proportioning: Improved Whale Optimization Method
abstract: Sintering proportion optimization plays a crucial role in determining the final product quality of sintered iron ore. However, the traditional approach of separating the optimization processes between the procurement and technical departments often fails to achieve the global optimum. In this paper, We propose a joint optimization approach for sintering proportioning based on digital twin (DT) technology. To tackle the complex constraints of this joint optimization problem, we develop a multiple improved whale optimization algorithm (MIWOA) that overcomes the issue of getting trapped in local optima. The proposed MIWOA incorporates three strategies, including a nonlinear convergence factor, Levy flight, and Gaussian mutation. Besides, the numerical simulations are conducted in order to analyze the influence of the convergence factors. Finally, various related approaches for sintering proportioning optimization are tested, and DT-based MIWOA achieved the best performance.

articleTitle: NeuTR: A Learnable Neural Data Augmentation Strategy for Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning in Fault Diagnosis with Limited Fault Data
abstract: Data augmentation techniques, such as rotations, masks, and noise, have become critical and effective tools in addressing the scarcity of common datasets in various deep learning tasks. This article proposes a novel learnable neural data augmentation strategy specifically tailored for the task of supervised contrastive representation learning (SCL) in fault diagnosis when faced with limited fault data. The core concept revolves around generating a set of transformations that maintain similar semantic information to the original sample while exhibiting dissimilarity from one another. Our approach encompasses two stages: the generation of augmented data and SCL-based feature extraction. Many experiments conducted on the Tennessee Eastman process (TEP) benchmark dataset reveal that our method outperforms existing data augmentation strategies and fault diagnosis methods, surpassing performance even without the utilization of any prior information.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Semantic Image Translation with Prototype Correction
abstract: Image translation plays a crucial role in computer vision and has extensive applications in various visual fields, including image stylization and image super-resolution generation. Labeling datasets can be challenging and expensive, especially when it comes to semantic labeling. This paper presents a framework for few-shot semantic image translation with prototype correction. It mainly encompasses three modules, namely the StyleGAN module, the semantic similarity regressor module, and the pSp encoder module. First, to prevent overfitting during training by using the pre-trained StyleGAN model as a generator, which can expand the number of training samples and obtain prototype vectors in sparse samples. Secondly, when considering the variations within the sample semantic class, the framework designs a semantic similarity regressor helps to correct the prototype, thereby improving the accuracy of the pseudo-label and enhancing the model optimization. Third, the cyclic synthesis of semantic information is achieved by training the regressor with an unsupervised loss by combining label feature maps, synthetic feature maps, and prototype vectors. The pSp encoder is trained using pseudo-label images to get the style parameters and achieve semantic image translation. Experimental results show that the proposed framework is superior to state-of-the-art methods in terms of excellent generalization performance and the diversity of synthesized images.

articleTitle: Constrained Residual Race: An Efficient Hybrid Controller for Autonomous Racing
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has shown promise in solving the autonomous racing problem without requiring an accurate dynamics model, but random sampling of actions can lead to inefficient exploration. This paper proposes an efficient racing method, Constrained Residual Race (CRR), which combines a geometry-based reactive obstacle avoidance algorithm, Follow-The-Gap Method (FTG), with DRL. CRR generates safe guided actions with FTG and complementary actions with DRL, which are then fused into a final control action through a constraint equation. Using FTG as a prior controller enhances exploration efficiency and produces safe driving actions. Constraining the DRL policy output ensures that it does not overwrite the prior policy during early stages of exploration. Additionally, the DRL policy improves over the performance of the prior controller during training, reducing the lap time of the car. Validation on the F1TENTH simulator shows that CRR achieves lower lap times in most cases and exhibits excellent generalization capability.

articleTitle: Tensor Multi-Task Learning for Multi-View Representation of 3D Shape
abstract: Research on 3D representation has sprung up recently. However, most existing view-based methods lack interpretability and few researchers explore to mine high-order correlation for multi-view features aggregate in 3D shape representation. This paper presents a tensor multi-task model learning, T-MTL, which transforms the original multi-view classification problem into constructing a common space in which the multi-view representation can be compared. The proposed method can construct a tensor structure in the classifier weight subspace with multiple viewpoints and use a tensor low-rank constraint and Bregman discrepancy to capture high-order correlations between multi-view images and 3D models. In the classifier weight subspace, our method makes the inter-class divergence larger and the intra-class divergence smaller. Moreover, the proposed model can improve recognition performance further by unifying multiple visual features in a flexible manner. Abundant experiments on these challenging benchmark datasets show that our method achieves comparable results to the deep learning models approach.

articleTitle: Multi-Time Scale Optimization Scheduling Method for Integrated Energy Systems Based on Model Predictive Control
abstract: Although integrated energy systems with multi-energy coordination characteristics can improve energy efficiency effectively, the source-load uncertainty within the system causes great difficulties in its optimal operation. Previous studies on optimal scheduling methods for integrated energy systems have largely focused on improving the economic efficiency of the system, with less consideration of environmental issues. The core contribution and novelty of this paper is to propose a multi-timescale optimal scheduling method for integrated energy systems based on model predictive control, which takes into account the economy, stability and environmental protection during the optimal operation of the system. Firstly, the day-ahead scheduling incorporates the stepped carbon trading mechanism, with the goal of minimizing the total cost of energy purchase, operation and maintenance, and carbon trading. This approach ensures optimal economic performance while reducing environmental pollution. Then, acknowledging the significant difference in adjustable time between the equipment for heat-cold energy and electricity, introducing the idea of model predictive control, the rolling optimization of heat-cold energy for 1 hour and electricity for 15 minutes is conducted, with the aim of minimizing the change of power between the day-ahead and the intra-day. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by the analysis of the optimal scheduling results in a typical case.

articleTitle: Seismic Response Mitigation of Building via Inerter-Based Tuned Liquid Damper
abstract: This work investigates the use of inerter-based tuned liquid dampers (ITLD) to mitigate building vibrations under seismic excitation. ITLD is derived from tuned liquid dampers (TLD) by installing a mechanical network based on inerter. The building is modeled as a mass-chain system, and an equivalent linear model is applied to obtain the state-space model of the whole system. Subsequently, the performance indices are formulated to optimize both the top-floor displacement and top-floor acceleration of the building. Based on the optimization results, mechanical network layouts are obtained using the network synthesis method. The influence of weights on the H2 norm of the top-floor displacement and top-floor acceleration of the building is analyzed, and the RMS values of top-floor displacement and top-floor acceleration under eight different seismic excitations are provided. The results indicate that the optimal mechanical network can effectively mitigate building vibrations under almost every type of seismic excitation. Considering both the mechanical complexity and the vibration mitigation performance, the second-order mechanical network performs the best. Finally, through simulation verification and theoretical analysis, this paper finds that ITLD has the best effect of mitigating building vibration when it is installed on the top floor.

articleTitle: Effects Investigation of Critical Spiking Neuronal Feature on Dendritic Credit Assignment for Efficient Spike-based Learning
abstract: As a model inspired by biological neural network mechanism, spiking neural network plays an important role in realizing brain-inspired computing with higher cognitive functions. The credit assignment problem is the basis of the internal decision-making process of network learning. Its solution directly determines the learning performance of spiking neural network. This paper focuses on the influence of features of spiking neurons on credit assignment processes with dendritic compartments. We study the calculation and transmission of feed-forward and feedback signals in dendritic credit assignment. The results show that the changes of membrane potential, leakage conductance and dendrite conductance affect the credit assignment process. Credit assignment is closely related to the error calculation of feedforward signals and feedback signals in network learning, which makes its change affect the learning performance. This is due to these features acting on the plateau potential and weight updating. The results also reveal the effects of long time constant, short time constant and maximum neuron firing rate on credit assignment. These features affect learning performance by the response kernel of the error calculation process that acts on credit assignment. The exploration of these critical features in this work is helpful for improving network learning performance. This work can be applied in areas such as smart healthcare, intelligent navigation and edge computing.

articleTitle: Design of Parallel Simulation System for Target Range Ballistic Accuracy Test
abstract: This paper combines the temporal relationship of target range ballistic accuracy testing with the deep interaction characteristics of parallel systems in order to develop a parallel simulation framework and work paradigm for target range ballistic accuracy testing. The principles for optimal ballistic solution based on the actual task requirements and test conditions is designed, and a parallel simulation method based on adaptive optimization of ballistic solution is proposed. The parallel simulation system is applied to the actual flight test of multi-station time-difference ballistic positioning, and the results demonstrate the parallel simulation system's efficacy in testing target range ballistic accuracy.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of Soft Actuator with Rope-Driven Magnetic Variable Stiffness
abstract: Compared with rigid structure actuator, soft actuator has higher degree of freedom, but its load output capacity is insufficient. In order to further improve its load capacity, a fast variable stiffness rope-driven soft actuator based on magnetorheological elastomer is proposed, and the theoretical mathematical model of deformation and stiffness of variable stiffness soft actuator is established. The experimental results show that the designed and developed magnetorheological variable stiffness soft actuator can achieve multi-level variable stiffness under rope-driving and the effect of the magnetic field of the electromotive force, and the maximum stiffness can be improved by about 51%, and the response time of stiffness adjustment is less than 0.5s. The end load experiment of the soft actuator shows that the load capacity of the soft actuator under 40mT magnetic field is 1.51 times that of the soft actuator without magnetic field.

articleTitle: Optimal Policy Replay: A Simple Method to Reduce Catastrophic Forgetting in Target Incremental Visual Navigation
abstract: Visual navigation is a critical task in robotics and artificial intelligence. In recent years, reinforcement learning-based approaches have gained popularity for visual navigation. However, existing methods lack flexibility in learning multiple navigation targets and suffer from catastrophic forgetting. To address these challenges, we propose a novel paradigm called “target incremental visual navigation” and introduce a method called Optimal Policy Replay (OPR). Target incremental visual navigation aims to study the performance of visual navigation in continuous learning of navigation targets. OPR enables continuous learning of navigation targets without the need for relearning all targets. Our method divides the learning process into on-policy and off-policy stages and stores only the optimal experiences in memory. Experimental results show that OPR effectively alleviates catastrophic forgetting and achieves good performance with a small memory size.

articleTitle: Safety Control of Uncertain Nonlinear Systems Based on a Neural Network-Based Control Barrier Function
abstract: The primary focus of this paper is on the safety control problem of uncertain nonlinear systems. Based on the idea of proving the invariance of the superlevel sets of scalar constraint functions with Control Barrier Functions (CBFs), we propose a novel neural network-based control barrier function (NNCBF) control scheme to achieve safety control of uncertain nonlinear systems with state constraints. According to the CBF and neural network (NN) technology, the uncertain system is reconstructed and the relative definitions of NNCBF are presented. Subsequently, by resolving a quadratic program (QP) using the NNCBF condition as a constraint, the nominal controller is adapted to achieve safety control without violating constraints. Finally, an illustrative example is performed to validate the efficacy of the proposed safety control method utilizing NNCBF - QP.

articleTitle: ATNet: Unsupervised Point Cloud Registration Network Integrating Adaptive Graph Convolution and Transformer
abstract: Unsupervised point cloud registration algorithms often suffer from poor registration accuracy when dealing with partially overlapping point clouds due to the lack of effective internal monitoring. Traditional convolution methods, such as dynamic graph convolution, tend to extract partially indistinguishable features, resulting in limited ability to learn features. To address these challenges, inspired by adaptive graph convolution dynamically learning point cloud features based on adaptive kernels for point cloud generation, we propose an unsupervised point cloud registration network called ATNet, integrating adaptive graph convolution and transformer to improve point cloud evaluation by ensuring domain consistency. Firstly, we employ adaptive graph convolution to extract point cloud features, transformer to encode these features to preserve geometric information.Next, we use the graph optimization module to estimate a point-to-point graph by combining neighborhood matching scores. The aggregated neighborhood information is helpful to the generation of pseudo-target point clouds and high-quality correspondences. The point cloud evaluation module takes advantage of significant structural differences between outliers in the source and related pseudo-target clouds, while the structural differences of the interior points are minimal. By leveraging these geometric structural differences, the module scores the confidence of each estimated correspondence. Subsequently, the network uses the correspondences and inner confidence scores to compute the rigid transformation. The experimental results on the 7Scenes and KITTI datasets show that ATNet reduces the mean absolute error by 0.0115 and 0.7344, respectively, compared with RPM-Net.

articleTitle: Global Information Interactive of ViT for Rain Removal on Single Images
abstract: In adverse weather conditions, the quality of outdoor captured images is significantly compromised, primarily due to the presence of rain streaks that severely degrade image clarity and consequently disrupt image recognition and analysis. The spatial variations of rain streaks within individual rainy images pose a considerable challenge for their removal. Despite the notable achievements of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based methods in recent years, their limited receptive fields and lack of adaptability to input content make it difficult for them to cope with real-world scenarios and restore high-quality rain-free images with accurate structural details. To address this issue, we propose an image restoration model based on the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture. Specifically, our model first employs a U - ViT to capture contextual information, which is then fused with a high-resolution branch that preserves local details. At each stage, attention mechanisms are introduced to reweight local features, leading to the design of a novel information interaction pattern. The model achieves accelerated convergence by performing global information interaction during rain removal, resulting in image restoration that closely resembles the reference images. Furthermore, to mitigate the loss of fine grained details, we introduce a detail fusion module. The resulting tightly interconnected hierarchical structure is referred to as GIVTNet. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm yields substantial performance improvements across multiple synthetic and real-world datasets.

articleTitle: Pipeline Inner Surface 3D Reconstruction and Depth Prediction Based on Fast-MVSNet for Intelligent Sewer Robot Vision
abstract: Ensuring the regular operation of drainage pipes has significant implications for the maintenance of regular city order. Currently, the inspections of urban drainage pipes are mostly based on monocular CCTV videos. However, these videos only provide simple 2D images without localization information, which makes it challenging to comprehend the complete internal details of the pipelines. Therefore, this paper investigates 3D reconstruction and depth prediction based on monocular vision, in order to restore the pipeline information in real scenes through the monocular video acquired by the robotic CCTV inspection system, and to provide assistance in locating the disease at a later stage. ORB-SLAM3 is employed to estimate the camera's extrinsic parameters for each of the views to obtain the camera poses and uses the currently more innovative Fast-MVSN et for model training, and this paper uses the model to predict depth maps of the pipeline image. Finally, outliers are filtered through photometric consistency and geometric continuity to suppress noise during the reconstruction process and ensure a certain degree of completeness and accuracy. On the pipeline test dataset, the best model in this framework achieves an absolute relative error of 0.458 in depth prediction, which enables obtaining a denser 3D point cloud scene of the pipeline.

articleTitle: Attention Generative Adversarial Network with Transformer Encoder for Missing Sensor Time Series
abstract: This study focuses on the imputation process of equipment sensor data with missing time-series values. To address this challenge, the main approach is to reconstruct the missing data in the sensor system by developing an attention generative adversarial imputation network learning model called ATGAIN. The model input is formatted by the sliding window method and the introduction of a mask matrix. Next, the Transformer and convolutional neural network architectures are integrated into ATGAIN's generator and discriminator, respectively, with careful design to effectively capture the temporal correlation and feature correlation within the remaining data. Finally, the proposed learning model is evaluated using an aircraft engine C-MAPSS dataset to demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection Algorithm of CAN Bus Data Flow Based on Inception-ResNet Model
abstract: With the rapid development of the industrial internet, the volume of data in industrial networks is increasing, and network attacks are becoming more concealed and complex. Traditional machine learning methods are no longer suitable for the new scenarios of industrial intrusion detection. Therefore, this study addresses the difficulties in feature selection and overfitting when applying traditional machine learning methods to handle industrial bus data. It proposes a Deep Convolutional Neural Network Intrusion Detection (DCNN-IDS) model and verifies it using the natural gas dataset from Mississippi State University. The DCNN-IDS model utilizes the Inception-ResNet model as its underlying structure, optimizes the model size, redesigns the network architecture, and introduces an image generator module to generate two-dimensional CAN data images with sequentially ordered bit identifiers. Experimental results demonstrate that the DCNN-IDS model defeats other machine learning algorithms and exhibits excellent performance in detecting intrusion attacks in industrial networks.

articleTitle: SCAAE: Using Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning in Adversarial AutoEncoder for Anomaly Detection of Multivariate Time Series in Cyber Physics Systems
abstract: The network security protection of Cyber- Physical Systems (CPS), represented by power monitoring systems, is a significant research area. Anomaly detection of multivariate time series generated during CPS operation plays a crucial role in preventing industrial accidents and ensuring system security. However, the field of industrial multivariate time series anomaly detection still faces two main challenges: (1) the lack of more efficient representation methods for multivariate time series data; (2) the difficulty in acquiring a sufficient amount of anomaly data in practical industrial processes. This paper introduces a novel unsupervised anomaly detection method that combines the self-supervised learning mechanism with multivariate time series anomaly detection. The proposed method is named Self-Contrastive learning and Adversarial Autoencoder-based Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection (SCAAE). The autoencoder structure of SCAAE enables it to learn feature representations in an unsupervised manner. Moreover, the introduction of data augmentation techniques and contrastive learning during the training process allows the model to better utilize data characteristics, leading to improved performance even in the presence of data noise.Finally, the effectiveness and characteristics of the proposed method are validated through experimental studies on public datasets.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Observer Based Integral Terminal SMC for Converter-Driven Motor Systems with Mismatched Disturbances
abstract: Converter-driven motor systems play crucial roles in contemporary industrial applications owning to the advantages of smooth starting and stepless speed regulation. For such fourth-order systems with both immeasurable states and mismatched disturbances, a finite-time control solution is proposed to address the speed tracking problem in this paper. Firstly, a finite-time observer is constructed to precisely estimate the immeasurable states and mismatched disturbances. Then, based on integral terminal sliding mode control (ITSMC), a continuous finite-time controller is designed for the systems to achieve both rapid response and superior speed tracking performance. Furthermore, a rigorous global finite-time stability analysis for the closed-loop system is presented. Finally, simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed control method. As compared with existing methods, the composite ITSMC algorithm design demonstrates reliable finite-time speed tracking performance and exceptional capability in disturbance rejection.

articleTitle: Target Neighborhood-Aware Enhanced Small Infrared Target Detection Algorithm*
abstract: The low detection rate of small targets is a common problem in CNN-based general object detection models. In particular, the detection of small targets in infrared imaging is more challenging due to the high false detection rate caused by low contrast in complex backgrounds. Insufficient perception of contextual information around small targets in convolutional operations is the main reason for false detection. To address this issue, this paper proposes a transformer-based method for enhancing neighborhood perception in infrared small target detection. For two-stage object detection methods, this paper first proposes candidate region resampling to collect as much contextual information as possible for the target regions generated by RPN. Then, a transformer encoding structure is utilized to enhance the global perception ability of features for the neighbor-hood. Finally, a classifier is designed to evaluate the differences between potential target regions and their neighborhoods, which is used to determine whether the RPN candidate region contains a real target. With detection accuracy, recall rate, and F1 score as evaluation metrics, the proposed detection framework achieves 92.39%, 97.28%, and 93.63% on the MDvsFA dataset and 95.25%, 98.35%, and 96.13% on the ALCNet dataset. The proposed infrared small target detection algorithm, which enhances neighborhood perception, combines the advantages of traditional algorithms and transformer structures to achieve more accurate results.

articleTitle: Research on Low Power Routing Algorithm for Train Wireless Sensor Network
abstract: As the terminal of the train maintenance network, vehicle sensors are deployed in large quantities on the bogies of high-speed rail vehicles to collect signals such as axle temperature, instability, and vibration for vehicle safety monitoring and maintenance. According to actual use feedback, traditional wired sensors have drawbacks such as difficult wiring installation and limited power supply. If wireless sensors are used to replace wired sensors, challenges such as complex environment, co-channel interference, reliability and security will be faced. To address the aforementioned challenges, this paper proposes a low-power cluster routing algorithm specifically designed for train wireless sensor networks. This algorithm begins by employing an enhanced K-means algorithm to cluster the train wireless sensor network. The ordinary nodes cluster together by selecting the most suitable cluster head based on the cost function. Then, network cluster head election is conducted based on the prediction of node life cycles. Ordinary nodes cluster together by choosing cluster heads based on the cost function, followed by the incorporation of a limited message acknowledgement mechanism in the data transmission stage to enhance the reliability of the network. Finally, the strategy was implemented through simulation software to verify its effectiveness. The results indicate that this method can achieve long-term and reliable operation of sensor systems in complex environments, reduce the number of train signal lines, and improve installation, adjustment, and maintenance efficiency.

articleTitle: Trajectory Optimization of Hypersonic Glide Vehicle Based on Pseudospectral Method Assisted by BP Neural Network
abstract: Pseudospectral method is often used to find the optimal trajectory of hypersonic glide vehicle. Considering the influence of the initial guess value on the calculation speed of the pseudospectral method, this paper presents a trajectory optimization strategy using BP neural network to generate the initial value of pseudospectral collocation points to assist the calculation of pseudospectral method. The dataset is obtained by offline optimization using pseudospectral method under random flight missions. By using specific flight mission generalization methods, the neural network scale is reduced and the convergence speed of the network is improved. A BP neural network model is established with the generalized flight mission as input and the initial guess value of pseudospectral collocation points as output. Numerical simulations in validation set show that, compared with the pseudospectral method based on the traditional initial value generation method, pseudospectral method assisted by neural network has significantly improved in solving speed and reliability.

articleTitle: Marker-Free Extrinsic Parameter Calibration for Wide Baseline Binocular Stereo Vision Systems
abstract: The extrinsic parameter calibration of wide-baseline binocular stereo vision (BSV) systems faces significant challenges due to the large differences between binocular images. To this end, we propose a marker-free extrinsic parameter calibration method for wide baseline BSV systems tailored to the observation of airborne group targets. The core of our method is to construct feature point pairs of the binocular images. We first use the inter-frame difference algorithm to extract feature points from the images. Afterwards, we construct constraints using epipolar geometry to match these feature points and then obtain a fundamental matrix. By decomposing the fundamental matrix, we can derive the extrinsic parameters. In order to verify the performance of our method, we built a simulation environment for airborne group target flight using Blender software. Within this simulation environment, a series of simulation results demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method. Without relying on markers, our method can solve the matching problem caused by the similarity of features in images of airborne group targets that are difficult to distinguish.

articleTitle: A Short-Term Load Forecasting Method for Large-Scale Power Distribution Systems Based on a Novel Spatio-Temporal Neural Network
abstract: The existing body of research on load forecasting in power distribution systems has given limited consideration to the spatial relationships among nodes. To address this gap and effectively analyze the spatio-temporal heterogeneity and non-stationarity of load in distribution systems, this study introduces a novel spatio-temporal information learning architecture aimed at accurately predicting load under evolving graph structures. The proposed architecture named Meta-graph Enhanced Convolutional Recurrent Network (MegaECRN), combines a Transformer-Encoder module with a graph convolutional recurrent module. Furthermore, the architecture incorporates a dynamic topology structure learning module driven by a meta-graph repository into the graph convolutional recurrent encoder-decoder framework. To evaluate the performance of the proposed model, extensive experiments are conducted on the IEEE 8500-node test feeder, and comprehensive performance evaluations are carried out by comparing the model with baseline and state-of-the-art (SOTA) models. The results demonstrate the superior performance of our model on this dataset.

articleTitle: Learning to Embed Seen/Unseen Compositions based on Graph Networks
abstract: Composability allows known concepts to form newer and more complex ones. This coupling process is the research interests of Compositional Zero-Shot Learning (CZSL). The goal can be described as building a classifier for unknown compositions in the testing set based on known attribute primitives (e.g., old, cute) and object primitives (e.g., cats, cars) in the training set. There are many challenges in this process. For example, the same attribute primitive behaves significantly distinct on different objects. Common CZSL methods introduce auxiliary classification information into the model by using the pretrained model or external knowledge base, but the distribution of introduced auxiliary information is usually inconsistent with the distribution of the class information contained in training set itself, resulting in the model's misunderstanding of combined features. In view of this deficiency, we proposed a novel Compositional Graph Convolutional Network model, which consists of two embedding networks for image and label text modal data respectively. With graph convolutional networks, we can eliminate potential differences in information distribution in the pre-training data. Besides, we add a quintuplet loss to cross-entropy loss to generate a smoother feature representation. The results on three benchmarks including MIT-States, UT-Zappos and C-GQA datasets show that the proposed model exceeds the seven state-of-the-art methods in terms of Area Under the Curve (AUC) and classification accuracy. This confirms that our method can generate more recognizable compositional features.

articleTitle: A Natural Lane Change Decision Model Using Extreme Value Theory for Mixed Traffic Flow
abstract: Given the prevalence of frequent highway accidents, investigating the potential of connected automated vehicles (CAVs) to enhance both traffic efficiency and safety emerges as a pivotal concern. This study addresses how CAVs can harness connected information for informed decision-making, proposing a novel natural lane-changing model rooted in extreme value theory to accommodate mixed traffic flow. Initially, this research develops acceleration, deceleration, and randomization rules for a cellular automata model of two-lane mixed traffic flow, grounded in an analysis of diverse vehicle behaviors. Subsequently, utilizing extreme value distribution, the model determines the maximum probability of CAVs changing lanes at various distances. The study concludes with a numerical simulation analyzing trajectory-velocity diagrams, average travel time, and average speed across different CAV penetration rates. Results demonstrate the model's efficacy in mitigating traffic risks while significantly improving traffic efficiency and safety.

articleTitle: Path Loss Map Construction Based on RadioResUNet
abstract: Propagation path loss prediction is critical in wireless communication, playing a significant role in wireless network planning, signal transmission optimization, and wireless coverage evaluation. However, traditional path loss prediction methods often rely on complex physical models and environmental parameters, leading to time-consuming and computationally intensive calculations. Several machine learning methods have been proposed to predict path loss, but their accuracy still needs improvement. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel machine learning method called RadioResUNet, which is an improved version of ResUNet. RadioResUnet incorporates progressive multilevel encoder, attention mechanism, depthwise separable convolution, and fine-grained downsampling into ResUnet to adapt to the path loss prediction problem. Compared to traditional path loss prediction methods, our method directly predicts path loss from the input (city map) by learning map features and spatial relationships, reducing the reliance on complex physical models and environmental parameters, simplifying the computation process, and enhancing path loss prediction accuracy. Through experiments on the RadioMapSeer dataset, we demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms the existing methods in terms of prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Dual-Threshold: A Hierarchical Label Assignment Scheme Considering Scale Information For Small Object Detection
abstract: Small object detection has always been a focal point and challenge within the object detection task. Despite the availability of various advanced object detectors, the performance of detecting small objects in general scenes remains unsatisfactory. A crucial factor contributing to this is the imbalance of samples between small objects and objects with other scales within general scene datasets. In order to address this issue, we approach it from the perspective of label assignment. Specifically, we distinguish between small objects and objects with other scales, employing a dual-threshold approach based on pseudo anchors. By setting different threshold criteria for small objects and objects with other scales after generating pseudo anchors during label assignment process, we increase the sample ratio of small objects without any additional computational cost or extra parameters for training and testing. By incorporating dual-threshold metric into an anchor-free object detection framework, we observe consistent improvements of the proposed method for small objects on general object detection benchmarks such as PASCAL VOC and MSCOCO. Our method achieves 40.6% AP on MSCOCO and reaches 24.0% AP_s, which is 0.4% higher than the anchor-free baseline and behaves better than other recent state-of-the-art detectors.

articleTitle: Face Feature Point Detection Based on a Novel Two-Branch Network Model
abstract: Face recognition technology is gradually maturing, and many face recognition techniques are based on accurate feature point detection, such as facial expression recognition. Previous research has focused on images with relatively small facial changes, where the detection results are relatively good. However, the robustness of feature point detection decreases for images with large facial changes, such as exaggerated expressions and occlusions. Also, data imbalance constrains the accuracy of detection. Due to many factors such as the complexity of the model and the amount of computation, it is difficult to meet the practical requirements. Therefore, accurate, efficient and compact face feature point detection becomes a challenge. Considering these three objectives, a two-branch face feature point detection model is proposed. The model has good detection accuracy in unconstrained environment and outperforms other models. Specifically, in terms of processing speed and model compactness, a lightweight network MobileNet-v2 is utilized to construct a backbone network to predict the locations of feature points. In the training stage, an auxiliary network is constructed to locate geometrically regularized feature points by calculating three Euler angles to estimate the rotation information of each sample. In this paper, a new loss function is designed to reduce the imbalance of data by adjusting the loss weights of each sample in the training set. In this study, the model is proved to be highly advantageous in all aspects through a large number of experiments, and comparative experiments are conducted on the challenging datasets of 300W, AFLW and WFLW. The experimental results are analyzed to achieve accurate, efficient and compact face feature point detection.

articleTitle: An End to End Spatial Point Instance Network for Lane Detection of Autonomous Driving
abstract: Lane detection is a critical aspect of autonomous driving systems. However, existing studies have indicated that the effectiveness of lane detection in complex scenarios is often below satisfactory levels. To address this challenge, we propose an integration of the encode-decode structure from PINet (Point Instance model), with SCNN, which leverages a spatial CNN. Through a comparative analysis of our approach against other methods, we have observed a remarkable superiority of our newly introduced model, SPINet (Spatial Point Instance model), specifically in complex scenarios. The exceptional performance of SPINet in the field of lane detection holds significant potential for enhancing the safety of autonomous driving. In summary, the notable advancements achieved by SPINet can make a substantial contribution to the safety of autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Air Conditioning Load Forecast Based on LSTM Combining Improved Particle Swarm Algorithm and Attention Mechanism
abstract: Air-conditioning load forecasting is of great significance for saving building energy consumption and maintaining stable load operation of equipment, so research on air-conditioning load forecasting has high practical significance and social value. The building model is established, the air-conditioning load data is obtained by TRNSYS load simulation software, and the IPSO-AM-LSTM neural network model is established by Python. Use the IPSO algorithm to find the best parameters predicted by its model and make predictions. Several different neural network models were trained and validated on building air conditioning load data. Compared with the traditional LSTM model, the MAE, MAPE, and RMSE of IPSO-AM-LSTM are reduced by 61.9%, 46.4%, and 47.1% respectively.

articleTitle: The Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Segmented Composite Function Sliding Mode Observer
abstract: A piecewise composite function with variable boundary layer is used to replace the Sign function in the traditional sliding mode observer; Further optimize the position sensorless control strategy for PMSM. The experimental results show that the observation accuracy of the improved SMO for motor speed and rotor angle is higher than that of the traditional SMO, and the improved SMO further weakens the inherent chattering problem of the traditional SMO, verifying that the control accuracy of the improved sliding mode observer for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is further improved.

articleTitle: Image Registration with Learned Regularization
abstract: Image registration is one of the important tasks in medical image processing. The accuracy of image registration greatly affects the subsequently intelligent analysis. In this paper, we focus on the medical image registration via deep learning, and propose the unsupervised deep learning framework based on model decoupling and regularization learning. Specifically, as a highly ill-posed inverse problem, we first decompose the image registration into two simpler sub-problems to reduce the complexity of model solving. Further, two light neural networks are constructed to approximate the solutions of the two subproblems, where the training strategy of alternative iteration is used. Secondly, we introduce regularization learning module to form an end-to-end deep learning architecture. Here, we approximate the regularization term via the ISTA net, and make the regularization constraints more consistent with the actual data distribution. It reduces the registration errors caused by the deviation between the pre-set prior knowledge and the actual data distribution, and then realizes a higher accurate and data adaptive registration approach. Finally, to validate the performance of the proposed algorithm, we compare it with the VoxelMorph algorithms on brain MRI images dataset LPBA40 and lung CT image dataset DIRLAB. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithms obtain the best performance.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Adaptive Neural Predefined Performance Control of Non-Affine Multi-Agent Systems with Input Delay
abstract: In this paper, observer-based adaptive neural pre-defined performance control is studied for non-affine multi-agent systems with input delay. Compared with existing results, a variable parameters predefined performance control method for multi-agent system is proposed. In addition, Pade approximation and mean value theorem are used to solve the obstacles of input delay and non-affine term. Different from the dynamic surface control(DSC) method, the command filter (CF) method can also solve the problem of computational explosion in the backstepping design, and the filter error generated is well eliminated. By utilizing adaptive backstepping technique and Lyapunov stability theorem, it is proved that all signals in multi-agent systems are cooperative semi-global uniform and ultimately bounded (CSUUB). The observer estimation errors and the tracking errors within a predefined range converge on a small neighborhood. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improved Sliding Window Smoothing for Video Temporal Action Segmentation and Recognition
abstract: Despite substantial research on human action segmentation in videos to determine the type and timing of activities, the topic is still unresolved because of the dearth of large-scale annotation data in video analysis applications. Supervised video action segmentation employs a number of temporal convolutional network (TCN) models to address this problem. The process is still difficult, because of the intricate temporal duration division of the movements in the videos. In order to create a soft and flexible video partition, we incorporate an improved sliding window smoothing (ISWS) technique into a TCN baseline model in this study. When screening the target video segmentation sequence, our research method carefully selects three discriminative frames and cleverly integrates them into the adaptive sliding window to more specifically optimize the smoothing effect of the entire prediction sequence. It is particularly worth noting that we implement a doubling penalty mechanism when the window slides to the wrong category position. In order to learn the resultants of effective and ineffective segmentation paths, we designed a new loss function to smooth the candidate frames of the segmentation points in the sliding window using the ISWS scheme. So that our method can increase the receptive field of video segmentation effectively to gain the optimal action segmentation. Experiments on the breakfast, 50salads, and GTEA datasets demonstrate that our method significantly improved the frame accuracy for action segmentation in videos when compared to the state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: Scenario Digitalization Autonomous Driving Based on Digital Twin Maps
abstract: Constrained by the complexity of mixed traffic environments, autonomous driving is currently operational only within certain enclosed scenarios and is not yet equipped to cater to the daily commuting needs of the populace. In response to this challenge, we propose a novel approach to autonomous driving, referred to as scenario digitalization autonomous driving. Scenario digitalization autonomous driving commences with the utilization of high definition map to render a static digital repre-sentation of the driving scene. This is then coupled with vehicle-to-cloud communication to construct a real-time digital twin scene of both the vehicle and its environment in the cloud. The allocation of road rights for autonomous vehicles is subsequently managed through a cloud control dispatch platform. This process creates a structured, efficient digital driving environment that fundamentally circumvents the endless predicament of game-theoretical scenarios potentially encountered by autonomous vehicles, thereby ensuring the smooth operation of the traffic network. In conclusion, the feasibility of scenario digitalization autonomous driving is corroborated through two experiments. These tests confirm the efficacy of the cloud control dispatch platform in terms of its robust scheduling capabilities and its precise interventions for safety, thereby endorsing the viability of this novel approach to autonomous driving,

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Agent Task Allocation and Path Planning Based on Pri-MADDPG
abstract: In this paper, we aim to develop a reinforcement learning (RL) based algorithm for the task allocation and path planning problem of multi-agent systems where all agents autonomously head to task points with obstacle avoidance. To address the challenge of slow convergence speed and insufficient reward setting when using traditional RL methods, the named Pri-MADDPG algorithm based on prioritized experience replay is proposed. By integrating task allocation and path planning problem, we first construct a framework for multi-agent reinforcement learning training by designing essential elements including appropriate observation space, action space, and reward functions. Then a prioritized experience replay method, in which the value network loss is employed for the priority evaluation, is utilized to enhance policy learning performance. A reward mechanism is further improved through taking into consideration of both global task objectives and individual objectives. To verify the effectiveness of Pri-MADDPG algorithm, experiments are finally carried out with the well-designed reward mechanism. The results demonstrate that all agents can autonomously accomplish task allocation with smooth and highly safe trajectories while achieving faster convergence speed, better stability, and superior performance.

articleTitle: Distributed Model Predictive Control Based on Predictive Spacing Strategy for Heterogeneous Vehicle Formation with Constraints
abstract: This paper considers the vehicle formation problem with nonlinear and heterogeneous dynamic model and constraint conditions. A predictive spacing strategy (PSS) is put forward, which utilized the present velocity information of the vehicle to predict the distance traveled over a period of time. A distributed model predictive control (DMPC) based on the new PSS is presented for the heterogeneous vehicle formation with velocity, acceleration constraints and general communication topology. A sufficient condition to ensure the asymptotic stability of the vehicle formation is derived, and the design process of the distributed model predictive control is given. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed PSS and DMPC algorithm is proved by experimental simulation, and the results show it can effectively improve the effectiveness of vehicle formation.

articleTitle: Aleatoric Uncertainty Based Label Distribuion Leanig for Pose Estimation of Sichuan Peppers
abstract: Sichuan peppers are delicious spices and its autonomous robotic harvesting requires the estimation of pepper pose on the farm. The pepper pose estimation task can be casted as ordinal classification problems by defining a number of pose labels. Since adjacent pose labels share resembling appearance, there exists label ambiguity in many pepper images and ambiguity degree of different images is changing. Label distribution learning (LDL) can handle label ambiguity by converting a single label to a label distribution. Recent LDL methods measure ambiguity degree through training losses, which mainly indicate epistemic uncertainty (EU) and consequently prone to underestimate the ambiguity variations among different samples. To address this issue, we propose a novel LDL method for pepper pose estimation, by measuring ambiguity degrees through aleatoric uncertainty (AU) rather than EU. In specific, we fist leverage Bayesian neural network to quantify sample AU values, which express the inherent noise in observations and thus can sufficiently capture the variations in pose ambiguity. Then, AU values are used to adjust the variance of label distributions so that samples with higher AU values are associated with more flattened distributions. Finally, the instance-aware label distributions are leveraged to train networks for pepper pose estimation. Experimental results on pepper images collected on the farm show that, our method achieve the overall accuracy of 81.28%, outperforming recent leading LDL methods in performance.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fault Diagnosis for EHA Based on Muti-Source Fusion Hypergraph Convolutional Neural Networks Under Small Sample
abstract: Electro-Hydrostatic Actuator (EHA) is widely used in the aerospace industry due to its ability of high-precision control and high load-carrying capacity. During their extensive service life, aviation EHA's hydraulic systems inevitably experience failures, leading to a degradation of control performance and potential safety incidents. Moreover, the diagnosis of hydraulic systems is challenged by their intricate structural, elusive failure mechanisms, and the difficulties in obtaining representative fault samples. To address this, a novel approach based on Muti-source fusion hypergraph convolutional neural networks (MF-HGCN) is proposed. In this study, a fusion approach is employed to integrate multiple fault features extracted from the EHA's hydraulic system. By calculating the Euclidean distance between various signal sources, a hypergraph structure is constructed. Each node corresponds to a specific signal channel. Subsequently, this hypergraph data is fed into the designed hypergraph convolutional neural network, enabling classification of the entire graph. Finally, the trained network model is utilized for intelligent fault diagnosis of the hydraulic system. The experimental results of EHA hydraulic system test rig from Nanjing University of Science and Technology demonstrate that the proposed intelligent fault diagnosis method has better diagnostic performance under limited fault samples.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Neural Network Optimal Model Based on Multi-Channel CNN and BiLSTM with Attention Mechanism
abstract: In order to figure out the issue that the current CNN and RNN do not extract enough text features and fail to capture key information when performing sentiment analysis tasks, this paper proposes a hybrid neural network model WCAFB with attention mechanism, which combines CNN and BiLSTM. The proposed model uses two pre-trained word vector models, Word2vec and Fasttext, to learn word vectors in combination with embedded layer fine-tuning. The proposed model uses multiple CNN with different sizes of convolutional kernels to capture local features of text at different scales and integrates attention mechanisms into the extracted features to dynamically adjust their weights. BiLSTM is used to extract semantic information from the context, and then the local and global features extracted from CNN and BiLSTM are fused. Finally, use the Softmax classifier to obtain the sentimental polarity of the text. The experimental results indicate that this model can extract more abundant text features than other single models, and the classification accuracy has been improved to varying degrees compared with other models.

articleTitle: Federated Ophthalmic Disease Diagnosis Based on Weighted Averaging and Local Optimization
abstract: Deep learning and computer vision (CV) can easily recognize pictures that the human doctor would have to spend a lot of time and labor to process. Thus, they have a wide range of applications in the field of ophthalmology, which is highly dependent on fundus images. However, training a robust and highly accurate model requires a large number of labeled high-quality images, which is often difficult for a single institution to provide. A natural solution is to use data from multiple medical centers to train the model. But due to privacy protection, data heterogeneity, and other problems, these data cannot be shared directly. Based on a real case of ophthalmic disease diagnosis with multiple data sources, this paper proposes solutions to the heterogeneity of data amount and features between datasets, establishes a heterogeneous federated learning framework, and applies federated learning to the diagnosis of multiple types of ophthalmic diseases for the first time. The experimental results show that federated learning can greatly improve the diagnostic accuracy of clients with less data, and the accuracy of clients with more data can also be slightly improved. The ablation experiment has demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method for handling data heterogeneity. Our research shows that through heterogeneous federated learning, we can use multi-source, non-independent-identical data to build accurate disease diagnosis models, and make clients who cannot obtain effective models get a practical level disease diagnosis model.

articleTitle: An efficient grasp pose detection method based on Point-PN
abstract: Grasp pose detection is crucial in robotics and automation, but generating reliable and humanoid grasps in unstructured environments remains a challenge. Deep learning neural networks have gained attention in computer vision, leading to the development of grasp detection methods. Existing methods generate multiple potential grasp poses, but in practical applications, only one suitable grasp position is typically chosen, resulting in wasted resources and decreased effectiveness. Moreover, these methods often suffer from computational overhead. In this paper, we propose an efficient grasp pose detection method based on Point-PN to solve these problems. We are able to generate a single optimal grasp pose for objects in the scene by decoupling the grasp pose prediction task into subtasks of grasp approach vector, grasp rotation angle, and grasp depth, and evaluating the pose quality using grasp confidence scores. Additionally, We introduce a multi-structure network that utilizes Point-PN as the network backbone, enabling efficient learning of point cloud features and reducing training costs and resource consumption. For our network, we proposed a joint loss function in order to better adapt to the various grasp pose prediction subtasks. Experimental results demonstrate significant achievements in network evaluation and real robot experiments.

articleTitle: Extended State Observer-Based Distributed Dual Closed-Loop Model Predictive Formation Control for Multi-AUV System
abstract: This paper centers around the three-dimensional formation control for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) amidst composite disturbances within intricate ocean. We present a distributed dual closed-loop model predictive control scheme based on an extended state observer (ESO). In the initial phase, a well-designed ESO is employed to effectively compensate for model uncertainties, unknown disturbances, and unmeasured velocities for each AUV. Next, an outer-loop position prediction and inner-loop velocity prediction controller is developed. After considering the complicated constraints, the local optimization problem is solved to determine the optimal inputs. Finally, comparative simulation results under the connected directed topology validate the feasibility and robustness of this method.

articleTitle: Multi-Conditional Adjacency Learning and Grouping Method for Monitoring Gas Turbine Generation Process with Nonstationarity
abstract: Gas turbines are widely used in power generation, their reliable operation ensures the electric power transmission. However, the switching operating conditions and complex structure of gas turbine brings the typical nonstationary characteristics and complex variables coupling, which makes it difficult to monitor the gas turbine generation process and trace the fault component accurately. In this work, a multi-conditional adjacency learning and grouping method is proposed to deal with these problems. First, a graph-driven adjacency learning strategy is proposed to extract information from operating data and physical structure of gas turbine for representing the nonlinear coupling relationships between variables. Then, a multi-conditional variable grouping strategy is developed to divide variables into groups according to the learned variable relationships and multiple condition indicators. Condition-driven monitoring sub-models are established on those variable groups to realize fine-grained monitoring for each component of gas turbine. All sub-models are built by sequential condition-mode division and principal component analysis algorithm to realize accurate monitoring for the nonstationary process. Finally, a model fusion strategy is designed to estimate sub-model contributions and merge all monitoring statistics to obtain the overall monitoring result. A real gas turbine failure case illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Robust Optimization for Industrial Utility System Integrating Wind and Solar Energies
abstract: Utility systems provide power and heat for chemical plants and drive production processes, while large amounts of greenhouse gases are emitted. The introduction of renewable energy sources can help reduce carbon emissions from traditional utility systems. A data-driven robust optimization for utility systems that introduce wind and solar energy is presented in this paper. The paper proposes a superstructure model for utility systems with renewable energy equipment, as well as physical models for wind turbines, photovoltaic power generation, and electrical energy storage. A robust optimization method is employed to solve the optimization problem in case of uncertainty in wind and solar energy. Then, an environmental and economic multi-objective optimization model was formulated to balance economic costs and carbon emissions. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed methods was demonstrated by a case study of a real industrial chemical plant.
