The image depth information and pose information are fused by the depth estimation network and the pose estimation network, and the tightly coupled training of the two-branch network is realized by using the view reconstruction loss. In order to further improve the feature representation ability of the network, the occlusion mask module and the attention mechanism module are respectively integrated, the binary mask is constructed using the depth information of adjacent images and the photometric loss is optimized, and the saliency of key features is improved by using channel attention and spatial attention. The experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively improve the feature representation ability of the network, alleviate the problem of scale error accumulation under long-term sequence tracking, and obtain higher localization accuracy.

articleTitle: Structure Guided Unsupervised Condition Monitoring of Wind Turbine Pitch System: A Deep One-Class Classification Approach
abstract: Currently, the operation and maintenance of wind turbine (WT) pitch systems have gained increasing attention and data-driven monitoring approaches have been widely studied. However, existing data-driven methods often cause false positives and alarms due to their purely data-driven nature. To further improve the monitoring performance, we proposed a deep one-class classification network model named Pitch-OC to detect early faults with the available supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) data. The training of the Pitch-OC model does not require data labels but only learns the WT pitch system health behavior characteristics. Pitch-OC integrates the prior knowledge of the pitch system structure. Specifically, we design a structure-guided group learning layer to combine the prior knowledge of the pitch structure and further capture the complex intervariable relationship in a group manner. Then, we map the hypersphere aggregation layer to obtain a hypersphere model. This hypersphere model is used to monitor the pitch system online. Our experiments on the SCADA data of two WTs prove that our model outperforms existing methods.

articleTitle: Image Stitching Algorithm of Concrete Crack Based on Bridge Inspection Robot
abstract: Aiming at the problems of difficult, low efficiency, and limited scope of manual bridge disease inspection operations, an image stitching algorithm based on grid deformation alignment and iterative optimization of suture lines is proposed by combining the structural features of bridges and the field of view constraints of inspection robots. In the image registration step, mesh deformation is used instead of the homography transform to improve the local alignment capability. Furthermore, by introducing line segment features based on point features, it mitigates the distortion of the image caused by grid deformation. In the image fusion step, given how much texture intensity is perceived by the human eye, we introduce structural similarity to quantitatively assess the merit of suture lines, and the adaptive saliency is used as a weight for the smoothness term to solve for the optimal suture line via iterative optimization. The experimental results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper can stitch concrete bridge crack images quickly and accurately, and solve the problems of ghosting, position shift, and color inconsistency in image stitching with high accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: MSCR-HRNetV2: High-Resolution Remote Sensing Image Segmentation for Railway Scenes
abstract: Remote sensing image semantic segmentation not only enables the acquisition of valuable category information regarding surface objects but also provides crucial spatial information. This foundational data, with its high research value, plays a pivotal role in advancing the understanding and utilization of spatial environmental resources. To construct a suitable space for railway transportation and improve the channel information mismatch problem in the multi-scale fusion unit of HRNetV2, in terms of data, a high-resolution remote sensing image dataset of two railway sections of Kaha Railway and Ganquan Railway was collected, and annotated, including 210 original remote sensing images with a resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4800 \times 2986$</tex>, a viewing altitude of 2km, and a spatial resolution of 0.24m. In terms of methods, an embedded self-attention mechanism module was introduced and a multi-scale consistency regularization (MSCR) method was introduced to propose MSCR-HRNetV2, achieving pixel-level semantic segmentation representation of high-resolution remote sensing images. The experimental results show that the MIoU results of MSCR-HRNetV2 on the self-built railway dataset and the public Potsdam remote sensing image dataset reached 0.8137 and 0.7596 respectively, which were 0.0313 and 0.0201 higher than the original HRNetV2. Compared with other typical remote sensing image semantic segmentation methods such as Deeplabv3+, the segmentation accuracy has also been improved by 0.0386 and 0.0219. The high-resolution remote sensing image dataset constructed in this study provides an important data source for studying the segmentation problem of high-resolution remote sensing images around railways. The proposed MSCR-HRNetV2 benchmark method lays the foundation for the full development and utilization of railway transportation space resources.

articleTitle: Research on Error Compensation Method of SINS/GNSS Integrated Navigation System Based on NARX Neural Network
abstract: This study proposes a new algorithm combining integrated navigation and neural networks, which combines a nonlinear autoregressive neural network (NARX) with an extended Kalman filter (EKF), based on the global navigation satellite system (GNSS) and strapdown inertial navigation system (SINS). The purpose is to use the NARX neural network to predict the measurement update of EKF during GNSS signal interruption, to compensate for the errors of SINS instead of EKF,to correct the divergence error of SINS, and to ensure the accuracy of the system. The NARX neural network uses the Levenberg-Marquard algorithm to train the neural network, which speeds up the neural network's convergence rate. As a dynamic neural network model, the NARX neural network takes into account the dependence of the current output on the past input and output. As a result, it uses the output at the current time as the feedback input at the next time. The simulation results demonstrate that employing the NARX neural network for error compensation during GNSS signal interruption can somewhat increase the location and speed accuracy of the SINS/GNSS system.

articleTitle: A Constrained Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on an Infeasible Archive
abstract: In the field of engineering design, there is a class of constrained multi-objective optimization problems where the optimal solutions are often found at the constraint boundaries. However, effectively utilizing the infeasible solutions at these boundaries poses a challenge in solving these problems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on an infeasible archive (CIA). CIA utilizes two populations: one considers both objectives and constraints, while the other ignores all constraints. Additionally, an archive is implemented to store non-dominated infeasible solutions. To improve the search coverage in the initial stage and accelerate convergence in the later stage, a strategy is implemented that reduces infeasible solutions using the infeasible archive. Furthermore, a neighborhood-based offspring generation mechanism is developed, which combines feasible and infeasible solutions to enhance the ability of the algorithm to explore constraint boundaries. Experimental results from three test suites demonstrate that the proposed algorithm performs competitively when compared to four representative algorithms.

articleTitle: Target Threat Assessment Method Based on Modified Weighting-Cloud Reasoning
abstract: As a process of real-time state change, the battlefield situation information of air combat also has the characteristics of fuzziness, incompleteness and randomness. Aiming at the problems that the traditional weighting method is too one-sided, simple linear combination is not strong in explanation, and it is difficult for decision makers to accurately and objectively describe fuzzy information, and take into account the randomness of the battlefield for reasoning analysis, this paper proposes to use the improved multi-condition cloud model reasoner to evaluate the threat index of the target. On the basis of the proposed combination weighting method of objective entropy weight to modify subjective weight, the multi-conditional reasoners are divided into several single conditional reasoners and the rules are fused according to the weight, and the reasoning is repeated many times to reduce the error caused by randomness in the process of cloud reasoning. Finally, the threat level of enemy aircraft is obtained, and the specific threat index of enemy aircraft is also obtained. It provides a reasonable basis for the subsequent fire distribution between the enemy and us.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network with Sinc-Layer and Adaptive Feature Weight Distribution for Motor Imagery EEG Recognition
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signal decoding is instrumental in the brain-computer interface (BCI) system. Complex characteristics of EEG pose challenges to the decoding work. In this paper, a multi-scale convolutional neural network with sinc-layer and adaptive feature weight distribution is proposed to decode motor imagery (MI) EEG signals. Sinc-layer can transform kernels of one-dimensional convolution into band-pass filters and it designs the cut-off frequency as learning parameters which can effectively decode the temporal features in the EEG signal. Then a multi-scale convolution module is established, which exploits two one-dimensional convolution and a two-dimensional convolution to extract features from EEG signals. An adaptive feature weight distribution layer is designed to assign weights to features after multi-scale convolution module, aiming to reduce the negative impact of redundant features on recognition accuracy. The results reveal that the method proposed in this paper obtains better results compared with the baseline model in the BCI IV dataset 2b and the dataset collected in our laboratory. Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed method is feasible performs well in the BCI system. Therefore, the proposed method can stimulate the development of human-computer interaction.

articleTitle: Embedded-based Analyzer for Total Organic Carbon in Water
abstract: To meet the demand for monitoring organic pollutants in water, this study developed and implemented a water total organic carbon analyzer based on embedded technology. The instrument uses the photooxidation method to oxidize the water, and measures the total organic carbon content embedded; photocatalytic oxidation; differential method; analyzer for total organic carbonby comparing the difference in conductivity of the water before and after oxidation using differential subtraction. This study also analyzed the conductivity at different temperatures and improved the detection accuracy of conductivity by using an improved temperature compensation formula. Experimental results demonstrate that the analyzer has good anti-interference ability and repeatability, producing stable and reliable results. The analyzer's relative error is between 0.076% and 8.333%, which meets analysis standards and has good on-site applicability. The data generated by this study provides technical support for monitoring organic pollutants in water.

articleTitle: Generalized Mixture Model for Extreme Events Forecasting in Time Series Data
abstract: Time Series Forecasting (TSF) is a widely researched topic with broad applications in weather forecasting, traffic control, and stock price prediction. Extreme values in time series often significantly impact human and natural systems, but predicting them is challenging due to their rare occurrence. Statistical methods based on Extreme Value Theory (EVT) provide a systematic approach to modeling the distribution of extremes, particularly the Generalized Pareto (GP) distribution for modeling the distribution of exceedances beyond a threshold. To overcome the subpar performance of deep learning in dealing with heavy-tailed data, we propose a novel framework to enhance the focus on extreme events. Specifically, we propose a Deep Extreme Mixture Model with Autoencoder (DEMMA) for time series prediction. The model comprises two main modules: 1) a generalized mixture distribution based on the Hurdle model and a reparameterized GP distribution form independent of the extreme threshold, 2) an Autoencoder-based LSTM feature extractor and a quantile prediction module with a temporal attention mechanism. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on multiple real-world rainfall datasets.

articleTitle: Integrating Reinforcement Learning and LSTM for Raw Material Procurement Optimization in Salt Lake Chemical Manufacturing
abstract: In the process industry, fluctuations in raw material prices and changes in production demand pose significant challenges to formulating effective raw material procurement plans during production and operation. Existing procurement optimization methods typically assume known values for price sequences and production demand, which may not adequately address market volatility risks. To overcome these challenges, this study introduces a long-short-term memory (LSTM) model for short-term prediction of raw material market prices and production demand. Subsequently, deep reinforcement learning methods are utilized to make sequential decisions on raw material procurement plans to effectively navigate complex procurement environments. To validate the efficacy of our proposed method, the coal procurement process of a Salt Lake chemical company was chosen as an example. The real operating data was used to compare the difference between the proposed method and the traditional methods regarding decision-making performance. The results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly reduces procurement costs while improving overall enterprise production efficiency.

articleTitle: Efficiently Optimizing Drone Nest Deployment for Transmission Line Inspection Based on Heuristic Algorithm
abstract: This research introduces a novel and promising approach to optimize the deployment of drone nests for transmission line inspection by enhancing the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm with penalty functions and dynamic inertia. By effectively utilizing penalty functions, the study addresses the constraints of the optimization problem, transforming it into an unconstrained optimization task and allowing for more effective exploration of the search space. Additionally, the dynamic inertia strategy enables the algorithm to strike a balance between global exploration and local exploitation, leading to improved convergence rates and enhanced solution quality. Through a comprehensive comparison with both static inertial weight PSO and genetic algorithm (GA), the enhanced PSO algorithm exhibited superior performance, highlighting its ability to efficiently overcome the limitations of traditional algorithms and optimize the placement of drone nests effectively. The proposed approach demonstrates encouraging results in minimizing flight costs and generating near-optimal solutions for large-scale drone nest placement problems. The study's modest yet significant contribution lies in its potential to advance intelligent drone-based inspection platforms, offering the promise of increased inspection efficiency and potential cost savings for power grid inspections.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv5 for High-Resolution Ore Image Detection
abstract: During ore dressing production, the size of the ore significantly affects the grinding and classification efficiency and is a crucial control parameter. In the past, most ore image detection algorithms focused on the detection tasks of high-resolution ore image. At the same time, due to the sparse data set for industrial production applications, the generalization ability and robustness of the model are low, and it has poor performance on tiny ore target detection tasks. To remedy these shortcomings, this paper proposes the ODA-YOLOv5 network model for ore image detection. In this paper, we adopt a multi-scale training strategy to address the difficulty of detecting tiny ores in high-resolution images. A self-built dataset is constructed by fusing multi-scale ore images. The input image size is dynamically adjusted during training to enhance the robustness of the detection model for ore of different scales. In order to improve the performance of the detection algorithm, we introduce the C3-ECA attention module, which fully takes into account the local cross-letter road interactions and considerably reduces the model complexity. Our algorithm achieves approximately 97.9% mAP and approximately 62.11 FPS on the self-built dataset. Our algorithm sufficiently demonstrates the superiority of our detection model algorithm for industrial ore detection.

articleTitle: Drivable Area Segmentation Based on HybridNets and Text Prompt Network
abstract: Drivable area segmentation and traffic object detection are important prerequisites for autonomous navigation of intelligent vehicles. Recently, multi-task network is used for segmentation and detection task because of its high efficiency brought by multiplexing features. However, the existing benchmarks mostly perform poorly when the top-level tasks show significant differences. Inspired by text prompt network from Natural Language Processing, we propose a text-prompt-based feature enhancement optimization method of object detection and drivable area segmentation in traffic scene. We design text prompt and fuse it with image feature. The end-to-end multi-task neural network is used to realize the object detection with higher precision and the drivable area segmentation based on traffic rule semantics with small data volume. Experimental results show that our proposed text-prompt feature enhancement approach on HybridNets achieves competitive performance on Gazebo simulation scene.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Domain Distribution Dilation For Text-Based Person Retrieval
abstract: The goal of text-based person retrieval is to recognize a corresponding target person from a mass of person image dataset according to a provided text query. Many previous methods are faced with a limited domain distribution (LD2) dilemma. To solve this tough problem, we propose a novel Multi-modal Domain Distribution Dilation (MD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) framework for text-based person retrieval. MD3 consists of two streams, namely an original distribution stream (ODS) and a dilated distribution stream (DDS). A Visual Distribution Dilating (VDD) module is proposed to perturb the key attributes (such as brightness, contrast, and saturation) of an input raw image. A Textual Distribution Dilating (TDD) module is also adopted to make a variation on the textual domain distribution. In order to achieve the purpose of adapting to various domain distribution in a reasonable and effective way, we adopt a mutual learning mechanism that facilitates communication and learning between two streams with diverse distribution information. We carried out a large number of experiments on the widely-used CUHK-PEDES, RSTPReid and ICFG-PEDES datasets to verify the effectiveness of MD3. Compared with the existing methods, MD3 is superior and has achieved the state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Organic Matter Segmentation From Images of Scanning Electron Microscope for Shale Gas Reservoir Discovery
abstract: The micro-pore characteristics of shale gas reservoirs are the focus of unconventional oil and gas exploration. The shape, size, and connectivity of pores determine the reservoir performance of shale reservoirs to a large extent. Therefore, shale gas exploitation requires a complete understanding of pores. At present, it is an important method to obtain pore structure parameters of shale based on the threshold segmentation method. However, some problems still need to be solved, such as small analysis areas, poor accuracy, and weak quantitative analysis caused by human factors. To solve these problems, an intelligent segmentation technique based on energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) analysis data is proposed in this paper to achieve intelligent segmentation of organic matter region in Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) images. Identifying organic matter can lay a foundation for the intelligent identification of shale pores. In this paper, EDS analysis technology is introduced, EDS analysis images are used as label images, and a data set including 1943 EDS analysis images and corresponding SEM images of shale is established. We use U-Net and nested U-Net for organic matter intelligent prediction. Using an SEM image of a shale gas reservoir, intelligent segmentation of organic matter region based on EDS data learning is realized. The results show that the method has high accuracy, can reduce the intervention of human factors, improve the efficiency of analysis, and make the analysis results more accurate and scientific. At the same time, the degree of automation and generalization ability are higher than traditional forecasting methods.

articleTitle: Knowledge distillation- based lightweight network for power scenarios inspection
abstract: To address the problem of target detection networks in power scenarios requiring a large number of parameters and complex structures to ensure accuracy, a knowledge distillation method is proposed to transfer intermediate feature knowledge and output logic knowledge from the teacher model to the student model. The distilled student model achieves high accuracy while maintaining the advantages of fewer parameters and faster inference speed. GFL-ResI8 is used as the student model and GFL-Resl0l as the teacher model. The distilled student model achieves an accuracy of 78.8% with 19.1M parameters, an inference speed of 24.9 img/s, and a computational cost of 155.2 GFlops. Experimental results show that our distillation method achieves the highest accuracy for the student model compared to other distillation methods.

articleTitle: Traffic Flow Forecasting based on Adaptive Graph Structure for Spatio-Temporal Attention Mechanism Network
abstract: With the diversification of information collection, traffic flow data has been expanded from specific areas to large-scale networks, which are represented as spatiotemporal sequence data. Recent research on spatiotemporal graph neural networks (ST-GNNs) has demonstrated excellent performance in capturing these correlations. However, most ST-GNNs rely on predefined graph adjacency matrices or fail to utilize valuable traffic information in node attributes to derive better graph structures. We propose an adaptive graph structure for spatiotemporal attention mechanism network (ASTAMN) model. The learning module for graph structure is based on node properties and constructs the ideal graph structure through weight fusion. The designed spatiotemporal convolution is applied to capture complex spatiotemporal correlations. Experiments on real data sets confirm the effectiveness and robustness of our model.

articleTitle: Refined Background Matting Technology Based on Implicit Neural Representation
abstract: Background matting technology is widely used today, and numerous studies have been conducted in this field. Recent research has revealed that although current background matting frameworks have increased processing speed, the quality of their output results still need improvement by solve the inaccurate edge detection and hard to handling complex backgrounds. In order to achieve more accurate results, we propose a refinement module based on implicit neural representation (INR, model complex relationships between variables in data automatically) for existing background matting frameworks. This technology combines an INR approach with a fully convolutional neural network (FCNN) to automatically label each pixel with its foreground and background attributes. We tested our technique using some matting datasets, and the results demonstrate superior accuracy to traditional methods. Therefore, this paper introduces a new background matting technology based on implicit neural representation that strives to deliver improved output accuracy, and the proposed technology provides a new way to solve the challenging task of background matting.

articleTitle: An Online Education Effect Assessing Method Based on YOLOv8 and Vision Transformer
abstract: Due to the rapid growth of online education worldwide, assessing the learning effectiveness of students during online classes has become increasingly challenging for teachers. In this paper, a method of assessing online education effect based on YOLOv8 and Vision Transformer is proposed. Firstly, the drowsiness state of students in an online teaching unconstraint environment is estimated by using YOLOv8, and then the gaze direction of awake students is estimated by using Vision Transformer to assess the students' attention levels during online education. The results from YOLOv8 are determined based on the calculated probabilities of drowsiness or wakefulness. And then gaze estimation method proposed in this paper was compared with state-of-the-art methods on the MPIIFaceGaze and Gaze360 datasets in which the angular errors of gaze estimation are 4.58° and 12.27°, respectively. We conducted experiments and analysis on a self-made dataset, from which the results demonstrate the feasibility of our method in an unconstrained environment.

articleTitle: Study on Five Typical Optimization Models of LSTM
abstract: LSTM is a special recurrent neural network, which can solve the problem of long-term dependence common in general recurrent neural networks. It can effectively transmit and express the information in a long time series without causing the useful information of a long time ago to be ignored (forgotten). At the same time, LSTM can also solve the problem of gradient disappearance/explosion in RNN. In this paper, we introduce five types of LSTM optimization models, including the current mainstream convolutional neural network (CNN) optimized LSTM model, end-to-end mixed deep learning network model M-B-LSTM, particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) optimized LSTM model, deep Long and short term memory network research, and genetic algorithm LSTM structure. The current development trend of LSTM in time series prediction is summarized to provide certain targets for the follow-up research and forecast.

Author Keywords: long and short term memory neural network

articleTitle: Gradient-guided Mechanism for Long-Tailed Medical Image Classification
abstract: Due to the difficulty of collecting data samples and the cost of annotation, medical image datasets often exhibit a long-tailed distribution. In the long-tailed distribution, the head classes have a large amount of data, which can dominate the model performance in the training process, leading the model biased towards the majority classes. We find such performance bottleneck is mainly caused by the imbalanced gradients and the positive negative gradients ratio can be seen as a balance indicator in the training process. In this study, we propose a novel loss function considering the accumulative positive-to-negative gradient ratio to reweight the contributions of different classes to solve the long-tailed problems. We conduct experiments on two datasets with different class imbalance ratios using the mainstream classification models with common loss functions and the proposed loss. The results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive or even superior performance compared to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) techniques.

articleTitle: Eye Movement Detection Using Self-Supervised Deep Learning
abstract: Eye movement event detection is crucial to analyzing and understanding human visual information. While deep learning has demonstrated remarkable potential in eye movement detection, the effectiveness of fully supervised learning approaches in practical scenarios is often contingent on access to extensive datasets. Given the challenges of acquiring substantial and meticulously curated eye tracking data, we introduce a self-supervised deep learning technique for the task of detecting eye movement events. In order to take full advantage of the temporal sequential nature of eye tracking data, this work introduces a Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC) framework in the pre-training of self-supervised to learn efficient representations for the eye movement classification. We adapt and tailor the CPC method to suit the specific needs and limitations inherent in eye movement detection. Subsequently, we carry out experimental assessments using the GazeCom dataset, a large-scale, publicly accessible resource with manual labeling. Our results show that the performance is comparable to or close to that of fully supervised methods. Moreover, our proposed method is able to enhance classification performance especially when limited labeled data is available, demonstrating the effectiveness of self-supervised learning in mitigating the problem of a lack of labeled data for detecting eye movements.

articleTitle: A Distributionally Robust Joint Chance Constraint Optimization Model for Vehicle Battery Swapping Station Location Problem
abstract: The successful adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) hinges greatly on the provision of robust infrastructural support. This study introduces a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model aimed at identifying the optimal locations and capacities for battery swapping stations (BBSs). The primary objective of this model is to minimize the total cost of the BBS system, encompassing operator and customer costs. Our model effectively mitigates over-conservatism by tackling the uncertainty issues associated with battery swapping demand, a prevalent challenge in existing models. Moreover, we encapsulate demand uncertainty within an ambiguity set and incorporate joint chance constraints, thereby enhancing the reliability of the BBS system. To make this complex, non-convex model tractable, we reformulate it into a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) problem, thus enabling commercial solvers to effectively solve it. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed model can effectively determine optimal solutions for the BBS system's location and capacity, satisfying battery demand while simultaneously minimizing total system costs. The experimental results also underscore the importance of the risk parameter and Wasserstein radius on BBS location and capacity. Our proposed model could serve as a valuable tool for relevant decision-makers in the design of BBS systems, thereby promoting the wider adoption of EVs.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Based System Identification for Linear Time-Invariant Systems
abstract: System identification is an important basis for understanding the behavior characteristics of unknown systems and for further optimization and control purposes. In this brief, we focus on the model identification for LTI systems using a finite set of sampled data and noise bounds. In order to precisely capture the dynamics of the unknown system, a 2-step approach is proposed. Imprimis, a set operation based on zonotope is applied to compute all the possible matrices that describe the system dynamics with an estimated noise set. The computed result is consistent with all data points and noise bound which is represented by matrix zonotope. Secondly, by solving a proposed optimization problem to find the fittest system dynamic matrix. The aim of the problem is to minimize the noise zonotope. The foregoing 2-step approach is capable of effectively approximating the actual systems. Numerical example demonstrates the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Upsampling Network Using Spatially Biased Adaptive Graph Convolution
abstract: Point cloud data plays a vital role in representing the three-dimensional (3D) world and finds extensive use in autonomous driving and three-dimensional cultural heritage displays. However, technical and cost constraints often lead to acquired point cloud data exhibiting density disparity, making it unsuitable for direct use in downstream tasks. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel network called PU-SpaAGCN, using spatially biased adaptive graph convolution. PU-SpaAGCN overcomes the limitations associated with traditional graph convolution, such as the presence of isotropic edge features, by effectively capturing precise point cloud edges and local features. Additionally, the network introduces a spatial bias term to the graph convolution, facilitating the extraction of global features. The fusion of local and global features enables the network to generate higher-quality dense point clouds. Furthermore, unlike previous point cloud upsampling networks, the network introduces a feature space interpolation module, enhancing both network performance and interpretability. Experimental evaluations conducted on the PU1K dataset demonstrate that the dense point cloud produced by PU-SpaAGCN exhibits significant improvements in terms of point cloud uniformity and realism.

articleTitle: An Improved Multi-Agent Consensus Control Method for Virtual Coupling Train System
abstract: The Virtual Coupling Train System (VCTS) is an innovative blocking mode that effectively solves the problems of low efficiency and high energy consumption in conventional high-speed railways. The stable operation of high-speed trains in a clustered formation is the core of the VCTS. This paper proposed an improved multi-agent consensus control method for VCTS by operating at optimal speed while maintaining the desired train tracking interval. Firstly, basic models were established to calculate the ideal interval. Then, the Improved Gravitational Search Algorithm (IGSA) was used to optimize the energy consumption of high-speed trains, and the optimal speed was used in the consensus speed control. To achieve a multi-train formation, a consensus-based control method was developed to realize that all trains operate at the ideal speed. On this basis, an improved multi-agent consensus control strategy was proposed, and the minimum adjustment method was applied to meet the actual constraints. Experimental simulations demonstrated that the algorithm can achieve stable operation of 5-train formations in less than 20 seconds and stabilize the tracking interval at 4.19 km when the train speed reached 304 km/h. The effectiveness of the algorithm was demonstrated by system stability analysis and actual simulation, providing a theoretical basis for research on distributed control algorithms for VCTS.

articleTitle: Integrated Virtually Coupled Train Timetable and Rolling Stock Circulation Plan Optimization for an Urban Rail Transit Line
abstract: Due to the increase of passenger demand, urban rail transit lines are faced with significant challenges. To enhance transport capacity, researchers have introduced the concept of virtual coupling, which replaces physical train connections with wireless communication. This innovation allows trains to couple and decouple during their operation, offering advantages in transport capacity. The virtual coupling technology not only reduces the train headway, but also facilitates flexible coupling and decoupling operations to adapt to varying passenger flow. While there has been extensive research on train timetabling and rolling stock circulation planning, most researchers do not take the virtual coupling into consideration. In this paper, with the unique characteristics of virtual coupling considered, we present a mixed-integer linear programming model for solving the integrated train timetabling and rolling stock circulation planning problem under virtual coupling. This model incorporates binary variables to denote virtual coupling operational states between two trains and considers coupling and decoupling operations in sections and stations. The proposed model can be solved using commercial solvers. To validate the effectiveness of the model, a case study is conducted using data from the Beijing Daxing International Airport Express. The results of the study demonstrate that virtual coupling technology can improve the performance of train timetable.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Load Balancing Strategy for Routing Selection in Multi-Service Networks
abstract: Quality of Service (QoS) routing aims to maximize the use of network resources while subject to a series of QoS constraints. Due to the progressively intricate network environments and escalating demands for bandwidth, how to provide efficient multi-service scheduling and routing is crucial for improving network QoS. However, it is challenging to take both routing and network bandwidth resources into account in a global view. Motivated by these challenges, a method under the mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model is proposed firstly to find the optimal solution for routing selection, which is efficient in multi-service networks. Consequently, a heuristic algorithm based on load balance is proposed to make the scheduling problem tractable while keeping the solution quality satisfactory. The main idea of the heuristic algorithm is to achieve load balance in multi-service networks by dynamically sorting multiple services and selecting appropriate routes from multi-alternative paths. Extensive simulations demonstrate that satisfactory results can be obtained with low computational complexity for both small-scale and large-scale networks.

articleTitle: Learning Quadruped Locomotion Method Integrating Meta-Learning and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The capacity for learning stands as a characteristic of advanced animal cognition. To explore the learning mechanisms underlying quadrupedal locomotive skills, this study delves into the gait learning task of quadrupedal robots, also reviewing several seminal algorithms proposed in recent years within the realm of reinforcement learning tailored to quadrupedal robotic platforms. In contemporary times, serving as an archetype in the domain of deep reinforcement learning, the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm has been extensively deployed in the context of quadrupedal gait learning tasks, yielding commendable experimental outcomes with a reduced demand for hyperparameters. However, the exclusive application of the PPO algorithm imparts a limitation on the agent's capacity to process high-dimensional information effectively. In response to the aforementioned concerns, sparked by insights from meta-learning and capitalizing on meta-learning's prowess in capturing high-dimensional abstract representations of the learning process, this paper introduces a novel fusion of meta-learning and the PPO algorithm, coined as the MAML-PPO algorithm. This innovation empowers quadrupedal robots to acquire enhanced gait proficiency. Simulated outcomes on the PyBullet simulation platform affirm that the algorithm posited in this study successfully imparts walking skills to quadrupedal robots. In comparison to the state-of-the-art SAC and PPO algorithms, the MAML-PPO algorithm advanced in this study not only accelerates training time but also bestows advantages such as heightened walking velocity upon quadrupedal robots.

articleTitle: Research on the Chain Risk Identification of Large-Scale Skiing Events
abstract: Large-scale skiing events are commonly conducted in complex outdoor terrains and weather conditions, where adverse weather conditions can significantly impede the smooth progress of these events. The occurrence of adverse weather conditions increases the risk of domino chains caused by meteorological disasters during large-scale skiing events. To promptly identify the cascading risks caused by adverse weather, this paper proposes a solution to promptly identify cascading risks caused by adverse weather by integrating information related to adverse weather risks of skiing events and constructing a domain knowledge ontology. The paper analyzes and identifies the risk transmission paths of adverse weather, and constructs the risk identification rule base of related event chains to enable global risk chain reasoning driven by spatiotemporal semantics. The proposed approach is demonstrated through the skiing events of the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics, from which the study correctly identifies the risk events caused by adverse weather encountered in multiple skiing events through reasoning. The results show the accuracy and feasibility of the event chain inference model.

articleTitle: Bean Optimization Algorithm Based on Lévy Flight Mechanism
abstract: Bean Optimization Algorithm (BOA) is a kind of swarm intelligence algorithm constructed by the principles of natural seed propagation and population distribution evolution. Its bionic significance is clear and computational efficiency is high. In order to improve the diversity of BOA global search and enhance the performance of fine search, a bean optimization algorithm based on Lévy flight (LBOA) was proposed. LBOA introduces the Lévy flight mechanism into the offspring population distribution module of the BOA, which perturbs different positions of a certain proportion of individuals. By setting a larger Lévy flight step weight in the early and middle stages of BOA evolution, the global search ability and convergence speed of BOA are improved. In the fine search stage of BOA evolution, setting a smaller Lévy flight step weight improves the fine search performance of BOA. Finally, through comparative experiments with other mainstream swarm intelligence algorithms, it is shown that LBOA has better optimization performance.

articleTitle: Robust Time-Delay Force Control for Piezoelectric Actuators without Hysteresis Dynamics
abstract: Accurate force output control of piezoelectric actuators (PEAs) is particularly important in piezo-driven devices. Existing control methods are mostly designed based on system models and require complex parameter identification process, resulting in low control accuracy and poor robustness. Therefore, this work proposes a robust model-independent time-delay force tracking control scheme for PEAs without hysteresis dynamics. The designed control is mainly composed of three parts: 1) a desired error dynamics term based on fast nonsingular integral terminal sliding mode, which ensures fast convergence and high tracking accuracy; 2) a time-delayed estimation (TDE) part that avoids the continuous nonlinearities and realizes the model-free control; 3) a correction part on the basis of the fuzzy logic system (FLS), compensating the TDE error induced from discontinuous nonlinearities and improving the robustness. The stability and finite time convergence of the control system are given using the Lyapunov stability principle. Experiments demonstrate that compared with the conventional TDE-based force tracking control methods, this control scheme has faster converging speed and higher accuracy.

articleTitle: LightBTSeg: A Lightweight Breast Tumor Segmentation Model Using Ultrasound Images via Dual-Path Joint Knowledge Distillation
abstract: The accurate segmentation of breast tumors is an important prerequisite for lesion detection, which has significant clinical value for breast tumor research. The mainstream deep learning-based methods have achieved a breakthrough. However, these high-performance segmentation methods are formidable to implement in clinical scenarios since they always embrace high computation complexity, massive parameters, slow inference speed, and huge memory consumption. To tackle this problem, we propose LightBTSeg, a dual-path joint knowledge distillation framework, for lightweight breast tumor segmentation. Concretely, we design a double-teacher model to represent the fine-grained feature of breast ultrasound according to different semantic feature realignments of benign and malignant breast tumors. Specifically, we leverage the bottleneck architecture to reconstruct the original Attention U-Net. It is regarded as a lightweight student model named Simplified U-Net. Then, the prior knowledge of benign and malignant categories is utilized to design the teacher network combined dual-path joint knowledge distillation, which distills the knowledge from cumbersome benign and malignant teachers to a lightweight student model. Extensive experiments conducted on breast ultrasound images (Dataset BUSI) and Breast Ultrasound Dataset B (Dataset B) datasets demonstrate that LightBTSeg outperforms various counterparts.

articleTitle: A Virtual-Physical Interaction Framework for Mobile Robotics Testbeds
abstract: Mobile robotics research testbeds play a crucial role in verifying the effectiveness of the robot hardware architecture and control policies, among other aspects. However, physical testbeds are costly and less safe, while virtual testbeds are subject to limitations in simulation algorithms, resulting in lower accuracy. This paper introduces a virtual-physical interaction framework in the context of mobile robotics research testbed that leverages the concept of virtual-physical modeling in digital twins. The framework constructs a bridge that connects the traditional physical hardware platform and virtual simulation testbeds, providing scalable, interactive, high-fidelity simulation and tests on both sides. The proposed framework enables the convenient integration of various applications and experimental scenarios, and it is capable of continuously optimizing the virtual testbed using data from both the virtual and physical testbeds. Robots in the virtual testbed optimized by the proposed framework exhibit dynamics more similar to their physical testbed counterparts, thereby reducing the reality gap to 5%-8% of the maximum value. Furthermore, the proposed framework is generalizable, as the optimized virtual system can perform control tasks that are of a different type but within the same category as the tasks that generated the dataset while maintaining a low reality gap. Extensive experiments demonstrate the performance of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Superheat Degree Category Refinement of Aluminum Electrolysis Cell Using Flame Hole Video Apparent Spatio-Temporal Feature Clustering Network
abstract: Flame hole video (FHV) is an important data source that can effectively evaluate the energy balance (superheat degree category, SDC) of modern aluminum electrolysis cell. This data source has time-varying apparent spatio-temporal features, and exists the issues of high acquisition cost, small amount of data, manual labeling, and few label categories. To address the above issues, a flame hole video apparent spatio-temporal feature clustering network (ASTFCN) is proposed for superheat degree category refinement of aluminum electrolysis cell (SDCRAEC). Firstly, the method of dividing FHV into multiple spatial region nodes is proposed to better capture detailed apparent spatial features. Secondly, the Gaussian filter and the DoG filter are respectively used to obtain the apparent low-frequency features and the apparent high-frequency features of each frame in the spatial-regional node, and the feature dimension of the spatial-regional node is reduced to 1-dimension by 3D convolution and pooling operations. Then, the apparent features obtained by matrix splicing of low-frequency features and high-frequency features are used as the input of the structural deep clustering network (SDCN) to perform the FHV clustering task and achieve the superheat degree category refinement. Finally, experiments are conducted on an actual industrial aluminum electrolysis FHV dataset, and the clustering results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Map Completion for SLAM Systems Based on Neural Radiance Field
abstract: Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) systems aim to enhance the capabilities of robots in complex environments by building maps of unknown surroundings. Creating a dense and detailed map can significantly improve the robot's perception of the environment and enable it to perform more challenging tasks. However, traditional algorithms often struggle to balance localization, tracking, and mapping. Recently, neural radiance fields-based 3D reconstruction has emerged as an efficient and accurate method, offering a potential solution for map completion in SLAM systems. In our work, we integrate neural radiance fields with the SLAM system, providing a real-time solution for tracking, localization, and initial scene reconstruction, along with offline map completion. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach sacrifices some tracking accuracy to achieve complete map construction.

articleTitle: Hidden Danger Detection Around Power Transmission Lines Based on Improved YOLOv5
abstract: Timely detection of hidden dangers around power transmission lines is particularly important in the power field. With various challenges such as few data, large image sizes, complex backgrounds, and small object scales, accurate detection of hidden dangers around power transmission lines remains difficult. In this paper, we propose an effective approach to hidden danger detection around power transmission lines by improving YOLOv5. Firstly, by converting global detection to local detection, an Equal Size Slicing Module (ESSM) is presented to increase the detection ability of small objects and the generalization ability of the model. Secondly, an Adaptive Small Object Enhancement Module (ASOEM) that integrates feature elimination, intact information fusion, attention mechanism, and adaptive feature fusion is used to improve the localization and recognition performance of small objects. We build a dataset of hidden dangers around power transmission lines and verify the validity of our approach on this dataset. The experimental results show that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art ones. In particular, compared with YOLOv5, the mAP of proposed approach is improved by 8.4%.

articleTitle: Industrial Control System Modeling Based on Knowledge Graph
abstract: In the context of “Industry 4.0”, the integration of industrialization and informatization has deepened. Industrial Control System (ICS) is more based on heterogeneous data and knowledge integration for cyber-physical production, and the openness and integration make ICS more vulnerable to attacks. Since ICS directly controls physical equipment, a breach could cause an irreversible disaster. It is especially important to have a security defense for ICS. Existing research has found that modeling the cyber and physical information of ICS helps security defense. Knowledge graphs, as an important technique of knowledge modeling, can mine the potential relationship between data and organize information effectively. Modeling ICS with knowledge graphs suits its data-intensive and relationship-rich requirements. This work proposes a knowledge graph-based information modeling for ICS, which focuses on ICS's monitoring and control layers and considers the relationships between network and physical devices. The model provides support for the subsequent safe operation and defense of ICS. A specific example study of the Secure Water Treatment for water treatment systems illustrates the potential for modeling ICS using knowledge graphs.

articleTitle: Short-Term Prediction of Energy Consumption in Smart Buildings Based on AC-BiLSTM
abstract: To enhance the accuracy of short-term energy consumption forecasting for smart buildings and fully utilize their temporal characteristics and influencing factors, this paper proposes an CNN-BiLSTM-Attention (AC-BiLSTM) based framework. Firstly, the Prophet algorithm is employed to perform feature analysis on building energy consumption data. The obtained features at various time scales are then correlated with environmental factors such as temperature and atmospheric pressure using the Maximum Information Coefficient. Subsequently, the Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS (STL) is utilized to transform the complex original data into more stationary components. These strongly correlated factors and energy consumption data components are collectively utilized as inputs to the AC-BiLSTM network, which incorporates the attention mechanism of neural networks to fully exploit energy consumption features. Experiments are conducted on an open dataset of building energy consumption, and the results demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed model. Compared to other algorithms, the proposed approach exhibits significant improvements in multiple evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Online Data-Driven Event-Triggered Control for Heterogeneous Nonlinear Platoons Under Communication Constraints
abstract: In this study, we propose an online learning data-driven event-triggered control approach for the synthesis of control in heterogeneous nonlinear platoons under communication constraints. The system is estimated using a Gaussian process(GPs) regression based on a squared exponential(SE) kernel, while the controller design is implemented through feedback linearization. Furthermore, event-triggered conditions are constructed to guarantee system stability. Through simulation comparisons with time-triggered control utilizing fixed sampling, the superiority of the proposed method is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Novel Comprehensive Similarity Measure for Networked Operation Sequences
abstract: With the increasing development of knowledge-based technologies in manufacturing, it has been shown as a promising way to solve problems by reusing related knowledge discovered from existing data. When it comes to computer aided process planning (CAPP), however, most efforts have been done on serial operation sequences, ignoring the urgent and practical requirement of networked operation sequences, which can provide more flexible process options. Therefore, we propose a novel comprehensive similarity measure for networked operation sequences in this paper. First, the information embedded in the networked operation sequences is deeply analyzed and classified into four types: operation similarity, precedence relationship, number of common operations, and structure similarity. For each kind of information, an intermediate similarity measure is present considering the specific information need of the networked operation sequence. Then, principal component analysis (PCA) is used to obtain a comprehensive metric without repeatedly calculating the common part of the aforementioned four types of information. Finally, the performance of this proposed measure is evaluated by a numerical illustration, in which a data set of different similarity cases is also built.

articleTitle: Pursuit-Evasion Game of Multiple Unmannd Surface Vessels in Partially Observable Environments
abstract: The pursuit-evasion game for unmanned surface vessels (USVs) is a topic of great interest in the field of ocean engineering. Most of the previous studies only focused on ideal scenarios with fully observable environments, which are beyond the practical applications. In this paper, we present a reinforcement learning (RL) model for the real marine environment including signal shielding regions, depots, and obstacles. Suppose in the signal shielding regions, the vessels' position information is unknown to each other except for the leader pursuer, and the new environment model is partially observable to ordinary USVs. Then, a distributed multi-agent RL algorithm is proposed and a leader-follower implicit communication mechanism to train the pursuer's strategy is introduced. Weighting the distance, number of captures, and other relevant parameters, a new reward function of the pursuit-evasion game is designed to optimize the pursuit strategy continuously. As shown in the simulation results, the ordinary pursuers can predict the movement direction and capture points of the evader with high accuracy, even when it is in the signal shielding area. This is due to the implicit communication with the leader pursuer in the partially observable environment, which can also effectively optimize the pursuit strategy in the new environment.

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of Carrier Airwake and Aircraft Dynamics Using Invariant Extended Kalman Filter
abstract: This paper presents a novel state estimator for carrier-based aircraft that utilizes the theory of invariant observers. By integrating the carrier-based aircraft's position, attitude, velocity, and wind speed onto the Lie group, the proposed estimator can combine information from sensors such as the pitot tube and IMU, and use the Right-Invariant Extended Kalman Filter to provide accurate and real-time estimates of the aircraft's attitude, speed, and wind speed during landing. To further enhance estimation accuracy, information from the GNSS is incorporated, and the state variables are estimated using a robust and accurate Left-Invariant Extended Kalman Filter. The use of a federated filtering approach to combine the estimation results from different sensors enhances the accuracy and reliability of the estimation results. The effectiveness of the proposed estimation method is demonstrated through a detailed theoretical analysis, while extensive simulation experiments validate its superior performance.

articleTitle: Indoor Temperature and Humidity Control System Based on Transfer Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: When adjusting the temperature and humidity of multiple rooms simultaneously, the training process can be time-consuming. To address this issue, we propose an indoor temper-ature and humidity control system based on multi-agent transfer deep reinforcement learning. This approach combines transfer learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning to enhance the adaptability and efficiency of the indoor climate control system. Each agent controls an air inlet, achieving indoor temperature and humidity control through multi-agent cooperation. Transfer learning is employed to transfer knowledge learned from a source domain to the target domain, which can significantly reduce the amount of data required for learning and improve the control sys-tem's performance in the target domain. The results demonstrate that the multi-agent transfer deep reinforcement learning-based control system reduces adjustment time and energy consumption by 95% compared to direct control, with a 14.4% and 15.1% improvement in temperature and humidity accuracy, respectively, and a 6.2% and 3.3% improvement in uniformity. This approach holds considerable potential for enhancing the performance and energy efficiency of indoor temperature and humidity control systems in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Penetration Testing Framework for TSN Industrial Control Systems
abstract: Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN), the next generation of deterministic Ethernet communications, is propelling industrial control systems to new higher levels. However, since TSN industrial control systems face security difficulties such as “low vulnerability mining and low device protection”, penetration testing of TSN industrial control systems is essential. The paper presents a framework for penetration testing TSN industrial control systems. Based on traditional penetration testing, the proposed framework tests the system across its entire life cycle by thoroughly studying the TSN industrial control system and mining possible vulnerabilities. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework can conclude the testing of extranet and intranet attacks, which validates the overall system security and confirms the practicality of the framework.

articleTitle: Control Method for Desorption Tower Liquid Level in Fluidized Catalytic Cracking Based on LESO-DMC
abstract: Fluidized catalytic cracking (FCC) units are crucial equipment in the petroleum refining process, and the level of control directly impacts product quality and yield. To improve the control level of the desorption tower in FCC, this paper proposes a dynamic matrix control (DMC) approach based on the active disturbance rejection strategy. Based on DMC, a linear extended state observer (LESO) is constructed to compensate for model plant mismatch (MPM) and unknown disturbances. The observer bandwidth parameters are determined to optimize robustness, enabling the implementation of active disturbance rejection model predictive control in FCC units. A comparative experimental study is conducted, comparing the proposed method with the traditional DMC approach that does not account for uncertainties and disturbances. The impact of different disturbances on the control strategy is discussed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits superior control performance and stronger disturbance rejection capability for the liquid level in the desorption tower of the FCC unit.

articleTitle: Modelling and Control of Timed Event Graphs with Shared Resource in Dioids
abstract: The purpose of this work is modelling and control of a timed discrete event system with shared resources under dioids algebraic structures, i.e, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}_{max}$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{Z}_{min}$</tex> (also denoted as (max,+) or (min,+)). Conflicting Timed Event Graphs (CTEG) considered in this paper is a class of timed Petri net, which can exhibit phenomena such as parallelism, synchronization, and resources sharing, whose behavior can be breezily described in the form of dioids algebraic by using a switching model method. By using the residuation theory and open-loop control laws, control methods that can achieve a desired system performance are proposed. And in the open-loop control strategy, two kinds of constraints are considered respectively. An example is utilized to verify the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Review of Human Activity Recognition Based on Millimeter-Wave Radar
abstract: With the fast development of radar technology, millimeter-wave radar has gained widespread attention in the field of medical and healthcare research and applications. Due to the technological advantages in single-chip integration and cost control, millimeter-wave radar has emerged as an ideal choice in the field of human activity recognition. This paper first introduces the fundamental theory of millimeter-wave radar and information fusion. Secondly, it systematically reviews recent research on human activity recognition based on millimeter-wave radar technology. Thirdly, a comparison is drawn between unimodal perception methods and multi-modal information fusion approaches for human activity recognition. Finally, the challenges and future development trends of millimeter-wave radar in the domain of human activity recognition are outlined.

articleTitle: Spatial and Color Information-Based Foreign Object Attachment Detection and Device-Foreign Object Segmentation Method
abstract: This paper proposes a method for foreign object detection and equipment-foreign object segmentation based on spatial and color information, with the context of intelligent inspection in substations. The method addresses the challenge of accurately locating foreign objects, which cannot be reliably achieved using existing image-based approaches, by integrating multi-source sensor information at the edge of the inspection device. The proposed method, when combined with inspection robots, enables automated foreign object removal. The approach starts by capturing multiple frames of three-dimensional point cloud data using point cloud and visual acquisition devices. Subsequently, processes such as stitching, downsampling, and extraction of the main point cloud are performed. The PointN et framework is then utilized to fuse spatial and color modalities of the point cloud to predict the occurrence of foreign object attachments and perform segmentation on the main point cloud. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through a case study involving foreign object detection and segmentation on power lines. Compared to detection and segmentation methods based on single-frame data and single position information, the proposed approach achieves higher accuracy in the segmentation task.

articleTitle: Cloud-Native Based Task Scheduling and Resource Allocation for Internet of Vehicles
abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) technology has been introduced to the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) to provide the sufficient computing resource. However, designing an efficient task offloading and resource allocation strategy in a distributed MEC system is challenging. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cloud-native based task scheduling and resource allocation strategy. First, we introduce the cloud-native based Vehicular Edge Computing Framework (CVEF), which ensures fast task response and efficient system execution through the collaboration of multiple edge clusters. Next, we jointly formulate task scheduling and resource allocation to minimize total task execution latency and energy consumption, taking into account network features, task properties, microservice characteristics, and computation resource constraints of the cluster. Finally, we model the problem as a Markov game and design a MADDPG based adaptive task scheduling and resource allocation algorithm, where the edge clusters make decisions in a decentralized manner. Numerical simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed solution in reducing time and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Atten-ganCV: An End-to-End Close-Coupled Image-Generating Cross-View Network
abstract: Cross-view geo-localization aims to match the query input ground-view image and the aerial-view images in the reference dataset one by one to determine the ground image's geographic location. This research is extremely challenging because the variation of the observation angle between cross-view images brings about great geometric appearance differences between image pairs. Nowadays, the introduction of generative networks into matching models has been shown to work well on the CVUSA (Cross-View USA) dataset, and the latest models clarify the paradigm of end-to-end generative cross-view image matching methods. However, this result relies on an assumption on the dataset: for all query input ground images, there must exist a reference aerial image that is exactly centered on the location of that image, which is clearly not consistent with real-world application scenarios; and the performance of state-of-the-art generative models degrades significantly when departing from this assumption of center alignment. To address this problem, this paper provides a generative model (atten-ganCV) for non-center-aligned datasets. This model feeds the query ground image directly into a generative adversarial network to obtain a generated aerial view image, where the generator atten-UNet innovatively introduces an attention mechanism. Then, model matches the synthesized image with the real aerial image in the reference dataset one by one, and finally obtains the matching result with the highest similarity, thus determining the geographic location of the query input. The model is tested on both the center-aligned CVUSA dataset and the non-center-aligned VIGOR (Cross-view Image Geo-localization beyond One-to-one Retrieval) dataset. In the VIGOR dataset, this model achieves approximately the same accuracy as the state-of-the-art model with 3 times the inference speed.

articleTitle: Double-loop Human-Robot Shared Control for Trajectory Tracking of an Underwater Robot
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of achieving a compromise between tracking a desired trajectory and responding to a human operator's command for a remotely operated underwater robot. The proposed human-robot shared control scheme is structured as a double-loop system, comprising a kinematic controller and a dynamic controller. The outer-loop kinematic controller incorporates the control commands provided by the human operator. To enable a rapid and smooth transition between trajectory tracking and human command following, we employ a convex blending law that uses the human intent measure to adjust the weight of human input and the automatic control signal. The inner-loop dynamic controller tracks velocity reference in the presence of significant system uncertainties, external disturbances, and limitations in actuator saturation. The sparse online Gaussian process technique is leveraged to learn and compensate for unknown dynamics. By integrating the posterior means and variances into an integral sliding mode control framework, the designed dynamic controller ensures asymptotic convergence of velocity tracking errors with a speci-fied probability. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed shared-control method.

articleTitle: Minimizing the Number of Leaders in Impulsive Multi-Agent Systems Under Switching Topologies
abstract: In this paper, the leader selection problem is studied for impulsive general linear multi-agent systems under switching topologies, which minimizes the number of leaders subject to the consensus tracking performance. First, a consensus criterion for the studied multi-agent systems is derived. Second, leader selection metrics are established via the submodular optimization technique according to the proposed criterion. Third, a leader selection scheme is presented, with a polynomial-time algorithm that returns candidate leader sets. Finally, the effectiveness of the developed leader selection scheme is verified by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Terrain-Adaptive Central Pattern Generators with Reinforcement Learning for Hexapod Locomotion
abstract: Inspired by biological motion generation, central pattern generators (CPGs) is frequently employed in legged robot locomotion control to produce natural gait pattern with low-dimensional control signals. However, the limited adaptability and stability over complex terrains hinder its application. To address this issue, this paper proposes a terrain-adaptive locomotion control method that incorporates deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework into CPG, where the CPG model is responsible for the generation of synchronized signals, providing basic locomotion gait, while DRL is integrated to enhance the adaptability of robot towards uneven terrains by adjusting the parameters of CPG mapping functions. The experiments conducted on the hexapod robot in Isaac Gym simulation environment demonstrated the superiority of the proposed method in terrain-adaptability, convergence rate and reward design complexity.

articleTitle: Research on Intrusion Detection Methods for Industrial Control Networks
abstract: Industrial control systems are an essential component of national infrastructure, widely used in industries such as energy, manufacturing, transportation and defense. They represent a critical resource that directly impacts the country's economy and people's livelihoods. Industrial control protocols serve as vital links, enabling real-time data exchange, data acquisition, parameter configuration, status monitoring, anomaly diagnosis, command issuance, and execution in control systems. The security of these protocols is closely related to the reliable and stable operation of industrial control systems. Detecting anomalies in industrial control networks is a crucial aspect of ensuring the stable operation and security of industrial automation systems. This paper focuses on researching methods for detecting anomalies in industrial control networks, with a primary emphasis on intrusion detection. We construct an industrial control network device fingerprint library based on behavioral patterns and combine ISSA and TWSVM algorithms to conduct research on intrusion detection methods in industrial control networks. The aim is to achieve functions such as secure monitoring, anomaly alerting, and threat warning for industrial control networks, and promote the application of this system in various industrial control industries.

articleTitle: Road Underground Target Detection in Ground Penetrating Radar Images Based on YOLO Models
abstract: Ground penetrating radar (GPR) is extensively employed for subsurface road target detection, offering benefits such as convenience, nondestructive testing, rapid data acquisition, and superior resolution. Despite these advantages, interpreting GPR data often depends on the expertise of professionals, resulting in low detection efficiency and low accuracy. To address these challenges, this study introduces an intelligent detection technique for GPR images, utilizing an enhanced YOLOv5 framework. First, considering the problems of the small amount of GPR image datasets and the unclear characteristics caused by the complex underground media, a Dense-C3 module is built by utilizing the structure of DenseNet to enhance the network's capability for extracting features. Subsequently, a channel and spatial hybrid attention module is introduced into the backbone for feature refinement and improving the efficiency. Finally, the multi-class focal loss function is devised to enhance the precision in cases of imbalanced sample classes. Experimental results show that the proposed model surpasses the original YOLOv5 model and various contemporary advanced models.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning-Based UAV Swarm Threat Perception and Evaluation Scheme in Air-Ground-Integrated Networks
abstract: With the advancement of 5G and artificial intelligence technologies, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) has emerged as crucial elements in modern warfare. However, their small size and slow speed make them difficult to detect and easily mistaken for birds or other flying objects, posing challenges for defenders to respond promptly. Moreover, existing methods for evaluating UAV threats heavily rely on subjective expert scoring, leading to inefficiency, uncertainty, and ambiguity. In this paper, we propose a comprehensive approach for UAV swarm threat perception and evaluation in integrated air-ground networks. By integrating historical observation data, we establish an indicator quantification method to evaluate the perception of UAV swarm threats. Initially, we employ convolutional neural networks for intent recognition, allowing for coarse-grained classification of enemy UAVs. Subsequently, we utilize transfer learning to in-corporate the trained intent recognition model into the threat evaluation framework, significantly enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of UAV threat evaluation. Experimental results confirm the superior performance of our UAV swarm threat perception and evaluation model compared to existing approaches.

articleTitle: P2W: Improving the Cognition of Object Wholeness for Weakly Supervised Object Detection
abstract: In the Weakly Supervised Object Detection (WSOD) task, the detector is trained solely by image-level labels, which significantly reduced the learning cost. However, in doing so, the model lacks precise instance-level supervision, which hinders its ability to accurately understand the full object structure. As a result, the model tends to focus on easily distinguishable local regions and make imprecise predictions. To address this problem, this paper proposed a Part to Whole (P2W) approach, consisting of two main components: the Hierarchical Relationship Extraction (HRE) module and the Object Component Integration (OCI) module. The HRE module synchronously extracts hierarchical relationships among proposals in conjunction with Selective Search. The OCI module uses these relations as clues to explore higher-level proposals for seeking core boxes and generating more complete object bounding boxes. With these bounding boxes as pseudo-labels, the model's understanding of object wholeness is enhanced and hence its performance will be better. Experimental result on the VOC 2007 reached 59.3% mAP, becoming the new state-of-the-art result. And the result on VOC 2012 reached 54.3% mAP, also closing to the state-of-the-art result.

articleTitle: A Unified On-Demand Driving Behavior Model Based on Automated Machine Learning (AutoML)
abstract: An ideal driving behavior model should be able to adapt to constantly changing environments. Most of the existing models are proposed for specific traffic scenarios, so their transferability is insufficient and they may fail to face inexhaustible and unknown scenarios in the real world. This paper proposes a unified model that innovatively combines the transformer model and Automated machine learning (AutoML), which addresses the challenge of handling out-of-domain scenarios through the designed search space and flexible automatic search strategies. A naturalistic driving dataset was used to validate the model's effectiveness. The results show that the proposed model can accurately predict driving behavior in both scenarios and scenes, with the average displacement error (ADE) being controlled within 0.17 meters and the final displacement error (FDE) being within 0.35 meters. More importantly, the key parameters of the unified on-demand driving behavior model that adapt to different environments are identified. Scenarios with clear patterns, such as car-following and lane-changing scenarios in the road segment scene, expect eight heads of attention or more, while too many heads are redundant for complex scenarios taking the roundabout as an example.

articleTitle: Structural Embedding Pre-Training for Deep Temporal Graph Learning
abstract: Thanks to the fact that many real-world data can be modeled as graph-structured data, graph deep learning is gradually attracting close attention from researchers. As an integral component of graph learning, temporal graph learning abandons the data format of adjacency matrices and instead utilizes interaction sequences to record and observe real-time changes in nodes. However, temporal graph learning both benefits from and is constrained by this approach. The data format of interaction sequences often leads temporal graph learning methods to focus only on the closest neighborhoods, making it difficult to capture high-order structural information and resulting in noticeable information loss. To ensure that temporal graph learning methods can consider both high-order structural information and maintain their flexibility, we propose SET, a temporal graph method which introduces Structural Embedding pre-training to enhance Temporal graph learning. Specifically, we achieve this by introducing classical methods to pre-train the data, generating node initialization embeddings that focus on high-order structural information.
