Furthermore, we constrain the model to optimize not only based on these embeddings but also to approach them as signals for data augmentation. By incorporating structurally embedded features through pre-training, we are able to obtain a broader receptive field without compromising model efficiency. We conducted experiments on several datasets, the experimental results validate the performance of our proposed method SET.

articleTitle: Mobile Photography Guidance System via Aesthetic Assessment
abstract: Mobile photography guidance has emerged as a highly regarded research area within the field of human-computer interaction. With the widespread adoption of smart-phones, individuals increasingly rely on the built-in cameras of their mobile devices for photography. However, the majority of users lack knowledge on how to capture aesthetically appealing photographs, which poses a significant challenge within the realm of human-computer interaction. To assist users in enhancing their photography skills, we designed a robust and dependable aesthetic evaluation model based on a large-scale dataset collection. This model has been deployed on mobile devices to create a photography software known as “AI Photography Tutor”. This mobile application offers real-time feedback, presenting information about light, color, composition, and overall aesthetic scores to guide users in capturing more artistically appealing photos. To evaluate the performance and guidance effectiveness of this application, we conducted comparative experiments with three other photography applications employing different guidance methodologies. We performed both subjective and objective analyses of the experimental results. The findings from these experiments demonstrate that our proposed photography guidance approach, along with the mobile application developed based on it, significantly enhances the photography skills of smartphone users. Furthermore, results from user satisfaction surveys indicate that “AI Photography Tutor” surpasses other applications in terms of interactivity, usability, applicability, improvement in photography results, and overall satisfaction. We believe that this innovative application holds the potential to become an essential tool for photography enthusiasts, offering robust support for users to capture higher-quality photos.

articleTitle: Asynchronous Containment Control of Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems Under Denial-Of-Service Attacks
abstract: The asynchronous containment control problem of second-order multi-agent systems under random Denial of Services(DoS) jamming attacks is investigated in this paper, where the attacks can destroy the dynamic transmission of information. The asynchrony means that each agent receives and updates state at its own clock independently. By applying a transformation strategy, the containment control under DoS attacks is equivalently transformed into a stability problem of the error system. Based on the graph theory and non-negative matrix theory, a sufficient condition is proposed to guarantee the achievement of containment control. Moreover, the condition is feasible in noisy communication. The numerical simulations are presented for both cases without and with white-noise disturbance finally.

articleTitle: FedCPSO: Federated Learning with Combined Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: The development of the Internet of Things (IoT) has allowed devices to collect massive amounts of data, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) provides the ability to analyze those data. Moreover, researchers adopt Distributed Machine Learning (DML) methods to train neural networks collaboratively using different users' data. However, DML suffers from privacy issues, and Federated Learning (FL) has been an effective solution. FL transfers the model instead of the data to protect privacy, but the trained models have low accuracies over local datasets due to statistical heterogeneity. Thus, personalized FL (pFL) algorithms have been proposed to handle such heterogeneous data distribution. However, the communication overhead in the pFL algorithms is significant as it requires transmitting additional information. Thus, we propose Federated Learning with Com-bined Particle Swarm Optimization (FedCPSO) in this paper. FedCPSO replaces the aggregation process of FL algorithms with PSO, and we design a velocity in PSO specifically for FL algorithms, using the best global model, the best client models, and the best neighbor models. In addition, we also implement magnitude pruning to reduce the communication volume. The experimental results illustrate that FedCPSO can reduce up to 50% communication volume while having less than a 2% accuracy drop compared with the State-of-the-art (SOTA) pFL algorithm.

articleTitle: Divide and Conquer in Video Anomaly Detection: A Comprehensive Review and New Approach
abstract: Video anomaly detection is a complex task, and the principle of “divide and conquer” is often regarded as an effective approach to tackling intricate issues. It's noteworthy that recent methods in video anomaly detection have revealed the application of the divide and conquer philosophy (albeit with distinct perspectives from traditional usage), yielding impressive outcomes. This paper systematically reviews these literatures from six dimensions, aiming to enhance the use of the divide and conquer strategy in video anomaly detection. Furthermore, based on the insights gained from this review, a novel approach is presented, which integrates human skeletal frameworks with video data analysis techniques. This method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the ShanghaiTech dataset, surpassing all existing advanced methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Online Optimization Control Method Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Large envelope deformable aircraft pose higher requirements for guidance and control technology, requiring control law parameters to be able to adaptively optimize online based on flight uncertainty and dynamically enhance flight control capabilities. At present, coefficient freezing is commonly used in engineering to design typical feature work points, but in large envelope flight, there are more and more feature work points, and traditional design methods are more complex and highly dependent on manual experience; On the other hand, traditional gain scheduling methods can only switch preset control laws based on flight status. Once the control laws are deployed, their performance is solidified, and their adaptive ability is relatively limited, making it impossible to perform online optimization. This article adopts deep reinforcement learning to design a universal PI state feedback control law parameter self-learning architecture, achieving autonomous learning of control law parameters at different working points; At the same time, the trained parameter adjustment network is deployed together with the control law, and online learning optimization of control law parameters is achieved during flight based on the control effect, enhancing adaptive ability. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method was verified using a specific pitch angle tracking control scenario as an example.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Command Attackers for Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the security of commands in cyber-physical systems at the supervisory control layer from an attacker's perspective. With observation capabilities comparable to the supervisor, the attacker can deliberately intercept and modify commands to disrupt the control logic and inflict damage or blockage upon the system. It is worth noting that we consider the issue of command security in systems that utilize event-based scheduling for the first time. In this system, sensors transmit readings at specific intervals, and the supervisor can consecutively send commands within these intervals. Within this context, we propose a novel architecture called the Command Attack Structure (CAS) within the framework of discrete event systems, which provides detailed insight into attack processes within the supervisory control layer. In addition, we also develop a CAS construction algorithm that guarantees the inclusion of all possible attacks. And the attacker can achieve the damage-infliction goal and the blocking-reachable goal by selecting specific attacks.

articleTitle: Driver Steering Intention Prediction Based on Fusion of EEG and Eye Movement Signals
abstract: With the development of intelligent driver assistance systems, the need to anticipate the driver's intentions earlier becomes urgent. Among them, steering serves as a common driver operation. In order to make the intelligent driver assistance system effective, a driver steering intention detection method is proposed. In this paper, three scenarios of driving steering experiments are designed to compare the effect of driver steering intention classification based on the fusion of EEG and eye-movement signals under two different fusion strategies, and the feasibility of driver steering intention detection based on the fusion of EEG and eye-movement signals at the data layer is verified.

articleTitle: Generating Adversarial Examples for White-Box Attacks Based on GAN
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) are susceptible to adversarial examples attack and generate error output. Traditional adversarial examples generation methods are generated from the perspective of optimization. Based on the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) framework, this paper proposes a method of adding an attentional mechanism and an autoencoder extractor to generate adversarial samples (SEAdvGAN). Firstly, the self-attention mechanism is introduced into the GAN framework of sample generation, so that the generator can generate and extract more important picture information, so as to generate more real samples. What's more the discriminator can discriminate the input pictures more effectively. Secondly, based on the GAN model, the text adds an autoencoder to extract potential variable features to reduce the loss between potential variable features and the output of the generator, constrains the quality of generated adversarial examples, and improves the success rate of attack. Experiments were carried out on MNIST and CIFAR-10 data sets to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: PointRCNN++: Towards More Accurate Two-Stage 3D Object Detection from Point Cloud
abstract: With significant potential in autonomous driving, and robotics, 3D object detection has garnered increasing attention among researchers. Leveraging its reliability in depth information, lidar stands out as one of the pivotal sensors in the realm of autonomous driving. PointRCNN, a point-based twostage object detector tailored for point cloud, has demonstrated commendable performance on many benchmarks though exhibiting certain limitations. Before being fed into neural network, raw point cloud undergoes down-sampling procedure, which potentially results in the loss of foreground points. Recognizing the non-uniform nature of point cloud distribution, we introduce an enhanced sampling approach termed distance bin-based FPS. This novel method adaptively adjusts the sampling rate based on the proximity of points, allocating lower rates for dense nearby points and higher rates for sparser distant points, in order to retain more foreground points within small or distant objects. Furthermore, we incorporate Point-Attention into the PointNet++ backbone to capture long-range relationships within point clouds. By combining the distance bin-based FPS and an enhanced backbone, our proposed model PointRCNN++ exhibits improved perceptual capabilities, facilitating more precise object detection. Experimental results on the KITTI dataset substantiate our model's effectiveness, showcasing a substantial performance enhancement over the baseline, thus validating the efficacy of our proposed enhancements.

articleTitle: Research on Mission Capability Testing and Evaluation System of UAV Swarm
abstract: According to the unique mission form of unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV) swarm, the elements of UAV swarm cooperating to complete missions are analyzed, and an index system for evaluating UAV swarm mission capability is proposed from two dimensions of autonomy capability and coordination capability, based on which the testing and evaluation algorithm for UAV swarm mission capability is proposed. According to the proposed index system and evaluation algorithm, a complete testing and evaluation process of swarm mission capability based on semi-physical simulation test is proposed, and a scenario generation system for constructing evaluation scenarios is presented. The proposed testing and evaluation system is verified by a semi-physical simulation example of UAV swarm, whose results show that the proposed testing and evaluation system is effective, and can accurately evaluate the mission capability of UAV swarm.

articleTitle: PNAT: A Petri Net based Analysis Tool for Discrete Event Systems
abstract: We develop a Java based software PNAT in our previous work to solve several basic problems of Petri nets modeling of discrete event systems. Advanced data structure and search algorithm are implemented such that the traditional analyses, e.g., reachability graph, can be achieved in an efficient way. Since then, a lot of analysis modules have been developed in this tool. Over the years, several new features are introduced based on different requirements. In this paper, we extend the functionality of PNAT in three aspects. The first is robustness analysis for failure-prone automated manufacturing systems. The second is new structure analysis for detecting deadlocks. The last is the extension of PNAT to handle uncontrollable and unobservable events.

articleTitle: Monitoring System of Robot Based on Digital Twin
abstract: This paper presents the monitoring system of robot based on digital twin. Digital twin technology is an innovative approach to create a virtual of robot system. The robot model based on digital twin is studied to mapping the entire system. The management and process of digital twin for robot is researched for realzing the robot digital twin system. The verification of robot digital twin technology is provided to improve operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Mission Capability Evaluation Testing System for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Swarm
abstract: There is currently a lack of evaluation methods and tools for evaluating the mission capability of unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV) swarm. To solve this problem, a semi-physical simulation evaluation test system is firstly proposed in this work. Then the evaluation framework is established based on evaluation indexes and algorithms. As a case study, the feasibility of this evaluation testing system is verified by using a three-UAV swarm performing city patrol search mission. The results show that the system possesses the capability of evaluating and testing UAV swarm mission capability.

articleTitle: Distributed Event-Triggered Control for DC Microgrids with Quantization Information
abstract: In this paper, DC micro grids with digital communication networks are taken into consideration, and a distributed event-triggered control strategy based on quantization information is proposed for accurate load current sharing in DC micro grids. According to the designed control strategy, each distributed generator (DG) sends the quantization information to its neighboring DGs only when a specific condition is triggered. As a result, the control signal is updated by discrete-time quantization information. It is analyzed by the Lyapunov stability method that accurate current sharing is achieved. An example of DC micro grids is used to verify the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Conflict-Free Dispatching Method for Aivs in Automated Container Terminals
abstract: This research proposes a dispatching approach that takes advantage of the precision capabilities of Automated Intelligent Vehicles (AIVs). The method bears the following features: (i) Improving transport efficiency; (ii) Planning conflict-free path for AIVs; (iii) Enabling a fast-dispatching plan generation. To evaluate the model, a microscopic simulation is conducted. The baseline adopted is a widely utilized method named First-Come-First-Serve (FCFS). Sensitivity analysis is conducted across various numbers of AIVs, Yard Cranes (YCs) distribution (demand distribution). The results show that performs consistently with various numbers of AIVs, and YCs distribution. The transport efficiency is enhanced up to 38.21%. The conflict probability is reduced within 1%. The solution time for 500 containers remains within 31 seconds. The method could serve for real-time dispatching of automated vehicles.

articleTitle: A Co-Simulation Framework for Distribution Network Analysis: Case Study of Hosting Capacity Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a co-simulation framework to analyze the distribution networks using two software (OpenDSS and MATLAB). The proposed framework is demonstrated using hosting capacity assessment as a case study, on an IEEE 123-node feeder. In addition, this paper also proposes a two-step approach for hosting capacity assessment in distribution networks. While the first step calculates the node-by-node hosting capacity, the second step multiplies the node-by-node capacity by a coefficient to calculate the network-level hosting capacity (i.e. considering all the candidate nodes can host distributed generation (e.g. rooftop PV systems) or extra demand (e.g. EV charging)). The analysis shows that hosting capacity varies based on the location of DG or load, and network topology. The presented co-simulation framework can be easily extended to perform any complex studies on modern distribution networks, and this framework can serve as a guideline to develop other co-simulation frameworks (e.g. PowerFactory with Python).

articleTitle: Depth-Based Lightweight Feature Fusion Network for Category-Level 6D Pose Estimation
abstract: Estimating the 6D object pose has attracted a quantity of research attention because it is significant for intelligence manufacturing, autonomous driving, and virtual reality. Previous works have focused on using complex network structures to improve the accuracy of pose estimation, ignoring real-time performance. In this paper, a lightweight and effective network is proposed for high-precision category-level 6D pose estimation based on depth image. Specifically, our network has three steps. Firstly, we use PointNet++ to extract the geometric features of the instance and the shape prior, respectively. Then, the extracted geometric features are input to the proposed lightweight feature fusion encoder. By doing so, the shape prior geometric features are introduced into the instance to make its shape information more reliable, and the geometric information of the instance is fused into the shape prior so that it can have a better generalization effect on different instances within a category. Finally, the normalized object coordinate space (NOCS) model is reconstructed according to the output of the feature fusion encoder, and the 6D object pose is solved by point cloud registration of the reconstructed NOCS model. The experimental results on the benchmark REAL275 and CAMERA25 datasets demonstrate that the proposed network achieves excellent performance using only depth image.

articleTitle: Channel-Wise Weighted SDAE for Pilot's Cognitive Workload Assessment
abstract: The complex aerial environment usually leads to overload of the pilot's cognitive workload, and thus leads to misoperation and impaires the task performance during the flight. Therefore, to improve the efficiency of human-machine coordination, it is meaningful to assess the pilot's cognitive workload. In this paper, a channel-wise weighted Stacked Denosing Auto Encoder (SDAE) is proposed, which extracts label-related features layer-by-layer from original EEG channels. Through the correlation analysis between features in each layer and labels, the important features are extracted and assigned weights wisely. Then, the channel-wise autoencoder is stacked as deep neural network. The proposed method is validated by the Electroencephalogram(EEG) signals when the participant is playing the Digital Combat Simulator(DCS) game, and the results indicate that channel-wise weighted SDAE saves training time and improves generalization ability for pilot's cognitive workload assessment.

articleTitle: A Novel Sparse Array for Non-Gaussian and Quasi-Stationary Sources
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel super sparse nested array with larger virtual array aperture. Specifically, the number of consecutive lags, the number of different lags and virtual array aperture are derived with quantitative evaluation and comparison, and the corresponding array composition parameters for optimized array structures are also provided. In the non-Gaussian and quasi-stationary scheme, the subspace method and the cumulant method are used for source characteristics. Some simulation results prove that the proposed array exhibits a superior performance.

articleTitle: Improved Control Strategy for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor System Based on Speed Sensorless Control
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) has the characteristics of high efficiency, large rotational inertia, and fast dynamic response. In recent years, the speed sensorless control technology of PMSM has significant advantages, such as reduced costs, smaller volume, and enhanced system anti-interference. Therefore, it has become a research hotspot. This article relies on a set of 50kw AC-DC-AC SiC inverter, adopts a composite control strategy, and focuses on the optimized control method of PMSM without speed sensors at low, medium and high speeds. With the help of high-performance digital signal processor DSP28335, the switching of two control methods can be achieved and the system experiment in the full speed domain is completed. The experimental results are basically consistent with the measured values of the speed encoder. This verifies the effectiveness and accuracy of the speed sensorless control algorithm which has good theoretical guidance significance for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-Based Dynamic Learning Control for Sampled-Data Strict-Feedback Systems Using Neural Networks
abstract: In this paper, the dynamic learning control problem of sampled-data strict-feedback nonlinear system is investigated. Initially, the consistency condition is derived from the exact and the approximate discrete-time model. At the same time, a sampled-data adaptive neural dynamic surface control method is presented to overcome non-causality issue by integrating the backstepping and digital first-order filter. A recursive approach is used to verify the stability and the recurrent property of the neural network (NN) input vectors, which guarantees the convergence of the NN estimated weights. Later, the disturbance observer-based neural network learning control scheme is developed using a combination of convergent weights and the disturbance observer. Finally, the benefits of the suggested strategy are verified by simulation results, including control performance, online computational effort, and robustness.

articleTitle: Research on Distributed Energy Storage Aggregation Considering Dynamic and Static Parameters
abstract: Under the background of high proportion of new energy connected to the distribution network, distributed energy storage participation in demand response has become an effective measure to improve the active support capability of new energy power generation and the level of safe and stable operation of the system. However, the direct participation of distributed energy storage with small capacity and large quantity in demand response will cause control difficulties and other problems. For this reason, the parameters of distributed energy storage system level and its own level are selected, and a distributed energy storage aggregation method based on K-means algorithm considering dynamic and static parameters is proposed. First, three static parameters of system stability, system reliability and responsiveness at the level of distributed energy storage connection system are considered for aggregation. Subsequently, on the basis of static parameter aggregation, the three dynamic parameters of energy storage output power, energy storage convergence time and energy storage dispatchable capacity at the level of distributed energy storage itself are considered for secondary aggregation. Finally, the effectiveness of the aggregation method is verified by evaluating the effect of dynamic parameter aggregation, which realizes the efficient aggregation of massive distributed energy storage.

articleTitle: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Pavement Crack Segmentation
abstract: Pavement crack segmentation based on images is important for detecting and repairing pavement cracks in a timely manner. In this paper, we collect a dataset consisting of 7000 pavement crack images, called PCSeg7000, to reflect real road scenarios. Then, we propose a pavement crack segmentation method based on the U-Net framework. Our method combines a strip-attention mechanism and a self-supervised pyramid network structure to the U-Net framework, enhancing crack feature extraction and fusion results. We report experiments on the PCSeg7000 dataset. Compared to the original U-Net method, our method achieves higher accuracy, recall, and F1-measure, with improvements of 1.60%, 0.47%, and 1.04%, respectively. Additionally, our method outperforms some existing methods on other public datasets.

articleTitle: Unifying Feature Space from Heterogeneous Images for Unsupervised Change Detection
abstract: Domain transformation is playing an increasingly important role in heterogeneous change detection. Existent methods, however, cannot guarantee the consistency of reconstructed feature spaces. To solve this issue, we propose an unsupervised change detection method based on the unification of feature space (UFS). First, we construct a convolutional autoencoder based on adaptive instance normalization to unify feature space. Then, we use fuzzy local information c-means to reduce the over-reliance on reconstructed features. Finally, we design a dynamic superpixel-based label assignment (DSLA) rule to increase the number of reliable pseudo-labels used to learn a binary classifier to obtain the CD results. Experimental results on heterogeneous datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of UFS.

articleTitle: Filter-Based Cascaded Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control for Uncertain Systems with High-Frequency Measurement Noise
abstract: The linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) method has been proven to be effective for overcoming various system with uncertainties, but its high-gain characteristic is very sensitive to the output noise. So for a class of uncertain nonlinear systems with high-frequency measurement noise, the amplification effect of LADRC on noise is first to be analyzed, and then a cascaded LADRC method based on engineering filter is proposed to realize filtering while compensating for amplitude loss and phase loss of the system output, which ensures the tracking accuracy of closed-loop system. Finally, the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method is verified by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-solution Problem for Unmanned Ships Path Planning Based on Improved Artificial Potential Field
abstract: Traditional Artificial Potential Field (TAPF) method can only work out a single solution when solving path planning problem. This paper proposes a method to obtain multiple solutions by reconstructing the potential field by means of a new repulsive function. Firstly, the attractive function is simplified to improve the unbalanced attraction in traditional potential field. Next, a line-obstacle model is introduced to modify the structure of the repulsive potential field. Finally, the path planning with multiple solutions can be achieved through a multi-round iterative strategy. After MATLAB simulations conducted, the results demonstrate that this strategy can achieve high success rates for multi-path planning in a single scenario, with smooth paths and strong robustness.

articleTitle: Siemens 1500 PLC-Based Continuous Production Process Control System for Emulsifiers
abstract: Taking the process device of continuous emulsifier production in a Chinese enterprise as the research object, the control process is analyzed in depth. The process consists of five sections, which are raw material loading section, pre-treatment section, main reaction section, exhaust gas condensation section and post-treatment section. On this basis, a PLC-based continuous production process control system of the emulsifier is designed to achieve the control, optimisation and monitoring functions in the continuous production process. Siemens S7-1500 series PLC was selected for the electronic control system and Siemens TP1900 Comport panel was selected for the upper computer. Through the fieldbus, data such as temperature, pressure, liquid level and flow rate at the site are interacted with the host computer, and the data in the production process is monitored and modified in real time, thus effectively responding to unexpected situations in the production process. The system takes advantage of safety, stability and accuracy to improve the production efficiency of emulsifiers and reduce wasted resources, and can be regarded as an important reference for the design of monitoring systems of the same type in this field.

articleTitle: Cloud Migration of High-Speed Railway CTC System
abstract: As cloud computing technology advances rapidly, various industries are evaluating the possibility of transitioning their systems to the cloud. This paper presents a case study on the cloud migration of high-speed railway centralized traffic control (CTC) systems, a critical component responsible for safe and efficient railway operations. In this study, we emphasize our contributions and originality in the following aspects: 1. Resource Utilization Enhancement: We have designed and im-plemented a high-availability cloud platform using OpenStack to promote resource utilization and facilitate resource sharing among different components of the high-speed railway signaling system. 2. Comprehensive Migration Details:Our paper provides a comprehensive overview of the migration process of the CTC system to the cloud platform. This includes intricate details about the high-availability cluster architecture, deployment procedures, and a thorough analysis of fault reconstruction performance. 3. Performance Enhancement: Through our study, we demonstrate that the proposed OpenStack-based cloud platform significantly enhances scalability, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness, all while upholding the essential reliability and safety standards required for railway operations. In conclusion, our work introduces a high-availability cloud platform for high-speed railway signaling systems based on OpenStack. This platform ensures the safe and dependable operation of railways, contributing to the ongoing evolution of cloud technology in critical infrastructure.

articleTitle: Research on Knowledge Graph Embedding Methods for Cement Clinker Pre-Decomposition Process
abstract: The pre-decomposition process is a crucial step in cement clinker production, which is influenced by numerous parameters. To gain a deeper understanding of the conditions that lead to different process states, it is necessary to explore the relationships among these factors. Knowledge graphs have emerged as a powerful technique for representing relationships between entities and have been applied to various real-world tasks such as disease diagnosis, recommendation systems, and traffic prediction. In this study, we propose a novel knowledge graph embedding model based on convolutional neural networks, designed specifically for the constructed pre-decomposition knowledge graph. This model aims to uncover hidden relationships within the knowledge graph and provide insights into the process.

articleTitle: Mixed Kernel Regularized K-Nearest Neighbor Based Weighted Twin Support Vector Regression for Nonparametric Modeling of Ship Maneuvering Motion
abstract: In this study, an innovative method, mixed kernel regularized k-nearest neighbor based weighted twin support vector regression (MRKNNWTSVR) is designed for modeling the maneuvering motion of ships. This method effectively integrates regularized k-nearest neighbor based weighted twin support vector regression (RKNNWTSVR) with a mixed kernel function, thereby facilitating the accurate identification of a nonparametric model for ship maneuvering. The mixed kernel function, combining the attributes of the radial basis and polynomial kernel functions, significantly enhances both the accuracy and the generalization. To further increase the model's accuracy, a parameter optimization strategy based on a dung beetle optimizer has been incorporated. The model's performance and generalization potential have been validated using the KVLCC2 ship model, with data sourced from the SIMMAN 2008 database. The results from these tests demonstrate the MRKNNWTSVR model's exceptional generalization ability and its overall efficacy.

articleTitle: A Lightweight and Efficient Network for Maritime Object Detection
abstract: Maritime object detection is a crucial task in the environmental perception of unmanned surface vehicles. It faces challenges such as complex backgrounds, varying object scales, and numerous small objects. To address these issues, we propose a lightweight network based on YOLOv7-tiny. Our proposed method introduces the P2 detection head with high resolution to improve small object detection, the parameter-free attention module SimAM for better object feature extraction in complex maritime backgrounds, and the CARAFE module to reduce the loss of feature information during upsampling. We conducted experiments on a self-made maritime object detection dataset, and our proposed model outperforms the original YOLOv7-tiny by 2.6% mAP@.5:.95, achieving a real-time inference speed of 101 FPS. Furthermore, our proposed model performs better than other lightweight models.

articleTitle: EEG Emotion Recognition Based on 4D Fusion Features and Coordinated Attention
abstract: Emotion recognition through EEG serves as a vital task within the realm of brain-computer interfaces (BCI). To improve recognition accuracy, this paper proposes an emotion recognition method based on 4D fusion features and coordinated attention mechanisms. First, the raw EEG signal undergoes a transformation, resulting in a 4D representation that encompasses frequency, space, and time, then a Convolutional Neural Network based on a Coordinated Attention (CACNN) mechanism is used to learn the frequency and spatial information in the 4D representation, and finally a long-time dependency in the 4D representation is extracted using a long short-term memory network (LSTM), and the classification results are output by the final layer of the LSTM. Our model achieves advanced performance on the single-subject DEAP dataset, with Arousal and Valence binary classification accuracies of 96.22 % and 95.75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>.

articleTitle: Cucker-Smale Flocking Control of Networked Agents Under Eavesdropping Attacks
abstract: In this study, the flocking control issue for a group of agents under eavesdropping attacks is investigated. It is assumed that there is an external eavesdropper, whose purpose is to infer the states (e.g., positions or velocities, etc.) of agents by eavesdropping on the data transmissions over the communication links between agents, causing information leakage from multi-agent systems. In order to prevent information leakage, a method of injecting noises is proposed, where time-varying noises satisfying zero-sum properties are added to the real transmission states of agents to form unreal states, so as to deceive the attacker. Based on the convergence technique of infinite products of sub-stochastic matrices, an algebraic condition is established to realize flocking behavior without revealing the information of agents. Finally, the obtained theoretical result is verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: An Attributed Graph Clustering Approach Based on Nearest Neighbor Graph
abstract: The traditional attribute graph clustering approaches suffer from low computation efficiency and poor accuracy problems. How to design a general attribute graph cluster method, which leverages both the attribute and structure characteristics, has become a new challenge. This paper proposes an attribute graph clustering algorithm based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> Nearest Neighbor(kNN) graph, called KAGC, which leverages both the traditional structured graph clustering method SCAN and kNN graph. KAGC performs a three-step fusion. Firstly, KAGC constructs a weighted graph based on the mixed similarity of attribute and structure, then clusters the nodes based on high similarity edges in DFS order, and finally merges the small clusters by joint strength. Experimental results demonstrate that the KAGC can effectively cluster the attribute graph and better balance the attribute and structural information of nodes.

articleTitle: Skeleton-Based Multi-Stream Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network for Indoor Scene Action Recognition
abstract: With the rapid advances in computer vision, human action recognition has gradually received attention, but the current methods still exhibit some problems in indoor environments. The human skeleton, as the framework of human motion, contains high-quality actional feature information, and the skeleton-based action recognition method effectively avoid the interference of interior background noise and has advantages in indoor action recognition. The outstanding effect of graph convolutional networks on graph structure data processing has led to its rapid development and wide application in skeleton-based action recognition. Second-order skeletal information also contains a large number of actional features but is not effectively utilized. The artificial predefined topology of the human skeleton map has limitations, and cannot reflect the interaction between limbs. To solve the above problems, this article designs an adaptive weighted multi-stream graph convolutional network (AM-GCN) based on skeletal information, using an attention mechanism to enhance the network's ability to extract actional features, and an adaptive layer to make the construction graph more flexible, incorporating second-order skeletal features through a dual-stream architecture. In this article, the NTU-RGB+D dataset has been used for the experiments, the results show that the method in this article has good results.

articleTitle: Image Restoration Based on Multi-Scale Feature Enhancement and Fusion
abstract: One of the most challenging issues in computer vision is image restoration with large-scale irregular missing patches. Considering existing image restoration methods do not adequately integrate structure and texture information, this causes the problem of structure distortion and texture blurring in the final generated image. This paper proposes a multi-scale feature enhancement and fusion image restoration network. Based on a dual-stream restoration network, a multi-scale augmented attention method is produced to capture multi-level semantic information in images and facilitates the fusion of structural and textural elements. In the feature fusion module, fast Fourier convolution is added to the processing of structure features to draw attention to edge features and enhance the contrast and clarity of the edges in the image. Numerous experiment results show that our method can effectively repair large-scale irregularly missing images in complex backgrounds, and metrics like peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity perform better than existing comparison techniques.

articleTitle: Visual Positioning System of Intelligent Robot Based on Improved Kalman Filter
abstract: The paper presents improved Kalman Filter for visual positioning of the robot. Firstly, the process of robot visual position system is studied in detail. Secondly, the improved Kalman Filter based on Cubature Kalman Filter is researched and used to fuse the data and obtain the positioning data with high precision. The experiments and simulations provide calibration coefficients for camera calibration and verify the improved Cubature Kalman Filter method can effectively improve the positioning accuracy of robot.

articleTitle: Automatic recognition and calculation of softwood ray height based on tangential section images by using YOLOv5
abstract: In order to achieve rapid acquisition, identification and measurement of the average ray height of softwood based on tangential section photographs, a new method is proposed. Firstly, labels the digital image of the softwood tangential section with the 100 magnification, that is, mark the rays and scales on the image, and establish the dataset; Secondly, the dataset is randomly divided into training set and validation set. YOLOv5s is used for model training to obtain the best target recognition model of rays and scale. The experimental results show that the model trained with YOLOv5s can achieve 93.5% accuracy, 95.6% recall and 96.7% average accuracy in the validation set; Thirdly, using the YOLOv5s trained model, a visual program for automatically calculating the ray height and obtaining the ray characteristics of softwood is designed, which lowered the threshold for wood identification workers to use such software.

articleTitle: Dynamic Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Under Composite Rules with Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In modern manufacturing industries, with the dramatic increase in uncertainty and complexity of production processes, dynamic scheduling methods are urgently needed. To address this issue, this paper proposes a scheduling method based on deep reinforcement learning. First, the DFJSP is modeled as a mark decision process, and five generic features are designed to normalize the states. Moreover, four composite scheduling rule is proposed to select the best scheduling solution by combining several single scheduling rules. Finally, a deep Q network algorithm with softmax action selection policy is constructed. The experimental results show that the scheduling effect of our method is significantly better than the rule-based heuristic algorithm and the meta-heuristic algorithm in the dynamically changing manufacturing environment.

articleTitle: Multi-Satellite Mission Planning Method for Dynamic Targets Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The autonomous mission planning problem of space targets tracking with multi-satellite is studied in this paper. For effective evaluation of different candidate tracking resource combinations, a tracking performance evaluation model based on GDOP is proposed firstly, then a tracking priorities evaluation model for maneuverable dynamic targets is designed to autonomous evaluate and update the planning priorities during the tracking. To solve the problem of conflict resolution of tracking resources scheduling, the reinforcement learning algorithm is applied, considering of restricted computation resources onboard. A pointer network is utilized as the strategy model, with the tracking targets and corresponding priorities, the tracking performance evaluation of each potential candidate tracking resources combinations as input tensors, and the tracking tasks allocation of multi-satellites will be inferenced by the network accordingly. The actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm is selected for training. It is shown that the algorithm proposed can formulate better planning strategies than the heuristic method, which reduces the mean tracking error by 21% during the whole tracking process.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-Triggered Control Under the Round-Robin Protocol for 2-D Continuous System in Roesser Model
abstract: In this work, we address the issue of event-triggered control under the Round-Robin protocol (RRP) for a specific class of 2-D continuous system in Roesser model that is subject to communication constraints. Our approach not only considers network congestion but also takes into account the problem of data collision. To reduce network overloads and save bandwidth, we propose a dynamic event-triggered scheme that determines whether a datum should be transmitted or not. Additionally, RRP is utilized to assign priority to the actuator at a given moment. Sufficient conditions of performance are established to ensure the considered system is stable. Moreover, an event-based control law under the RRP is constructed. The effective of the proposed methods are demonstrated by a numerical example in the end.

articleTitle: Identification of Breast Cancer Biomarkers Based on Improved Gene Co-Expression Analysis
abstract: Biomarkers of breast cancer was identified in this paper by an improved gene co-expression analysis. Biomarkers can be used for disease diagnosis and evaluate the safety and effectiveness of new therapies in the target population. Wilcoxon rank-sum test was proposed as an additional processing step to conventional gene co-expression analysis to improve gene data quality. This better model was used to process data of breast cancer in The Cancer Genome Atlas(TCGA) database. Three breast cancer markers, NME3, MRPS34 and MCRIP2, were found by this method. NME3 has been proved to be highly associated with breast cancer.

articleTitle: High-Order Iterative Learning Control for Distributed Parameter Systems Under Sensors/Actuators Networks
abstract: The iterative learning control (ILC) problem of distributed parameter systems in sensors/actuators networks is studied, and a high order ILC algorithm is proposed. The high order ILC algorithm feeds back the historical input and error according to different weights to achieve fast convergence. In this paper, the convergence condition of the system is obtained by strictly mathematical analysis. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Modeling and Control of Multi-Rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle System
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) is a kind of vehicle controlled by radio remote control apparatuses or automatic control devices. Compared with manned aerial vehicles, UAVs can carry out more complex and dangerous tasks and have been widely applied in the various fields, such as fire fighting, rescue, circuit inspection, aerial photography, and so on. In addition, in the military field, UAVs can perform reconnaissance, strike, and transport tasks, and play an essential role in the national defense. The unmanned multi-rotor crafts like quadrotor UAV and tilt-rotor UAV, which are capable of taking off and landing vertically, can install various devices to complete different tasks. There are three methods to connect the unmanned rotorcraft with the payload: connecting the payload rigidly, grabbing the payload by robot arms, and connecting the payload by a soft cable. In contrast to the other two connection methods, connecting the payload by a soft cable possesses the following advantages: the shape and size of the payload do not need to match that of the UAVs, and the UAVs can load and unload without landing.

articleTitle: Thermal Field Temperature Prediction Based on SPBO-SCN for Semiconductor Silicon Single Crystal Growth Process
abstract: The prediction of thermal field temperature is crucial for achieving diameter control and online quality inspection during the Czochralski silicon single crystal growth process. However, in practical industrial applications, it is difficult to directly measure the thermal field temperature in real time. To address this issue, this paper proposes a thermal field temperature prediction method based on SPBO-SCN. In this method, considering that the regularization parameter and scale factor of the Stochastic Configuration Networks (SCN) have a significant impact on the accuracy of the prediction outputs, an adaptive optimization algorithm is employed to select the model parameters of SCN, avoiding the subjectivity of manual parameter selection and the cost of trial and error. This approach constructs an SCN model with optimal parameter configuration to improve the accuracy of temperature prediction. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed temperature prediction model is tested based on actual operational data of semiconductor silicon single crystals, and the results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other modeling methods in terms of prediction accuracy and generalization performance.

articleTitle: Recommendation Algorithms against the Malicious Competition in the Market
abstract: In recent years, sequential recommendation tasks have made significant progress with the support of deep learning. Existing recommendation algorithms mainly rely on the historical interaction information between users and items to capture the sequential features of user behaviors and make precise personalized recommendations. However, malicious market competition often influences recommendation decisions through fake user behaviors in real-world scenarios. Previous research has often ignored whether the algorithms can maintain robustness against malicious attacks, which has led to a large gap between research and applications. In this work, we propose the DF-Rec model, which is a self-attentive neural structure with learnable filters for sequential recommendation tasks. The model introduces the concept of dynamic filters, Fourier transform-based filters that effectively achieve attenuation of user behavior data noise in the frequency domain, while allowing our model to have lower time complexity and learnable filters that are robustly adaptive, increasing the model flexibility without over-increasing the number of model parameters. Experiments on the public dataset RecSys Challenge 2017 show that our proposed approach outperforms the widely used CNN and transformer-based methods.

articleTitle: Automobile Emergency Collision Avoidance Control for Pedestrian Crossing Based on Deep Q-Learning
abstract: In urban roads, pedestrians crossing the road suddenly is very dangerous, with great uncertainty and complexity. At this time, the emergency collision avoidance control of vehicles is particularly important. Therefore an autonomous emergency collision avoidance control that leverages deep Q-learning (DQN) which can learn and adjust accordingly to make realtime braking decisions based on input from integrated image and sensors information was proposed. Considering the varying range of initial vehicle speed and the impact on pedestrian, the reward function is divided into several piecewise functions based on different stopping distances of ego-vehicle. This paper train the policy using the deep Q-learning with this reward function, in order to let the agent to learn how to get as close as possible to pedestrians and stop in place while avoiding collisions with them. Finally the experiments focus on a pedestrian crossing scenario in an urban road and shows that ego-vehicle not only prevents collisions, but also ensures a smooth change in brake application as the vehicle exits the emergency situation, much like human driving.

articleTitle: Foreign Fiber Classification Algorithm Based on Continuous Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
abstract: Aiming at the foreign fiber classification task of the same type in different fields in the cotton spinning industry scene, a foreign fiber classification method based on continuous unsupervised domain adaptation (Cotton Adaptation-Net, CAN for short) is proposed. The algorithm applies continuous learning combined with domain adaptation method to the cotton spinning industry scene, so that the model can continuously learn the data characteristics of the source domain and improve the generalization performance in the target domain. At the same time, the classification performance of the model is enhanced by increasing the attention mechanism and optimizing the convolution method. Experimental data show that the average accuracy rate of the algorithm reaches 82.46%, and the network predicts each picture time is about 0.52ms; compared with the three classic domain adaptation methods, the average accuracy rate is increased by 12.21 %, respectively, 4.96% and 3.25%. Therefore, the algorithm meets the requirements of foreign fiber classification tasks in different fields of the same type in industrial scenarios.

articleTitle: Sensorless Vector Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on EKF
abstract: This article takes permanent magnet synchronous motors as the research object. Usually, when we control the motor, we need to install sensors on the motor to obtain the dynamic information of the motor, such as the rotor speed and angle. However, in the actual working situation of the motor, many times we cannot install sensors, which requires us to use mathematical algorithms to estimate the dynamic information of the motor, Furthermore, it can replace the installation of sensors, which can greatly save costs. This article constructs a model for motor vector control

articleTitle: Proximal policy optimization with proportional-differential feedback for tracking control of unmanned surface vessel
abstract: Reinforcement learning has proven effective in guiding the motion of unmanned surface vessel (USV) without the need for intricate models or precise computations. In this paper, we propose a proximal policy optimization with proportional-differential feedback (PPO- PD) algorithm, building upon the proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework, to address the USV trajectory tracking control challenge. Drawing inspiration from the stability augmentation system (SAS) concept, we introduce a proportional-differential (PD) feedback controller into the environment prior to PPO controller training. This collaborative effort between PPO and PD optimizes the control strategy and enhances system convergence. Furthermore, a sim-ulation environment is set up based on the kinematic model of the USV. Experimental simulations demonstrate that the PPO-PD controller exhibits commendable performance in terms of tracking stability and robustness.

articleTitle: Research on two-degree-of-freedom PID control based on tracking differentiator
abstract: For production systems with input disturbance and output noise, a two-degree-of-freedom PID control method is proposed, which can effectively suppress the input disturbance of the system and ensure the controller setpoint tracking performance. The designed two-degree-of-freedom controller consists of a disturbance rejection controller and a setpoint tracking controller. The disturbance rejection controller consists of a PID controller based on the interference observer and the expectation model. The parameters of the setpoint tracking controller are tuned using a differential evolution algorithm (DE). At the same time, a tracking differentiator (TD) is used to process the output noise to suppress the effects of output measurement uncertainty. Finally, compared with the existing algorithms, the feasibility and superiority of the proposed algorithm are verified.

articleTitle: Spatio-Temporal Fusion Graph Convolutional Networks for Skeleton-Based Action Recognition
abstract: The analysis of human actions through skeletal patterns takes a prominent role in research. In contrast to methods utilizing RGB images or optical flow data for action recognition, skeletal information demonstrates intrinsic re-silience, unaffected by dynamic background, lighting variations, and other environmental factors. Hence, the exploration of action recognition through the human skeleton holds significant research merit. ST-GCN (Spatio-temporal Graph Convolutional Network) is an advanced performance model in human skeleton action recognition. ST-GCN mainly consists of temporal and graph convolution, which process data in two dimensions respectively, but these two parts are split when performing data processing, and the data are not effectively communicated with each other. In addressing this challenge, we introduce a spatio-temporal fusion module (STFM) that seamlessly integrates graph convolution and temporal convolution. This integration effectively merges temporal and spatial dimensions, facilitating improved communication between them. Through the incorporation of STFM into ST-GCN and its combination with dynamic topology, we formulated a spatio-temporal graph convolutional network for recognizing skeleton behaviors. Experimental findings on the NTU RGB+D and NTU RGB+D 120 datasets demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method in both recognition accuracy and model complexity when compared to mainstream behavior recognition approaches.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Tracking Control Scheme for a Quadrotor with Time-Varying External Disturbances
abstract: To solve the tracking issue of a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) with time-varying external disturbances, this paper presents the control method utilizing the fixed-time approach. First of all, the fixed-time disturbance observer (FxTDO) is designed to estimate external disturbance, the estimated time of disturbance is independent of initial condition and can be strictly guaranteed to be within a fixed upper bound. Secondly, a fixed-time sliding mode controller (FTSMC) is proposed for quadrotor. The fixed-time characteristics of the UAV closed-loop system is verified via the Lyapunov criterion. Finally, simulation cases and actual flight experiments illustrate the superiority and effectiveness of the constructed control strategy,

articleTitle: A Fixed-wing UAV Swarm Coverage Search Path Planning Method Based on Adaptive Evolutionary Ant Colony Algorithm
abstract: For the problem of fast dive search in unknown sea area. In this paper, a fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm coverage search path planning algorithm based on adaptive evolutionary ant colony algorithm is proposed. Firstly, a fixed-wing UAV kinematic model and an environment map model are established according to the mission requirements and environmental constraints. Then the search path planning of the fixed-wing UAV swarm is carried out by the adaptive evolutionary ant colony algorithm. The adaptive evolutionary ant colony algorithm has two methods of setting up the initial pheromone map and two ways of updating the search starting point, so there are four search strategies. The path planning simulation experiments are carried out using different shapes of mission sea area, the results show that the best search strategy is to not use a priori pheromone map and the search starting point is updated by selecting the historical optimal path starting point.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation with Binary Mask and Lightweight Network
abstract: Self-supervised scale-consistent depth estimation is crucial for monocular camera tracking and dense 3D reconstruction. Existing self-supervised depth estimation methods constrain the depth scale of adjacent video frames by minimizing their depth difference. However, these methods usually ignore the inherent depth difference caused by moving objects and occlusions. In this paper, we propose to adopt an effective consistency mask to reduce the impact of moving objects in both geometry consistency loss and photometric reprojection loss. Besides, we also present a lightweight model of DepthNet, LSC-Depth, to facilitate its deployment in resource-constrained devices. Experiments on the KITTI dataset are carried out to demonstrate that our model can perform on par with the SOTA scale-consistent depth estimation model with only 14% parameters.

articleTitle: Sampling Load Frequency Control of Time-Delay Power System Based on Warm-Up Grey Wolf Optimizer
abstract: Power system load frequency control (LFC) usually uses PID control to regulate the active power output of generator to maintain the stability of power grid frequency. LFC using wide area communication network for signal transmission is affected by transmission delay and data sampling, and its control performance may become worse. In this paper, the problem of LFC of power system under the influence of transmission delay and data sampling is discussed, and a parameter optimization strategy of PID based on Warm-up Grey Wolf Optimizer (WGWO) is proposed. A power system LFC model including transmission delay and data sampling is established, and then an LFC system PID parameter optimization strategy considering transmission delay and data sampling is designed based on WGWO. Finally, the proposed parameter optimization strategy is tested in a single-area power system LFC to verify the necessity of LFC considering transmission delay and data sampling and the superiority of WGWO in parameter optimization of LFC controller.

articleTitle: An Overhead Crane Anti-Swing Control Method Integrating Clustering Salp Swarm Algorithm and Fuzzy PID
abstract: To address the anti-swing problem in the overhead crane system, fuzzy PID is a common approach. However, the requirement for expert involvement in parameter configuration of fuzzy PID poses challenges for its widespread application. In order to address this issue, we introduce clustering operators into the enhancement of the Salp Swarm Algorithm. By integrating Clustering Salp Swarm Algorithm and fuzzy PID and conduct comparative experiments with other classical swarm intelligence algorithms, the proposed approach enables effective fuzzy control even in the absence of expert experience. Simulation validation of this method has been conducted in the overhead crane system.

articleTitle: Real-Time Precise Control Technology of Multidimensional and Stereoscopic High-Speed Photogrammetry System
abstract: During the flight test, the high speed photogrammetric stations are characterized by a large number, scattered distribution and separation of man and machine. In order to simultaneously acquire multi-target real-time measurement data in two separate areas of the takeoff and landing section, a distributed high-speed photography network system based on the multicast concept is proposed. An efficient trigger judgment algorithm for high-speed cameras with unassociated signals is designed, which can be used to acquire a variety of on-board and moving platform data in real time, and achieve real-time accurate and intelligent control of multi-dimensional stereoscopic high-speed photogrammetry system and real-time mass unloading of data by image processing. Through the real-time acquisition of multiple airborne and moving platform data, the real-time accurate and intelligent control of multi-dimensional stereoscopic high-speed photogrammetry system and real-time mass data unloading by image processing are achieved, realizing intelligent acquisition of test images from 8 different types of high-speed cameras. The false triggering rate of the measurement system is reduced to 0.76%, which effectively improves the work efficiency and ensures the accuracy and efficiency of flight test data.

articleTitle: Super-Twisting Control for Re-entry Rigid-Elastic Coupled Hypersonic Vehicles
abstract: A super-twisting control strategy is proposed to tackle the complex problem of attitude stabilization control for rigid-elastic coupled hypersonic vehicles experiencing significant aerodynamic perturbations. Initially, the elastic modes are treated as uncertain factors, leading to the construction of a control-oriented dynamic model. To design the attitude subsystem, a combination of a super-twisting algorithm and a non-singular terminal sliding mode is proposed. A first-order differentiator is introduced to address the “derivative explosion” issue commonly found in traditional control methods, thus eliminating the need for intricate differential computations. Moreover, a switching control strategy is integrated into the nonlinear feedback control law design, ensuring robust velocity tracking. Simulation results validate that the proposed control method surpasses conventional methods in both tracking performance and robustness.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Personalized Attention Mechanism for Federated Learning in Smart Grid Load Forecasting
abstract: In recent years, smart grids have increasingly be-come the lifeline of national economies. Faced with intermittent power generation and dynamic demand patterns, accurate load forecasting plays a critical role in power systems. Federated learning, with its benefits in privacy protection, has been grad-ually adopted in the field of load forecasting. However, the heterogeneity of data from different power users severely impacts the performance of the model. To achieve high accuracy in load forecasting and ensure data privacy protection, this paper proposes a personalized federated learning model, FedDuM, based on the attention mechanism and a two-layer structure. Firstly, the attention mechanism is used to capture the feature correlation among high-dimensional power load data. Secondly, a two-layer local model is designed on the client side, preserving a unique personalized attention layer for each client and using the other layers for global model aggregation, realizing the design of personalized modules. Finally, through simulation experiments, it is demonstrated that the proposed FedDuM model outperforms other federated learning models in the performance of smart grid load prediction, significantly improving the convergence speed while maintaining model accuracy.

articleTitle: An Optimal Circulating Current Injection Strategy to Suppress Capacitor Voltage Fluctuation and Minimize Capacitance Value of MMC Submodule
abstract: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) submodule capacitor voltage fluctuation causes several technical difficulties. Therefore., this paper establishes a comprehensive mathematical model for capacitor voltage fluctuation under second harmonic circulating current injection. This study proposes an injection approach that accounts for current restrictions on bridge arms., and the ideal amplitude and phase angle of the second harmonic circulating current is identified. The proposed method can significantly reduce the peak-to-peak voltage fluctuation of the submodule capacitor and successfully minimize the required submodule capacitance. Finally., a MATLAB/Simulink model of a three-phase inverter is constructed to confirm the feasibility of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Cooperative Strategy for Multi-Trains with Unknown Resistance Parameters and State Constraints
abstract: With the problem for dynamic change of train resistance parameters due to complex and varied environment in cooperative operation of high-speed trains, this paper proposes an adaptive cooperative control strategy for multi-trains with unknown train resistance parameters and state constraints. First, a multi-train model with unknown train resistance parameters is developed, and the state constraints are described and approximated. Then, an adaptive controller and the adaption laws are designed to overcome the uncertainty of train resistance parameters while realizing cooperative control of multiple trains. Finally, the stability of multi-train system is proved by using the Lyapunov function method. The experimental results show that the designed adaptive strategy can realize the cooperation of multiple trains with unknown resistance parameters.

articleTitle: RUL Prediction of Turbofan Engine Based on WGAN-Trans Under Small Samples
abstract: The prediction of the remaining useful life of the turbofan engine of an aircraft is a very important part of its PHM. With the arrival of the era of Big data, data driven RUL prediction methods are gradually emerging, however, in the actual industry, it is often difficult to collect sufficient data to predict the RUL under deep learning which means there will be a problem of small samples. Moreover, in the early stage of degradation, it is difficult to accurately classify the health status of equipment, resulting in the inability to provide early warning before the rapid degradation of equipment performance, thus losing the significance of developing maintenance strategies in advance. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a WGAN-Trans model, which expands the data set by improving the Gener-ative adversarial network, uses the one-dimensional Convolutionl Neural Network to divide the health state, and finally uses the Transformer model to predict the RUL, which is verified on the commercial aircraft turbofan engine data set provided by NASA. The results show that the proposed model has good performance.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Fading CKF-Based Method for Estimating the Line of Sight Rate with Strapdown Seeker
abstract: Due to the coupling effect of attitude angles, the extraction of line-of-sight angular rate in the terminal guidance stage of low-cost guided munitions is often inaccurate. To address this issue, this paper proposes an estimation method for line-of-sight angular rate based on adaptive fading CKF, which eliminates the coupling effect of body attitude angular rate. The mathematical model of the line-of-sight angle is established to derive the estimation model of the line-of-sight angular rate. Different from the basic method, this paper uses an adaptive fading CKF and introduce a fading factor based on residual sequence to adjust the predicted state covariance. In order to show the superiority of our proposed method, this paper conduct comparative simulation experiments with the line-of-sight angular rate estimation methods based on EKF and classical CKF, the results indicate that AF-CKF has better filtering performance.

articleTitle: Development of a Flexible Electronic Skin for Collaborative Robot Collision Detection
abstract: With the rapid development of industry 4.0 and intelligent factory, the safe cooperation between collaborative robot and workers is a challenge for robot development. The use of sensitive electronic skin to realize collision detection and actively control is a more practical and reliable solution. In this work, we propose an easily fabricated highly flexible, sensitive and adaptable electronic skin based on triboelectric nanogenerators, which is constructed from a BTO/Silicone nanocomposite with a fully embedded conductive sponge, which significantly enhances the dielectric permittivity and leads to a higher output performance and sensitivity. The experimental results demonstrated the capability of the electronic skin in detecting the collision velocities, forces and difference external object materials. It have provided an alternative solution for improving the safety, cooperativeness and intelligence of the robots in near future.

articleTitle: EEG-Based Cross-Subject Emotion Recognition Using GADF and CADAN
abstract: In recent years, EEG emotion recognition based on deep learning has received great attention. However, most of the EEG signals which input into deep learning models are unidimensional time series, resulting the inability to utilize the superiority of deep learning in images classification. To deal with this problem, the paper uses Gramian Angular Difference Field (GADF) to transform unidimensional EEG signals into two-dimensional images. Based on transfer learning, we adopt Domain Adaptation Network with Channel Attention (CADAN) consisting of channel attention mechanism and domain adaptation network for cross-subject emotion recognition task. Then, by using the leave-one-out method, the two-dimensional grayscale images obtained by GADF are divided into source and target domains. Then, these images are input into the CADAN model for cross-subject experiment. The experiment achieves the average accuracy of 0.6898 on the SEED dataset, indicating that the GADF _ CADAN method can effectively perform cross-subject task.

articleTitle: Stationary Base Self-Alignment of Inertial Navigation System Without Velocity Covariance Matrix
abstract: In the process of stationary base self-alignment in the inertial navigation system, covariance matrix of velocity noise is relatively hard to be determined properly in advance. In this paper an improved Kalman filter, termed as IKF-RCE, is applied to solve the engineering problem of error estimation when the covariance matrix of velocity noise is completely unknown during the process of self-alignment. Finally, the simulation experiment of self-alignment under stationary base conditions will be carried out based on Monte-Carlo method to verify that the error estimation sequence from IKF-RCE algorithm will be asymptotically convergent to the optimal from the ideal Kalman filter with exact statistical characteristics of velocity noise.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Adaptive Grasp Mechanism for Soft Gripper
abstract: This text introduces a new soft gripper with dual adaptive mechanisms, which exhibits good gripping adaptability for gripping objects with different shape and size parameters. The novel point of this soft gripper is that its mechanical structure can perform both passive and active adaptive gripping mechanisms. The soft gripper designed in this text does not rely on a complex mechanical structure, the single driving source for its hardware system is an electric putter, which therefore results in its overall structure that can be more easily designed to be very compact as compared to conventional soft grippers. In conclusion, the passive adaptation of the new structure of the passive rotating unit compensates for the shortcomings that exist in the active adaptation alone, the soft gripper can fully fit the grasping object in the contact position and has good grasping adaptability for a wide range of objects with varying geometries, and the greatest weight that can be gripped by the soft gripper is approximately 167 percent of its weight.

articleTitle: Easy One-Stream Transformer Tracker
abstract: To replace the traditional two-stream tracking paradigm, exploiting a one-stream tracking architecture has recently drawn extensive interest. But redundant computations occur as not all tokens are attentive in MHSA, introducing the noise brought by inattention information interaction and matching. To address the aforementioned issue, we introduce an easy one-stream transformer track(EOTrack), which reorganizes search tokens by retaining attentive ones and merging inattentive ones. This approach accelerates subsequent computations, enhancing the tracker's discrimination against the target by gradually mitigating noise. Additionally, we eliminate background information when updating templates without increasing training costs to provide diversified and high-quality positive samples for the tracker. Our designed easy one-stream framework is effective and concise, and its effectiveness has been proven on three datasets.

articleTitle: Multi-Time Infrared Image Generation Algorithm Based on DP-MAST Network
abstract: In comparison to visible light images, infrared images are less susceptible to factors like illumination and weather conditions, making them more suitable for applications in security, military, and various other fields. The utilization of infrared image generation techniques enables the rapid and cost-effective acquisition of a considerable number of simulated infrared images. Considering the characteristics of low contrast, low texture, weak information, and high noise in infrared images, this paper proposes a comprehensive strategy that includes a fusion of adaptive segmented linear transformation for image enhancement and arithmetic mean filtering for image denoising, in order to preprocessing infrared image data. Furthermore, an algorithm named Data Preprocessing-Arbitrary Style Transfer via Multi Adaptation Network (DP-MAST) is provided, based on a multi-adaptation network, to achieve the generation of multi-time infrared image data from a single time period to any multi-time periods. The experimental results show that compared to other image generation techniques, the similarity between the infrared images generated by DP-MAST and the real images has reached 91.4%.

articleTitle: Development of a YOLO-Based Model for Bird Droppings Occlusion Detection on Photovoltaic
abstract: The obstruction of bird droppings in photovoltaic power plants can cause phenomena such as hotspots on the solar panels and a decrease in power generation. To address the problem of slow detection rates and high false detection rates caused by bird droppings, which are often small targets, a bird droppings detection method called YOLOv8-NCS (YOLOv8-based method for bird droppings detection in photovoltaic arrays) is proposed. In order to achieve fast detection and localization of small targets in complex scenes, this algorithm first introduces the RFBNet feature extraction network on the basis of YOLOv8 to achieve simple and fast multi-scale feature fusion, thereby enhancing the detection ability of small targets. Secondly, to reduce the detection load of the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection system, the WIoU loss function is adopted. Finally, the NAM (non-local attention module) attention mechanism is introduced in the C2f module to better capture the dependencies between sequences and reduce background interference, thereby improving the ability to resist background interference. Experimental results show that compared to YOLOv5, YOLOv7, SSD, Faster-rcnn and CenterNet, the proposed YOLOv8-NCS achieves higher accuracy and detection speed on the bird droppings dataset in photovoltaic arrays, with precision and recall reaching 93.18% and 91.71% respectively.

articleTitle: Lightweight Driving Behavior Detection Algorithm Combined with YOLOv5 and Pruning Distillation
abstract: Irregular driving behavior exhibited by drivers could result in road traffic accidents, posing significant risks and potential dangers. The implementation of real-time detection systems for identifying irregular driving behavior emerges as a promising approach to address the problem effectively. In this paper, We design a light-weight irregular driving behavior detection algorithm combined with pruning distillation algorithm and integrate the proposed algorithm into the YOLOv5 model. Knowledge distillation is applied to the pruned model, facilitating fine-tuning and enhancing the accuracy of the model's detection capabilities for irregular driving behavior. To validate the feasibility of our algorithm in detecting irregular driving behavior, we conducted object detection experiments using three models: the original YOLOv5n algorithm, the pruned YOLOv5n-finetune-pruned, and the fused channel pruning and knowledge distillation YOLOv5n-distillation. The results demonstrate that the improved YOLOv5n-distillation algorithm achieved the remarkable P (98.6%) and R (98.9%) values, while reducing the model size by 20%. This reduction enables efficient deployment on small edge devices, without compromising the accuracy of detecting irregular driving behavior.
