articleTitle: Vehicle Following Model Using Dynamic Spacing Strategy Based on V2X
abstract: Addressing the limitations of the constant headway car-following model, this paper introduces a V2X-based dynamic headway car-following strategy. It considers both vehicle speeds and the preceding car's acceleration to enhance adaptability and flexibility. By utilizing real-time V2V communication, accurate preceding car data is obtained, improving data reliability and overall effectiveness. MATLAB/Simulink is employed to establish a vehicle dynamics model for verification. Experimental results demonstrate the strategy's improved performance across various acceleration and deceleration scenarios. Overall, this dynamic strategy surpasses the traditional constant headway approach, aligning better with real-world car following conditions. It allows flexible spacing adjustments for increased safety during rapid deceleration. With gentler speed changes, it reduces the maximum speed difference by 21.72%, enhancing driving comfort. Thus, this dynamic headway car-following strategy effectively addresses the challenges of low headway adjustment capability in complex scenarios.

articleTitle: Improving YOLOv7's Remote Sensing Image Object Detection
abstract: In order to address the challenge of poor detection accuracy concerning both dense and smaller targets within remote sensing images set against complex backgrounds, we propose an algorithm for target detection within remote sensing images utilizing an enhanced YOLOv7 framework. Initially, the ELAN module within the backbone segment is replaced with the cascade fusion Network, aiming to more effectively leverage the parameters within the backbone network. This augmentation enhances the model's aptitude for multi-scale feature representation. Subsequently, the EMA attention mechanism is introduced and integrated into the prediction location, serving to encode global contextual information and recalibrate channel weights within the features. This adjustment notably amplifies the feature representation capability. Experiments were conducted on the DIOR and NWPU VHR-10 datasets, in comparison with the YOLOv7 algorithm, the mAP exhibited improvements of 2.6% and 2.2% on these respective datasets. Moreover, detection accuracies were enhanced compared to several existing mainstream algorithms. The outcomes underscore the improved algorithm's effectiveness in substantially augmenting the detection accuracy of remote sensing image targets within complex backgrounds and diminishing instances of leakage and false detections in remote sensing targets.

articleTitle: Research on Algorithm of Building Overall Contour for Planar CAD Drawing
abstract: In the study of automatic modeling of building climbing frame based on building CAD plans, recognizing the building's contour is a very critical step. In order to realize the automatic recognition of building contour and realize from 2D building drawings to 3D building entities, this paper generates 3D Autodesk Revit model from building plan AutoCAD 2D graphic recognition of building contour to realize BIM reconstruction. On the basis of adaptive chunking algorithm, combined with convex packet algorithm and depth search algorithm, an algorithm based on the recognition and processing of straight line Line and multi-segmented line PolyLine in architectural CAD drawings is proposed, and the building contour is automatically acquired and generated into a 3D entity. The algorithm links the CAD drawings in Revit, reads the text information by connecting to the. dwg database with the help of Teigha library, filters the straight lines and polylines of the target layer, processes them, and obtains and stores the endpoint information. The points on the building contour are obtained by scanning and comparing the endpoint coordinates. Finally, all the points on the contour are connected in an orderly manner to get the 2D contour of the building. Finally, the contour is solidly stretched in Revit to get the 3D building solid, which lays a certain foundation for the subsequent research on the automatic generation of the 3D model of the climbing frame. The algorithm is of great significance for realizing the automatic modeling from AutoCAD 2D graphics to Revit 3D model and the automatic modeling of building climbing frame, which has strong application value in the field of computer-aided building construction design.

articleTitle: Research on Predicting Mud Flow Rate of Trailing Suction Dredger Based on PSO-LSTM
abstract: Aiming at the difficulty of applying the mathemati-cal model of the dredger with rake suction in actual engineering, a data-driven method was used to predict the mud flow rate in the pipeline. In order to improve the prediction accuracy, the offline construction data are preprocessed on the basis of the measurement data from the relevant sensors on the rake suction dredger. Then, the mud prediction model was established using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm for optimizing Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network and compared with LSTM network and BP neural network. The results show that the prediction performance of this method is better than that of LSTM network and BP neural network, which can accurately predict the mud flow rate and provide theoretical guidance for dredging operations.

articleTitle: Research on Screening and Evaluating Virtual Samples by Multi-Gaussian Process Regression Models
abstract: On the issue of virtual sample generation, researchers are now generally focusing on how to generate more virtual samples, while neglecting the evaluation and screening of virtual samples. In this work, a virtual sample evaluation and screening method based on multiple Gaussian process regression (GPR) is proposed. In this method, we firstly screen the virtual samples for outliers according to partial priori knowledge to get the candidate samples. Then the candidate samples are evaluated one by one according to the prediction results of multiple GPR models. Samples whose outputs were within the confidence range of the predicted outputs of one GPR model were regarded as passing the test of that model. In the screening stage, the candidate samples were screened according to the number of times they passed the tests and the actual modeling needs. By this way, we can get optimized virtual samples which can maintain or even improve the accuracy of prediction model with minimum number of virtual samples. Finally, the validity of this virtual sample screening method was verified on the dataset of extracting liquiritin by dual-frequency ultrasound.

articleTitle: Effect Exploration of the Spiking Neuron Property and Heterogeneity on Brain-Inspired Context-Dependent Learning
abstract: Brain-inspired computing uses the information processing method of human brain to process unstructured information in real time. It is an important way to artificial general intelligence. Spiking neural network (SNN), as the most representative network framework for brain-inspired computing, can realize advanced cognitive functions. Context-dependent learning is to retain the cognition of old knowledge when learning new knowledge, make flexible response to changing situational information in the environment, so as to achieve advanced cognitive functions. This study explores how neuron property and network structure heterogeneity affect SNN with winner-take-all mechanism. It directly determines the performance of context-dependent learning. This study shows that the property of neurons and the heterogeneity of network structure play a decisive role in the effectiveness of context-dependent learning. Results reveal the membrane capacitance and conductance affect the charging and discharging time of neuron cells and thus change the learning convergence rate. We summarize the effect of distance between the threshold of membrane potential and the resting potential on the overall accuracy of learning. Moreover, the addition of Gaussian noise to simulate the small fluctuations in the SNN shows that the heterogeneous network can improve the learning ability of neurons. This work can be potentially used in intelligent navigation, low-power edge devices, unmanned system, and neuro-robotics.

articleTitle: SAR Ship Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv7
abstract: A Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) SAR ship target detection algorithm with improved YOLOv7 is proposed for the problems of slow detection speed, high leakage rate, and poor recognition in complex scenes in SAR ship detection tasks. In the improved algorithm, ResNet50 with small size structure is used instead of the backbone feature extraction network of YOLOv7 to reduce the number of parameters of the network, and the Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) attention module is added to the feature fusion network to improve the feature expression capability of the network. The experimental results show that the improved algorithm achieves 91.7% accuracy (Precision, P), 82.5% recall (Recall, R), 24.64×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> number of parameters, and 39.27×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> floating point operations ( FLOPs) on the test set. Average Precision (mAP) is improved by 3.34% compared with YOLOv7. The number of parameters and FLOPs are reduced by 34.38% and 61.11%, respectively. The improved algorithm is used in real scene detection tasks. The improved algorithm effectively reduces the workload of detectors as well as the target miss detection rate and error detection rate, and shows good performance.

articleTitle: A PSO Inverse Kinematic Solution Algorithm for Dulcimer Music Robot Based on Improved Compliance Criterion
abstract: The dulcimer music robot is a heterogeneous robot that does not satisfy the Pieper criterion. In this paper, a PSO inverse solution algorithm based on the improved compliance criterion is developed and designed for the problem that the dulcimer music robot cannot find the inverse kinematic analytical solution, combining the robot arm joint constraints and aiming at smooth operation and achieving point accuracy, which is of great research significance to achieve fast and smooth tapping of the dulcimer music robot. The method was simulated in MATLAB for different trajectories. The experimental results show that the tracking trajectory curve is continuous and smooth, and the tracking error accuracy is kept within 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, which has good trajectory tracking performance. And the joint velocity fluctuation is small, which meets the requirement of robot motion stability.

articleTitle: Online Detection Method for Welding Profile Based on Optical Low-Coherence Technology
abstract: At present, there is a lack of effective methods for real-time detection of welding profile feature parameters in laser welding processes. In this paper, a method for detecting the appearance of weld seams based on optical low-coherence technology is proposed. Firstly, the three-dimensional point cloud information of the welding surface is obtained in real time using the fast measurement speed of optical low- coherence technology. Secondly, the three-dimensional contour of the weld seam point cloud is extracted, and the contour line and curve fitting are realized by an improved RANSAC algorithm and gradient descent algorithm, respectively. Finally, the feature equation is used to determine the feature points of the profile, and the feature parameters of the weld seam profile such as weld height and width are obtained. Experimental results show that the proposed method has both real-time and accuracy advantages, with a detection accuracy of up to O.004mm, satisfying industrial production requirements.

articleTitle: GIVFuse: Global Infrared-Visible Fusion Method Based on L1 Distance
abstract: Visible cameras frequently fall short of satisfying the visual requirements of individuals in low-light conditions partic-ularly at night. Considering the principle of thermal imaging in infrared cameras, a network framework that involves encoding, fusion, and decoding was proposed to fuse visible images and infrared images, leveraging the strengths of both modalities. The encoding network utilizes densely connected convolutional layers to globally extract features from visible images and infrared images. The proposed fusion network based on L1 distance, integrates complementary information and enhances contrast and texture details through its fusion capability by fusing globally extracted features from the encoder in three different dimensions. Finally, the decoding network reconstructs the fused global features to obtain the fused image. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate the proposed method achieves promising performance in both subjective and objective evaluations.

articleTitle: Warship Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images with Improved YOLOv5
abstract: Aiming at the task of detecting ships on the sea surface in remote sensing images, there are a lot of disturbances such as variable object sizes, cloud occlusion, complex image backgrounds, and different ship orientations, etc. In this paper, we propose a ship rotating object detection network based on the improved YOLOv5, which is constructed through the strategies of introducing Swin Transformer as a feature extraction network to enhance the feature extraction performance of the network, introducing a rotating detection head to realize the detection of the rotation angle, and modifying the network loss function to accelerate the convergence of the network. The network finally achieves a 71.7% map on ShipRSImageNet validation set, which is an improvement of 2.4% compared with the original network model. The network proposed in this paper solves the problem that the YOLOv5 algorithm is unable to detect rotating objects, and the network based on the self-attention mechanism is used to further enhance the ability to detect small objects. Finally, a ship object detector that can be used in real remote sensing satellite images is obtained.

articleTitle: Path Planning of Mobile Robot Based on Improved Artificial Potential Field Algorithm
abstract: The energy of mobile robots is limited, and the energy consumption must be optimized during task execution. However, the classical artificial potential field method has the problem of path oscillation under certain conditions such as narrow channels, which leads to extra energy consumption. In order to reduce this energy consumption, the advantages and disadvantages of the artificial potential field method are first introduced, and it is proposed to add a fuzzy controller to reduce the degree of oscillation of the path generated by the traditional artificial potential field method. In the simulation experiment, the total rotation angle of the mobile robot decreases from 13875° to 359° after the fuzzy controller is added.

articleTitle: Research on Wireless Sensor Network Localization Method for Real-Time System
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) inherently face constraints arising from limited computing power, data storage, and communication bandwidth. These inherent limitations necessitate innovative solutions. This study underscores the importance of ultrawideband technology, media access control, and routing protocols in the domain of WSNs. A key application of WSNs is real-time mine safety monitoring, which plays a critical role in preventing serious accidents by detecting hazardous areas. This research adopts a system-centric approach to real-time WSNs, rooted in an exhaustive literature review. It provides a comprehensive evaluation of the current WSN technology landscape, with a specific focus on unraveling the complexities of real-time system-oriented wireless sensor network technology. The investigation covers ultrawideband technology and medium access control within the real-time system paradigm, all supported by simulation verification. The simulations unequivocally confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method, making a significant contribution to the advancement of wireless sensor network technology, especially in real-time applications. This highlights the practical significance of the research.

articleTitle: Formation Control of Multi-Quadrotors Under Nonlinear and Disturbance Conditions
abstract: This article investigates the problem of robust control for multiple quadrotors formation with underactuation, high nonlinearitices, strong couplings, and disturbances. A distributed controller using the back-stepping approach and the robust compensation theory is designed to make multi-quadrotor fly in a fixed formation shape. The visualization simulations consist of four quadrotors are conducted through Rflysim platform and the results indicate that the proposed scheme has certain effectiveness.

articleTitle: Industrial Process Data Fault Detection Using Improved OCSVM
abstract: In this paper, a fault detection method based on One-Class Support Vector Machines(OCSVM) using im-proved particle swarm optimization to find optimal parame-ters is proposed. The feature recursion elimination support vector machine method is used to reduce unnecessary fea-tures, and the particle swarm algorithm combining particle mutation ideas and adaptive particle velocity improvement methods is used to optimize the relevant parameters of One-Class Support Vector Machines for fault detection. After being applied to the benchmark Tennessee Eastman problem dataset, the proposed algorithm is proved to have superior performance over One-Class Support Vector Machines with deterministic parameters,and it can take into account the detection effect of the training set and the test set.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer Based Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Attitude Control of a QUAV Using FNTSM
abstract: In this paper, a novel adaptive fault-tolerant controller based on fast non-singular terminal sliding mode (FNTSM) and a disturbance observer are developed for a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (QUAV) with external disturbance and actuator fault. Firstly, a fault-tolerant controller is devised to ensure QUAV's stability in flight even in the event of actuator fault. Subsequently, a finite-time disturbance observer is developed to offset the effects of disturbances, including external bounded disturbances and internal uncertainties in the system. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed control methods is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Squatting and Standing Motion of a Novel Bio-Inspired Single Robot Leg
abstract: The article introduces a novel bio-inspired compliant robot leg configuration and its motion controller. The paper is primarily divided into two parts for description. Firstly, the overall leg configuration design is presented, wherein a bio-inspired compliant robot leg driven by a brushless DC motor is constructed and analyzed by simulating the joint and tendon coordination of quadrupedal animals. Secondly, while many high-degree-of-freedom robots employ complex designs and intelligent controllers to mimic human motion, they may incur high costs and inefficiencies. This paper demonstrates the implementation of a simple analytical geometric controller on the robot leg, respectively, and selects squatting and standing motions as a preliminary study of bipedal locomotion. Additionally, the application of bio-inspired compliance principles in the mechanism design further enhances its practicality and adaptability.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of the Chiller Under Imbalanced Data Environment via Combining an Improved GAN and the Random Forest Algorithm
abstract: Fault diagnosis is crucial for chiller's safe operation. However, current methods neglect the imbalanced data issue of chiller, which results in reduced the precision of the minority fault patterns. In order to address this problem, an enhanced fault diagnosis method of chiller via an improved GAN method and random forest algorithm (IGAN-RF) is developed in our work. Firstly, a multi-head attention method is incorporated into the GAN method. The multi-head attention mechanism enables the generator to focus more on the key features of minority class samples during the generation process, which makes the generator generate high quality rebalanced fault pattern datasets. Then, the rebalanced training dataset obtained by the IGAN is used to train multiple decision trees using the random forest method. Finally, the chiller's fault pattern is determined using the majority voting method. The effectiveness of the IGAN-RF method under imbalanced data environments is confirmed through specific diagnostic results obtained from the ASHRAE RP-1043 datasets.

articleTitle: A Shortest Path Query Approach for Encrypted Graphs Based on Padding Dictionary Structure
abstract: Hybrid intelligence has emerged as an innovative approach that synergistically combines the strengths of human intelligence and artificial intelligence (AI) to address complex problems. In this paradigm, knowledge graphs play a pivotal role by supplying vital background information and contextual understanding to hybrid intelligence systems. However, due to limitations in local storage capacity, managing large-scale graph data often requires outsourcing to cloud servers. Nevertheless, the use of untrusted cloud servers poses a risk of potential user data leaks. To address these concerns, this paper presents an encryption scheme specifically designed to protect graph data, enabling queries involving intermediate nodes in the shortest path between two nodes within the graph. The proposed scheme ensures the privacy and security of outsourced data by employing a novel method that utilizes padding dictionary structure encryption. This method ensures strict limitations on the cloud server's capabilities, restricting it solely to query operations, it effectively prevents any compromise of user data or unauthorized access to sensitive information, users can securely store and process their graph data on servers, significantly reducing the potential risk of data leakage and unauthorized breaches. To validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed solution, practical experiments were conducted using real-world data.

articleTitle: Improved Active Disturbance Rejection Control of Inverted Pendulum Based on Differential Flatness
abstract: Aiming at the control problem of an underdriven inverted pendulum with instability and uncertain external disturbances, a novel improved active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) method based on differential flatness is proposed. Firstly, the non-minimum phase characteristics of the inverted pendulum model are established and analyzed. A flat output is found to overcome the input-output imbalance inherent in underdriven system. Secondly, to address the limitations of the fal function, an improved extended state observer based on a new nonlinear functions is proposed. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the improved performance in terms of tracking speed and accuracy. Furthermore, based on the improved extended state observer, an ADRC method is designed for the flat inverted pendulum system, enabling precise control of the cart displacement and pendulum angle with external disturbances. Finally, simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed observer and control strategies.

articleTitle: A Novel Adaptive Kalman Filter for Markov Jump Linear System with Unknown Measurement Loss Probability
abstract: This article studies the state estimation problem of Markov jump linear system (MJLS) subject to unknown measurement loss probability. Compare to the conventional single-mode method, the proposed method can adaptively estimate the state and measurement loss probability for MJLS. Specifically, under system dynamic and measurement loss are independent, the system states and the measurement loss probability are jointly inferred based on variational Bayesian (VB) inference. A simulated fermentation process verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method compared with the existing methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Attitude Control for Rigid Spacecraft With Disturbances and Uncertainties
abstract: This paper addresses the fault-tolerant control problem for rigid spacecraft with actuator failures, disturbances, and uncertainties. Firstly, a sliding mode variable is constructed to make the closed-loop system robust to unknown nonlinear terms including disturbances, uncertainties, and the drift fault. Secondly, a robust fault-tolerant control algorithm is developed to achieve stability when actuator failures occur. It should be noted that the proposed algorithm via the sign-like function and the adaptive method will not generate chattering. Finally, a simulation example illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed control policy.

articleTitle: Research on Probabilistic Production Simulation of Grid Connected Renewable Energy Generation with Flexibility Evaluation
abstract: For the probabilistic production simulation of the grid-connected renewable energy generation, the quantification of time-series and stochastic characteristic of renewable generation output are modeled. And then the flexibility of power system is described from two aspects: regulation capacity and regulation rate. Based these, a complete algorithm and analysis flow for probabilistic production simulation of grid connected renewable energy generation with flexibility evaluation and the corresponding case study are provided. The results show that this is a useful method, which can be used in the optimal plan and operation of renewable generation.

articleTitle: SGNet:A Lightweight Defect Detection Model for New Energy Vehicle Battery Current Collectors
abstract: The quality of the current collector, an essential component in new energy vehicle batteries, is crucial for battery performance and significantly impacts the safety of vehicle occupants. However, detecting defects in battery current collector in real-time industrial applications with limited computational resources poses a major challenge. To address this, our paper proposes SGNet (ShuffleNet V2 + G_GFPN), a lightweight model for current collector defect detection. SGNet utilizes ShuffleNet V2 as the backbone feature extraction network and a designed G_GFPN as the feature fusion network, reducing parameter redundancy to ensure high detection accuracy while minimizing computational costs. Our experimental results demonstrate that the SGNet model achieves an impressive 90.7% detection accuracy. Boasting a compact model size of merely 3.5M and remarkably low GFLOPs of 4.1, SGNet achieves an outstanding FPS (Frames Per Second) rate of 178.6. In comparison to other sophisticated lightweight network models, SGNet surpasses them by delivering superior detection accuracy while demanding less computational resources. The successful deployment of the SGNet model on the embedded NVIDIA Jetson Nano platform paves the way for real-time defect detection. With a swift detection time of 0.073 seconds per image, the model meets the stringent requirements for accuracy and real-time performance in identifying battery collector tray defects within real-world industrial environments.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Iterative Learning Control Strategy for Human Centrifuge
abstract: In order to improve the control accuracy of multi-axis human centrifuge, an adaptive iterative learning control strategy is designed in this paper. Firstly, an adaptive iterative learning controller with variable gain is designed, and the variable gain rule is introduced to improve the convergence rate. The convergence of the algorithm is proved by Lyapunov function. Then, the dynamic simplified model of human centrifuge is established by Lagrange method, and the adaptive iterative learning control model and the traditional PD control model are built by MATLAB / SIMULINK. The comparison shows that the adaptive iterative learning control has superior trajectory tracking performance.

articleTitle: Probability-Based Monotonic Basin-hopping Algorithm for Packing Equal Circles in a Rectangular Container
abstract: The problem of packing equal circles in a rectangular container refers to the task of placing a given number of non-overlapping equal circles into a fixed rectangular container while maximizing the radius of the circles. This problem is a well-known global optimization problem with a number of applications. To solve this challenging problem, we propose a new heuristic algorithm called the probability-based monotonic basin-hopping algorithm which includes a probability-based monotonic basin-hopping method and an adjustment method for the radius of circles. The performance of algorithm is tested on a number of popular benchmark instances and the experimental results show that the proposed algorithm is very efficient and improves the best-known solutions for 25 out of 51 benchmark instances tested.

articleTitle: Task Pre-Assignment Method for UAV Swarm Based on Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: As an important part of UAV combat, task preallocation, which is to assign UAVs to different tasks prior to its combat, has received intensive attention for its ability to reduce the computation cost and enhance efficiency of UAV swarms. For small scale tasks, the existing task pre-assignment algorithm can give accurate results in a short time. However, when the scale of tasks increases, the efficiency could dramatically reduce, and the computation time could significantly increase. Aiming at the problem of UAV swarm's task pre-assignment, a novel pre-assignment method for UAV swarm based on sequential generative adversarial network is proposed. The Long-short Term Memory (LSTM) network and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) are adopted to construct generator model and discriminator model respectively., and a policy gradient algorithm based on Monte Carlo search is adopted along the backpropagation. The simulation results show that, compared with existing task pre-assignment methods, the new method can solve the problem more quickly and effectively, which also provides relatively better assignment results.

articleTitle: Edge-Constrained Point Cloud Segmentation for Plants
abstract: Point clouds is the powerful and practical data representation for plant parameterization and plant growth monitoring. The most critical step in the precise extraction of plant parameters is the accurate segmentation of plant point clouds, especially in the edge regions, as this directly affects the accuracy of the parameters. This research introduces an edge extraction algorithm to obtain edge points from the point cloud and utilizes these edge points to construct an edge module to enhance the Stratified Transformer model. The proposed method can better constrain the edge and learn the edge features of the point cloud. In this research, we compare our method with various methods on Pheno4D and S3DIS datasets. Our method shows significant improvement in edge segmentation, such as stem-leaf edges and window-wall edges.

articleTitle: Deep- Hammerstein - Model- Based Predictive Control for Piezoelectric Actuators in Trajectory Tracking Applications
abstract: With the high motion resolution and rapid response ability, piezoelectric actuators (PEAs) have been used for many precision systems. However, the inherent hysteresis nonlinearity is very difficult to deal with, due to the amplitude-, frequency-, and memory-dependent characteristics, which severely limits the tracking accuracy of the PEA. In this paper, we first propose a deep neural network based Hammerstein (dHam) model to predict the displacement of the PEA, which consists of a hysteresis block and a linear block in series. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the satisfactory performance of the dHam modeling method. Based on the trained dHam model, a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) approach is proposed to address the trajectory tracking problem under constraints. The tracking results demonstrates the efficiency and efficacy of the NMPC approach.

articleTitle: Improvement of DPos Consensus Algorithm Based on Reputation Authorization
abstract: To address the issues of malicious nodes being easily selected as consensus nodes and the problem of untimely processing of malicious nodes in the DPoS consensus algorithm, we propose a Trust-authorized Delegated Proof of Stake (Ta-DPoS) consensus algorithm based on reputation authorization. The Ta-DPoS consensus algorithm uses the PowerTrust model to conduct global reputation evaluation of nodes, enhances the authority and credibility of selected consensus nodes, balances the competition for bookkeeping rights while ensuring a fair selection process, and improves decentralization. At the same time, under a reputation reward and punishment mechanism based on dynamic games, malicious nodes are promptly excluded from the network edge, achieving constraints and incentives for blockchain node behavior. Experimental results show that to some extent, the Ta-DPoS consensus algorithm overcomes security issues that exist in node election and consensus processes and achieves relatively better performance in consensus efficiency, decentralization, and scalability.

articleTitle: Attention U-net for Cell Instance Segmentation
abstract: As a major cause of human death and disability, neurological diseases have profound impacts worldwide, yet there is still a lack of effective research to quantify such diseases. As a fundamental but challenging task in the field of medical imaging, segmenting neuronal cell types measured by microscopic observation images to help assess patient status plays a crucial role in the accurate quantification of the disease. To this end, we propose an instance segmentation network of Improved Attention U-net for segmentation of different types of neuronal cells. Specifically, we introduce adaptive mechanism on the basis of U-net structure to enhance the robustness and discriminability of the model. This measure can capture the most important parts in the field of view to filter out redundant information in the target optimization process. In addition, considering the irregular and unique morphology of neuronal cells, we introduce deformable convolution kernels to adapt to the detection needs of various types of cells and lesions. Experimental results show that the algorithm has excellent performance in cell instance segmentation.

articleTitle: Charging and Discharging Scheduling Strategy of Electric Vehicle Clusters Considering User Responsiveness
abstract: Aiming at the problem of high dimension of optimization variables and insufficient consideration of user responsiveness in traditional scheduling model of electric vehicles, a charging and discharging scheduling strategy of electric vehicle clusters considering user responsiveness is proposed. Firstly, based on Weber-Fechner Law, an evaluation model of user responsiveness of electric vehicles considering charging and discharging price and vehicle state of charge is established, and a realtime schedulable capacity of clusters evaluation model is established on that basis. Secondly, a schedulable potential evaluation model of electric vehicles is proposed from the perspective of both time and space, through which the electric vehicles are partitioned into several clusters. Finally, an optimization model with the minimum variance of the power grid and the lowest user charging cost as the objectives is proposed, which is solved by the NSGA-III optimization algorithm. The results of the simulation show that the proposed model not only keeps the dimension of the optimization variables within a reasonable range but also fully considers the influence of user responsiveness on the schedulable capacity, which reduces the difficulty of solving and ensures the flexibility and accuracy of scheduling.

articleTitle: Distributed Consensus-Based Economic Dispatch for Power System Over Directed Network*
abstract: Economic Dispatch Problem (EDP) is one of important issues in the smart grid consisting of the main grid, energy routers (ER) and connected microgrid. Most of the current researches focus on the island mode and the undirected communication network. In this paper, we propose a distributed algorithm that can work in both grid-connected operation mode and isolated mode, and achieves flexible transformation between two modes. The proposed algorithm is a leader-following mechanism, when the microgrid operates in grid-connected mode. It utilizes feedback in the form of an estimated total average power mismatch, while the leader ensures that the incremental cost of each generator aligns with the electricity price of the distribution system. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the algorithm even if the communication graph is a directed graph.

articleTitle: Option-Based Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for UAV Multi-Objective Path Planning
abstract: This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning approach to solve the multi-objective path planning problem for UAV material delivery in a dynamic multi-obstacle environment. The approach uses option-based hierarchical reinforcement learning to decompose the problem into single-objective subtasks, and a novel network structure is designed to extract and fuse state and obstacle information to facilitate decision-making. A twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is used for centralized training and distributed execution. The approach also introduces a new reward function to speed up convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in completing the task with faster convergence and generalization compared to traditional TD3 algorithm,

articleTitle: ARCE: Adaptive Real-time Convergence Estimation for Wireless Networks Time Synchronization
abstract: Real-time convergence-estimation for time synchronization of wireless sensor networks remains unexplored by researchers. This work proposes a novel real-time convergence estimation using an adaptive real-time convergence estimation (ARCE) algorithm. The algorithm is based on synchronization error and distribution of both synchronous and asynchronous time synchronization algorithms. The actual distributions of synchronization error are analyzed and evaluated using significant amount of experimental results. According to the experimental results and simulations, the ARCE can effectively detect the convergence state for all the comparisons. Therefore, the ARCE can be used to develop an adaptive time synchronization protocol based on synchronization error distribution, which could be robust and scalable for a large-scale and random-deployed wireless networks.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Attention Graph Convolution Networks for Relationship Extraction
abstract: Attention mechanisms have gained significant prominence in the realm of natural language processing. When it comes to relation extraction in the form of a graph, the complex sentence structure and uncertain entity positions pose considerable challenges. To address these limitations, we propose a hierarchical attention graph convolutional neural network (HAGCN) for relation extraction. The HAGCN model reflect the extraction process at multiple levels spanning the graph, sentence, and word levels; In addition, the proposed model incorporates three levels of attention mechanisms which precisely adjust feature vector distribution in the semantic space to prioritize essential vocabulary information and facilitate the extraction of dependency distances between nodes and entities, enhancing the comprehension of intricate sentence structures. The experimental results of TACRED and SemEval indicate that the proposed model performs better than other baseline models.

articleTitle: A Novel YOLOv5-Based Hybrid Underwater Target Detection Algorithm Combining with CBAM and CIoU
abstract: The algorithm for detecting underwater targets plays a critical role in facilitating the effective operation of an underwater robot in an aquatic environment. Currently, a wide array of land-based target detection methods are accessible. Nevertheless, the use of these algorithms in underwater target identification situations is challenging due to the intricate underwater environment, encompassing factors such as low light conditions, significant occlusion, wave interference, and other complexities. This study presents a unique approach for detecting underwater targets, utilizing the YOLOv5 framework. The integration of the CBAM attention mechanism module, featuring the PRelu activation function, with YOLOv5 is undertaken as an initial step to augment the network's capability in extracting intricate details. Additionally, the framework for target detection incorporates the CIo U Loss activation function and one cycle learning rate mode. These additions aim to expedite the convergence time of the network model and improve its detection precision. In conclusion, a novel approach for integrating characteristics is introduced, which effectively integrates more precise and detailed information. The experimental findings confirm the efficacy of the suggested framework in detecting submerged targets. The detection of small underwater targets is achieved with a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 83.9%, surpassing the performance of RCNN, Fast RCNN, and YOLOv5 target detection models.

articleTitle: A Switching Strategy for Run-to-Run Control Using Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Algorithm and Integral Controller
abstract: An end-to-end strategy based on the deep determin-istic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm is an effective adaptive method for run-to-run control, which allows exploration in a semiconductor manufacturing environment to overcome the limitations of the model. However, the tracking performance of DDPG can be compromised by inefficient sampling and inadequate training. To address such issues, a switching control strategy based on DDPG and integral controller is proposed. First, the target tracking is built as a Markov decision process. Given the current state, two actions are obtained from the integral controller and the DDPG, respectively. Then, an optimal action that provides a greater reward is selected as the output of the switching strategy. Therefore, the developed scheme not only guarantees the basic performance of the integral controller, but also fully exploits the exploration advantages of DDPG in unknown manufacturing environments. Simulation results demonstrate the improvement in tracking performance of the presented strategy compared to the standalone DDPG and integral controllers.

articleTitle: Weed Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv8 with Neck-Slim
abstract: Weed threat is a significant factor impacting food production. Manual weeding is not only time-consuming and physically demanding but also introduces the potential for human error, thereby negatively affecting production yields. Consequently, the proposition of mechanized agricultural production has emerged. This approach committees to precise weed detection and subsequent weed management through the application of chemical agents or laser technology. In this research, we employed the one-stage object detection model YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once Version 8), and realized slim-neck optimization by replacing part of the network in the Neck layer of the framework with GSConv and VoV-GSCSP pairs of models. The resulting system implements weed detection inside crops and supports mechanized weed control. Our system achieved competitive performance compared to related algorithms.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Formation Control for Second-Order Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: We develop an event-triggered control methodology, which includes a distributed protocol and an event sampling strategy, to address the formation control problem for second-order nonlinear multi-agent systems. We use the Lyapunov method and design a control protocol which ensures that all agents can maintain the formation under the influence of event-triggered mechanism. Additionally, we ensure that endless triggering events in finite time, commonly referred to as Zeno behavior, do not occur by incorporating an event sampling technique that obeys certain criteria. Ultimately, the efficacy of the algorithm is confirmed through simulations.

articleTitle: Investigation of Factors Influencing the Accuracy of Multi-Sensor Fusion with Extended Kalman Filter
abstract: An extended Kalman filter-convex combination fusion algorithm with time synchronization and a variable sampling rate extended Kalman filter fusion algorithm have been designed. Based on these algorithms, simulation analysis has been conducted. The impact of time synchronization on accuracy, the influence of constant velocity motion model and the “current” statistical model on system performance, performance comparison of the two systems under the “current” statistical model, the effect of low-quality inputs on system performance, and the influence of sensor spatial relationships on system performance have been investigated. This work provides insights into system construction and strategies for improving system tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Obstacle Avoidance of Rope-driven Hyper-redundant Robot Based on Gradient Projection Method
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the main body cannot achieve obstacle avoidance when the end of the rope-driven hyper-redundant manipulator performs the main task, this paper proposes an obstacle avoidance algorithm based on the gradient projection method. In this method, the four control points are evenly distributed on the body of the robot arm, and the shortest distance between the control point and the obstacle calculated in real time is used as the optimization index, combined with obstacle modeling and dynamic selection of the amplification factor, to achieve better obstacle avoidance effect. A six-joint twelve-degree-of-freedom rope-driven hyper-redundant manipulator was used for simulation experiments in MATLAB. The results show that the algorithm can realize obstacle avoidance for the rope-driven hyper-redundant manipulator while maintaining a high-end end-effector tracking accuracy, and at the same time the change of the joint angle and the change of the rope length are stable, and there will be no large-scale oscillation.

articleTitle: An eco-driving evaluation method based on multi-factor fusion
abstract: With the development of the Internet of Vehicles, the research of eco-driving technology has a new turning point. Relying on the maturity of Vehicles to Everything(V2X) technology, data interaction and information sharing can be realized between vehicle-vehicle, vehicle-road and vehicle-network. Therefore, an eco-driving grade evaluation method based on the collection of big data by the Internet of Vehicles is proposed. By using the Internet of Vehicles, multi-source objective factors such as vehicle performance, traffic flow, road level, and weather are collected to construct a vehicle driving feature model. The K-means improved by genetic algorithm (GA-Kmeans) is used to cluster vehicles with the same characteristics, and vehicle clusters with different characteristics are divided. Then, the energy-saving driving grade is evaluated in the same feature vehicle cluster. Finally, the driver is given the recommended speed in real time through the on-board device. The experimental results show that the improved GA-Kmeans algorithm has better clustering effect, and the characteristics of different vehicle clusters are more obvious compared with the traditional clustering method. In different characteristic vehicles, the energy-saving driving suggestions given by this method are objective and fair, which is conducive to taking real-time ecological driving suggestions for drivers in different environments.

articleTitle: Multiscale Feature Extraction Fusion Network for Semantic Segmentation of High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images
abstract: In recent years, semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing images has attracted much attention. However, the large size difference, complex background, and numerous small objects in remote sensing images bring challenges to the existing methods. For this purpose, we developed a high-resolution remote sensing image semantic segmentation network based on a multi-scale deformable Convolutional module (MDC) and multi-scale Attention Fusion module (MFF). Firstly, a multi-scale deformable convolution module is used to extract features of different scales and shapes. Then the multi-scale attention fusion module is embedded into the FPN module, and the multi-scale feature fusion is realized better through the mutual guidance of deep feature and shallow feature. In the end, we achieved 83.40% average cross-linking (MIoU) on the Postam dataset and 74.97% average cross-linking (MIoU) on the Vaihingen dataset.

articleTitle: Optimization for Pickup Vehicle Scheduling in Steel Logistics Park Based on Enhanced SPEA2
abstract: Pickup vehicle scheduling in the steel logistics park is a critical issue in determining the outbound effciency of steel products. Steel products are distributed in the yards of the steel logistics park with mixed storage, and the optional yards for each pickup operation are not unique, which greatly increases the scheduling complexity. To overcome this challenge, in this paper, we propose a pickup vehicle scheduling problem with mixed steel storage (PVSP-MSS) to optimize makespan of pickup vehicle and makespan of steel logistics park simultaneously. The optimization problem is described as a multi-objective problem, and an enhanced Strength Pareto Evolutionary Algorithm 2 (ESPEA) is proposed to solve the problem with high efficiency. Experiments are executed based on data collected from a real steel logistics park. The results confirm that ESPEA can significantly reduce both makespan of each pickup vehicle and makespan of steel logistics park.

articleTitle: A Novel Kernel Canonical Variable Analysis Method for the AHU Fault Detection Based on the Multi-Batch Running Datasets
abstract: The air handling unit (AHU) system is employed within heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems to efficiently control and distribute air throughout a building. The AHU operation represents a unique process with distinct nonlinear characteristics and multi-directional dynamics that encompass both temporal and batch variations. To address these challenges, we propose the multi-batch data-based KCVA (MBKCVA) to address the nonlinearity and multi-directional dynamics by integrating the multi-batch data analysis into the KCVA model. To handle the AHU's batch variation dynamics, the multi-batch data analysis technique is employed to rearrange the three-way training dataset into a variable-wise two-way matrix. To figure out the time-wise dynamics and nonlinearity, the KCVA is then adopted to effectively capture the slow-varying symptom in a nonlinear manner by considering the data's temporal serial correlations. The experimental results on the ASHRAE Research Project RP-1312 datasets show significant enhancements achieved by our proposed MBKCVA based approach in terms of fault detection.

articleTitle: Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging Using AdaGrad-ADMM
abstract: Non-line-of-sight (NLOS) imaging aims to reconstruct the hidden scene using transients reflected from the relay wall. The reconstruct task can be formulated as an inverse problem and many methods have been proposed using convolutional kernels to solve this problem, which are either inefficient or inaccurate to complete the reconstruction. Here we use the convolutional approximation of the Gram operator of the transportation matrix to formulate the reconstruction as a computationally-efficient optimization problem. As the inherent features of sparsity and positivity are added as regularization to the above optimization problem, we employ the ADMM method to find the suitable regularization coefficients. We further use AdaGrad-Norm, an adaptive gradient descent algorithm, to efficiently solve the reformulated optimization objective. Finally, we test our method via both simulated and real scenes and demonstrate its advantages of reconstruct accuracy and efficiency in comparison to other commonly-used methods.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Multivariate Predictive Control Technology in Gas Fractionation Unit
abstract: An advanced process control (APC) based on multivariate predictive control is designed to address the multivariate characteristics in the depropanizer tower of gas fractionation unit. The advanced control strategy of depropanizer tower is introduced. The implementation process of advanced control scheme in the gas fractionation unit is described in detail, including OPC communication configuration, step test of model, DCS control configuration and control effect. The control effect of the gas fractionation unit is significantly improved via applying the proposed advanced control method. It shows that the proposed advanced control is effective, which can strongly offer reference for the advanced process control systems of other industrial process.

articleTitle: Model-Free Robust Joint Control of Flexible Joint Robots
abstract: In this paper, an uncertainty and disturbance estimator(UDE) based joint torque robust control method is proposed for robot with flexible joint. The conventional approaches to controlling flexible manipulators mostly focus on the motor side of the joint since it is much stiffer than that of the link side. However, this method reduces the position accuracy of the joint. Here we propose a model-free UDE-based robust torque control method on the joint link side. This method can estimate system disturbances and uncertainties, requiring only knowledge of the system's bandwidth. The numerical simulation results show that the proposed robust controller in this paper can achieve higher positional accuracy.

articleTitle: An APSO-Based Resource Scheduling Algorithm for UAV-Aided MEC System
abstract: The widespread use of resource-intensive applications has imposed a challenge for user equipments (UEs) which may lack the necessary resources to support them. Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) aided Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) systems offer an innovative solution to this problem by providing additional resources. Our paper introduces a model in which a UAV outfitted with an edge server is utilized to offer service for a cluster of UEs. In each time slot, each UE has a latency-critical task that need to be processed. With the aid of UAV, UEs can choose to partially offload the computation tasks or perform local computing. A minimization problem whose goal is to reduce the overall energy consumed by jointly optimizing the computation offloading strategies and time slot scheduling is formulated. To solve this problem, an adaptive particle swarm optimization (APSO) based algorithm is proposed in this paper to search the optimal solution iteratively by analogizing the iteration procedure to the movement of particles. The parameters of the algorithm are updated through a carefully designed adaptive approach. Based on the simulation results, our proposed algorithm outperforms the benchmark algorithms by providing lower energy consumption. Besides, It is able to improve fairness among users.

articleTitle: Learning of Quadruped Robot Motor Skills Based on Policy Constrained TD3
abstract: The agile movement of quadruped robot requires rich professional knowledge and tedious manual adjustment. However, reinforcement learning does not require any professional knowledge to enable the quadruped robot to learn better movement gait and skills. The TD3 algorithm is widely used in continuous motion control, but it tends to converge to boundary actions, resulting in inability to learn the optimal strategy and overfitting. Inspired by behavior cloning, this paper proposes a policy constrained TD3 algorithm(PC- TD3), which adds behavioral constraints during the policy update process of TD3, updates the policy in the direction of expected behavior, and reduces boundary actions. The experiment was conducted on the Pybullet platform. The experimental results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper can enable the quadruped Robot learning to learn the walking skills. Compared with other mainstream algorithms, the experiment shows that PC- TD3 has better performance.

articleTitle: Parameterization Process of Multi-value Logic Networks
abstract: This paper presents a generator for creating pa-rameterized multi-value logic models. It can be challenging to precisely capture the behavior of a biological system and translate it into a set of multi-value logic network functions due to the difficulty of gathering sufficient data. However, these issues can be addressed to some extent by using parameterized multi-value logic networks, as this model allows for leaving some update functions unspecified. The generator employs various complex network models, including the Watts-Strogatz model and ErdOs-Renyi random network model, among others. In this study, either existing non-parametric networks are parameterized or new net-works are constructed based on specified criteria. Additionally, the generator is capable of producing visual model graphs and conducting relevant analyses. Finally, the dynamic structure and description of the parameterized multi-value logic network are provided to demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed generator.

articleTitle: An Improved Rail Crack Classification Method Based on Wavelet Multi-Resolution Analysis and Signal Separability
abstract: Rail crack is a serious threat to the safety of train operations. Accurately classifying various types of rail crack is a crucial aspect in preventing potential accidents. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an improved rail crack classification method based on wavelet multi-resolution analysis (WMRA) and signal separability. By using electromagnetic acoustic emission (EMAE) technique, crack-related acoustic emission (AE) signals are generated, which are then decomposed into sub-signals using WMRA. Subsequently, the best feature set (BFS) is obtained from each sub-signal based on the constructed feature separability index (ST). The signal separability index (SSI) is constructed to evaluate the information quantity of each sub-signal for subsequent signal analysis. Finally, by leveraging the BFS and the most informative sub-signal, crack classification is performed. Comparative analysis with conventional approaches reveals a remarkable enhancement in the accuracy of rail crack classification, specifically within a reduced feature dimension. Noteworthy, this method demonstrates the frequency band concentration effect of EMAE, thereby providing valuable insights for further research in the field of rail crack classification.

articleTitle: Tracking-Differentiator-Based Sliding-Mode Control for Tracking Control
abstract: Tracking control has attracted significant attention because of its close link with industrial applications. Tracking control requires that a control algorithm can ensure that an actuator follows control commands, with a fast response anti-disturbance abilities and small chattering. A tracking-differentiator-based sliding-mode control approach for tracking control is proposed in this paper. A tracking differentiator has the ability to obtain the desired signal's differential signal, even when there is noise in the desired signal. A differential signal is often required in the design of sliding-mode controllers. When tracking differentiator is applied to a sliding-mode controller, the chattering of the control commands (caused by noise disturbance) can be reduced while the fast response of the sliding-mode controller can be maintained. The simulation results show that the proposed controller is effective.

articleTitle: Distributed Privacy-Preserving State-of-Charge Balance Control for Multiple Energy Storage Systems in Smart Grid
abstract: This paper studies the distributed state of charge (SoC) balance control strategy in battery energy storage systems (BESSs), satisfying privacy-preserving requirement of BESSs privacy-sensitive data, i.e., configurations and SoC, which may be transmitted among BESSs. Considering each BESS communicates with its neighboring BESS, we use a distributed dynamic average consensus algorithm to do parameter estimations. Using obtained parameters, we set proper power output of each BESS and maintains overall maximum capability. Different from common algorithms, this algorithm not only converges to the exact average of reference signals and thus help set control power outputs, but also ensures the desired differential privacy by adding zero mean Laplace noises, thus protecting privacy-sensitive data from possible adversaries. Effectiveness of the presented approach is demonstrated by simulations.

articleTitle: Deployment of Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems via a PDE Approach
abstract: Spatial deployment of large-scale heterogeneous multi-agent systems (HMASs) over desired 2D or 3D curves is investigated in this paper. With assumption that HMASs consist of numerous first-order agents (FOAs) and second-order agents (SOAs) that could obtain local information of desired curves and their positions relative to their closest neighbors, the collective dynamics of large-scale HMASs are modeled as heterogeneous partial differential equations (PDEs). In particular, this paper introduces series-dependent topological weights between neighboring agents, which are more versatile and practical than constant topological weights commonly used in previous studies. A novel single-point control scheme is proposed, where an informed agent is situated between the last FOA and first SOA. This operation could not only ensure successful implementation of spatial deployment, but also guarantee well-posedness of the constructed heterogeneous error PDEs. By utilizing inequality techniques, sufficient conditions for exponential convergence of error system are derived. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate effectiveness of the proposed approaches.

articleTitle: When Partial Differential Equations and Neural Networks Meet 3D Printing: A Case Study of 3D Printing of PINN Solutions
abstract: In the past decades, the PDE and the 3D printing communities have developed rapidly in parallel. However, surprisingly, they have very little interaction. The PDE-based 3D printing technique is almost the only reported combination that uses PDE to model and optimize the behavior of mate-rials during the printing process. In this paper, we propose another application that also bridges the gap between the PDE community and the 3D printing community by 3D-printing the numerical solutions of PDE for educational purposes. Specifically, we apply the PINN technique to solve the PDE with initial conditions and boundary conditions, export it as a STL file through triangulation, and feed it to the 3D printer for printing. Numerical simulations and experiments have verified the process. The scheme may be enjoyably used for educational demonstration and scientific art.

articleTitle: A Method of Axis Trajectory Measurement Based On Laser Ranging
abstract: Aiming at the requirement of measuring the axis trajectory of helicopter rotor, an axis trajectory measurement method based on the combination of laser ranging sensors is proposed. Firstly, on the basis of laser interference, the rotor axis trajectory measurement system based on the combined laser ranging sensor is designed and constructed for the tiny measurement of high-speed rotating body. Secondly, according to the data missing and outliers caused by occlusion, a real-time anomaly recognition and correction processing algorithm for multi-channel high frequency data is established by combining the data characteristics. Then, based on the spatial geometric relationship, the measurement datum calibration, axis coordinate calculation and axis locus fitting methods are discussed. Finally, the ground accuracy verification test and the simulation platform axis trajectory measurement test are carried out. The experimental results show that this method is accurate and reliable, and can achieve the static micro-measurement of better than 1 %, and can realize the dynamic measurement of sub-millimeter axis locus. The method can be applied to other dynamic micro-measurement tasks.

articleTitle: Adaptive Finite-Time Braking Control of Vehicle Platoons Using a Terminal-Sliding-Mode Approach
abstract: In this article, the issue of cooperative braking control of vehicular platoon under unknown disturbances is proposed. Ground on the finite-time theory and the nonlinear sliding mode control, a distributed terminal sliding mode (TSM) control scheme is proposed, which the control objects can be achieved within finite time. A adaptive laws is designed to deal with the effects of unknown external disturbances. In addition, the Lyapunov technique is used to analyze the convergence of the TSM controller, and the string stability is also guaranteed through the use of transfer function method. The validity of the presented control theorem is demonstrated by three examples.

articleTitle: Optimal PID Tuning for Plants with Random Parameters
abstract: In this paper, the randomized algorithm is established to solve the variance-optimal tuning problem of PID controller for plants with random parameters. The tuning problem of the PID controller is reduced to an optimization problem to minimize the expected value of output variance in the sense of probability based on the established randomized algorithm, in which the Newton's iterative method is employed to find the optimal solution viz. the tuning parameter of PID controller. The validity of the proposed approach and randomized algorithms will be verified through case studies.

articleTitle: Research on the Effect of Firing Threshold on Spike-Based Context Dependent Learning Network
abstract: Context-dependent learning allows the network model to learn and adjust autonomously according to the environment. SNN allows the network to run at high speed and low power consumption. The selection of the threshold value allows the network to achieve the highest correctness and the fastest response time. Through the observation of experimental correctness, response time, SI place, SI item, SI context, and Binariness, it is concluded that when the threshold value of this model is 5, the experimental correctness is highest and the fastest reaction time can be achieved by choosing different thresholds for different situations. This experimental result lays the foundation and guarantee for the future establishment of other models to directly find the discharge threshold with the highest experimental correctness or to seek for the fastest experimental response time.

articleTitle: Research on Software Architecture of Hardware-In-The-Loop Simulation System for Aircraft Electric Braking
abstract: For the aircraft electric braking system which is applied more and more widely in the field of aircraft braking, to better validate the product performance of aircraft electric braking under the condition of low cost, a software architecture of hardware-in-the-loop(HIL) simulation system for aircraft electric braking was designed in this study. The software architecture of HIL simulation system is constructed by using the host computer software, MATLAB / Simulink modeling simulation software and DSP integrated development environment composer code studio (CCS) software. The results of the simulation tests show the efficacy of the software architecture developed in this study for the HIL simulation system dedicated to aircraft electric braking. It provides a platform with complete functions, high reliability for the research and development of a aircraft electric braking system. Compared with full digital simulation for aircraft electric braking, HIL simulation is more real and reliable.

articleTitle: Distributed Gain-scheduling Output Regulation of Discrete-Time Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: The objective of this note is to explore the robust cooperative output regulation (COR) challenge faced by discrete-time linear multi-agent systems with parameter-dependent uncertainties that are represented by linear fractional transformation (LFT) models. To achieve cooperative tracking with disturbance rejection, an innovative scheme is devised, which is based on distributed observers and gain-scheduling output regulation. By employing appropriate coordinate transformations, the existence conditions of distributed controllers are formulated as solvability of output regulator equations plus stability of an equivalent parameter-dependent LFT system. Under some standard assumptions, independent sets of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) and regulator equations are then given to formulate the controller synthesis. By resorting polynomial and LMI techniques, solvability of the proposed method is guaranteed. Finally, a numerical example is simulated to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: An Intention Inference Method for BiGRU Integrating Multi-head Self-Attention in Share Control
abstract: Human-machine cooperative systems based on human-artificial intelligence (AI) in share control have made substantial progress in recent years. Intention inference, a core component of share control, determines the degree of accuracy with which artificial intelligence agents recognize human intent. A good intent reasoning algorithm can enable the intelligent body to efficiently assist the user in accomplishing the target task. However, existing intent inference methods cannot flexibly capture the sequential relationships among user control trajectories. In this paper, we propose a novel intent inference method named GEMH-BiGRU that incorporates a multi-head attention mechanism and bidirectional gating recurrent unit (BiGRU). The BiGRU outputs hidden states containing contextual information, and the multi-head self-attention mechanism parses the feature connections between target attributes and combines them by means of weights, which fully considers the correlation and sparsity of trajectory data. We create intelligent agents that mimic different human strategies and employ a practical evaluation method. Experimental results show that all our models have strong consistency and prediction results.

articleTitle: KAN:Keyframe Attention Network for Person Video Captioning
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm named Keyframe Attention Network (KAN) for video captioning, which combines keyframe feature extraction with an attention allocation mechanism. The proposed method first utilizes a threshold-based keyframe extraction technique to obtain keyframes. Subsequently, keyframe representation module is employed to extract essential features from these keyframes, this module is built by deep residual network. Finally, the extracted feature vectors, along with reference captions, are fed into an attention allocation module to generate descriptive captions. The inclusion of deep residual network ensures an increased network depth without encountering gradient explosions. Moreover, the attention module adopts an Encoder-Decoder structure with additional attention layers, enabling effective attention allocation and yielding more accurate captions.

articleTitle: Active Structural Control for Offshore Wind Turbines with Soil Effect Consideration
abstract: This paper proposes a reduced-order model-based control method for a class of offshore wind turbines with the soil-effect consideration. High-order or multi-state models are normally demanded for active structural control problem of offshore wind turbines, which would complicate the controller design. Therefore, to simplify the complexity of the obtained control strategy, this paper attempts to use a reduced-order model for the active structural control problem of offshore wind turbines, where a LQR control based on a 2 degree-of-freedom (DOFs) model is established. Considering the importance of soil effect on the stable operation of offshore wind turbines, an 11-DOFs wind turbine model including the soil effect and external loads are derived by using the Euler-Lagrange method. The accuracy of the obtained 2-DOF and 11-DOF models is verified by comparing with the well-used wind turbine simulation tool FAST. Finally, extensive simulations are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, where it is shown that the 2-DOF model-based LQR control can effectively reduce the tower displacement of the wind turbine and effectively mitigate the motion of the platform.

articleTitle: An Efficient Heuristic Algorithm for the Rectangular Packing Problem
abstract: This paper studies the classic two-dimensional rectangle packing (2DRP) problem in a fixed rectangular container. To address this problem, we propose an efficient variable neighborhood search (VNS) algorithm based on several new neighborhood structures and a new decoding procedure. For a given sequence of rectangles, the new decoding procedure can generate a packing configuration by sequentially placing the rectangles on the boundary of partial configuration. To assess the performance of algorithm, the extensive computational experiments were conducted on a set of benchmark instances widely used in the literature. Computational results show that the proposed algorithm is very efficient compared to the state-of-art algorithms from the literature and able to obtain the best-known solution for 19 out of the 21 benchmark instances.

articleTitle: A soft measurement method for the freezing point of diesel based on the ASKPCA-LSSVM model
abstract: Traditional methods for determining the freezing point of diesel fuel are complex, expensive, and susceptible to human and environmental factors. Soft measurement methods offer a technical solution for estimating and controlling the prediction of such variables. In this paper, we apply adaptive Lasso penalties to sparse kernel principal component analysis (SKPCA), resulting in adaptive sparse kernel principal component analysis (ASKPCA). ASKPCA achieves non-linear dimensionality reduction while applying different penalties to features with varying importance. This reduces the dimension dependence and improving the model's explanatory power while preserving essential features. The data processed by ASKPCA is used as input for the least squares support vector machine (LSSVM), leading to the establishment of a soft measurement model based on ASKPCA-LSSVM. Simulation results show that the ASKPCA-LSSVM model has better prediction accuracy than the four other methods, underscoring its efficacy as a modeling approach.

articleTitle: An Elitist-Based Multi-Objective Moth-Flame Algorithm for Engineering Design Problem
abstract: The utilization of meta-heuristic algorithms for addressing complex engineering problems is widely recognized as an effective approach. However, it's still challenging to obtain diverse solutions to a problem through meta-heuristic algorithms. A new multi-objective moth-flame optimization algorithm(EMMFO) is proposed in this paper. The EMMFO algorithm is a novel optimization approach that integrates the principles of the moth-flame optimization (MFO) algorithm and the elitist strategy. In the flame environmental selection stage, EMMFO employs a non-dominated sorting method to maintain an elite set of solutions. Additionally, the EMMFO algorithm incorporates the Levy flight mechanism to enhance global exploration capability. To evaluate the performance, DTLZ and ZDT test function is employed to test the performance of EMMFO. Meanwhile EMMFO is applied to the gear train design problem and compared with several multi-objective optimization algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that EMMFO exhibits superior performance and robustness in solving the gear train design problem.

articleTitle: Interpretable Fault Diagnosis of Fiber Optic Gyroscope Based on Belief Rule Base with Projection Gradient Method
abstract: As an important type of navigation equipment in inertial navigation systems, fiber optic gyroscopes (FOG) play a very important role. Due to the complex operating environment, it is inevitably subject to failure. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct the fault diagnosis on FOG. In this paper, an interpretable fault diagnosis method using belief rule base (BRB) is proposed to provide trustworthy diagnosis results. The work of this article consists of two parts: First, BRB is constructed based on expert expertise and used as an interpretable knowledge base for fault diagnosis. The evidential reasoning (ER) algorithm is used to infer fault states. Then, to maintain the interpretability of the fault diagnosis process, the projected gradient method is proposed to optimize the initial BRB. A FOG fault diagnosis case is conducted to verify the practicability of the proposed method. The case indicates that the BRB-based FOG fault diagnosis model achieves better diagnostic accuracy and better interpretability than other models.

articleTitle: Adamer: Adapting Transformer Modules For Training-Efficient Image Restoration
abstract: Recently, Transformer model shines in the field of image restoration due to its unique global modeling capabilities. However, as Transformer models get larger and larger, training from scratch becomes expensive on some edge devices. In addition, due to the low computing power of edge devices, complete finetuning of the Transformer model becomes unaffordable (becomes very expensive). In our paper, we innovatively utilize the already trained partially structured network to Adapt pretrained Transformer modules (Adamer) for training-efficient image restoration. We froze some weights and introduced fast and memory-friendly Adapters. We propose Adaptation Transformer Block (ATB) to fusion of local information from CNN and global information from MDTA. Adamer achieving performance comparable to prior arts with lower computing resources in some major image restoration tasks, including image deraining, image deblurring, and image denoising.

articleTitle: The Grid Searching Positioning Method Based on the Ultra Wide-Band
abstract: With the development of the Internet of Things and communication industry, ultra wide-band (UWB) technology is increasingly widely applied in the field of positioning. However, in some complex scenarios, the traditional three-circle intersecting algorithm is difficult to give positioning results, and it also requires at least three anchors to work properly. To solve this problem, this article proposes a positioning method based on searching grids, which divides the positioning site into a number of grids and finds the grids where the tag is located based on the distance from the anchors to the tag. When the number of ranges between the anchors and the tag is insufficient, a dynamic threshold is used to ensure that there are still grids to be selected. After selecting grids, Kalman filter is being used to optimize the position and dynamic and static experimental results show that this method has good results.
