articleTitle: Anomaly Detection Based on Principle of Justifiable Granularity and Probability Density Estimation
abstract: Anomaly detection is essential to ensure the safety of industrial processes. This paper presents an anomaly detection approach based on the probability density estimation and principle of justifiable granularity. First, time series data are transformed into a two-dimensional information granule by the principle of justifiable granularity. Then, the test statistic is constructed, and the probability density and cumulative distribution functions of the test statistic are calculated. Next, the confidence level determines the test threshold. Finally, the time series data of a key parameter in the sintering process is used as a case study. The experimental result demonstrates that the proposed approach can detect abnormal time series data effectively, providing an accurate and effective solution for detecting time series anomalies in industrial processes.

articleTitle: A novel full-state feedback control combined FTO and SMC of electro-hydraulic systems
abstract: The paper proposes a nonlinear full-state feedback controller to overcome model uncertainty as well as external disturbances in electrohydraulic servo systems. The controller combines sliding mode control and a finite time disturbance observer through the backstepping method to achieve effective control performance. First, the finite time observer estimates the full state signal, including the position signal, velocity signal, acceleration signal, and the lumped disturbance in the electro-hydraulic systems. Furthermore, a composite reaching law using a novel hyperbolic tangent function, along with sliding mode control, adaptively adjusts the convergence rate of the equilibrium point while effectively improving the chattering problem. Using Lyapunov theory, it is proven that the proposed controller achieves asymptotic convergence, while the observer ensures finite-time convergence. Finally, in order to prove the performance of the designed control strategy, simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: A Flexible Crosstalk-Free Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor Array Based on Interdigital-Electrode for High-Precision Pressure Mapping
abstract: Flexible piezoresistive pressure sensor arrays have become an attractive field of research due to their extensive use in human-machine interface, human posture monitoring, healthcare, and other scenarios. However, the inherent crosstalk issue always affects the sensing performance of piezoresistive sensor arrays. In this study, a flexible crosstalk-free pressure sensor array with an interdigital-electrode layout structure is demonstrated. The device mainly consists of an interdigital-electrode (IDE) array on a flexible printed circuit (FPC) board, pressure-sensitive Velostat films, and current-regulating diodes. The combination of IDE and diodes allows a simplified sensor structure with an excellent ability to pattern crosstalk-free pres-sure distributions. The performance of a single sensing unit has been fully characterized, and a high spatial resolution pressure sensor array of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9\times 14$</tex> sensing units is successfully fabricated and tested. As examples of pressure mapping, the proposed sensor array has been used to measure the pressure distribution of foot stepping, palm pressing, and sitting with high precision.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Guidance Law with Impact Angle Constraint
abstract: Addressing the challenge of ineffective impact angle control when employing conventional biased proportional navigation guidance for precision-guided missiles against maneuvering targets, this study proposes a guidance law with impact angle constraint by integrating deep reinforcement learning algorithms with biased proportional navigation guidance. The algorithm enhances traditional proportional navigation guidance by introducing a target maneuver compensation bias term. This bias term is treated as an action in a learning framework and optimized using the Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm. Simulation experiments validate that the proposed algorithm, compared to conventional proportional navigation guidance, not only reduces miss distance and impact angle error but also shortens flight time.

articleTitle: Defect Detection Method of Small-Diameter Ferromagnetism Pipeline Based on Uniform Electromagnetic Field
abstract: In view of the high requirement of the small-diameter pipeline for the passing ability of detection equipment, a defect detection method of double coil structure is designed based on the uniform electromagnetic field. Firstly, the principle of uniform electromagnetic field detection technology is introduced. Secondly, based on the principle of uniform electromagnetic field detection, the characteristics of the detection signal are studied by finite element simulation method. And the structural parameters of the detection device were further optimized. Finally, a uniform electromagnetic field defect detection experimental device was built in the laboratory. The experimental results show that the uniform electromagnetic field defect detection technology can accurately detect the defects of small-diameter ferromagnetic pipes, and has the advantages of light weight, weak magnetic adsorption force and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Analysis and Impedance Control of B-Ultrasound Detection Robot
abstract: In order to achieve constant force control during B-ultrasound robot detection, a six-dimensional force sensor is installed at the end of the robot arm to directly measure force and torque. Then, the dynamic parameter identification of the manipulator was studied and verified, and the position-based impedance control model was simulated to analyze the control performance and parameter influence. Moreover, Simulink simulation frameworks of B-ultrasound robot were built to verify the impedance algorithm. The simulation results demonstrate that the impedance control algorithm can effectively track the constant force and improve the position control accuracy of the system.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic VSG Control with Power Reference Regulation Using Fuzzy PI
abstract: Virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control strategy is widely used for photovoltaic grid-tied inverter to provide better stability for low inertia green energy generation. However, due to the fluctuation of photovoltaic output, the traditional virtual synchronous machine control strategies with constant power reference cause significant fluctuations in the DC side voltage, which does harm to the stable operation of the system. Energy storage equipment is generally used to stabilize the DC bus voltage, which imposes high cost to the customer, especially for the distributed roof photovoltaic generation. To deal with this problem, the active power reference of the VSG is regulated using the proportional integral (PI) control framework according to the error between the DC bus voltage reference and the measured DC bus voltage. To accelerate the regulation speed, a set of fuzzy rules are proposed to adjust the proportional integral parameters, which also avoid the difficulty in the traditional PI parameter adjustment. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the DC side voltage stabilization method, and the improved performance using the fuzzy interference parameter adjustment for PI controller.

articleTitle: Research and Development of Non-Destructive Testing System for Aqueous Zinc Ion Batteries Based on Ultrasound
abstract: Water-based zinc ion batteries (ZIBs) have become a highly potential energy storage system due to their simple manufacturing process and high safety performance. Then, during the charging and discharging process, gas evolution will occur inside the battery, resulting in a local nonvacuum state. This phenomenon can cause irreversible loss of electrode materials and electrolytes, leading to reduced battery performance and safety issues. This paper explores the application of ultrasonic non-destructive testing technology in the field of battery gas evolution detection. An ultrasonic detection experimental system was established and gas evolution experiments were conducted on a simulated aqueous zinc ion battery. After verification, the experimental equipment can effectively detect the presence of gases, accurately locate the emitted gases, and has the advantages of convenience, non-destructive, and real-time. It can promote the development of zinc ion battery testing and provide a feasible reference for future research on internal defect detection of batteries.

articleTitle: A Positioning Algorithm Based on Multi-Sensor Fusion for Automatic Driving Vehicles in Underground Mines
abstract: Aiming at the problem of Ultra Wide Band (UWB) positioning accuracy being reduced due to non-line-of-sight (NLOS) errors in complex underground mining environments, and that a single sensor cannot meet the positioning accuracy of underground autonomous vehicles. A multi-source sensors fusion positioning algorithm based on the Improved Federal Kalman filter is proposed to improve navigation and positioning performance of the underground autonomous vehicles. This algorithm uses the NLOS discriminant to detect whether the sub-filter contains non-line-of-sight errors. It determines the performance of the sub-filter, and then the noise factor of each sub-filter is derived from the discriminant function. Thus the factor adaptively adjusts the information allocation coefficients of the Federal Kalman filter, which can effectively reduce the impact of non-line-of-sight errors on the system's positioning accuracy. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional Federal Kalman filter, the Improved Federal Kalman filter algorithm can control the positioning error within 20cm and improve the positioning accuracy by 48.8%, which verifies that the algorithm can effectively improve the positioning accuracy of vehicle navigation system in the complex environment of the underground mines.

articleTitle: Nonsingular Terminal Sliding-Mode Control For Robotic Manipulator System With Adaptive Uncertainty and Disturbance Rejection
abstract: This paper investigates the fast adaptive tracking control problem for robotic manipulator system subject to parametric uncertainties and external disturbance. Based on the screw theory, the iterative algorithms for the kinematics and dynamics of composite rigid body have been established. To achieve desired trajectory tracking performance, an nonsingular terminal sliding-mode controller is engineered, where the lumped uncertainties and disturbance are well-rejected through adaptive techniques. Additionally, a boundary layer of sliding-mode manifold is introduced to eliminate the chattering phenomenon generated during switching the controller. At the same time, the influence of actual control frequency on the consequently discretized proposed controller is carefully discussed. Experimented on the Webots platform, simulations conducted on a 6-DoF open chain robotic manipulator, GLUON-2L6-4L3, verify the capability of the designed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Gas Leakage Source Positioning and Estimation Algorithm Based on Deep Neural Network (DNN)
abstract: Gas leakage source positioning and estimation is a crucial approach to ensuring urban safety. This paper presents a gas leakage source estimation method based on deep neural network. The gas leakage diffusion model and machine learning model are applied to the estimation method of leakage gas source. Taking into account the characteristics of the leakage gas, we proposed the usage of both the Gaussian plume model and the DNN model. Then corresponding observation models are compiled based on these different models. The Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm is applied to analyze and predict the observation data. Simulation results show that compared with traditional modeling methods, the improved DNN algorithm has better performance, further reducing the source estimation and positioning error.

articleTitle: Motion Planning of Vehicle Obstacle Avoidance by Quantum Reinforcement Learning
abstract: With the development of artificial intelligence, autonomous driving technology is becoming a promising solution for reducing the number of accidents caused by human factors of drivers. Motion planning of vehicle obstacle avoidance is a key part of autonomous driving technology, re-planning the driving path or trajectory based on real-time traffic information. How to ensure the safety of autonomous vehicles (AVs) within limited computing resource is one of the research difficulties. In this paper, a vehicle motion planning algorithm in the hierarchical quantum reinforcement learning (HQRL) framework that combines quantum reinforcement learning (QRL) and hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) is proposed. In the option-critic framework of HRL, the QRL agent is applied to make choice in different options. The experimental results showcase our algorithm has better performance on safety average scores compared to classical HRL in the case of less number of model parameters. Therefore, this paper shows the potential of HQRL on solving vehicle motion planing safety problems.

articleTitle: Predictive racing control using model-mismatch learning for autonomous racecars
abstract: Autonomous racing remains an extremely challenging problem due to the strong nonlinearity of tire forces and unknown road conditions. The strong nonlinearity of tire forces and unknown road conditions result in model-mismatches, degrading the performance of model-based approaches. A predictive racing controller using model-mismatch learning is proposed to enhance the performance of autonomous racing. To balance model accuracy and complexity, a single hidden-layer fully neural network is employed to learn model mismatches, and the learned model mismatches are then incorporated directly into the prediction model of model predictive control(MPC). A CarSim/Simulink co-simulation test is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme. Result shows a 3.36% improvement in the average lap speed of racing cars compared to the nonlinear MPC.

articleTitle: Efficient Object Localization for Unseen Object 6D Pose Estimation
abstract: Object localization is utilized as the first step in standard 6D object pose estimation methods to obtain the position information of the objects. However, these object localization methods cannot be directly applied to unseen objects, which is the focus of recent research on 6D object pose estimation. In this paper, an accurate and efficient localization method for unseen object is proposed, based on a template matching strategy. The Hybrid Channel-Spatial Attention Model (HCSAM) is designed to focus on the target object by enhancing the contextual differences between the target object and background. Additionally, The Multi-Scale Integration Transformer (MSIT) module is designed to eliminate noise interference and enhance semantic information in low-dimensional features by integrating multidimensional information. Our method outperforms existing approaches on the complicated occluded dataset LINEMOD, as well as on the challenging generalized pose estimation dataset GenMOP.

articleTitle: Learning Human Behavior for Bot Detection: A Perspective on Mouse Movement
abstract: The issue of bot detection has garnered increasing attention among researchers due to its significant impact on the daily lives of human users. Researchers have proposed various detection methods from different perspectives to identify malicious bots. In response, bot developers strive to evade existing detection mechanisms by incorporating human-like behavior into their bots. To advance research in the field of bot detection, this work introduces MouseAgent, an adversarial generative network-based approach that generates human-like mouse movements through learning from human user behaviors. MouseAgent offers two key advantages: Firstly, it demonstrates better similarity and evasion capability compared to existing function-based generative approaches in accurately mimicking the mouse movements of normal users. Secondly, once the generator model is trained, it can be readily utilized to generate a large number of unrestricted samples. Experimental results validate the efficacy of MouseAgent in generating mouse movements, showcasing its ability to easily evade existing detection models designed for the function-based generation of bot samples. The proposed mouse movement trajectory generation method using adversarial networks presents a new challenge for further research on mouse movement-based bot detection, and inspires the development of bot detection techniques.

articleTitle: The Active Disturbance Rejection Control Method for Stabilizing the Roll Channel in High-Dynamic Missiles
abstract: During the flight of a high-dynamic spinning missile, the roll channel severe dynamic environment and significant nonlinear alterations in disturbance coefficients due to the influence of complex aerodynamic environments, which can result in deviations and instability of the missile. Thus, the roll control channel must possess robust anti-disturbance capability. Accordingly, active disturbance rejection control theory-based roll stabilization controller is designed to fulfill this requirement. Through analysis of the roll control channel of a high-dynamic spinning missile, a mathematical model of the channel is established, and noise received by the system is filtered via a tracking differentiator. Additionally, the uncertain section of the control object model and unknown target information are estimated and dynamically compensated through the linear extended state observer. Utilizing the nonlinear error feedback control law can convert the object feedback into an “integral series” system, leading to the ideal controller's design. Simulation comparison between the proposed method, traditional PID control techniques and the second order sliding mode controller for active disturbance rejection demonstrates this method's fast control speed, strong anti-interference capabilities, and excellent robustness.

articleTitle: A Gas Negative Pressure Power Regulation System with Fault Diagnosis Function and The Design of Diagnosis Method
abstract: Combining the characteristics of traditional negative pressure power regulation system, this paper designs a negative pressure power regulation system with fault diagnosis function. When the system is faulty, it can accurately locate the faulty parts to facilitate timely maintenance treatment and improve the efficiency of system troubleshooting; the double insurance design of shut-off valve and gas commutator is adopted for each vacuum pump inlet to prevent the negative pressure power unit from leaking and having an adverse impact on the whole negative pressure power regulation system; the negative pressure power unit is easy to maintain separately and does not affect the normal use of the system; the system can realize the precise control of system negative pressure power regulation, effectively improve troubleshooting efficiency and reduce energy consumption. The design can be realized on the original device through upgrading and transformation, which has good practical and promotional value.

articleTitle: A Novel Map Representation for Automatic Construction of Topological Map and Lane-Level Route Planning
abstract: Traditional road-level topological maps cannot meet the demand for high precision navigation services required by human drivers and autonomous vehicles. Meanwhile, current enhanced lane-level topological maps with redundant details pose practical challenges for automatic map construction and efficient lane-level route planning. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel topological map representation. Based on this representation, a hierarchical mapping framework is established, which includes the extraction of road primitives, generation of directed graph, and automatic construction of lane-level topological map. The constructed topological map enables efficient lane-level route planning by the shortest path search algorithm with having the minimal nodes of topological graph. The proposed mapping framework and lane-level route planning have been extensively tested and evaluated on two real urban traffic scenarios, demonstrating the feasibility and effectiveness of this novel topological map representation.

articleTitle: Application of Adaptive Kalman Filter Method in Linear Motor Propulsion System
abstract: In the linear motor propulsion system, there is a phase lag problem between the position and speed information collected by the positioning speed measurement system and the actual value of the control system, which will lead to a decrease in the tracking accuracy of the control system. In order to improve the tracking accuracy, an adaptive Kalman filter method with delay compensation is proposed. First, calculate the state prediction matrix and prediction error variance matrix at the current time through the model, then extrapolate according to the position obtained by the sensor, and fuse with the position estimated by Kalman to obtain the estimated velocity and acceleration, and use the obtained acceleration value as the observation value, calculate the adjustment factor; correct the forecast error variance matrix and maneuver frequency; finally, update the forecasted output information with the corrected parameters. Both the simulation and experimental results show that the estimated position and velocity phase are basically consistent with the real-time position and real-time velocity phase, which has the effect of delay compensation, and the error is small, and the system control accuracy is high.

articleTitle: Novel Predictive-Reconstructive Feature Filtering LSTM-Based Autoencoder for Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Feature extraction plays a crucial role in data-driven fault diagnosis. To further extract features that better fit the needs of industrial process fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a predictive-reconstructive feature filtering LSTM-based Autoencoder (PRFFLAE) network. In PRFFLAE, LAE is utilized to predict the key performance indicators and reconstruct industrial process data for improving the accuracy of fault diagnosis. Additionally, permutation importance is introduced into PRLAE to select the feature related to fault diagnosis. Guided by the feature filtering ranking results based on key indicators for predicting performance, highly contributing features are selected to solve the challenge of evaluating the best fault diagnosis feature. The Tennessee-Eastman Process (TEP) is used to verify the performance of PRFFLAE. The simulation results indicate that PRFFLAE can effectively extract fault-related features and achieves better accuracy than other feature extraction methods.

articleTitle: An adaptive path tracking controller for autonomous vehicles based on the Pure Pursuit algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the problem of unmanned vehicle path tracking, this paper proposes an adaptive path tracking controller based on the Pure Pursuit(PP) method. The controller replaces the traditional manual selection of the lookahead distance in the traditional PP algorithm with the Deep Q Network (DQN) algorithm. The controller dynamically adjusts the lookahead distance based on lateral error, heading error, and vehicle speed to adapt to different operating conditions and improve path tracking performance. This paper obtained the Deep Q Network - Pure Pursuit (DQN-PP) adaptive controller model through reinforcement learning training. In order to verify the control effect of the DQN-PP adaptive controller, this paper designed a simulation experiment and analyzed the experimental results. The results show that compared with the traditional method, the DQN-PP adaptive controller has better path tracking performance, and the average error value of path tracking has been reduced by 21%. This paper provides an effective adaptive solution for path tracking control in autonomous vehicles and has practical application value.

articleTitle: Safety Control of Time-Delay Systems with Input Disturbances in Dynamic Environments
abstract: To ensure the safe control of complex systems in real-world scenarios, it becomes essential to establish their robustness in dynamic environments while accounting for uncertainties within the system. This paper places specific emphasis on the safety of systems exposed to input disturbances in dynamic environments. This paper proposes the concept of tunable input-to-state safe environmental control barrier functions (TISSf-ECBFs) to facilitate the attainment of secure control within such systems. Even when dealing with input delays, this paper guarantees system safety through the implementation of appropriate predictors. The efficacy of the proposed approach is ultimately showcased within the domain of an adaptive cruise control (ACC) ploblem.

articleTitle: A Consistency Diagnosis Method of Series-Connected Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Charging Curve Transformation
abstract: In new energy storage applications, lithium-ion batteries are usually used in parallel and series connections to meet the power and energy requirements. However, the inevitable capacity and state of charge (SOC) inconsistency within the series battery pack can decrease the available capacity and result in accelerated aging and safety issues. In this paper, a consistency diagnosis method based on charging curve transformation is utilized to diagnose capacity and SOC differences within the battery pack. Since traditional curve transformation method impose high data storage and computational requirement to battery management system, it is difficult to implement the algorithm in real-time. A charging throughput-voltage (QV) curve transformation model is proposed and the consistency diagnosis is realized by parameter identification of the model. Finally, the proposed method is verified on a battery pack with six cells connected in series. Experimental results indicate that the propose method can achieve good diagnosis accuracy on both capacity inconsistency and SOC inconsistency conditions.

articleTitle: Identification and Compensation Method for Detection Signal Unbalanced-Phase-Delay-Error of Hemispherical Resonator Gyro
abstract: High precision vector control is an important guarantee for the performance of Hemispherical Resonator Gyros(HRG). In this paper, the control method of HRG is introduced at first, and the negative impact caused by detection signal unbalanced-phase-delay-error(UPDE) of HRG on multi-loop amplitude-modulation control, standing wave azimuth calculation and control vector decomposition is analyzed. On this basis, the error identification method and a closed-loop error compensation method are proposed based on the control circuit. The effectiveness of the proposed methods were verified through experiments in kind, and the experimental results demonstrate that the performance of each control loop were significantly optimized and the non-ideal precession of hemispherical resonator standing wave was effectively suppressed. Ultimately, the accuracy of gyro under two output forms of angular position and angular rate are further improved and the method proposed is also widely applicable to other kinds of Coriolis Vibrating Gyros(CVG).

articleTitle: Positioning and Transmission Using Zigbee-Based Environment Monitoring by Power-Over-Fiber with Signal
abstract: A positioning and transmission using Zigbee-based environment monitoring system is proposed on the Power-Over-Fiber with Signal. The system can achieve target localization and information transmission for the target positioning nodes with a laser input of 55mW. It can also perform data collection of environmental sensing parameters.

articleTitle: A Review of Image and Point Cloud Fusion-Based 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Driving
abstract: With the application of multi-sensor fusion technologies in object detection, Self-driving automobiles have received more and more attention. The complementary advantages of different types of sensors (camera, LIDAR) can provide accurate and reliable environment perception for autonomous driving systems. We categorize the 3D object identification methods based on image and point cloud fusion into early, intermediate, and late, focusing on the camera and LIDAR combination in autonomous driving, furthermore, the characteristics of various methods and the performance of different models are analyzed and compared. Finally, the possible future opportunities and challenges for 3D object detection are evaluated.

articleTitle: A Human-Robot Interaction Dual-Arm Robot System For Power Distribution Network
abstract: The current live-line maintenance robot in the power distribution network faces a significant challenge. The commonly used operational methods have their limitations. Teleoperation heavily relies on the operator's experience and manual intervention, which places a burden on the operator. Autonomous operation requires a high level of intelligence from the robot, which is currently insufficient to handle the complexities of the power grid environment. To address the challenge, this paper proposes a human-robot interaction (HRI) dual-arm robot system. This system includes a human-in-the-loop operational framework, where human operators handle tasks that are difficult to automate using HRI devices. The robot's autonomous operations are guided by a standard trajectory library constructed using Dynamic Movement Primitives (DMP). Several experiments were conducted to validate the feasibility of the proposed robot system.

articleTitle: Research on Association Rule Mining and Knowledge Graph Construction for Low-Carbon Scheme Design in Transmission Line Passageways
abstract: Due to the complex coupling effect of multiple factors, the selection of transmission line routes is mainly dependent on manual methods. Utilizing artificial intelligence technology to mine the hidden association rules in the regulations of the power system and constructing a Knowledge graph can improve the efficiency of transmission line route selection and reduce the cost of manual operations. Therefore, this paper proposes a method of mining associated rules for the design of transmission line channels using Knowledge graphs, aiming to overcome the limitations of manual handling in transmission line route selection. The efficiency of line selection is enhanced through the rich semantic information provided by the Knowledge graph.

articleTitle: Exploring Highway Overtaking and Lane Changing Based on Soft Actor Critic for Discrete Algorithm
abstract: Highway is one of the important scenarios faced by autonomous driving. However, in this scenario, smart cars need to meet the requirements of high efficiency (i.e. high speed) and high safety, and provide passengers with high comfort (i.e. fewer lane changes), which poses a serious challenge to autonomous driving. This work uses highway-env as the simulation platform and proposes a discrete action based SACD (soft actor critical for discrete) algorithm that combines CNN(convolutional neural networks) and LSTM(long short term memory) to solve the safety, efficiency, and comfort issues of smart cars during highway driving. The simulation results indicate that although smart cars have high driving efficiency, they perform poorly in terms of safety and comfort. Based on this, this work adopts the idea of distributed sampling and proposes a dual buffers structure combined with safety module. The final simulation results show that the introduction of dual buffers combined with safety module architecture can significantly improve the safety and comfort of smart cars driving on highway while maintaining high efficiency.

articleTitle: Topology and Improved Selective Harmonic Elimination Method for the Series-Connected T-Type Multi - Level Inverter
abstract: The T-type three-level inverter (T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>3LI) topology has been extensively employed in various industrial applications. This article further proposes a novel series-connected T-type multi-level inverter (SCT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>MLI), whose phase leg is formed by two series-connected T-type three-level inverter phase legs. First, the basic operating principle of the SCT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>MLI is analyzed, and the impact mechanism of different switching states on the dc-link capacitor voltages is obtained. An improved selective harmonic elimination (ISHE) method is subsequently designed, which can simultaneously restrain the common-mode voltage (CMV) and eliminate the selective low -order harmonics, while the performance of ac output voltage is not influenced. In addition, the voltages across dc-side capacitor voltages are controlled by adopting redundant switching states. When using the proposed ISHE method, the CMV is significantly restricted in comparison with the traditional SHE method. The evaluation results prove the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Self-Attention Multi-Scale Pyramid Stereo Matching Network
abstract: At present, the learning-based stereo matching networks focus more on the effective extraction of features and less on the effective selection of features and at the same time, stereo matching of weak texture areas are still a difficult research point. To tackle the problem above, a self-attention multi-scale pyramid stereo matching network (SAMPSM-Net) is proposed. The channel and spatial feature fusion module is used to effectively select the channel and spatial features, strengthens the expression of effective channels and spatial features, and suppresses the obstruction of redundant features. Moreover, the multi-scale pyramid aggregation module is used to improve the matching accuracy of the network for weak texture regions. Several stereo matching benchmark tests show that the proposed SAMPSM-Net achieves competitive results compared with other models.

articleTitle: Development of Cloud Service Platform for Suspension Durability Testing System
abstract: The suspension durability testing system can complete fatigue life testing and the simulation of the real-world working condition of automotive air suspension in the laboratory. However, due to its self-enclosed architecture, it usually does not have functions such as remote interaction and unified data management. To address the above issues, we propose an industrial cloud service platform for the testing system in this paper. Specifically, by analyzing the principles of the testing system and the requirements of the cloud service platform, we rigorously design the data forms and functions on the cloud platform. Moreover, our designed platform completes the data communication between the end layer, edge layer, and application layer based on the ThinkPHP framework and the TCP Socket communication protocol. Thus, it is possible to realize the management of the user information and the transmission, storage, and remote display of the testing data, making our platform capable of remote monitoring. We implement our platform as a fully-functional software. The testing results indicate that the developed cloud service platform of the suspension durability testing system can accurately monitor the testing system in real-time and standardize the management of testing data.

articleTitle: Research on the algorithm of searching building contour line by line segment based on Revit
abstract: The extraction of building contour line is an important computer-aided design work for the layout of building climbing frame walkway plates. So a study is conducted on the identification of building components and their characteristics for planar CAD drawings, and an algorithm for searching building contour line by line segment is proposed. Import CAD building plan data in Revit, read CAD drawing geometric information through Teigha class library, identify the walls forming the building frame, analyze the geometric features of the walls forming the building contour, the algorithm of searching the building contour line is proposed by line segment, which can effectively solve the problem of identifying the corner contour of wall break and inward depression, and can automatically extract the whole building contour from the plan CAD drawing data, laying the foundation for the optimized layout of the auxiliary climbing frame walkway plates. The experimental results show that the line segment search algorithm can effectively extract the contour of buildings from existing CAD drawing data, improving the efficiency of building climbing frame BIM modeling.

articleTitle: Predictive Active Disturbance Rejection Control with Matched Delay for 2-DOF Helicopter Under Disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates the control problem of 2-DOF helicopter with different input delays and disturbances. To handle the different delays in the dynamics of pitch and yaw angles, a new predictive active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) featured with matched delay information is proposed. The proposed predictive ADRC consists of three steps, including transferring the actual inputs to virtual inputs with matched delay, constructing the transferred virtual inputs by ADRC strategy, and designing a predictive module of actual inputs. To show the capability of the proposed ADRC, the comparative simulations with traditional ADRC are provided under different cases of delays.

articleTitle: On Cluster Consensus of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems with Unknown Control Inputs
abstract: This article proposes a novel distributed adaptive cluster consensus protocol for nonlinear multi-agent systems with unknown non-zero control inputs. The protocol relies on local state information, operates in a fully distributed manner, and serves as a foundation for our future research to achieve fully distributed consensus in nonlinear multi-agent systems without requiring knowledge of the leader's control input bounds.

articleTitle: Frequency Dispersion Effects on Time-Varying Magnetic Field-Induced Cellular Transmembrane Potentials: A Simulation Study
abstract: In this work, we developed a simulation model to evaluate the effect of frequency dispersion effects on the time-varying magnetic field (TMF)-induced transmembrane potential (TMP) of cells. The simulation results show that the effect of frequency dispersion effect on TMP is not obvious when the frequency of the time-varying field is low, but when the frequency of the time-varying field exceeds 20 MHz, there is a large enhancement of TMP, and the effect of frequency dispersion effect on TMP becomes more and more obvious as the frequency increases. In addition, by comparing the distribution patterns of induced electric field and TMP on the cell membrane and the effect of dispersion effect on both, the feasibility of the TMP calculation model with dispersion effect constructed in this paper is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A New Efficient Transformer With Blueprint Pixel Network for Image Super-Resolution
abstract: In recent years, Transformer-based methods have achieved remarkable results in various vision tasks, including super-resolution (SR). However, the difficulty of stabilizing the training process and reducing the model complexity without compromising performance has limited their applications in lightweight SR tasks. To address these challenges, we propose a new efficient Transformer with blueprint pixel network (TBPN). Specifically, we first apply pixel normalization instead of batch normalization in the self-attention module, which makes the training process more efficient and stable. Then, we adopt a blueprint separation convolution to assemble depth features after the attention calculation to reduce the model parameters effectively. To exploit the long-range image dependency, our TBPN uses multiple blueprint pixel in Transformer modules (BPTMs), which aggregate the blueprint convolution and the embedded pixel normalization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TBPN achieves a better performance with less complexity than existing Transformer-based and convolution-based SR methods.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Model-Based Design for UAV Intelligent Decision-Making and Control System
abstract: Researching and developing relevant algorithms for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle(UAV) intelligent decision-making and control systems involves a lot of experimentation and testing. However, utilizing advanced languages such as C/C++ and Python for system development, testing, and hardware deployment takes time and effort. In order to solve this issue, a model-based design (MBD) method for designing and implementing UAV intelligent decision-making and control systems is presented in this paper. This method builds a model of an intelligent decision-making and control system for UAVs using MATLAB/Simulink. It deploys the flight control system to the PIXHAWK embedded hardware through automatic code generation and deploys the intelligent decision-making system to the Jetson Xavier NX edge computing device. The high-fidelity UAV dynamics model is deployed to the Box03 high-performance real-time simulation machine. These operations achieve real-time simulation of the system's software/hardware-in-the-loop. Finally, the UAV dynamics model is replaced with an actual UAV system. The experiments demonstrate that UAVs with intelligent decision-making and control algorithms accomplish real-time tasks such as obstacle avoidance and path planning. The design of the UAV's intelligent decision-making and control system can be achieved more conveniently and efficiently through the aforementioned methods, providing valuable insights for further research and application in this field.

articleTitle: H-Infinity Control of Network T-S Fuzzy System for Multi-Area Power Systems Under Deception Attack
abstract: The problem of Load Frequency Control (LFC) is investigated in this paper, and a new event-triggered scheme for T-S fuzzy control with deception attacks is proposed in multi-area power systems. First, the load frequency control system being considered is represented using the T-S fuzzy model. Second, the event triggering mechanism is taken into account to realize effective utilization of network bandwidth resources. In addition, a random variable satisfying Bernoulli stochastic binary distribution is used to describe the effects of random network attacks. Based on this model, the main results for ensuring the asymptotic stability of systems were established using Lyapunov stability theory and linear matrix inequality techniques. Under sufficient conditions for derivation, the controller gain is given. Lastly, the feasibility of the designed controller was validates through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Construction Site Layout Optimization Algorithm Based on MOPSO
abstract: This paper investigates the construction site layout problem. A multi-objective optimization problem is formulated with the objectives of minimizing the layout cost and the negative impact coefficient of the site scheme. A piecewise linear attenuation model is established to describe the negative influences among different areas, and the penalty function method is employed to handle the constraint conditions. Subsequently, the problem is solved using the Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm. Instead of seeking a single optimal solution, this study focuses on finding as many mutually non-dominated solutions as possible for decision-makers to choose from. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is validated through experimental case studies. The results demonstrate that the method can provide reliable layout schemes that can be applied in practical decision-making processes.

articleTitle: Fast Terminal Quasi-Sliding Mode Control for Spacecraft Formation Flying Systems via RBFNN
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of relative control for spacecraft formation flying systems. With elliptical orbit, the model is built by relative position vector. To improve the tracking performance, a controller is designed and proven stable as a fast terminal quasi-sliding mode controller with feedback control based on radial basis function neural network (RBFNN). The performance of the proposed method is validated with numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Master-Slave Vascular Interventional Robot with Passive Haptic Feedback
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel master-slave vascular interventional robot aimed at reducing the radiation exposure of interventionalists during endovascular procedures. The unique design of our robot enables surgeons to utilize their traditional interventional skills seamlessly. On the master side, we incorporate haptic interfaces with magnetorheological fluids (MRF) and a magnetic flux guidance structure to offer passive haptic feedback along the operating catheter. This feature enhances the surgeon's tactile perception during the catheterization. Meanwhile, on the slave side, we utilize the current of the DC motor to estimate the contact force between the catheter and the vessel. Additionally, the bionic graspers imitate the natural movements of a surgeon's hand, while the friction wheel structure allows for the continuous delivery of the catheter/guidewire. We have also implemented different force feedback thresholds that enable the surgeon to perceive any changes in the resistance of the catheter within the vessel during the insertion procedure. To validate the effectiveness of the robotic system, we conduct evaluation experiments in vitro. The results indicate that the catheter-based haptic force feedback can provide an immersive operating experience during the endovascular procedure. Compared to this robot, the joystick operation robot requires the surgeons to learn new methods to control, so our robot reduces the cognitive workload of the surgeons.

articleTitle: Robust Attitude Control for Flying-Wing UAV Using Modified Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion
abstract: This paper proposes a modified incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion (MINDI) control scheme for attitude tracking control of flying-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). Based on the incremental dynamic inversion formulation, the angular rate controller is designed to alleviate the nonlinearity and coupling characteristics of the flying-wing configuration. Then, in order to address the impact of factors such as angular acceleration measurement errors and actuator faults on the control performance, a super-twisting-like fixed-time convergence algorithm is introduced to replace the linear control law in the nominal INDI method, ensuring rapid convergence of tracking errors. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively mitigates the impact of such errors and faults. Compared to the nominal INDI, the modified method exhibits stronger fault tolerance and robustness in the attitude tracking control of the flying-wing UAV.

articleTitle: Research on Mobile Robot Path Planning in Angle-Guided Ant Colony Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Addressing the issues of slow convergence, low smoothness, and long computation time in the basic Ant Colony Optimization algorithm, this paper proposes a novel variant of the Ant Colony Optimization algorithm. The proposed algorithm improves the heuristic function by introducing angle guidance. It incorporates the idea of the estimation function from the A* algorithm to enhance the direction toward the target point. Simultaneously, the information pheromone update rule is improved, with increased pheromone concentration on the optimal paths and reduced concentration on the worst paths, while introducing a dynamic pheromone evaporation factor. These enhancements increase search effectiveness and quality while also speeding up algorithm convergence. To test the efficacy of the proposed algorithm, the authors conducted simulation comparisons with three existing algorithms. The experimental findings show that the suggested method is capable of producing pathways with higher smoothness, fewer turns, and faster convergence.

articleTitle: Stability control of VSG based on damped inertia adjustment under small disturbances
abstract: Virtual synchronous generators (VSGs) simulate the damping and inertia characteristics of synchronous generators (SGs), but also introduces the transient stability problem faced by synchronous generators. That is, the operating point of VSGs fluctuates in the power-angle characteristic curve when it is disturbed, which has an impact on grid stability. While the conventional rotational inertia regulation strategy is not sensitive enough and is susceptible to noise disturbance. In this paper, by analyzing the relationship between inertia and angular frequency and considering the damping ratio constraint, an inertia and damping ratio regulation strategy is proposed to improve the small signal stability of VSGs. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Research on the Energy Storage Device of Super Capacitor for Electric Vehicles
abstract: With the popularity of electric vehicles, the support of national policies and the inflow of market funds, the electric vehicle charging station and its operation management system have been greatly developed, and the electric vehicle charging fire events occur frequently, thereby it is very important to enhance the charging safety. Because of the features of battery management strategy, such as large performance difference, off-line delivery and difficult to control, its BMS is not reliable in charge safety assessment. In order to evaluate the health status of power battery effectively, advanced information processing technology and safety evaluation algorithm are needed. The three-phase isolated DC/DC converter was selected as the transmission circuit, the double closed loop control model for such kind converter was designed, so as to ensure the bus voltage stability. When DC bus voltage increases, super capacitor (SC) is charged, otherwise, it is discharged. Testing results proved the advantages of proposed control algorithm for that converter via DSP of SC.

articleTitle: Short-Term Passenger Flow Prediction of Railway Station Based on Improved LSTM
abstract: Accurately predicting passenger arrivals helps ease the pressure on rail passenger station operations. In order to realize the traffic forecasting of railway passenger station, according to the time distribution characteristics of passenger flow, traffic forecasting method of railway passenger station is studied. Using the ticket data as the research object, this paper research the time distribution of passenger traffic flow in railway station under different time dimensions, hierarchical clustering algorithm and threshold clustering algorithm are taken to cluster the passenger flow, and the improved LSTM traffic forecasting model was built. Aiming at LSTM model input data hierarchical segmentaion scale is large, which lead to the depth of network layers is not enough, we rebuild the LSTM model. The method is verified by the actual AFC data of QingHe Station, the prediction results of traditional prediction model are compared. It shows that: the improved model has the higher prediction accuracy than other traditional forecasting models, mean absolute error is 10% lower. It shows that this method can better describe the time correlation of passenger flow, and deeply mine the internal mechanism of passenger flow change.

articleTitle: Structure Design and Implementation of The Automatic Bowl Feeding Device
abstract: With the rapid development of automatic control technology, the automatic bowl supply function has great application value and prospects in many life occasions, such as the automatic cooking in the canteen, the automatic bowl supply in the restaurant, the automatic processing of the assembly line and so on. Therefore, this paper designs and produces a fully automatic bowl feeding device to realize the function of automatic bowl feeding in multiple scenes. Through the fully automatic bowl feeding device, the efficiency of bowl adding can be improved, at the same time, the labor cost can be saved, and the application in unmanned environment can be realized. Through the production of the real object and the analysis of the experimental data, the fully automatic bowl feeding device can efficiently complete the corresponding functions, meet the design requirements and indicators, and can be applied to the automatic bowl feeding function in canteens, restaurants, automatic assembly lines and other occasions, and provide a safe and environmental protection application research basis for automatic bowl feeding.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Graph Matching Network Using Topological Features
abstract: Graph similarity computation is an important problem for research in the field of complex networks, which can further facilitate tasks such as graph classification, clustering and similarity search. Graph similarity is usually measured by the graph edit distance (GED) metric; however, the exact computation of GED is an NP-hard problem with high computational complexity and difficult to solve. In recent years, graph similarity computation using graph neural networks (GNN) has emerged to achieve efficient metric results. To fully exploit the deep information in the graph and obtain more accurate graph similarity computation results, we propose a multidimensional graph matching network model using graph topological information. Firstly, to capture the rich fine-grained information in the graph, a multidimensional graph matching module is proposed in the model, including cross-graph feature interactions at the node-graph level as well as at the multi-level graph-graph level, and the expressiveness of the model is improved by the graph matching module. Secondly, graph topology feature matching is added in the similarity calculation to focus on how similar a pair of graphs are in terms of topology and to utilize topology information more fully. We conducted experiments on real-world datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: Hardware-Aware Quantization and Performance Evaluation for Tensor Accelerator VTA
abstract: In order to improve the quantization inference accuracy of the deep learning compiler framework TVM(Tensor Virtual Machine), we proposed a quantization deployment inference scheme, which is designed for accelerated INT8 calculation of deep neural network based on VTA, using quantization-compilation collaborative optimization algorithm. Firstly we analyzed the limitations of quantization scale calculation in the original Post-Training Quantization scheme of TVM. According to the Hardware-Aware strategy, we carried out the fixed-point calculation optimization of scale and other model operators in the process of QAT (Quantization Aware Training) to optimize the integer tensor acceleration characteristics of VTA(Versatile Tensor Accelerator), meanwhile the fixed-point inference error including quantization error was considered. The scheme is hardware-friendly, reduces the data memory occupancy, and can be used for multiple tasks such as image classification and object detection. Experiment results show that compared with the original TVM scheme, the model inference speed and accuracy are significantly improved, which provides an efficient and lightweight solution for deep neural network model deployment using fixed-point accelerator.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant Scheduling Optimization of Cloud Workflow Based on Multi-objective Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Many scientific workflow applications can be deployed on cloud computing services to obtain convenient services. However, due to various hardware and software problems, virtual machine faults may occur, and workflow fault-tolerant scheduling is necessary. Reliability is a measure of the possibility that workflow will not fail under fault-tolerant scheduling. Previous algorithms did not simultaneously consider the three objectives, i.e. completion time, resource usage and reliability. It is quite challenging to make the algorithm perform well on all three objectives. An enhanced multi-objective optimization algorithm is proposed in this paper to generate scheduling strategies, alongside the development of a heuristic fault-tolerant allocation strategy. The experimental results demonstrate an effective improvement in the overall performance of the three objectives when compared to other recent algorithms.

articleTitle: Generalized Error-Based Active Disturbance Rejection Control for 2-DOF Unmanned Helicopter with Time-Varying Disturbances
abstract: In this paper, the control problem of 2-DOF unmanned helicopter with time-varying disturbances is studied and a new generalized error-based active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) is proposed. The innovation of this paper mainly lies in two aspects. To solve the problem that the reference signal is acquired instantaneously and the derivative of the reference signal is unknown, an error-based design is established. In order to improve the estimation of polynomial time-varying disturbances, a generalized extended state observer (ESO) is designed by increasing the expansive order of disturbance estimation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by three types of time-varying disturbances.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Fixed-Time Cooperative Guidance law with Impact time Constraints
abstract: In this article, we propose fixed-time cooperative guidance laws for achieving simultaneous attacks on a maneuvering target by multiple missiles at desired terminal angles. The 3-D guidance commands encompass radial acceleration along the line-of-sight (LOS) direction to enable coordinated attacks, as well as normal acceleration perpendicular to the LOS direction to ensure interception with terminal angle constraints. Firstly, the radial acceleration is designed from a nonlinear fixed-time cooperative protocol to achieve the fixed-time consensus of impact times for multiple missiles. Secondly, based on the fixed-time sliding manifold and fixed-time reaching law, the normal acceleration is designed for each missile to converge the LOS angle to the desired value within a fixed time. Furthermore, the unknown target acceleration is treated as a system disturbance, estimated by fixed-time observers, and compensated in the guidance commands, ensuring effective handling of uncertainties introduced by the target's acceleration. Finally, simulations are conducted to demonstrate the performance of the guidance law in the 3-D guidance scenario.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Formation Control under Dynamic Complex Configuration Transformation
abstract: In this paper, the formation control of multi-agent system based on complex configuration transformation in complex domain is studied. An event-triggered formation algorithm under dynamic complex configuration transformation is proposed, which solves the problem of insufficient communication resources during formation realization, and allows the desired formation configuration to be complex and variable. The proposed algorithm can ensure that the desired formation control target can be realized flexibly. In addition, a simulation example is used to verify the feasibility of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Compound Property Learning Based on Molecular Fingerprints and Complex Network Metrics
abstract: Molecular fingerprints map molecular structures into vectorized sequences and can be applied to QSAR/QSPR model learning to predict molecular properties. In this paper, we obtain fingerprint embedding matrix based on molecular structure, while deriving complex network metrics based on molecular graph structure. Inserting complex network metrics into molecular fingerprints, we construct a new molecular embedding fingerprint and construct a better CNN-based QSAR/QSPR model for compounds with the same/similar graph structures. Experiments on relative retention time prediction of PCB dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Landslide Susceptibility Using Machine Learning Based on Information Value Sampling Method
abstract: In landslide susceptibility prediction using machine learning (ML) models, the selection of appropriate negative samples significantly impacts the accuracy of the predictions. Many existing studies tend to randomly choose negative samples from the entire research area or specific attribute areas such as low slopes, leading to inaccuracies and biases that decrease the reliability of susceptibility mapping. To address this issue, this paper proposes an ML model based on the coupled information value (IV) method for susceptibility modeling. In this approach, the attribute values of environmental factors are transformed into information values, representing their contribution to landslides, using the information quantity method. Very low and low prone areas are then identified based on these information values, and random points are selected from these areas as negative samples for training and verifying subsequent machine learning models, which include the Random Forest (RF) model and Support Vector Machine (SVM) model.The study focuses on the Three Gorges reservoir area in the Zigui-Badong area as an example. The comparative analysis of models trained using traditional sampling methods reveals that the RF model and SVM model, which were sampled using the information value method, achieve accuracies of 95.33% and 91.13%, respectively. In contrast, models trained using traditional sampling methods achieve accuracies of 90.43% and 88.69%, respectively.

articleTitle: Detecting Fake Human Pose
abstract: We propose a special attention-based authentication model for fake human pose images, that is, multi-scale feature authentication model. The model parses an image into eight parts by human parsing, the source image, the background image and the human image as the global information are extracted through the chain attention mechanism. Six local information, such as face and limbs, are input into Light-VGG to capture local features. Finally, the extracted features of multiple scales are fused for authenticity detection. Lack of human fake pose image data, we use three algorithms based on DeepFashion to generate fake human pose images with the target pose and the appearance of the source human. We construct FakePose, a dataset containing 3000 pairs of real and fake human pose images. Experiments and the quantitative comparison of the two state-of-the-art baseline methods on FakePose demonstrate the effectiveness of our authentication model, and the authentication accuracy has reached 95.2%.

articleTitle: Atrial Fibrillation Detection Method Based on Inception-CNN-BiLSTM Model
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) automatic classification is an important auxiliary diagnostic method for diagnosis of arrhythmia. In order to improve the accuracy of beat extraction of dynamic ECG anomalies, a method for atrial fibrillation de-tection and beat classification based on Inception-CNN - BiLSTM is proposed. First, wavelet denoising and heartbeat splitting are carried out for ECG signals in the original dataset to remove interference in the original ECG signal and unify data dimensions for model training. Then, the data is trained and tested by using the Inception-CNN-BiLSTM model. The model outputs are divided into three categories: atrial fibrillation (A), normal (N) and other arrhythmia (O). Finally, several evaluation metrics are used to evaluate the performance of the model. It is found that the performance of the proposed model is improved and the number of parameters could be reduced compared to the CNN-BiLSTM model, and the accuracy rate is increased by 0.75% and 4.87% compared to the CNN and BiLSTM models, respectively.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning and Disturbance Observer Based Optimal Control for Uncertain Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the robust adaptive optimal control problem for linear systems in the presence of matching uncertainties. A nominal controller utilizing Q-Iearning algorithm is designed for the nominal linear system without uncertainties. Introducing a disturbance observer serves the purpose of actively estimating uncertainties, enabling proactive compensation for matching uncertainties. The analysis of the closed-loop system's stability under the robust adaptive optimal controller is conducted, presenting sufficient conditions to ensure its stability. Finally, the control algorithm is validated using a two-wheeled mobile robot as the experimental platform.

articleTitle: Design of Adaptive Control Law for Ship Second-Order Nonlinear Systems Based on Backstepping Method
abstract: For nonlinear systems, backstepping control algorithm is a widely used control algorithm whose basic principle achieves control by recursion. By dividing the complex system into several independent sub-systems, controlling the sub-systems individually and using the Lyapunov function to judge the stability of the system, the control of the whole nonlinear system is achieved. In this paper, the second-order nonlinear system of ship heading is studied. Combining backstepping with adaptive thought while considering system interference items. The unknown parameters of the system are traced and estimated, and the designed controller is simulated by Simulink. The simulation results validate that the designed controller has better stability and control performance, while reducing the impact of system disturbance.

articleTitle: Remote sensing image small target detection network based on optimized YOLOv5s
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an enhanced model named YOLOv5s-SMF, which is a refinement of YOLOv5s designed to address the challenges of small object detection in remote sensing images, including small target size, limited feature information, and complex background. It introduces the SPD-Conv as a re-placement for the original downsampling method, reducing information loss during downsampling. Moreover, a tiny object detection layer is added to fully utilize the features of small objects. Adopting a multi view fusion module to enhance the model's comprehensive perception ability to address complex background issues. Additionally, a feature refineme-nt fusion module is used to further improve feature extraction capabilities. Experimental results on the Visdrone2019 dataset demonstrate that the YOLOv5s-SMF model exhibits significant improvements over the original model, with a 10.7% improvement in mAP@0.5 and a 7.2% increase in mAP@0.5:0.95.

articleTitle: Fault State Identification and Active Suppression of Zero Sequence Oscillation in Resonant Grounded Distribution Networks
abstract: Resonant grounding distribution networks generally typically uses overcompensation to prevent the arc suppression coil and system-to-ground capacitance from creating a zero-sequence loop resonance once the fault is cleared. This paper proposes an active injection method to identify the fault status and an active suppression method for zero-sequence resonance to solve this problem. Firstly, the online identification of the impedance parameter of the system to the ground employs the recursive least square (RLS) algorithm. The system's fault condition is then ascertained based on this impedance identification value. Secondly, as soon as the fault disappears, appropriate resistor is put into dissipate the fault transient energy. Finally, two-stage model predictive control (TSMPC) is used to adjust the injected current, clamp the neutral-to-ground voltage and suppress system oscillation. On this basis, the optimal dissipation resistance calculation method is derived. The correctness and feasibility of the method and control strategy are confirmed through both theoretical analysis and simulation.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Convolutional Neural Network for SSVEP Task
abstract: Steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) are widely utilized in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) due to their exceptional stability and performance. However, extracting abundant information for object recognition in a deep learning framework remains a formidable task. To tackle this challenge, this paper introduces a multi-scale spatio-temporal convolutional neural network (MS-STCNN). The network considers the combination of multi-scale spatial filters and temporal filters from both reference signals and SSVEP signals, resulting in enhanced feature information extraction and improved model performance. The detection of SSVEP is accomplished by considering spatio-temporal information at different scales and employing distinct weights to combine the correlation scores obtained from the final correlation analysis layer for various categories. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, experiments are conducted using the Benchmark dataset. The results demonstrate a significant enhancement in the classification performance of SSVEP achieved by proposed method.

articleTitle: Application of Normal Vectors and Color Features in Semantic Segmentation of Colored Point Clouds
abstract: Point cloud semantic segmentation is one of the fundamental tasks for 3D scene understanding. The solution based on fully convolutional neural network is the mainstream practice of 3D semantic segmentation. Recent works combining transformers have achieved stunning performance. However, most of these methods focused more on the 3D space coordinates, little attention has been drawn to the normal vectors and color features, which play a significant role in LIDAR point cloud registration and 3D rendering tasks. In this paper, we propose several novel modules utilizing these features to improve the semantic segmentation of colored point clouds. To leverage the normal vector features, we propose an efficient normal vector constraint to supervise the results of semantic segmentation through robust geometric relationships between objects. To harness the color information, we design the relative color encoding to improve the position encoding module in transformer architecture. Furthermore, we introduce a color-domain contrastive learning method that performs neighborhood search in the color domain, enhancing feature learning from distant contexts. Extensive experiments show that our model achieves better performance than baseline method.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised Training for Bearing Fault Diagnosis via Momentum Contrast Learning
abstract: With the development of modern industry, data-driven intelligent fault diagnosis has become increasingly popular. The conflict between the need for large amounts of data and the high cost of manual labeling has led researchers to focus on how to better utilize the data itself to reduce costs. In the case of vibration signals, factors such as the category and severity of failure, mechanical operating environment, bearing operating speed, and compound failures can influence them in real environments. These excessive uncontrollable factors make datasets collected from industrial environments nearly unusable. In this paper, we address this issue by introducing momentum contrast. The model is trained by treating all samples except the current one as negative samples and comparing them with positive sample. This approach avoids the need to know the number of fault categories in the dataset in advance. Based on this idea, we conducted experimental validation and found that the pre-trained model possesses high classification accuracy after fine-tuning.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Business Model for Orderly Charging of EVs Under the Unifled Construction and Operation
abstract: Under the background of the current oil energy crisis and serious environmental pollution, the contradiction between energy supply and demand is becoming more and more prominent, which has aroused great attention around the world, and the popularization of electric vehicles on a large scale has become an inevitable trend. The uncontrolled access of large-scale electric vehicles to the power grid will have an impact on the power grid, bringing a series of problems such as overloading of the distribution network, power quality and so on. Therefore, this paper designs and analyzes the orderly charging business model for electric vehicles. First of all, the definition and current situation of EV orderly charging are analyzed, and the main conclusions and results of typical EV orderly charging projects at home and abroad are also analyzed. Then the business model of electric vehicles in Shanghai is analyzed as an example, and the business model of orderly charging of electric vehicles under the background of unified construction and operation is proposed. Combined with the development of China's industry and electric vehicles, it puts forward suggestions for future development with regard to the limitations of the orderly charging of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Robust Non-Fragile H∞ Control for Active Suspension System with Parameter Uncertainty
abstract: An approach to devising multi-objective robust non-fragile H∞ controller for vehicle suspension systems with parameter uncertainties and controller disturbances is put forward in this paper. Based on the performance evaluation indicators of the suspension system, Ride comfort is reflected through H∞ performance, while using state-space ellipsoids to capture time-domain hard constraints. The circumstance for the presence of multi-objective robust non-fragile H∞controller is proposed, as derived from the Lyapunov stability theory, and the designed controller can be obtained by solving a linear matrix inequality (LMI). The simulation results of quarter vehicle suspension model show that although there is parameter uncertainty and controller gain variation, the proposed control strategy can achieve good ride comfort under given constraint conditions and meet the requirements of dynamic suspension deflection, dynamic tire load, and required control force.

articleTitle: RBFNN Based Platoon Control for CAVs with Input Constraints
abstract: This paper studies the platoon control problem for connected automated vehicles with control input constraints and model uncertainties, and a RBFNN based distributed adaptive platoon control scheme is developed for the considered vehicle platoon. Firstly, a discrete vehicle longitudinal dynamic model is established by using the sampling method, and then a constant spacing strategy based distributed vehicle platoon controller is designed by combining backstepping method and RBFNN. RBFNN is used to approximate model, and a constraint function is used to limit the vehicle control input to preset domain. Single vehicle state stability and vehicle platoon stability are analyzed by using Lyapunov method. Finally, simulation experiments are carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. Simulation results show that the scheme can guarantee stable movement of vehicle platoon with the desired distance, while satisfying amplitude and change rate constraints of control input.

articleTitle: A Surface Defect Detection Algorithm for PCB Based on MobileViT-YOLO
abstract: With the development of printed circuit board towards higher density and higher reliability, printed circuit board may exist many kinds of surface defect like open circuit, short, spur and so on. It has been becoming a new challenge that how to detect these surface defect. In this paper, we propose an improved model called MobileViT-YOLO based on YOLOX. The model uses MobileViT as the backbone network, a new multi-scale feature fusion structure called ASFFPN, and a decoupled head structure. On the PCB defect dataset released by Peking University, MobileViT-YOLO achieves an accuracy of 98.45%, which is 0.76% more accurate than YOLOX with 17.6% fewer parameters.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Network Dynamic Surface Tracking Control of a VTOL Aircraft
abstract: The problem of asymptotic tracking control for a vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft system is addressed in this paper, in which unknown external disturbances and nonlinear dynamics are added. Unknown nonlinear dynamics are deal with by using neural networks, and some adaptive laws are addressed. Additionally, some control laws for unknown parameters are developed to address unknown nonlinearities resulting from the analysis process. Based on the dynamic surface control approach and neural network control, the adaptive control laws with dynamic surface method and neural network are developed for the system. The results show that the developed control laws insure that the system under consideration asymptotically follows the given desired signal, and the system's tracking errors can converge to zero. At last, a simulation case is shown to validate the effectiveness of developed control strategies.

articleTitle: DRM-SLAM: Robust Visual SLAM Based on Dynamic Region Mask for Dynamic Scenes
abstract: Currently, most visual SLAM is based on a strong assumption of static scenes and has low localization accuracy and weak robustness in dynamic scenes. For dynamic scenes, we propose a robust visual SLAM system based on a dynamic region mask, named DRM-SLAM. In DRM-SLAM, we design a dynamic region mask generation module combining semantic segmentation and geometric constraints, which performs pixel-level dynamic region segmentation on RGB image frames captured by visual cameras. The generated dynamic region mask is used to extract static feature points, rejecting the negative influence of dynamic objects in the environment. We evaluate DRM-SLAM using the dynamic scene sequences of the TUM public dataset, and the results show that DRM-SLAM demonstrates excellent positioning accuracy in dynamic scenes while still maintaining robustness.

articleTitle: Multivariable System Prediction Based on Parallel GRU-LSTM Neural Network
abstract: For complex multi-input/output systems, this paper proposes a parallel GRU-LSTM neural network prediction strategy with self-attention mechanism. In order to eliminate the influence between variables, the multidimensional input time series in the system is normalized. The convolution layer is used to extract the initial feature from the sampled data. One branch uses LSTM network to extract and memorize long-term features. The other branch uses GRU network to improve the ability of short-term sequence feature memory. The self-attention mechanism is integrated to realize the strengthening of memory information. The two branches are fused with different weights, and then the predicted value is output through the fully connected layer. The results of comparison with existing network show that the proposed parallel neural network model has better prediction accuracy under the same number of iterations.

articleTitle: YD-SLAM: An Visual SLAM Based on Object Detection in Dynamic Environment
