abstract: Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (V -SLAM) is widely utilized in robot localization and navigation with the rich image information. Although remarkable progress has been made in static environments during the previous decade, research in dynamic environments is a formidable research challenge. Aiming to enhance the resilience and real-time capabilities of visual SLAM in dynamic environments, the study introduces a novel visual SLAM system that leverages the YOLOv5 object detection and ORB-SLAM2 framework. The feature points of dynamic objects are eliminated by using the bidirectional pre-matching mechanism and geometric constraints. This approach adequately diminished the influence exerted by dynamic objects on pose estimation accuracy. Meanwhile, an octomap is created for advanced tasks. The YD-SLAM conducted experiments on a publicly available TUM RGB-D dataset to evaluate its performance, and the absolute trajectory error of YD-SLAM is one order of magnitude higher than that of ORB-SLAM2. In contrast to the associated SLAM algorithms, the presented approach demonstrates enhanced operational velocity and mapping precision.

articleTitle: Optimizing Brake Curves to Enhance High-Speed Railway Capacity
abstract: To meet the rapid growth of passenger flow in rail transit, this paper takes the theme of improving passing capacity of high-speed railways. It analyzes the theoretical algorithm of braking curves of onboard equipment in depth, combines the optimization of braking parameters of vehicle sides, and explores the space for optimizing braking curves. Simulation calculation shows that the passing capacity of high-speed railways changes before and after optimization of braking curves of onboard equipment. The results indicate that: on a high-speed railway line with a maximum speed of 350 km/h, based on CTCS3-300S onboard equipment (abbreviated as “300S”), optimization of braking curves of onboard equipment and braking parameters of EMU (Electric Multiple Unit) can effectively improve the passing capacity of high-speed railways.

articleTitle: Distributed MPC for Vehicle Platoon Control with String Stability
abstract: In this paper, a distributed model predictive control (DMPC) approach is proposed for the undirected networked vehicle platoon under state constraints. Unlike the existing results, Lyapunov and string stability of the closed-loop systems are simultaneously guaranteed for the undirected vehicle network. Specifically, the designed terminal constraints ensure the iterative feasibility of the DMPC algorithm. Then, the control design problem is formulated as a distributed optimization problem by using the state information of itself and its neighbors. The closed-loop stability of the system is established by using the cost functions as a Lyapunov function. In addition, two state constraints are designed to ensure the string stability under the constant distance strategy. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed DMPC controller is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Distributed Lattice Kalman Filtering
abstract: The traditional single target real-time positioning accuracy is low and the multi-target centralized positioning requires information fusion center and large communication volume. In the nonlinear Kalman filter frame-work, the target groups are divided into clusters according to the link topology. The distributed lattice Kalman filter (DLKF), which is a quasi-Monte Carlo method (QMC) based on lattice rules, was derived by splitting and analyzing the state information obtained by sensors configured on cluster targets. The proposed lattice Kalman filter (LKF) method is based on Cranley-Patterson shift method and uses Korobov lattice rules to determine the low-difference sample points that generate random shifts. Then, in the distributed network system, the weighted rules are updated based on the weighted average consistency (WAC) algorithm to improve the precision of the fusion results within a limited consensus step. The test inferences evidence that the explored approach requires fewer sampling points and reduces the difficulty of integration, which is the most important core factor that DLKF is superior to other filters.

articleTitle: Domain Adaptive Multitask Model for Object Detection in Foggy Weather Conditions
abstract: Object detection in foggy weather conditions is a challenging problem, facing image degradation and feature space mismatch. A well-known method is to use image restoration methods to enhance degraded images before object detection. However, due to the limited availability of real-world datasets, these methods are based on synthetic datasets and have limited effectiveness in real-world scenarios. To address such issues, this paper proposes a domain adaptation-based multitask foggy weather object detection method, aiming to improve object detection performance in real-world foggy images. Firstly, we design an efficient Mini-AOD-Net as an image restoration network, which effectively enhances image clarity and preserves clean features for the detection network. Secondly, we introduce a domain adaptation module to address the object detection generalization problem in real-world scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate varying degrees of improvement in detection accuracy for both synthetic and real datasets using our proposed method. Furthermore, our approach can achieve a detection speed of 5.2 frames per second on an embedded system.

articleTitle: Distributed resource power aggregation prediction considering photovoltaic and wind power
abstract: To achieve the targets of carbon peak and neutrality, more and more distributed resources are connected to the distribution network and provide auxiliary services to the grid. However, it is difficult for a single distributed resource to provide effective power support to the grid due to its small controllable power and geographically dispersed location. In this paper, graph convolutional network (GCN) is used to perform power aggregation prediction for distributed resources. Firstly, an Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm is used to optimize the prediction model with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to improve the prediction accuracy of individual photovoltaic (PV) power. Secondly, taking spatial characteristics and topological connectivity of distributed resources into account, the GCN-based power aggregation prediction algorithm is proposed. The analysis is conducted through typical cases to first verify the accuracy of the ABC-LSTM PV power prediction model, and then to verify the feasibility of GCN for power aggregation prediction of distributed resources.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fixed-Time Robust $H_{\infty}$ Tracking Control of UUVs with Asymmetric State Constraints
abstract: This paper focuses on a practical fixed-time stable trajectory tracking control problem based on a prescribed performance constraint for an unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) system. First, a barrier function (BF)-based prescribed performance control (PPC) strategy based on fixed-time convergence is proposed by combining the error transformation with an asymmetric obstacle function to achieve the global control performance requirement and realize performance with an asymmetric output constraint, followed by a novel filter based on the practical fixed-time criterion, and a robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> controller without the singularity problem is designed.

articleTitle: Error Compensation-Considered Wind Power Forecasting: A Hybrid Deep Learning Method
abstract: Wind power is one of the most promising renewable energy, characterized as clean, safe and inexhaustible. Wind power forecasting is affected by multivariate meteorological data, showing strong randomness and instability. Accurate forecasting of wind power is a serious challenge, but can play a significant role in minimizing operating costs, and improving reliability and security of power systems. This paper proposes a hybrid deep learning method considering error compensation to accurately forecast wind power generation. The deep learning architecture consists of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), gated recur-rent units (GRU) and fully connected neural networks. In order to improve the forecasting accuracy, the attention mechanism and error compensation mechanism based on meteorological statistics are introduced to extract the correspondence between multivariate meteorological data and wind power generation. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated against some advanced methods in terms of MAE, RMSE and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex>-score. The proposed forecasting method demonstrates higher accuracy in MAE, 38.77% in RMSE and 10.97% in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex>-score as compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Design of SOME/IP Oriented Automatic Test System
abstract: With the advancement of intelligent and electrified express delivery of automobiles, traditional in-vehicle networks such as Controller Area Network (CAN) can no longer meet the bandwidth rate requirements of existing technologies, a new generation of in-vehicle networks and architectures is urgently needed. As a result, automotive Ethernet technology and service-oriented architectures have been introduced into the development of automotive software. The SOME/IP protocol is one of the application layer protocols for automotive Ethernet and is a middleware protocol for implementing service-oriented architectures (SOA). Perfect testing is the premise of the wide use of new technologies, this article will explain the SOME/IP communication mechanism, build a software and hardware test platform to realize the automated testing of SOME/IP.

articleTitle: Identification of USV Maneuvering Model Based on Multi-Output Gaussian Process Regression
abstract: The dynamic modeling and parameter identification of ships are the foundation for motion control. In this paper, a nonparametric identification method based on multi-output Gaussian process (MOGP) is proposed for the parameter identification of unmanned surface vessel (USV). Propeller speed and rudder angle serve as input excitation signals for a ship motion model with 3 degrees-of-freedom (DOF), and the speeds of the 3 DOF serve as output signals. The ship's maneuvering model is identified through the aforementioned input and output data, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through data collected from the HUSTER-12 USV lake experiments and the superiority is demonstrated by comparing it with the parameter identification method based on single-output Gaussian process (SOGP).

articleTitle: A Lightweight Detection Model for Wearing Masks Based on Optimized YOLOv3-Tiny
abstract: To address the problems of existing algorithms for mask-wearing detection, such as complexity, low accuracy, and insufficient capability of detecting mask-wearing status, Light-YOLO3, a lightweight detection model for wearing masks based on optimized YOLOv3-tiny, is proposed. To start with, the enhanced ShuffleNetv2 architecture is employed as the primary network to diminish the computational load of the model. Secondly, the third, fourth and fifth layer feature maps extracted by the backbone network are fused as a separate detection branch layer, so as to further strengthen the information fusion flow of the upper and lower layers to enhance the precision of target detection. Subsequently, Rapid spatial pyramid pooling (SPPF) is implemented towards the conclusion of the backbone network and succeeding the fusion branch layer to amplify the receptive field of the feature map. GSConv, a lightweight convolution, takes the place of the conventional convolution in the Neck segment, and the CIoU-Loss is utilized instead of the initial loss function, which further accelerates the model training speed and reduces the regression loss. Experiments show that the mAP of the improved Light-YOLO3 algorithm is increased by 1.1%, the volume of parameters is decreased by 49.6%, which can meet the needs of practical applications.

articleTitle: FVFH: An Improved Navigation Algorithm for UGVs in the Complex Disaster Environment
abstract: The problem of navigation by unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) in disaster areas is widely investigated. An environmental simulation model of disaster areas is established in order to solve this problem. The Focus Vector Field Histogram (FVFH) navigation algorithm for UGVs is designed: 1) A screening mechanism for the moving direction of the UGV is proposed; 2) The dynamic constraints of realistic UGVs are considered. The performance of the algorithm is tested on the Gym and CoppeliaSim platforms. The experimental results show that the FVFH algorithm can effectively shorten the planning time and navigation paths, and overcome special terrain obstacles with a high navigation success rate. Thus, the FVFH algorithm is helpful for navigation in complex disaster environment.

articleTitle: Robust Image-Based Visual Servoing Constraints Controller with Guaranteed Field of View
abstract: This article addresses the problem of visual features escaping from the cameras field of view when implementing the visual servoing task, by designing a constraint image based visual servoing controller. An asymmetric barrier Lyapunov function is introduced to define a strict pre-specified range for the feature tracking error to indirectly ensure that it is limited to the FoV of the camera, while guaranteeing the transient behavior of the tracking error and achieving exceptionally high precision in tracking. Finally, the stability analysis is illustrated using the asymmetric BLF, and the experiment results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Superconducting Linear Induction Heater and Analysis of Its Performance
abstract: A superconducting linear induction heating device is proposed, which utilizes the characteristics of superconducting coils to generate a constant magnetic field in the air gap of the iron core with the characteristics of non-resistance and large current. The finite element analysis model of the superconducting linear induction heating device is established, and the characteristics of the air gap magnetic density distribution and its influencing factors are analyzed. Through parametric analysis, the effects of the excitation current and the operating speed of the sheet metal on the eddy current density and the loss in the sheet metal are obtained. By changing the number of slots in the iron core, the influence of the change in magnetic resistance in the air gap on the eddy current loss is studied. The research results illustrate the feasibility of the linear motion heating device and can provide a reference for the development of the superconducting induction heating device.

articleTitle: A Map Segmentation Method Based on Deep Learning for Complete Coverage Path Planning
abstract: Path planning is one of the key technologies for autonomous robot navigation and operation. Based on global and local planning, full-coverage path planning is an essential method for solving tasks such as cleaning, inspection, and harvesting in a given area. In this work, complete coverage path planning of a known area is studied. First, navigation and operation within simple graphics like rectangles and triangles are realized. Then, a map segmentation method based on image processing and deep learning is proposed to segment the map built through the lidar into several basic graphics. Full coverage path planning is then carried out for each basic graphic, and finally, the sub-areas are connected to achieve a complete coverage of the entire region. To validate the feasibility of the method, a coverage rate calculation method was proposed. A series of experiments were conducted in simulation worlds. The experimental results showed that the proposed method can help the robot to achieve full coverage driving and operation in complex areas. Combining with the robot's operating range, the final achieved operational coverage rate was 97% or more. In the presence of obstacles, a maximum coverage rate of 95 % was still achieved through a local obstacle avoidance strategy.

articleTitle: Design of Wearable Knee Therapy Instrument System Based on STM32
abstract: Red LED irradiation has a good therapeutic effect on knee osteoarthritis, but traditional LED light therapy equipment is bulky and expensive. In order to solve this problem, this paper designs a wearable knee phototherapy instrument system based on STM32, uses Solidworks software to design the three-dimensional structure diagram of the phototherapy instrument, designs the LED array according to Sparrow's law, builds the LED driver circuit with the STM32 single-chip microcomputer as the control core, and finally realizes the different light intensity adjustment control of the flexible LED array board through PWM technology. The results show that the system can realize the linear adjustment of light irradiance, and the heat generation of the light source meets the safety requirements.

articleTitle: A Dynamical Artificial Bee Colony for Energy-Efficient Hybrid Flow Shop Scheduling with Batch Processing Machines and Reentrant
abstract: Energy-efficient hybrid flow shop scheduling problem (EHFSP) with batch processing machines (BPM) is seldom considered, let alone EHFSP with BPM and reentrant. In this study, EHFSP with BPM and reentrant is solved and a dynamical artificial bee colony (DABC) is presented to minimize makespan and total consumption of energy of all batch processing machines simultaneously. To produce high quality solutions, swarm decision is used to dynamically determine employed bee swarm and onlooker bee swarm. Adaptive onlooker bee phase and adaptive scout phase are implemented. A lot of experiments are conducted. The results of computation demonstrate that the new strategies of DABC are valid and DABC is very competitive on solving EHFSP with BPM and reentrant.

articleTitle: Model-Free Adaptive Iterative Learning Fault-Tolerant Control for Nonlinear Systems With Sensor Fault and Measurement Noise
abstract: To solve the challenge of fault-tolerant control (FTC) with both measurement noise and sensor fault, a model-free iterative learning adaptive fault-tolerant control strategy (IL-FTC) is proposed. An improved data-based featureless Kalman filter (IUKF) mechanism is devised for FTC. Then, an iterative estimation structure is designed using the dynamic linearization-based method to enhance the online estimation of some key parameters. Meanwhile, a new data-based fault detection (FD) algorithm is presented using an incremental broad learning system (IBLS) technique to detect sensor faults, avoiding the need for accurate model parameters for designing a fault detection observer. Based on this, controller reconfiguration is achieved by valid fault estimation. To improve the control performance of the system, a model-free adaptive controller (MFAC) that fully utilizes more historical information is developed. Finally, the superiority of the developed method is illustrated by a robotic arm simulation.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Multi-Dimensional Encoding and Multi-Level Reconstruction Network for Hyperspectral Denoising
abstract: A hyperspectral image denoising network based on Transformer with multi-dimensional encoding and multilevel reconstruction is proposed in this paper. The network aims to extract spatial and spectral information more effectively from hyperspectral images and improve the image reconstruction performance. Specifically, a combination of 2D and 3D convolutions is employed for feature extraction. Multidimensional encoding is utilized to preserve the integrity of the encoded information. The image denoising quality is enhanced through a multilevel transformer reconstruction approach. Additionally, residual structures are introduced in the network to enhance the restoration of image details and further improve the denoising performance. Extensive experiments on a large dataset for hyperspectral image denoising demonstrate that the network achieves cutting-edge visual effects and objective assessment criteria under various noise settings.

articleTitle: Surface Defect Detection of Wooden Boards Based on Multi-Modal Fusion
abstract: Automated wood defect detection is of great significance for improving wood utilization. However, the stains on the wood surface resemble defect features and it is difficult to distinguish the appearance of wane from defect-free regions. Relying solely on machine vision for extracting surface features of wood makes it difficult to achieve accurate defect detection. To address these challenges, we propose MMDNet, a multimodal detection network that combines point cloud and image data. By adaptively fusing point cloud and image features at multiple stages, the network effectively highlights wood surface defect regions. Additionally, we introduce an Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module into the network, which expands the network's receptive field and enables a comprehensive perception of the defects. Furthermore, we employ a deep supervision strategy to encourage the network to learn discriminative feature representations, enhancing the model's ability to differentiate defect regions. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of our method in detecting defects that are similar to the background and reducing interference from stains.

articleTitle: Fractional Order Time-Varying Sliding Mode Attitude Controller for Unpowered Reentry Vehicle
abstract: Inthis article, a fractional order time-varying sliding mode attitude controller for unpowered reentry vehicles is present. The time-varying term eliminates the arrival stage made by the initial system errors, which makes the fractional order sliding mode control system globally robust. The stability and globality of the system are demonstrated by the Lyapunov second method and the properties of fractional calculus. The proposed attitude controller shows better convergence performance than the existing ones with simulations.

articleTitle: Efficient 3D Siamese Transformer Tracker with Bird's-Eye View Representation
abstract: LiDAR-based 3D single object tracking(3D SOT) has received remarkable attention due to its crucial role in robotics and autonomous driving. However, existing Siamese-based trackers generally employ expensive 3D convolutions to decode bird's-eye view (BEV) features. Exploring an efficient method for decoding BEV features holds special significance. Therefore, we propose an efficient 3D SOT tracker based on BEV representation named ETT, which efficiently decodes BEV features and enhances tracking performance. Our framework encompasses two crucial designs that contribute to accuracy and efficiency: (1) We employ a 3D siamese transformer network to capture the three-dimensional shape information of objects. Simultaneously, we design an attention-based feature correlating module to associate the template with potential targets in the search area. (2) We design an effective BEV encoder that reduces the spatial dimensions of voxel feature maps. We demonstrate that these designs significantly contribute to more accurate and efficient regression of 3D object centers. Extensive experiments on the KITTI and nuScenes benchmark datasets validate that our approach obtains outstanding performance in the task of 3D SOT.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Prescribed-Time Observer-Based Globally Consensus Control for High-Order Multiagent Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the globally consensus control problem for nonlinear high-order multiagent systems (MASs) under a directed graph. A novel distributed event-triggered prescribed-time observer (EPTO) is first formulated for the followers, and it is able to accurately estimate the information of the leader agent in a prescribed-time interval. Additionally, the event-triggered condition is constructed for each distributed EPTO to avoid continuous transmission of the neighbor states. The prominent feature of this paper is the designed consensus control scheme, which ensures that the closed-loop system achieves globally prescribed-time stability under the control framework of the backstepping technology. The simulation example further verify the effectiveness of the EPTO-based consensus tracking control scheme.

articleTitle: Design of a Data Provenance Scheme with Virtual Tuple-Based Database Watermarking
abstract: The security of power grid is closely related to national security and social stability. With the development of smart grid and big data, grid data security has ushered in new challenges. The data provenance is one of the key issues. Considering the complexity of grid data storage types, this paper designs a virtual tuple-based data provenance scheme. This scheme firstly embedding the watermark with user identity through virtual tuple injection. Then, the data with watermark is distributed in the form of table splitting, which makes it possible to quickly locate the suspect user when a data leakage event occurs. Finally, the leaker is identified through watermark extraction and comparison. The simulation experiments show that our scheme has good robustness against insertion, replacement and deletion attacks.

articleTitle: Mechanical Fault Diagnosis Using Audio Signal Feature Fusion and Fuzzy Inference
abstract: Fault diagnosis is one of the key technologies for achieving intelligent manufacturing. However, implementing fault diagnosis in special environments, such as high-pressure, high-altitude, and toxic conditions, presents a significant challenge. The method of mechanical fault diagnosis based on audio signal analysis (MFDA) offers unique advantages in handling fault diagnosis in special environments, as it enables non-invasive and non-contact measurements. This paper proposes a feature called “spectral similarity” for MFDA and validates the effectiveness of the proposed feature through experiments. Additionally, this paper combines feature fusion with a fuzzy inference system to propose an MFDA method suitable for high-noise and small-sample scenarios. Firstly, the audio signals are preprocessed and then segmented into frames. Next, the spectral similarity feature, sound quality features, and time-domain features are extracted. Subsequently, feature fusion is performed based on the results of correlation analysis and kernel principal component analysis (KPCA). Then, a fuzzy inference system is established by determining the membership functions and linguistic terms, and defining fuzzy rules. Finally, the fused features are input into the fuzzy inference system to obtain the diagnostic results. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy of 98.16% for motor fault diagnosis in low-noise scenarios and an accuracy of 97.64% for tool wear diagnosis in high-noise scenarios. The proposed method outperforms the one-class support vector machine (OCSVM) method, the K-Means clustering method, etc.

articleTitle: Combined Online Estimation of State-of-Charge and State-of-Health of Lithium-Ion Power Battery Based on Dual Extended Kalman Filters
abstract: Accurate online estimation of the state of charge (SOC) and state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries during charging and discharging processes remains a formidable challenge in Battery Management Systems (BMS). In response to this issue, an effective online estimation method is proposed in this work. Initially, a second-order RC equivalent circuit model is established. Subsequently, to fully adapt to the time-varying characteristics of the model's internal parameters, an improved recursive least square method is integrated to realize the online identification of the model parameters. Ultimately, according to the model parameters identified online, the state equation and the observation equation under the Dual Extended Kalman Filter (DEKF) are established, and the battery capacity is substituted into the DEKF algorithm as a parameter vector to realize the online estimation of the SOC and SOH. By simulating the Federal Urban Driving Status (FUDS), the estimated error of SOC and SOH are, respectively, only 1.14% and 1.55%.

articleTitle: A Double-Neighborhood Local Ratio-Difference Contrast Method for Infrared Small Target Detection
abstract: Detecting infrared small targets swiftly and reliably has posed a significant challenge in recent times. Existing algorithms are often plagued by problems such as noise residuals and insufficient background suppression capabilities due to the complexity of the imaging environment. A double-neighborhood local ratio-difference contrast method (DNLRDC) is proposed in this paper. First, a tri-layer sliding window is designed to move through the input infrared image. Second, the salience map can be obtained by calculating the DNLRDC to achieving the target enhancement and background suppression. Finally, the real target is segmented from the salience map by employing a simple threshold segmentation method. Experiments shows that the proposed method is more robust than methods used as controls in the experimental stage.

articleTitle: A Train Identification Method Based on Sparse Point Clouds Scan Dataset
abstract: When monitoring the railway environment through trackside equipment, lidar data could be affected by number of factors: such as the equipment installation location, the different shapes of freight and passenger trains, the low reflectivity of train windows and others. The lidar point cloud data is always sparse and irregular, thus the train is usually identified incorrectly. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a train identification method based on point cloud projection to filter the lidar data. In this method, the groundpoints was segmented by the algorithm of patchwork++, the point of track was extracted based on the geometric position analysis. Then the point cloud is rasterized into x and y directions, and use the connected component analysis to calculate the area of missing-groudpoints in the current frame. There are two conditions will be used to judge whether the object is a train: the positional relation of the non-ground points and the track, the difference in the size of missing part between the current frame and template. At the same time, the time taken for train to pass through the lidar's view also is considered as an auxiliary judgment condition. The experimental results showed that this algorithm has promise application values with its short consum ing-time and high recognition accuracy. And it has been successfully applied in the trackside detection equipment in the specific department of railway maintains.

articleTitle: Low-Light Image Enhancement Conditioned On Hierarchical Illumination Proposal
abstract: Low-light enhancement is a challenging task that requires improving contrast, enhancing illumination, and resolving degradations simultaneously. We model the enhancement process following the simplified Retinex model and employ V-channel image to obtain illumination proposals of multilevels by utilizing the pixel-wise illumination enhancement curves (LE-curve). We then embed the illumination proposals features into the encoder-decoder architecture hierarchically by designed Pyramid illumination proposal embedding module (PIPEM) which contains a stacked spatial pyramid pooling (SSPP) module and four proposal embedding attention module (PEA) with different scales to align and interact cross-domain features. In addition, a novel fusion net is proposed to suppress noise problem. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive and impressive performance with existing advanced methods quantitatively and qualitatively.

articleTitle: Multi-Sensor Fusion Model-Free Adaptive Control for Systems with False Data Injection Attacks
abstract: A control problem of unknown nonlinear networked systems with false data injection attacks is studied in this paper. A multi-sensor fusion model-free adaptive control method with subjected to attacks based on I/O data is proposed, where the random false data injection attacks are estimated to enhance the control performance. Then the weights are optimally taken using an intelligent algorithm, moth-flame optimization algorithm. Finally, simulation is used to confirm that the suggested algorithm is available.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Electric Vehicle Charging Control System Based on LoRa Frequency Communication
abstract: With the invention and popularization of electric vehicles, the phenomenon of large-scale charging of electric vehicles has brought enormous pressure to the power system, and some regions cannot meet the charging power of electric vehicles. Therefore, this article proposes a control system that can schedule charging behaviors of electric vehicles through the telecommunication of LoRa(LoRa, Long Range Radio) module, ensuring the stable operation of local transformers under the condition of orderly charging of electric vehicles. The article firstly analyzed the hardware structure and device selection of the control system, with a focus on the functions and advantages of the LoRa module; Secondly, the workflow of the control system was clarified; Next, under the RT-Thread framework, the detection task of charging signal line voltage, the PWM(PWM, Pulse Width Modulation) transmission task of charging pile, and frequency communication task based on LoRa module are constructed for task scheduling to achieve the functions of the control system. The effectiveness of the control system has been verified through operational testing and result analysis.

articleTitle: Optimization Study on Structure of Null-Flux Coils in Electrodynamic Suspension System
abstract: In the null-flux electrodynamic suspension (EDS) system, the structural parameters of the null-flux coils (NFCs) have a significant impact on the electromagnetic force performance of the system. According to the specific index requirements of the null-flux EDS system, the mathematical model of the null-flux EDS is combined with swarm intelligence algorithms such as particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm and genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the structural parameters of the NFCs, which can improve the performance of the system.

articleTitle: Low Carbon Economic Dispatch of Integrated Energy Systems with Integrated Demand Response
abstract: The underutilization of demand-side dispatchable resources such as electricity, thermal, cold, and natural gas is a key problem that increases the operating cost of integrated energy systems (IES). To address this and reduce both IES operation costs and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>emissions, a dispatching model has been constructed with the goal of optimizing IES comprehensive efficiency. This model takes into account the economic and low-carbon aspects of IES operations, the potential for demand response in electricity, gas, heat, and cooling. Firstly, an IES model is created that includes equipment such as photovoltaic (PV) panels, wind turbines (WT), gas boilers (GB), gas turbines (GT), electric chillers (EC), and others. This is combined with a comprehensive demand response model that considers the energy conversion relationship between electricity, gas, thermal, and cooling loads. Secondly, a stepped cost model is introduced to limit CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>emissions. Finally, the objective of optimizing the overall operating cost, including energy purchase cost, equipment operation cost, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>related cost, and demand response cost is optimized using the Cplex solver. Simulation results demonstrate that the model successfully reduces both system operation cost and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>emissions.

articleTitle: Fixed-Point Navigation of Parafoil Using Improved Infrared Patch-Image Algorithm
abstract: The parafoil navigation system is of great significance in material transportation, target positioning, and other aspects. However, nighttime, foggy, or fire environments increase the difficulty of target positioning. To achieve target positioning with multiple interference points in environments with poor visibility, an improved infrared patch-image algorithm is proposed. Taking aerial images as targets, the single frame algorithm is expanded to a multi frame algorithm, which provides more data and perspectives through information fusion between multiple frames based on the randomness of interference positions, and then identifies the correct target points; Afterwards, an image without interference points is obtained by approximating the values of neighboring pixels. Locate the ground coordinates of the target point in the aerial image and design simulation experiments to control the parafoil system to achieve precise landing navigation at a certain height, ultimately controlling the parafoil navigation error within 0.5 meters.

articleTitle: Self-triggered Adaptive Neural Network Control for Uncertain Time Delay Nonlinear Systems with Prescribed Time
abstract: This paper is concerned with the adaptive neural networks (NNs) prescribed-time control problem for a class of strict-feedback uncertain nonlinear systems with time dealy via the self-triggered control (STC). The Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals (LKFs) are employed to compensate for the effect of the state delay. An adaptive NNs self-triggered controller is designed to solve the problem of prescribed-time performance (PTP). The self-triggered mechanism can greatly save computing and network communication resources. The proposed strategy ensures that the system is stable within the prescribed time, with all variables in the system being bounded. Finally, a physical simulation experiment is used to verify the practicality of this method.

articleTitle: Flexible Spider Web-Like Tactile Sensor Based on Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Robotics Multidimensional Force Sensing
abstract: Developing the robots that are capable of performing intricate tasks has been a primary objective. In pursuit of this goal, flexible tactile sensors with multi-dimensional force sensing capabilities have shown promise for intelligent robotics. Herein, we present a triboelectric-based spider web-like sensor (TSS) for robotics multi-dimensional sensing. The experimental results reveal that its single unit can perceive the stretching ratio ranging from 1% to 60% with a fast response time of 12.5 ms. And the sensing unit is also capable of detecting the contact forces. Additionally, the device not only allows for the simultaneous perception of strain direction and intensity but also facilitates the localization of contact objectives through arranging 6 sensing units in the spider-web like structure. Considering its merits of low cost, high flexibility and the nature of self-powered, it is believed that the newly designed TSS has provided a prospect method for the robotics perceiving technology.

articleTitle: Bias-eliminated parameter estimation for sandwich nonlinear systems
abstract: In this paper, a bias-eliminated parameter identification method is proposed for application to sandwich nonlinear systems under stochastic measurement noise. By linearizing such a system expression based on the key term separation technique, a multi-innovation recursive least-squares algorithm is developed to simultaneously estimate the parameters of a class of sandwich systems with one nonlinear static subsystem embedded between two linear dynamic subsystems. Moreover, an auxiliary model strategy is introduced to solve the problem of consistent estimation on inner unavailable variables of the sandwich nonlinear systems. Besides, an adaptive forgetting factor is used to guarantee asymptotic convergence of parameter estimation. Finally, the upper bound of estimation error and unbiased estimation performance are clarified under a persistent excitation condition. An illustrative example is shown to validate the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Improved SCA-BP Delay Prediction Method for Networked Control Systems
abstract: A networked control system is a system that uses communication networks to connect the various parts. However, network delay affects the performance and stability of the networked control system. In order to eliminate the impact of network delay on the control system, an improved SCA-BP delay prediction method is proposed in this paper. The proposed method optimizes the initial weights and biases of the BP neural network, and further optimizes them through backpropagation gradient descent, obtaining the final prediction model. The proposed method introduces a random perturbation factor in the sine and cosine functions, which increases the explorability and diversity of the method. And they are sorted and grouped according to the fitness values of the candidate solutions. At the same time, different update strategies are adopted based on the different groups, enabling the method to perform global and local search simultaneously. In the update strategy, a linear function is also introduced in addition to the sine and cosine functions, enabling the method to maintain the direction of the current optimal solution to a certain extent. Finally, the superiority and effectiveness of the method compared with traditional methods are verified through some comparative simulations, indicating that the method has a strong delay prediction ability.

articleTitle: Cooperative Output Regulation of Heterogeneous Linear Multi-Agent Systems: A Distributed Output Feedback Control Approach
abstract: In this article, we investigate the cooperative output regulation problem of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems. Recently, the same problem is solved by a state feedback control approach. We aim to design a control law to address this problem. In particular, first, we construct a novel control law which fully depends on the output information. Then, a rigorous proof is given to show that by a small-gain condition, the problem is addressed under the proposed control law. Finally, an example is given to demonstrate the method.

articleTitle: Robust Spacecraft Image Interest Point Detection and Description with Transformer Under Variable Illumination Conditions
abstract: The spacecraft image matching serves as the foundation for various space vision applications, such as vision-based relative pose estimation of target spacecraft. Currently, feature-based methods employ the extraction of local image features to compute interest points and descriptors for image matching. However, significant variations in spacecraft image local features occur when illumination conditions change, posing challenges for image feature matching. This paper proposes a Transformer-based self-supervised network for interesting point detection and description, which is trained under varying lighting conditions. The global receptive field provided by the Transformer enables the establishment of more robust feature descriptors, thereby allowing robust feature matching under varying lighting conditions. Additionally, a multi-illumination-angle spacecraft image dataset is created for training and testing the proposed algorithm. Compared to other state-of-the-art interesting point detection and description algorithms, the proposed algorithm achieves the best results in terms of matching effectiveness.

articleTitle: GTDNet: A Dual-branch Domain Adaption Network for Graphic-rich Text Detection
abstract: In recent years, text detection methods based on convolutional neural networks have been extensively studied and obtained successful results in various datasets. However, many graphic- rich text instances are still difficult to detect due to their irregular appearance and easy confusion with graphics. To address this issue, we construct a dual-branch domain adaption network for graphic-rich text detection (GTDNet). Due to the coexistence of ordinary text (source domain) and graphic-rich text (target domain) in real scenarios, our dual-branch domain adaptation network can complete two tasks well at the same time. We incorporate a feature alignment module in one branch, and use an attension fusion module for fully combining two branch features. We have created a clothing printing dataset that comprises both ordinary text and graphic-rich text. Ex-tensive experiments on this dataset show that GTDNet achieves best performance on graphic-rich texts with a hardly decline performance on ordinary texts.

articleTitle: Scheduling Strategy for Energy Storage System in Microgrids Employing Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Energy storage system (ESS) plays an essential role in microgrids (MGs). By strategically scheduling the charging/discharging states of ESS, the operational cost of MG can be reduced. In this paper, we consider ESS charging and discharging as decision-making behavior to achieve the goal of minimizing operation cost of MG. The ESS scheduling problem is transformed into a Markov decision process (MDP) by defining ESS action, system state, and reward function. We adopt a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method of Deep Q-Network with Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD-DQN) to efficiently search for the optimal ESS scheduling policy. The convergence reward value of our proposed MMD-DQN method is higher than that of the baseline DQN and D3QN methods. The comparative experiment results display that our MMD-DQN approach can significantly reduce the system operation cost by optimizing the ESS scheduling strategy and outperform the strategies obtained by using existing methods.

articleTitle: Pursuit-Evasion Game Based on Fuzzy Actor-Critic Learning with Obstacle in Continuous Environment
abstract: This paper employs the fuzzy actor-critic learning (FACL) and the Kalman filter (KF) to tackle the pursuit-evasion game (PEG) within a continuous environment, considering a scenario involving multiple pursuers and a single evader. We design reasonable reward functions for the pursuer and the evader, enabling them to complete the pursuit-evasion task and achieve obstacle avoidance. The strategies for both the pursuer and the evader are acquired through the FACL algorithm, while learning is extended from the discrete domain to the continuous domain. Additionally, pursuers use the KF to predict the evader's position, enhancing their ability to enclose and capture the evader. We demonstrate the advantage of the pursuers moving toward the evader using a geometric method, which compresses the evader's movement space and reduces capture time. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in capturing the evader and avoiding obstacles has been validated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Path Planning Based on Potential Field Dense Reward in Unknown Environments with Static and Dynamic Obstacles
abstract: Due to unknown environments with static and dynamic obstacles, unmanned aerial vehicle trajectory planning remains challenging. Multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) algorithm performs well in multi-UAV trajectory planning. Traditional sparse reward function adopted by MADDPG leads to slow convergence and the trained path planning policy is difficult to adapt to the complex scenario. To address the above problems, an improved MADDPG algorithm with a potential field dense reward function called PF-MADDPG for multi-UAV trajectory planning in complex unknown environments is proposed. By introducing the attraction and repulsion mechanisms of potential field, the learning efficiency is accelerated and the optimality of the path planning policy is improved. Simulation results show that the multi-UAV path planning policy trained by PF-MADDPG performs well in complex unknown environments with static and dynamic obstacles.

articleTitle: Complex Substation Scene Segmentation Method Based on Optimized Straight Line Detection
abstract: This paper proposes a scene segmentation method based on optimized line detection to address the difficulty of segmenting spatially independent equipment in complex substation scenes. The method first employs the RANSAC method to simulate the ground plane and extract the ground point cloud. Then, it projects the 3D point cloud scene onto a 2D plane to obtain a 2D image of the substation. Straight line segments of the power line are extracted from the image using the edge detection algorithm and an improved line detection algorithm. The straight line segments that do not belong to the power line are filtered out using the surrounding features of the 3D point corresponding to the 2D point on the line. The power line's straight line segment is extended using the region-growing algorithm. Finally, the power line clustering is completed using European clustering based on the three-dimensional coordinates of the two ends of the power line, thereby completing the scene segmentation. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively segment substation equipment. Compared to traditional segmentation methods, this method has an average power line identification accuracy of 14% higher.

articleTitle: A Pedestrian Navigation Method Based on Dual MIMU for Complex Gait Patterns
abstract: A pedestrian navigation method based on dual MIMU for complex gait patterns is proposed, to address the problem that the heading of pedestrian navigation system based on foot mounted MIMU drifts over time in satellite denied environments. A constraint model for dual foot, as well as a gait recognition method based on the characteristics of inertial measurement data are designed. The constraint threshold of the distance between two feet is adaptively adjusted according to the gait recognition result. The pedestrian position correction is completed by combining zero velocity update (ZUPT) and inequality constrained Kalman filtering algorithm. The experiments show that in a mixed motion pattern that includes six gaits, the positioning error of the pedestrian navigation system based on dual MIMU using adaptive threshold constraint is 0.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>D, which is reduced by 11.03% and 2.53% compared to unconstrained and fixed threshold constraint methods, respectively.

articleTitle: Cooperative Active-Reactive Power Optimization Strategy for Distribution Networks Based on Improved African Vultures Optimization Algorithm
abstract: In recent years, with the high proportion of distributed generation (DG) connected to the distribution network, a series of problems such as voltage overrun and network loss increase have arisen, and the difficulty of reactive power optimization has been increased. This paper establishes a reactive power optimization model for distribution networks with DG, obtains the scenic output through Monte Carlo sampling, considers the safe operation of distribution networks, takes into account the cooperative scheduling of energy storage devices and reactive power compensation devices, sets network losses and operating costs as the optimization objectives, and introduces the crossing penalty function as an index to measure the voltage stability of distribution networks, and proposes a reactive power optimization strategy for distribution networks with DG based on an improved African vultures optimization algorithm. The results show that the proposed optimization strategy can effectively reduce the network loss, improve the system voltage stability, and reduce the comprehensive operation cost of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Power System Outlier Detection Based on Improved EKF Algorithm
abstract: The impact of outliers on power system state estimation cannot be ignored. These outliers are usually caused by aging system equipment, sensor failures, line connection errors, and so on. In this paper, we propose the use of the Weighted Expanded Kalman Filter (WEKF) algorithm based on projection statistics (PS). The algorithm first uses the projection statistics algorithm to detect outliers in the time-varying detection matrix, and subsequently introduces a weighting function to reduce the weight of these outliers, thereby effectively minimizing the impact on the state estimation. Simulation experiments on the IEEE 14-bus system, the results of the study show that the PS-based Weighted Extended Kalman Filter (WEKF) algorithm exhibits stronger robustness compared to the traditional EKF algorithm. Through the use of the algorithm, it is possible to have the more stable estimation of the state of the power system.

articleTitle: ISAR phase correction imaging algorithm based on fractional gradient descent method
abstract: In this paper, the fractional stepwise descent method is used to realize the phase correction method of minimizing the Tsallis entropy. This algorithm utilizes the Tsallis entropy of a two-dimensional image to achieve autofocus for radar images. The Tsallis entropy is gradually minimized, resulting in the autofocus of the radar image. The results of Matlab simulation data proved that compared to the other two commonly used methods, this method has good focusing effect and Rate of convergence., and achieves a good compromise between the two.

articleTitle: A CPN -Based Reliability Analysis of a Wireless Communication System in a Virtually Coupled Train Set
abstract: Wireless communication system is the solid foundation for a communication-based train control system, especially for the control of train tracking with a short headway in a virtual coupling scenario. This paper proposes a hierarchical timed colored Petri Nets (HTCPN s) approach to analyze the reliability of train-to-train (T2T) communication links and the relationship between communication link reliability and train operation safety. A T2T communication link model in the context of virtual coupling operations is developed. Specifically, HTCPN models are built to describe the communication link with handover and communication link failure. Data collector monitors are deployed to collect the emulated data. That data is used to analyze the reliability of the T2T communication link in a Virtually Coupled Train Set (VCTS). We found that the error rate of the communication link and handover latency are the main factors for train operation safety in a VCTS.

articleTitle: Object-Oriented Semantic SLAM Based on Weighted Scoring of Pose Initialization
abstract: Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (vS-LAM) is essential to autonomous robot navigation and AR/VR systems. As deep learning technologies improve rapidly, researchers integrate object detection into traditional vSLAM frameworks to acquire objects from images. The object detection modules allow the SLAM system to construct object-level maps with the estimated pose, location, and scale estimation of detected objects. Since pose estimation is a non-linear process, an accurate pose initialization is crucial to improve the optimality of the estimation result, which is vital to constructing an object-level map. Although existing works have achieved remarkable progress in object pose initialization, the accuracy still needs to be improved to meet the needs of real applications. In this paper, an improved object pose initialization strategy based on weighted adaptive sampling is proposed, which is robust to noise in the extracted line features. In addition, a SLAM system that can construct an object-level map with semi-dense line features based on the proposed weighted scoring of pose initialization is presented. The qualitative and quantitative evaluation experiments on public datasets show that the proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art works in accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Host Protection State Anomaly Detection Based on Multidimensional Features
abstract: The features extracted from traffic data can characterize the communication behavior and operational status of software. However, the accuracy of detecting abnormal host protection status of internal network terminals using only traffic data is not high. This article proposes a anomaly detection method based on multidimensional feature for host protection state detection. The method consists of two stages. In the first stage, a basic dataset is generated using traffic data, software logs, and login logs. In the second stage, a multilayer clustering method and a small amount of labeled data are applied to identify abnormal terminals. In practical applications, the proposed method can effectively detect abnormal terminals with software not installed and abnormal heartbeat.

articleTitle: Research on the County Innovation Ability Monitoring Index System
abstract: Innovation capability is the main driving force for countries' and regions' economic and social development. Scientifically, objectively, and accurately measuring the level of innovation and development in countries and regions, grasping the trends and characteristics of innovation and development, identifying the crux of innovation and development, and proposing effective improvement measures are important links in the construction of innovation systems. Based on the principles of comprehensive objectivity, highlighting key points, authenticity and reliability, overall consideration, and simplicity, and after thorough investigation and research, comprehensive consideration of the actual situation of county innovation, overall consideration of regional development differences, and drawing on relevant research results, a monitoring indicator system for county innovation capacity has been formed. This indicator system consists of four primary indicators, 30 secondary indicators, several tertiary indicators, and alternative indicators. Grasp the status of county-level innovation, break comprehensively and objectively through the obstacles in county-level innovation, and smooth grass-roots innovation management provide a reference.

articleTitle: Research on Current Sharing Method for SiC MOSFETs in Parallel Based on Adjustable Gate Voltage Driver
abstract: The Solid-State Power Controller (SSPC) is an intelligent switch composed of power switches, voltage-current sensors, and a microcontroller. It integrates functions such as overvoltage protection, overcurrent protection, status reporting, and remote control. It is employed in industries with high reliability demands to perform on-off control of electrical loads. Due to the high voltage withstand capability, low on-resistance, and superior temperature tolerance of SiC MOSFETs, they are preferred as power switches in solid-state power controller to enhance their reliability. However, individual SiC MOSFETs have limited current-carrying capacity, necessitating the use of multiple devices in parallel to increase their current-carrying capability. Nevertheless, due to the inherent parameter variations among devices, straightforward parallel connection of silicon carbide devices fails to achieve automatic current sharing over the entire temperature range. Consequently, prolonged operation leads to thermal imbalances, severely impacting the reliable operation of the devices. Indeed, achieving current sharing in parallel SiC MOSFETs is crucial for ensuring the safe operation of the system. In light of this, a gate voltage adjustable active current sharing method for SiC MOSFETs has been proposed. This method takes advantage of the temperature-dependent on-resistance characteristic of SiC MOSFETs and introduces a novel SiC MOSFET driver circuit. By independently adjusting the gate voltage of each SiC MOSFET within the parallel configuration, the proposed method achieves effective current sharing control. By employing the Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) algorithm, control precision and response speed are enhanced, allowing for precise adjustment of the gate voltage. Consequently, this approach significantly improves the balancing and reliability of the parallel operation of SiC MOSFETs. Through simulation and experimentation, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method have been validated successfully.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Model-Free Adaptive Predictive Control for Discrete-Time Nonlinear System
abstract: In the setting of discrete-time nonlinear systems, a data-modeling-based control technique that combines observer and predictive control is presented in this study, where a mix of model predictive control (MPC) and dynamic linearization approaches is used to construct a data-driven strategy focused on output optimization. First, the equivalent conversion from nonlinear to linear systems is realized by compact format dynamic linearization(CFDL) method, and a pseudo-partial derivative (PPD) method of estimation with only data information is created using an adaptive observer. Second, a predictive control function containing the observer output, control input and observation error is defined and combined with continuous optimization of actions to generate the optimal control action. The convergence performance of the parameters arising from the application of the suggested method to a nonlinear system, such as PPD estimate error, observer error, and systematic error, is obtained mathematically. Ultimately, numerical simulation studies were carried out to verify the suggested algorithm's value in raising control precision.

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control Algorithm Based on Memory Data and Online Computation
abstract: In this paper, a disturbance compensation control algorithm based on memory data and online computation is proposed for a class of affine nonlinear systems. The basic idea is to use the information stored and measured at the previous two moments to calculate the disturbance at the previous two moments and add it to the control input for compensating the disturbance at the current moment. This method has obvious physical meaning, and its effectiveness is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Saturation-Degree-Dependent Event-Triggered Control for Saturated Systems
abstract: In this paper, a saturation-degree-dependent event-triggered scheme is proposed for linear systems affected by actuator saturation, and the sufficient conditions to ensure the asymptotic stability of the system under the designed event-triggered control are derived. In addition, an optimization algorithm is presented to estimate the stable region of the system. Finally, a numerical example is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: A Textured Feature Enhanced Efficient Network to Classify Tobacco Strip Structure Types
abstract: Tobacco strip structure is the size and sheet structure of tobacco leaves in the process of leaf beating, which is the key economic indicator of cigarette manufacturing. In this article, we turn the problem of getting the tobacco strip structure into a classification problem by dividing our photographed images in the complex industrial scenarios into 14 types of tobacco strip structures according to expert knowledge and then using deep learning to recognize them. We use Efficientnetv2 as the backbone and develop it based on the characteristics of our dataset. As for the proposed method, the overall image classification accuracy reaches 92.82%, which is 2.33% higher than the accuracy before our improvements. 14 types of tobacco strip structures after leaf beating can be identified quickly and efficiently by using our present model. The results of this study can provide a theoretical basis and technical support for the intelligent identification of tobacco strip structure after leaf beating.

articleTitle: Networked Load Frequency Control of Multi-Rate Sampled-Data Multi-Area Interconnected Power Systems Under Denial-of-Service Attacks
abstract: This article investigates the load frequency control (LFC) problem for multi-rate sampling multi-area interconnected power systems with load disturbances subjected to denial-of-service attacks. First, a multi-rate sampling mechanism based adaptive event-triggered mechanism is proposed to save more limited network resources. Then, under the DoS attacks, a sampled-data PI-type controller is constructed to ensure system performance. The exponential stability criterion for the networked LFC systems and the design method of the controller are proposed respectively, which is verified by an example of three-area interconnected power systems.

articleTitle: Multimodal-Based Pedestrian Crossing Intention Recognition Method*
abstract: The ability of autonomous vehicles to accurately predict the future intention of pedestrians has become critical for ensuring road safety. However, accurately recognizing pedestrian behavioral intention remains a significant challenge. To address this challenge, we propose a novel multimodal-based pedestrian crossing intention recognition method that takes into account the pedestrian's abstraction and subjective mobility from the perspective of individual pedestrian behavior. Our proposed network architecture comprises three sub-networks, each dedicated to extracting specific features from different parts of the pedestrian. Specifically, one sub-network is designed to extract pedestrian skeleton features, another to capture head features, and a third to extract leg features. Additionally, a fusion network is incorporated to effectively combine these extracted features in an adaptive manner. The adaptive fusion process leverages the attention mechanism to learn fusion weights, dynamically adjusting the contribution of each feature channel based on their importance or relevance to the given task at hand. Overall, the proposed pipeline provides new state-of-the-art results on pedestrian intention recognition.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimized Generative Adversarial Networks For Video Anomaly Detection
abstract: The objective of video anomaly detection is to distinguish events within videos that deviate from expected normal behavior. An effective anomaly detection model requires strong spatio-temporal feature extraction capabilities to capture both appearance and motion information from the video. We utilize a generative adversarial networks model to perform anomaly detection by predicting future frame. The model is trained with multi-objective loss function for appearance and motion constraints. We introduce multi-objective optimization algorithm to guarantee the convergence of training objectives, including intensity loss, gradient loss for appearance constraints, optical flow loss for motion constraints and adversarial loss for adversarial training. By ensuring corresponding generative outcome for both normal events to confirm to expectation and anomaly events not to do so, we obtain an anomaly detection model with satisfying experimental result on video anomaly detection datasets, showing the success of the proposed training strategy.

articleTitle: A Research on Wide Voltage Range DC-DC Converter for DC Distribution System
abstract: In order to construct a low-voltage bipolar DC distribution system with a wide input voltage range, a DC-DC converter and a voltage balancer are required. A boost-type LC resonance is proposed to achieve voltage balancing without an additional voltage balancer. By integrating two interleaved parallel Boost inductors, the gain range of the LC converter can be broadened and the input current ripple can be reduced. Additionally, each bipolar output is independent, so that if one path fails, the other path can still output normally, ensuring the reliability of the system. A hybrid control method of pulse width modulation (PWM) with single-phase shift is also proposed to achieve zero-voltage switching (ZVS) for all switches. Finally, the effectiveness of the converter is verified through a l-kW simulation model.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv8 method for Ship Instances Segmentation of Small targets in Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Since traditional instance segmentation methods have low accuracy and slow speed for small target in remote sensing images, an improved YOLOv8 method is proposed to improve the detection accuracy of small targets. Firstly, we adopt a dual-level routing attention module based on the Vision Transformer architecture to effectively capture long-range depen-dencies among targets and detailed information within individual targets. This facilitates a better understanding of interconnections among small-scale target ships, consequently leading to enhanced accuracy and robustness in the segmentation process. Secondly, Wise IoU Loss function based on dynamic nonmonotonic focusing mechanism is used. By introducing a weight map to dynamically adjust the model's precise matching of target boundaries, the robustness of the model is improved and missed detections caused by small target sizes are avoided. Finally, a small object detection layer is added to connect shallow and deep feature maps for multi-level information fusion, making the network more focused on small object detection. The results show that the improved YOLOv8 method improves the AP by 2.5% compared with the baseline model (YOLOv8) on the HRSID dataset. In contrast to other state-of-the-art instance segmentation methods such as Mask RCNN and Mask Scorning RCNN, the AP of the improved method increased by 5.8% and 5.4%, respectively. Experimental results show that the modified method significantly improves the segmentation performance of small objects in remote sensing images.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Filter Design for IT2 Fuzzy Multi Agent Systems Under Dynamic Event-Triggered Scheme
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of fault detection (FD) filter for nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) with uncertainty and randomly occurring faults. In order to save network bandwidth occupation, the dynamic event-triggered scheme (DETS) is adopted and an intermediate variable is introduced to make the triggering intervals larger, and still ensure an excellent FD performance. And then, the co-design of DETS and the FD filter is achieved and the robustly stochastically stable of the closed-loop system is guaranteed. Finally, a numerical example is given to illustrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis and Tolerance Control for the Sticking of the Fuel Metering Valve in Aeroengine
abstract: In an aeroengine, the fuel regulator controls the fuel flow by adjusting the flow area of the fuel metering valve (FMV). The flow area of the FMV is regulated by controlling the motion of the spool of the FMV relative to the sleeve of the FMV. However, the FMV can become stuck due to pollutants entering the gap between the spool and sleeve, resulting in a decreased aeroengine performance. It is called the sticking of the FMV (SFMV). To address the damage caused by the SFMV, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on the Extended State Observer (ESO) to estimate the levels of the SFMV. Additionally, we employ the Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) to achieve fault tolerance control and eliminate the impact of SFMV, thereby enhancing the reliability of the aeroengine.

Author Keywords: Sticking of the fuel metering valve (SFMV)

articleTitle: Induced attack on formation control of multiagent systems via robust H∞ scheme
abstract: This paper investigates an induced attack problem against the formation control of multiagent systems. A new induced attack strategy based on the robust H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> scheme is proposed, which can guide the whole formation of multiagent systems to a prescribed reference trajectory. In comparison to deception attacks and denial-of-service attacks, the stability and formation structure of the multiagent system are not destroyed by the induced attack. First, the attack generation exosystem is designed to produce the induced attack signal and the prescribed reference trajectory. Based on the induced attack signal among partial agents, a new induced attack protocol is proposed and the specific impacts of the induced attack signal on formation control are discussed. Then, sufficient conditions are given to ensure the multiagent system to be induced. Finally, a simulation is conducted to further verify the main results.

articleTitle: Imbalanced Fault Diagnosis of Key Components in Spacecraft ACS via Collaborative ResNet
abstract: In this paper, a fault diagnosis method based on Collaborative Residual Network (Collaborative ResNet) is proposed to address the problem of imbalanced fault diagnosis for key components of spacecraft attitude control system (ACS). The designed Collaborative ResNet consists of two branches, the conventional learning branch and rebalancing learning branch, which conduct representation learning and classifier learning, respectively. A new Dynamic Complementary Loss (DC Loss) is introduced in the rebalancing learning to dynamically alleviate the excessive gradient of negative samples on the few sample classes and compensate for the gradient of misdiagnosed samples, which enhances the network sensitivity to the class with few number samples. Then the features extracted by two branches are adaptively integrated through the collaborative learning strategy to combine the strengths of both approaches. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated on the imbalanced data collected on a ground semi-physical platform.

articleTitle: Neural-Network-Based Filtering with Encoding Mechanisms: Applications to Multiple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
abstract: In this paper, the neural-network-based filtering problem is investigated for multi-sensor systems with dynamic encoding mechanisms. The sensor nodes and the remote filter are connected through bandwidth-constrained communication networks. To alleviate the communication burden, a novel dynamic encoding-based data compression-decompression mechanism is proposed so as to encode the data into a limited number of bits. Then, with the aid of the neural network learning method, a neural-network-based set-membership filter is developed for estimating the system states. Sufficient conditions are obtained to ensure that the filtering error remains within the bounded ellipsoidal set. In addition, the neural network tuning parameters and the filter gains are calculated by solving constrained optimization problems. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed filtering algorithm is verified through a scenario of maneuvering target tracking using multiple unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Tracking Control with Prescribed Performance of Free-Flying Space Manipulator Under Actuator Saturation
abstract: The trajectory tracking control problem of the free-flying space manipulator considering parameter uncertainty, external disturbance under actuator saturation constraint with prescribed performance is studied in this paper. In order to cope with the specified performance, a modified appointed-time performance function for error transformation is introduced. Based on the robust integral of the sign of error (RISE) feedback control method, we designed a PPF-RISE-Saturation controller, which can simultaneously guarantee the prescribed tracking performance and closed-loop asymptotic stability. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed controller is validated through comparative numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Transient Modeling and Scheduling for Heterogeneous Serial Lines with Bernoulli Machines and Finite Buffers
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing emphasis on intelligent manufacturing at the national level, the influence of flexible manufacturing systems and distributed production in the manufacturing industry has been expanding. Meanwhile, serial lines with limited buffers and random machine failures have been commonly seen in practical flexible production. When orders from the same customer are produced in different lines, the required production processes and cycles may differ. In such cases, these serial lines can be referred to as heterogeneous lines. This paper offers a model and analysis of a mixed-series assembly line featuring Bernoulli machines and finite buffer storage, followed by a discussion on the optimal scheduling problem for job allocation. A novel strategy is introduced for addressing the scheduling problem, utilizing a discrete particle swarm optimization algorithm. The effectiveness of the algorithm is demonstrated through numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Defect Detection for Steel Strip Surface Based on SG-YOLOv5
abstract: The steel strip is widely used in the industrial sector as a crucial raw material. However, various forms of damages can occur on the surface of steel strips during production and usage, necessitating the quick and accurate detection of these defects. Current detection methods are faced with challenges such as large model parameters, low detection accuracy, and slow detection speed. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the SG-YOLOv5 algorithm. Firstly, we introduce the SIMAM non-parametric attention mechanism at the output end of the backbone to enhance the feature extraction capability and stability of the detection algorithm without introducing additional parameters. Additionally, we utilize GSconv lightweight convolution kernels and a lightweight module named VGSCSP, which is optimized based on GSconv, to reduce the complexity of the backbone network. The SG-YOLOv5 algorithm significantly reduces the model parameters, accelerates the detection speed, and improves the accuracy of the model. The final model achieves a reduction in parameters by 15.26%, an increase in detection accuracy by 1.8%, and a frame rate of 35.5 frames per second (fps).

articleTitle: Jump-NERF: An Approach to Removing Glare and Pseudo Shadows Caused by Glass in Architectural Spaces
abstract: considering the optical factors of glass specular reflections on NERF (Neural Radiance Fields) rendering, this article focuses on optimizing NERF technology in the aspect of glass occlusion, mainly addressing the problem of its impact on indoor space model construction. By inferring distances and incorporating constraint elements, the sampling mechanism of the neural radiance field is improved to eliminate specular occlusion, while reducing the number of invalid sampling points through adaptive constraints based on limiting factors, thus accelerating the rendering and reconstruction process of the NERF model.

articleTitle: Robust Fault-tolerant Control of Periodic Piecewise Time-varying Systems Based on Matrix Polynomials
abstract: This paper investigates the robust fault-tolerant control issue for a type of periodic piecewise time-varying systems (PPTVSs). The PPTVS is modeled considering the coexistence of external disturbances, structural parameter perturbations, and actuator failures in the system. Stability analysis is conducted for the considered PPTVS, and a sufficient condition concerning the exponential stability of the closed-loop system is given.
