Through a matrix polynomial approach capable of decoupling time-varying parameters, the robust fault-tolerant controller synthesis is transformed into a convex optimization problem. Flexible controller gains are enabled through selectable subinterval partitioning parameters. A sufficient condition is presented for maintaining the exponential stability, achieving <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> disturbance attenuation, and obtaining a tractable robust fault-tolerant controller. Simulation verification using a multi-input multi-output PPTVS model shows that the designed controller can maintain the exponential stability under actuator failures, satisfy the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> performance index, and exhibiting robustness against structural parameter perturbations.

articleTitle: PDR Algorithm for Particle Filtering Based on Motion Optimization Models
abstract: In this paper, for the problem of decreased positioning accuracy of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) in urban environment due to signal occlusion, reflection and other factors, combined with the demand of ordinary pedestrians for high-precision positioning, we propose a Pedestrian Dead Reckoning (PDR) combination positioning technique based on GNSS assistance. The double threshold energy detection method is used to detect the MEMS data after wavelet noise reduction, to realize accurate and efficient pace recognition, so as to improve the PDR positioning accuracy, to establish the observation model with the GNSS information, and to correct the PDR algorithm through the improved particle filtering, which can effectively inhibit the cumulative error caused by the long time working of MEMS and the positioning error caused by the reduced accuracy of GNSS in the complex environment. Experiments are designed to demonstrate the algorithm, and the pace recognition rate reaches more than 99% and the mean square error of the positioning result is 1.2m when tested in the complex test section, indicating that the algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy of positioning.

articleTitle: Formation Control Technology Based on Backstepping Method with the Estimation of the Leader's State
abstract: In order to solve the problem of formation control, a cooperative control method based on backstepping method is proposed, which can make the UAV converge to the desired formation and achieve steady state. To facilitate the engineering application, the models are established by using the leader-follower formation mode, and the communication mode between the UAVs is constructed based on the graph theory. The corresponding formation control structure is devised by backstepping method, and the stability proof is given. A distributed state observer is added to estimate the state of the leader in a finite time without affecting the formation control. The simulation results show that the UAVs can quickly converge to the corresponding position and still maintain high precision during maneuvering.

articleTitle: A Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Controller Based on Extended State Observer of Flying Boom
abstract: Flying boom refueling is a more complex system than hose-and-drogue refueling. Correspondingly, its refueling efficiency is much higher than hose-and-drogue refueling, and its flying boom can be controlled, which can greatly improve the success rate of docking. Considering that there are some problems in the control process of the flying boom, it is difficult to control well because the flying boom is a nonlinear system, and meanwhile, disturbances including the tanker wake and atmospheric turbulence may interfere with the flying boom. To solve the above problems, a super-twisting sliding mode control method is designed to improve the control quality of the flying boom nonlinear system, and an extended state observer is introduced to anti-disturbance. The simulation results demonstrate the proposed attitude controller's effectiveness and robustness.

articleTitle: Application of Dual Motor Synchronous Control System in Pollination Equipment
abstract: With the increasing level of agricultural mechanization, the dual-motor synchronous control system has been widely used in agricultural production. In view of the motor asynchronism caused by delayed start and stop and uneven load on both sides during operation of auxiliary pollination equipment, the traditional master-slave control is improved and used as the motor synchronization control method in this paper. Due to the large area and humidity of rice fields, The wired communication method will not only increase the cost of wiring, but also the wiring will be damaged by corrosion. In this paper, LoRa (Long Range Radio) is used as the wireless communication module for two motors to realize the local data transmission of the motors and solve the problem of unsynchronized two motors. Finally, the experimental platform was built to analyze the operating data of the master and slave motors. The experimental results show that the LoRa-based dual-motor synchronization system shows better synchronization and can be well applied to pollination equipment.

articleTitle: Null-Space-Based Elegant Anti-Disturbance Control Allocation for Autonomous Berthing
abstract: To mitigate the impact of multi-source disturbances, such as environmental loads, bank effects, model uncertainties, and control allocation (CA) errors, during autonomous ship berthing, we propose an anti-disturbance control allocation method based on the null-space. This method considers the real-time and precision requirements of motion control allocation algorithms, as well as the characteristics of disturbances and their corresponding responses. The first step involves establishing models for ship berthing motion, multi-source disturbances, and control allocation. A passive elegant extended state observer (PEESO) is designed to estimate ship states and multi-source disturbances in real-time. Moreover, null-space technology is employed to develop a CA algorithm that ensures real-time and accurate results. This algorithm achieves the scheme of stabilization control outside the berth and then parallel berthing. Simulation and comparison experiments demonstrate that this method ensures the accuracy of berthing motion control and significantly reduces computation time, thereby decreasing the maximum allocation error.

articleTitle: Distributed Fixed-Time Nash Equilibrium Seeking via an Estimator-Based Approach
abstract: In this paper, a fixed-time algorithm is proposed to solve the Nash equilibrium seeking problem of multi-agent systems in aggregative games. The purpose of this paper is to minimize the cost function of each player. The cost function for each player includes not only the player's own actions but also the sum of all other player actions. We divide the algorithm into two layers: the estimation layer implements the search for Nash equilibrium, while the local control layer implements the tracking of the estimated state. The stability of the two-layer algorithm in fixed-time is proved by the Lyapunov function method. Finally, a simulated example is provided to confirm the algorithm's efficacy.

articleTitle: Master-Slave INS Transfer Alignment Based on State-Transformation Extended Kalman Filter
abstract: In this study, a fast transfer alignment algorithm that fuses the velocity-attitude-position of the Master-Slave INS is proposed. A state-transformation extended Kalman filter (ST-EKF) with better filtering robustness is used instead of the conventional extended Kalman filter (EKF) for the transfer alignment of the Master-Slave INS. The accuracy of the proposed algorithm is verified by three sets of on-board field transfer alignment experiments under different maneuvering trajectories. The results show that the proposed ST -EKF -based transfer alignment algorithm has higher alignment accuracy and faster convergence speed, and the 180s localization accuracy RMSE of the ST-EKF algorithm is improved by 23.29% on average compared to the EKF algorithm.

articleTitle: Joint Train Timetable Optimization for Short-Turning Strategy and Flexible Train Decomposition
abstract: In order to adapt to the passenger demand with uneven spatial and temporal distribution, this paper studies the train timetable optimization problem and proposes a timetable optimization method that combines short-turning strategy and flexible train decomposition, i.e., rolling stock is able to determine whether it is required to be uncoupled and whether it should perform a short-turn strategy according to passenger demand. A mixed integer nonlinear programming(MINLP) model has been constructed to minimize the number of stranded passengers at all stations on the line. Numerical experiments are designed to evaluate the validity of the proposed method based on real data of Beijing Metro Yizhuang Line during morning peak hours. The results show that the introduction of flexible train decomposition mode can better decrease the amount of stranded passengers without increasing the amount of rolling stocks compared with the conventional short-turning operation strategy.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Graph-Based Muti-Agent Learning Method for Dynamic Scheduling of Flexible Job Shop
abstract: Dynamic scheduling is a complicated problem with high research value in the production field, because it requires a fast response to the dynamic disturbance event. In this paper, knowledge graph is combined with reinforcement learning to solve this problem. In the proposed method, knowledge graph model is constructed by a series of steps, including ontology-based knowledge modeling, knowledge extraction, and knowledge fusion. In the knowledge graph model, the state information of the shop floor is extracted from the production data, including the information about machine, job, and process. On this basis, reinforcement learning model is designed, which is composed of machine assignment agent and job sequence agent. Thus, the real-time scheduling decisions can be made rapidly under the dynamic production environment. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified on a case study of aviation component production workshop. Compared with other methods, the proposed method obtains the best results.

articleTitle: Constructivism-Inspired Meta-Knowledge Learning and Reuse
abstract: Efficient continual learning of humans is enabled by interactions of a series of learning mechanisms and human memory system. Constructivism is a theory in education that proposes learners construct knowledge from their experiences, assimilation and accommodation are key to this process. Also, research shows knowledge in human memory system is represented as a high-dimensional and sparse vector. Motivated by these, in our paper, we propose a continual feature learning method based on constructivisim and memory system. We divide continual feature learning into two stages. In assimilation stage, assimilation model captures knowledge that cannot be represented by meta-knowledge in knowledge base and update the knowledge base according to new knowledge. Furthermore, in accommodation stage, accommodation model updates its learning ability based on new tasks and new knowledge base, ensuring the continual feature learning of new tasks without forgetting previous knowledge. Experimental results show our proposed method can further alleviate the forgetting effect of the model.

articleTitle: Control Design for a Class of Cascaded Nonlinear Systems: Backstepping vs Fully-Actuated System Approach
abstract: This paper deals with the control problem for a class of cascaded nonlinear systems holding a wide application. The nonlinear system is firstly given and analyzed. In what follows, the classical backstepping method and the Fully-actuated system approach are sequentially utilized to derive the nonlinear controllers. The controllers are then compared from the theoretical perspective and furthermore some advice is proposed for the future applications of the above two approaches.

articleTitle: DA-Zero- DCE
abstract: Tunnel images are affected by the shooting environment, resulting in uneven illumination distribution, local occlusion, and a high amount of noise. To address the overexposure and distortion issues in existing image enhancement algorithms, this paper proposes a tunnel image enhancement algorithm called DA-Zero-DCE (Denoising-Attention based Zero-Reference Deep Curve Estimation). Firstly, based on the Zero-DCE model, the U-Net is used to improve the backbone network DCE-Net for curve estimation, and a coordinate attention mechanism is added to enhance the dark light perception ability of local image areas. Secondly, the NAF-Net noise removal module is added after the curve estimation backbone network to effectively suppress the noise after low-light enhancement by Zero-DCE. In addition, to alleviate the distortion and overexposure of the enhanced images, the 4-neighborhood calculation method of the spatial consistency loss function is extended to an 8- neighbor hood calculation method, enhancing the smoothness of the output results. Through the ablation experiment conclusions on the LOL dataset, the DA-Zero-DCE model compared to the Zero-DCE model has a PSNR improvement of about 10dB and an SSIM improvement of about 0.1, verifying the effectiveness and feasibility of the model.

articleTitle: Image Semantic Segmentation Based on Few-Shot Learning
abstract: The convolutional neural network-based semantic segmentation is emerging few-shot learning, which is quite popular in the field of image processing. Semantic segmentation can make good use of a small number of datasets to achieve image segmentation effectively. This paper takes image segmentation as an entry point to study few-shot learning algorithms, focusing on the deep convolutional network-based image segmentation algorithm for semantic segmentation. In this paper, the network module construction includes the feature extraction module, the support-query module, and the query-support module. Then, a variety of small sample datasets were collected separately and the dataset production was carried out, dividing the datasets into support and query sets, training and testing the small sample datasets in a variety of scenarios. Finally, we compare and analyze the image segmentation effect of the model under various small sample datasets.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Hydrogen Fuel Cell Test System Based on Hadoop Architecture
abstract: Traditional file storage and analysis tools can no longer adapt to the growing mass data storage and complex and multi-structured data analysis. Aiming at the problem that the test data analysis of key components of hydrogen fuel cell needs to deal with high concurrency and massive data, this paper adopts Hadoop big data architecture to establish a big data platform for test data management of key components of fuel cell. The test system based on big data analysis can monitor the test environment parameters in real time, complete the analysis and calculation of the test environment parameters, design the big data platform architecture, and verify the feasibility and advantages of the platform design by building the Hadoop cluster environment.

articleTitle: Stereo-Camera 3D Multi-Object Tracking Based on Optimized PMBM Algorithm
abstract: Multi-object tracking technology is a key technology for environment perception of autonomous vehicles. In this paper, we propose a 3D multi-object tracking method based on PMBM filter with binocular images as input. The algorithm uses stereo camera to obtain the positions of multiple objects in the scene and track them. To run the tracking method online requires a detection method with high real-time performance, but higher speed 3D detection algorithm has poorer performance in the detection, the change of illumination and object occlusion will lead to frequent missed detection. To address this problem, we added tracking feedback correction to the original PMBM filter and optimized the object born and death models of the original algorithm. Our tracking algorithm was evaluated on the public dataset KITTI, proving that it can accurately track objects in a variety of urban environments. The effectiveness of tracking feedback correction and optimized birth and death models is also demonstrated by ablation experiments,

articleTitle: Bi-YOLOv8 Based Safety Detection Algorithm in Power Plant Environment
abstract: Timely safety detection is essential to prevent the accidents in the power plants. So far, research in the safety helmets detection has mainly focused on the features such as shape or color. However, it could be severely compromised by various factors, such as numerous facilities, complex shadow occlusions and the presence of smoke and dust. In this paper, a practical safety helmet wearing detection system is proposed, which utilizes a unique backbone network structure, called Bi-YOLOv8 with the improved backbone network structure. A pedestrian safety detection simulation dataset (PPW-dataset) is first formed in the power plant environment. This dataset can not only simulate the real scene of the power plant, but also meet the requirements of common safety detection tasks. Further, a feature extraction method is developed to improve the occluded target recognition by assigning shallow position information to deep features while preserving the original features of the image. Finally, a large number of the experimental results on different public datasets as well as PPW-dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed object detection method.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Gaussian Integration-Based Real-Time Mapping Method of Spline Length and Parameters
abstract: The real-time determination of precise mapping relationship between spline curve length and parameters is essential for efficient spline path planning. This paper proposes a general solution method for the mapping relationship based on the idea of predictor and corrector. The proposed method utilizes first-order derivatives to predict the target parameters. The calibration method employs adaptive Gaussian integration, which avoids uncontrolled errors in traditional Taylor expansion methods. This prediction-correction method ensures real-time performance while guaranteeing mapping accuracy. The correction of the proposed method is verified by simulation result.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon and Economic Operation Scheduling Method of Multiple Energy Stations Based on Analytical Target Cascading
abstract: Aiming at the multi-objective problems such as carbon emission reduction and economic operation of multiple energy stations in integrated energy system, an optimal scheduling model considering low-carbon and economic operation is adopted. In the dispatching mode of the integrated energy system, a variety of energy conversion equipment is mainly used to optimize the energy distribution, and the charging and discharging power of the energy storage station is used to enhance the regulating ability of the multiple energy stations. In this paper, the balance constraints of electricity, heat, cold and gas in multiple energy stations system as well as the operation constraints of capacity equipment and energy storage equipment are established. Finally, the multi-objective model is optimized based on the energy balance and operational constraints of the multiple energy stations system by using analytical target cascading. The effectiveness and rationality of the proposed method are verified by an example. The results show that the proposed method not only enables the low-carbon operation of the multiple energy stations, but also takes into account the economic operation of each energy station, and at the same time realizes the full absorption of renewable energy output.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a High Reliability General Test Platform for Spacecraft
abstract: In order to solve the problems of wide variety of test device, poor versatility and high requirement for tester, a general test system design method based on standard backplane bus is proposed. A general test platform based on 1553B bus is developed based on the principle of hardware modularization and software configuration, the functional requirements and system composition of the platform are described. The platform has been verified in the process of product test and subsystem joint test of spacecraft’ TT&C subsystem. The test results show that the platform has the advantages of high degree of automation, friendly interface and good scalability, which can meet the requirements of spacecraft’ testing during the periods of producing, testing and launching. It can greatly improve the test efficiency of spacecraft's product, has obvious economic benefits and wide application prospects. It has important reference significance for the general research and design of test device for the other spacecraft.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Quadruped Robot Using HQP-Based Virtual Model Control
abstract: This paper proposes a virtual model control framework based on hierarchical quadratic programming to achieve the optimal distribution of foot forces for a quadruped robot. The framework comprises the optimal force distribution of the support phase and acceleration adaptive virtual stiffness control of the swing phase. In the support phase, the optimal distribution of the foot force is transformed into a hierarchical quadratic programming problem. The goal is to achieve task priority coordination in different stages of the support phase. The mapping relationship between the ground reaction force on the foot and the virtual force on the torso is used for this purpose. In the swing phase, the virtual stiffness is adaptively adjusted to improve the trajectory tracking performance according to the acceleration demand of the foot trajectory tracking. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the robot performs trot and other gaits with significant stability improvement, and the results validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed control framework.

articleTitle: Research on Revit-Based Turning Algorithm of Climbing Frame Type Mold for High-Rise Building Construction
abstract: To assist the Construction of a climbing frame for high-rise building construction and enrich the family of climbing frame parts, this paper proposes an algorithm for the molding of climbing frame parts, which automatically molds the Revit 3D model and forms the family file according to the CAD 2D drawings of climbing frame parts. The original information, such as text and geometric elements in the drawing of the part, is extracted in Revit. The algorithm is designed to calculate the data such as bottom profile, height, and hole position, and the 3D model of the part is built, and the family of the part is formed by stretching the bottom profile and cutting the hole. For the same type of parts, the differences between the parts are parameterized, and the structure of the parts is determined according to the parameters. The model is built, and the family of parts is formed. It improves the design efficiency of the climbing frame for high-rise building construction, lays the foundation for the subsequent overall design of the climbing frame, and provides specific value in promoting the application of BIM technology in the architectural design industry.

articleTitle: Fault location in distribution network with high penetration distributed generations based on wavelet ConvNeXt network
abstract: When a fault occurs in the distribution network, distributed generation may self-protect and operate off-grid, leading to more complex system fault characteristics. The hazards are even greater when the penetration of distributed generation is high, making it more difficult to locate faults accurately, especially arcing and high-resistance ground faults. In this paper, multiple fault type localization methods adapted to dynamic changes in permeability are proposed. First, using wavelet packet decomposition and reconstruction, the voltage and current signals along the line are transformed into the time-frequency matrices. Using interval scaling and pseudo-color coding, the time-frequency matrix encompassing the system conditions is transformed into a color map of the time-frequency information. Then, the fault features are extracted with the help of ConvNeXt deep neural network. Constructing the network structure and parameters and tuning them globally, a model of fault location algorithm is generated. Simulating the fault operation of a high permeability distribution network, a traditional CNN network is introduced for comparison to verify the fault localization performance of the algorithm. The proposed method has high localization accuracy at different fault moment, fault type and transition resistance, and also is adaptable in different neutral grounding modes, network topologies and dynamics of the penetration rate.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Event-Triggered Output-Feedback Control for Uncertain Nonlinear Systems Under FDI Attacks
abstract: The paper considers the output-feedback issue of uncertain nonlinear systems under false data injection (FDI) attacks. A fuzzy state observer is constructed to observe unavailable state values and compensate for adverse effects caused by FDI attacks. Since the event-triggered mechanism (ETM) is introduced to the controller-to-actuator and sensor-to-controller channels simultaneously, the system output is discontinuous, which leads to a non-differentiable virtual control law in the backstepping method. In this scenario, the conventional backstepping approach becomes impractical. The dynamic surface control (DSC) scheme is utilized to overcome the above obstacle, where first-order filters are introduced to avoid differentiating the virtual control laws. Unlike the existing literatures that consider output triggering, our method doesn't require the system function to satisfy the global Lipschitz continuity condition. Finally, numerical simulation outcomes are provided to showcase the efficacy of the designed control strategy,

articleTitle: Distributed Hierarchical Control and Economic Dispatch in AC Microgrid
abstract: In the development of smart grids, microgrids serve as an intermediate stage, promoting the penetration of renewable energy sources and enhancing power supply reliability. Traditional control and optimization strategies for microgrids often employ a hierarchical approach, where the economic dispatch layer operates at a larger time scale compared to the frequency restoration control layer. However, due to challenges in accurately predicting renewable energy generation and significant forecasting errors, the increasing integration of stochastic and intermittent renewable energy sources in microgrids can undermine the system's economic efficiency when using traditional separate optimization and control strategies. To address this issue, this paper introduces a distributed hierarchical control strategy designed for microgrids. This method enables simultaneous handling of frequency restoration and economic dispatch within the microgrid, operating on a shorter time scale. By eradicating the temporal mismatch between the frequency restoration and economic dispatch control layers, this proposed strategy improves the economic effectiveness of the microgrid system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Prescribed Finite-Time Asymptotic Tracking Control for a One-Link Manipulator Regardless of Initial Angle Position
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive prescribed finite-time asymptotic tracking control (ATC) scheme is proposed for a one-link manipulator, which is independent of the initial angle position. To obtain the prescribed performance control (PPC) without dependence on the initial angle position, a hyperbolic tangent function (HTF) is employed to transform the error of the angle position to a new variable. Then, the control design is transformed to constrain the new variable. In addition, to avoid the overlarge initial control voltage caused by the large initial error, an input control function (ICF) is introduced to obtain the control signal with zero initial value. Meanwhile, the asymptotic tracking performance (ATP) of the angle position is verified based on Barbalat's Lemma. As a result, the designed controller guarantees the prescribed finite-time performance and the ATP of the manipulator as well as the boundedness of all the system signals. Finally, the effectiveness and applicability of the designed controller are demonstrated by simulations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Monocular 3D Object Detection with Occlusion Compensation
abstract: In the context of autonomous driving, occlusion significantly impacts the accuracy of monocular 3D object detection. To address this issue, a monocular 3D detection occlusion compensation algorithm is proposed to optimize the detection results affected by occlusion. The approach involves integrating an occlusion processing module into the 3D object detection pipeline. This module analyzes and handles occluded vehicles by leveraging 2D object detection results to infer occlusion relation-ships. Subsequently, the occluded local features associated with these relationships are captured by the local feature processing module and then input to the occlusion processing network. The resulting occlusion compensation offset is fed into the 3D object detection branch. Experimental results demonstrate that the method outperforms existing approaches on the KITTI 3D object detection benchmark.

articleTitle: Discrete-Time Event-Triggered H-Infinity Stabilization for Networked Cascade Control Systems with Transmission Delay
abstract: This paper focuses on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H\infty$</tex> suppression problem of network cascade control with double time delay and perturbation, where the design of multiple controllers in a control system is a difficult problem when there are perturbations in the system. In order to solve the influence of perturbation on controller design, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H\infty$</tex> control theory is introduced in this paper. First, a discrete network cascade control system with double time delay is modeled. Based on this, a suitable Lyapunov function is constructed to provide sufficient conditions for the stability of the system. Then the stability and co-design problems of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H{\infty}$</tex> controller are analyzed. Finally, the feasibility of the co-design scheme is verified by a simulation example of a boiler in a thermal power plant.

articleTitle: Interactive Trajectory Planning of Autonomous Vehicle Based on State Lattice and Potential Field
abstract: In order to solve the problem of trajectory planning in complex traffic scenarios, such as falling into local optimization and generating trajectory machinery, it will lead to low acceptance degree of users. We propose an interactive trajectory planning framework based on the combination of state lattice and potential field. The lattice search method is used to discretization the driving environment and reduce the solution space. At the same time, by constructing an interactive road environment potential field, considering changes in traffic participants' intentions, the trajectory is updated in a timely manner, and the trajectory is optimized based on the scene. This article conducts real-world experiments in various challenging and complex scenarios, and the experimental results verify that the trajectory planner can generate safe, comfortable, and flexible trajectories with high timeliness.

articleTitle: Research on Non-contact Measurement of Ship Shafting Thrust Under Rotating Speed Change
abstract: This paper proposes a new non-contact measurement method to solve the problem of accurately measuring the shafting thrust in the complex environment. According to the principle of shafting deformation, the small change of axial displacement is sensed by the light-receiving sensor, and then the accurate shafting thrust value can be obtained. However, due to this method's high precision and high sensitivity, the results are easily disturbed by the complex environment. This article is based on shafting speed change in ship navigation; the error interference of axial displacement deformation in the non-contact thrust measurement method is calculated theoretically, simulated by the ANSYS model and verified by experiments. The final results show that with the increase in rotating speed, the axial displacement deformation increases gradually with the trend of the quadratic function.

articleTitle: Bumpless Transfer Control for Event-Triggered Switched Cyber-Physical Systems Subject to DoS Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the bumpless transfer (BT) control problem for event-triggered switched cyber-physical systems (SCPSs) subject to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. A state-dependent switching signal is designed and an event-triggered mechanism is proposed. First, based on the absence or presence of DoS attacks, the SCPS is divided into two modes, and then the control problem under DoS attacks is transformed into a switching control problem. Second, the definition of BT performance for SCPSs subject to DoS attacks is given. Third, conditions are established to ensure asymptotic stability and BT performance of the closed-loop system. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified through a simulation example.

articleTitle: A Grasping Pose Detection Algorithm for Occluded Objects
abstract: To solve the problem of difficult grasping detection of occluded objects, this paper proposes a Channel Attention Grasp Convolution Neural Network (CA-GraspNet) based on convolution neural networks and channel attention mechanisms. CA-GraspNet integrates residual module and the SENet module. This module enables CNN to focus more on the no occluded area and less on the occluded area, overcoming the low accuracy of the existing methods in identifying occluded objects. The occluded datasets are obtained through data enhancement of Cornell and Jacquard grasp datasets, and the occluded datasets are used for algorithm verification. The experimental results show that CA-GraspNet can obtain 97% detection accuracy on Cornell occluded datasets, and 88% on Jacquard occluded datasets, which is higher than similar algorithms. Furthermore, CA-GraspNet also shows approximate performance in grasping detection.

articleTitle: Resource Orchestration and Scheduling Algorithms for Enhancing Distributed Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In modern distributed computing, effective resource allocation assumes a paramount role in bolstering application performance. Kubernetes leverages localized scheduling algorithms to ensure astute resource utilization and alignment with application requisites. Nonetheless, the domain of distributed reinforcement learning poses challenges rooted in the intricate landscape of multi-node agent training and environment simulation, which engenders resource contention issues and heightened communication overhead. This paper introduces the LeaderFirst and Batch Tasks Centralized algorithms to counteract these challenges. The LeaderFirst algorithm demonstrates judicious allocation of Learner resources, disentangling reinforcement learning tasks to attain synchronization and proficiently alleviate competitive dynamics. Conversely, the Batch Tasks Centralized algorithm concentrates on the efficient bundling of tasks to maximize resource employment, all while judiciously addressing the mitigation of distributed communication overhead. Through empirical assessment, these algorithms showcase pronounced advantages over their Kubernetes native counterparts.

articleTitle: Intelligent Lifting Path Planning of Tower Crane Based on Glowworm Swarm Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the problems of unstable transportation paths and many inflection points affecting system safety planned by tower cranes in complex working environments, an improved Glowworm Swarm Optimization algorithm is proposed to carry out intelligent lifting path planning for tower cranes. Based on the working scene of the tower crane, a three-dimensional map environment model is established to simulate the complex building environment with many obstacles, and the standard Glowworm Swarm Optimization algorithm is improved according to the operating characteristics of the tower crane. The step factor of the Glowworm Swarm Optimization algorithm is adaptively designed for accurate path planning outcomes. The problem of slowing down or discontinuous crane movement brought on by the twisted path is resolved by reducing the variety of directions in which glowworms can move to the direction toward the goal point. The incorporation of a mutation strategy aimed at enhancing the stability of crane path planning. B-spline data interpolation is used to fit the curve to obtain a smooth and obstacle-avoidance path that is more suitable for the tower crane in order to prevent the crane from constantly braking. The simulation results demonstrate that the improved algorithm can locate a tower crane's ideal obstacle avoidance path in a challenging construction environment. The resulting path is smoother and has fewer inflection points, increasing the tower crane's safety and carrying capacity.

articleTitle: Terminal Data Perception Architecture of Intelligent Subway
abstract: This paper carries out an architecture of terminal data perception for intelligent subway and presents a valuable applied method for Internet of Things (IoT) technology. Firstly, the typical business scenarios of subway and the requirements of terminal data perception are analyzed. Secondly, this paper proposes the general framework, typical system architecture, network architecture and functional architecture of the intelligent subway system based on terminal data perception. Finally, this paper takes the Capital Airport Line and Beixinqiao Station as examples, and demonstrates the application from both line and station levels. By comparing with the original system, the advantages of the proposed architecture are illustrated.

articleTitle: Learning Multi-Talented Image Restoration with Knowledge Factorization
abstract: Restoring images degraded by various corruptions using only one multi-talented network has been investigated recently. While the functional redundancy caused by the predefined multiple degradation types makes them inflexible to be deployed when applied on limited computational resources or degradation conditions. Correspondingly, we propose a novel and challenging task to decompose a multi-talented image restoration (IR) model into several task-specific models, termed as Image Restoration Knowledge Factorization (IRKF). To this end, we construct the decomposed subnetwork mainly consisting of common knowledge block(CKB) and task-specific block(TSB). During training, an activation module is first incorporated to select which TSB to handle the specific degradation task, whereas the CKB learns the undiversified representation across tasks. We employ knowledge distillation to factorize task-relevant knowledge from the multi-talented teacher to the dedicated student model. The problem is further solved by adopted contrastive regularization between TSBs, which enables the arbitrary combination of subnetworks. Experiments on two settings show that IRKF can be applied to existing multi-talented IR methods and get improvement on most tasks.

articleTitle: Bird Sounds Recognition Algorithm Using a Time Delay Neural Network
abstract: Bird monitoring is an effective method to investigate and research the environmental health status. Traditional bird monitoring relies on labor-intensive manual methods while computer vision monitoring is constrained by the environment and is not suitable for all bird monitoring scenarios. This paper proposes a time delay neural network-based bird sounds recognition algorithm that builds a dataset, extracts audio features and uses an enhanced time delay neural network for training to achieve efficient bird sound recognition. The algorithm was then tested on the collected audio data and proved to be effective.

articleTitle: Robust Active Visual Tracking of Space Non-Cooperative Objects
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) based Active Visual Tracking (AVT) algorithms targeting Space Non-cooperative Objects (SNCOs) is very vulnerable to various perturbations such as temporal action control command failure, actuator failure or signal transmission failure. Such perturbations can severely affect the performance of active visual trackers. Thus in this paper, targeting action failure, a robust DDPG based AVT algorithm is proposed which uses a new reward function to prevent DRL over-fitting. The proposed algorithm shows resistance to the perturbation and is able to perform outstanding tracking under high action failure probability. Sufficient experiments were conducted to verify the effectiveness and advancement of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Load Frequency Control System with Time-Varying Delays
abstract: In this paper, the stability analysis of Load frequency Control (LFC) systems with time-varying delay is conducted. Firstly, an augmented Lyapunov-Krasovskii (L-K) functional is designed to incorporate the relevant information of the delay state. Then, the functional derivatives are estimated using an auxiliary-function-based integral inequality in conjunction with an improved reciprocally convex inequality. Furthermore, the correlation function is processed through a quadratic function negative definite derivation. Finally, case studies established on a one-area LFC system are conducted to demonstrate the superiority of the method, and its accuracy is verified through a simulation case.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Framework for Dynamic Local Trajectory Planning
abstract: To enhance the mobility efficiency, safety, and ensure the dynamic feasibility of mobile robots, a local trajectory planning algorithm is proposed within complex two-dimensional environments. The method employs a hierarchical framework for trajectory planning – one layer densely maintains data and computes detailed path and velocity ranges offline, while another layer sparsely maintains data and selects specific trajectories online. This framework leverages the insight that obtaining all feasible trajectories during offline computation is most effective, and local trajectories are acquired by weighing scores in online scenarios. We recommend avoiding online searches to reduce computational complexity. This approach doesn't prioritize searching for the lowest-cost path (often the shortest path), but rather maximizes the likelihood of reaching the goal when determining the next navigational step. The method employs a two-layer linear programming algorithm to ascertain the maximum feasible velocity along the path, thereby generating dynamically feasible local trajectories. Ultimately, the effectiveness of this approach is validated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Matrix Approach to Verification of Nonblocking for Partially Observed Discrete Event Systems
abstract: To ensure the safety of discrete event systems, detecting the nonblocking property of the system is an effective approach. This paper proposes a matrix-based method to address the nonblocking property detection problem for partially observed discrete event systems. Firstly, we introduce nondeterministic output functions to represent the state dependency and nondeterministic of partial event observations, and model the partially observed discrete event systems as Mealy finite state machines with nondeterministic output functions. Furthermore, we utilize a novel matrix method called semi-tensor product to establish algebraic expressions for the finite state machine. Based on the obtained algebraic expressions, we analyze the nonblocking property verification problems of the finite state machine from a state perspective. We propose an algebraic algorithm to identify potentially blocking states in the finite state machine.

articleTitle: Adaptive Time-Varying Formation Control of ASVs with Model Uncertainties and External Disturbances Under Directed Topology*
abstract: In this brief, the time-varying formation control problem of autonomous surface vessels with model uncertainties and external disturbances is investigated under directed graph. Based on the backstepping method and dynamic surface control, a novel virtual control law is designed. Radial basis function neural network is utilized to deal with the model uncertainties exist in ASV system. Two different adaptive laws and a formation controller are proposed. It is proved that all signals in closed-loop system are semi-global uniformly ultimately bounded. A simulation is presented to validate the effectiveness of theoretical results.

articleTitle: Soft Four-Leaf Clover Physiotherapy Robot for Traditional Chinese Medicine Massage Physiotherapy
abstract: The new coronavirus may cause some people to be in a state of physical suboptimal health and leave behind sequelae. This article uses traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) massage physiotherapy to effectively prevent and alleviate the body suboptimal health condition, we design a pneumatic soft four-leaf clover physiotherapy robot that is both portable, safe and universally applicable. An embedded control system with a micro controller is set up, which solves the problem that the traditional physiotherapy robot has a single physiotherapy site. Combined with acupuncture point physiotherapy and TCM massage physiotherapy, the relevant motion control strategy is developed to regulate physical health condition, which effectively alleviates the symptoms caused by suboptimal health. Then, the proposed strategy to the control system is applied, the characteristics related to soft physical therapy robots is analyzed. Finally, some experiments are conducted to verify the feasibility of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Low-carbon economy optimal dispatching method considering integrated energy system of carbon capture and storage park
abstract: To efficiently utilize the carbon reduction capacity of the integrated energy system (IES) and optimize the overall operation cost of the park-level integrated energy system(PLIES), an operation optimization method of the PLIES that takes into account low-carbon and economic operation is proposed. First, the composition structure of the PLIES is designed, and key subsystem models such as carbon capture device model, multi-energy supply subsystem model with hydrogen storage function, and hierarchical carbon trading mechanism(CTS) model are constructed. Secondly, with the objective of minimizing the sum of energy procurement cost, wind abandonment cost, carbon trading cost and CO2 sales profit, a low-carbon economic optimization operation model of the PLIES with carbon capture device under the hierarchical CTS is constructed. The model is solved by using CPLEX software. Finally, through the simulation analysis of various scenarios, it is verified that the operation cost and carbon emission are both ideal under the graded CTS with carbon capture equipment in the PLIES, with a view to providing reference for the implementation of the “carbon reduction and peaking” energy strategy in China.

articleTitle: Automatic Microinjection Assistance System Based on Deep-Learning Visual Positioning
abstract: With the development of life sciences, the requirements for biological cell injection technology are getting higher and higher. Nowadays, most of the injection work is done manually, which is not only time-consuming and laborious, but also difficult to maintain a stable injection efficiency. Some automatic microinjection systems have been developed to improve efficiency, but it is essential to accurately identify and position cells and injection needles. This paper proposes a method for visual positioning work using a hardware device in combination with a deep learning target detection algorithm. The microinjection task is then completed by the integration of visual positioning and motion control via the upper computer control module. This microinjection assistance system is guided by visual positioning to reduce the difficulty of automatic microinjection and increase injection efficiency. Finally, the effectiveness of the microinjection assistance system is verified by using zebrafish embryos as an example, which lays the foundation for the subsequent development of automatic and intelligent cell microoperation systems.

articleTitle: Synthesising Controllers for Quadrotors via Imitation Learning
abstract: In this work, we present a quadrotor control solution using neural networks with imitation learning. Instead of mapping raw sensory variables to control outputs, we leverage a feature engineering method to design neural network input attributes, according to expert controller inputs. This improves the capability of the learning-based control policies on tracking different trajectories. Moreover, the neural network outputs of the collective thrust and torque can be directly fed to the quadrotor control allocator, without requiring any further data transformation. During the training process, we also use the Data Aggregation (DAgger) algorithm for the improved control performance. The simulation results show that the quadrotors, using the trained neural network controller, can achieve expert-like behaviour (i.e. tracking square trajectories).

articleTitle: Attacks Detection Against Two-Channel Partial FDI in CPS: A Moving Target Defense Method
abstract: In this paper, a problem of detection method based on moving target defense is studied for two-channel partial FDI attacks in CPS. Firstly, a two-channel partial FDI attack strategy is designed and its stealthiness is analyzed. Then, the detection mechanism is designed by weighting the time before and after the control signal of the system. Secondly, the analysis and deduction show that there exists a difference between the system residual under attack and the normal residual, which proves that the residual detection index after attack is divergent. Unlike the existing physical watermarking methods, the moving target item introduced only need to utilize the control amount of the previous moment, and do not need additional calculation and injection of the watermarking signal. It will not affect the residual of the system in normal operation, and can reduce the performance loss of the system. The feasibility and validity of the proposed method are verified through numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Research on State Estimation Algorithm of Maze Robot Based on Multi-Sensor Fusion in Complex Environment
abstract: In order to further improve the efficiency of the maze robot searching the maze and the accuracy of state information, this paper proposes a state estimation algorithm for maze robot based on multi-sensor fusion, Firstly, the algorithm uses an adaptive weighted batch estimation algorithm to measure the distance of the infrared sensors Fusion, get more accurate distance information. Secondly, the accurate distance information is combined with the sensory data of the gyroscope and the encoder, and the extended Kalman filter is used for fusion to obtain the position, angle, speed, angular velocity and other information of the maze robot. Finally, the experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively improve the positioning accuracy and robustness of the maze robot, and accurately feed back the state information of the maze robot. The problem of low positioning accuracy caused by the large error of the state information of the maze robot is solved.

articleTitle: Respiratory Rate Measurement Method Based on Singular Value Decomposition
abstract: In order to enhance the measurement accuracy of respiratory rate, a respiratory rate measurement method based on high-speed vision is presented in this paper. Initially, a high-speed camera is utilized to capture the experimenter's chest breathing movement video sequence, and singular value decomposition (SVD) is applied to extract the displacement resulting from respiratory movement. However, the extracted motion waveform contains some noise signals due to the poor denoising capabilities of SVD. To address this issue, an improved wavelet denoising approach is proposed in this paper to enhance the accuracy of respiratory measurement frequency. Finally, the respiratory frequency measurement method based on high-speed vision is simulated and experimented, and the respiratory rate is calculated through spectral analysis. The experiments indicate that the proposed method can accurately extract the respiratory displacement signal and effectively denoise it, making it convenient for practical use.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Integrated Energy Systems with User Comfort Consideration for Flexible Load Management
abstract: In recent years, in order to realize the goal of “double carbon”, the research and development of integrated energy system is very rapid, and the operation mode of the power grid is gradually changing from “source follows load” to “source-load interaction”. In order to strengthen the interaction between customer loads and grid loads, this paper proposes a flexible load optimization scheduling scheme that takes into account customer comfort. First, an integrated energy system model including photovoltaic, wind turbine, gas turbine, energy storage, etc. is established; second, an IES scheduling model with the optimization objective of cost minimization is established by considering the adjustable characteristics of demand-side flexible loads such as shiftable loads, transferable loads, and reducible loads, and considering the user comfort as an important constraint. The results of the study show that the program has obvious effectiveness in reducing the comprehensive operating cost by regulating the flexible load while satisfying the user comfort.

articleTitle: Kinematic Analysis and Trajectory Planning of Excavator Auxiliary Construction System
abstract: Based on the analysis of actual application scenarios and requirements, a model-based motion control algorithm and polynomial trajectory planning method are studied for the design of unmanned or assisted construction systems for engineering machinery. Excavators are selected as the research object. The kinematic model is established using a modified DH method based on the structural motion characteristics of excavators under general working conditions. The correctness of the model is verified using the Robotics toolbox. The trajectory of the determined end effector Cartesian space of the excavator is planned in joint space by using the five-order polynomial fitting method. To verify the reliability of the model, a calculation software is developed and a testing system is built for experiments in actual scenarios. The experimental results show that the excavator model can complete the calculation and planning within the expected accuracy range, achieving the expected effect, which lays a foundation for further exploration of excavator motion control and subsequent development of assisted construction systems.

articleTitle: TFENet: Topological Feature Extraction Network for 6D Object Pose Estimation
abstract: Grasping is an essential and challenging skill for robots to interact with their environment. Accurately obtaining the 6D pose information of the grasped object is the key to successful grasping. Due to the influence of illumination changes and object textures, the previous methods had problems with low utilization of depth information and inaccurate feature information. We study feature information extraction and fusion to address these issues and proposed a topological feature extraction network (TFENet). Firstly, we design TFE module to achieve global feature extraction from object point clouds, through which features can be identified to use depth information efficiently. Secondly, we design a MFF module to fuse color and geometric embedding better. Finally, experiments show that the proposed method outperforms existing methods with two datasets, LineMOD and YCB-Video.

articleTitle: Autonomous Exploration Motion Planning Method for Mobile Robot Based on Predicted Paths
abstract: Effective and safe autonomous exploration of mobile robots in complex unstructured environments is a challenging research problem. In this paper, we design a predictive motion decision mechanism based on frontier exploration, and then propose a novel motion planning method for autonomous exploration. The autonomous exploration process is decomposed into two stages: the exploration stage and the planning stage. The exploration stage expands the selection of optimal frontier points based on RRT, and the planning stage generates and tracks the optimal frontier points to obtain the most efficient and safe path. An exploration-motion decision mechanism is constructed to regulate the motion speed of the mobile robot and efficiently avoid the local minimum region. Experimental validation shows that the proposed method can safely and stably explore complex unknown scenes and obtain a complete environment grid map.

articleTitle: Policy Iteration Adaptive Dynamic Programming Based Control for Hypersonic Flight Vehicles
abstract: A novel approximate optimal tracking control scheme using policy iteration adaptive dynamic programming is proposed for hypersonic flight vehicles. By analysing the uniqueness of the equilibrium point during stable level flight of a hypersonic flight vehicle after achieving tracking objective, the output tracking problem is transformed into a state regulation problem. The initial admissible control law is obtained based on feedback linearization and sliding mode control under the discrete quadratic form cost function. Policy iteration adaptive dynamic programming algorithm is used to design the approximate optimal control law and the neural network approximation method is applied to approach the cost function. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Research on Modular Operation Optimization of Circulating Cooling Water System
abstract: This paper studies the optimization problem of modular operation of circulating cooling water system. Different from the operation optimization mechanism of the traditional circulating cooling water system, this paper proposes a method for modular operation optimization, the circulating cooling water system is divided into three operating units - heat exchange unit, circulation unit and cooling unit. First, in this paper, the system is divided into units, and the internal thermodynamic and kinetic models of each component unit are established. Secondly, use the method of integer programming to select the number of each component unit participating in the system operation. Finally, optimize the operation of the system according to the operation data collected on the project site. Experimental results show that this research can reduce costs for industrial enterprises and bring considerable profits.

articleTitle: A Calibration Method of DVL Based on Truncated Total Least Squares
abstract: In view of the fact that the traditional least squares calibration method of doppler velocity log (DVL) lacks the ability to deal with the ill-posed problem of the measurement equation and the random errors at both ends of the measurement equation, this paper extends the total least squares method and combines the truncated singular value decomposition method to propose a truncated total least squares DVL calibration method. The proposed method can obtain more stable and accurate calibration parameters by dealing with the errors at both ends of the measurement equation and suppressing the ill-posed problem of the measurement equation during the DVL calibration. Simulation outcomes indicate that the installation error angles for the x-axis and z-axis obtained through the truncated total least squares method introduced in this study are more aligned with the true values when contrasted with those derived from the conventional least squares approach. Through the actual sea trial, the applicability and superiority of this method are further proved.

articleTitle: Decentralized Tracking Control Scheme for Interconnected Nonlinear Systems with Input Saturation and Unknown Control Coefficient
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative decentralized adaptive tracking control strategy designed for interconnected systems by input saturation and unknown control coefficient. Broad learning system (BLS), a novel nonlinear approximation technique, is utilized for the identification of the unknown function. Leveraging the properties of Gaussian function, the auxiliary dynamic system is introduced to compensate for the input saturation effect. The Nussbaum-type function is introduced to counteract the difficulty produced by unknown control coefficient existed in the considered interconnected systems. On this basis, the decentralized control scheme is presented for the interconnected nonlinear systems utilizing both of adaptive control and dynamic surface control (DSC). To address the challenge of the “explosion of complexity”, a linear filter, accompanied by a compensation signal, is introduced. According to Lyapunov theory, all signals within the closed-loop systems remain bounded and the tracking errors exhibit convergence to the compact set near the origin. Ultimately, simulation studies are conducted to demonstrate the practicality of the approach.

articleTitle: Research on Distributed Temperature Monitoring System for Gasifier Based on Optical Fiber Sensors
abstract: Monitoring the wall temperature of gasifiers in the chemical industry can not only timely detect hot spots and avoid accidents, but also predict the thinning degree of refractory bricks and optimize maintenance cycles. In order to achieve distributed temperature measurement, this paper studies a distributed temperature monitoring system for gasifiers based on optical fiber sensors. The system includes four parts: on-site high-temperature resistant temperature sensors, network transmission system, temperature monitoring host, and temperature monitoring analysis software platform. The experimental results indicate that this system can achieve real-time measurement of the temperature in different areas of the gasifier wall.

articleTitle: Internet Data Collection Industry: Status and Perspectives
abstract: The Internet's role as an efficient platform for information dissemination has led to vast data accumulations, particularly due to increased social media usage. This surge in online data has promoted extensive research and innovations across various sectors. The development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has further enriched insights derived from this data, making Internet data collection a central focus for both academia and industry. Methods for data collection vary, with platforms like Twitter offering direct API access, while others require manual or automated techniques, such as data scraping. Despite technological advancements, programming challenges remain a hurdle for many analysts, boosting the Internet data collection industry's growth. Current research on this topic covers data acquisition techniques, the unique applications of Internet data in different domains, and the ethical implications of data collection. However, a comprehensive analysis of the global data collection landscape is still lacking. Our study delves into a comparative assessment of global and Chinese data collection practices, culminating in recommendations for data collection industry development in China.

articleTitle: SLAM Algorithm Based on Variational Bayesian Noise Adaptive Kalman
abstract: Traditional filtering methods can achieve accurate results when the observations follow the assumption of a Gaussian distribution. However, in real-world motion scenarios, the shaking of the mobile robot platform and environmental disturbances often lead to outliers in the observations, resulting in heavy-tailed noise that deviates from the Gaussian distribution. In such cases, the performance of traditional filtering Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithms is significantly compromised due to the violated assumption. To address the presence of outliers in observations that do not conform to the Gaussian distribution, this paper proposes an adaptive SLAM algorithm based on the Student's t-distribution. Compared to the Gaussian distribution, the Student's t-distribution has thicker tails and is less sensitive to outliers, making it a more appropriate choice for modeling observations. By modeling the observations using the Student's t-distribution and employing variational Bayesian methods, the algorithm estimates the posterior probability distribution of the joint distribution of the mobile robot's state and observation parameters. This adaptation enables tracking of changes in observations and improves the accuracy of the algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that when outliers are present in the observations, the VB-GCKF-SLAM algorithm achieves significantly higher localization accuracy compared to the Covariance Filtering SLAM algorithm (CFK-SLAM).

articleTitle: Design of GNSS/INS Integrated Navigation Spoofing Algorithm Under Road Environment Condition
abstract: Aiming at the spoofing demand of integrated navigation system for ground targets, this paper proposes a GNSS/INS integrated navigation spoofing algorithm under road environment condition. Firstly, the road network topology map of the target area is constructed, and the constraint conditions of path planning based on graph search are established. Then, the pruning strategy and the breadth-first search strategy are used to search for the spoofing start point and the spoofing target point that meet the constraint conditions. When the spoofing target reaches the spoofing start point, the spoofing target is spoofed. Next, the navigation and positioning result of the spoofing target is spoofed to the spoofing target point, so the navigation system of the spoofing target will regenerate a spoofing route, the spoofing target will be spoofed to the spoofing destination according to the navigation instructions of the spoofing route. Finally, the effectiveness and correctness of the algorithm are verified by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Performance-Guaranteed Adaptive Sliding Mode Control of UAV Via a Super-Twisting Algorithm
abstract: The paper studies the finite-time tracking control of perturbed quadrotor systems with prescribed performance requirement. A non-singular terminal sliding mode finite-time control scheme is proposed combining with performance-guaranteed technique and super-twisting algorithm. Firstly, to achieve fast convergence rate and avoid the singular problem, a new non-singular terminal sliding surface is proposed where a novel piecewise differentiable function is constructed in sliding mode surface. Furthermore, incorporating with this non-singular terminal sliding surface, performance constrained functions are constructed to ensure the dynamic prescribed performance of tracking errors. Secondly, adaptive compensators are designed to deal with the disturbance in quadrotor system. In addition, super-twisting algorithm are employed to further suppress the impact from the disturbance and the switching in sliding mode control, so as to maintain the relatively smooth transient performance of system. Finally, strict stability analysis is provided, and an simulation example has also given to illustrate the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: An Empathetic Dialogue Generation Model Based on External Knowledge Fusion
abstract: Aiming at the problem that traditional dialogue systems are difficult to capture the hidden emotional factors in dialogue history, this paper proposes an external knowledge-enhanced empathetic dialogue generation (KEDG) model based on external knowledge fusion. The model explicitly understands and expresses the corresponding emotion in the dialogue history, thus realizing the empathy ability of the model. First, a context map of emotional context is constructed by enriching the dialogue history by fusing with external knowledge. Then, the model is broken down into three main parts and described separately, including emotion context encoder, emotion prediction and emotion-dependent decoder. Based on the emotional features extracted from the dialogue model, user emotions can be modeled to generate empathic responses. Finally, extensive experimental results on benchmark datasets verify the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Underwater Acoustic Image Classification Based on Image Denoising and Transfer Learning
abstract: With the potential shown by artificial intelligence in recent years, deep learning has been widely used in the field of marine environment monitoring such as underwater image classification. It will be disturbed by the marine environment in the acquisition process of underwater acoustic images, which will lead to the acquisition of images containing a lot of noise information. In addition, it is very difficult to collect a large amount of underwater acoustic image data because it is expensive and time-consuming to do so. Both of these factors will reduce the accuracy of underwater acoustic image classification. In order to overcome the influence of the above factors, we proposed an underwater acoustic image classification method based on image denoising and transfer learning. Firstly, we use curvature filtering for image denoising to eliminate the noise contained in the image, which can effectively remove noise while maintaining the edge information of the image. Then we utilize the transfer learning technique to improve the accuracy of underwater acoustic image classification. The experimental results show that the curvature-filtered images have better image evaluation indexes than other methods. Moreover, the classification methods based on transfer learning has better classification accuracy than the ones without transfer learning.

articleTitle: Research on Trajectory Tracking Control of 4WID High Ground Sprayer Based on Adaptive Weight Coefficient MPC
abstract: Traditional Model Predictive Control (MPC) trajectory tracking control algorithm considering the road curvature information rarely, poor adaptability to the environment. In order to solve the track tracking accuracy of the sprayer in the complex field environment, an adaptive weight coefficient based MPC track tracking control strategy was proposed. The linear time-varying MPC controller was established based on the kinematic model and model predictive control theory of the high ground sprayer, and the front wheel Angle was solved. Finally, the fuzzy MPC controller is designed according to the actual field conditions. The simulation and experimental results indicate that compared with the traditional model prediction controller, the adaptive weight coefficient MPC has better trajectory tracking effect and smaller lateral error, which has certain practical significance.

articleTitle: Mixed Multi-Vehicle Cooperative-Driving Control Considering Communication Delays at Non-Signal-Controlled Intersections
abstract: To improve the safety performance and car-following performance of mixed traffic under the time-varying communication delay at non-signal-controlled intersections, the mixed multi-vehicle cooperative-driving control method is proposed. In the method, the mixed-platoon model-free adaptive prediction and cooperative-driving controller and mixed multi-vehicle formation scheme are studied, respectively. By adaptively adjusting the data mapping model parameters of the corresponding mixed platoons using only the real-time data during dynamic driving, the Edge Cloud Computing (ECC) controller is able to adaptively calculate the parametric cooperative control law equivalent to the desired states of the system according to the dynamic environmental changes, and then realize the effective cooperation and control of the mixed vehicle group by using Intelligent Connected Vehicles (ICVs) to guide the speed of the mixed platoons. Finally, a two-junction micro-traffic scenario is constructed to verify the effectiveness and feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Carbon Emission Reduction Strategy of the Construction Supply Chain Under the Cost-Sharing Contract
abstract: With the development of the low-carbon economy and environmental awareness, considerable academic attention has been devoted to reducing carbon emissions within the building supply chain. At the same time, consumer preference for low-carbon building products in the construction market is increasing, amplifying the potential benefits of these products. The highlight of this paper is that on the basis of the original research, introducing the potential benefits of the market, increasing the game strategy of bilateral cost-sharing contract, calculating the balance strategy under the two strategies through constructing a differential game model, and makes a comparative analysis. it is revealed that the bilateral cost-sharing contract strategy is more conducive to the coordination and cooperation of carbon emission reduction in the construction supply chain than the unilateral cost-sharing contract strategy and the optimal feedback balance strategy of the construction supply chain is also reached the optimal level through the introduction of bilateral cost-sharing contracts.

articleTitle: Research on DNS Resolution Technology based on Blockchain
abstract: DNS completes the resolution of domain names to IP addresses, which is an effective means to realize various In-ternet applications, and is also an indispensable part of Internet infrastructure, playing an important role. However, the resolution efficiency and security of DNS have always been a hot spot in the industry. This study deeply discusses the principle of Blockchain-based DNS resolution and conducts extensive re-search on Blockchain-based DNS resolution schemes. Based on compatibility with traditional DNS, these schemes are divided into two categories: compatible and incompatible. For different scenarios, we conduct a detailed analysis and comparison, focusing on the technical characteristics and performance of each so-lution. Finally, the future research direction is looked forward to, and the full text is summarized.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of FBG Based Sensor for Positioning Guan in Pulse Diagnosis
abstract: In Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), the radial artery on the medial side of the radial styloid process is called Guan, where the pulse wave is felt and analyzed for diagnosis. However, most of the current research on digitalization of TCM pulse diagnosis lacks discussion of the positioning of Guan, and the existing few positioning methods also have some problems. This paper proposes a sensor structure based on FBG, which can detect the fluctuation of radial styloid process and pulse force through two contact ends, so as to determine the position of Gao Gu and radial artery, and realize the purpose of positioning Guan. The finite element simulation analysis was carried out for the designed sensor. The simulation results show that the input pressure and the input displacement are respectively proportional to the change of FBG wavelength. The displacement sensitivity of the sensor is 574.86 pm/mm, the input displacement range is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\sim 3\text{mm}$</tex>, the pressure sensitivity is 1561.65 pm/N, and the input pressure range is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\sim 2.5\mathrm{N}$</tex>, which can meet the needs of detecting the radial styloid process and radial artery pulse.

articleTitle: Combining Enhancement and Fusion for Low-Light Visible and Infrared Image
abstract: Visible and infrared fusion aims to create a fused image that encompasses not only complex texture details and target-specific information but also facilitates advanced visual analyses. However, existing fusion algorithms rarely focus on the fusion of visible and infrared images in low-light environments. Therefore, in this article we propose a enhancement and fusion network for low-light visible and infrared that processes images in two stages. In the first stage, we correct the color shift of the visible light image caused by abnormal-light source and enhance the brightness of the image. In the second stage, we use the fusion network to fuse the enhancement results of the first stage with infrared, and use the loss function to constrain the network. Finally, we explore the performance of our fusion results for object detection tasks. Experimental results show that our fusion results have obvious brightness enhancement effect, high color contrast, obvious texture details and target information, and also achieve good performance in target detection tasks.

articleTitle: Constrained Robust Backstepping Steering Angle Control for A Novel Magnetic Screw-integrated Steer-by-Wire System
abstract: With the progression of automotive electrification and intelligence, Steer-by-Wire technology has emerged as a pivotal factor propelling the advancement of X-by-Wire chassis technology. Nonetheless, the intrinsic mechanical traits of the mechanical transmission within the Steer-by-Wire system-such as friction, wear, aging, and jamming—significantly undermine the system's dependability, efficiency, and control performance. To mitigate these detrimental effects, this paper introduces an innovative magnetic screw integrated Steer-by-Wire system. This novel approach employs a magnetic screw to achieve the conversion between rotary and linear motion in the steering-by-wire system, thereby sidestepping the adverse outcomes associated with conventional mechanical transmission mechanisms. Subsequently, a constraint robust backstepping control algorithm converging in finite time is formulated for managing the steering angle of the integrated Steer-by-Wire system featuring the magnetic screw. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is verified through simulations conducted in Simulink.

articleTitle: Optimization Study of Setting Reference Values based on Combined Cement Grinding System
abstract: In order to mitigate excessive fluctuations in control indicators and ensure stable performance of cement products, this paper proposes a research method for optimizing setting reference values in a cement combined grinding system. Based on an analysis of the cement combined grinding process, historical production data is utilized to establish a predictive model for process indicators using particle swarm optimization with extreme learning machine.
