Subsequently, an objective function is established, and in combination with the predictive correlation model, the differential evolution particle swarm algorithm is used to offline compute the set reference values for the rotational speed of the circulating fan and the rotational speed of the powder separator. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of this method in establishing setpoint values for process indicators in cement combined grinding, laying a foundation for stable control in practical production processes.

articleTitle: Efficient Fabric Defect Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5
abstract: In order to address the issues of real-time performance and the low dependency between feature channels in fabric defect detection networks, this paper proposes the ESE_YOLOv5 network based on YOLOv5. Firstly, to address the relative redundancy of the neck detection network feature channels, a relatively lightweight and efficient convolution module is adopted to ensure accuracy while reducing computation and parameter volume. Furthermore, the Efficient Squeeze-Excitation (ESE) module is introduced into the backbone to optimize the dependency of feature channels, which enhances the model's feature extraction capacity and improves detection accuracy. Experimental results show that compared to YOLOv5, the proposed ESE_YOLOv5 model reduces computation and parameter volume while improving accuracy, meeting the needs of fabric defect detection for recognizing fabric defects that have similar characteristics to the background while maintaining real-time performance.

articleTitle: An Improved Extended Kalman Filter for UAV Localization in UWB Navigation System
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach to estimate yaw angle of UAV operating in UWB navigation system. Absolute orientation algorithm which is commonly used to match images is used to align optical-flow-inertial coordinate to UWB navigation coordinate. An improved extended kalman filter fusing optical-flow data and initializing with absolute orientation estimation is designed. A simulation and experiment are conducted to verify the feasibility of the approach of yaw estimation along with accuracy of localization and reach a satisfied result.

articleTitle: Study on Pressure Control Method of Combustion Chamber of Single-Stage Solid Rocket Motor
abstract: This article focuses on analyzing and studying on the combustion chamber of a single-stage solid rocket engine based on thermodynamics. The goal is to address issues with pressure control in the engine. In this paper, a nonlinear model was developed to validate and analyze the dynamic characteristics during the combustion process. Secondly, the nonlinear system is researched and designed by using linearization theory. Based on the dynamic characteristics and performance requirements during the combustion process, linear tools are used to design the controller. The inner loop adopts a Pseudo Differential Feedback (PDF) controller, while the outer loop adopts a bipolar controller. Finally, simulation experiments were conducted to verify that the combustion chamber pressure was controllable and met the expected requirements. The designed control system meets the requirements of system performance indicators and has good robustness.

articleTitle: Completely Distributed Observer Design of LTI Systems with Disturbances
abstract: In this paper, the distributed state estimation problem of a linear time invariant system with external disturbance by using multiple measurements is studied, where each sensor of the measurement only has to measure a part of outputs. The investigations are carried out by designing a novel estimation algorithm under the jointly observable assumption of the measured outputs, where both the high-gain observer technique and the matrix coupling based adaptive consensus protocol are used. It is proved that the error between the state and the estimation can be made arbitrarily small by tuning the high-gain parameter in the high-gain observer and the adaptive parameter in the adaptive consensus protocol. Simulations are provided to support the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Investigation on Flexible Interconnected Device Based on Multi-Terminal SOP
abstract: The Application of flexible interconnection technology is an effective method to realize dynamic capacity expansion and rapid transmission of power restoration. Aiming to realize flexible close-loop operation of urban distribution network, the flexible interconnected device based on multi-terminal soft open point (SOP) is investigated in this paper. A four-terminal SOP topology scheme is designed, and the three-phase two-level voltage source converter (VSC) is adopted as the key equipment. One converter adopts DC voltage close loop control to stabilize DC voltage as master converter, the other three converters adopt power control as slave converters. A hierarchical control strategy based on different time scales is proposed in this paper. It is divided to local control layer, centralized control layer and dispatching layer of distribution network. A simulation model of four terminal SOP topology is built to analyze its normal operation performance. The simulation result verifies the feasibility of the flexible interconnected device proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Cooperative Transmission Line Inspection Between Inspection Vehicle and UAV
abstract: In order to improve the automation degree and efficiency of inspection, this paper puts forward the electric inspection mode of cooperative operation of vehicle and machine. The mathematical programming model of TSP-D is established. In this paper, ant colony algorithm is used to solve the above model. By analyzing the endurance capability of UAVs, the location of the return point was determined, and then go back to breakpoint and continue (GBC) method is adopted to plan the remaining operation path. Finally, experimental results show that the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: A Pruning Method for Echo State Network Based on Neuron Importance and Iterative Fine-Tuning
abstract: Edge intelligence provides intelligent services at the network edge and improves the performance of the applications. Deploying neural networks on edge devices can bring intelligence closer to users. As a new type of recurrent neural network, echo state network (ESN) is widely used in many fields. However, edge devices usually have very limited resources. In order to reduce the network size and the performance loss, so as to deploy ESN on resource-constrained edge devices, this paper proposes a pruning method for ESN based on neuron importance and iterative fine-tuning. First, a neuron pruning algorithm based on neuron importance is proposed. The importance of each neuron is evaluated by integrating the mutual information and the weight, and then the unimportant neurons are pruned. Second, an information compensation algorithm based on iterative fine-tuning is proposed. The reservoir weight of the high pruning rate network is fine-tuned with the reservoir weight of the low pruning rate network to compensate part of the performance loss. Finally, simulation results on theoretical and real datasets show that the proposed method has better performance compared with other pruning methods.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Airport Refueling Vehicle Based on Improved NSGA - II
abstract: In order to reduce overall costs and improve operational efficiency of airport refueling vehicle, an improved fast non-dominated multi-objective genetic algorithm is proposed. Firstly, more elite individuals are obtained by selecting elite parent individuals with different objective functions for mutation; secondly, the population quality is improved by deleting duplicate individuals of the offspring; finally, an adaptive crossover probability function based on the number of duplicate individuals is designed to improve merit-seeking ability. The effectiveness of the improved algorithm is verified by the actual operation data of an airport. Furthermore, after verified the effect of vehicle speed and load capacity, it is concluded that the scheme with a speed of 40 to 60 km/h and a load of 75% to 85% can reduce total cost without increasing vehicle waiting time at the airport.

articleTitle: Environmental Target Detection Technology for Autonomous Driving Based on Improved YOLO v7
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low accuracy of road environment detection in automatic driving technology, an automatic driving road environment target detection technology based on improved YOLO v7 algorithm is proposed. The road environment data set is constructed by image acquisition. The CBAM is added to the YOLO v7 backbone network to enhance feature extraction capability. The loss function is replaced by Focal-EIOU Loss to improve detection accuracy. The Deformable ConvNets v2 is added to the YOLO v7 backbone network to enhance the performance of the model by enhancing the modeling ability. After testing, the accuracy of the improved model reached 85.6%, which was 3.9 % higher than that of the original model. The results show that the improved model can detect a series of objects such as cars, pedestrians and various traffic lights in the road environment more accurately, which is of great significance to ensure the safety and practicability of automatic driving and has broad development prospects.

articleTitle: Research on Parameter Identification and Model Verification of Battery Energy Storage System
abstract: Battery energy storage technology can be used to stabilize the power fluctuation of power system, improve the transient response ability of power system and maintain the safe and stable operation of power system. As the core device of battery energy storage system, energy storage converter is the key to analyze the transient response characteristics of energy storage system. In this paper, simulation analysis is carried out based on typical examples, and the simulation results verify the correctness and effectiveness of the above methods. In this paper, a grid-connected simulation model suitable for battery energy storage system is established based on DIgSILENT/PowerFactory, and the model parameters of the energy storage system are identified by least square method, and a model verification method suitable for battery energy storage system is proposed. In this paper, simulation analysis is carried out based on typical examples, and the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the identification strategy and the accuracy of the energy storage converter model.

articleTitle: An IT2FNN with a Novel Hierarchical Learning Algorithm for Nonlinear System Modeling
abstract: Interval type-2 fuzzy neural networks (IT2FNNs) have been widely used for modeling in industrial processes, and the efficient parameter learning methods are crucial for obtaining accurate models. However, the problem of low computational efficiency and poor convergence performance still exists in existing learning methods. In this study, a novel hierarchical learning algorithm is proposed for constructing IT2FNN with better learning ability and generalization performance. Firstly, the improved recursive least square (RLS) method with an adaptive forgetting factor is designed to learn the consequent parameters. Next, the advanced stochastic gradient descent (SGD) method is adopted to learn the antecedent parameters. Finally, the proposed method is applied to real industrial processes and compared with various state-of-the-art IT2FNNs. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Human-Machine Co-Driving Evaluation System Based on the Integration of Subjectivity and Objectivity *
abstract: The integration of human-machine co-driving marks an inevitable stage in the progression of autonomous driving technology. Situations where a driver's intentions differ from those of the automated driving system can pose risks to both the vehicle and other road users. Hence, accurately measuring these disparities becomes a crucial challenge in promoting a smooth and safe human-machine co-driving experience. This research delves into quantifying conflicts that arise during human-machine co-driving by combining subjective and objective approaches. Using a simulation platform and devices to capture physiological signals during collaborative driving scenarios, the study explores effective methods for evaluating these inherent conflicts. In this paper, a new human-machine co-driving system based on visual feedback is introduced and validated through experiments in a simulated driving environment. By correlating subjective driver perceptions with empirical data, the reliability of the conflict quantification metric is ultimately confirmed.

articleTitle: Distributed Fusion Estimator for Multi-Rate Multi-Sensor Systems with Unknown Inputs, Time Delays and Fading Measurements
abstract: A distributed fusion estimator (FE) is proposed for multi-rate multi-sensor systems (MMSs) with unknown inputs (VIs), one-step time delays and fading measurements, in which the state update (SU) rate is a positive multiple of the measurement sampling (MS) rates of different sensors. The fading measurements are described by using independent random variables with known intervals and obeying the certain probability distributions. Firstly, the time-delayed MMS is transformed into a single-rate system at the MS points without delays. The local filter (LF) at the SU point is derived based on the filter with Kalman filtering form that does not depend on UI information. Then, the estimation error covariance matrix is derived on the basis of LFs, and the distributed optimal FE is proposed. Finally, simulation results of numerical examples validate the effectiveness of FE.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Object Detection for High-Speed Rail Infrastructure Defects
abstract: Ensuring the safety of high-speed rail infrastructure relies on effective defect detection. With the advancements in artificial intelligence, deep learning-based detection methods have been increasingly applied for daily inspections of high-speed rail infrastructure. However, detecting defects in high-speed rail infrastructure poses challenges due to limited samples, small targets, and difficulty in detection. To address these issues, this article proposes a few-shot object detection method based on a multi-scale attention mechanism, aiming to enhance the performance of defect detection in high-speed rail infrastructure. While most existing few-shot object detection methods employ two-stage models that require training on a large number of base class samples followed by fine-tuning on a small number of novel samples, we introduce gradient transmission separately for the gradient decoupled layer in Decoupled Faster R-CNN to better detect novel classes. Additionally, we incorporate the feature pyramid structure and Coordinate Attention into the original network architecture to enhance the detection of HSR infrastructure defects across different scales and improve the model's sensitivity to channel and location information. Experimental evaluations using UAV-captured image datasets, with normal class representing the base class and defects as the novel class, demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Undersampling Ensemble and Deep Learning - Based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Method for Geological Hazard Warning
abstract: Landslide is the most frequent geological hazard. Landslide susceptibility mapping (LSM) can be used to predict the possibility of landslide occurring at a certain location. In this paper, an undersampling ensemble and deep learning - based landslide susceptibility mapping method for geological hazard warning is proposed. The Zigui to Badong section of the Three Gorges Reservoir is taken as the study area. Firstly, the correlation analysis of fourteen landslide influencing factors is carried out and two unimportant factors are eliminated. Then, an EasyEnsemble - one dimensional convolutional neural network (EE-1DCNN) model is constructed with the remaining twelve factors as inputs. Finally, the proposed EE-1DCNN model is compared with two well-known methods on test data, and a landslide susceptibility map of the study area is obtained based on the EE-1DCNN model. As the experimental result shows, the proposed EE-1DCNN model achieves superior AUC, accuracy and recall of 0.909, 91.7% and 85.1%. The applicability of the proposed method is proved.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Adaptive Coordinated Tracking Control for Multi-Agent Systems with Prescribed Performance
abstract: This paper proposes a predefined-time tracking control method for multi-agent systems based on prescribed performance. First, a novel prescribed performance function is designed to effectively meet the performance requirements of the system. Second, a coordinated tracking control approach with predefined time convergence is proposed within a directed network topology, and a novel filter is designed to improve the quality and accuracy of data in the multi-agent system. Finally, simulation experiments are performed using a dual-joint robotic arm to verify the efficacy of the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Regulated Output Synchronization of Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems with Desired Convergence Rate via Scale-Free Protocol Design
abstract: This paper outlines scalable collaborative protocols for achieving regulated output synchronization in heterogeneous multi-agent systems (MAS) in presence of arbitrary desired convergence rates. The proposed protocol design is scale-free, i.e., only requires knowledge of the agents' models, without any networks information and the number of agents. With our protocols, only adjusting a single parameter allows output synchronization to be achieved at any convergence rates.

articleTitle: A Bipartite Graph Based Method for Traffic Continuous Data Imputation
abstract: Traffic information missing conditions are common in Intelligent Transportation System and would cause huge challenges for sequential traffic tasks, such as traffic speed prediction. Rare models are designed to tackle the long-range continuous data missing problems. Thus, in this paper, we propose a Bipartite Graph-based message passing Imputation Network (BGIN) to reconstruct traffic features data of nodes. In BGIN, the nodes are divided into two types: known nodes that contain traffic information and imputed nodes without data. First, a known information depth extraction module is given to achieve the messages passing among known nodes. Then, we construct a bipartite graph to represent the correlations between known and imputed nodes. Bipartite graph propagation module propagates the known information to imputed nodes. Finally, a imputation output module aggregates the messages to complete the imputation task. To evaluate the performance of our method, extensive experiments are conducted on a newly traffic imputation dataset called PeMS-impute. Experiment results demonstrate that BGIN achieves the best imputation effects than some graph based traffic prediction models and imputation models.

articleTitle: A Multi-scale Normalizing Flow Network for Surface Defects Detection
abstract: Surface defect detection has gained significant importance in driving intelligent manufacturing processes, improving product quality, and ensuring process stability. However, the scarcity of labeled data and the intrinsic uncertainty of anomalies continue to pose challenges in defect detection and localization. Although normalizing flow models have been developed to address these challenges, they are not suitable for industrial environments with high real-time requirements as they contain a large number of parameters that need to be trained and inferred. In order to improve the computational efficiency of normalizing flow models, we propose a new multi-scale normalizing flow network architecture for surface defect detection. The proposed multi-scale normalizing flow network can effectively reduce inference time while maintaining a certain level of detection accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through the real-world industrial dataset, and the application results demonstrated that the proposed method satisfies the requirement of real-time detection of surface defects in industrial environments.

articleTitle: Multimodal Behavior Analysis for Virtual Reality Learning Environment
abstract: Since 2020, the e-Iearning systems have been accepted by more and more people. However, it is important to acquire the learning state of all online learners in real time. A research framework for addressing situational understanding in teaching and learning environments is proposed, which integrated multimodal data to recognize learning states based on behavior analyses. As a case study, the research framework is applied for a virtual reality learning environment. The experimental results show the usage of this research to achieve situational understanding and aid decision-making for online teaching and learning.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Control Of Stewart Parallel Robots Based On High Gain Observers
abstract: Aiming at the Stewart parallel robot, a trajectory tracking sliding mode control method based on high-gain observer is proposed in this paper. A non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control method is adopted to realize trajectory tracking of the displacement of the driving rod of the parallel robot, which has fast finite-time convergence and stability. The introduction of a high gain observer can observe the speed information of the drive rod, and has a better inhibition effect on external interference and uncertainty. The inverse kinematics of the parallel robot is used to solve the displacement and velocity information of the driving rod, and the high gain observer is used to estimate the speed information of the driving rod. At the same time, in order to reduce the effect of buffeting on the stability of the system, a new sliding mode reaching law is adopted. With the input of the reference trajectory of the parallel robot, it can quickly track the length of the six driving rods in 0.3 seconds and the speed of the six driving rods in 0.8 seconds. It can observe the length and speed of the six driving rods with high accuracy, the buffeting amplitude of the driving force is obviously reduced, and the pose of the parallel robot can be tracked well. Therefore, the Stewart parallel robot controller has the characteristics of good trajectory tracking performance, faster convergence speed, reduced buffeting phenomenon, and strong robustness to external disturbance. The trajectory tracking of the drive rod is realized by the designed controller, simulation results verify the effectiveness of designed controllers.

articleTitle: Global optimization of ORC process parameters based on SSL artificial neural network
abstract: The Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) is a commendable technology for waste heat recovery. However, the optimization problem of ORC operating parameters based on its mechanism model is not easy to be solved for obtaining the global optimal solution, and it is time-consuming. To deal with this problem, a global optimization method of ORC process parameters is proposed to maximize the net output power of the system. Utilizing the SSL Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is utilized as a surrogate model in the optimization, based on this, the parametric optimization problem can be converted into a Mixed-Integer Linear Optimization Problem (MILP). The optimization results show that, compared with the process parameter optimization method based on the ORC mechanism model, the solution time of the optimization is greatly reduced, and the obtained solution is globally optimal.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment Analysis Under Mixed Traffic Flow Scenario
abstract: Mixed traffic flow has gradually become a developing trend, in this trend, safety is the cornerstone of autonomous and manual driving vehicles. How to reduce the driving-related collision and improve people's feeling of road traffic safety is an urgent problem to be solved. In order to accurately identify and predict high risks and reduce security dangerous, we propose scenario-driven machine learning algorithms. Firstly, the Krauss model and the Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) are selected as the manual and autonomous driving models, four types of highway mixed traffic scenarios are reconstructed based on SUMO. Secondly, based on the collected simulation data, two type of risk identification algorithms are applied by using the logistic model and BP neural network model. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that compared with the Logistic model, the BP neural network model has higher recognition accuracy and is more suitable for high-risk recognition and prediction.

articleTitle: Simulation and Modeling for Mixed Traffic Flow on Urban Roads
abstract: In order to achieve effective, secure, and sustainable urban growth, smart cities are described as the smart and digital transformation of urban infrastructure, services to the public, and social governance. The use of intelligent driving technologies is essential to the mobility of smart cities. The intelligent transformation of infrastructure, public services, and social governance is necessary for the development of a smart city. The development of intelligent driving technology can provide technical support for the transportation sector of smart cities, while the implementation of information technology and the Internet of Things in smart cities can provide additional data and application scenarios for intelligent driving technology. As a result, intelligent driving and smart cities are related and complementary.

articleTitle: A Less Conservative Stability Criterion on Amplidyne Electrical Systems via a Generalized Quadratic Function Negative-Definiteness Approach
abstract: When it comes to amplidyne electrical systems (AESs), signals are transmitted through the network transmission channels, inevitably generating time-varying delay. When assessing the stability of such AESs with respect to the Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional, the quadratic polynomial function is always generated that takes into account the time-varying delay. This paper presents an approach for segmenting delay intervals by proposing a method for tangent intersection. The method utilizes the cross point between every two tangent lines to produce negative-definiteness conditions for the generalized quadratic function. This reduces the conservatism of existing conditions without the need for unexplained adjustable parameters or additional decision variables. Additionally, a less conservative approach is used to derive the stability criterion for AESs with time-varying delay. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stitching Transformer and Convolution in U-Net for Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Medical image segmentation is a crucial aspect of medical image analysis. While U-Net is one of the most widely used models for medical image segmentation, its intrinsic locality of convolution often fails to learn global context and long-range spatial relations. Recent research has attempted to introduce Transformer into U-Net to address this issue. However, the Transformer requires large-scale pre-training and does not work well on small datasets. Additionally, medical images tend to have low contrast and fuzzy boundaries, which are sensitive to both global and local information. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel network by stitching transformer and convolution in U-Net, which follows the multiscale symmetry structure of U-Net to make full use of the respective advantages. Specifically, we propose a CTC block by adding a self-attention layer between two serial convolution layers. The first convolution layer integrates position information, the self-attention layer extracts long-distance dependencies, and the second convolution layer explores inductive bias and aggregates global information. Moreover, we construct a cross-attention module in the skip connection procedure to further strengthen the recovery of feature information in the decoder. We evaluate the proposed model on two public datasets, and the experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code for our model will be available on Github.

articleTitle: Simulation System of Cement Decomposition Furnace Based on Digital Twin
abstract: This paper presents a system for simulating the temperature field of a cement decomposition furnace based on digital twin technology. The system achieves accurate simulation and prediction of the internal temperature field of a cement decomposer by combining the physical processes of the actual cement decomposer with a mathematical model. Through the digital twin technology, the system is able to update and adjust the temperature field in real time based on real-time sensor data, thus providing accurate temperature field predictions.

articleTitle: Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Transformer and CNN
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are attention-based encoder-decoder architectures widely used in computer vision (CV) and have shown excellent performance. However, ViTs are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. In actuality, the adversarial samples produced by various models exhibit some degree of overfitting. The primary challenge with anti-sample crossmodel transfer is based on this. In this research, a novel approach to enhance the transferability of adversarial samples between various ViTs and between ViTs and CNNs is proposed. The main steps of this method include: dividing the original image (224*224) into patches (16*16), extracting high-frequency information and calculating interaction values, and then applying momentum attacks to reduce the interaction between patches. (The negative correlation between game interaction among adversarial perturbation units and adversarial transferability has been verified in the work of Xin Wang et al. [1].) According to experimental findings, the suggested technique may significantly enhance the transferability of ViTs and between ViTs and CNNs.

articleTitle: Design of Model-Free Industrial Robot Automatic Programming System for Complex Components
abstract: In the field of construction lifting machinery, etc., there are a large number of welding manufacturing requirements for small amount, flexible components that lack computer geometric models, for which model-based offline automatic programming systems are unsuitable. In response to this situation, a model-free robot automatic programming system for large complex components is designed. In this system, 3D reconstruction of machining components is carried out quickly, and the machining scheme is planned according to the reconstruction results, and the robot program is generated automatically. The results show that the system can analyze the complex components without models online, and complete the corresponding welding tasks effectively without the assistance of the working fixture, which provides a technical basis for the further automation of robot machining.

articleTitle: The long and short-term memory neural network based on attention mechanism for soft measurement of free calcium oxide in cement clinker
abstract: On industrial sites where cement is produced, an important basis for operators to assess the quality of cement clinker is the free calcium oxide (f-CaO) content of the clinker. This indicator is of great importance for reducing energy consumption and improving product quality at the production site. Currently, the f-CaO content of clinker is still mainly obtained by laboratory testing. This off-line testing usually takes half an hour to one hour, which is time-consuming and has a significant lag. In this paper, a modeling method for soft measurement of clinker f-CaO content based on LSTM (Long and Short Term Memory) model with attention mechanism is proposed to achieve online detection of cement clinker f-CaO. The method uses the LSTM model combined with the attention mechanism to monitor and predict the f-CaO content of clinker in real time without the need for time-consuming offline sampling and analysis. It is an important guide for timely production information at production sites.

articleTitle: PEAP-Net: Edge-Wise Attention Pooling for Point Cloud Classification and Segmentation
abstract: The irregularity and disorderliness of the point cloud data pose significant challenges for feature learning. Currently, most point cloud processing methods use symmetric pooling functions to aggregate local features. However, this approach may result in local point clouds being less sensitive to global features. In this paper, we develop an aggregated pooling module to construct a new network called PEAP-Net for point cloud classification and segmentation. The network primarily consists of two key modules: the Edge-wise Attention Pooling (EAP) block based on attention mechanisms and the Local Feature Aggregating (LFA) block based on graph convolutions. The EAP module incorporates the Edge-wise Attention structure, enabling efficient encoding of structural features for each input. To facilitate the integration of global features, we adopt a spatial attention strategy to fuse the input information. Additionally, we introduce a residual module to alleviate issues of information similarity and redundancy. The LFA module combines graph convolutions to group points and aggregate local features in the point cloud. We thoroughly evaluate the performance of the PEAP-Net model on two benchmark datasets: the ModelNet40 classification dataset and the ShapeNet segmentation dataset. Through numerous experiments, we demonstrate that our approach achieves significant improvements in both of these tasks.

articleTitle: Deep Graph Matching Based on Neighbor Matching
abstract: The purpose of graph matching is to find the correspondence between nodes of two graphs. Existing graph matching models only consider the similarity between nodes when performing cross-graph convolutions, ignoring the consistency of the structure. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a new graph matching model that incorporates neighbor matching into the cross-graph convolution module. Neighbor matching calculates the attention weights for cross-graph convolution based on the local topology of nodes and neighbor dissimilarity. Because different neighbors have differing importance to the central node, neighbor matching first assigns aggregate weights for different neighboring nodes based on feature correlations. The cross-graph neighbor matching model then captures the distinctions among neighbors. Finally, the attention weights of cross-graph convolutions are jointly determined by the similarity between nodes and the consistency of their neighbors. This paper conducts comparative experiments on two public datasets. The experimental results show that on the Pascal Visual Object Classes(Pascal VOC) dataset, compared with the baseline model, the matching accuracy of the proposed model on 20 categories is increased by 0.9% on average; on the Spair-71k dataset, the average accuracy is increased by 1%.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of Discrete-Time Linear Systems Based on the Equivalent-Input-Disturbance Approach
abstract: This work introduces a novel model predictive control (MPC) technique for discrete-time linear systems. In order to actively mitigate the negative effects of external disturbance on the system output and enhance the system's disturbance rejection performance, we utilize an active disturbance rejection method in this article termed EID. First, a model predictive control law, which contains disturbance information and performance metrics, is designed based on the EID method. Then, by introducing a Lyapunov function, the problem of solving the performance index's ideal value is transformed into a semi-positive definite problem consisting of an objective function and a linear matrix inequality. By solving this optimization problem, a model predictive control algorithm can be obtained. Through simulations of a numerical example, the proposed method's validity is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Pneumatic pressure stability control of ring pendulum polishing machine based on double closed loop active disturbance rejection algorithm
abstract: A double closed loop active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) method was proposed to control the pressure of pneumatic pressure servo system of loop swing polishing machine, which is difficult to control the pressure accurately due to the strong nonlinearity, model uncertainty and disturbance. Based on the dynamic mechanism model of pneumatic pressure servo system of ring pendulum polishing machine, the parameters of the known model structure are identified by Matlab system identification tool. In the case of unknown disturbance and load disturbance, the extended state observer is designed to estimate the uncertainty and disturbance of the system, and the error feedback law is used to give real-time active compensation, so as to achieve accurate pneumatic pressure control. The simulation and experimental results show that the pneumatic pressure servo system not only has good tracking performance, fast response speed, strong anti-jamming ability, but also is easy to implement in engineering.

articleTitle: FedGLCD: A Federated Learning Intrusion Detection Algorithm with Combined Distillation
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing awareness of privacy protection, federated learning has received wide attention as a distributed machine learning method and has been applied in the field of intrusion detection. However, traditional federated learning algorithms perform poorly in such data scenarios due to the non-independent and identically distributed nature of network traffic data from loT devices. To solve this problem, we propose a novel federated learning algorithm called FedGLCD. The algorithm coordinates the local drift and global drift by combining global distillation and local self-distillation to significantly improve model performance. Specifically, FedGLCD dynamically incorporates local historical and global knowledge into the labels to guide model updates in the form of softened labels. We have conducted extensive experiments on the N-BaIoT dataset, and the results show that FedGLCD can achieve better performance in intrusion detection tasks.

articleTitle: A Process Monitoring Model Based on Data Whitening and Dynamic Radius Support Vector Data Description Method
abstract: Due to the large number of equipment and complex technical processes involved in industrial production, various faults are inevitable during the production process, which may affect the quality of the final product. This paper proposes a method that uses data whitening technology to process data, which can efficiently reduce the dimension of the original data and an eliminate redundant information. And then establish a dynamic radius model based on support vector data description (SVDD) method, which retains useful features and achieves accurate monitoring result of industrial process faults. We name the method as S-DRSVDD. To evaluate the new model, comparisons have made between it and other advanced models in a typical industrial fault dataset, Tennessee Eastman Process. The new model shows superiority from the perspectives.

articleTitle: Novel Stability Results of Generalized Neural Networks Subject to Mixed Delays via Quadratic Polynomial Inequality
abstract: This dissertation considers the stability issue for generalized neural networks (GNNs) subject to mixed delays. Firstly, an appropriate Lyapunov-Krasovskii functionals (LKF) is constructed by containing two new delay-product-type (DPT) terms, augmented terms and double integral terms. Then, to cooperate with the established LKF effectively, an improved finite-interval quadratic polynomial inequality is utilized to handle the quadratic function negative-determination. As a consequence, a new less conservative stability condition is achieved. Finally, some well-studied simulation examples are included to show the superiority of the presented conditions.

articleTitle: Research on Time-Sensitive Network Scheduling Based on Substation Service Flow
abstract: With the development of new power systems, the problem of large delay and large jitter in the transmission of time-sensitive data streams in power systems has put forward higher network performance requirements. This paper proposes a time-sensitive network scheduling method for substation traffic transmission problem for substation service flow. The method starts from two aspects, path and scheduling, path this paper uses genetics algorithm to optimize on the basis of K shortest path, and scheduling this paper combines the content of bandwidth reservation technology in the TSN standard protocol to schedule the substation traffic and solves it by SMT modelling using Z3 solver. The experimental results compare the scheduling method proposed in this paper with the heuristic list scheduling algorithm (HLS) and greedy adaptive search algorithm (GRASP), in which the end-to-end delay of the traffic is reduced by about 15% and the packet loss rate is reduced by about 17%.

articleTitle: Heuristic-Based Task Assignment and Multi-Agent Path Planning for Automatic Warehouses
abstract: In recent years, the problem of task assignment and path planning for multiple agents in automated warehouses, known as Task Assignment and Muti-agent Path Finding (TAPF) problem, has gained increasing attention. The TAPF problem aims to find task assignments and conflict-free path plans for agents while optimizing the objective function. However, existing algorithms are not well-suited to solve the TAPF problem in large-scale and densely populated environments while ensuring optimality. In this paper, we propose the Add Heuristics to Conflict-Based Search with Task Assignment (CBSH-TA) algorithm as an extension of the CBS-TA algorithm. Our algorithm introduces several key enhancements: 1) classifying conflict types and prioritizing conflicts, 2) incorporating heuristics into task assignment to expedite the search for optimal assignments, and 3) integrating CG, DG, and WDG heuristics into the high-level search process. We compare the proposed algorithm with the CBS-TA algorithm on maps of different sizes and densities. Experimental results demonstrate that CBSH - TA significantly reduces the number of expanded nodes, decreases runtime, and requires less memory, making it suitable for large-scale and densely populated environments.

articleTitle: Glass Detection Network Based on RGB-Infrared Image Fusion
abstract: Humans can easily distinguish glass in indoor and outdoor scenes. However, when robots work indoors or outdoors, they struggle to perceive the presence of glass, relying on sensors accurately. They may mistakenly interpret objects reflected by the glass as obstacles and even fail to detect the presence of glass, leading to collisions and potential hazards. Accurately identifying transparent objects like glass in the environment has become a challenging problem in robot environment perception tasks. This paper first introduces the characteristics of previous glass recognition methods. A lightweight RGB-Infrared fusion glass detection network IRGNet was designed based on low power consumption requirements and high real-time performance for mobile robots. The network includes an information fusion module (IFM) integrating complementary feature information from RGB and infrared images at multiple scales. We conducted experiments on Trans10k and the self-made dataset IRG dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that this network outperforms previous detection speed and accuracy methods.

articleTitle: Fuel-Saving Oriented Model Predictive Control of Truck Platoons
abstract: Fuel consumption problem of truck platoons is considered in this paper, in which a distributed model predictive controller (DMPC) based on lateral and longitudinal coupling dynamics is designed. A two-layer control structure is adopted,in which the upper layer is based on the fuel consumption model and combines the road information to plan the speed of the leading truck. Simultaneously, the tracking ability of the following trucks is considered, the optimal fuel-saving velocity of the platoon is obtained and transmitted to the lower truck control layer. A coupling controller is designed based on the five-degree-of-freedom model in the platoon control layer, co-simulation experiments are provided on joint simulation platform of Trucksim/Simulink, which the simulation results show that the fuel consumption of the platoon based on speed planning is less than that of the platoon based on constant speed cruise. While meeting the safety control of the platoon, fuel consumption has been reduced.

articleTitle: Learning Representations for Continual Learning Based on Information Bottleneck and Metric Loss
abstract: Continual learning, also known as lifelong learning, addresses the fundamental challenge of enabling machine learning models to learn from a continuous stream of data and adapt their knowledge to changing environments, without forgetting previously acquired information. This paradigm emulates the human ability to accumulate knowledge and skills over time, allowing models to build upon their past experiences to enhance their performance in new tasks. To this end, continual learning algorithms need to learn robust and stable representations that can generalize to new data. In this paper, we present an algorithm which can learn more concise and semantic representations that are beneficial for continual learning based on information bottleneck and metric learning. Combined with Core Set which leave a small part of data from previous tasks, our algorithm attains high performance on benchmark datasets: MNIST in solving continual incremental tasks.

articleTitle: Discrete Event-Triggered Control of T-S Fuzzy Network Control System with Time-Varying Delays
abstract: This article investigates the dynamic event-triggered fuzzy control of nonlinear networked control systems. For the problem of transmission delays, the following improvements are made: Firstly, considering the network state of transmission delays, a more general event-triggered scheme (ETS) is proposed. Secondly, the Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy time-varying delays network system is established. Thirdly, the sufficient and unnecessary conditions for the existence of the expected fuzzy controller are derived, and the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system is demonstrated while ensuring the communication efficiency on the sensor controller side. Finally, an example is used to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: SBD-YOLOv5: An Enhanced YOLOv5-Based Method for Transmission Line Fitting Defect Detection
abstract: One key method to ensure the proper functioning of the power transmission system is the detection of defects in transmission line hardware. The utilization of deep learning technology to analyze hardware defects in transmission line photos captured by drones has emerged as a significant technique in power system inspections. However, current techniques still exhibit limitations in terms of recognition accuracy. To address this issue, this paper presents a YOLOv5-based algorithm for detecting defects in transmission line hardware, named SBD-YOLOv5, derived from the initials of its three improvement methods. Firstly, to address the deficiency in recognizing small targets, a feature extraction module based on Swin Transformer is incorporated into the backbone network, enhancing the model's capability for feature extraction. Secondly, BiFPN is introduced to further enhance feature fusion. Lastly, DRConv is employed to emphasize key features in different semantic regions. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms the original model with a 4.1% improvement in mAP@0.5:0.95. GradCam heatmaps visually confirm that the improved model places higher significance on the detected targets, underscoring their significance within the enhanced model.

articleTitle: Detection of Lump Coal based on Lightweight Network and Attention Mechanism
abstract: Safe operation of the conveyor belt is a necessary condition for the safe and efficient transport of coal production. In the process of transferring large pieces of coal, Due to the fast operation of conveyor belts in underground coal mines and the height difference at the interface, the impact force of large pieces of coal is large, which will cause damage to the conveyor belt. Aiming at the above problems, proposed a novel approach for real-time surveillance of the conveyor belt operation in large coal management. This method leverages the YOLOv5 algorithm to achieve efficient monitoring, which firstly preprocesses the data through adaptive histogram equalization, and secondly, introduces a lightweight neural network to reduce the volume and complexity of the model. Finally, the fusion of the attention mechanism improves the detection performance of the model, so as to realize the real-time monitoring of bulk coal. The experimental results show that the number of model parameters and floating-point operations of the improved algorithm are reduced by 62.8% and 86.4%, respectively, and the detection speed reaches 96.77fps, which has an obvious lightweight advantage, while the detection precision is 60.48%. Therefore, the real-time monitoring method of mining conveyor belt based on lightweight neural network and attention mechanism can better cope with the dim and complex environment of underground coal mine.

articleTitle: Distributed Spectrum Resource Allocation via Stochastic Learning in Potential Games
abstract: Aiming for closer-to-optimal solutions to the distributed opportunistic heterogeneous spectrum access (OHSA) problem, we study from the perspective of game theory and propose a memory and regret based learning algorithm (MRLA). Firstly, aiming for the optimization of the total throughput in a cognitive radio network, we build a weighted congestion game (WCG) by considering each cognitive user as a game player and introducing a differentiating coefficient. Afterward, we propose the MRLA in which each player makes choices from the action set based on its identity and memory. Thirdly, we prove that the MRLA converges to a Nash equilibrium solution in a distributed manner within a finite number of coordination steps. Finally, comparative simulations validate MRLA's advantages in terms of solution accuracy and convergence speed.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Based on Multi-Objective Optimization in Multiple Scenarios
abstract: In order to solve the problem of accuracy and stability of path tracking for autonomous vehicles in multiple scenarios, we propose a model predictive control (MPC) method based on multi-objective optimization. Firstly, we establish the single-vehicle kinematics model. Secondly, we use optimization theory to construct a multi-objective optimization MPC algorithm considering three factors: trajectory tracking accuracy, ride comfort and autonomous driving safety, which can perform rolling optimization of multiple objectives under multiple constraints. Then, we propose a behavior tree strategy in multiple autonomous driving application scenarios. When the behavior tree is executed, it starts from the root node and reaches the leaf node to execute the behavior. Finally, we deploy the Apollo simulation platform to verify the feasibility of the algorithm, and our proposed method improves the lateral control performance by 34% compared with the traditional LQR method. The simulation results show that the behavior tree realizes the autonomous driving task in Apollo multi-scenarios, and the multi-objective optimization MPC algorithm has great control accuracy.

articleTitle: Hybrid Metric-Induced Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
abstract: NMF is a promising feature representation method for data analysis. Matrix decomposition losses can be described using different metrics, based on which different NMF algorithms can be developed. However, a small Euclidean distance metric is not guaranteed to have a small cosine similarity metric, and vice versa. To overcome the shortcomings of these metrics, we integrate these two metrics to present a novel hybrid metric-induced NMF (HMNMF) model. The update rules for the HMNMF algorithm are obtained using the gradient descent method to resolve the optimization problem. The proposed algorithm is proven to be convergent, which implies that it is reasonable and stable. The proposed HMNMF approach is compared with different metric-induced NMF algorithms for face recognition, the experimental results confirm the effectiveness and good performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Fast Template Matching Method with Heuristic Initialization Oriented to Railway Patrol Robot
abstract: This paper proposes a fast target template matching method based on best buddies similarity to realize the integration of railway patrol robot and video surveillance system for railway safety assurance. Railway patrol robots are a viable way to address the challenges of blind spots in the field of vision and dependence on manual line inspection in video surveillance systems. The video surveillance system covers the whole line and can quickly identify the target. This supplements the limited vision of the robot. The multifunctional sensors carried by the patrol robot provide flexible on-site disposal methods for the monitoring system. In this process, the key issue is how to hand over the target quickly and accurately between the two systems. Existing methods are not suitable for our scenario because cross-device and cross-viewpoint targets have serious non-rigid deformation due to factors such as perspective, illumination, and occlusion. We propose a fast target template matching method based on best buddies similarity, which utilizes edgebox to screen out texture-rich regions in overlapping fields, and introduces region inevitability-guided particle swarm optimization to search for targets, thereby achieving the acceleration. The method utilizes color-feature-based best buddies similarity as the fitness function and can handle non-rigid deformations scenarios. We verify the performance of our method by carrying out comparative experiments and simulation experiments on real railway scenes. Our method achieves fast and robust target handover while maintaining the accuracy of the original BBS algorithm and improving its robustness. Our method has advantages such as reducing human labor, improving efficiency, and enhancing railway safety.

articleTitle: Cooperative Spacecraft Formation Flying Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This article introduces an approach for spacecraft formation flying on elliptic orbit, combining multi-agent system theory with reinforcement learning algorithms. The contributions include a game-based strategy for local neighbor-to-neighbor information interaction and a novel reinforcement learning algorithm for optimal spacecraft formation control. The proposed multi-agent dual heuristic programming (MADHP) algorithm ensures stability by considering local interactions and is successfully applied to achieve spacecraft formation flying on elliptic orbit. Numerical simulations confirm the effectiveness of the approach. This study demonstrates potential applications of reinforcement learning in autonomous space missions and cooperative multi-agent systems.

articleTitle: A Two-Degree-of-Freedom FIMC-GESO Control Method for DC Speed Servo System
abstract: The tracking performance and the anti-disturbance performance cannot be balanced in a DC speed control system. The issue is resolved by a two-degree-of-freedom fractional-order internal mode controller (FIMC) with a generalized expanded state observer (GESO). Secondly, The system's tracking performance can be improved by adjusting only the filter parameters in the FIMC, while the system's ability to combat disturbance can be improved by adjusting the bandwidth in the GESO. This greatly reduces the complexity of the system parameter design. Finally, simulation and experiment are used to confirm the effectiveness and viability of the FIMC-GESO control in the DC servo system in terms of speed tracking performance and anti-disturbance performance.

Author Keywords: fractional order internal mode PID control

articleTitle: Intelligent Creation Cloud Platform Based on GPT Technology
abstract: With the rapid development of mobile internet, more and more information is inclined to be published on official Weibo, social media platforms, and other internet platforms. People are surrounded by a massive amount of text information in their daily and work lives. How to quickly and accurately obtain the content people need from massive text information has become a very urgent demand in today's society. Commonly, automatic text summarization technology used methods currently include extraction and generative summarization. This paper combines two methods to design an intelligent creative platform based on GPT technology. Based on the collected dataset, a GPT-2 pre training model was proposed to achieve automatic title generation according to the requirements, and it was optimized; This paper uses the Text Rank algorithm and extractive Snow Flake algorithm respectively to achieve the functions of abstract generation and saving the generated file ID. Finally, carry out practical operations on relevant functions.

articleTitle: Study on Dynamic Prevention and Control System of Urban Safety Risks
abstract: In the background of industrialization, accelerated urbanization, and normalization of COVID-19 pandemic, strengthening the construction of urban safety dynamic risk system will improve comprehensive and rapid perception of urban safe operation state, comprehensive risk assessment, accurately prediction and linkage efficient disposal of disasters, which continuously enhances capacity for prevention, control and response to urban major risks and emergencies. This paper analyzes the development status and existing problems of urban safety risk prevention and control, and puts forward the framework and path for systematic construction of urban safety risk dynamic prevention and control, which covers five aspects: building a comprehensive urban safety monitoring network integrating air, space and earth, accelerating the integration of business data in the field of urban safety, strengthening comprehensive monitoring and early warning in addition to risk assessment, unifying construction standards and data interfaces, and strengthening theoretical and technical research in key fields. With the aim of promoting urban safety risk prevention and control capacity with informatization in order to build a solid safety barrier for high-quality urban development, the study puts forward four countermeasures or suggestions, namely, improving the emergency command system and the safety prevention and control system, establishing a specialized monitoring and early warning system, building intelligent comprehensive monitoring and early warning capacity, and strengthening the ability to enhance security through science and technology.

articleTitle: MGFusion:A Large-Scale Realtime 3D Reconstruction Based on Movable Grid
abstract: In this letter, to solve the problems of large memory occupation, small reconstruction range and low efficiency of the existing realtime 3D reconstruction algorithms on truncated signed distance function, we improve it based on movable grid. Specifically, we put the point cloud obtained by the depth camera into the grids. Then, the space required to reconstruction is calculated from the coordinates of the grids. Grids will be reconstructed in the GPU. The space that was reconstructed and will not reconstructed recently will convert to the point cloud on condition that the GPU memory is insufficient. To rebuild the area again, we can convert the previous point cloud to a small voxel grid to initialize the memory in the GPU. In this letter, the large-scale 3D reconstruction is solved through the movable grid and the use of explicit memory rationally. For the tasks requiring high precision, the reconstruction can be carried out with a reasonable configuration. It significantly improves the range and efficiency of 3D reconstruction. Source code is available at https://gthub.com/sky3139/MGFusion.

articleTitle: Study on Load Prediction Based on the MPGA-BP Neural Network Model
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of power load prediction with randomness and complexity, a new power load prediction method is constructed by using multiple group genetic algorithms (MPGA). By improving the genetic algorithm, using the traditional genetic algorithm to optimize the weights and threshold of neurons in BP neural network, improve the prediction accuracy of BP neural network, thus greatly improve the prediction performance of BP neural network, but at the same time, because the traditional genetic algorithm is easy to precocious, into the local optimal, so the choice on this method for improvement. By comparing the prediction error of genetic algorithm (Geneticalgorithm, GA) - BP neural network model and MPGA-BP neural network model, it is found that the prediction results of MPGA-BP neural network model are better than GA-BP and BP neural network model, which proves that the proposed method can better improve the accuracy of load prediction. The results show that the prediction performance of multiple genetic GA is better than GABP and BP methods.

articleTitle: A Model-Free Detection Strategy for False Data Injection Attacks in Networked Control Systems
abstract: In this paper, a model-free detection strategy is proposed for stealthy false data injection (FDI) attacks targeted at setpoints of control systems. A redundant item is added to the transmitted data, and decoding is carried out at the receiver before a few detection rules are checked against. Furthermore, this model-free detection scheme is proved effective in detecting FDI attacks on setpoint signals while combined with watermarking method or the idea of random point. Finally, effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified through numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Smart Operation Optimization Methods for Hydrogen-Based Energy Systems Under Uncertainties
abstract: The operation optimization of hydrogen-based energy systems (HESs) contributes to the reduction of operational cost and carbon emission. In existing works, operation optimization methods either require prior information of uncertain parameters or do not consider the nonlinear characteristics of electrolyzers and fuel cells. To overcome the drawbacks in existing works, we investigate an expected operational cost minimization problem related to HESs with the consideration of nonlinear characteristics and propose an online operation algorithm to minimize the total operational cost of HESs based on proximal policy optimization and expert knowledge. Moreover, the proposed algorithm does not require any prior knowledge of uncertain parameters. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can reduce the total operational cost of HESs by 2.7%-20.5% and carbon emission by 15.6%-44.3% compared with the rule-based scheme.

articleTitle: A Probability-Dependent Optimal Kalman Predictor for Networked Systems Based on SCP
abstract: The optimal Kalman prediction algorithm relying on the communication probability is investigated for the networked linear discrete time-invariant system with stochastic communication protocol (SCP) and correlated noises. To mitigate data transmission conflicts and losses caused by the limited network bandwidth. Using SCP scheduling ensures that one measurement component is only sent from the sensor side to the predictor side in each communication. In situations where the predictor is unaware of the received measurement component but knows the communication probability of each component, an optimal recursive Kalman predictor relying on the transmission probability of each component is derived by applying the projection theory. Stability and steady-state properties are examined, and a condition sufficient to establish the presence of a steady-state predictor is yielded. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed algorithm is verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Residual Life Prediction Method of Lithium Battery Based on HHT-ARIMA-PF
abstract: The energy storage system is an important facility for energy conversion and storage in the energy Internet, and lithium batteries are widely used in the construction of current energy storage systems, which occasionally cause accidents and losses due to battery aging or failure. The remaining life prediction can provide a basis for the predictive maintenance of the battery and ensure the safe and stable operation of the energy system. Aiming at the problems of capacity degradation and noise information affecting the performance of the algorithm in the existing lithium battery remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, this paper proposes a lithium battery remaining useful life prediction method based on HHT-ARIMA-PF. Firstly, the feature factors are extracted from the charge-discharge curves of the battery to construct the battery capacity feature data set. The empirical mode decomposition is used to decompose the battery capacity feature data set into IMF components and trend items, and the Hilbert transform (HT) is used to determine the noisy components and the Bessel low-pass digital filter is used to process the noisy components. Then, all the internal modal function IMF and trend terms in the processed battery capacity signal were predicted using ARIMA and PF models, respectively, and the predicted values were obtained, respectively. Finally, the prediction results of the intrinsic mode function based on ARIMA and the prediction results of the trend term based on PF are summed up as the predicted value of the battery capacity, and the predicted value of the remaining lifetime RUL of the lithium battery is calculated. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper can realize the differentiation processing of a large amount of data with high prediction speed and prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on the Participation of Electric Vehicle Clusters in Grid Peak-Shifting Services Under the Aggregated Commercial Framework
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs), being a valuable resource capable of interacting with the power grid, are widely distributed across various regional power grids. Aggregating a large number of dispersed EVs to participate in auxiliary services of the power grid has emerged as a novel approach to promote the development of a modern power system. This study focuses on the aggregation management of EVs and peak load regulation of the auxiliary power grid. Based on the time scale, the EV clusters are categorized, and the aggregation management areas are defined. The Latin hypercube method is employed to simulate the random distribution of EV clusters. The dispatchable potential of EVs is evaluated through index analysis, and the dispatchable potential of EV clusters is assessed using fuzzy theory. A peak load regulation strategy for EV clusters under the aggregator model is proposed, and simulation and case analysis demonstrate that the proposed strategy enables EV clusters to effectively fulfill the peak load regulation tasks of the power system.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Control of Tunneling Machine Based on PSO-BP Neural Network PID
abstract: In order to improve the response speed and control accuracy of the tunneling machine control system, and to address the limitations of traditional algorithms that are prone to falling into local extremum and weak generalization ability during the solving process, a PSO-BP neural network PID adaptive control method for tunneling machines is proposed. The weights of the BP neural network are optimized by the global search ability of the PSO algorithm. The neural network outputs the fitness values of the PID parameters, and the initial weights of the neural network are updated. The PID parameters are adjusted in realtime. The results show that the unit Step response curve of the system reaches the stable state of the system after 0.85 s in the traditional PID control, while the PSO-BP neural network PID controller only needs 0.4 s to be stable, and the overshoot of the PSO-BP neural network PID controller is far less than that of the traditional PID controller. Therefore, the PSO BP neural network PID controller has good dynamic and static characteristics, which can maximize the generalization ability of the traditional BP neural network and ensure the Rate of convergence and learning ability.

articleTitle: A Method of Vehicle Peripheral Objects Detection Based on Binocular Vision
abstract: Aiming at the collision problem that may occur when the passenger opens the door after the vehicle stops, this paper proposes an obj ect detection algorithm around the vehicle based on binocular vision. Due to the high computational complexity of binocular registration, the stereo correction of the image is realized by combining the dual-target fixed parameters and Bouguet Reprojection Algorithm, so that the binocular image is corrected into coplanar line alignment, and the operational efficiency is improved. The You Only Look Once algorithm is used to realize the recognition of people and vehicles on the road. In order to reduce the probability of missing detection and wrong detection of the algorithm in the remote scene, the up-sampling fusion method of the feature pyramid is adopted to detect the target on three feature layers, so as to realize the real-time detection and tracking of the target. Then, Scale-invariant Feature Transform Algorithm is used to obtain the matching points in the target area, and the distance between the feature points in the image and the camera is measured through coordinate transformation. At last, the system is tested at National Supervision &Inspection Centre for Inside Vehicle. The accuracy of the proposed algorithm for measuring the distance of various types of targets is above 96%.

articleTitle: Achieving Spherical Longitude Circumnavigation of One Target in 3D
abstract: This paper investigates the localization and circumnavigation problem of an unknown target in 3D space. The agents use only bearing information of the target and the distance information is not available. To fit for the characteristics of three-dimensional space, the spherical longitude circumnavigation pattern is proposed, which is significant in military areas such as target attacking. As first step, an estimator is presented to locate the target using bearing measurements. Based on this, a control protocol combined with a normal vector coordinator are designed by longitude deviation to drive multiple agents to desired different planes. Theoretical proof and simulations indicate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Cluster Control Strategy of Thermostatically Controlled Loads Under Asynchronous Communication Mechanism
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed cluster control strategy for thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs) to enable precise tracking of the reference power by the aggregated TCL cluster. The proposed strategy takes into account temperature-based priority to ensure fair scheduling among TCLs. Besides, as priorities tend to equalize across all TCLs after multiple control periods, a sub-cluster splitting strategy is introduced to enhance power tracking accuracy. The proposed strategy operates in a distributed manner, significantly reducing the aggregator's resource consumption in communication and computation. Furthermore, it employs asynchronous communication, making it suitable for practical implementation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can realize the accurate tracking of TCLs cluster aggregated power to the reference power.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Image Rotation Target Detection Algorithm Based on Attention Mechanism
abstract: Although strides in target detection, challenges persist in remote sensing image target detection due to complex backgrounds, small targets, and interference from background and other target information within the horizontal bounding box. To enhance remote sensing image target detection, this study introduces a YOLOv7-based attention mechanism for rotation target detection. The network model's loss function is first enhanced to extract rotating target angle information, ensuring accurate detection of the rotation angle. Subsequently, the ELAN module undergoes optimization to augment the model's feature extraction capability in remote sensing images by integrating an improved attention mechanism module and structural re-parameterization concept. Experimental testing on a self-built dataset demonstrates an overall detection accuracy of 92.7% for the proposed method, surpassing other mainstream rotational target detection algorithms in mAP. Results affirm that the proposed approach effectively enhances the rotation detection performance of remote sensing images.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Suppression of Brushless DC Motor Under an Improved Segmented PWM
abstract: This paper mainly describes a segmented PWM control method to minimize commutation torque ripple to achieve smooth operation of the motor at high and low speeds. The reasons for commutation torque ripple generated by brushless DC motors in three-phase six-state and two-phase conduction mode were analyzed. and a commutation torque ripple suppression strategy under ON-PWM modulation is proposed. This strategy considers the influence of the change of back EMF on the torque ripple during the commutation process, and further improves the compensation effect of commutation torque ripple, so as to realize the low torque ripple operation of the motor at low speed and high speed. By establishing a system simulation model in Matlab/Simulink environment, it is confirmed that the new control strategy can effectively reduce the commutation torque ripple, and verify the effectiveness and theoretical correctness of the control method.

articleTitle: Parallel Operation Control Strategy of High-Frequency-Link Single-Phase Full Bridge Full Wave Inverter Based on Virtual Impedance
abstract: The high-frequency-link single-phase full bridge full wave inverter with bidirectional active clamp circuit can realize safe commutation, and the secondary side of the transformer has no voltage spike. However, the capacity of a single high-frequency inverter is limited, and it cannot run for a long time at high load, which is difficult to meet the requirements of high-power applications. In this paper, a droop control strategy based on virtual impedance is established to realize the parallel operation of two high-frequency-link single-phase full-bridge full-wave inverters, which effectively improves the system capacity, and optimizes the circuit topology by simplifying the clamp circuit, and realizes the elimination of voltage spikes. The employment of virtual impedance improves the performance of the parallel system, and effectively solves the problem that the reactive power of the parallel system of inverters with different capacities is excessive and difficult to balance. Finally, through matlab/simulink simulation, the effectiveness of the droop control based on virtual impedance in the parallel operation of high-frequency- link single-phase full-bridge full-wave inverter is verified.

articleTitle: Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Logic System Based on Batch Normalization and Uniform Regularization with Application to Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Time series data are ubiquitous in life, and it is necessary and meaningful to predict important time series data such as power loads. Firstly, a noval interval type-2 fuzzy logic system is proposed for time series forecasting task with strong randomness and volatility. Then, batch normalization and uniform regularization are used to optimize the proposed interval type-2 fuzzy logic system, which can further improve the generalization ability of the model and obtain better prediction accuracy. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is tested on two comparative experiments. The statistical results show that the proposed interval type-2 fuzzy logic system based on batch normalization and uniform regularization (IT2FLSBNUR) achieves the best forecasting effect compared with the comparative methods.

articleTitle: Distributed Unscented Kalman Filtering Method for Maneuvering Target State Estimation in Passive Sensor Network
abstract: The distributed unscented Kalman filtering (DUKF) method in passive sensor node pairs is proposed to addressing the challenge of tracking maneuvering target. The passive sensor node pairs measure model and the observation system model of passive sensor network are firstly constructed, then the UKF method of passive sensor node pair is proposed to estimate the maneuvering target states. Furthermore, applying the passive sensor node pair UKF method to passive sensor network and combining with the cooperative consistency theory, a distributed unscented Kalman filtering method is proposed to solve the issues of large precision errors and easy divergence during the state estimation procedure. Finally, four simulation experiments are set up for comparison, which verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the DUKF method.

articleTitle: Edge Point Detection in CIELAB Parameter Time Series Using Predictive Enhanced TEO Operator
abstract: In the process of automated titration in automation chemistry, in order to smoothen the curve near the titration endpoint, it is necessary to dynamically measure the curve's edge points in real-time. This is done to proactively adjust the flow rate of the liquid dispensed by the flow pump. To address this, a real-time time series edge point detection algorithm based on GWO-SVR-TEO is proposed. Initially, the GWO algorithm is employed to optimize the penalty factors C and interval ∊ of the SVR model. The optimized SVR model is then utilized for multi-step prediction of the detection points. Finally, the TEO operator is combined to identify the edge points. This study innovatively applies time series prediction to edge point detection, achieving real-time detection of edge points within time series data. A comparison is made between the GWO-SVR-TEO algorithm and the slope judgment method using CIELAB parameter time series. The results indicate that the GWO-SVR-TEO algorithm generates fewer interference points and offers more accurate determination of edge points compared to the slope judgment method.

articleTitle: Efficient Low-Resolution Human Pose Estimation with Knowledge Bridge
abstract: In the field of human pose estimation, the problem of knowledge transfer among models with different learning objectives and input resolutions remains unresolved.
