In this paper, we propose a novel framework specifically designed for low-resolution human pose estimation, aiming to obtain an efficient and powerful model for this task. Specifically, we introduce an intermediate model as a knowledge bridge between the teacher model and the student model. We perform knowledge transfer from the teacher model with different learning objectives and resolutions to the student model through cross-learning-objective pose distillation between the teacher model and the bridge model, as well as cross-resolution pose distillation between the bridge model and the student model. Experimental results on the COCO dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our model in low-resolution human pose estimation tasks.

articleTitle: Design of Shocks & Vibrations Monitoring System for Long Distance Transportation in Confined Spaces
abstract: In real life, many valuable products and highvalue important products are transported in long distances. Shocks and vibrations are caused during transportation, loading and unloading for various reasons. Any shock and vibration exceeding the regulations may cause damage to the transported products. So, it is necessary to monitor and analyze these data of shocks and vibrations scientifically, while considering that some transportation conditions have special requirements for installation space and transportation time. Therefore, an ultra-thin and long-lasting monitoring system has been developed based on MEMS accelerometer technology to measure shocks and vibrations. After series of independent tests and calibration tests conducted by a third party on the product, the results show that it can record and store the threeaxis acceleration, temperature, humidity, pressure, time and other parameters of the transportation process in real time, and complete the preliminary assessment of the transportation status of high-value products. Then engineers can conduct professional analysis of the data to obtain scientific transportation monitoring reports, and provide scientific basis for taking safety prevention and treatment measures for subsequent transportation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Iterative Reconstruction Rescue Detection Intelligent Robot Based on ROS Platform
abstract: At present, most rescue and detection robots are expensive, structurally complex, and have few functions. They only have modules such as tracking, obstacle avoidance, fire extinguishing, ultrasonic ranging, amphibious, and smoke detection. However, the use of these modules cannot perform deep detection in harsh environments and does not have predictive power. In order to make the intelligent robot carry out dynamic three-dimensional mapping of complex environment while rescuing, so as to better understand and analyze the environmental conditions and reduce the probability of dangerous events, a dynamic iterative reconstruction rescue detection intelligent robot based on ROS is designed. This design uses Nvidia's Jetson TX1 as the ROS master control, the ubuntu system as the carrier, and first uses the TOF ranging method and ROS of Lassen N10_ Cartographer carries out dynamic 2D reconstruction of the mine environment and scans the mine foundation, then uses Astra Pro to carry out dynamic iterative reconstruction of various environments with ORB-SLAM2 as the basic framework and scans the harsh environment obstacles to obtain the final environment, finally realizing the purpose of dynamic Iterative reconstruction of the environment by intelligent robots while rescuing.

articleTitle: Extended Dissipative Stabilization for Dwell-Time-Constrained Discrete-Time Switched Linear Systems via Hybrid-Triggered Intermittent Control
abstract: This paper studies the extended dissipative stabilization problem for discrete-time switched linear systems (DSLSs) via hybrid-triggered intermittent control. By using the hybrid-triggered intermittent control scheme and a non-increasing switching-path-dependent Lyapunov functions (SPDLFs) approach, sufficient conditions ensuring the stability and extended dissipative performance of the closed-loop DSLSs are obtained. The research results show that hybrid-triggered mechanism can save control resources while ensuring the extended dissipative performance of the system. All the controller gains can be gotten by solving a set of strict linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Finally, a numerical example is provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the results.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Turbine Speed Control System Based on Improved Tunicate Swarm Algorithm
abstract: The turbine speed control system has the features of variable operating conditions, time-varying parameters and complex nonlinearity. The use of PID controller makes the system has long adjustment time, a large overshoot and low adjustment accuracy. To calibrate the parameters of this system, a revised algorithm is proposed. Firstly, Tent chaotic initialization is introduced on the basis of the original algorithm to make the tunicates more evenly distributed in the solution space. Secondly, a golden sine partition factor is introduced to generate new individuals before the position is updated, which increase the diversity of optimization particles and reduce the incidence of local optimal solutions. Finally, the nonlinear adaptive weight factor is introduced to adjust the development ability and discovery ability to achieve equalization. By adding frequency disturbance and load disturbance to the turbine speed regulation system, its dynamic characteristics are observed. And the results show that the PID control based on the revised TSA makes system have better dynamic stability characteristics.

articleTitle: PEMFC System Modeling and Control of Oxygen Excess Ratio in Air Supply Systems
abstract: To enhance the net output power of the proton exchange membrane fuel cell, it is necessary to ensure that the cathode of the stack has an appropriate air flow supply. First, a state space model of the third-order PEMFC air supply system including air compressor speed, supply pipeline pressure and stack cathode total pressure was built. Then, CSA and ANFIS were introduced on the basis of PID control, and a method was proposed. CSA has improved the PID and ANFIS cascade control methods so that when the fuel cell load current changes, by adjusting the air compressor's output flow rate, the proton exchange membrane fuel cell can track and maintain the optimal oxygen ratio. The simulation results demonstrate that implementing CSA to enhance the PID and ANFIS cascade controllers leads to improvements., the average adjustment time is shortened by 51.49 % and 66.32 % respectively compared with the CSA improved PID controller and PID controller. The error integral criterion is used to verify that the cascade control has Excellent control effect.

articleTitle: Robust Stereo Matching Method Using the Improved ADCensus Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a new alternative algorithm for the centre pixel based on the Census transform, which effectively reduces the problem of over-reliance on the centre pixel in the traditional Census algorithm. In addition, this paper calculates the AD cost in the V-channel, and then the two are normalized to achieve fusion, and the resulting fusion cost is cost-aggregated through the crossover domain. The experiment proves that the improved algorithm has significantly reduced the false matching rate and is more robust to different lighting and noise conditions.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of Chaotic Systems Based on Least Squares Method and Pauta Criterion
abstract: In this study, an offline parameter identification approach based on the measured time series of chaotic system is proposed. In this approach, least squares method is firstly introduced to minimize the time series error and Pauta criterion is then employed to pick out the wrong extreme value point. Two representative cases are conducted to verify the effectiveness of our proposed approach. Numerical results are in agreement with theoretical analysis. Comparing to other existing methods, our proposed approach just needs to obtain the measured time series to estimate the parameters, which is simple in theorem and easy to be implemented.

articleTitle: Learning Spatial-Temporal Decoupling Representations for Few-Shot Action Recognition
abstract: Few-shot action recognition is the task of predicting unlabeled actions based on a limited number of labeled actions. Recently most of few-shot action recognition methods adopt GCNs to encode the skeleton clips and predict the label by calculating the distance in spatial-temporal feature space. However, coarse encoded features will lead to confusion between ambiguous actions with similar spatial or temporal information, which results in misclassification among these actions. To solve this problem, we propose a effective method called Spatial-Temporal Decoupling Matching (STDM) consisting of a spatial-temporal decoupling module and a spatial-temporal matching strategy to model the spatial and temporal information effectively. The spatial-temporal decoupling module maps confusing encoded features to spatial and temporal feature spaces respectively. The spatial-temporal matching strategy simultaneously recognizes the actions from the spatial and temporal perspective. We have conducted numerous experiments on NTU RGB+D 120 and Kinetics datasets. Our method achieves comparable results and surpasses most of the SOTA methods.

articleTitle: Design of Software for Real-Time Optimizing of the Multi-Module High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor Nuclear Power Plant
abstract: The modular high-temperature gas-cooled reactor is a promising technology in fourth-generation nuclear energy systems. It adopts the structure of multiple nuclear steam supply system modules driving a common steam turbine generator. Due to its complex structure and stringent safety requirements, its operation needs to be optimized in real time. In this paper, we design a set of software, which includes a communication module and a computation module based on the model-based real-time optimization strategy. This software can perform real-time optimization functions under load change scenarios and has good visualization to assist engineers in decision-making.

articleTitle: Underwater Biological Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv5
abstract: Aiming at the current problems of low underwater image quality in underwater biological target detection, low detection accuracy and high leakage rate caused by underwater biological occlusion and overlapping, an underwater biological target detection method based on improved YOLOv5s is proposed. Firstly, the SE attention mechanism is introduced at the end of the backbone network to enhance the feature proposing capability of the network. Secondly, BiFPN network is introduced in the neck network to replace the original structure, and different weights are assigned to different scale features for better feature fusion. Finally, the prediction frames are screened using the Soft-NMS strategy to minimize the missed detections. The experimental results show that compared with the original YOLOv5s algorithm, the improved algorithm improves the mean accuracy precision (mAP) by 3.2% on the URPC dataset, which validates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in underwater biological target detection.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Load Prediction Based On Real-Time Road Traffic
abstract: As an environment-friendly transportation, electric vehicles have the characteristics of both transportation and mobile load, and they have great uncertainty in travel time and space, which are two important factors affecting the charging load prediction of electric vehicles. The prediction of EV charging load considering spatiotemporal distribution is of great significance for studying its interaction with the power grid and the location and capacity determination of EV charging stations. In this paper, an EV load prediction method based on residual neural network considering spatial and temporal distribution is proposed after analyzing the behavioral habits of three objects, namely, private cars, cabs and public vehicles, to start with. Firstly, a travel probability model is established based on the travel habits of users, then the real-time traffic flow predicted by the residual neural network framework taking into account the date, weather, temperature and other factors is used to invert the starting and finishing points of EVs, then the vehicle travel speed and power consumption are calculated based on the traffic flow, and finally the continuous change of battery charge state is considered, and the charging load model of EVs is established based on the Monte Carlo method.

articleTitle: Data Augmentation and Improved Deformable DETR for Polyp Detection
abstract: Endoscopy examination is an important method for treating gastrointestinal diseases. The advent of the era of deep learning has provided a more reliable basis for Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD). The successful application of Transformer in the field of object recognition has further advanced object detection techniques beyond the convolutional neural network (CNN). In this study, a general data augmentation method for polyp target detection is proposed, effectively improving the impact of the small-scale polyp dataset; an improved polyp detection network based on deformable DETR has been proposed, resulting in enhanced detection accuracy; the loss function of the network is improved, enhancing the network's performance.

articleTitle: CSWin-Unet: Fusion Multi-scale Feature Insulator Segmentation Model
abstract: Insulator image segmentation is a process of separating and extracting the insulator part from the complex background in insulator image, which is of great significance to the automatic detection and fault diagnosis of power system. Convolutional neural networks have been performing well in image segmentation tasks for the past few years, and Transformer has been applied to computer vision tasks with great success. Transformer has the advantage of building global connections, but at the same time it lacks CNN's ability to generalize local information. In order to achieve fast and accurate identification of insulators under complex background, a U-shaped insulator image segmentation method is proposed in this paper. The proposed method utilizes the generalization ability of local features of CNN and the generalization ability of global features of Transformer to carry out feature extraction respectively. Then, global features and local features are fused through the feature fusion module, in which way the model can learn more robust features.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of A Fully Flexible Wheeled Robot
abstract: Wheeled robot has the advantages of strong capacity, fast walking speed and high work efficiency. This paper presents a fully flexible wheeled mobile robot based on waterbomb structure, which has deformable wheels and a collapsible body. On this basis, the mathematical model of wheel and body is established. Moreover, kinematics simulation of the robot is carried out by ADAMS, and the rationality of structure design and the validity of mathematical model are verified. Finally, the prototype of the robot is made and the basic performance of the robot is tested.

articleTitle: Modified SMC-Based Formation Tracking Control for a Multi-Missile System with Input Saturation
abstract: A fully distributed consensus protocol with fixed-time property is proposed to tackle the formation tracking issue for a multi-missile system in the presence of input saturation and external disturbances. A novel sliding manifold with a predefined time convergence is constructed, which can avoid the singularity of input signals. To enhance the robustness and control accuracy of the controller, a predefined time SMC-based consensus protocol combined with a fixed-time disturbance observer is proposed, in which the external disturbances are estimated and compensated adaptively. Furthermore, a dynamic model of modified consensus tracking errors combined with a second-order anti-windup compensator is constructed to cope with the manipulation saturation problem. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Distributed Weighted Least Squares Estimator Based on ADMM
abstract: This paper is concerned with a distributed tracking estimator with nonlinear measurement, which aims to achieve a consensus estimate over the entire network. To this end, we first employ a named sigma point transform (SPT) technique to convert measurement into Cartesian coordinates. In this setting, each node retains a weighted least squares (WLS) style without any prior distribution information, so that the centralized WLS filter is decomposed into several local parallel optimization problems with consensus-based constraints. To yield a closed-form expression in both the estimate and error covariance (information matrix), we use the alternating direction method of multiplier (ADMM) technique to perform an inner iteration. The proposed estimator is found to increase the tracking accuracy over alternative approach in a dynamic scenario.

articleTitle: Reconfigurability Evaluation of VSCMG Based on Power Consumption Constraint
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurability evaluation method for Variable Speed Control Moment Gyroscope (VSCMG) based on power consumption constraint is proposed. Based on the spacecraft attitude dynamics model and the VSCMGs system model, the spacecraft state space equation is established with the VSCMGs system fault factor vector. And then, by judging the controllability and power consumption performance of the system, a multiple composite reconfigurability evaluation method based on power consumption and reliability constraints is designed. Finally, the simulation analysis of whether the VSCMGs system has reconfiguration after failure is carried out, and the simulation results are in line with the actual situation, which verifies the correctness and effectiveness of the evaluation method.

articleTitle: Stability and Bifurcation Analysis of Fractional Transcriptional Regulatory Networks
abstract: Fractional differential equations capture changes in genes over time better than integer-order differential equations. Due to the complexity of the system caused by fractional order integrals, the regulatory network for fractional order differential equations lacks stability analysis and HOPE bifurcation condition analysis. In this paper, the dynamical behavior of the time-delay system is studied based on fractional differential equations. By adding two delay factors and PD controllers, the stability and HOPF bifurcation conditions of fractional-order gene regulatory networks with time delay are deduced through analyzing Caputo fractional derivatives theory. The influence of order on system bifurcation is verified by the use of numerical simulations. At the same time, it is found that changes in controller parameters will make the HOPF bifurcation of fractional order systems occur in advance or be delayed.

articleTitle: Time-Cooperative Trajectory Optimization Method for Hypersonic Vehicle based on Improved Grey Wolf Artificial Potential Field Method
abstract: Multiple hypersonic vehicles can achieve saturation attack on the target by means of attack time coordination, and can also greatly improve the success rate of penetration in the denial environment. At present, a typical time cooperative guidance scheme is the bank angle corridor adjustment strategy based on time prediction. However, the controllable margin of time prediction accuracy is limited, which will inevitably lead to frequent reversal of the bank angle, which will cause the oscillation of the flight trajectory. Aiming at this problem, this paper designs a trajectory optimization method based on improved GWO (grey wolf optimization) algorithm, which reduces the number of bank angle reversals and improves the trajectory safety and reliability under the premise of ensuring the accuracy of constraint management. In this paper, the shortcomings of the traditional GWO algorithm in population initialization and iterative strategy are improved, and it is applied to the time cooperative trajectory optimization problem of the vehicle. After simulation verification, the designed algorithm can effectively reduce the bank angle inversion frequency during the flight of the hypersonic vehicle, save the energy of the vehicle, and ensure the safety and stability of the flight process.

articleTitle: Quality Prediction of Rocket Engine Combustion Chamber Shell Spinning Process Based on CGAN and Hybrid Neural Network
abstract: The combustion chamber shell is one of the main structures of rocket engines, and the quality prediction of its spinning process is crucial to improve the stability of the engine and the subsequent improvement process. In this article, we propose a quality prediction method based on data augmentation and a hybrid neural network model combining feature attention (FA) and temporal convolutional network and long short term memory network (TCN-LSTM). First, the feature multi-collinearity problem is solved by principal component analysis dimensionality reduction of the equipment time series data of the shell machining process. Then, conditional generative adversarial network is used for data augmentation to generate more samples using quality indicators as condition information to solve the problem of insufficient data collection in actual engineering. Finally, the key feature information is enhanced using the FA mechanism, while the dual quality metrics are predicted by TCN-LSTM, and the prediction results are corrected using the least squares method. In this paper, a real rocket engine combustion chamber shell machining dataset is used to validate the model effect, and the experimental results show that the method has higher prediction accuracy by comparing with different machine learning methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Filtering for UAV Integrated Navigation Based on Noise Variance
abstract: The Kalman filter is often used as the data fusion algorithm in the GPS/SINS integrated navigation system of the UAV. However, in practical applications, the traditional Kalman filter lacks the ability to deal with the statistical characteristics of noise, which are difficult to obtain and vary with the environment. Therefore, this paper first designs a noise estimator based on reliability for the problem that it is difficult to obtain the statistical characteristics of noise in practical applications; secondly, the measurement noise is updated separately after the Kalman measurement update to reduce the noise caused by noise changes. Finally, the simulation experiment verifies that the adaptive filter designed in this paper can achieve better data fusion in the application of UAV GPS/SINS integrated navigation, and has higher robustness and fault tolerance.

articleTitle: Within-Hand Manipulation with an Underactuated Dexterous Hand Based on Pre-Trained Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper investigates a dexterous manipulation method for multi-fingered hands based on the approximate policy optimization (PPO) algorithm. First, a prior knowledge base of dexterous manipulation demonstration data is provided for the PPO algorithm, and the original model is pre-trained to guide fast network training. Second, a new reward function is proposed to optimize rotational manipulation action decisions based on hand joints, fingertip tactile, and object pose infor mation. Finally, a three-fingered hand is used as an example for rotational manipulation experiments, and the comparative simulation results show that the method is more efficient than the traditional PPO algorithm and provides ideas for dexterous manipulation of multi-fingered hands.

articleTitle: Enhancing Industrial Safety: A Comprehensive Approach to Detecting and Mitigating Potential Hazards
abstract: Industrial safety has always been one of the important factors that restrict the sustainable development of enterprises. These safety hazards threaten the lives and health of workers at all times. Therefore, improving industrial safety levels is a necessary condition for the sustainable development of enterprises. Currently, most detection devices only address single problems, and these single-task devices cannot meet the monitoring needs of multiple safety hazards. This study uses object detection technology to achieve real-time monitoring and identification of safety helmets, fires, and industrial instruments, which can simultaneously solve multiple safety hazards and improve industrial safety levels. Specifically, we employ the PP-YOLOE algorithm for multi-task target detection, enabling real-time detection of these three safety hazards with recognition precision reaching 51.2%. Furthermore, building upon target detection, we employ image segmentation and computer vision techniques to achieve accurate readings of industrial instruments, achieving a precision of up to four decimal places. Finally, the system is successfully deployed on a quadruped robot, coupled with autonomous navigation and path planning techniques, facilitating robot inspections in industrial environments. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach in enhancing industrial safety levels and ensuring the sustainable development of enterprises.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Sliding Mode Terminal Guidance Method
abstract: This article designs a sliding mode terminal guidance law for high-speed targets by modifying the approach law. Firstly, the relative motion equation of the chaser and escaper is established; Then adjust the aircraft based on the changes in the distance of the chaser and escaper and approach speed, design a self adaptive approach law, and derive the guidance law. At the same time, prove the stability of the guidance system by constructing a Lyapunov function; Finally, simulation verification was conducted. The simulation results showed that the designed guidance law can achieve the encounter between the chaser and the escaper. By comparing it with proportional guidance under different operating conditions, it was verified that the method has higher adaptability to different operating conditions, thus verifying the effectiveness of the guidance law designed in this paper and providing certain reference value for further research.

articleTitle: A LiDAR-Inertial-Encoder Odemetry with Global Optimization
abstract: Accurate state estimation is the key to realize robot autonomy, LiDAR-inertial odometry has become one of the most widely used methods because it is capable of accurate and fast state estimation. However, LiDAR-inertial odometry could only obtain relative pose, and global position drift is easy to occur at large scale. Driven by the objective of achieving pose estimation without long-term drift, a positioning system with global optimization integrating GNSS measurements and LiDAR-inertial-encoder odometry is proposed in this paper. LiDAR, IMU and encoder data are fused by a nonlinear optimization framework to obtain an accurate local state. The GNSS measurements are prone to electromagnetic interference, satellite rejection, and other various influencing elements. Therefore, we fuse the GNSS, IMU and encoder measurements by Error-state Kalman filter to accquire more robust and smooth global position. In the global optimization module, the local state estimation and the global positioning information are fused in a pose graph optimization to get a global pose without drifts. We evaluate the performance of our algorithm on challenging datasets. Compared with other state-of-the-art algorithms, the positioning accuracy and robustness in our algorithm has been greatly improved and the global drifts are corrected by the global optimization module.

articleTitle: Loop Closure Detection Based On Semantic Information In Dynamic Scenes
abstract: This paper proposes an approach to optimize visual loop closure detection (LCD) algorithms for dynamic scenes. Although loop closure detection has been widely used in visual SLAM systems, there are still some deficiencies when running in real scenes, such as the vulnerability in scenes with dynamic targets, which severely interferes with the similarity calculation between images and greatly degrades the performance of loop closure detection. In addition, existing loop closure detection algorithms rely on traditional image features, making them more sensitive to lighting, rotation, etc., resulting in high sensitivity. Our approach aims to enhance the correlation between images by utilizing semantic information, improving the original feature matching algorithm based on the Bag-of-Words (BoW), and constructing a semantic matching algorithm based on the results of semantic data association, thereby improving the accuracy of loop closure detection in dynamic scenes. Extensive experiments on public datasets have demonstrated the reliability and effective-ness of our method, achieving better global localization accuracy compared to other loop closure detection algorithms.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition Based on EEG and DE-CNN-RNN
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can extract local spatial features from data well, but it cannot capture long-term dependencies contained in serial data. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can compensate for this defect. In the study, according to the differential entropy (DE) feature of electroencephalogram (EEG), DE-CNN-RNN model is proposed to explore emotion recognition based on EEG signals. Experimental tests were conducted with the SEED emotion dataset to compare the accuracy of emotion classification of DE-CNN, DE-RNN, CNN-RNN, and DE-CNN-RNN models. The proposed DE-CNN-RNN model could improve the accuracy of emotion classification by 10% and effectively identify emotion types.

articleTitle: Real-Time Aiming Strategy Optimization of Heliostat Field of Solar Power Tower via a Modified PSO Algorithm(SPSO)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient and intelligent real-time optimization algorithm based on meta-heuristics, named SPSO, to manage the operation of SPT under various meteorological conditions, such as cloud shadow changes. In order to reduce the complexity of the real-time optimization metaheuristic algorithm, the population individuals of the metaheuristic algorithm are modeled as intelligent agents of heliostats. A population inheritance mechanism is proposed to improve the classical PSO algorithm and minimize redundant calculations, which extracts the similarity of the heliostat field running continuously. The proposed method is tested in a simulation environment that includes heliostat fields, cylindrical receivers, and cloud movement models. The results show that the proposed SPSO has higher convergence efficiency, better robustness, and shorter optimization time under dynamic cloud shadow conditions. Finally, the convergence of SPSO is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Novel Functional Link Neural Network with Pearson Correlation Coefficient: Application to Soft Sensing
abstract: Nowadays, with the expansion of the dimension and the scale of chemical industry, building an accurate soft sensor model becomes more difficult. Fortunately, Functional Link Neural Network (FLNN) has proven to be a dependable model for soft sensing and has been successfully implemented. Traditional FLNN ignores the fact that the input attributes have different correlations and go through function expansion blocks as a whole, which may lead to modeling accuracy can not meet the requirements. To solve this problem, a novel functional link neural network with Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC-FLNN) is proposed in this paper. The input attributes are categorized based on their Pearson correlation coefficients, with one group having positive coefficients and the other group having negative coefficients. After function expansion, these two groups of input attributes create two separate subnetworks. The proposed method has a remarkable feature: it is able to improve the modeling accuracy without increasing the training parameters. Both the UCI standard dataset and the pure terephthalic acid (PTA) process dataset are used to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed method. The findings indicate that the PCC-FLNN outperforms the FLNN in accuracy.

articleTitle: Road Disease Detection based on Improved RTMDet
abstract: In order to better maintain road diseases, efficient and accurate detection is required. It is feasible to use computer vision instead of manual and sensor for automatic road diseases detection accompanied by the development of deep learning. The actual road background is complex, and the types of diseases are diverse, and the detection and classification of road diseases still face great challenges. We propose a road diseases detection algorithm based on RTMDet to resolve these issues, and it meets real-time and high precision requirements. First, we reconstructed the detector head, combined with an efficient attention mechanism, and reduced the computational load and model complexity of the algorithm. Then we redesigned the algorithm's Loss function, and used the TAL label assign strategy, Varifocal loss, and Distribution Focal Loss to improve the association for classification and regression tasks, and effectively enhance the precision of the algorithm's classification and bounding box.

articleTitle: Bolt Detection and Precise Positioning Method for High-Voltage Live Working Robot
abstract: A bolt detection and precise positioning method combining neural network and RGB-D camera is proposed for the disassembly and installation task of distribution line insulators, which is used to assist the robot to quickly determine the accurate location of insulator bolts. An improved YOLOv5s network is used to detect the target bolt, after which the bolt end center is predicted by a bolt end center prediction network, and finally the three-dimensions coordinates of the bolt end center are obtained by combining the depth information of the RGB-D camera. The improved YOLOv5s reduces the detection time of a single image by 25.3% and reduces the number of parameters by 22.2%. The average prediction error of the bolt end center prediction network is 8.6 pixels, and the maximum prediction error is 12.4 pixels. Combined with the RGB-D camera for testing, the XY plane positioning error is no more than 4.2mm, and the depth error is no more than 2mm. At experimental site, the method is tested on a live working robot and meets the requirements of practical operations.

articleTitle: Research on Cognitive Mining Method of Ship Formation Behavior Law Based on Knowledge Graph and Fuzzy Association Logic
abstract: With the continuous development of sensor and communication technology, the ability to acquire the situation information of naval battle field has been continuously improved, and the importance of accurately understanding and explaining ship formation behavior for military decision-making has been realized. In order to solve the problem of inaccuracy and delay caused by manual analysis of situation information, this paper aims to explore a cognitive mining method of behavior law based on knowledge graph and fuzzy association logic, so as to deeply recognize and mine the target situation information of ship formation. Firstly, based on knowledge graph construction technology, knowledge extraction, knowledge fusion and knowledge processing, the multi-source data of ship formation is structurally represented, and the knowledge graph including ship formation, interception and interference is constructed. Then, the applicability and effectiveness of the fuzzy logic reasoning method in the mining of ship formation behavior law are analyzed by introducing fuzzy correlation logic. Then we study the effect of knowledge graph and fuzzy association logic reasoning on the mining of behavior rules, including association information introduction and fuzzy rule weighting. Finally, based on this method, the law mining and cognitive architecture of ship formation release behavior in chaff are constructed, including the dynamic updating of cognition and mining process and knowledge graph. It is found that the cognition and mining method based on knowledge graph and fuzzy correlation provides a feasible solution for the cognition and mining of ship formation behavior law.

articleTitle: Research on Technology Convergence Based on Patent Knowledge Flow Network - A Case Study of Industrial Robotics
abstract: Significant convergence has occurred between new-generation artificial intelligence technology and industrial robot technology. However., there are still limitations in the research to use quantitative methods to analyze the technology convergence process. This study proposes to analyze the technical knowledge contained in patent data from the perspective of knowledge flow, to describe the development trend of technology convergence by building a patent knowledge flow network and technology convergence network, to identify the technology convergence path and key convergence components, and to conduct empirical research in the field of industrial robots. The study has identified the technology convergence clusters with high technical control force and high technical value. The results can support relevant researchers to grasp technological opportunities in advance in the rapid development of industrial robots.

articleTitle: The Study on the Ultrasound-Based Anti-Interference Following Robot
abstract: The demand for following robots is expanding with the aging population and smart cities. Ultrasonic-based following robots are a cost-effective solution. Considering that ultrasonic waves are easily interfered with by co-frequency ultrasonic waves, this paper proposes an ultrasonic-based anti-interference following scheme. Based on this, a car-shaped following robot is designed and implemented. Experimental results based on real scenarios show that our robot can achieve accurate linear-following and turn-following under the interference of co-frequency ultrasound, which demonstrates a high value of application.

articleTitle: Detection method for driver's gaze direction based on improved VGG network
abstract: Gaze detection is the basis for driver state monitoring and intent recognition as well as vision-based human-vehicle interaction. This paper proposed an appearance-based gaze direction vector detection model, taking the eye image, head posture and pupil center position as sample data and the gaze direction vector as sample labels, and using the improved VGG deep learning network for training to obtain the driver's gaze direction vector, and completing the gaze direction detection of the driver's gazing at different target regions. In the real car environment, we carried out experiments to recognize 6 different regions of the windshield, and the results show that the gaze direction detection method proposed in this paper is basically unaffected by changes in head posture and driving environment illumination, and the average detection accuracy for 10 drivers is 96.53%.

articleTitle: A Multi-Path Unequal Clustering Energy-Efficient Routing Algorithm for Monitoring Networks in Coal Mine Tunnel
abstract: Tunnels in underground coal mine are complex and variable environments, where the lack of scalability of wired monitoring systems leads to complex wiring and high maintenance costs. In wireless sensor networks, due to the limited energy capacity of sensor nodes, how to balance the energy consumption, extend the network lifetime, and achieve the optimal resource utilization is a critical issue. To stably monitor the underground coal mine tunnels and ensure the safe production of underground coal mines, we propose a multipath unequal clustering energy-efficient routing algorithm based on ideal communication hop distance according to the characteristics of the underground coal mine tunnel. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can be applied in underground coal mine tunnels and solve the problem of uneven energy distribution of nodes in different tunnel regions, which greatly improves the service life of the underground monitoring network.

articleTitle: A Novel Distributed and Hierarchical Control Method for the Series-Parallel-Type Microgrid
abstract: The series-parallel-type microgrid has been proposed to integrate various distributed generation (DG) units, such as photovoltaic (PV) and energy storage. This article further proposes a novel distributed and hierarchical control method for accurate power sharing and restoration of AC output voltage magnitude. First, the basic working principle of the series-parallel-type microgrid has been briefly introduced, based on which the proposed method is elaborated. Each converter module only communicates with its neighboring converter module, and the central controller is not needed, which avoids the failure of central controller on the whole system and increases the reliability. The correction values of AC voltage magnitude and angular frequency are calculated. The proposed method is suitable for both resistive-inductive (RL) and resistive-capacitive (RC) loads. Evaluation results are provided to validate the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: DR-DiT: Image Deraining using Diffusion Model with Transformer
abstract: Rain removal in images is a significant challenge in the field of computer vision, as it is necessary to restore the visual quality of images degraded by rain streaks or droplets. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for rain removal using the diffusion model with a Transformer-based structure instead of the traditional U-Net architecture. The Transformer architecture has recently gained popularity for its ability to capture long-range dependencies and attention mechanisms. To reduce the computational complexity of self-attention in the Transformer, we used multi-head external attention instead of multi-head self-attention. Additionally, we design a multi-scale gated feed-forward network for improved local information capture. Our method is trained on a large dataset of rainy and corresponding clean images, and its performance is evaluated on various test images with different rain densities. Our experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves excellent results in terms of both quantitative metrics and visual quality.

articleTitle: Formalizing the Term Substitution Theorem in First-Order Logic within the Coq Proof Assistant
abstract: The term substitution theorem is a vital theorem in mathematical logic that concerns the replacement operation of variables within terms. In this study, we present a comprehensive formalization and verification of the term substitution theorem using the Coq proof assistant. We define the elementary concepts and theorems of first-order logic embedded in Coq, including terms, variables, assignments, and substitutions. Our findings not only offer a method for constructing a suitable nested recursive function for Coq's inductive types but also establish a solid foundation for further investigations and applications in first-order logic. By verifying the term substitution theorem in Coq, we showcase the capabilities of the Coq proof assistant in the machine-checked verification of mathematical proofs and enhance the robustness and dependability of mathematical reasoning across diverse disciplines.

articleTitle: Control Design of Flight Simulation Turntable Based on Model-Free Adaptive Control
abstract: Aiming at the problem of periodic interference in flight simulation turntables, a design method of full-form dynamic linearization model free adaptive control (FFDL-MFAC) is proposed. An equivalent dynamic linearized data model is established at each dynamic operating point of the closed-loop system to achieve adaptive control of the nonlinear system, which gives the controller the advantage of online adjustment of internal parameters and improves the robustness of the control system. Aiming at the difficulty of parameter adjustment caused by the increase of dimension of the pseudo partial derivative matrix, a PID-like MFAC parameter adjustment method is proposed, which greatly reduces the difficulty of parameter adjustment of the model-free adaptive controller. The simulation results of MFAC and PID show that the designed FFDL-MFAC controller outperforms the conventional PID in tracking command signals and suppressing periodic disturbances.

articleTitle: Bionic Fishtail-Shaped Proprioceptive Sensing Technology Based on Triboelectric Nanogenerator
abstract: Accurate motion posture prediction is crucial for bionic robot fish (BRF) to fulfill military strategies and perform efficient underwater detection. Inspired by the proprioceptive sensing ability of caudal fins, we propose a prototype of tri-boelectric nanogenerators fish-tail-shaped proprioceptive sensing (FPSP) to assist BRF in predicting its self-motion posture. The FPSP consists of a flexible tail fin-like shell and three triboelectric nanogenerator sensing units, which are able to convert the bending of the flexible shell into a voltage output. The motion posture of BRF can be predicted by analyzing the voltage output of FPSP in a complex flow field environment. Experimental results have demonstrated the promising potential of proprioceptive sensors in augmenting the control capabilities of BRF.

articleTitle: Interval Optimal Controller Design for Uncertain Systems Based on Interval Neural Network
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for designing interval optimal PID controller for uncertain systems, which utilizes the key technologies of interval BP neural network (IBPNN) and interval particle swarm optimization algorithm (IPSO). The IBPNN is employed to model the uncertain plant as an interval system, and the output of the interval PID is applied to this interval network. By using the IPSO, the parameters of the interval PID are optimized, resulting in the determination of the parameter domain. This method effectively tackles the challenges associated with designing interval controllers based on Kharitonov's theorem, such as the dependence on interval plant models, intricate calculations, and the inability to handle nonlinear plants. Moreover, it circumvents the issue of interval expansion caused by interval operations. By ensuring the stability of the interval system, the proposed method can also optimize the system's performance. The simulation results validate the effectiveness and generalization of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Path Planning of UAV Based on Improved White Shark Optimization Algorithm
abstract: To overcome the problems of standard white shark optimization algorithm (WSO) in UAVs path planning, like expensive cost of path length and turning, this paper proposes an upgraded WSO, called the EAGWSO. Firstly, aiming at the uneven population distribution in WSO, the elite reverse learning strategy is utilized to establish the population of white sharks, which boosts the solution quality. Secondly, an adaptive control factor is used to further adjust random white sharks' location, so that the algorithm approaches the worldwide ideal solution gradually. Then, the Gaussian evolution mechanism is integrated to disrupt the greatest white sharks position of the partial optimum. Finally, the proposed EAGWSO is employed to address the UAVs path planning issues. In contrast to the WSO, the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed EAGWSO has faster convergence speed, shorter path length and lower turning cost, which is excellent for handling path planning problem of UAVs.

articleTitle: Stability and L1-Gain Analysis for Switched Time-Delay Positive Systems With Persistent Dwell Time Switching
abstract: In this article, the stability and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-gain performance analysis of switched time-delay positive systems (STDPSs) is explored. The more general persistent dwell time (PDT) switching is used to investigate STDPSs for the first time. Then, a co-positive type Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (CPTLKF) is constructed. The stability conditions of the STDPSs are established based on the CPTLKF and PDT. Furthermore, based on the stability analysis results, the unweighted L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-gain for STDPSs is explored, which has explicit physical meaning compared with the weighted results. The upper bound of the unweighted L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-gain can be obtained by a linear programming (LP) problem. Compared with the results obtained by dwell time (DT) or average dwell time (ADT), the results obtained by PDT in this article are less conservative. An example verifies the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Pain Expression Recognition Method Based on Fusion Attention Mechanism Capsule Network
abstract: Facial expression serves as a crucial indicator for pain recognition. However, existing approaches often face challenges in accurately extracting features from complex spatial information in facial expressions. To address this, this study introduces a pain recognition method based on a fusion attention mechanism capsule network. The main contributions of this paper are outlined as follows. Firstly, a comprehensive pain expression database is established by using video image sequences. Subsequently, the capsule attention mechanism is introduced after the primary capsule layer of the network, facilitating more effective feature extraction and improving the accuracy of information transmission within the capsule network. Additionally, the fully connected decoder in the capsule network is replaced by the deconvolution decoder, resulting in a reduction in the overall parameter count. Experimental results on the pain expression database demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed capsule network, achieving an impressive accuracy of 98.21%. Importantly, the proposed approach outperforms other deep learning models in terms of accuracy for pain recognition.

articleTitle: Ascent Trajectory Optimization Design of Solid Launch Vehicle Based on Newton Iteration Method
abstract: In this paper, a trajectory optimization design method based on solid launch vehicle ascent phase trajectory is proposed. We have created a Newton Iteration Method for the best possible trajectory track design and a trajectory program for the vehicle's active stage. The Newton Iteration Method algorithm successfully handles solid rocket trajectory optimization design issues, as shown by analysis and simulation results. It satisfies requirements for separation point inclination, height, and other parameters while optimizing the trajectory path scheme in the ascending trajectory. The technique improves convergence stability and speed, making engineering implementation easier. This work provides a theoretical framework for ascent trajectory optimization design and offers valuable insights for practitioners in the field.

articleTitle: Optimal Trajectory Tracking for Unknown H∞ Constrained Systems Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This letter obtains a solution for the optimal trajectory tracking of unknown H∞)-constrained systems using reinforcement learning to derive the Nash equilibrium. To illustrate the H∞) tracking, a discounted performance function with multi-inputs in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-gain is provided. An augmented vector, consisting of known bounded reference trajectory and tracking error, is constructed to describe the augmented system. Along the augmented system, a new index function is introduced to formulate the optimal tracking control problem. This letter presents a policy iteration algorithm that provides the Nash equilibrium solution, even without the system dynamics information. By applying Pontryagin's maximum principle and introducing a novel costate, the system's stability is ensured through the determination of its upper bound. Thorough examination verifies that the suggested tracking algorithm converges effectively when using the Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs (HJI) equation.

articleTitle: A Study of Soil Shear Strength Sensing Based on Soil Shear Save Velocity
abstract: The study on the relationship between shear wave velocity and soil shear strength holds significant importance for landslide disaster warning. However, currently, there is a lack of mature methods for continuously monitoring soil shear strength, and existing in-situ soil shear wave velocity measurement devices suffer from complexities in operation and limitations in long-term monitoring. To address these issues, this study proposes a convenient soil shear wave velocity measurement apparatus designed using piezoelectric elements, enabling rapid and straightforward measurement of soil shear wave velocity. Furthermore, to validate the effectiveness of the apparatus and explore the relationship between shear wave velocity and soil shear strength, a corresponding experimental platform was constructed for testing. Through meticulous analysis of the experimental data, the optimal fitting relationship between soil shear wave velocity and soil shear strength was obtained, exhibiting excellent fitting performance. This relationship indicates a strong correlation between soil shear wave velocity and soil shear strength under the condition of only varying soil stress, thereby preliminary validating the feasibility of indirectly measuring soil shear strength using shear wave velocity. These findings provide new reference criteria for landslide and debris flow disaster warning and offer fresh theoretical support and experimental basis for engineering applications and geological hazard prevention.

articleTitle: Path Planning for Wheeled Robots Based on the Fusion of Improved A* and TEB Algorithms
abstract: In this paper, we propose a hierarchical path planning method to address the issues of unsmooth path curves in autonomous navigation for wheeled robots using the original A * algorithm, and the adverse impact on robots caused by jumping changes in output commands of the original TEB algorithm. Firstly, we evaluate the curvature using the curvature smoothing function in the A * algorithm, followed by introducing interpolation to replace some of the unsmoothed path nodes to enhance path smoothness. Secondly, we add jerk constraints on multiple nodes in the TEB algorithm to reduce the impact of acceleration jumps in the output on the mechanical structure of the robot body, thereby improving the operation efficiency of the local path planning algorithm. Finally, we integrate the improved A * algorithm with the TEB algorithm to enable the robot to follow global path points better while bypassing obstacles on time. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves global path smoothing, output speed changes more smoothly, and the wheeled robot's motion smoothness is enhanced.

articleTitle: Local and Global Feature Refinement for Underwater Object Detection
abstract: Recently, underwater object detection has attracted a lot of interest. However, due to the blur and low contrast in the underwater scene, if deployed directly, generic detection methods show poor performance. To address this problem, we propose a local and global fusion underwater object detection algorithm with a receptive field refinement module (RFRM). Specifically, LGFB combines inductive biases and long-range dependencies to obtain high-quality visual representations. This module implements the interaction between the convolution block and the transformer block. RFRM takes the different receptive fields into consideration and suppresses the redundant information by exploring the relationship between adjacent layers. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method is superior to generic object detectors, achieving 80.9 mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> and 71.3 mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> on URPC2018 and UDD datasets. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/caiduoduo12138/underwater.

articleTitle: Unknown Fault Diagnosis Based on Transfer Learning Under Multiple Working Conditions
abstract: The rapid development of modern industry makes fault diagnosis more important. In engineering practice, equipment often works under different working conditions, and there may be several new faults, called unknown faults, which cannot be identified by the traditional intelligent fault diagnosis method. To solve the difficulty of unknown faults diagnosis under multiple working conditions, a fault diagnosis method based on adversarial transfer learning and multitask learning is proposed in this paper. First, known faults and unknown faults are distinguished by adversarial transfer method with sample weights. Second, the fault classification module and fault location module trained by multitask learning are used to classify and locate the known faults. Besides, the number of categories of unknown faults is identified by the Bisecting K-Means clustering algorithm with silhouette coefficient. Experiment shows that the proposed method can be well applied to unknown fault diagnosis, and has a better recognition rate than other comparison methods.

articleTitle: Robust Global Exponential Stability of Fuzzy Neural Networks with Bis-Disturbances
abstract: This paper provides a sufficient criterion guaranteeing the robust global exponential stability (RGES) of fuzzy neural networks (FNN) with bis-disturbances, i.e., derivative contraction coefficients and piecewise constant arguments. By using the generalized Gronwall inequality and modular inequality, the upper bound of bis-disturbances is derived by solving the binary implicit transcendental equation as well as external spontaneous constraints respectively, ensuring the primitive stable FNN can be stable again in the presence of external bis-disturbances. Furthermore, the feasible boundary derived from the established criterion can guarantee that the mutual restraint and dynamic interconnection effects between the bis-disturbances that allow the system to be stable again can occur instead of being independent. Finally, the validity of the derived theoretical results is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of Vanadium Dioxide-Based High-Sensitivity Microfluidic Calorimetric Sensors
abstract: Accurate measurement of microfluidic flow with high sensitivity is critical across numerous industries and applications. The calorimetric microflow sensor attracts attention among different MEMS flow sensors due to its excellent performance at low flow rates. To further improve the sensitivity and meet the nL/min to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{L}/\mathbf{min}$</tex> detection demand, we employed the metamaterial vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) as a thermally sensitive material of ultra-high temperature-coefficient-of-resistance (TCR) in the phase change region. Meanwhile, the significant and intricate temperature-dependent hysteresis behavior is thoroughly investigated. Hence, the major and minor hysteresis models of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> based on the physical mechanisms and the Preisach model are established, respectively, which enables a comprehensive analysis and performance evaluation of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based calorimetric microflow sensor using finite element analysis (FEA). The results show that the proposed sensor achieves a sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.456} \mathbf{V}/(\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{L}\cdot\mathbf{min}^{-\mathbf{1}})$</tex> in the linear range of 0 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.3}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{L}\cdot\mathbf{min}^{-\mathbf{1}}$</tex>, which is 83.82 times higher than the Pt-based calorimetric sensor and 5.17 times higher than the VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based anemometric sensor. This work provides a novel approach for designing high-performance thermal microflow sensors using metamaterials with hysteresis behavior.

articleTitle: Stability and Stabilization Conditions for 3D Printing Control Systems with Time-Varying Delay
abstract: In the 3D printing control system (3DPCS), the control and measurement signals are transmitted through the network channel, inevitably producing time-varying delay. In this paper, the stability and stabilization problem of 3DPCS with time-varying delay are studied. First, the 3DPCS framework and state space dynamic model with time-varying delay is proposed. Second, the stability and stabilization conditions of the 3DPCS are derived by constructing the augmented Lyapunov-Krasovskii(L-K) functional and using the relaxed mixed convex combination technologies. Thus, the corresponding controller gain is further obtained. Finally, the simulation results show that the upper bound of acceptable time delay of the 3DPCS are larger, which indicates that the stability criterion in this paper is less conservative. In addition, the controller designed based on the stabilization condition can ensure the stable operation of the 3DPCS.

articleTitle: Application Research of Wide&Deep Model in CATV Intelligent Video Recommendation System
abstract: Wasu Media & Network Co., Ltd has recently launched a brand-new intelligent cable television terminal with much improved hardware performance and optimized compute capacity. This infrastructure upgrade calls for a better recommendation system to serve users with higher accuracy, greater computing efficiency and more timely recommendations. This paper mainly introduces the practice and application of the recommendation model based on Wide&Deep in CATV Intelligent video recommendation. Provide algorithm solutions for the construction of real-time CATV intelligent recommendation systems.

articleTitle: TCN-LSTM: A Deep Learning-Based Temperature Prediction Model for Rotary Kilns
abstract: The inherent complexity of physical and chemical reactions within the rotary kiln poses a challenge for traditional mechanism models in effectively characterizing the dynamic kiln process. To address this issue, we propose a deep learning-based temperature prediction dynamic model to accurately track the temperature changes, with a view to providing model-based support for rotary kilns process control and optimization. Our proposed model combines a temporal convolutional network (TCN) with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network, incorporating a unique feature fusion technique along with a hybrid pooling layer and attention layer. This integration enables the extraction of both global and local features, thereby preserving detailed information efficiently while significantly reducing model complexity. Additionally, these enhancements mitigate the risk of overfitting and enhance the stability and robustness of the model. Experimental results based on the zinc rotary kiln dataset demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits a promising prediction accuracy of the rotary kiln's temperature. It outperforms the state-of-the-art prediction models such as LSTM, Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and TCN. In the future, this model can be readily implemented and applied in many industrial areas such as systems modeling, time series forecasting, and predictive maintenance.

Author Keywords: temporal convolutional network (TCN) long short-term memory (LSTM)

articleTitle: Based on Embedded Smart Coffee Maker Design
abstract: At present, the domestic coffee machine research and development has become a diversified trend, but its price is expensive, brewing process is very complex. In response to the above problems, this design system uses ST company MCU platform to study and design a smart coffee maker based on STM32F103C8T6 for microcontrollers, which is cheap enough to meet the needs of most consumer groups. The whole smart coffee pot is mainly composed of coffee bean grinding system, extraction system and water tank heating system. The design can complete the grinding, boiling water, extraction of coffee beans, and can also achieve the coffee powder thickness, water temperature, water flow control, in order to better realize human-computer interaction can be displayed through the LCD screen working information and Bluetooth APP control. This design system mainly realizes the function of intelligent coffee pot, assembles, debugs and continuously optimizes the system after the design of the hardware and software of the intelligent coffee pot control system.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of Multi-Dimensional Time Lag Fractional-Order Gene Regulatory Network
abstract: In this scholarly paper, we delve into the intricate realm of fractional gene regulatory networks (FGRNs), focusing primarily on their stability analysis. These networks, integral to the understanding of complex biological processes, are analyzed through the lens of fractional calculus, offering a fresh perspective in the study of their dynamic behavior. Our research revolves around the concept of time-delay. Time-delay, often encountered in gene regulatory processes, can significantly influence the stability and behavior of these networks.

articleTitle: Intelligent Fixed-Time Consensus for Uncertain Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the issue of adaptive fuzzy fixed-time control of non-strict feedback nonlinear multi-intelligent systems. In this regard, a fuzzy logic system (FLS) is utilized to tackle the unknown nonlinear dynamics, and a non-singular fixed-time consensus control approach based on the adding power integral technique is then developed by building a novel integral-type Lyapunov function. Technically, a fixed-time adaptive fuzzy consensus control solution is formulated by engineering an integral-type Lyapunov function, which means that the tracking errors can convergence to zero in a fixed time. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed asymptotic consensus control method is verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Image Inpainting Based on Efficient Group Attention Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: Inpainting methods based on generative adversarial networks are an important class in the field, and their excellent generative ability can effectively improve the details of the inpainting results. However, generative adversarial networks inherently suffer from training difficulties and model collapse, leading to the large size of models based on such structures and equally difficult training. In addition, most methods incorporate an attention mechanism to improve the inpainting accuracy, which leads to the loss of boundary details of images in the process of restoration, affecting the results. To address the above problems, we propose an inpainting method based on efficient group attention generative adversarial networks (EGA-GAN). The proposed method uses cascaded group attention modules and feature-aligned pyramid networks in the generator. The cascaded group attention module can effectively save computational costs and reduce computational redundancy, and the feature-aligned pyramid network can mitigate the loss of boundary details in the downsampling operation to some extent. Experimental results on two commonly used inpainting datasets, Paris Street View and CelebA-HQ, show that the proposed method can effectively accelerate the speed of restoration and improve the accuracy of results.

articleTitle: A Soft Sensing Technique Based on Weighted Variational Auto-Encoder and its Application in Industrial Processes
abstract: The steady development and popularity of data acquisition systems in the modern industry have led to a trend toward the application of soft sensors. Feature representation converting raw data into a more representative and easier-to-process feature matrix is an important step in building soft sensors. The powerful feature extraction capability of deep learning makes it a popular choice for modeling. However, the unsupervised training process of some typical deep learning methods such as Variational Autoencoder (VAE) makes the extracted features contain information that is not useful for modeling predictions. In order to learn how the extracted features are related to the target variables, this article presents supervised soft sensing based on the weighted Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC) for VAE (wMIC- VAE). wMIC-V AE computes the correlation between the advanced feature extracted by VAE and the output variable using weighted MIC. Thus, the extracted feature is supervised and weighted, making the model training process more purposeful and rational. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method were demonstrated by applying it to the Pure terephthalic acid (PTA) dataset.

articleTitle: Partially Occluded Face Expression Recognition with CBAM-Based Residual Network for Teaching Scene
abstract: In this paper, a deep residual network based on convolutional block attention module (CBAM) is proposed, which is utilized for feature extraction of partially occluded face expression data. The proposed method overcomes the problem of localized occlusion face feature extraction by focusing on the regions and channels containing important information in the occluded face data through CBAM. Multi-task cascaded convolutional networks (MTCNN) are firstly utilized to localize the key regions of face emotion, and then deep emotion features are extracted by CBAM-ResNet network. The final emotion labels are generated. The effectiveness of this paper's method is verified on the RAF-DB dataset and the occluded CK+ dataset. The experimental accuracy in the RAF-DB dataset is 76.3%, which is 3.74% and 1.64% higher than the accuracy produced by the method of RGBT, and the WLS-RF, respectively. Application experiments are carried out in the real teaching scenario, which verifies the applicability of the algorithm in the real teaching scene.

articleTitle: Robot Fault Knowledge Graph Completion Based on Relational Graph Convolutional Network
abstract: The internal mechanism of industrial robots is complex. When a fault occurs because knowledge is too scattered, relying solely on traditional text search methods often leads to inefficient fault diagnosis. This article designs a knowledge graph based on text data and uses the knowledge graph to integrate fragmented knowledge. Because the existing data cannot completely cover the entire natural world, and there are problems in the correctness and timeliness of knowledge, a knowledge graph completion method is proposed that combines knowledge graphs and relationship graph convolutional networks incorporating attention mechanisms(A-RGCN). The attention mechanism it contains is to overcome the fixed selection of normalization constants for adjacent node message aggregation in the RGCN and capture the relationship attribute characteristics between different entities. This method combines the advantages of the knowledge graph, attention mechanism and RGCN. It captures the relationship attribute characteristics between different entities, extracts the internal correlation between entities, and finally integrates all knowledge. The experimental results validate the superior performance of the proposed model.

articleTitle: CAE-Yolov5: A Vehicle Target Detection Algorithm Based on Attention Mechanism
abstract: The number of vehicles has grown quickly along with people's quality of living and consumption, placing a significant stress on social transportation. The intelligent transportation system (ITS), which satisfies societal development requirements and lessens traffic congestion, was created. The primary area of research and its concentration have always been on accurate vehicle detection models. In this paper, we propose an improved Yolov5 network target identification algorithm for road vehicles utilizing attention mechanisms, aimed at the issues of complicated traffic scenes in the natural world, such as diverse vehicle sizes, overlapping vehicle targets, and substantial occlusion. First, a new attention module called CAE is developed that focuses the detection points of target detection on important areas by utilizing the benefits of convolutional block attention modules (CBAM) and efficient channel attention networks (ECA net). In order to collect shallower feature information, a larger-scale feature map is created, and the loss function of the bounding box, eiou (effective IOU loss), is increased. This accelerates convergence and enhances positional effects. According to experimental findings, the upgraded Yolov5 algorithm's average detection accuracy has increased from 91.3% to 96.3% when compared to the Yolov5 algorithm. On the Kitti dataset, the revised method outperforms the traditional one-stage SSD (single shot multi-box detector) and two-stage rapid RCNN (region CNN) algorithms in terms of detection accuracy and recall rate.

articleTitle: Application of Laser-Induced Voltage of Salt for Nanosecond Pulsed Laser Detection
abstract: In recent years, ultrafast pulse lasers have been widely used in various fields. The realtime detection of the characteristic parameters of the single-pulse laser is necessary. In this work, a method was proposed to detect the nanosecond (ns) pulsed laser. The laser-induced voltage (LIV) response of table salt (TS) consists of a rapid rise and a slow fall with the response time of about 150 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{s}$</tex>. The bias voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{b}})$</tex> and laser energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{E}_{\text{in}})$</tex> have a strong influence on the amplitude of the LIV signal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{p}})$</tex>, which increases with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{b}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{\text{in}}$</tex>. Influenced by the impedance effect, the response speed and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{P}}$</tex> of the LIV signal increased as the external resistance (R) decreases. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}=100 \Omega$</tex>, the LIV trace has a similar shape to the nanosecond (ns) pulsed laser. At this point, the response time of the LIV is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$= 20$</tex> ns, which is completely limited by the duration of the laser pulse. This research demonstrates that LIV response of TS has the potential for ultrafast single-pulse laser detection in real time.

articleTitle: Research on C-V2X cross-domain data collaborative sharing scheme
abstract: In order to ensure the interconnection and interoperability of business data during vehicle operation, and improve the high reliability and safety of vehicle road collaborative services, this paper studies the collaborative sharing technology scheme of vehicle road collaborative infrastructure data. This paper introduces four high-value use cases of vehicle road collaborative infrastructure data collaboration and sharing, analyzes their requirements, and explores the reference architecture for vehicle road collaborative infrastructure data collaboration and sharing. In addition, this paper proposes two technical schemes for data collaborative sharing, including those based on edge computing platform, cloud platform and other methods, and defines the data request, authentication and sharing process. Finally, this paper comprehensively considers the supported services, synchronization latency, requirements for network and edge platforms, and analyzes the feasibility and challenges of different sharing schemes, providing new ideas for achieving data collaboration and sharing between different operators.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Elastic Formation Control for Multiple Autonomous Surface Vessels
abstract: This paper introduces a hierarchical elastic formation control approach for multiple autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) navigating through irregular narrow waterways. Specifically, the high-level elastic formation control strategy is developed to achieve two schemes by using a navigation vector field technique: the coordination of two subgroups of ASVs along sub-channels to merge into a single elastic formation pattern along the main channel, and the splitting of the elastic formation pattern into two subgroups to facilitate obstacle avoidance. The low-level individual regulator is presented for ASV to track the virtual control velocity. Sufficient conditions are derived for the input-to-state stability of the closed-loop multi-ASV systems. Numerical simulations are elaborated to empirically validate the effectiveness of the elastic formation control method.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Tracking Control For Complex-Valued Nonlinear Systems
abstract: This paper considers the tracking control (TC) of nonlinear complex-valued system (NCVS). First, an augmented NCVS is proposed. Then, based on ADP, a data-driven control policy is proposed to solve the control problem, which is formed by action network (AN) and critic network (CN). The AN is complex-valued neural network (CVNN) and is used to generate control policy. The CN is also CVNN and is used to generate the performance value. Moreover, Both the tracking error and the weight estimation error are proved to be uniformly ultimately bounded (UUB). Finally, a simulation is given to verify the effectiveness of the obtained result.

articleTitle: Identification of Industrial Process Time Series Events Based on Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering*
abstract: Pattern clustering of industrial time series contributes to enhancing process monitoring, anomaly detection, production optimization. However, conventional clustering algorithms often concentrate solely on the inherent data dimensions, disregarding the underlying process features present in original time series.
