Given this insight, we propose a novel concept of hierarchical event clustering. Specifically, driven by the detection of time series anomalies, industrial data is segmented using the P AA and SAX algorithms to obtain data segments tailored to event representations. Then, these events are subjected to agglomerative hierarchical clustering. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through comparative experiments with traditional algorithms on the TE process platform. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority and immense potential of event clustering in actual industrial applications.

articleTitle: Autonomous Vehicle Motion Control Using NMPC Based on Orthogonal Collocation Method: Integration Stability Study
abstract: Nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) has gained increasing interest in motion control of autonomous driving. Integration stability is one of the crucial factors influencing the effectiveness of NMPC, which has not been considered much for the applications of autonomous driving. Orthogonal collocation method is utilized in this study to address the integration stability problem. Compared with two explicit integration methods which are commonly used, the proposed method is A -stable and thus provides a much wider stable region. By integrating orthogonal collocation method into the framework of NMPC, the integration stability problem at low velocity motion can be settled. The simulation under a small turning radius U-turn maneuver at a low vehicle velocity is performed and the results also show that the stability problem at low vehicle speeds is successfully resolved.

articleTitle: Design and Experiments of Automatic Vehicle Platoon Management with Connected Autonomous Vehicles in Mixed Traffic
abstract: The algorithm of automatic platoon management has been proposed for connected autonomous vehicles with mixed traffic. The Level 4 autonomous vehicles are designed to be able to automatically join a platoon mode when a preceding one with wireless communication equipped human-driven or autonomous vehicle is available. These vehicles are pre-authorized as they are connected with the operation cloud. Identification of the preceding vehicle is carried out by fusion of the local sensor detection and wireless communication with limited information. Moreover, the platoon can be automatically dissolved when the follower's route is separated from the preceding one. Then, a two-layer trajectory planner is proposed to realize this automatic platoon mode. In the first layer, the route planner will not consider the vehicle as an obstacle. Thus, if the preceding one stops, the Level 4 autonomous follower stops behind as well. In the second layer, however, the velocity planner takes all the surrounding objects into account and generates its velocity profile as a self-driving vehicle, such that it avoids large acceleration to maintain a desired inter-vehicle distance with no collision. Simulation and experiments clearly show the connected autonomous vehicles can properly follow in the platoon to avoid unnecessary overtake, and to keep comfort and safe 90° turns around the intersection.

articleTitle: Simulation Research on MPC-Based Intelligent Vehicle Trajectory Tracking Control
abstract: In order to accomplish the objective of trajectory tracking control for a smart vehicle, a controller utilizing model predictive control (MPC) is designed. To this end, a nonlinear dynamic model of vehicle dynamics with tire slip rate is first established, and then linearized and discretized. Next, the vehicle's front wheel deflection angle is used as the controller input, and the objective of the control is to reduce the error between the actual track and the target trajectory while taking into account the vehicle's actual structure, various constraints under actual driving conditions, adding soft constraints to the system output, and optimizing trajectory tracking. To verify the efficacy of the aforementioned trajectory tracking controller, a joint simulation system is constructed utilizing the Carsim-Simulink platform. The system carries out the typical trajectory tracking simulation tests at different vehicle speeds. The results of the simulation indicate that the proposed controller exhibits a greater ability to follow the typical trajectory path while controlling intelligent cars, making it a viable option for trajectory tracking control of future smart vehicles.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Load Forecasting in Mountainous Cities Considering Traffic Behavior
abstract: In response to the unique topographical challenges posed by mountainous environments, this paper investigates a probabilistic model of electric vehicle charging load, taking into account the unique traffic behavior and regional characteristics of mountainous cities. Regarding the traffic behavior, first, a traffic road network model for mountainous cities is proposed. Next, the travel chain theory is combined with the road chain to consider the functional partition of the city, which can better describe the travel patterns and charging behavior of users. Based on the analysis of traffic behavior, by exploring the influences of ambient temperature, road grade, and the undulating nature of mountainous roads, an improved Floyd shortest path algorithm is used for path decision-making, leading to the development of an EV power consumption model specifically tailored for mountainous cities. Based on this model, the prediction of EV load in mountainous cities is subsequently conducted. Overall, this study proposes a more realistic EV load prediction model by integrating traffic behavior, regional characteristics and user travel patterns, and the simulation results demonstrate the adaptability as well as the effectiveness of the method for application in mountainous cities.

articleTitle: A Semantic Segmentation Network Exploiting Multiple Cues and Channel Exchanging
abstract: Semantic scene understanding is an important task in robotics and computer vision. In this paper, we propose an easily deployable and effective deep convolutional neural network structure for semantic segmentation of mobile robot platforms called Channel Exchange SegNet (CES). The network structure is based on SegNet, a typical semantic segmentation network, and incorporates the Depth-to-Normal (D2N) module and the Channel Exchanging (CE) module. The D2N module utilizes the depth image to generate the normal image by three specially designed gradient filters. The CE module dynamically exchanges the feature maps between the three channels to achieve parameter-free multimodal fusion. We test our CES on the NYUDv2 and SUN-RGBD datasets. These quantitative evaluations show that our network has higher segmentation accuracy than single-mode networks.

articleTitle: Composite Improved Phase-Locked Loop Design of LCL-Type Grid-Connected Inverter Based on State Disturbance Observer
abstract: An improved Phase Locked Loop (PLL) design scheme based on State and disturbance observer (SDO) for LCL-type grid-connected PV inverter is proposed for weak grid single-phase inverter system. In order to achieve the same harmonic attenuation characteristics as the conventional front second-order low-pass filter phase-locked loop, and without additional phase compensation links, an improved phase-locked loop control strategy is designed and the equivalent transfer function of the improved phase-locked loop is derived. In order to perform aggregate estimation of the uncertain disturbance problem and reduce the number of measurement sensors, a SDO with fast response and low jitter level is designed to observe the aggregate disturbance and the inverter-side current for feedback. Simulation results show that the strategy enables the grid-connected inverter system to be more robust to filter parameters and grid impedance variations and improves the grid current quality.

articleTitle: UFFusion: An Unified Feature Space for Infrared-Visible Image Fusion Network Based on Dynamic Domain Transformation
abstract: Infrared-visible images have a high information complementarity, making fusing them highly valuable for various applications. However, infrared-visible images also exhibit strong differences, which are crucial factors limiting fusion performance. To address this issue, we propose a unified feature space in which can transfer the infrared domain to the visible domain using the dynamic domain transformation method. This approach eliminates the modality differences and provides high-quality features for image reconstructor. Notably, we propose a dense attention module used to extract common and unique features. The method permits the model to learn the correlation of different layer features, thereby enhancing the model's performance. Moreover, we design a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}^{3}\mathbf{IM}$</tex> loss function to enhance dynamic range of fused images. The qualitative and quantitative experiments on publicly available datasets demonstrate the superiority of our UFFusion over the state-of-the-art, in terms of both visual effect and quantitative metrics.

articleTitle: A Multiple Kernel Minimum Entropy Kalman Filter
abstract: In this paper, a multiple kernel minimum error entropy Kalman filter is proposed to estimate the filter state under abnormal measurement pollution. Firstly, an augmented Kalman filter model is constructed, and the minimum mean square error criterion under the traditional Kalman filter is replaced by the traditional minimum error entropy criterion. Then the quadratic rational kernel function and Gaussian kernel function are combined to construct the cost function, and the state results are obtained by fixed point iteration. Finally, the effectiveness of the filter is proved by a master-slave inertial navigation transfer alignment experiment.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Object Detection Network for Industrial Robot Based YOLOv5
abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning, it has been widely applied in fields such as computer vision, natural language processing, and robotics. Despite the superior performance of deep learning in object detection, most industrial vision robots still rely on traditional object detection methods due to computational constraints of robot controllers. In order to improve the performance of object detection for vision robots, a lightweight 3D object detection network based on You Only Look Once version 5 (YOLOv5) is proposed for satisfying industrial production. YOLOv5 work to efficiently object detection using deep convolutional networks. In terms of model deployment, we adopt a novel OpenVINO-based model deployment approach. The OpenVINO framework significantly enhances the inference speed of models by model optimization and compression. Our model achieves a 70% reduction in inference time compared to the baseline model on CPU. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through experiments.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Adaptive Optimal Control for Switched Nonlinear Systems with Dead Zones
abstract: This paper tackles the problem of adaptive fuzzy optimal tracking control for switched nonlinear systems with dead zones. Fuzzy Logic Systems is employed for the critic-actor architecture, where the actor and critic enforce control actions and evaluate the system's performance. Subsequently, the more straightforward optimal control design is combined with the backstepping technique, with further step-wise feed-back and adjustment by the critic-actor architecture to achieve control goals. In addition, our proposed control scheme can stabilise the nonlinear switching system, as shown in the simulation results.

articleTitle: Rotational Viscometer Remote Firmware Upgrade System Design and Implementation
abstract: The rotary viscometer is the most commonly used device for measuring viscosity, after it is used in real applications, manufacturers need to program maintenance and add new software functions to the device. This paper designs and implements a remote upgrade system for a rotational viscometer based on the message queuing telemetry transport (MQTT) protocol and WiFi module to lower maintenance costs and enhance the convenience of updating. After receiving the firmware upgrade command and reporting packet creation information, the system receives the packet sent by the Internet of Things (IoT) platform and performs cyclical redundancy check (CRC) verification. The system uses the ESP8266 module as the communication module and uses the MQTT protocol for data transmission with the IoT platform. CRC is used to confirm the accuracy and integrity of data transfer, and if the CRC checksum is consistent, the packet is written to Flash using in application programming (IAP) technology. U ndownloaded packets are continually requested by the system until all packets are written to Flash. To minimize issues brought on by upgrade failure or other errors, the system offers breakpoint continuation and program rollback features. The system has undergone several tests to ensure its reliability and serve as a guide for remote firmware upgrades of embedded devices.

articleTitle: Research on GNC Architecture of On-Orbit Servicing Aircraft
abstract: Space on-orbit service vehicles have important applications in tasks such as on-orbit maintenance, life extension and orbital debris removal of spacecraft, GNC subsystem plays an important role in the task completion process. Due to the large differences in the dynamic characteristics of the target aircraft and the requirements of the task, there are many uncertainties in the process of task completion, it needs to take into account the needs of energy security, attitude safety, anti-collision safety, etc. GNC needs to plan different task conditions according to different target characteristics. This paper defines the GNC mission architecture model of the on-orbit service vehicle, and uses software-defined technology to implement task autonomous management under various working conditions. Colleagues realize the safety of the whole vehicle in fault mode through early warning mechanism.

articleTitle: Trend Features Extraction of Apparent Resistivity in Tunnel Engineering
abstract: Troublesome incidents like sudden water inflows increase the risk of collapse accidents in tunnel excavation. In this study, a data-driven underground water prediction method is proposed based on trend features extracted from apparent resistivity. A novel framework is developed for extracting trend features from the contour lines of apparent resistivity. These trend features are subsequently integrated with numerical features from the resistivity matrix for classification. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by apparent resistivity data from real tunnel engineering. The result indicates that the classification accuracy of the proposed method outperforms the method without feature extraction.

articleTitle: Resilient Consensus of Multi-Agent Systems on Time-Varying Directed Graphs Under Byzantine Attacks and Actuation Attacks
abstract: This work deals with the distributed attack-resilient consensus problem for continuous-time multi-agent systems on time-varying directed graphs. An unknown fraction of agents are Byzantine agents, which send false information to deceive their neighbors. Moreover, each normal agent suffers from actuation attacks. In order to ensure the resilience of all normal agents against the above hybrid attacks, a new kind of edge-based protocols is formulated, which achieves resilient consensus via signed feedback. Then, the finite-time zero-error control performance of the above protocol is proven for (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2f+1$</tex>) - robust time-varying directed topologies, based on strictly Lyapunov stability analysis.

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis Method with Multivariate Data Manifold Feature Learning for Industrial Process
abstract: Industrial process operation data generally have the characteristics of high dimensionality, nonlinearity and autocorrelation, which largely affect the fault detection accuracy of the process industry and cannot guarantee the normal operation of the industrial process. The high dimensionality of industrial process operation data makes the data contain uncertainty noise and feature invariant redundant information, so in order to save computation time and improve the efficiency of fault classification and diagnosis, we need to reduce the dimensionality of the data first. The nonlinear dimensionality reduction algorithm LLE can extract the local structural features of high-dimensional industrial process data by constructing K-neighborhoods, and maintain the flow shape characteristics of high-dimensional data. Choosing different neighborhood sizes and mapping dimensions can largely affect the accuracy of fault classification and diagnosis. To solve this problem, this paper adaptively determines the K-neighborhood size for LLE construction by independent principal element analysis method, and introduces Scatter matrix evaluation rules to search the mapping dimensions with optimal classification performance in the whole variable dimensional space, and uses LLE combined with CNN network to establish fault classification diagnosis model. And the effectiveness of the proposed method is proved by simulation study and experimental comparison.

articleTitle: A Swing-Up and Stable Control Strategy for Pendubot Based on Nonlinear Model Predictive Method
abstract: The control objective of Pendubot is to stabilise the system in a vertically upward position by swinging up from a vertically downward position. Facing various physical constraints in practical applications, this paper proposes a swing-up stabil-isation control strategy based on a nonlinear model prediction method to accomplish the above control objective. On the basis of the system dynamics model, the forward Euler method is used to construct a nonlinear prediction model of the system. According to the control objectives and physical constraints of the system, the performance index function is designed, and then the control inputs of each sampling cycle are obtained through rolling optimisation and feedback correction, so that the system state gradually converges to the target trajectory, thus achieving the motion control objective. Based on the simulation results, it can be seen that the strategy proposed in this paper is efficient and robust under external disturbances.

articleTitle: Defect Detection of Substation Instrumentation Equipment Based on Improved YOLOv4 Algorithm
abstract: In response to the problems of extensive number of parameters as well as the intricate model complexity prevalent in traditional deep learning detection algorithms, and taking the faults such as broken dials, blurred dials, and broken housings of substation instrumentation equipment as the research object, this paper proposes a lightweight substation instrumentation equipment defect detection method based on YOLOv4-Mobilenetv2-S. Firstly, the Mobilenetv2 backbone network is used to replace the CSPDarknet53 in the YOLOv4 backbone feature extraction network to decrease the quantity of parameters of the model; then, the SE attention mechanism module is added to the three preliminary effective feature layers of the backbone extraction network and the PANet to scale up the information extraction capability of the feature layer; lastly, all the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3 \times 3$</tex> standard convolutions in the PANet and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \times 5$</tex> convolutions in PANet are adjusted to depth-separable convolutions to streamline the model and computation. The practical outcomes demonstrate that compared with the original YOLOv4 network, the algorithm reduces the amount of parameters of the network by 83.1% and compresses the model by 83.7% under the premise of guaranteeing the accuracy, and the average recognition time of the image reaches 13.14ms with an accuracy of 85.99%, which can address the requirements for detecting defects in substation instrumentation equipment.

articleTitle: Image Smoothing via Local Structure Variation
abstract: To address the imbalance smoothing problem in structure and texture, we propose a local structure variation-based edge-preserving image smoothing method. Firstly, the structure measure and texture measure are built using variations in the local statistics of pixel values at distinct locations. Secondly, measures are converted into regularization items. A variation smoothing model is established, and multi-smoothness images are obtained by sparse solution. Finally, a structure extraction and fusion model is developed to maintain structure and suppress texture in complicated texture images by adjusting the smoothness of different image regions. The high-quality smoothing performance of our method is confirmed by the subjective and objective experiments.

articleTitle: A Notion of Robustness for Infinite Systems with Time Delays and its Applications on Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Since signal transmission and data processing often cause state delay of systems, it is necessary to investigate the input-output dynamical stability of infinite systems with time delays. In this brief, authors apply simulation relation and algebraic state space representation methods to model infinite systems with time delays as delayed logical networks. First, robustness of finite systems with time delays is analyzed via corresponding delayed logical networks. Second, robustness of infinite systems with time delays is also analyzed via corresponding finite systems with time delays. Finally, an illustrative example about cyber-physical systems with time delays and its simulation results verify the applicability of the proposed results.

articleTitle: M2PCode——A Mathematical Kit Applied in the Pocket Lab for Engineering Education
abstract: This paper introduces a mathematical tool called M2PCode integrated in the pocket lab of M2PLab (Mathematics to Practice Laboratory) for engineering education. The M2PCode allows users to write and execute M codes in the pocket laboratory conveniently, in which case, users do not need to relay on the mathematical calculation software such as Matlab for the lightweight calculation. M2PCode proposed in this paper has the contribution of the lightweight design that enables users to perform simple math operations in the pocket laboratory and reinforces the functionality of the pocket laboratory. Besides, for the reason that M2PCode is as a stand-alone feature in the pocket laboratory of the M2PLab, the operational efficiency is determined by the hardware performance of the pocket laboratory. This paper adopts the Raspberry Pi as the hardware where the M2PLab is deployed. Based on that, the operational efficiency of M2PCode is quiet well.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-Channel Wire Resistance Tester
abstract: In this study, a multi-channel wire resistance tester is designed. Multi-channel wire resistance tester is a device used to detect and diagnose wires and cables. The resistance value of the wire can be measured by integrating the operational amplifier circuit and using the resistance voltage divider rule so that it can quickly and accurately detect various problems in the wire, such as short circuits, poor contact, broken wire, and so on. The tester has a user-friendly interface and operation, and data can be analysed and stored via the display or connected to a computer. With this tester, users can quickly and accurately assess the quality and performance of wires and improve their reliability and stability. This equipment plays an important role in the wire manufacturing, installation and maintenance process.

articleTitle: Ensemble Label Correction for Hyperspectral Image Classification
abstract: The presence of noisy labels in the training sets poses a challenge to achieving high-precision classification of hyperspectral images (HSIs). To address this issue, this paper proposes an ensemble label correction (ELC) method for HSI classification that incorporates the concept of ensemble learning into deep neural networks. Our ELC model utilizes ensembles to gradually correct determined noisy labels during training epochs. At the end of training, most wrong labels will be corrected, and the model's robustness will also be increased. In our experiments, we use convolutional neural networks to implement our ELC model. Our experiments on two real HSI datasets illustrate that the proposed approach demonstrates promising results even in the presence of label noise.

articleTitle: Vibration Signal Reconstruction Based on K-SVD and Compressed Sensing in Wireless Sensor Network
abstract: In order to tackle the significant shortage of storage and the extensive latency in transmitting substantial vibration data in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN). A refined method that integrates Compressed Sensing (CS) with K-singular Value Decomposition (K-SVD) is suggested to boost the precision of reconstruction. Firstly, CS is employed for signal sampling, which surpasses the limitation of the Nyquist sampling theorem and acquires signals from a lesser quantity of samples. Then, the Alternating Direction of the Multipliers Method (ADMM) algorithm is implemented to attain a faster convergence speed. Moreover, to enhance the adaptability of the dictionary, the K-SVD method is employed for updating the dictionary in a way that is both adaptive and segmented. Comprehensive experimen-tal outcomes show that the suggested approach exhibits superior reconstruction precision and velocity compared to alternative methods.

articleTitle: M2S2: A Policy Transfer Framework for Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has greatly promoted the progress of investigations in robotic motion planning. However, when faced with different scenarios, the path obtained from each training for a specific scenario is unique, which means that the DRL needs additional resources to relearn and adapt the policy to the new scenario. Inspired by the mentor-student relationship, a multi-mentor-single-student (M2S2) framework is proposed in this paper to enhance the policy generalization performance among similar task scenarios. It promotes the learning efficiency of the student network by adding networks that have been trained in similar scenarios as the mentor networks in the training, where weight parameters are assigned to balance the relationship among all the networks. The experimental results show that M2S2 has good feasibility and superior performance for policy transfer of DRL among similar scenarios.

articleTitle: MDCN: A Dual-Branch Model Based on Difference Convolution for Non-Intrusive Load Disaggregation
abstract: Non-intrusive load disaggregation is one of the tasks of Non-intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM), aims to disaggregate appliances power from total power. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown excellent performance in NILM due to their powerful feature representation capabilities. However, when multiple appliances are working simultaneously, CNN models exhibit performance degradation and weak generalization ability. This is because the Power Superposition (PS) of multiple appliances is similar to shadows in images, which can cause information loss and interference. We propose a new model called Mix Difference Convolutional Network (MDCN) to improve the performance when PS occurs. MDCN is based on a dual-branch structure, and it performs supervised learning on both the power sequence and the on/off sequence of the target appliance. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to existing CNN models, MDCN achieves the best performance on the REDD and UK-DALE datasets, especially when PS occurs. In addition, ablation experiments were conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed difference convolution operators.

articleTitle: In-Situ Leak Detection in Urban Water Supply Pipelines Using Flexible Vibration Sensors
abstract: The urban water supply pipeline network is an important infrastructure for the survival and development of cities, and its leak problem has long lacked efficient detection methods. Existing leak detection methods mainly have limitations in micro-leakage detection and large-scale deployment and are susceptible to environmental interference. This work presents an urban water supply pipeline leak detection method based on flexible piezoelectric sensors. The flexibility of the thin film sensor allows it to be directly attached to curved pipe walls, enabling in-situ monitoring of local leakages. The acquired vibration leakage signals are further processed, and a support vector machine (SVM) algorithm is used to classify leakage conditions to various levels with a high accuracy of more than 95%.

articleTitle: Research on Single-Section Traffic Flow Prediction Based on BiLSTM
abstract: Traffic flow prediction has always been an integral part of intelligent transportation systems, which can help decision-makers to formulate effective traffic management strategies. In this paper, the Bidirectional Long and Short Term Memory Networks is proposed to solve the problem that the prediction accuracy decreases when the prediction sequence is too long in the Long short-term memory algorithm. In terms of the selection of optimizer and parameter, this paper picks out the best optimizer and parameters by continuously adjusting the optimizer and its parameter settings, calculating the MAE value of the future first-day prediction, and comparing them in each experiment. Finally, the paper applies the BiLSTM-based single-section traffic flow prediction model to predict the sensor 0, sensor 60, and sensor 120 traffic flow data respectively, from the dataset PeMS08 of the California highway network in the United States. By comparing the prediction results of MAE, RMSE, and MAPE, we found that the BiLSTM neural network made effective improvements in the degradation of prediction accuracy when the LSTM neural network sequence is too long. Thus, the model has a better prediction performance.

articleTitle: Research on RCS Sequence Prediction Based on ARIMA-TPA-LSTM Algorithm
abstract: The existing sequence prediction algorithm is difficult to meet the requirements of prediction accuracy when dealing with complex RCS. In this paper, a coupling method is proposed to effectively combine time series algorithm and neural network to accurately predict the relationship between single station RCS and incident Angle. Based on auto regressive integrated moving average(ARIMA) algorithm, bayesian information criterion (BIC) was proposed to optimize the order of the model.Then, temporal pattern attention(TPA) mechanism that pays more attention to RCS historical information is proposed and the residual value was combined with the long short term memory algorithm(LSTM) with TPA, and the ARIMA-TPA-LSTM prediction algorithm based on BIC was proposed to improve the prediction accuracy. At the same time, simulation test is carried out. The simulation results show that the accuracy of ARIMA-TPA-LSTM prediction algorithm proposed in this paper is higher than the existing prediction algorithm on average, and it can accurately deal with complex RCS prediction problems.

articleTitle: Koopman-Operator-Based Model Predictive Control for Constrained Spacecraft Attitude Reorientation
abstract: This paper proposes an attitude controller design for spacecraft attitude reorientation with angular velocity limitations, which utilizes the Koopman operator (KO) theory and linear control predictive control (LMPC) approach. The KO theory is utilized to derive a higher-dimensional linear model, which approximates the motion equation of rest-to-rest spacecraft attitude maneuvering. An LMPC scheme is then determined through the solution of an optimization problem that minimizes a quadratic cost function over a prediction horizon while considering the KO model and transformed state constraints. Subsequently, a three-dimensional attitude controller is obtained using the least-squares approach applied to the higher-dimensional LMPC. The proposed strategy is validated through simulations, demonstratina its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Transmission Optimization Method for Wireless Sensor Networks Based on Combination Prediction and Threshold Adjustment
abstract: The limited energy of sensor nodes restricts the service life of wireless sensor networks (WSN). Transmission is the most significant factor affecting energy consumption. Therefore, optimizing transmission to reduce the energy consumption of sensor nodes is particularly important for extending the service life of WSN. This paper proposes a transmission optimization method for WSN based on combination prediction and threshold adjustment. First, a combination prediction model based on correction is constructed with the least mean square algorithm making preliminary prediction, the long short-term memory network making in-depth prediction and the echo state network making corrected prediction. Second, a threshold adjustment algorithm based on congestion control is proposed. In particular, the threshold rises quickly in the fast attempt stage, rises slowly in the slow attempt stage, and shrinks as needed in the fast startup stage. Finally, simulation results on three actual datasets of WSN show that the proposed method has the high prediction performance and low energy consumption, thus reduces the amount of transmitted data.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of High Efficiency Flat wire Motor for Electric Vehicle
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is the driving component of electric vehicle, and its performance directly determines the power performance, reliability and economy of electric vehicle. Traditional round wire motors can not meet the needs of electric vehicles in terms of high efficiency range, heat dissipation performance and automatic production. Flat wire motor gradually replaces the traditional round wire motor because of its small size, high efficiency, strong heat dissipation and low noise. However, the ac loss of winding of flat wire motor was high under the influence of skin effect at high speed. Therefore, taking 65kW motor as an example, the size design and winding optimization of flat wire permanent magnet synchronous motor are carried out. Firstly, the main dimensions of ac motor are calculated by using the basic equations of ac motor design. Secondly, the mathematical model of ac resistance of flat wire conductor was calculated by Maxwell electromagnetic field equations, and the optimization method of flat wire winding was analyzed according to the model and verified by finite element simulation. Finally, comparing the running efficiency of flat wire motor and round wire motor under the test road conditions, the influence of different cooling systems on motor temperature rise under the test road conditions was analyzed. The results show that the ac loss was the lowest when the height of flat wire conductor was the critical point, which provides a certain basis for the design of flat wire winding conductor.

articleTitle: Joint Estimation of SOC and SOH of Lithium Battery Based on Dual Multi-Innovation Adaptive Unscented Kalman Filter
abstract: With the rapid development of UAVs, the estimation algorithm for State of Charge (SOC) with strong generalization ability and high accuracy can enhance the energy management performance of the entire UAV. However, as the number of cycles increases, the SOC of a lithium battery is easily affected by aging factors, and the noise from sensors in the vehicle Battery Management System (BMS) significantly influences data acquisition. This paper addresses the issue of insufficient accuracy in SOC and State of Health (SOH) estimation. To tackle this, a dual multi-innovation adaptive Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) algorithm is proposed based on the multi-innovation theory and adaptive theory. The algorithm is compared with the Dual UKF (DUKF) and multi-innovation adaptive UKF-Extended Kalman Filter (MIAUKF-EKF) algorithms using the Urban Dynamometer Driving Schedule (UDDS). The results of the verification demonstrate that the DMIAUKF algorithm improves the accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Controllability of Finite State Machine Under Function Perturbation Based on STP
abstract: This paper mainly studies the controllability of finite state machines (FSMs) whose state was perturbed during the transition. First, the FSM is transformed into its algebraic form by using the semi-tensor product (STP) of matrices method. Under the algebraic framework, a controllability matrix is constructed to determine the controllability of the perturbed FSMs. Then necessary and sufficient controllability conditions are derived. Finally, the effectiveness of our results is shown through an illustrative example.

articleTitle: A Dead Reckoning Method Based on Martian Atmosphere Polarized Skylight and Celestial Navigation for Mars Exploration UAV
abstract: Autonomous navigation technology plays a significant role in Mars exploration unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). Focus on the problem of position error drift caused by the lack of absolute heading information, a dead reckoning method based on Martian atmosphere polarized skylight and celestial navigation is proposed. The navigation reference model of Martian atmosphere polarized skylight is analyzed first. Subsequently, the navigation system model is established to fuse the information of polarization navigation, celestial navigation, optical flow, and inertial navigation system. The Monte Carlo simulation tests show that the proposed method can provided the stable and accurate heading, and the landing accuracy of the Mars UAV is improved.

articleTitle: Online Energy-Efficient Operation of Maglev Trains Considering Regenerative Energy Utilization
abstract: Maglev trains have the advantages of low noise, good climbing ability, and low environmental impact. Several maglev lines have been put into commercial operation in China in recent years, and the issue of energy saving in maglev trains has attracted many researchers' attention. Existing research on this topic mainly focuses on offline calculation of the optimal train control strategy and rarely considers the use of regenerative braking energy between trains. This paper proposes an online rolling optimization algorithm to obtain the energy-efficient control trajectory of maglev trains according to the actual running condition. In addition, the regenerative braking energy of nearby trains is also considered to adjust the maglev train's control stage to further reduce the net traction energy consumption. The pseudospectral method is used in each prediction horizon of the rolling optimization algorithm to solve the multi-phase optimal control problem. Finally, a numerical example is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: DOR-SLAM: A Visual SLAM Based on Dynamic Object Removal for Dynamic Environments
abstract: vSALM is a system that enables precise positioning of a mobile robot in an unknown environment and generates corresponding 3D maps. However, the feature matching process of the visual odometry in the SLAM system is easily disturbed by dynamic objects in real-world scenarios, such as moving pedestri-ans and vehicles, which will reduce the accuracy of positioning and mapping. To address this issue., a visual SLAM system with dyna-mic object removal., called as Dynamic Object Removal SLAM (DOR-SLAM)., is proposed based on the ORB-SLAM2 system. Firstly., a dynamic probability calculation formula of pixels based on optical flow and semantic information has been proposed to determine the motion state of object. Then., a process of instance segmentation is used to segment the recognized dynamic objects in the image frames. Next., these dynamic objects will be removed by using a flow-guided video inpainting network., while inpainting the background. To improve system efficiency., a simplified bidirecti-onal optical flow calculation method is proposed and applied to the video inpainting network. The effectiveness of the proposed meth-od is evaluated with dynamic RGB-D sequences from the TUM dataset. The results of the experiments indicate that the proposed DOR-SLAM can improve the accuracy of localization in dynamic environments while maintaining high computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Modeling and Sectional Compensation of Temperature Error of FOG Based on Random Forest Algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the single model compensation method has poor adaptability to the temperature error of fiber optic gyroscope(FOG), a sectional compensation method for the temperature error of FOG based on random forest (RF)algorithm is proposed based on the idea of sectional modeling compensation. During modeling, factors affecting temperature and temperature changes were added, and three hyperparameters were optimized to obtain the optimal compensation model. In order to verify the compensation effect of this method, temperature experiments of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-60\ ^{\circ}\ \mathbf{C} \sim 40\ ^{\circ}\ \mathbf{C}$</tex> FOG were designed, and the temperature errors were compensated using the proposed method, least squares method, and BOA-GBDT, respectively. The comparison results indicate that the BO-RF model can greatly reduce temperature errors. Compared with traditional algorithms, the average bias value of the gyroscope is reduced by an order of magnitude, and the BO-RF segmented model has the best compensation effect.

articleTitle: Parameter-Guided Image Generation with Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
abstract: Text-to-image generation models aim to generate visual images by leveraging the rich semantic information inherent in the input text. However, existing models encounter challenges in generating satisfactory images when the input text contains a substantial amount of domain-specific parametric information. To tackle this challenge, we propose a high-detail image generation method for parameterized text inputs, named PIG-DDPM. This method builds upon the Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model(DDPM) and utilizes a weighted bag of words model to create a concise and efficient representation of paramet-ric text features. Moreover, the existing DDPM model requires powerful hardware capabilities to generate High-Definition (HD) images, which limits its practical deployment on a large scale. To address this issue, our model incorporates positional information encoding in the textual features and generates HD images by training and stitching together multiple small-sized local images. Through a series of experiments, we substantiate that our method demonstrates noteworthy advantages in terms of both image quality and clarity when compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A Layered Multi-Rate Wireless Sensor Network Data Fusion Algorithm Based on Missing Measurements
abstract: To solve the problem of low data fusion accuracy in wireless sensor networks, a hierarchical multi-rate wireless sensor network data fusion algorithm based on missing measurement is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the measured data of each sensor node is estimated by Kalman filter, then the estimated and measured values are sent to the head node for consistency analysis and weighted data fusion. Under the premise of meeting the accuracy of data fusion, an adaptive multi-rate measurement model is proposed, which can reduce the energy consumption of wireless sensors. Finally, the cluster data fusion value of the head node is sent to the sink node, and the weighted data fusion value of the cluster data fusion value from different head nodes is performed on the sink node based on consistency analysis. The validity of improved algorithm is proved by an application instance, and the results show that the data transmission volume has been reduced, and the energy consumption of the wireless sensors has been reduced.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Model for Online Prediction of Rate of Penetration (ROP) in Drilling Process
abstract: In this paper, a novel hybrid model is proposed for online prediction of rate of penetration (ROP) in drilling process, which including two parts (online data pre-processing and online hybrid modeling). In the first part, threshold filtering and Savitzky Golay (SG) filtering are both employed to enhance the quality of drilling data considering the expert experience and data characteristics. In the next part, a novel hybrid model with error compensation is established, which is combined the Bingham sub-model and gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT) sub-model. To better capture the dynamic changes of ROP, the hybrid model is updated with moving window strategy. Finally, compared simulation results with well-known ROP prediction models indicate the efficiency of the hybrid model.

articleTitle: Knowledge Distillation Based Fast Degradation Estimator For Blind Super-resolution
abstract: Blind Super Resolution aims to enhance low-resolution images to high-resolution ones without the need to initially understand the detailed information of the original low-resolution images. In recent years, Blind Super Resolution techniques have attempted to guide image super-resolution reconstruction by designing explicit degradation estimators. However, these degradation estimators often come with a large number of parameters, slow processing speed, and less-than-ideal out-comes. In this study, we introduce an improved fast degradation estimator based on knowledge distillation, enabling the rapid and effective extraction of unknown degradation information from images. This estimator further guides the Super- Resolution(SR) network in achieving image super-resolution reconstruction. Ex-perimental results indicate that our enhanced fast degradation estimator doubles its operational efficiency and achieves super-resolution reconstruction for low-resolution images affected by various degradation factors. This advancement holds the promise of delivering superior performance and results for image super-resolution reconstruction tasks.

articleTitle: Intrinsic Dimension Estimation of Iudustrial Surface Defect Data and Its Impact on Classification
abstract: In today's era of rapid development of artificial intelligence, machine vision technology based on deep learning is widely used. In this paper, the intrinsic dimension estimation of industrial defect data and its impact on classification and generalization are studied based on machine vision in the detection of industrial defects. In this work, Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) algorithm is used to estimate the intrinsic dimensions of three common industrial defect data, and to verify the influence of the intrinsic dimensions on sample complexity and classification.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Networks for Chemical Process Fault Diagnosis Based on Hybrid Variable Feature Learning
abstract: Graph-based data representation allows us to take into account not only the behavior of each sensor signal but also the correlations and hidden relationships between them. Therefore, using graph neural networks can achieve better results in fault diagnosis. However previous fault detection methods tend to focus only on continuous variables, but industrial processes usually contain both continuous and discrete variables. To utilize this information, we propose a method named graph neural networks for fault diagnosis based on hybrid variable feature learning (HV-GNN). The method continuous discrete variables through a self-attention mechanism and then feeds them into the graph neural network as nodes along with continuous variables for fault diagnosis. Simulation experiments were conducted on an industrial coal gasification process platform and satisfactory results were achieved. Comparative experiments have shown that HV-GNN improves trouhlcshooting accuracy.

articleTitle: Interval Prediction of Lithium-Ion Battery Health State Based on Charging Feature Fusion and LSTMQR
abstract: In this paper, an interval prediction model of health state for lithium-ion battery is proposed, which is based on the fusion of multiple health indicators. Firstly, 12 HIs were extracted from the current and voltage variables of the charging process. Secondly, feature selection is performed by random forest (RF) training and the selected HIs are dimensioned using partial least squares (PLS). Finally, a long short-term memory network (LSTM) combined with quantile regression (QR) was used to derive the quantile values of the prediction points and each quantile was used as input information for Gaussian kernel density estimation (KDE) to get the SOH probability density distribution. The simulation results show that the SOH interval coverage is not less than 90% and the average width of the interval is not greater than 0.2941.

articleTitle: Rationality Evaluation of Transmission Line Planning Based on Combination Weighting Method and Cloud Gravity Center Evaluation Method
abstract: An evaluation method of transmission line planning rationality based on combination weighting method and cloud center of gravity evaluation method is proposed. The method first uses principal component analysis and analytic hierarchy process to solve the weight values of its assessment indexes; And the weighted deviation degree is used to measure the degree of the system state change, so as to determine its reasonableness level. Through cloud modeling, a mathematical model that can deal with uncertainty and stochasticity want to combine stochasticity and random numbers to be able to better reflect the reality of complex systems. Therefore the cloud-centered method can better integrate the ambiguity and randomness in the assessment information and ensure the scientificity of each weighting result. The experimental results show that the proposed state evaluation method based on combination weighting method and cloud gravity center evaluation method can effectively evaluate the rationality of transmission lines.

articleTitle: Encapsulated chip carrier missing assembly detection network based on sliding window affinity
abstract: Aiming at the problems of encapsulated chip carrier (ECC) missing detection, such as similar color texture between missing area and background, small difference between ECC pixels, and insufficient missing samples in actual production, an ECC missing detection network based on sliding window affinity (SWA) is proposed. Firstly, the data augmentation method of fast region transformation is used to expand the defect samples to eliminate the problem of class imbalance. Secondly, based on the local window affinity, the affinity map is calculated to strengthen the internal relationship between pixels, and the multi-scale feature fusion is used to enhance the defect features. Finally, on the ECC missing assembly detection dataset, 73.8 % of the mAP is achieved, which meets the actual production requirements.

articleTitle: Modeling Safe and Smooth Car-Following Behavior: An LSTM-Attention Based TD3 Approach
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is an effective and popular way to study car-following behavior due to its ability to deal with complex and dynamic environment. However, the performance of DRL based car-following models is degraded by inadequate network structure and unreasonable reward function design. In order to solve this issue, this study creatively proposes a car-following model which incorporates the long short-term memory (LSTM) network and the attention mechanism into the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradients (TD3) architecture. In our model, the historical driving information is considered to simulate the memory effect of human drivers. Additionally, to reduce the risk of rear-end collisions, a new safety-oriented driving feature is designed and integrated into the reward function. The experimental results reveal that our model can effectively speed up model convergence, while also obtaining the optimal results with the consideration of driving safety, efficiency, and comfort.

articleTitle: Research on Hammerstein Modeling of a Giant Magnetostrictive Actuator
abstract: The giant magnetostrictive actuator (GMA) is an intelligent actuator that utilizes magnetostrictive material as its core, renowned for its exceptional performance, making it extensively employed across various industries. Therefore, the modeling of hysteresis nonlinearity has been the focus of this field. The asymmetric PrandtI-Ishlinskii (PI) model, based on the Hammerstein structure, is employed to represent the nonlinear links within the system. Additionally, for capturing dynamic links in the Hammerstein structure, particularly those associated with high frequency signals, a second-order transfer function is utilized. Determine the model coefficients using the system toolbox. Finally, the developed dynamic rate-dependent hysteresis model is validated by an experimental platform. It is concluded that the asymmetric PI model with Hammerstein structure has higher accuracy, especially for larger frequency excitation signals.

articleTitle: New Double Loop Control Strategy for DC Motor Position Servo System
abstract: To enhance the tracking and disturbance resistance of the DC position servo system, a dual closed-loop control system is formulated, incorporating nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode (NFTSM) for the position controller and fuzzy internal model PID (FIMPID) for the speed controller. The position controller utilizes nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control to advance tracking performance. The speed controller employs fuzzy internal model PID, employing fuzzy principles for online adjustment of internal model PID controller parameters to enhance system robustness. Finally, the simulation and experimental results confirm the efficacy of the NFTSM-FIMPID control algorithm in achieving superior control performance for the DC position servo system.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Density Modeling and Updating for Autonomous Navigation During Mars Aerocapture
abstract: The uncertainty of atmospheric density during Mars aerocapture is investigated. The atmospheric density of Mars is modeled as a Gaussian Random Field, and it is truncated using Karhunen-Loève Expansion. To enable real-time updating of the atmospheric density model, a low-Rank Kalman Filter algorithm is introduced, which directly updates the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the Mars atmospheric density covariance matrix, avoiding the issue of high dimensionality. Finally, the updated atmospheric density is incorporated into the Unscented Kalman Filter for spacecraft navigation. Simulation results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Wind Power Prediction Based on Hybrid Neural Network and Wind Power Curve
abstract: In this paper, The traditional Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) can predict the time series data. However, there is always a certain deviation between the predicted value and the real value. In this paper, a hybrid neural network model consisting of attention mechanism (AM), convolutional neural network (CNN) and long and short memory network is constructed by using wind power curve. The experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement of the proposed model over traditional neural networks, particularly the traditional RNN network such as LSTM and CNN through the performance evaluation index parameters MAE and MSE, and the method has higher wind power prediction accuracy and smaller error value.

articleTitle: Study on Optimal Control Strategy of Urban Traffic Network Based on Minimum Emission
abstract: In this paper, an optimal control strategy is proposed aiming to minimize the traffic emission in urban road network. Car-following model embedded into VISSIM was analyzed and the total emissions was calculated in the traffic network through the call of VISSIM-COM interface. The calculated emission was converted into the fitness function value in the algorithm under the combination of VISSIM and VS environment. The optimal signal timing of each intersection and phase offset between each twin intersection in network was optimized through an improved annealing genetic algorithm. The simulation was conducted to verify the optimal model and the results show that the optimal control strategy is valid and the improved simulated annealing genetic algorithm can effectively solve the signal parameters in road network.

articleTitle: Research on Model-Based Thermal Updraft State Estimation Method
abstract: This paper proposes a pitching moment model for UAVs in a thermal updraft field based on the Gaussian distribution model of thermal updraft. The model can be applied to the positioning and tracking of environmental thermal updrafts using a state estimation algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to a single thermal updraft model or a UAV thermal updraft field rolling moment model, the algorithm's convergence speed and accuracy in locating the thermal center are significantly improved by introducing the UAV pitching moment model in thermal updraft state estimation.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Modeling and Vibration Reduction and Absorption of Superconducting Electrodynamic Suspension System
abstract: Superconducting electrodynamic suspension (EDS) technology is one of the important technologies of the future ultra-high speed maglev propulsion system, which can be applied to the ultra-high speed maglev vehicle and rocket (electromagnetic) sled at a speed of more than 600km/h. However, the study on the EDS system is still in its infancy, and in the practical application of engineering, the existence of passive electromagnetic force leads to the problem of vibration divergence of suspended vehicle body. It is found that the damping characteristics of the EDS system can not meet the practical needs. And whether the damping problem can be solved is the key factor for the stable operation of the suspension system. Therefore, the suspension vehicle body of EDS system is taken as the research object, and its dynamic modeling is carried out to analyze its motion characteristics. Finally, a method of damping and absorbing vibration is designed. Simulation results show that the proposed method can make the vibration of the suspended vehicle body converge. The research of this paper will provide an important basis for the development and practical application of EDS technology.

articleTitle: Adaptive Local Stereo Matching Based on Improved Census Transform
abstract: The local stereo matching algorithm based on traditional census transform has some problems, such as over-reliance on the center pixel, fixed transform window and poor matching effect in weak texture region. An improved census transform stereo matching algorithm combined with adaptive window is proposed. Firstly, according to the mean square error of pixel gray level in the initial transformation window, the size of the transformation window is adjusted. Secondly, the census transform is improved and combined with the improved AD algorithm to form the initial matching cost; Then, the cost aggregation adopts the cross domain algorithm; Finally, the winner-take-all algorithm and multi-step optimization are used to obtain disparity map. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm has good anti-interference performance against noise. By evaluating the standard images on Middlebury dataset, the average error of this method is reduced by 7.05<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> compared with the traditional census transform stereo matching algorithm.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of Finite-field Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the parameter identification problem of finite-field networks (FFNs). Firstly, an algebraic expression of FFNs is obtained by the technique of semi-tensor product, and then, the identification issue is converted into identifying the parameter matrices of linear system. Secondly, the forward and backward probability and their properties are addressed to facilitate the parameter identification procedure. Thirdly, the expectation maximization (EM) algorithm is proposed as an elaborate technique for parameter identification problem in FFNs. In addition, an useful index is introduced to describe the performance of network parameter identification. Finally, a typical example is employed to demonstrate the reliability of the proposed parameter identification approach.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Model of Tubular Permanent Magnet Synchronous Linear Motor Based on Deep Transfer Neural Network
abstract: During high-speed operation, tubular permanent magnet linear motors with slotted stators often experience large fluctuations in thrust, overheating of the coils and irreversible demagnetization of the permanent magnets. For the first two cases, this paper proposes a deep transfer neural network (DTNN)-based electromagnetic field model for TPMLM, the specific implementation steps of which include: (1) Using different geometric parameters of TPMLM as input and average thrust, thrust fluctuation and coil copper loss as output, finite element analysis (FEA) and analytical method (AM) are used to provide the electromagnetic parameter dataset of the motor respectively, and these two datasets are used as the source and target domains for transfer learning; (2) Based on the features of the sample dataset, the source tasks corresponding to the source domain are pre-trained using DTNN, and the target tasks corresponding to the target domain are fitted by fine-tuning the model parameters. Then, in order to verify the accuracy of the proposed model, this paper compares the output prediction results with some non-parametric models, such as Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Deep Neural Network (DNN), by dividing the target domain dataset with different scales. The results show that the best prediction results are obtained from the DTNN model, which fully combines the accuracy of FEA and the efficiency of AM, and shows better generalization ability in the case of insufficient real training data.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Formation Control for Multi-UAV Systems: A Saturated-Input Approach
abstract: Due to the limitation of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle(UAV)'s maximum velocity/acceleration, its control input needs to satisfy the saturation constraint. In this paper, we study the formation control problem for discrete-time multi-UAV systems with input saturation constraints. A hierarchical formation control law is constructed based on the flocking behaviour of birds that follows the head bird. This control law is shown to achieve system convergence when the communication topology graph contains a spanning tree rooted at the leader UAV and each UAV is asymptotically null controllable with bounded controls. Simulation results verify the validity of the theory.

articleTitle: Two-DOF H∞ Robust Controller Design for Radio Telescope Servo System
abstract: The pointing accuracy of radio telescope is affected by external disturbances. Additionally, the antenna's dynamic characteristics change with different working conditions due to the influence of gravity. To improve the radio telescope servo system's anti-disturbance and robust tracking performances, this paper proposed a two-degree-of-freedom (2DOF) H_inf robust controller. This controller is designed using the H_inf optimization procedure in a single step. The feedback controller designed, based on the loop shaping, is used to guarantee disturbance suppression performance and robust stability. A prefilter is employed to improve the robust model-matching properties of the closed-loop system. To verify the effectiveness of the control algorithm, a PI controller and the proposed controller are designed for the Nanshan 26m radio telescope (NSRT) servo system. Simulation results show that compared with the PI controller, the 2DOF controller can further improve both the tracking performance and anti-disturbance performance. Furthermore, the controller designed for the nominal model satisfies the robust tracking performance and disturbance rejection performance for the radio telescope working in any condition.

articleTitle: Dynamic Data Reconciliation for Improving the Forecasting Performance of Wind Power based on Long Short-term Memory
abstract: As one of the most promising power generation methods, effective forecast of wind power generation for uncertain environment contributes to the planning and operation of power systems. In this work, the long short-term memory (LSTM) network is developed for wind power forecasting. Then, a dynamic data reconciliation (DDR) method is proposed for suppressing sensor noise and improve the forecasting performance. LSTM extends the recurrent neural networks (RNN) through gate functions, which is a popular RNN variant with state memory. However, the modeling datasets with Gaussian (or non-Gaussian) sensor noise may degrade the expected performance of LSTM. The proposed DDR performs Bayesian estimation of the real information by extracting useful parts of the two process-related information, and the relatively accurate data obtained from DDR is used to improve the accuracy of modeling. Experimental results verify that the LSTM model with DDR is less affected by Gaussian or non-Gaussian sensor noise, showing a better wind power forecasting performance.

articleTitle: Detection of Pulmonary Nodules in CT Images Based on 3D Multi-Scale Retina Vnet
abstract: Currently, one of the most common and lethal malignancy is lung cancer, the early diagnosis and treatment of which are critical for prognoses and improving the survival rates of patients. Pulmonary nodules are the symptoms of lung cancer. And clinical distinguish between benign and malignant nodules is measuring their volumes and forms after segmentation. However, it is very inefficient to perform lung nodule segmentation by conventional manual methods. In this paper, a lung nodule identification system based on Retina VNet is suggested. The network inherits the structure of the original VNet while introducing Retina Net to extract multi-scale features of pulmonary nodule images. A deep supervision technique is also used for feature tuning, which may significantly increase the model's detection performance. The LIDC-IDRI lung nodule public dataset is used to assess the model's performance in this research. Results showed that the method proposed in this article is superior to the existing detection methods in lung nodule detection performance (especially in detection of lung nodules of various sizes). Average Precision can reach up to 88.7%.

articleTitle: Metro Passenger Flow Prediction Model Based on WT Transformer Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, we propose a deep learning neural network model WTransformer for multi-feature fusion input, which combines the Transformer model with multi-feature fusion input to capture the spatial and temporal characteristics of traffic data. The model couples weather, temperature and other relevant external factors to improve the overall prediction performance and enhance the stability of the model. In this paper, the model performance is validated using Nanjing Metro Line 1 and total metro passenger traffic data combined with Valid Loss, MSE, MAE, etc. The comparison results show that compared with typical forecasting models (LSTM, TransAD, etc.), the improved model WTransformer has higher prediction accuracy and stronger ability to predict the peak of metro passenger traffic.

articleTitle: Localization Method of Partial Discharge Based on 3D Sensor Array
abstract: In this paper, a method for optical localization of discharge sources based on a multi-normal photoelectric array is proposed. The core idea is to use the response of the photoelectric sensor to the ionizing light signal emitted by the partial discharge to achieve angular localization. The main analysis and synthesis steps include: firstly, testing the sensitivity of the photoelectric sensor to capture the discharge light signal; secondly, analyzing the principle of light source tracing based on the normal vector of the 3-dimensional sensor and giving the calculation steps of angular localization based on the proportional response; then, giving the cooperative localization method based on multiple normal vectors to improve the accuracy of light source localization. Finally, the validity of these obtained results is verified by a simple experiment test.

articleTitle: Offset-Free Data-Driven Model Predictive Control: Application for Aero-Engine Speed Control
abstract: This paper provides a data-driven model prediction control scheme for the unknown linear system. In order to remove the offset caused by the disturbance, we establish an uncertain model of external disturbances and connect this uncertainty model in series with the controlled plant. This scheme is based on the theory of behavior-based systems and utilizes offline input-output trajectories to describe the system dynamics and predict the behavior of controlled plants without prior knowledge of it. The effectiveness of the presented approach is proved with a numerical example which uses a commercial turbofan engine as the controlled plant on the Matlab.

articleTitle: Infrared Video Data Cleaning Based on LightWeight CNN-LSTM
abstract: Video cleaning is a pivotal technology for enhancing the quality of infrared video data. In order to achieve high-quality cleaning of infrared video data, the temporal correlation features in the video data are thoroughly taken into account. A feature extraction model is designed. This model integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM). It can extract infrared video features in both spatial dimension and temporal dimension. Considering the characteristics of low resolution and weak feature information in infrared video images, a lightweight strategy is adopted to achieve high-quality extraction of weak information in infrared images. In this paper, an infrared video data cleaning model lightweight CNN-LSTM is developed by incorporating a lightweight strategy and video spatiotemporal features. Through seven experimental comparisons, the model utilized in this study achieved improvement ranges of 0.6% to 43.8% in accuracy and 0.7% to 65.7% in recall.

articleTitle: A PEM Fuel Cell EIS Frequency Selection Method Based on Neural Network Gradient
abstract: The extensive commercialization of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) remains constrained by issues pertaining to their reliability and durability. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) has proven to be a valuable tool for assessing the health states of FCs. Nevertheless, the collection of EIS data is time-intensive, thus impeding the practical application of EIS-based methods. Consequently, in this study, we present a novel approach involving a deep learning-based Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) parameter estimation network, alongside a corresponding frequency selection strategy. The proposed method aims to reduce the time required for EIS data measurement by eliminating redundant frequency points in the EIS test frequencies, based on the requirements of ECM parameter prediction. This method ensures that the chosen frequency points remain sufficient to facilitate accurate predictions by the parameter estimation network. Specifically, a deep learning-based parameter estimation network is designed to directly predict ECM parameters from EIS measurements. The back-propagation gradients of this network are leveraged to quantify the influence of each frequency point on the prediction of ECM parameters. By solving the integer programming problem, the optimal frequency selection solution could be obtained. Finally, the experiments are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of each component in the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Research and Design of O&M Audit System Based on Commercial Cryptography Technology
abstract: Application and security evaluation of commercial passwords run through entire lifecycle of information systems., including development process, online maintenance, abandonment and deactivation. Operation and maintenance audit is one of the key systems. The current situation and problems of commercial password application of operation and maintenance audit system was analyzed, which was based on the understanding of “Information security technology - Baseline for information system cryptography application” (GB/T 39786–2021). A secure operation and audit system based on commercial cryptographic technology was research in the paper, and the implementation methods, application prospects of the system were also introduced.

articleTitle: N Free Control Moves Based MPC for Trajectory Tracking of Autonomous Vehicle with External Disturbances
abstract: This paper designs a new trajectory tracking model predictive controller for autonomous vehicle with external disturbances. Firstly, a linear error model is established to estimate the dynamic behavior of the vehicle system. Then, a model predictive controller is formulated, which involves the N free control moves to obtain better control performance. Finally, the quadratic boundedness theorem is used to ensure the stability of the vehicle system with external bounded disturbances, and the controller design problem is resolved using linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) technique. The results on Carsim/MATLAB co-simulation platform demonstrate that the controller has ideal control accuracy and desirable robustness.

articleTitle: Barrier Analysis of the Two-Deadline Game
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth study on the dead-line differential game, which is a fundamental type within qualitative differential games. Challenges exist in the research, primarily due to the complexity of the Retrograde Path Equations (RPEs) in the two-deadline game, often preventing the determination of the barrier's analytical form. To address this problem, we introduce a novel method using decomposition. We decompose the entire game into two subgames, apply Isaacs's approach to construct the barriers for each subgame individually, and then obtain the complete barrier of the entire game. In the two-dimensional space, this paper discusses the variations in the barriers and capture regions as the distance between the pursuer's position and the positions of the two deadlines changes. We have validated the methods and conclusions through a series of examples, demonstrating their effectiveness. This research offers new insights into the theoretical study of deadline games, providing more strategic choices for decision-makers in practical applications.

articleTitle: Energy Cost Analysis for Optimally Controlling Structural Brain Networks
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of energy cost in controlling brain networks, in which the difficulty of achieving brain state transitions is quantified from the perspective of energy cost. Among them, we utilize the controllability Gramian matrix, an energy related controllability metric. We estimate a new upper bound on the minimum eigenvalue of the controllability Gramian matrix to obtain the relationship between the control energy and the number of control nodes. Simulation examples of brain networks verify the validity of the results. The results can provide a useful tool to characterize the energy cost of controlling brain networks and make predictions about the energy required to complete different control tasks of brain networks, thus providing potential theoretical support for regulatory interventions in many brain diseases, such as Schizophrenia, Parkinsons Disease, Alzheimer's Disease (AD), and so on.

articleTitle: Risk Propagation Analysis of Complex Manufacturing System Based on Virus Propagation Model
abstract: In complex manufacturing systems, the risk propagation will cause the performence of system production to decline, or even interrupt. To ensure stable production of complex manufacturing system under risk conditions, attention must be paid to key resource nodes. This paper proposes a new network node identification indicator and applies it to the identification of key equipment in complex manufacturing systems. First, the manufacturing network model is constructed based on actual data from Bosch's production line. Then, in aspect of the limitations of traditional nodes indentification indicators, a node indentification indicator combining entropy theory and node deletion method is proposed, and SI virus propagation model is selected as the risk propagation model based on the characteristics of main risks of complex manufacturing systems. At last, combining the manufacturing network model and risk propagation model, the key resourse nodes are chosen as risk source nodes to conduct simulation experiments based on various identification indicators. The simulation results show that compared with the traditional evaluation index, the node indentification indicators proposed in this paper can indentify the key eauipments in the manufacturing system more accurately.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Attention GCN Network for Body-Hand Gesture Recognition
abstract: In this paper, we propose a hierarchical attention GCN network for body-hand gesture recognition that consists of three components. Part A: Body-Hand Skeleton Capture, which captures both body and hand skeleton data simultaneously; Part B: Spatial GCN for Hand Gesture, which recognizes static hand gestures, to obtain the motion parameters of the control; Part C: Multi-Attention GCN is embedded with three dimensions: channel, time, and graph spatial, respectively, to accurately identify dynamic body gestures and obtain the motion mode of the control. The information obtained from parts A and B are combined to obtain the complete control command. The final rich experiments were conducted on two public datasets, which showed that our proposed method achieves effective control of the UAV with significant advantages over advanced methods.

articleTitle: SD-SLAM: Visual SLAM Combining Semantic Segmentation and Dynamic Feature Point Detection
abstract: Most classical visual simultaneous localization and mapping (VSLAM) algorithms were researched on the basis of static scenarios. However, in the actual application environment, there are always some dynamic objects. Accordingly, a novel SLAM scheme based on semantic discrimination and improved dynamic feature point detection (SD-SLAM) is proposed which can achieve real-time localization and mapping via integrating the semantic thread and the corresponding semantic optimization thread. To be noted that the semantic thread and the localization thread are processed simultaneously and the localization thread does not need to await for semantic thread. In addition, the static feature point is taken usage for point cloud mapping and the non-prior dynamic feature point is adopted for dynamic feature detection condition.
