The extensive experiments for SD-SLAM on TUM benchmark dataset implies that the SD-SLAM achieves an improvement of 10.2% to 19.38% on absolute trajectory error and a decrease of 17.67<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on localization calculation time consumption for each frame, compared with SD-SLAM.

articleTitle: Chipless RFID Humidity Sensor Based on Rectangular-Stub-Loaded SRR
abstract: A chipless RFID humidity sensor based on a rectangular-stub-loaded SRR is proposed to solve the problems of considerable size, complex computing circuit, high cost, dependence on the power supply, and limited lifetime of conventional humidity sensors. The resonant unit of this sensor is improved by loading the rectangular stub at the opening of the open rectangular ring, which has a high-quality factor and good resonance characteristics. Changes in ambient humidity affect the polyvinyl alcohol (PV A) material layer coated on the surface of the sensing unit, which in turn changes the resonant frequency of the sensing unit and ultimately realizes humidity sensing. The hybrid coding technology of frequency position and amplitude modulation is used in the coding, and the coding unit consisting of five resonant units is capable of coding 10 bits of identity information, which significantly improves the coding capacity of the sensor and further miniaturizes the sensor. The dimensions of the sensor are 19x52x0.762mm3. Under the experimental environment of 50%-80% relative humidity, the operating band of the sensor is 3.54~4.95GHz, and the average moisture sensitivity reaches 6.6MHz/%RH.

articleTitle: YOLOv7-Based Real-Time Detection in Production Workshop Scenarios
abstract: Safety helmets and work clothes and other safety equipment are of great significance for ensuring the safety of workers. In view of the complex problems of the construction site scene, this paper proposes a real-time detection algorithm for the production workshop scene based on improved YOLOv7. First, the Dyhead module is added to the Head part of the network architecture, and the multi-head self-attention mechanism is coordinatedly combined in the scale-aware feature layer, the spatial-aware spatial position and the taskaware output channel. Then, the convolution kernel in the main network is replaced with CoordCov, and the input coordinate information is added to the input feature map of the network as an additional channel to help the network learn to process spatial-related information. The experimental results show that compared with the original model, the mAP of the improved model is increased by 1.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, Recall is increased by nearly 1%, precision is increased by 1.43%, and the improved model can effectively improve the detection performance of workers' safety equipment in the construction site scene.

articleTitle: RSD: A Safety Decision-Making Algorithm Under Cyber Attacks for Natural Disaster Monitoring
abstract: As global temperatures increase, forest fires have increased in frequency and size. The multi-robot system can monitor the fire spread trend in real-time and provide effective information for the global decision-making center. Furthermore, attackers may prevent some robots from making optimal decisions. Therefore, this paper studies the multi-robot cooperative forest fire monitoring problem under cyber attacks, where each robot has the ability to make autonomous decisions. First, the forest fire monitoring problem is considered as a maximum area coverage problem, and the single-step actions of each robot are selected based on the principle of maximizing the submodular function. Based on this, this paper proposes a robust decision-making algorithm that can minimize the attacker's influence on the decision, even in the worst case. Finally, the simulation results verify that the proposed algorithm can achieve maximum forest fire monitoring.

articleTitle: Knowledge Based Nested Frames of Discernment for Target Integrated Identification
abstract: In the context of multiple attributive classification, different frames of discernment (FoD) are often used to address discrepant identity attribute identification for the same target. Though these frames based on different tasks and purposes employ distinct perspectives and structures to identify targets, they exhibit complementary information mapping and transformation modes, revealing nested relationships among multiple FoD. Leveraging this relationship, we can expand the information source of a single FoD and enhance the decision accuracy of integrated target identification. However, the classification results obtained from multiple FoD remain uncertain due to the unknown sensor error in the transformation relation and the randomness of information acquisition. Therefore, this paper aims to develop a integrated identification algorithm for traffic targets based on the transformation relation of nested frames of discernment (NFoD), and construct nested frames transformation matrix and basic belief assignment (BBA) mapping rules using domain rule knowledge and historical data. The nested frame mapping results are obtained by minimizing target distance transformation optimization and calculating the transformation matrix, and the original belief assignment is fused to realize effective transformation between multiple FoD. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can obtain more accurate results compared to the single FoD, which effectively confirms that the transformation fusion method utilizing the NFoD can improve the capability of the integrated target identification system.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Manipulator Handling System with Five Degrees of Freedom
abstract: with the extensive use of intelligent robots and the development and innovation of robots, intelligent robots have promoted the innovative development of manipulators, and manipulators used in various occasions are the focus of current research. This paper designs an automatic handling manipulator system with five degrees of freedom, which can carry objects in three-dimensional space, and has the characteristics of simple structure and low cost. Through experimental verification and data analysis, the manipulator can accurately carry objects at all points, which verifies the stability and feasibility of the manipulator designed in this paper. The automatic handling manipulator can be used in small enterprises, non-standard enterprises and other automatic handling applications, and provides an efficient and feasible application research basic scheme for automatic handling.

articleTitle: An Acceleration Method of Data Table Parsing and Database Sorting Based on Mask Calculation
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence and big data has put forward a higher requirements for database performance. As one of the basic operations of database, the sorting based on CPU operation cannot meet the requirements. Therefore, a heterogeneous sorting method combining CPU and FPGA has been developed. However, these methods only sort the fixed format data, and are not optimized for the storage format of the database, so it is difficult to apply to the database directly. Aiming at the above problems, this paper proposes an acceleration method of data table parsing and database sorting based on mask calculation. This method combines the parsing of the data table with the sorting operation by calculating the mask, which saves the time of parsing the data table, simplifies the control logic, and improves the sorting efficiency. Moreover, the dynamic reconfiguration of FPGA supports the multi-mode deployment of the kernel in space and time. Experimental results show that compared with software sorting method, the proposed method has a speedup of 25.1 for single-field sorting and 27.4 for multi-field sorting. In addition, the proposed method has a higher speedup and fewer hardware resource usage than the separate data table parsing and FPGA sorting method.

articleTitle: Combined Model-Compensated And Quasi-Resonant Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control For PMSM Drives
abstract: When operating at ultra-low speeds, Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is subject to disturbances such as non-linear frictional torque and periodic disturbance torque. These uncertain disturbances can cause fluctuations in speed, which deteriorate the speed loop performance. To address the problem, this paper proposed a linear active disturbance rejection control strategy (LADRC) that combined model-compensation and quasi-resonant control. The Stribeck model was chosen to estimate the non-linear frictional torque and input it into the linear expanding state observer (LESO) to reduce the estimation burden of LESO; The introduction of a quasi-resonant term (QR) in LESO improves the suppression of periodic harmonics in the mid-frequency band by linear active disturbance rejection control. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: The Binary Beetle Antennae Search Algorithm for Sparse Filter Design
abstract: Sparse filter has attracted much attention in the field of signal processing and communication due to its low complexity. However, the sparse optimization problem has non-convex characteristics, which leads to difficulty in solving. A heuristic binary beetle antennae search (BBAS) algorithm is proposed in this paper, which imitates the foraging process of beetle and uses the principle of which beetle uses antennae to detect direction, and finally achieve the purpose of searching the optimal encoding. Encoding vector is introduced to indirectly select filter coefficients, and the sparse solution of filter is obtained by searching the optimal encoding. In each iteration of the algorithm, the synthesized candidate encoding is divided into O-region and 1-region, and the values of encoding elements related to the current iteration are determined by comparing the overall fitness of the two regions. The length of antennae in the algorithm represents the number of elements in the encoding vector that the algorithm can perceive. The larger the antennae length is, the better the global search effect is., but it also means a higher amount of computation. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce the number of non-zero coefficients of the filter.

articleTitle: Research on Occupation Strategy of Unmanned Surface Vehicles Considering the Constraint of Bow Turning Characteristics
abstract: In the process of multiple unmanned surface vehicles formation navigation, when the task changes, it is necessary to drive the following ship to change back to the expected position of the leader ship, so that the multiple unmanned surface vehicles can maintain the set formation and continue to carry out the task. Aiming at the problem of formation control of leader-following unmanned surface vehicles, this paper focuses on the influence of the bow turning characteristics of USVs on the trajectory in the process of changing the position. By constructing the speed equation and the position equation, this paper solves the change of the bow turning characteristics of USV s on the track, which provides a reference for practical engineering. On basis of simulation, it can be seen that the method of this paper owns good effect on the changing of occupation position. It can accurately reflect the impact of turning characteristics on the tracks of the leader ship and the following ship under different initial heading angles and initial positions.

articleTitle: Prediction-Assisted Task Offloading and Resource Allocation in Two-Tier Mobile-Edge Computing Network Based on LSTM
abstract: This work explores how to leverage the historical information of the system to assist decision-making in task offloading and resource allocation problem. The objective is to achieve higher network computing rates and lower cloud-edge service costs while subjecting to the conditions of stable task queues and power constraints. Initially, an algorithm without predictive assistance is briefly introduced. However, it cannot utilize predictive information. Subsequently, a multi-frame optimization problem was constructed to leverage predictive information provided by the long short-term memory model, and heuristic information was provided by the pretrained neural network from the algorithm without predictive assistance. We employed a heuristic search algorithm to search for solutions that are better than those obtained by the non-predictive auxiliary algorithm. Finally, numerical simulations demonstrate that the predictive algorithm performs better to a certain extent when dealing with randomly generated information that exhibits strong temporal characteristics.

articleTitle: An Optimization of SMOTE for Anomaly Detection Based on High Contribution Sample Screening
abstract: Detecting anomalies with high accuracy for data with imbalanced class distribution is an important goal for many real-world applications. The imbalance between the normal and the abnormal classes is the main challenge of anomaly detection, which is traditionally addressed by the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Techniques (SMOTE). In this paper, a new High-Contribution SMOTE is proposed to overcome the original SMOTE's limitation of not considering the high contribution from the boundary data for anomaly detection. First, the set of high-contribution samples is screened with a classifier constructed by the generated Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves, consisting of some minority class samples that are prone to misclassification. Then, these high-contribution samples are used to synthesize new minority class samples, different from the randomly selected samples in the original SMOTE. This new idea enhances the contribution of the boundary data and obtains a data distribution closer to the true picture, which is expected to significantly improve the performance of anomaly detection. Finally, comparison experiments with the Original SMOTE and the Borderline SMOTE are carried out, and the results show that the High-Contribution SMOTE proposed in this paper obtains the higher Recall Score and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{F}_{\mathbf{1}}$</tex> Score.

articleTitle: Pavement Pothole Detection Algorithm based on GCS-YOLOv5s
abstract: Road safety is crucial for people's normal driving, and potholes on the road surface will greatly reduce the comfort of people's traveling if they are not maintained in time. Due to the pothole target scale changes, complex background, and the existence of some small target potholes are difficult to detect, this paper introduces a GCS-YOLOv5s network model, derived from YOLOv5s, designed for the detection of road potholes. Firstly, this paper introduces the GFPN structure to reconstruct the neck part of YOLOv5s, effectively addressing the challenge posed by significant changes in target scale. Secondly, the paper presents the incorporation of the Coordinate Attention (CA) module into the backbone network as a means to improve the receptive field, thereby strengthening the model's precise localization capability for target potholes. Finally, we introduce the Soft-NMS algorithm instead of the NMS algorithm in the original YOLOv5s as a way to minimize the problem of missed detection of dense potholes. The experimental results indicate that GCS-YOLOv5s, as proposed, attains a Mean Average Precision (mAP) of 80.2% on the pothole test datasets. This represents a notable improvement of 2.8% over the baseline YOLOv5s model, showcasing a substantial enhancement in detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Cooperative Tracking of Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems Under DoS Attacks
abstract: The focus of this research is on the cooperative tracking of second-order nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) subjected to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. For reducing the influence of DoS attacks, a distributed secure strategy with state compensation is proposed. Firstly, the state compensation is designed to replace the combined states during the attack period. Meanwhile, sufficient conditions associated with the frequency and the length rate of DoS attacks are obtained to assure that the system is controllable. Lastly, the efficacy of the decentralized protocol is validated by a numerical experiment.

articleTitle: Adaptive Radial Basis Function-Based Sliding Mode Control for Platoons Under Multiple Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the homogeneous platoon control problem under multiple cyber attacks. Cyber attacks can lead to collisions or degradations to the vehicle platoons. To deal with this problem, an adaptive Radial Basis Function (RBF) sliding mode control method is designed for the attacked vehicle platoons. Then design the adaptive sliding mode controllers to achieve the control objective: the spacing error converges to zero, and the platoon maintains the string stability. Using RBF neural networks to approximate the unknown acceleration information when the platoons are attacked by False Data Injection (FDI) attacks. The adaptive control law is derived according to Lyapunov stability law. Sufficient conditions of string stability are obtained, and string stability is proved. Numerical simulation results showed the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Inertial Zeroing Neural Network for Robot Manipulator Control Described by Different-Level Dynamic Linear System
abstract: Enhancing the stability and precision of robot manipulator control represents a pivotal focus in engineering. In this paper, we focus on studying how to optimize the stability and accuracy of robot manipulator control. The proposed approach merges an inertial neural network with a discrete zeroing neural network, resulting in a remarkable reduction of shaking and error. The discrete zeroing neural network model is proposed in the basis of the different-level dynamic linear system. However, this model has the disadvantage of significant oscillations in solving different-level dynamic linear systems with great joint angle jitter and derivative of the change in joint values, which may result in hardware damage and control errors. In order to solve this problem, we put forward an inertial zeroing neural network. The tracking error of the inertial zeroing neural network is smaller than the tracking error of the general zeroing neural network. In addition, the joint angle jitter of the inertial zeroing neural network is smaller and the robot manipulator changes more smoothly at the initial phase. The results of the simulation confirm the superiority of the initial zeroing neural network.

articleTitle: Research on UAV Coverage Search Based on DDQN in Unknown Environments
abstract: The utilization of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) for area coverage search is highly sought after in both military and civil domains, including but not limited to traversal search, mission reconnaissance, patrol detection, wildfire suppression control, remote sensing mapping, agricultural preservation, and accident search and rescue. This paper focuses on the problem of area coverage search for a single UAV in environments with the presence of unknown dynamic and static targets as well as hazardous areas. Here the UAV only knows the state of a small area and remembers the actions of the last time step without long-term memory. The objective is to design an adaptive and transferable algorithm for the UAV to find all static and dynamic targets with the minimum path repetition rate in the task area where both dangerous areas and completely unknown target information exist. Because the UAV has limited ability to observe all the map information, a partially observable Markov decision process is first formulated. Then we develop a coverage search algorithm based on Double Deep Q Network (DDQN) with the help of curriculum learning. By designing multiple constraint reward functions and employing path repetition rate and target batting average as evaluation metrics, the proposed algorithm facilitates the rapid adaptation of UAVs to diverse task environments. Simulation environment and algorithm models are finally established to illustrate the efficacy of the algorithm, which shows that the proposed algorithm with curriculum learning has rapid convergence, minimal path redundancy, high target acquisition rate, robust portability, and adaptability to variations in map area, hazard zones, and target quantity.

articleTitle: High Resolution Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation Using Bayesian of Hyperparameters and Improved U-net
abstract: This paper proposes an improved method based on the U-net network, which aims to improve the semantic segmentation performance of high-resolution remote-sensing images, and accelerate the process of finding the optimal learning model. This model combines pyramid pooling with the U-net model to achieve feature extraction at multiple scales, and the atrous convolution is added to enlarge the receptive field, so that each result output contains a larger range of features than the original output, and the global information of remote-sensing images can be obtained. Simultaneously incorporating Bayesian optimization to optimize the model, and find the optimal parameters. The results show that compared with other commonly used semantic segmentation models, the proposed method has best segmentation accuracy and shorter training time.

articleTitle: Surface Defect Detection Method Based on Cross-Data Space Adversarial Defense
abstract: Surface defect detection is a crucial method for controlling product quality, and convolutional neural networks(CNN) have shown great potential in this field. However, the researchers found that adversarial examples can cause the CNN to produce inaccurate results. It remains to be studied whether CNN can be applied in important industries. In order to improve the adversarial defense capability of neural networks, this paper proposes a neural network training framework based on cross-data space adversarial defense(CDSAD) for classified neural networks. The framework CDSAD trains a network that can adapt to multiple data distributions. During the inference process, the network employs multi-perspective evaluation methods to defend, warn and detect adversarial examples. The defensive capability of the CDSAD was tested against multiple adversarial attack algorithms using the CIFAR 10 and triode surface defect datasets. Experiment results demonstrate that the CDSAD defends against multiple adversarial attack algorithms without requiring any information about the opponent. The defensive effect is further improved when the framework acquires opponent information for adversarial identification module(AIM) training.

articleTitle: Distributed Optimal H∞ Fusion Filter for Multi-Sensor Networked Systems with Sensor Saturations and DoS Attacks
abstract: The problem that considers multi-sensor distributed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> fusion filtering of networked systems is studied where sensor saturations and denial of service (Dos) attacks are considered simultaneously. The Dos attacks bring adverse influences on data loss, which is compensated by predictive input method. By means of a linear matrix inequality (LMI) method, constructing the distributed optimal fusion filter (DOFF) depends on local filters, which confirms stability and performance constrain condition of the fusion error system (FES). The performance level of the proposed DOFF is better than every local filter. A numerical simulation illustrates availability of the DOFF.

articleTitle: A purely data-driven modeling method based on subspace system identification for DC-DC converters
abstract: A purely data-driven modeling approach based on subspace system identification is proposed for establishing state-space models of DC-DC converters suitable for control system design. Unlike traditional modeling methods, this approach eliminates the need for prior knowledge of circuit topology or analytical equations. Instead, it leverages collected input-output data to accurately estimate the system's structure and parameters. When applied to DC-DC converters, the method achieves an impressive model fitting degree of approximately 97%, highlighting its effectiveness in practical applications.

articleTitle: Nonooperative Containment Control for Multiple Unmanned Surface Vehicles With Improved Extended State Observer
abstract: This paper investigates a distributed containment control problem of multiple autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) in the presence of internal and external disturbances. Considering some ASV s with individual tasks, a noncooperative game-based control scheme is developed to achieve the containment behavior of multiple ASV s. To deal with the internal and external disturbances, we design an improved extended state observer (IESO). Using the Nash equilibrium seeking strategy, an IESO-based noncooperative containment controller is presented. It is proved that the closed-loop system is input-to-state stable, and position and heading of all ASVs converge to the Nash equilibrium as far as possible. Finally, simulation results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed scheme.

articleTitle: 6-DOF Pose Estimation for Spacecraft Based on Soft Classification of Euler Angles Optimization
abstract: Pose estimation has important applications in on-orbit services such as spacecraft rendezvous, docking, and debris removal. This has become a highly challenging task due to varying lighting, cluttered backgrounds, and occlusions. This paper proposes a method for 6-DOF pose estimation based on soft classification of Euler angles optimization. First, we propose a multi-scale convolutional network with skip connections for better feature extraction. Second, optimization of Euler angles based soft classification is adopted for pose estimation based on the aforementioned network, and its core idea is that the network outputs the similarity of generated orientations and predicted orientation. According to evaluation results, our method achieves high accuracy on the SPPED+ dataset. This paper has also demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method through a series of ablation experiments and comparative validation.

articleTitle: Efficient Coflow Scheduling with Deep Reinforcement Learning and DAG Dependency Modeling
abstract: Cluster computing is widely used in fields such as massive data processing, data mining, and machine learning, it includes the computation stage and the communication stage. Cluster computing jobs include some computation stages and communication stages, typically modeled as DAGs. The communication stage between computing nodes transferring massive amounts of data has a significant impact on the time consumption of the whole job. Current research mostly optimize the completion time of the entire job by minimizing CCT or deadline missing rate without considering the time consumption of computation stages. Additionally, existing work neglect the expression of dependency relationship in the DAG. In this paper, in order to minimize JCT, we propose a reinforcement learning framework to generate coflow scheduling policies, taking into account the time consumption of computation stages. In addition, we introduce RNN to model the dependency between coflows and MPNN to generate the information representation of them. Finally, we achieve lower job completion time than FIFO in the real network environment, which proves that the coflow scheduling scheme proposed in this paper is more efficient.

articleTitle: Controller Design of Nonlinear Networked Cascade Control System with Multiple Delays
abstract: The controller design problem of networked cascade control system (NCCS) with multiple delays and nonlinear disturbances are studied in this paper for first time. Firstly, the influence of nonlinear control plant and networked delay in outer loop is considered, and an NCCS model with state delay in inner loop is established based on above. And secondly, the Lyapunov function is constructed and sufficient conditions for system stability are given by using schur complement. The gain of the controller is then derived using the LMI toolbox in Matlab. Finally, combined with the actual industrial application, a simulink simulation example of a thermal power plant based on NCCS is given to verify the effectiveness and performance of this method which shows that this methods can make the system stable and have good performance.

articleTitle: Cloud Fitness User Stickiness Issues and Development Suggestions
abstract: At the beginning of 2020, the sudden outbreak of COVID-19 pneumonia pressed the pause button for all outdoor activities, and the home fitness mode with new media platforms as the main medium not only became the primary choice for people to fight the epidemic scientifically, but also became a healthy lifestyle advocated during the epidemic prevention and control period. Under the grand blueprint of “Healthy China”, it becomes urgent to ensure the people's cloud fitness mode and maintain the stickiness of exercise. Based on the symbiosis theory, this study takes the interactive behaviour of cloud fitness platform and users' exercise as the entry point to explore the factors affecting users' stickiness, constructs the conceptual model of “symbiotic environment of cloud fitness platform → users' self-efficacy → users' participation → users' stickiness,” and verifies the model through questionnaire survey data.

articleTitle: Motion Control for a Manned eVTOL Aircraft with Cross Tilting Propellers
abstract: This paper considers the motion control of a manned electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing (eVTOL) aircraft with cross tilting propellers. This article mainly focuses on the challenging technical aspects of eVTOLs, including aerodynamic effects and cross-tilted rotor blade design, battery discharge effects, and control law design. First, we develop a system simulation platform for a large-scale manned eVTOL, incorporating aerodynamic effects and a discharge model for the power battery. Second, we design a cross-tilted configuration for rotor blades to enhance yaw channel control sensitivity and reduce power consumption in that channel significantly. Third, PID control law and Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) are integrated as the flight control algorithm for the large-scale manned eVTOL, achieving excellent experimental results in hover flight, waypoint tracking, path following, and other motion control tasks. This algorithm enables stable flight even in the presence of external disturbances. Simulations and experimental results complete the work.

Author Keywords: discharge model for the power battery

articleTitle: Path Control for Post-Impact Vehicle Based on BPNN-PID Algorithm
abstract: Lateral displacements caused by vehicle collisions makes the vehicle travel unstable, which causes most of the accidents and even leads to even more collisions. In this paper, we will discuss the possibility of a control strategy that maintains the stability of the vehicle's travel after an impact and restricts the vehicle's in-lane travel, aiming to reduce the risk of subsequent accidents. Based on PID control, the post-collision control system controls the lateral deviation of the vehicle's travel path to the desired path by using an active steering system to ensure the trajectory and stability of the vehicle. In this paper, the PID control system parameters are combined with BP neural network to make timely, optimized adjustments to make the vehicle trajectory under the BP neural network PID controller converge faster and oscillate with less amplitude. Moreover, the BP neural network PID control system can automatically adjust the PID control parameters according to different collision situations. The effectiveness and adaptability of the BP neural network PID control system after collision is demonstrated through the simulation of post-collision steering control of the controlled vehicle.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Omni-Directional Forklift Traveling System Based on Bayesian Network
abstract: The system structure and function of omni-directional forklift motion control system are more and more complex. The malfunction of some important components may result in the failure of the entire system. Aiming at this characteristic, a fault diagnosis method of omnidirectional forklift motion control system based on Bayesian networks is proposed. Firstly, the fault tree modeling of the omnidirectional forklift motion control system was carried out, and the system failure causes were decomposed and refined layer by layer to find out the root cause of the motion control system failure. Secondly, the causal relationship between events and faults in the fault tree is converted into nodes and directed edges in the Bayesian network respectively, and the Bayesian network is constructed according to the mapping relationship between the fault tree and the Bayesian network. The fault diagnosis of omnidirectional forklift motion control system is realized by using Bayes network reverse diagnosis technology.

articleTitle: A Study of Mobile Robot Path Planning by Fusing Improved A* And DWA Algorithms
abstract: The traditional A * algorithm has the shortcomings of low search efficiency, node redundancy, and intersection of trajectory with obstacle vertices. For performing dynamic obstacle avoidance of mobile robots in challenging environments, a fused version of the dynamic window technique (DWA) and an enhanced A * algorithm are presented. The comparison simulation experiments under MATLAB show that the improved A * algorithm optimizes the trajectory length, trajectory smoothness, and search time, satisfies the global optimum and can achieve real-time obstacle avoidance, with a better path planning effect.

articleTitle: Gesture Recognition Using FMCW Radar Based on Deep Neural Network
abstract: In recent years, radar based gesture recognition technology has attracted more and more attention. Among different types of radars, frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar has the greatest application potential due to its high range and velocity resolution and low cost. However, insufficient gesture information extraction and interference signals affect the performance of FMCW radar gesture recognition. To address the problems, a gesture recognition method based on multi-dimensional features and deep neural network is proposed in this paper. First, the range-time map (RTM) and velocity-time map (VTM) of the gesture are constructed from the range-Doppler map (RDM) with two-dimensional fast Fourier transform (2D-FFT). Then, the angle-time map (ATM) is constructed with the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. Subsequently, RTM, VTM and ATM are normalized and adaptively filtered to suppress interference signals, and the three maps are fused to construct the range-velocity-angle-time map (RV ATM) of the gesture. Finally, an improved VGG16 network with self-attention mechanism module is used for feature extraction and recognition. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an average accuracy of 98.3% for six gestures, and the improved VGG16 network outperforms other traditional convolutional neural networks.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Flexible Deformable Special Flying Robot
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the rigid structure of rotorcraft can not meet the requirements of flying in narrow space, a deformable flying robot with rigid and flexible structure is proposed and analyzed and verified by experiments. The test results show that the flying robot can effectively achieve normal flight under the condition of reduced flight radius, which verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of the flexible deformable special flying robot to cross the narrow space.

articleTitle: Analysis and Experiment of Fish Body Wave Motion of MFC-Actuated Flexible Structure
abstract: This paper demonstrates the application of a flexible structure driven by Macro Fiber Composites (MFC) to mimic and explore fish body wave motion. The assumed mode approach is used to derive the first three normalized mode forms of the flexible structure driven by MFC. It is found that the second-order mode shape closely mimics the swimming mode shape of a carangiform fish. The amplitude-frequency response and vibration shape monitoring experiments of the underwater flexible structure actuated by MFC are conducted. The experimental results reveal a node on the second-order vibration shape of the MFC-actuated flexible structure, which divides it into two parts with opposite vibration directions. Furthermore, the study also verifies the accuracy of the vibration model and the feasibility of mimicking the fish body wave motion by utilizing an MFC-actuated flexible structure. The results of this study offer important insights into the creation and performance improvement of underwater propulsors, thereby indicating potential areas for future research and development efforts.

articleTitle: Adaptive NN-Based Leader-Following Consensus Control for a Class of Second-Order Nonlinear Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: The leader-following consensus problem for a class of second-order nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) is examined in this study utilizing neural network (NN)-based approach. Generally the nonlinearity will influence the framework execution system performance, in this paper the differential mean theorem is used instead of the global Lipschitz condition to deal with the nonlinear term. Then the NN-based approximator and adaptive controller are constructed based on position and velocity estimations. By employing Lyapunov stability analysis, we established the viability of the leader-following consensus. Finally, the presented outcomes are illustrated with simulation results.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Time-Varying Group Formation Control for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems Under Jointly Connected Topologies
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of time-varying group formation for heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems (MASs) under joint switching topologies. In order to accomplish complicated coordination tasks, the MAS is divided into multiple groups, each consisting of a leader and multiple followers. The leader is responsible for providing trajectory as a reference for movement, while the followers form a certain formation around the leader within their respective groups. To address the situation of incomplete information availability of agents, compensators and observers are designed in this study. On this basis, an event-triggered formation control protocol is proposed for each follower to ensure that the output tracking error converges to zero. Finally, the effectiveness of the theoretical results is verified through a numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Research on the Deduction System of Panoramic Training with New Energy Involved in the Power Grid via Parallel Control
abstract: This paper aimed to propose a solution for deduction system of panoramic training, which can analog many kinds of complex situations in consideration of new energy involved in the power grid and provide the functions of simulation practice, wisdom deduction, as well as decision making reference. And then, to output intelligent reference solutions for the precise control of new energy involved in scenarios with high proportion under the new power system. We constructed a deduction system of panoramic training with new energy involved in the power grid by building cyber physical social system (CPSS). Besides, the ACP parallel intelligence theory has been used. Taking a training center of large scale as an example, first we discussed the shortcomings for current dispatching and control simulation training system for power grid and proposed the concept of the deduction system of panoramic training with new energy involved in the power grid via parallel control. After that, we introduced the construction of the system, which included the digital modeling of different substation, grid line, electrical source and so on. Following this, based on the ACP theory, intelligence deduction system with the function of virtual and real interaction had been built up. In the end, with a case analysis of a real training center, we provided the system design and implementation method, which confirmed the feasibility and practicability of the intelligence deduction system proposed in this paper.

Author Keywords: the deduction system of panoramic training

articleTitle: Discrete Whale Optimization Algorithm for Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem
abstract: Capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) is a classical combinatorial optimization problem, which plays an important role in the logistics field and belongs to the NP-hard problem. Discrete whale optimization algorithm (DWOA) with a routing first and grouping later solution generating technique is proposed to handle the CVRP. The algorithm redefines the classical whale optimization algorithm's encircling prey method, bubble-net attacking method, and exploration phase method. Through the improved whale optimization algorithm, the optimal planning of logistics distribution vehicle routing is realized. Finally, an experimental demonstration of the DWOA algorithm's success offers a novel approach for resolving CVRP.

articleTitle: Active disturbance rejection control for double-pendulum overhead cranes system
abstract: This paper proposes an anti-disturbance controller for bridge cranes with two-stage swing effects (DPOC). Firstly, the transition process is arranged by tracking differential (TD), which not only enhances the robustness of the controller, but also solves the contradiction between overshoot and rapidity. In addition, the expansion state observer (ESO) is designed to observe the uncertain state and external disturbance of the system, then the disturbance is compensated by the nonlinear control law (NLSEF), so as to realize the positioning and anti-swing of the double pendulum crane system. Finally, the auto-disturbance rejection ability of the system is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for Predicting Future Capacities of Lithium-ion Battery Based on N-BEATS Model
abstract: Owing to the high performance, lithium-ion batteries are widely applied in many industrial fields. In order to ensure the safety of lithium-ion batteries, it is essential to predict the future battery capacity accurately. In this paper, a novel hybrid approach is presented for future capacity forecast based on Gaussian process regression (GPR) and N-BEATS. First, the capacity degradation data is decoupled into a series of components by the variational mode decomposition (VMD). Second, in order to improve the accuracy and reliability of battery capacity prediction, the low-frequency parts and remaining high-frequency parts are predicted by GPR and N-BEATS respectively, and their forecast results are superposed as the battery capacity forecast. The experimental results in NASA battery data certify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: V2V Composite Routing Algorithm for Internet of Vehicles Based on Improved Q-Learning
abstract: Targeting the high maintenance costs and poor dynamic adaptability of existing routing algorithms for the Internet of vehicles, this study introduces a multi-hop clustering composite routing algorithm that builds upon an enhanced Q-learning approach. In the cluster maintenance phase, the cluster head selects the node with good communication performance and relatively stable speed with the edge vehicles as the gateway node according to the utility function of the gateway. During the route establishment stage, the link communication quality during the route establishment stage, the link communication quality and packet transmission direction are taken into account, and node mobility, a node performance evaluation function evaluates the comprehensive performance of the selected next-hop node to avoid the blind path problem. In the Q-learning stage, the duration and distance of adjacent links are quantified and employed as learning and discount rates to enhance the efficiency of Q-learning. Simulations on mobile datasets on Cologne, Germany and a city in China show that, compared with the Random, RSAR routing algorithms, the routing lifetime and throughput of the proposed algorithm improved by 16.57% and 31.54% on average respectively, and the communication delay and packet loss rate decreased by 13.5% and 64.32% on average respectively. These results indicate that the proposed algorithm can adapt to complex and Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs).

articleTitle: A Vision-Based Attention Deep Q-Network with Prior-Based Knowledge
abstract: In order to unveil the intrinsic workings of deep reinforcement learning(DRL) models and explain the regions of interest attended by the agent during the decision-making process, vision-based RL employs attention mechanisms. However, due to policy optimization leading to changes in the data domain, the agent may even fail to learn a policy. To address this, a vision-based attention deep Q-network(VADQN) method with a prior-based mechanism is proposed. Firstly, prior attention maps are obtained using a learnable Gaussian filter and spectral residual method. Nextly, the attention maps are fine-tuned using a self-attention mechanism to improve their performance. During RL training, both the attention maps and the parameters of the policy network are simultaneously trained to ensure explanations of the regions of interest during online training. Finally, a series of ablation experiments were conducted on atari games to compare the proposed method with human, nature convolutional neural network, and other approaches. The results demonstrate that our proposed method not only reveals the regions of interest attended by DRL during the decision-making process but also enhances DRL performance in certain scenarios.

articleTitle: Train Operation Control System Based on Vehicle-to-Vehicle Communication
abstract: The continuous evolution of the railway signal system towards digitization, networking, automation, and intelligence has generated a pressing need for new train control systems to enhance the intelligence level of the railway industry. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the development and changes in the existing signal system. It introduces the working principle of a train operation control system based on vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication and highlights the main characteristics of two key concepts: ‘Train-Ground Integration’ and ‘Train-Centric’ within the technical scheme. Furthermore, this study elucidates the promotion scheme for the Train Autonomous Control System (TACS), specifically focusing on the virtual coupling platoon.

articleTitle: Novel Cosine Distance Based Semi-Supervised Learning Using Discriminant Graph Convolutional Network for Industrial Fault Diagnosis
abstract: Semi-supervised learning can effectively utilize limited labeled data and large amounts of unlabeled data to achieve fault diagnosis on process industries. This paper proposes a novel cosine distance based semi-supervised learning using discriminant graph convolutional networks (CD-GCN) at node-level Firstly, the CD-GCN method uses the discriminant information to pull the training sample features of different classes farther away from each other. Secondly, CD-GCN replaces Euclidean distance with Cosine distance as the distance metric in the original samples space and feature space. With Cosine distance and discriminant information, CD-GCN better considers spatial structure information and improve the whole graph by the dual effects of graph convolution and nearest neighboring with these moving training sample features. Finally, a real industrial simulation case is carried out to verify the performance of the proposed method. Compared with other related and classic methods, the simulation results show that the CD-GCN method achieves the best performance in diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: BRViT: A Vision Transformer Approach for Enhancing Efficiency Under Bandwidth-Restricted Data Acquisition Conditions
abstract: Bandwidth constraints during data acquisition prevalently impede applications like real-time detection. For instance, the immense volume of hyperspectral data significantly burdens the acquisition, transmission, and processing capabilities, thus obstructing real-time hyperspectral detection. To this end, this paper proposes to leverage pre-acquisition modulation to reduce acquisition volume, with the modulation process controlled by a deep learning model trained on prior information. Building on this concept, we introduce BRViT, a Vision Transformer framework with a patch-embedding block tailored for pre-acquisition modulation and undersampling. Moreover, a three-stage finetuning strategy is proposed to fine tune BRViT. In the ImageNet-1k classification simulation task, BRViT achieved a precision loss within 4 % with a sampling volume of only one-tenth of the original pixels.

articleTitle: A novel deep CGRU model with feature attention for prediction of moisture content in Leaf moistening
abstract: The moisture content at the outlet of the leaf moistening process is an important process indicator in the production process, and its stability and accuracy directly affect the product quality. To address the issues, this paper proposes a moisture content prediction method based on feature attention mechanism and deep spatio-temporal representation. First, feature attention is applied to dynamically adjust the importance of different process variables based on their relevance to the target quality variable. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) structure is utilized to capture the coupling and correlation among the variables, and capture the long-term temporal dependencies. Additionally, a parallel GRU is constructed to explore the autocorrelation properties among historical quality variables. Finally, the paper utilizes a concatenation layer to merge the parallel information into a deep spatio-temporal representation, which is then fed into a fully connected layer network to predict the moisture content at the outlet. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the baseline methods in terms of prediction accuracy and stability, and provides effective decision support for operators and meets the requirements of industrial production.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Parameter Adaptive S-Plane Controller for Motion Control of Unmanned Underwater Vehicles
abstract: The complex dynamic characteristics and marine environment pose significant challenges to the motion controller design of unmanned underwater vehicles (UUV). However, the controller parameters are usually fixed once manually adjusted, so they cannot adapt to environmental changes. This paper aims to present a machine learning-based parameter adaptive S-plane controller for the motion control of UUVs. The Q-learning-based adaptive control method is adopted to realize the optimization and automatic tuning of controller parameters in different environments. The optimal mapping between the input state and output action is found through the self-learning mechanism of Q-learning. Simulation results indicate that the proposed controller can adjust the controller's parameters in real-time and online and has a good control effect and adaptive ability for the actual environment.

articleTitle: UIO-Based Prescribed Performance Attitude Tracking Control of UAV
abstract: A problem of prescribed performance attitude tracking control of quadrotor UAV with external disturbances is studied in this article. Firstly, for the attitude system with external disturbances, an unknown input observer (UIO) is designed to estimate disturbances accurately. One of the advantages of UIO is that the upper bound of disturbances and their derivatives do not need to be known in advance. Secondly, a control method is designed based on a new predefined-time prescribed performance function (PTPPF), combined with the estimates provided by UIO. The proposed control strategy ensures that tracking error converges to an arbitrarily small residual set within a predefined time. The Lyapunov stability criterion and simulations can verify the effectiveness and superiority of this scheme.

articleTitle: Evolution of the “Self-Bad, Partner-Worse” Strategy Within Networked Populations Motivated by Various Game Models
abstract: Evolution of networked collective behavior is a research highlight within the subject of evolutionary game theory and social systems owing that the strategy evolution on complex networks could simulate and further predict the collective behavior evolution in various human societies. The iterated game, which depicts individual long-term behaviors, has been widely studied. A new kind of iterated game called “self-bad, partner-worse” (SBPW) strategy has been proposed in Prisoner's Dilemma game recently. In this paper, we extend the individual interaction to more game models and indicate that SBPW strategy exists widely in various social networks. Our conclusion may be conducive to interpret the correlation of decision making in different game models and hint at some insights regarding collective behavior control in networked populations.

articleTitle: System Identification and Hysteresis Compensation of Piezo-Positioning System
abstract: In order to enhance the dynamic tracking performance and achieve a more precise model of the Piezo-Positioning system, this study focuses on investigating the modeling of the system and the compensation of its hysteresis characteristics. Initially, the dynamic hysteresis model of the Piezo-Positioning system is established by employing the P-I model and the Hankel matrix system identification method. Subsequently, a feed-forward-feedback composite control approach, based on the P-I inverse model, is proposed, and the adjustment of the system's bandwidth is achieved through the utilization of a notch filter. Finally, experimental validation is conducted to verify the accuracy of the identification model and the optimization effect of the hysteresis compensation method on the Piezo-Positioning system.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis Research on Edge Effects of Capacitive Grid Sensor
abstract: Aiming at the special nature of the torque testing environment for special vehicle transmission shafts, the torque testing method based on embedded capacitive grid sensors can solve the problems of small installation space, difficult leads, and easy signal interference. To solve the Edge effects problem of capacitive grid torque sensor, Ansoft Maxwell electromagnetic field finite element analysis software is used for simulation analysis. By changing the gate thickness and plate spacing with a fixed number of capacitor gate pairs, the trend of capacitance values with the two parameters can be obtained. Experimental research was conducted on this issue through a simulated rotating shaft experimental platform, and the experimental scheme was set by changing the gate thickness and plate spacing of the capacitive grid torque sensor. The results show that the change trend of the experimental data is the same as that of the simulation data. In the actual measurement experiment, the method of reducing the grid thickness and plate spacing can be used under the conditions of manufacturing technology and cost constraints to reduce the impact of Edge effects and improve the test accuracy.

articleTitle: Consensus- Based Flexible Group Formation Control for Multi-UAVs Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a comprehensive approach to group formation control by introducing the concept of flexible formation while analyzing maneuverability. A consensus-based formation control algorithm is integrated into the flexible group formation control, with the formation point of the flexible formation acting as the group leader. The effectiveness of the suggested algorithm is substantiated through simulations executed on a laboratory-developed platform with a realistic fixed-wing UAV dynamic model.

articleTitle: Distributed Generalized Nash Equilibrium Seeking for Energy Sharing Games
abstract: This paper is concerned with the problem of distributed generalized Nash equilibrium seeking in energy sharing games, where each prosumer aims to minimize its cost while satisfying global power balance. First, the existence and uniqueness of the Nash equilibrium can be verified by demonstrating the strong monotonicity of the game. Then, a distributed projected algorithm is proposed to ensure that all the prosumers can find the Nash Equilibrium (GNE) through local information exchange. The convergence analysis of the algorithm is conducted by using variational inequality and Lyapunov function. Finally, to substantiate the viability of our proposed methodology, we offer an illustrative instance employing the IEEE 5-bus system.

articleTitle: Sparse Representation Denoising of Roadsid Acoustic Signals Based on Wavelet-domain RLS Filters
abstract: When the train wayside acoustic signal is used for fault warning and fault diagnosis, Target acoustic signal with fault information and strong background noise are collected together, which affects the subsequent processing. Therefore, for the noise interference problem, this paper proposes a method combining wavelet transform as well as sparse representation, and also creatively adding RLS filter to perform noise reduction on the wayside acoustic signal. In the proposed method. Firstly, the wavelet coefficients after wavelet decomposition are adaptively attenuated using the sparse representation method. Secondly, the RLS filter with the set filtering threshold is then noise reduced. Finally, the signal is reconstructed by two wavelet transforms and inverse transform, which can maximize the sparse signal and recover the signal with higher quality. The simulation results show that this method has better noise reduction effect compared to the traditional wavelet transform and filter noise reduction.

articleTitle: Consensus of Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems with Observation Packet Losses*
abstract: This work investigates the issue of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{1}$</tex> output consensus in heterogeneous multi-agent systems (MASs) with observed packet loss. Unlike previous consensus researches, the fundamental difficulties involved are the distributed controller design and the state estimator design for stochastic systems with multiplicative noises. According to measured values, the optimal estimator is developed to estimate the state information of agents. Based on the developed estimator and internal reference generator, a new distributed dynamic output feedback control protocol is designed.

articleTitle: Automation Control System for Rail Transit Equipment in Forest Areas
abstract: The automation control system of railway transit equipment in forest areas is presented, especially the velocity control based on temporal-difference learning. The structure and components of rail transit equipment is introduced and analyzed. The dynamic model of rail transit equipment is built, and the velocity control based on temporal-difference learning is researched in detail. At last, the experiment of rail transit equipment in forest areas is verified the effectiveness of temporal-difference learning algorithm for velocity control.

articleTitle: Adaptive Trap-Based Noise Suppression Interference Suppression Algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the problem of poor anti-noise interference ability of linear FM fuzes, the noise FM interference suppression method based on adaptive trap is proposed, and the adaptive trap is applied to linear FM fuzes for the single-frequency characteristics of linear FM fuzes generated by the frequency-checking signals. By adaptively adjusting the weights of the trap, the trap has a trapping characteristic at the frequency Dian of the differential frequency signal, so as to achieve the effect of noise FM interference suppression, and experiments show that the algorithm can recover the target echo signal when the interference signal is stronger than the target echo by 10 dB.

articleTitle: Graph Neural Network-Based Task Assignment for Coordinated Tasks in Heterogeneous Unmanned Underwater Vehicle Cluster
abstract: Currently, unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) clusters have demonstrated effectiveness in performing oceanic tasks, with heterogeneity of UUVs becoming a prevalent trend in development. Therefore, selecting appropriate heterogeneous members is essential for achieving efficient and high-quality task execution. To address this issue, this study proposes a UUV cluster cooperative system task assignment method based on graph neural networks (GNN). This method models the UUV cluster as a graphical structure and utilizes a GNN-based approach that combines cluster topology with task requirements, which can learn to predict the optimal UUV cluster for a given task. In addition, this method is scalable and can be applied to different tasks and clusters.

articleTitle: Research on MEMS-IMU Attitude Estimation Based on the Kalman Method
abstract: MEMS-IMU technology is mature and widely used. However, the drawback of large noise remains a key factor restricting the large-scale application of MEMS-IMUs. In this paper, we study the data fusion methods for IMUs based on two types of Kalman logic, the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) and the Error-State Kalman Filter (ESKF). We attempt to improve the angular rate bias estimation in the ESKF by applying a filtering window. Through a comparison of the two Kalman filtering methods using actual measurement data, we analyze the improvement effects and explore their performance under noise interference. The results show that both EKF and ESKF can effectively suppress noise, and the improvement with the filtering window enhances the stability of bias estimation.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Fractional-Order T-S Fuzzy Neural Networks Under Event-Triggered Control
abstract: Based on event-triggered control strategy (ETCS), this paper analyzes and investigates the synchronization problem of fractional-order T-S fuzzy neural networks (FOTSFNN). A novel ETCS is introduced in this paper to maintain synchronization performance while reducing the frequency of the output measurement signal. By using the characteristics of fuzzy model, the nonlinear function is locally linearized, and the human control experience is integrated into the controller through fuzzy rules. High-level controller design is realised through the design of fuzzy rules. By exploiting the principles of fractional-order calculus and employing Lyapunov's methodology, a set of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs) is established to achieve asymptotic stability of the drive-response system for error-based systems. By analyzing the dynamic evolution of the error system, it is proved that the ETCS proposed in this paper does not exist Zeno behavior. A numerical demonstration showcasing the validity of this paper's findings is presented at the end.

articleTitle: Adaptive Optimal Fault-Tolerant Control for Strict-Feedback Nonlinear Systems Based on Zero-Sum Differential Game
abstract: This paper analyzes the adaptive optimal fault-tolerant control issue for a class of strict-feedback nonlinear systems with bias faults based on zero-sum differential game. A novel adaptive optimal controller is created by employing the adaptive backstepping technique, viewing the control input and the bias fault as two players in a zero-sum game, and using the adaptive dynamic programming method to obtain Nash equilibrium point, which ensure that all closed-loop signals are uniformly bounded, the tracking performance of the system, and the system's optimum performance. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the validness of this control scheme.

articleTitle: An Improved PSO Algorithm for Cooperative Mission Assignment of Space Recovery
abstract: As space exploration grows, so does the amount of space junk, even affecting the normal work of spacecraft and satellites. An improved particle swarm optimization(PSO) algorithm applied to perform space junk recovery tasks in parallel with multi-spacecraft is proposed in this paper. First, adaptive inertia weights and acceleration coefficient are designed to prevent the proposed algorithm from falling into local optimum; Second, utilizing the idea of variation and crossover in genetic algorithm for processing particle matrices can improve the efficiency of the algorithm. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm provides reasonable assignment results, the operation time is reduced by 3%, and the revenue is improved by 13 % at least.

articleTitle: Research on Digital Modeling and EKF-Based SOC Estimation for Lithium-ion Battery
abstract: Spacecraft power system health management is an important part of the intelligent control system. As the main energy storage unit, the status of the battery is critical to power security and mission success of the aircraft, and accurate estimation of SOC (State-of-Charge) is the basis for realizing intelligent health management of the spacecraft power system. An equivalent circuit model of second-order RC (Resistance-Capacitance) is used to identify the off-line parameters of the battery, and the battery parameters under different SOC are obtained by the method of least squares. Pulse discharge and charge tests verify the validity of the model, and the maximum error is no more than 0.08 V. The estimation of SOC is carried out by EKF (extended Kalman filter), and the effectiveness of algorithm is verified under three operating conditions of DST, FUDS and US06. The comparison results reveal that even under large initial error of SOC, the algorithm can still converge quickly and the errors are about 1%.

articleTitle: Time-Series Augmentation Based on Atmospheric Microwave Remote Sensing Data Under the Influence of Pacific Monsoon Climate
abstract: Microwave radiometer is a passive remote sensing instrument. The MP3000A microwave radiometer is used in this study. To address the problem of time-series augmentation of contour data, this paper uses a super-resolution network model based on convolutional neural network for time-series augm-entation of 34,568 temperature contour data measured by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex>P3000A from April 22, 2023 to June 15, 2023 in Harbin. High- resolution branches are added to the original super-resolution network, and the results are compared and analyzed by normal-izing and non-normalizing the original data. The heatmap of the temperature data error shows that the time series amplified temperature data is weakly different from the true value, with a mean square error MSE of 2.4831 and a mean absolute error MAE of 1.3213, and the network model performs well. It is shown that the use of super-resolution network model works well in time series for atmospheric microwave remote sensing data under the influence of the Pacific monsoon climate.

articleTitle: A Distributed Power Flow Optimization Method Based on Grid Decomposition
abstract: With the increasing complexity of power systems, distributed optimal power flow (OPF) calculation becomes an important part of ensuring efficient operation. The reasonable decomposition and simplification of the system can improve the computing speed while maintaining high accuracy. This paper addresses the above challenges and puts forward a distributed power flow optimization method. The power system optimization is modelled in the first step, and the constraints are converted into the formula with semi-definite relaxations. Then, the network topology of power systems is re-constructed by grid-broken. With the aid of grid decomposition and convex relaxation technique, distributed computing is realized by the improved alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) technique. The proposed method is verified by the case study and extended to a physical device.

articleTitle: PLPR-SLAM:Indoor RGB-D SLAM Utilizing Point-Line-Plane Features
abstract: In low-texture indoor environments, the scarcity of sufficient features often leads to issues like drift and tracking failures in feature-based Visual SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) systems. Existing approaches frequently involve incorporating line features into the SLAM system or relying on the Manhattan World (MW) assumption to address low-texture indoor scenarios. However, line features are more susceptible to noise and depth inconsistencies compared to point features. As a solution, we propose a Point-Line-Plane RGB-D SLAM (PLPR SLAM) system that integrates all three types of features. In this system, we leverage the RANSAC (Random Sample Consensus) algorithm along with depth consistency checks to robustly fit three-dimensional line features within the 3D space. Furthermore, to overcome the limitations of the MW assumption's applicability in various indoor environments, we employ the RANSAC algorithm in conjunction with the DASP (Depth Adaptive Superpixels) technique to extract plane features from depth images without relying on specific environmental assumptions. Our experimental results on the TUM dataset demonstrate that the PLPR SLAM system, by effectively utilizing the indoor structural environment, significantly enhances the accuracy of localization and mapping. It outperforms other prominent feature-based Visual SLAM systems such as ORB-SLAM2, ORB-SLAM3, and MSC-VO (which is based on the MW assumption).

articleTitle: Adaptive dynamic programming for optimal tracking control of stochastic linear continuous-time systems
abstract: This paper investigates optimal tracking control on stochastic continuous-time systems with multiplicative state-dependent and input-dependent noise. Preliminaries of stochastic systems and optimal tracking control are presented and an augmented stochastic differential equation of Ito's type has been constructed. To minimize the quadratic cost function, a model-dependent algorithm is shown to solve the stochastic algebraic Riccati equation. An adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) algorithm has been developed to scrap the reliance on the knowledge of system dynamics. The convergence and stability of the algorithm has been studied following. Finally, numerical simulations are performed to demonstate the effectiveness of the proposed ADP methodology on the tracking performance.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Sampled-Data Iterative Learning Control for Linear Time-Varying Switched Systems
abstract: Consider a class of continues linear time-varying switched systems and study its sampled-data iterative learning control output tracking problem under event triggering. Firstly, in order to reduce the update batch of the control input in the direction of the iteration axis, an event-triggered sampled-data iterative learning control law is designed and the event-triggered conditions are derived by the Lyapunov function method. Secondly, a fixed threshold method is proposed to accelerate the convergence of the system. Then, according to the activation intervals of the switched subsystem,triggered and untriggered are analyzed for convergence, and the sufficient conditions for consistent convergence of the system are derived by the compression mapping method. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by the numerical simulation.

articleTitle: DTR-Map: A Digital Twin-Enabled Real-Time Mapping System Based on Multi-View Stereo
abstract: Digital twins require efficient and cost-effective methods for updating virtual mappings to reflect changes in physical entities. In this paper, we propose DTR-Map, a realtime 3D reconstruction method based on multi-view stereo. Our method utilizes a moving monocular camera as an edge node to collect multi-view data and employs a publisher-subscriber communication framework. By leveraging deep learning-based monocular visual odometry and multi-view stereo matching network, we achieve accurate local camera motion estimation and high-quality output models. Our experimental results demonstrate the method's effectiveness, showcasing its high-quality realtime 3D reconstruction, reconstruction accuracy, and scalability.

articleTitle: Formalization of Dedekind Fundamental Theorem in Coq
abstract: The completeness of real numbers is a fundamental property in real analysis, serving as the cornerstone for the development of calculus and mathematical analysis, and finding wide-ranging applications. In recent years, the significance of mathematical formalization has been consistently on the rise in the fields of mathematics and computer science, with particular emphasis on the formalization of foundational mathematical theories. The Dedekind fundamental theorem represents one form of describing the completeness of real numbers, and its formalization holds significant importance. In this paper, we employ the interactive theorem proving tool Coq, based on the Morse-Kelley axiomatic set theory, following the methodology proposed by Landau in “Foundations of Analysis” to construct the real number system and accomplish the formalized proof of Dedekind fundamental theorem. The work presented in this paper holds crucial significance in the fields of analysis and related mathematical disciplines. It lays the foundation for constructing complex number systems and formalizing theories in analysis, topology, and geometry in Coq.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method for Laser Cutting Process Parameters Based on GPR and Seq2Seq
abstract: The setting of the laser cutting parameter is struggled for its sensitivity to environment. In this paper, a systematic method for optimizing parameters in laser cutting process is proposed, which combines gaussian process regression (GPR) and Sequence-to-Sequence (Seq2Seq) networks. Firstly, a laser cutting process simulator is developed based on GPR. The simulator is used to expand the dataset for machining parameters, enabling the handling of raw machining data with uneven distribution and limited work samples. Finally, a Seq2Seq-based model is proposed to forecast the laser cutting processing parameters under high-power (20,000 W), with the input of low-power machine operation parameter. The experimental results demonstrate the ability of the method to predict the parameters of high-power machines. The method's ability to predict the parameters of high-power machines is demonstrated by the experimental results, with a mean squared error of prediction for parameters of processed stainless steel less than 0.5 and for processed carbon steel less than 2.6. The proposed method can handle the optimization of the processing parameters for new power machines.

articleTitle: LookTwice: An Online Assembly Action Recognition Method Based on Deep Learning
abstract: In automotive production, ensuring the safe assem-bly of engines is critical. Currently, in industrial production environments, deep learning techniques are mostly used for surface defect detection, which can only play a post-control role and cannot detect problems during the production process. We propose a deep learning-based process detection method. We constructed a spatiotemporal action detection model that can detect whether the workers have properly installed the engine according to the procedural standard. This model aims to reduce the problems of misalignment and missing parts caused by relying on manual engine assembly, and to reduce non-standard assembly behavior of products, thereby further reducing manufacturing costs and improving the yield rate. Based on a limited training dataset, this project successfully applied the model to the recognition of engine assembly actions at the automotive engine workstation. Under the current environment, the model exhibits good generalization ability and can achieve low-latency online detection at 15fps on a single Quadro GPI00 graphics card.

articleTitle: Gait Classification and Recognition Based on ECA-LSTM Algorithm
abstract: The classification and recognition of gait patterns plays a decisive role in whether the exoskeleton robot can provide appropriate auxiliary effects for the lower limbs during the movement. Therefore, this article designs a gait classification method for horizontal walking (HW), going upstairs (GU) and going downstairs (GD) based on the data of inertial sensors and plantar pressure sensors. Compared with only using a single sensor, this method uses multi-source sensor data to reflect the movement pattern of human lower limbs more comprehensively. At the same time, this article suggests a gait classification model utilizing a long short-term memory neural network (LSTM)and efficient channel attention (ECA)module. The model can automatically learn the data representation of gait without manual feature engineering. Firstly, the data acquisition system is employed for gathering information on various walking patterns exhibited by diverse subjects, and the data set is constructed. The ECA module is employed to compute the attention weights for the initial data characteristics, following which the data is weighted and fed into the LSTM model, so that it can better learn the temporal dependence of the features. Comparative experiments reveal that the LSTM classification model achieves an accuracy of 0.858, a recall of 0.860, and a precision of 0. 872. The accuracy, recall and precision of the ECA-LSTM classification model with ECA module are 0.960, 0.961 and 0.961, respectively. This underscores the efficacy of the ECA module in enhancing gait classification recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Short-Term Traffic Flow Prediction of Highway Tunnels Based on SSA and Improved TSK Fuzzy System
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traffic flow has an low prediction accuracy due to varying randomness and high nonlinearity, an improved TSK fuzzy neural network prediction model by singular spectrum analysis is proposed.First, the original traffic flow time series can be decomposed into several subseries by singular spectrum analysis (SSA). Then, the Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) fuzzy system was trained using simulated annealing genetic algorithm (SAGA) and minibatch gradient descent method (MBGD) combined with three techniques (RDA) of regularization, DropRule and AdaBound.The prediction model of TSK fuzzy neural network is established to predict each subseries independently, and the forecasted traffic flow is obtained by superimposing the prediction results of each subseries. Finally, the traffic flow dataset of expressway tunnels in a city is used to verify the effectiveness of the model. Experimental results can show high traffic flow prediction accuracy of the model, and the model can accurately predict multiple different highway tunnels.

articleTitle: The Unified Topology Construction Method for Basic Non-Isolated Combined-Type DC/DC Converters
