abstract: Basic non-isolated combined-type DC/DC converters have always played an important role in the field of power electronic converter topology, usually including the three-level DC/DC converters, double-frequency DC/DC converters and interleaving DC/DC converters. At present, the topology construction methods about them are different, and not very uniform. In this paper, from the perspective of unity, the topology construction ideas and processes for the three kinds of basic non-isolated combined-type DC/DC converters above are integrated by combining the basic circuit theory. Thus, a unified topology construction method is proposed by the way of series-connection or parallel-connection between the voltage-type conversion unit and current-type conversion unit. The specific results of topology construction are analyzed and relevant conclusions are also given.

articleTitle: Image Segmentation with Multi-Scale Feature Fusion of Local Binary Patterns for Flexible Integrated Circuit Packaging Substrates
abstract: Image segmentation is employed to address the problem of recognizing the Region of Interest (ROI) in detecting defects. However, detecting defects in Flexible Integrated Circuit Packaging Substrates (FICS) has several challenges, including low brightness, diverse defect types, and defect textures that resemble the substrate textures. Existing image segmentation methods fail to distinguish the ROI region from the substrate texture, leading to misjudgments during detection. This paper introduces a method for Image segmentation using a multi-scale feature fusion technique based on Local Binary Patterns (LBP). Firstly, the image undergoes preprocessing using the histogram equalization theory, significantly enhancing its contrast. Next, the multi-scale feature fusion technology based on LBP is utilized to obtain the multi-scale feature saliency map. Lastly, a morphological closing operation is performed on the image to fill any holes within the circuit and eliminate small target areas that are below the predefined threshold. The results demonstrate that the proposed method in this study achieves higher segmentation performance, compared to the threshold method, region method, and edge method.

articleTitle: Optimal Control Design of Multi-Agent Pursuit-Evasion Game with Malicious Pursuer Environment
abstract: This paper proposes optimal control policies for multiagent pursuit-evasion game problem under a malicious environment based on reinforcement learning method. Firstly, the healthy pursuers and malicious pursuers are established by using subjectively malicious factor in the cost function and establish a game framework to study the relationship between healthy pursuers, malicious pursuers, and evaders. Then the Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) equations are used to gain the optimal control strategys. In addition, Nash equilibrium analysis is given. Then the adaptive weight adjustment of the critic-actor neural networks(NNs) are used to achieve the approximation of the control strategys and value functions. Finally, numerical simulation verifies the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Interval Observer Design for Multi-Rate Systems with Multiplicative Noises
abstract: An interval observer is designed for multi-rate systems with multiplicative noises in this paper. First, a multi-rate sampling system is investigated. At the same time, the presence of multiplicative noise would couple with the multi-rate sampling mechanism, which brings a significant challenge for the estimate of the system states. To address this problem, some arithmetic rules are proposed to separate the noise-contaminated terms, and the multi-rate system is transformed into an equivalent system with a uniform sampling period using the lifting technique and augmentation methods. Based on this, an interval observer is developed to estimate the bounds of the system states, sufficient conditions to ensure the effectiveness of the interval observer, and the input-to-state stability (ISS) of the estimation error dynamics are derived. Finally, simulations verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Nets Model Based on Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network for Multi-Step Prediction
abstract: The precise forecasting of traffic data holds significant importance for numerous practical applications in the real world. The challenge lies in the nonlinear spatio-temporal dependencies of the data, as well as rapid error accumulations for multi-step predictions. Therefore, we propose a Generative Adversarial Nets model based on a Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network (STGAT-GAN). Utilizing spatio-temporal graph attention proves to be an effective method for capturing the spatio-temporal dependencies, while GANs can learn a rich distribution over spatio-temporal data implicitly to produce realistic data adversarially. Experiments are carried out on two public traffic datasets. Comparative experimental analysis reveals that the proposed STGAT-GAN has better performance.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling of Wireless Channel Characteristics in Mobile Internet of Things
abstract: Channel feature analysis and channel modeling are the foundation for designing mobile IoT wireless communication systems. Firstly, for different application scenarios, channel characterization and channel models of the characteristics of wireless channels in the mobile Internet of Things are analyzed from two aspects: large-scale fading and small-scale fading. Then, three types of channel modeling methods, deterministic modeling, statistical modeling, and machine learning modeling are summarized. Finally, the future challenges of wireless channel modeling in the mobile Internet of Things were explored.

articleTitle: A Novel Fractional Order Non-Singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control Scheme for Quadrotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
abstract: This work gives a novel fractional order non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control (FONFTSMC) method, which can solve the problem of trajectory tracking of quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The controller design of the UAV is divided into a position subsystem controller and an attitude subsystem controller, the required roll and pitch angles are generated by the outer loop control subsystem. The proposed method introduces the fractional order operators to a non-singular fast terminal sliding surface. The new method can drive UAV to achieve tracking tasks faster than corresponding integer order methods. The convergence process of each state of UAV is also relatively smooth. The stability analysis is studied by the Lyapunov theory. And the superiority of new method is verified by numerical validation.

Author Keywords: non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control

articleTitle: Text Spotting of Electrical Equipment Nameplate Based on CTPN and Transformer
abstract: Given the complex image background, non-uniform text format, and diverse character types of electrical equipment nameplates, we propose a text spotting method for electrical equipment nameplates based on CTPN and Transformer. First, to overcome the disadvantage that the original CTPN cannot detect the tilted text lines, we add a nameplate localization and correction network based Xception to locate the nameplate region and correct it before text detection. Second, we use ResNet50 to replace the feature extraction network of CTPN, adjust the width of the text proposed region, and add a L2 regularization term during the training process to better adapt to the text detection of electrical equipment nameplate. Third, a text recognition network based on Transformer using ResNet50 to form an encoder and Transformer as a decoder is employed to improve the recognition accuracy of multiple kinds of characters. Evaluated on a self-built nameplate dataset consisting of 550 equipment nameplate images and a public nameplate dataset consisting of 3,949 text instance images, the F1 score of the nameplate text detection model is 88.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and the character recognition accuracy and text line recognition accuracy of the nameplate text recognition model are 92.3% and 85.6%, respectively. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively reduces the effects caused by complex backgrounds and skewed captured images, and is better adapt to the text spotting of electrical equipment nameplate.

articleTitle: Automatic mouth sampling based on computer vision and robot control
abstract: With the increasing application of robots, the automated and unmanned operation is becoming a new trend. In the scenario of nucleic acid sampling, the medical staff are under great exposure to high-risk substances. Compared to humans, unmanned sampling has higher accuracy and round-the-clock service capabilities, most importantly, it protects the medical staff from getting infected. To accomplish the benefit reached by the robot, an automatic nucleic acid sampling method based on computer vision and robot control is proposed in this paper. The pipeline first obtains 2D image coordinates of the target sampling points by YOLO detection algorithm, then translates the 2D image coordinates to 3D robot base coordinates, and finally controls the robot to achieve automatic mouth sampling. Experiment results demonstrate the feasibility and accuracy of the pipeline.

articleTitle: State-of-Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Battery Based on Linguistic Description Considering Capacity Regeneration
abstract: Owing to the wide application of lithium-ion batteries in industry, it is of great significance for accurate prediction of battery state of health (SOH) to ensure the safety and stability of equipment. The battery capacity regeneration (CR) during capacity degradation affects the accuracy of capacity prediction. This study proposes a hybrid estimation method for state of health of lithium-ion batteries based on linguistic description (LD) considering capacity regeneration. First, the capacity degradation data is decoupled into the trend component and the capacity regeneration component by the variational mode decomposition (VMD). Second, in order to improve the accuracy and reliability of battery capacity prediction, the capacity regeneration part is described by linguistic description. Finally, the trend part and the linguistic description sequence of capacity regeneration are predicted by support vector regression (SVR) model and long short term memory network with attention mechanism (Attn-LSTM) respectively, and their forecast results are superposed as the battery capacity prediction. The experimental results in NASA battery data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Equivalent Inertia Assessment Method of PV-Battery Hybrid System Considering VSM
abstract: The large-scale application of photovoltaic power generations effectively reduce the greenhouse gas emissions in the field of power production, further more promote the realization of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals; but increasing proportion of photovoltaic power generations with the power electronic equipment as the interface also make the power system characterized by low inertia, low damping and weak support. In response to this, photovoltaic power plants often enhance their inertia by installing energy storage or modifying control strategies, thereby enhancing their frequency and voltage support capabilities. In this paper a reasonable operational architecture for the photovoltaic-battery hybrid system is proposed, which is based on the principles of virtual synchronous machine and the inertial response mechanism of energy storage, additionally an equivalent inertia evaluation method is presented, which considers virtual synchronous machine. Finally, through simulation based on typical cases, the mechanism of inertia enhancement is analyzed, and the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed inertia evaluation method are verified.

articleTitle: Research on Amphibious Spherical Robot with Water Surface Posture Self-Stabilization
abstract: This paper presents an amphibious spherical robot with water surface posture stability. The robot is equipped with two sets of propulsion systems: an internal pendulum and a pair of main-secondary motors for rolling motion, and external left and right propellers for water surface propulsion motion. To enable autonomous motion of the water surface spherical robot, a path planning framework is designed, and linear and angular velocity controllers are developed based on the PID control algorithm. Additionally, by controlling the main-secondary motors, the robot exhibits both stranding resistance and self-stabilization posture capability. The experiments confirm that the robot autonomously follows predefined paths with accurate linear and angular velocity control and exhibit satisfactory self-stabilization ability on the water surface.

articleTitle: Adaptive Optimal Stabilization Regulation of Continuous-Time Systems via Virtual System and Measurement Feedback
abstract: This study presents a novel technique to solve stabilizing regulation for continuous-time systems via adaptive/approximate dynamic programming. To be more precise, first, a new virtual system is created to replace the existing one. Then, the state and state differential virtual values are created by an observer utilizing the output and input virtual values. To develop the controller based on data-driven, we take into account the value iteration approach. Compared with existing adaptive dynamic programming methods, the method proposed in this study does not require integral operation and observation of all states. Finally, a simulation example concludes by demonstrating the algorithm's usefulness.

articleTitle: A Regularized Non-Parametric Denoising Method
abstract: In the previous non-parametric denoising algorithms, there are problems in that the denoised curves deviate from the distribution of the expected result and are not smooth enough. In this paper, we propose a regularized non-parametric denoising method (RegNP) to tackle it. Aiming to suppress the shift of the curve, we introduce a regularization term to the objective function. For the improvement of smoothness, move the improved initialized data by gradient descent. During the experiments, the relationship between the standard deviation of the estimated noise and the optimal coefficient of the regularization term is established. We also propose a new workflow for denoising the signals with spikes. Experimental results indicate that compared with state-of-the-art methods, RegNP has achieved 3% to 53.6% performance gain under the root-mean-square-error(RMSE) metric.

articleTitle: Virtual Machine Software Aging Prediction of Cloud-Based Safe Computing Platform
abstract: With the application of cloud computing in rail transit signal system, the reliability of long-term application and service based on cloud computing has been paid more and more attention. Research has shown that software aging is an important factor affecting the safe operation of cloud platform. In response to the problems of poor universality, low prediction accuracy, and lack of research on cloud platform in train control system that exist in traditional aging analysis methods and prediction models, based on Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Time Convolution Network (TCN), a hybrid prediction model for virtual machine (VM) operation data on cloud platform is proposed. First, the original data is decomposed using the VMD optimized by SSA, and then each component is predicted using the SE-TCN model. Finally, use a fully connected network (FC) to fuse each component to obtain the final cloud resource usage prediction result. The analysis of the collected operational data shows that the prediction accuracy of the hybrid model is improved by 22% for Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and 27% for Mean Absolute Error (MAE), compared with that of other models, it has high prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Guidance Law with Impact Angle Constraints Considering Autopilot Dynamics
abstract: For maneuvering threats, a unique guiding law with considerations for impact angle constraint, autopilot dynamic features, and fixed-time convergence is devised. First, a backstepping approach is used to build the guiding law based on non-singular terminal sliding mode control. To address the issue of “differential expansion” in traditional backstepping control, a first-order nonlinear filter is introduced to filter the virtual quantity. To tackle the lag problem in the autopilot, a second-order dynamic model of the autopilot is incorporated to reduce the delay. Then, the fixed-time convergence of the guidance law is demonstrated using the Lyapunov stability theory. Lastly, the superiority and efficacy of the suggested guidance law are illustrated by simulations.

articleTitle: Modeling and Strategy Consensus of Networked Evolutionary Games with Random Variations of Payoff
abstract: This paper studies a kind of networked evolutionary games (NEGs) with random variations of payoff (RVP). The strategy update rule is unconditional imitation rule. Firstly, a procedure is proposed to model the NEGs with RVP. Secondly, a criterion is given for the finite-time strategy consensus of NEGs with probability one. Thirdly, the robustness analysis is carried out for the strategy profile dynamics in a particular anti-coordination game. Finally, several examples are proposed to illustrate the primary results.

articleTitle: Application of Random Forest MR Spinal Image Labeling Based on Multi-Feature Mergence
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is one of the important auxiliary methods in the diagnosis of spinal diseases. In this paper, an automatic labeling method of random forest spine based on multi-feature mergence is proposed. Since the coccygeal vertebrae feature is prominent and easy to identify, this paper firstly adopts HOG and GLCM meshing to extract mergence features from the coccygeal vertebrae, and combines the mergence feature with random forest to identify and label the coccygeal vertebrae. On the basis of coccygeal vertebra identification, the HOG feature after 2DPCA is combined with the random forest to identify and label the other vertebra. In addition, the multi-scale sliding window search method is used for image traversal, the redundant information of recognition results is removed by calculating IOU, and the overall sequence image annotation results are optimized by combining the matrix coordinate information between each layer of the magnetic resonance image, which increases the recognition accuracy and improves the robustness of the algorithm. Compared with MLP, SVM and other algorithms, the algorithm adopted in this paper has better recognition accuracy, faster recognition speed, and lower hardware resource consumption.

articleTitle: Research on Denoising Method Based on Iterative SVD Decomposition
abstract: In response to the poor denoising ability of Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), and the extracted motion waveform containing some residual noise signals, this paper proposes an iterative SVD decomposition denoising method. Firstly, the original signal is constructed into a binary recursive matrix form, and then SVD decomposition is used to obtain singular values with different contributions to the original matrix. Then, singular values with small contributions are discarded, while those with large contributions are retained. By modifying the signal reconstruction method, the denoised signal can be obtained once, and the required signal can be obtained by repeating the above process continuously. In simulation experiments and tuning fork vibration experiments, this article uses the iterative SVD decomposition denoising method and two existing denoising methods to denoise signals containing noise and uses signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and root mean square error method (RMSE) as denoising performance indicators for data comparison, confirming the effectiveness and superiority of iterative SVD decomposition denoising method and its excellent denoising ability. In the tuning fork vibration experiment, the error between the measured results and the actual results is 0.3125%, proving that this denoising method has practical application value.

articleTitle: Observer-based Sliding Mode Control of Non-commensurate Fractional-Order Flexible Manipulator Against Actuator Attack
abstract: This article addresses the sliding mode secure control problem for fractional-order flexible manipulator subject to actuator attack. By designing a fractional-order super-twisting sliding mode extended state observer (FOSTSM-ESO), a sliding mode control scheme based on the estimated system states and unknown actuator attack is proposed. The system stability is analyzed based on the fractional Lyapunov function. Numerical simulations are finally provided to demonstrate the validity of the proposed secure control method.

Author Keywords: Super-twisting sliding mode extended state observer

articleTitle: Kinematic Analysis and Trajectory Planning of a Series-Parallel Hybrid Peristaltic Robot
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the kinematic model of a series-parallel hybrid peristaltic robot and investigate its trajectory planning in an obstacle environment. The kinematic model of the series-parallel hybrid peristaltic robot was analyzed and developed. The C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>ODE and Tau theory are used to plan the trajectory of the peristaltic robot with the shortest joint space path as the objective function and obstacle avoidance as the hard constraint. Finally, the results of simulation tests demonstrate that the proposed trajectory planning method has successfully planned smooth, collision-free and low energy-loss joint space trajectories for the peristaltic robot.

articleTitle: Sparse Full Space Industrial Process Monitoring Method Based on Deep Autoencoder Neural Network
abstract: Deep autoencoder (DAE) is widely used in nonlinear feature extraction and dimension reduction, and also plays an important role in industrial process monitoring. The existing studies on process monitoring based on DAE do not make full use of the information in the feature space, which makes it difficult to improve the monitoring performance. To solve this issue, this paper proposes a full space process monitoring method. Furthermore, a sparse constraint method based on £2,p norm is proposed in this work to address the potential feature redundancy issue in full space process monitoring. The experimental results on the Tennessee Eastman Industrial dataset and Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on UAV Control Based on ESO-Based Global Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Adaptive Control
abstract: In this paper, a global fast terminal sliding mode controller based on an extended state observer is proposed for for precise tracking of reference trajectories of unmanned aerial vehicles with uncertain parameters. First, for the dynamics model of underdriven strong coupling of quadrotor, the theory of differential flatness is introduced to transform the model into a fully driven model, and the coupling terms in the model are considered as external perturbations. Then a global fast sliding mode controller is designed based on the position error and velocity error, and an extended state observer is introduced in the controller to observe the internal and external perturbations of the system. Finally, the adaptive law estimation parameters are designed for the problem of parameter changes when the quadrotor performs its mission to ensure the accurate and stable tracking on the trajectory of the quadrotor. The simulation experiments prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Road Segmentation for Remote Sensing Images Based on Global Feature Attention ResUnet
abstract: In current road segmentation methods for remote sensing images, high-level semantic features (such as roads and shadows) are often lost in the decoding process, resulting in a decrease in the accuracy of road segmentation. To solve this problem, we strengthened the correlation between shallow and deep features in a typical U-Net framework using two global attention mechanisms (channel and spatial) as follows. We first extract the features of the image in ResUnet's decoder and calculate channel attention on these features. we then map all features to shallow features and define spatial attention, which enhances the representation of deep spatial semantic information on the shallow feature. The feature maps processed by the global channel attention and global spatial attention are then combined with the ResUnet decoder for feature fusion and up-sampling, finally producing the road segmentation result. Experimental results show that our model effectively resolves the discontinuity problem in road segmentation and significantly improves the accuracy of road extraction from remote sensing images.

articleTitle: Adaptive Neural Networks Control for Fractional-Order Uncertain Nonlinear Systems via Command Filter Technique
abstract: This work investigates the adaptive neural networks (NNs) control for non-strict feedback fractional-order nonlinear systems (FONSs) while considering the presence of external disturbance and uncertainty. To address the issue of the “explosion of terms”, an adaptive neural controller is devised utilizing the fractional-order command filter, backstepping method and Lyapunov stability theory. The adaptive NNs controller can not only ensure the stability of the closed-loop FONSs but also drive the tracking error to converge to a neighborhood near the origin. Simulation example demonstrates the effectiveness of algorithm.

articleTitle: Disturbance Utilization-Based Alignment Control for Laser Communication Satellites With Multiple Disturbances
abstract: The alignment control of laser communication satel-lites is influenced by multiple disturbances such as alignment mechanism vibration and external disturbance, which makes the control design of the alignment system more challenging. To address this difficulty, an alignment control scheme based on disturbance utilization is proposed. Firstly, considering the influence of alignment mechanism vibration and external distur-bance, the deep coupled alignment model of laser communication satellites is established. Subsequently, a disturbance observer is designed to estimate the mechanism vibration and external disturbance. Based on the disturbance observer, a disturbance discrimination operator is constructed to distinguish the ben-eficial and detrimental disturbances. Finally, according to the disturbance observer and disturbance discrimination operator, a disturbance utilization controller is designed to compensate for detrimental disturbances and utilize beneficial disturbances, thereby achieving high-precision alignment control for laser communication satellites. Furthermore, prescribed performance function is introduced to ensure that the alignment error of satellites converges according to the predefined convergence rate and residual set. The feasibility of the designed control scheme is verified in simulation.

articleTitle: Surface Defect Detection of Heat Sink Based on Federated Learning and Improved UNet
abstract: Surface defect detection directly affects product quality and is essential for industrial production. However, the detection accuracy is limited due to the imbalanced ratio between defective and normal pixels in the samples. In order to address this issue and achieve efficient and accurate heat sink surface defect detection, a federated learning-based Ghost-ECA Separable UNet (FL-GESUNet) model is put forward. Firstly, the GESUNet model is proposed, which contains the Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) module, Ghost module, and separable convolution. This novel combination can reduce the model parameters while maintaining high accuracy. Secondly, in order to overcome the problem of the large gap between the proportion of defective and normal pixels, a hybrid loss function is proposed. The Lovasz Softmax loss and Softmax loss are combined to improve the model's ability to detect defective pixels. Finally, a federated learning (FL) detection framework is introduced to protect data privacy and improve data security. Comparative experiments show that GESUNet achieves an accuracy of 97.99 %, which outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on the heat sink surface defect dataset.

articleTitle: Internal Model Control of Piezoceramic Actuator Based on The Normalized Boue-Wen Model
abstract: The hysteresis nonlinearity of the piezoelectric actuator is the primary factor influencing signal tracking accuracy. To address this issue, we introduce an Modified normalized Bouc-Wen model specifically tailored to capture the hysteresis characteristics of the piezoelectric actuator. The model parameters are identified based on the differential evolution algorithm. Compared with the traditional Bouc-Wen model, the improved normalized Bouc-Wen model we propose is more suitable for modeling actual piezoelectric actuators. In addition, based on the invertibility analysis of the improved normalized Bouc-Wen model, an internal mode control scheme is designed in this article using the established hysteresis inverse model. Thus to realize the precision tracking control of piezoelectric actuators. Subsequently, we validate the efficacy of our proposed control scheme on a piezoelectric experimental platform utilizing dSPACE. Experimental results demonstrate that the relative error of the tracking control, based on internal model control, is less than 9%, meeting the necessary engineering requirements.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Attitude Tracking Control for Quadrotor UAV with Input Delay
abstract: In this paper, the predefined time attitude tracking flight problem for a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) system with input delays is investigated. By means of a novel auxiliary system, the effects of input delay are solved. Then, on the basis of the backstepping method and predefined performance control technology, the predefined-time attitude tracking controller is constructed to make UAV attitude tracking. Simulation results verify the validity of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Model-Based Adaptive Neural Control for Discrete Nonlinear Systems Using Round Robin Protocol
abstract: This paper studies the output tracking control problem for a class of networked discrete strict-feedback non-linear systems. To avoid data collision and make rational use of the limited communication resources, a model-based neural network control scheme using round-robin protocol for sensor-to-controller communication scheduling is proposed. First, to avoid possible data collision caused by the exclusive use of the sensor-to-controller channel, the round-robin protocol is adopted for communication scheduling. Then, to ensure the continuous update of the system data, a neural network dynamic model is constructed to continuously estimate the system states. Afterwards, an adaptive neural controller with a novel weight updating law is designed on the basis of constructed dynamic model. Finally, stability analysis and a simulation study on a numerical model and a three-wheeled mobile vehicle are presented to illustrate the validity of this scheme.

articleTitle: Circle Formation Control for Multi-Agent Systems: A Distributed Optimization Perspective
abstract: This paper presents a distributed algorithmic frame-work for solving the circle formation control problem with multi-agent systems. Distinct from the existing approaches, our work starts from the distributed optimization perspective. Building on the game theory, we develop two sequential update schemes, i.e., the Gauss-Seidel iteration and Jacobi iteration, both of which are theoretically proved to be capable of forming the desired circle formation. Though our algorithms end up with the quite similar form as compared to the existing ones, our proofs of convergence are completely new and provide more insights on the formation control problem. In addition, an exclusively promising benefit of our algorithms is the plug-and-play feature, i.e., adapting the change of agents automatically without requiring a prescribed configuration beforehand. Extensive numerical results are finally provided to show the effectiveness of our algorithms.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking of Wheeled AGV Based on Adaptive Sliding Mode Control Using Backstepping Method
abstract: The objective of this paper is to investigate the application of adaptive sliding mode control using backstepping method (ASMC) to a differential-wheeled automatic guided vehicle (DWAGV) system. Traditional sliding mode control methods are prone to system parameter variations and external disturbances, while ASMC can adapt to these changes by dynamically adjusting the controller parameters. The paper begins by introducing the modeling of the DWAGV system, followed by the design of a sliding mode function using the backstepping method. The controller is then designed based on the method of constant speed convergence. However, since the coefficients in the convergence law are constant, they cannot achieve realtime control. To address this problem, an adaptive convergence law is proposed that online adjusts the gain parameters of the controller to improve system performance. Additionally, to account for noise interference in real-world conditions, a low-pass filter is designed to filter the noise in the control quantity. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted using Matlab, with Gaussian noise added at each time step to test the system's anti-interference capability. The result demonstrates that ASMC method can maintain good control performance of DWAGV system under external disturbances and has excellent trajectory tracking performance. These findings confirm the effectiveness and feasibility of ASMC in the autonomous navigation control of the DWAGV.

articleTitle: Deep Census Weight Correlation Stereo Network
abstract: Stereo depth estimation is of great importance in autonomous driving, unmanned system operation and other intelligent visual tasks. At present, large textureless and uneven illumination regions are still the difficult problems for stereo matching tasks. To promote the stereo matching network to effectively utilize the feature information of the uneven illumination regions and the large textureless regions, we proposed the census weight correlation cost volume construction method which can selectively construct the illumination feature informaiton into the cost volume. The census weight correlation volume is a differentiable transformation of the traditional census-based matching cost computation. Extensive experiments show that the proposed census weight correlation volume can effectively improved the performance in the large textureless and uneven illumination regions compared with the original correlation volume and our network has achieved excellent performance on Scene Flow datasets, KITTI 2012 datasets and KITTI 2015 datasets.

articleTitle: Real-Time Tobacco Leaf Image Segmentation for Tobacco Strip Structure Based on Improved STDCNet
abstract: In cigarette production, tobacco strip structure directly affects the quality of tobacco in subsequent flue-cured tobacco processes, which in turn is related to the quality of cigarettes and the consumption of tobacco leaves.We propose an improved STDCNet algorithm for real-time segmentation of tobacco leaf images, which has excellent performance in our dataset. The IoU reaches 94.82%, which is 3.61% higher than the baseline algorithm STDCNet; FPS has reached 108.54, meeting the real-time requirements in industrial production.

articleTitle: Global Path Planning of AUV Based on GA-SQP Algorithm
abstract: In actual navigation of Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV), global path planning and local path planning should work in coordination. However, when applied to large-scale complex underwater environment, most algorithms have the disadvantage of low search efficiency. In this paper, factors such as terrain threats, navigation distance and energy loss are considered to construct the constraints and objective function of AUV global path planning. By combining integrating Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) algorithm, the GA-SQP algorithm is proposed to realize the global path planning of AUV in complex underwater environment. This method has the strong robustness and global optimality of the GA algorithm, and effectively inherits the advantages of SQP algorithm in convergence speed and computing efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that the GA-SQP algorithm can plan the shortest path for AUV in complex underwater environment, and meet the requirements of underwater safety constraints and minimum energy loss.

articleTitle: Common-Mode Resonance Current Suppression Method for the Transformerless Reduced Switch Count Three-Level Inverter With LCCL Filter
abstract: The LCCL filter can be employed with the transformerless inverter to mitigate the leakage current, which however generates the common-mode resonance current (CMRC) and oscillations in the inverter-side currents. Owing to the inherent features of the reduced switch count three-level inverter (RSC-TLI), the medium vectors are unable to be generated, which implies that the conventional method cannot be applied straightforward. This article presents a novel strategy to suppress the CMRC in the RSC-TLI with LCCL filter, which regulates the duty cycles of small vectors by using distribution factors. Compared to conventional passive damping technique, the CMRC and leakage current are restrained by the presented strategy. As a result, the oscillations of inverter-side currents are mitigated, while the system cost is reduced. Evaluation results confirm the feasibility of the presented method.

articleTitle: Parameters Estimation of Three-Phase Induction Motors Using Whale Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Accurate parameters estimation is essential for efficient vector control and beneficial for energy-saving control for induction motors in the context of carbon neutrality. The whale optimization algorithm (WOA) is employed in this study to estimate several particular parameters of three-phase induction motors (TIMs). In this paper, two-phase stationary coordinate system is adapted for motor modeling. In the WOA, the square differences between the measured and the estimated currents of the TIM are minimized. The computational results show that the currents calculated from the parameters estimated by the WOA are highly consistent with the measured values. Finally, the comparison study among the WOA, the grey wolf optimization (GWO) and the particle swarm optimization is conducted. The comparative results also demonstrate the superiority of WOA in estimation accuracy and convergence speed.

articleTitle: Optimal Tracking Control For Linear Time-Varying Systems With Unknown System Dynamics
abstract: Conventionally, there needs two equations to solve the traditional optimal tracking problem, a Riccati equation solved in a feed-backward way and a non-causal difference equation solved in a feed-forward way. In this paper, an alternative augmented system is introduced to show that in the time-varying case, the tracking problem can be resolved in a similar way as the regulation problem since they are equivalent. In this study, we employ a reinforcement learning method to develop an off-policy policy iteration algorithm that solves the linear optimal tracking problem for time-varying systems with unknown system dynamics. The simulation example provided in this paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Global-Local Contrastive Learning for Graph Self-Reconstruction of Node-Attacked Complex Networks
abstract: Graph self-reconstruction (GraphSR) has the potential to improve the functional robustness and information transmission connectivity of a complex system that is under attack in many realistic scenarios. This paper proposes a global-local contrastive learning (GLCL) model for solving the GraphSR problem in node-attacked complex networks. In the GLCL model, the contrastive process is performed between the high-dimensional feature embeddings of the unattacked graph and that of the node-attacked graph to capture the projective relationship and obtain a self-reconstructed graph (SRe-Graph), whose function is similar to that of the unattacked graph. Specifically, by learning the relation of local and global feature embed dings between the unattacked graph and the SRe-Graph, the GLCL model strengthens the robustness and connectivity of the SRe-Graph. Numerical experiments simulating airport flight scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Registration Based Feature Core-Set Model for Defect Detection
abstract: Defect detection is an important issue in industrial applications. In this paper, we propose a few-shot defect detection model named registration based feature core-set model (RegiCore). The model learns the method of aligning image samples through a task-independent data set. It calculates the defect scores by comparing the registered features between the normal and the target images. The experimental results show that our model can effectively complete the task of defect detection and outperforms the comparison methods. Meanwhile, our model exhibits excellent ability to detect small defective targets.

articleTitle: Bionic Seal Whisker Based on Piezoelectric Nanogenerator for Vortex Perception
abstract: In order to perceive the vortex in the flow field environment and obtain the disturbance frequency of the vortex, a vortex sensor based on the seal whisker was proposed by imitating the mechanism of the seal whisker to perceive and track prey. The designed bionic seal whisker imitates the unique biological structure of seal whiskers and combines the principle of piezoelectric nanogenerators. The bionic seal whisker uses polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) as the main material, and a piezoelectric perceiving unit made of polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) is encapsulated at the bottom. By comparing and analyzing simulation data with experimental data, the results indicate that the bionic seal whiskers have great vortex perception effects and great potential in underwater flow field vortex perception.

articleTitle: Goal-Biased Rapidly-Exploring Random Trees for Efficient Marine Path Planning
abstract: This paper presents a goal-biased rapidly-exploring random tree (RRT) approach for rapid path planning in marine environments. The key innovation integrates a goal-biased sampling strategy to enable more efficient exploration towards the goal region compared to the traditional RRT algorithm. The implementation also incorporates an artificial potential field-inspired steering method for smoother paths and a path optimization technique adapted from prior work to reduce redundant nodes. The proposed goal-biased RRT planner was validated on a real-world marine map, demonstrating significantly improved path planning performance over state-of-the-art RRT variants, like Informed-RRT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> and RRT*-Smart algorithm, including optimized path length, faster computation, and better scalability. The efficiency gains address challenges of robotic marine navigation to some extent by providing a rapid, smooth, and optimized planning algorithm well-suited for applications like autonomous surface vehicles (ASV) in complex seascapes. Results highlight the method's characteristics and advantages for efficient path generation across real-world environments.

articleTitle: Synchronization of Second-Order Networked Multi-Agent Systems with Relative Delay
abstract: In this paper, the synchronous control of second-order networked multi-agent systems with relative state delay between agents is studied. A synchronous protocol based on relative state feedback is proposed and the condition of system state synchronization is obtained. The results show that the Rendezvous Speed of the system tends to zero asymptotically under positive relative delay, and give a sufficient condition for the Rendezvous Speed of the system to reach zero. The theoretical results are verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analyses of Integral-Type Zhang Neurodynamics with Disturbances Inhibited Handling Temporally-Varying Nonlinear System of Equations
abstract: We design and present an integral-type Zhang neurodynamics (ITZN) model for handling temporally-varying nonlinear system of equations (TVNSE). To investigate the disturbances inhibition of the model, the general form of the disturbed ITZN model is presented, and it is instantiated by introducing the constant disturbance, bounded random disturbance, and linear-form temporally-varying disturbance, resulting in three corresponding disturbed ITZN variants. Finally, by means of Lyapunov theory and Laplace transformation, we theoretically prove the globally exponential convergence of the ITZN model and the effective disturbances inhibition of the three disturbed ITZN variants.

articleTitle: Research on the self-powered and flexible pressure tactile sensor based on triboelectric nanogenerator for manipulator
abstract: With the wide application of manipulators in various fields, the requirements for manipulators are also increasing. Stable grasping of tools and unknown objects is one of the important capabilities of manipulators, which is inseparable from the good tactile perception system of manipulators. As the information of tactile sensing system, it is still a great challenge to provide accurate pressure tactile information for manipulators. An electromechanical pressure tactile sensor based on triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) is presented in this paper. The device is inspired by cats. The soft-convex structure effectively senses pressure information and provides support and cushioning. The sensor is composed of a convex hemisphere of ecoflex film, copper film and conductive sponge. As a result of the experimental results, PT-TENG has proven to be able to detect pressures between 1N and 10N with great accuracy. As a pressure sensor, it is characterized by self-power, flexibility, high durability, and high-frequency applicability, which provides a new idea and research direction for pressure haptics in manipulators.

articleTitle: Virtual Sample Generation Methods and Application in Few-Shot Object Detection for Industrial Scenarios
abstract: Due to the long-term relatively fixed state of industrial installations, the diversity of industrial data is low, with high repetitiveness and uneven distribution, which makes industrial few-shot object detection still challenging. Therefore, from the perspective of handling the dataset, this paper proposes a virtual sample generation method based on virtual reality. Firstly, by using a virtual engine, the target workpiece model is created to directly simulate the states of the workpieces captured by the visual system in various environments. Secondly, random algorithms are added and improved to simulate workpieces with different materials and degrees of wear, distributed in random positions with different poses and types in the visual system, thereby generating virtual samples containing workpieces. Finally, virtual samples are introduced for experimental testing in the target detection network. The proposed method is tested in both YOLOv5 and YOLOv7 and compared with datasets without virtual samples, resulting in an improvement of 3.06% and 2.23% in mAP values, respectively. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves the issue of industrial small-sample object detection.

articleTitle: Active Fault Tolerant Control of Networked Control Systems with Random Packet Loss
abstract: A new fault diagnosis (FD) and fault-tolerant control (FTC) methodology for networked control systems (N CSs) subject to random packet loss is studied. The Bernoulli process is utilized to describe the packet loss. A robust FD observer is constructed to reconstitute the system state and fault. On the basis of the estimated fault information and other measurement data, the model predictive tracking fault-tolerant controller is designed to make the output of the post-fault NCS can still track the given output. The efficacy of the put forward algorithm is authenticated by computer simulation.

articleTitle: Target Circumnavigation Control with an Unmanned Surface Vehicle based on Relative Range Measurements
abstract: This paper considers the problem of uncooperative target circumnavigation with an unmanned surface vehicle (USV) in the marine environment. The vehicle is driven to circumnavigate the target with the desired radius. A coordinate-free controller with a designed saturation function is proposed using only the local relative range information. The stability of the proposed algorithm is theoretically guaranteed by Lyapunov control theory. Moreover, a second-order sliding mode (SOSM) observer combined with linear and nonlinear terms is designed to estimate the range rate with respect to the target. The global stability and convergence are also proved using the Lyapunov theory. Finally, numerical simulations and real experiments with a USV are carried out to show the effectiveness of proposed approach. The results show that the steady-state circumnavigation error converges to zero and the SOSM observer can recover the real range rate within finite time.

articleTitle: Pseudo Huber Functions-Based NMPC for Tracking of Agricultural Harvester
abstract: The nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) based on pseudo-Huber functions is studied for the trajectory tracking problem of agricultural harvesters. For the unstable value of the huber function, an improved pseudo-Huber functions is designed to get better stability and control accuracy. The pseudo-Huber function, and the quadratic punishment function are combine to construct cost function. The trigonometric function of heading error is introduced to avoid the problem of heading circling. The dynamic model of the harvester is raised, and the nonlinear solver CasADi is used to optimize the solution of the controller. Subsequently, simulation is carried out in the straight line and the steering trajectory, and a new evaluation index is proposed to prove the effectiveness of the controller. In comparison with the traditional NMPC based on error cost function, the tracking accuracy is obviously improved.

articleTitle: Variations in Right Ascension of Ascending Node of Sun-Synchronous Orbit Under the Lunar and Solar Perturbations
abstract: Earth-observation satellites carrying synthetic aperture radar (SAR) instruments are typically deployed on the exact repeat-ground-track (RGT) sun-synchronous orbit (SSO) in order to achieve effective repeat-pass SAR interferometry. The exact RGT maintenance of these satellites have stringent requirements on the variation modeling accuracy of right ascension of ascending node (RAAN). Due to the significant effects of third-body attraction on the orbital plane evolutions, variations of RAAN under the lunar and solar perturbations are modeled for the SSO with local time of descending node at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00, and 18:00. An analytic method for RAAN variation modeling is proposed based on the quasi-mean element method. Coupling effects between the J2 perturbation and third-body attractions are considered to achieve a high precision of the variation model. Comparisons with precise numerical orbit propagator show that the analytical method provides good results for lunar and solar perturbation modeling on the variations of RAAN. The maximum relative error is only 2.6% and 5% for lunar and solar perturbations, respectively.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Boundedness for a Class of Nonlinear Descriptor Hamiltonian Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the finite-time boundedness problem for a class of nonlinear descriptor Hamiltonian systems. First of all, a controller is designed to transform the nonlinear descriptor Hamiltonian system into a strictly dissipative differential-algebraic system. Then, the finite-time boundedness of nonlinear descriptor Hamiltonian system is proved by strictly dissipative differential-algebraic system. Finally, a nonlinear descriptor circuit system, for example, to prove the effectiveness of the designed controller.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Line-of-Sight Guidance Law for Trajectory Tracking of USV with LADRC
abstract: This article proposes an trajectory tracking control strategy for underactuated unmanned surface vessels (USVs) by combining an improved line-of-sight (LOS) guidance law and an adaptive disturbance rejection control (ADRC) approach considering unknown model parameters and time-varying external disturbances. In terms of kinematics, to eliminate the influence of wind, waves, and ocean currents, the proposed guidance law compensates for sideslip angle by means of adaptive control and is proved to be globally k-exponentially stable. With respect to kinetics, this study develops separate longitudinal velocity and heading angle controllers for USVs without requiring prior knowledge of the vessel's characteristics. These controllers are designed using the linear adaptive disturbance rejection control (LADRC) approach, which minimizes the number of parameters that need adjustment. The resulting composite trajectory tracking controller exhibits a concise form that facilitates practical implementation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: LW-PointNeRF: A Point-Based Neural Radiance Field with a Lightweight Multi-View Stereo Network
abstract: In recent years, there have been significant advancements in novel view synthesis using Neural Radiance Fields (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> eRF). NeRF's application is limited because of a considerable amount of training time. In this paper, we present a method called LW-PointNeRF. This method can rapidly reconstruct radiance fields while reducing the number of model parameters and computational requirements. Specifically, LW-PointNeRF comprises two main modules: the LW-MVS module and the Radiance Field module. The LW-MVS module employs a lightweight convolutional neural network to extract image features. It then uses plane sweeping to construct a cost volume for depth estimation, generating an initial point cloud. The Radiance Field module aligns the image features with the initial point cloud to get a neural point cloud. Finally, it aggregates the features of neighboring points to construct the radiance field. Experimental evaluations of LW-PointNeRF are conducted on the DTU, NeRF synthetic, and ScanNet datasets. LW-PointNeRF performs similarly to PointNeRF, but uses 25% fewer parameters and 14% less computation.

articleTitle: A Trajectory Re-Planning Method of Launch Vehicle Based on Multi-Source Information
abstract: Spacecraft will deviate from originally planned orbit during flight because of deviations, and the flight trajectory needs to be re-planned. Considering the remaining control capabilities of multiple information, the optimal shutdown and backup tracks were designed. Adaptive pseudo spectral and sequential quadratic programming algorithms can be used to ensure orbit insertion. Select the optimal target orbit that matches current capability based on current flight state and fault level, while satisfying constraints and residual capability. Finally, select the optimal guidance strategy to complete flight mission.

articleTitle: Optimization Study of ADRC Anti-Disturbance Improvement in Denitrification of Power Plant
abstract: NOx control has always been a difficult problem in power plant process control, often resulting in problems such as excessive ammonia injection and large control fluctuations. To solve this problem, a disturbance-reject control (DR-ADRC) scheme is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the steady-state error of the disturbance channel transfer function is analyzed. The results show that the system under traditional ADRC control is a type I system that can only overcome constant disturbances. For slope and acceleration disturbances, their steady-state errors will not converge to 0. Furthermore, based on the above complex disturbance characteristics, the DR-ADRC structure is proposed by ADRC controller structure modification, which can completely suppress slope disturbances and also have better suppression effects on other types of disturbances. Simulation and actual power plant testing results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed DR-ADRC method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power Equipment Status Perception in Unmanned Areas: A Micro-Energy Harvesting Self-Powered Wireless Sensor System
abstract: Insufficient capability for power equipment status perception in unmanned areas such as deserts and plateaus poses a challenge to improving operational efficiency. These regions boast abundant wind energy resources due to their unique geographical environment and climatic conditions, characterized by high and stable wind speeds. Additionally, they receive ample sunlight radiation, making the combined utilization of solar and wind energy an effective approach for energy development. However, challenges such as weak network coverage, high equipment maintenance costs, and battery replacement difficulties are commonly encountered in these uninhabited areas. To address these issues, this paper proposes a new micro-energy harvesting self-powered wireless sensor system. The monitoring nodes gather wind and light energy from the environment, converting it into electrical energy for power supply. The gateway, powered by fiber optics, collects sensor data from these self-powered monitoring nodes and transmits it to the substation. The gateway eliminates the need for additional batteries or backup power, enabling flexible deployment on transmission line towers without being constrained by network coverage limitations. Experimental results demonstrate that self-powered monitoring nodes can continuously operate without interruption when sufficient energy is available. Moreover, the gateway achieves data reception, with zero packet loss and zero bit error rate.

articleTitle: Adaptive NN Fault-Tolerant Control for Underactuated MSVs with Input Quantization
abstract: In this work, we have studied the problem of trajectory tracking control for underactuated marine surface vehicles (MSV s) subject to uncertain model parameters, unknown external disturbances, actuator undesirable faults, and input signal quantization. To effectively handle input signal quantization, a hysteresis quantizer is employed. The uncertain dynamics of the MSVs are approximated by using neural networks (NN). By resorting the adaptive technique to estimate an upper bound for the compound disturbances are lumped by time-varying external disturbances, actuator faults, and NN approximation errors. By introducing a continuous smooth function, the trajectory tracking control law was developed within backstepping frameworks. The theoretical deduce and simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the developed control strategy.

articleTitle: Establishment of a BOPPPS-AHP Model for Curriculum Quality Evaluation
abstract: Aiming at teaching of specialized courses, this paper constructs a model for addressing both teaching and evaluation methods. Taking the bridge-in, objective, pre-assessment, participatory learning, post-assessment and summary (BOPPPS) model as a teaching objective, the curriculum evaluation system is established by using the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) scheme. As a result, the course model of BOPPPS-AHP is proposed. The AHP evaluation model is established in the form of expert judgment and questionnaire survey, three first-level indicators, and twelve second-level indicators are established. By calculating the evaluation weights of each index and consistency test, it shows that the curriculum quality evaluation system with the proposed model is feasible to the course of Sensor Principle and Application. Through the comparison between the experimental group and the control group, the BOPPPS-AHP model is conducive to enhancing students' learning interest and comprehensive ability.

articleTitle: Predefined-Time Consensus Tracking of Uncertain Leader-following Multiagent Systems With High-Order Dynamics via Event-Triggered Control
abstract: In this paper, the predefined-time consensus of uncertain high-order leader-following multiagent systems is studied. First, a state observer that can achieve predefined-time consensus is proposed, so that the follower can quickly achieve consensus with the leader and stability. Then a new distributed controller is designed to enable the system to achieve consensus within a predefined time. In order to save network resources, an event-triggered controller based distributed controller signals is adopted. Finally, a simulation experiment is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in this paper.

articleTitle: An Artificial Bee Colony with Diversified Operators for Energy-Efficient Hybrid Flow Shop Scheduling with Batch Processing Machines
abstract: In this study, energy-efficient hybrid flow shop scheduling problem (EHFSP) with BPM at a middle stage is investigated, which exists in many real-life manufacturing processes such as casting, an artificial bee colony with diversified operators (DOABC) is presented to minimize makespan and total energy consumption. Four global search operators and three neighborhood search operators are applied and a dynamical way is used to dynamically decide search operator for each solution. The whole population is divided in some groups and reward and communication are conducted for groups. Four methods are adopted to select food source and an adaptive onlooker bee phase is implemented. The computational results demonstrate that the diversified operators are effective and DOABC has promising advantages on solving EHFSP with BPM.

articleTitle: EEG Channel and Spectrum Weighting Based Attention State Evaluation
abstract: Accurate and rapid attention state evaluation (ASE) is of great significance for many practical applications by providing criteria for diagnosis of diseases such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Common ASE methods including questionnaires, neurophysiological tasks and nervous system test, etc, heavily rely on the subjective judgment of professional clinicians leading to the cumbersome process of diagnosis. Recent studies showed that scalp EEG signals have a strong correlation with attention state. Therefore, a deep learning and EEG signals based ASE algorithm is proposed. Specially, two novel feature weighting modules for EEG electrode channels (CW) and spectrums (SW) are developed, respectively. The different weights are assigned to different electrode channels and spectrums by the CW and SW to extracted more important feature representations. Experiments are conducted on real-world physiological dataset for attention assessing (PhyDAA). The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Modeling Contagion Dynamics Based on Individual Contact Patterns Using Bond Percolation Theory
abstract: In recent years, various infectious diseases have erupted frequently worldwide, which has had a huge impact on people's health and social development. Therefore, it is necessary to study the transmission mechanism and control strategies of infectious diseases. In this paper, we propose a new epidemic transmission mode by using bond percolation in quantum physics. We character the real-life individual contact patterns as different transmission path trees and calculate binomial distribution function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P^{*}(p,\ n)$</tex> based on bond percolation. We fuse bond percolation into the SEIRD model and study percolation patterns how to influence outbreak threshold of epidemics. By analyzing key factors in the transmission process such as blocking probability, number of transmission paths, and configuration patterns, it shows that complex number of transmission paths will lead to larger scale of infection and virus transmission effectively suppressed by blocking probability. Then, experiments were conducted on BA scale-free networks to study the temporal relationships between different nodes and the impact of network structure on virus propagation. The experimental results demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed model. The model effectively describes the epidemic spreading process under different contact modes and the interactions between different nodes in networks, which provides theoretical basis and practical value for controlling epidemics.

articleTitle: STSR: Sequence-Based Scene Text Image Super-Resolution
abstract: When faced with low-resolution scene text images, the text recognizers often perform unsatisfactorily. Therefore, the super-resolution can be used as the preprocessing work to improve the accuracy of text recognition. However, current existing image super-resolution approaches mostly aim to recover the details of images while ignoring the text feature in text images. Besides, there is no specially designed loss functions for text images super-resolution. In this study, we propose a Sequence-based Scene Text Image Super-Resolution Network (STSR), in which the Bi-directional Text Sequential Block (Bi-TSB) is designed to capture the text sequential features. Meanwhile, the text sequential loss is proposed to supervise the text readability of the reconstructed image. The experimental results indicate that STSR outperforms the baseline methods in terms of SSIM and recognition accuracy in TextZoom dataset.

articleTitle: Orderly Charging Strategy for Electric Vehicles Based on Credit Evaluation
abstract: Introducing “Ability to fulfill contract” and “Willingness to fulfill contract” dual mode credit evaluation indicators into the orderly charging strategy of electric vehicles. Conduct credit evaluation and rating on electric vehicles, and modify the schedulable duration of electric vehicles participating in orderly charging strategies based on the credit rating results. Build a multi-objective optimization model to reduce the charging costs of electric vehicles and stabilize the load fluctuations of public alternating current charging station distribution network, and use the hybrid adaptive single parent genetic algorithm proposed in this paper to solve. The simulation results show that credit orderly charging strategy can significantly reduce charging costs of electric vehicles and reduce load fluctuations of public alternating current charging station distribution network. Compared to orderly charging strategies, credit orderly charging strategy better reflect the real situation of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Design of a Double Claw Pole-Climbing Robot
abstract: Aiming at the problem of human safety and work efficiency in high altitude complex environment, a rod-climbing robot system based on double-claw structure is proposed in this paper to realize real-time and reliable detection of rod-shaped objects. With seven movable joints and seven degrees of freedom, the robot system can flexibly complete tasks such as obstacle crossing, rotation and climbing. Through the establishment of the mechanical model of the robot system, the kinematics formula is derived, and the gait analysis and theoretical verification are carried out, which further proves the feasibility of the double claw pole-climbing robot system. Using high-strength alloy and servo motor, the prototype of the robot system is constructed. And the climbing experiment is carried out on the surface of the pole. The experimental results show that the structure and scheme of the robot system are feasible.

articleTitle: Infrared and Visible Image Fusion Based on Mutual Structure Extraction
abstract: Most existing methods for fusing infrared and visible images do not take into account the complementary and redundant relationships between the source images, resulting in a situation that the common information is improperly retained and the unique information is not adequately retained in the resulting image. To address this problem, this paper introduced an infrared and visible image fusion method based on mutual structure extraction. The mutually guided image filter is utilized to separate the common and unique information between source infrared and visible images firstly. Secondly, the unique information layer is decomposed into multiple scales and information exchange is performed in corresponding infrared and visible detail layers. Then the common information layer is fused based on visual saliency; the unique base layer is fused based on infrared information injection; the unique detail layers are fused based on local visual saliency and weighted average fusion rules. The fusion result generated by image reconstruction not only reasonably selects redundant features and fully retains complementary features but also significantly weaken the impact of noise, which is more convenient for human eyes to observe. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms other methods.

articleTitle: A Fixed-Wing UAV Swarm Coverage Search Strategy Based on Improved Weighted Mean of Vectors (IINFO) Algorithm
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm coverage path planning is computationally intensive and difficult to converge. For the problem of rapid acquisition of unknown sea information by UAV swarms, this paper proposes a fast coverage search strategy for fixed-wing UAV swarms based on improved weighted mean of vectors (IINFO) algorithm. First, a two-dimensional mission space model is established based on the mission environment and the flight characteristics of fixed-wing UAVs, and the trajectory planning problem is transformed into a multi-dimensional function optimization problem. Then, the mission area is divided to each fixed-wing UAV by IINFO algorithm. Finally, within the assigned mission area, this paper uses the planning method with the minimum number of turns to obtain the UAV trajectory. This paper selects a swarm of fixedwing UAVs carrying synthetic aperture radar (SAR) as a research object, comparing the improved beluga whale optimization (IBWO) algorithm, the improved brain storm optimization (IBSO) algorithm and the IINFO algorithm, the simulation results show that the trajectory search time planned by the IINFO Algorithm is the shortest, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dense Attention Network Based on Ordered Operation for Point Cloud Processing
abstract: Deep learning based 3D point cloud processing has become a new research hotspot. Existing methods either fail to fully exploit the three-dimensional characteristics of the points or ignore the connection among layers that are not directly connected. To solve these problems, this paper proposes a dense attention network based on Ordered operation for point cloud processing. We propose the O-edge module and a Residual Dual Channel Attention module (RDCAM) for point cloud feature extraction. The O-edge module is designed to extract edge features from ordered information by leveraging a series of one-dimensional convolutions, enabling better exploitation of the relations among points while retaining permutation invariant. RDCAM is used to draw network attention to key feature region. At the same time, we introduce the dense connection to point cloud processing to enhance information flow between layers. Experimental results show that the proposed network has higher classification accuracy than the existing networks on public benchmark of point cloud classification.

articleTitle: Dynamic Study of Underwater Submersible with Cable
abstract: Underwater submersible with cable is a common system in the field of marine engineering. In this paper, the submersible is considered as a rigid body, and a spatial six-degree-of-freedom model is developed by Newton's second law, and the flexible cable is modeled by the concentrated mass method to derive the equations of motion of the submersible with cable. Finally, the dynamic behavior of underwater submersible with cable is modeled and simulated using MATLAB Simulink to analyze the mutual influence of the cable and the submersible in separate and joint motion states.

articleTitle: Dynamic Alarm Causality Analysis Method Integrating Monitoring Contribution and Transfer Entropy
abstract: Alarm flooding poses a significant safety hazard in industry. It is of paramount importance to uncover the causality behind alarm flooding at its early stages. On one hand, limited data samples make it challenging to accurately determine the causal relationships among alarms. On the other hand, a massive volume of data samples may lead to delays in causal inference. This paper proposes a Contribution and Transfer-entropy based Dynamic Alarm Causality analysis method (CT-DAC) to address this. CT-DAC reconstructs the contribution of each monitored variable to the dynamic anomalies in the system, enabling dynamic causal relationship mining based on limited data. This approach offers a faster and more accurate solution for identifying the initial alarm causality triggering alarm flooding problems. Experimental work conducted on the Tennessee Eastman Process demonstrates the superior performance of the CT-DAC method.

articleTitle: A Semantic- Driven Multimodal Model for Chinese Spelling Checking
abstract: Chinese Spelling Checking (CSC) is a task to detect and correct spelling errors in Chinese text, which is important for natural language processing applications. Previous works on CSC have used pre-trained language models and multimodal information to improve the performance. However, most existing CSC models do not fully exploit the rich context knowledge contained in context, nor do they emphasize the role of semantic information for text error correction. In this paper, we propose a semantic-driven multimodal CSC model that can learn the heterogeneous knowledge of speech, vision and meaning from context. Our model consists of three encoders: a semantic encoder, a phonetic encoder, and a graphic encoder. To emphasize the role of semantics in text correction, we feed the output of the semantic encoder to both the phonetic encoder and the graphic encoder, along with the original input. The outputs of the three encoders are fused by an attention mechanism and decoded by a transformer model to generate the spell-check results. We evaluate our model on SIGHAN benchmark datasets. The experimental results show that our model outperforms the state-of-the-art methods on these datasets, especially on correcting long sentences with errors. We also conduct ablation studies and qualitative analysis to show the effectiveness of our model components and the semantic-driven mechanism.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Hierarchical Sliding Mode Control Scheme with Accurate Positioning and Sway Suppression for Underactuated Tower Cranes
abstract: Due to the non-linearity, high-coupling and under-actuated characteristics of tower cranes, the dynamics analysis is challenging. Although a simplified dynamic model of tower cranes is advantageous for analysis, the stability and accuracy of the system are difficult ensured, especially when the state variables deviate far from equilibrium points. Furthermore, the harsh working environment of tower cranes makes it difficult to obtain accurate friction parameters. Considering these factors, an actuated dynamic model for tower cranes is developed via a model transformation approach. The model is not simplified, moreover the unknown frictions and underactuated characteristics are fully considered. Based on the developed model, an adaptive hierarchical sliding mode control (AHSMC) scheme is proposed, which can guarantee the fast and accurate arrival of the trolley and the jib to the desired positions while suppressing payload swings effectively. A hierarchical sliding mode surface is designed to suppress payload oscillations; a sliding mode convergence law is presented to attenuate chattering problem and to increase convergence rate; an adaptive friction function is used to compensate for the influence of unknown frictions. The stability of the closed-loop system is proven rigorously by utilizing the Lyapunov technique and LaSalle's invariance theory. A series of comparative simulations are carried out to verify the control performance, chattering suppression performance and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Integral Event-Triggered Formation Control for General Linear Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: In this paper, to solve the formation control problem, we focus on an integral event-triggered control with an undirected topology graph which is connected. Considering the classical general linear multi-agent systems, the agents could achieve the expected formation from initial positions and the larger average inter-event intervals would be yielded by using the integral event-triggered mechanism. Moreover, we demonstrate that the Zeno behaviors could be strictly avoided by gaining the positive lower bound between two triggering inter-event intervals. Finally, the numerical simulations show that the proposed event-triggered strategy is effective.

articleTitle: Peaking Control Strategy of Stackelberg Game for Buildings Based on Cluster Classification Incentive
abstract: In the current power market environment, the building group load-side adjustable resources are abundant, the regulation potential is huge, and it has an important participation status in the peaking scenario, but the power grid and building users as the main body of different interests, the economic trade-off between the two is crucial for the enhancement of peaking participation in the building group and the excavation of the regulation potential, therefore, a cluster classification incentive mechanism is designed to promote the active participation of building users in demand response, based on the Stackelberg game theory, and an optimal control model is established to maximize the economic benefits of the participating users in demand response, and a control strategy to satisfy the demand is obtained by optimizing the tariff information released by the grid, and adjusting the electricity consumption strategy of the building user group to achieve Nash equilibrium; after simulation, it is verified that the proposed model can satisfy the demand of the grid for peak shifting while optimizing the economic performance of the main bodies and give full play to the response potentials of multiple loads in the building.

articleTitle: KPCA-Based Hybrid Data-Model Driven Wind Farm Equivalence Modeling
