abstract: In this paper, we propose an equivalent clustering modeling method based on Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) with error correction model. Firstly, the mathematical modelling of the doubly-fed wind turbine is carried out to obtain the relevant state parameters of the turbine, and the state parameters are processed using KPCA to extract the clustering indicators; secondly, the K-means algorithm is used to cluster the wind turbines; finally, the clustered equivalence model is optimized by setting an error correction model. The simulation of three-phase short circuit fault and wind speed fluctuation using Matlab/Simulink platform proves the effectiveness of the modeling method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Tracking Intruders Algorithm Based on Single-Line LiDAR Point Cloud for the Platform End of Railway Passenger Stations
abstract: Platform end security control is of utmost importance in railway passenger station safety management. Station personnel track intruders using a single-line LiDAR. This paper analyzes the characteristics of intruder targets at the platform end and the point cloud features of intruders collected by the single-line LiDAR. An algorithm for tracking intruder targets at the platform end of the single-line LiDAR point cloud is proposed in this paper. By integrating spatial and temporal factors, spatial data processing is conducted in the first stage to process the single-frame data and construct multi-arc rectangles of intruder targets. In the second stage, data correlation calculations are performed on the radar frames based on the time series, resulting in a correlation matrix. The Hungarian algorithm is employed for multi-object correlation between frames. Specifically, for one-to-many matching situations, the dynamic time warping method is used to associate and match the arcs within the multi-arc rectangles, enabling secondary matching for inter-frame target alignment and achieving intruder target tracking at the platform end using the single-line LiDAR point cloud. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can track platform intruder targets.

articleTitle: Output Feedback Control for Set Stabilization of Asynchronous Boolean Control Networks with Double Q-Learning Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, the output feedback control problem of asynchronous Boolean control networks (ABCNs) is inves-tigated by reinforcement learning (RL). First, the algebraic state space representation of ABCNs is constructed by taking advantage of the semi-tensor product (STP) method. Following that, the Q-learning algorithm is introduced. Secondly, a nec-essary and sufficient condition for judging whether an ABCN is asymptotically stabilizable in the infinite field is proposed. Additionally, double Q-learning (DQL), an upgraded Q-learning technique, is utilized to create optimum state feedback controllers. Moreover, the relationship between output feedback and state feedback is discussed, and the output feedback controller is designed by virtue of the nature of the DQL. Finally, a biological network model is employed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed algorithms.

articleTitle: A Trust-Region Based Real-Time Optimization Scheme for Modular High-Temperature Gas-Cooled Reactor Nuclear Power Plant
abstract: The advanced fourth-generation modular high-temperature gas-cooled reactor (MHTGR) nuclear power plant is designed with a unique multi-module with one-turbine layout, which provides significant advantages for module coordination and flexible matching to the load demand of the power grid. However, a major challenge is to maintain stable and reliable operation during load changes under unfavorable conditions of limited process data and operational experience. This work proposes a model-based real-time optimization (RTO) scheme to assist in the operation and regulation of the nuclear system, ensuring the safety of wide-ranging load changes. A parameter mapping based on support vector regression (SVR) is integrated into the RTO scheme to adapt model modification in a derivative-free manner. To ensure the global convergence of RTO iterations, a trust-region policy is incorporated into the algorithm framework. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through simulation and compared with the gradient-based trust-region optimization scheme.

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategy to Improve Power Angle Stability of New Energy Power System
abstract: As the proportion of new energy installed capacity in the power system continues to increase, the influence of new energy power generation on the stability of the power system is also more prominent. At present, most new energy units use current inner loops, so that they do not participate in the oscillation of the power Angle. However, since it does not have moment of inertia, it will reduce the equivalent inertia of the system as a whole after being connected to the system, thereby weakening the power angle stability of the system. Therefore, it is very needful to improve the power angle stability of the power system by improving the control strategy of the new energy unit. In this work, by adjusting the output of new energy units during the fault period, partly offset the drop in external power due to short-circuit faults, and reduce the difference between thermal power mechanical power and electromagnetic power, thereby improving the power angle stability of the system. This work not only reveals its mechanism through theoretical analysis, but also the effectiveness of this method is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Formal Proof of the Mean Value Theorem Based on Coq
abstract: This paper introduces the formal proof of the three mean value theorems of differentiation in detail. The differential mean value theorem is the core theorem of differential calculus, an important tool for studying functions, and a bridge between functions and derivatives. Based on the formalization of function, limit, function continuity, and function derivation, etc. We strictly formalized the three median value theorems of differentiation: Rolle's theorem, Lagrange's median value theorem, and Cauchy's median value theorem. This work lays a solid foundation for our subsequent proofs of important theorems in mathematical analysis, not only promoting advancements in the field of education but also contributing to the progress of mathematical mechanization. All the codes involved in this article have been verified in Coq, which fully reflects the high reliability of Coq.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Terminal Sliding Mode Control for Connected Vehicles Platoon
abstract: To address the issue of error convergence, this paper proposes a finite time terminal sliding mode control strategy, and considering the interaction between vehicles to prevent inappropriate accelerations, negative speeds, and negative spacing error (SE). First, a new terminal sliding surface is designed based on the kinematics model. Aiming at the sliding mode chattering problem, an appropriate reaching law is designed. Then the controller is obtained according to the kinematics model and the designed sliding surface. And we use Lyapunov technique to prove system stability, and use Laplace technique to analyze string stability. Finally, the feasibility of the control scheme is proved through simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Model Predictive Control Strategy Based on Slip Angle of Omnidirectional Mobile Robot
abstract: When the host computer controls the omnidirectional mobile robot to track the expected trajectory according to the planned path task, it needs to make timely corrections and feedback for possible trajectory deviations in order to meet the flexibility and reliability of the omnidirectional mobile robot. In this paper, a model predictive control improvement method based on slip angle is proposed to effectively improve the real-time as well as tracking characteristics without affecting the dynamic performance of the omnidirectional mobile robot tracking. Through MATLAB simulation software, it is demonstrated that the model predictive control strategy based on the slip angle meets the reliability of the omnidirectional mobile robot in performing trajectory tracking.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Guidance Strategy Based on Markov Decision Model
abstract: The charging station malfunction may deny the charging service for the electric vehicles at the station. As a result, the affected owners have two options of leaving or continuing to wait. The owner's leave / stay selection is modeled as a two-state Markov decision model. Then, based on the objective factors such as the state of charge (SOC) and queuing order of electric vehicles, a fuzzy inference algorithm is proposed to solve the state transition matrix of Markov decision model. And then the owner's choice result is obtained. Furthermore, the charging guidance strategy based on Markov decision model and weighted complex network model is designed for owners who choose to leave. Subsequently, the owner's charging satisfaction index is defined to evaluate the charging guidance results. Finally, the feasibility of Markov decision model in describing the charging choice of vehicle owners is verified by simulation experiments, and the superiority of the scheduling strategy is verified by comparative experiments.

articleTitle: sCARS-LSTM Model for Energy Consumption Prediction of Heat Setting Machines
abstract: The paper proposes an energy consumption prediction model based on sCARS-LSTM to solve the problem of difficult energy management of the heat setting machine in textile dyeing and finishing industry. Firstly, the sCARS screening method is used to screen the key factors that affect energy consumption, with the dimensions of the external input samples are compressed from 277 to 34, which is reduced by 87.7%. Then, the LSTM network is used to learn and predict energy consumption, and the prediction error RMSE of model used sCARS gets <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$125.96\ \text{kW}\cdot \mathrm{h}$</tex>, which is 9.36% lower than the best-performing baseline model. The proposed model has excellent predictive performance.

articleTitle: A 3D Path Planning Algorithm for the UAV Based on the Improved Double-DqnAlgorithm
abstract: In this paper, in order to solve the 3D path planning problem of the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in unknown environments with obstacles, an improved Double-deep Q network (DQN) algorithm is proposed. In order to solve the problem of sparse rewards in the process of deep reinforcement learning training, a mechanism of energy efficiency reward is designed, and then the 3D path of the VAV is shortened and smoothed. In addition, a mechanism of priority experience replay based on the queue is proposed to improve the sampling probability of relatively good experience, so that the training time is reduced and the success rate is improved. Simulation results show that, compared with the traditional method, the algorithm proposed in this paper can shorten the average number of steps required to reach the maximum score and improve the training success rate.

articleTitle: Observer-Based Consensus Security Control for Multi-Agent Systems Under FDI Attacks
abstract: To solve the consensus security control issue of fake data injection (FDI) attacks on the communication link of discrete-time multi-agent systems (MASs), a consensus control protocol based on discrete state observers is proposed. First, a distributed state observer is built based on the relative outputs of the neighboring agents in order to estimate the leader's state and tracking error. A discrete consensus control protocol is additionally created to allow followers to monitor the leader's state trajectories despite FDI attacks and to confirm the system's stability. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is then verified using numerical simulation and simulation using a model of a smart grid system.

articleTitle: A Local-Global Multi-Scale MLP Network for Plant Leaf Segmentation Based on Context Masking
abstract: The health status of plant leaves directly reflects whether the plant has healthy growth. By accurately segmenting the leaf area in plant leaf images, real-time monitoring of leaf diseases can be achieved. Although existing Transformer-based segmentation methods can capture long-range dependencies between pixels, they are computationally intensive and do not fully utilize edge information. To address these issues, this paper proposes a local-global Multi-scale MLP network framework, called LGM-MLP. The LGM-MLP architecture comprises an encoder network, an local-global multi-scale MLP module, and a decoder network. The LGM-MLP module divides the input features into two branches: the global multi-scale MLP branch captures long-range dependencies in the image, while the local multi-scale MLP branch focuses on extracting local feature maps. The local-global attention mechanism dynamically adjusts the weights of global and local features. In the decoder network, the CRD module is incorporated into the convolutional layer to enhance the extraction of boundary features. Comparative analysis with U-Net and state-of-the-art models reveals that our proposed method significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of plant leaf image segmentation.

articleTitle: Stochastic Evolutionary Game Analysis of Low-Carbon Regulation of Cloud Manufacturing Services
abstract: Aiming at the low-carbon cooperation between service providers and demanders in the cloud manufacturing mode, a tripartite stochastic evolutionary game model of low-carbon cooperation among service providers, demanders and the cloud platform is established. According to the stability criterion theorem of stochastic differential equations, the conditions for strategy evolutionary stability are analyzed. Finally, the impacts of important factors on the strategy evolution are analyzed, such as reward and punishment of cloud platform. Simulation shows that: low-carbon costs and random factors have a negative impact on low-carbon cooperation between providers and demanders, and the appropriate rewards and punishments have a positive impact on low-carbon cooperation between providers and demanders.

articleTitle: Identification Method of Demand Response Potential Households Based on Multi-Source Heterogeneous Data Association Rule Analysis
abstract: Accurately identifying the potential demand response of residential users and establishing a certain scale of aggregated resources for participation in grid interactions can further enhance the demand response regulatory capabilities. Presently, the identification research relies solely on load data mining, making the precise identification of potential demand response among residential users challenging. Hence, this study proposes an approach for identifying potential households for demand response based on the analysis of association rules using multiple heterogeneous data sources. To address the limitations of single-dimensional user potential evaluation indicators and uniform indicator weights, this method integrates multiple heterogeneous data sources for association rule analysis, constructs a multidimensional demand response potential evaluation indicator system, and assigns objective weights to these indicators based on correlation and redundancy analysis. Subsequently, the user potential values are determined using the approximate ideal solution ranking algorithm. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through numerical examples.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Oscillating Buoy for Efficient Wave Energy Harvesting
abstract: In recent times, oscillating buoy wave energy conversion systems have garnered significant attention globally. These buoys facilitate wave energy conversion into mechanical motion, subsequently harnessed into electricity through Power Take-Off (PTO) systems. The effectiveness of energy capture by these oscillating buoys directly impacts their overall power generation efficiency. Consequently, this paper aims to enhance energy capture efficiency by optimizing the hydrodynamic attributes of the oscillating buoy. Employing a frequency domain analysis approach and utilizing AQW A software, hydrodynamic simulations were conducted to analyze the impact of distinct structural parameters and draft depths on Response Amplitude Operator (RAO), a measure of buoy motion. Concurrently, based on wave characteristics in the Yancheng coastal area in Jiangsu Province, optimal buoy diameter and draft depths were determined using response surface methodology. The findings reveal that increased draft depths elevate the buoy's natural period at which RAO reaches its peak, while the buoy diameter's influence on the same is relatively marginal. As both draft depth and diameter increase, RAO follows an ascending then descending trend, culminating in specific buoy dimensions that maximize energy conversion efficiency during a particular period. For the wave characteristics in the sea area near Yancheng, Jiangsu Province, the optimal diameter of the buoy is around 1.8 m, and the draft depth is approximately 3.1 m.

articleTitle: Improved Trilateration Algorithm Based on Unscented Kalman Filter
abstract: In order to solve the problem of decreased positioning accuracy caused by ranging errors in indoor or occluded situations, this paper uses the TOF algorithm based on UWB positioning system to achieve ranging, and proposes an improved trilateration positioning algorithm based on weighted centroids to solve the positioning coordinates: using three circles intersect to calculate the weighted center of mass of the intersection point. When the three circles cannot intersect, the radius is enlarged proportionally. The Local Outlier Factor is used to eliminate the abnormal points and then the positioning result is calculated; the Unscented Kalman Filter is used to further improve the accuracy of the positioning results, and at the same time Achieve smoothing of the trajectory. Experimental results show that the overall positioning accuracy of the algorithm proposed in this paper is improved by 15.98% compared with the algorithm without outlier detection and the unscented Kalman filter.

articleTitle: A Novel Data Acquisition Equipment for Distribution Systems Based on FFT Single-peak Interpolation Algorithm
abstract: In recent years, internet of things(IoT) development has brought new vitality to modernizing power grid equipment. In the smart IoT era, collecting distribution equipment data has also become intelligent. However, existing acquisition devices often have fixed functions, making them unable to accommodate diverse sensors. This paper develops a multifunctional acquisition device based on fast fourier transform(FFT) single-peak interpolation to enable dynamic port configuration. This allows effective collection of pressure, temperature, current, voltage, and other sensory data from distribution equipment. The device also enables real-time grid voltage harmonic calculation. Field testing showed the device maintained stability with good data upload rates under multiple sensor connections. The harmonic calculation accuracy met requirements, with an average 0.001% relative frequency error, 0.13% relative amplitude error, and 0.25° angular error.

articleTitle: Adaptive Observer-Based Fault Diagnosis and Model Predictive Fault-Tolerant Control for Actuator Faults in Robotic Manipulators
abstract: This article proposes a fault diagnosis scheme for the fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant control of a robotic arm actuator based on an adaptive fault observer. The research focuses on the dynamic model of the robotic arm. In case of an actuator fault, an adaptive fault observer is designed to obtain fault information, complete fault detection and fault estimation, and then utilize the Lyapunov stability theorem to analyze the stability of the observation error system. Based on this analysis, a model predictive fault-tolerant controller is designed to enable the robotic arm to accurately follow the desired trajectory. The effectiveness of the algorithm is then verified through simulation examples.

articleTitle: Adjust-RippleNet Recommendation Algorithm for Big Data Analysis in Technology
abstract: The integration of recommendation systems with knowledge graphs to perform hybrid recommendations has significant research value and implications. Addressing the technological service needs of Qinghai, we have researched and established a method for technological service recommendations. By harnessing the distinct characteristics of Qinghai's technological data and the recommendation requirements for technological services, we introduced the Adjust-RippleNet algorithm, building upon the foundational RippleNet recommendation algorithm. This method replaces the user's historical behavior data in the original algorithm with the most recent background data of entity objects. The accumulated latent preferences of entity objects across different ripple sets are then represented as vectors of the entity objects, forming an entity object-background interaction matrix. Ultimately, based on the labels of entities in the knowledge graph, we executed categorized recommendations and confirmed the efficacy of this algorithm through comparative experiments.

articleTitle: Pose Estimation for Spherical Robot with Kinematics-Based Encoder-Inertial Odometry
abstract: The spherical robot based on pendulum is a novel type of mobile robot whose motion is realized by changing the center of mass. Since the exteroceptive sensors such as camera and LiDAR are significantly hindered or even uninformative inside the spherical shell, the pose estimation for spherical robot is challenging. In this paper, we present a concise kinematic model for pendulum-driven spherical robot and propose a low-cost kinematics-based encoder-inertial odometry algorithm to estimate position and orientation. Practical experiments results demonstrate that our approach is efficient for short-term localization. Despite the accumulated errors problem in long-term localization, our approach provides a baseline in further study on localization for pendulum-driven spherical robot and can serve as an initial estimate or interpolating instances for further simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) for spherical robots.

articleTitle: Adaptive Finite-Time Control for the Chemotherapy of Brain Tumor via NN-Based Backstepping Approach
abstract: A brain tumor is a significant class of diseases that pose a threat to human health. Based on the logistic growth law of brain tumor cells and host cells, a brain tumor with drug model is constructed. N ext, a NN - based backstepping tracking controller is designed to control the dosage of chemotherapeutic drug to effectively treat brain tumors. In contrast to the existing works, the considered brain tumor model allows for parameter uncertainties due to measurement errors and physical limitations. It proved by the Lyapunov stability theory that the number of brain tumor cells can be reduced to a desired reference value in a finite time. Simulation results show that the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy for reducing brain tumor cells. Notably, the proposed approach has potential implications for the development of treatment plans for brain tumor chemotherapy, and provides theoretical support for controlling the dosage of chemotherapeutic drug.

articleTitle: An Improved Bi-Directional RRT* Based Path Planning Algorithm for Mine UAV Inspection
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) inspection plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and efficiency of coal mine operations. However, the unstructured nature of coal mine tunnels and the limitations of traditional path planning algorithms have hindered UAV inspection effectiveness. In this paper, we propose a path planning algorithm based on an improved bi-directional RRT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> approach to address these challenges. Our algorithm focuses on optimizing path generation efficiency and obstacle avoidance. By enhancing the sample point generation strategy and incorporating an extended step function, the algorithm significantly reduces the number of generated sample points, leading to faster path planning. To ensure the UAV's safety during movement, we introduce corner constraints and an obstacle avoidance strategy, which minimize the steering angle and maintain a safe distance from obstacles. Moreover, the generated paths are further improved using B-spline curves to comply with UAV dynamics constraints, resulting in smoother planned trajectories. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate that our improved bi-directional RRT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> algorithm effectively avoids obstacles while achieving substantial gains in path generation efficiency.

articleTitle: Talent Training Mode for Automation Specialty with Integration of Expertise and Innovative Thinking
abstract: The automation specialty of Qingdao University is a national first-class undergraduate major construction site and has passed the engineering education certification of the Ministry of Education. To meet the needs of education in the new era and the construction of new engineering subjects, we further deepen the reform of innovation and entrepreneurship education. Based on the current situation of the construction and development of the automation specialty in Qingdao University, and according to the talent training practice of automation specialty in recent years, we investigate the talent training mode of automation specialty under the integration of expertise and innovation from three levels of culture, teaching system and institutional guarantee, and explore a new mode for training complex innovative talents.

Author Keywords: Integration of Expertise and Innovative Thinking

articleTitle: Noise Generation Algorithm for Test Set Based on Part-of-Speech Retention
abstract: Considering the gap between training and inference phases of author imitation models trained with Denoising AutoEncoder loss, this paper proposes a noise generation algorithm for test set based on part-of-speech retention. Leveraging linguistic definitions to identify the part-of-speech associated with the primary elements of a sentence, this algorithm selectively retains elements with corresponding parts-of-speech during the addition of noise, while introducing normal noise to other components of the sentence. The proposed algorithm ensures maximum extraction of source text information during the model's inference stage and reduces the gap between the training and inference stages. Moreover, this paper also improves the noise generation algorithm employed during the training phase of De-noising AutoEncoder. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed noise generation algorithm achieves a relatively well-balanced combination of stylistic intensity, content preservation, and fluency, surpassing other types of noise generation algorithms.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation in Adverse Weather via Dual-Alignment-Based Pseudo-Label Optimization
abstract: Semantic segmentation is of great importance to self-driving vehicles for accurately identifying and understanding the driving environment. In adverse weather conditions, degraded image quality caused by rain and fog can affect the accuracy and reliability of semantic segmentation. It is also difficult to obtain and annotate the data set for training the fully supervised model. To solve the above problems, we design an adaptive semantic segmentation network (ASSNet) in adverse weather without the need for annotations in adverse weather. Facing the problems of significant stylistic differences and large dynamic differences between images captured in adverse weather conditions and those captured in normal weather conditions, we propose the dual-alignment-based pseudo-label optimization framework. Specifically, addressing the significant stylistic differences, we introduce a differentiable image processing module to make images captured in normal weather conditions stylistically similar to those captured in adverse weather conditions. As for the large dynamic differences, we propose to use feature point matching to optimize the pseudo-labels of normal weather conditions, thereby improving the quality of pseudo-labels for supervising the model in adverse weather. Experimental results show that our method can improve the quality of pseudo-labels efficiently, and thereby improve the segmentation accuracy.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization Scheduling of Microgrids Considering Demand Response
abstract: Currently, uncertainty, demand side response, and multi-objective optimization issues of renewable energy have become important research topics in microgrid optimization. An optimization strategy considering economic indicators, security indicators, and demand response is proposed to address these issues. The optimization scheduling uses a complementary power generation method combining diesel engines and energy storage systems to address the uncertainty of large-scale renewable energy grid connection. With the aim of reducing the overall operating costs of microgrids and the power fluctuations between micro grids and the main grid interconnection lines, a coordinated operation model for distributed power generation and demand side load optimization management is established in the context of time-of-use electricity prices. The design problem is solved using the enhanced multi-objective Particle Swarm Optimization method and Pareto optimum solution theory, and the best solution is found using the fuzzy membership function. According to the calculation results, demand response reduces the microgrid's total operating costs by 12.46% when compared to when it is not used, and it also lessens line power fluctuation by 11.11 %, which has positive effects on both the economy and public safety.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Dark Field Partial Slight Discharge of GIS Coaxial Busbar Using KPCA-SVM-Based Heuristic Sequence Comparison Method
abstract: In this paper, a heuristic sequence comparison method based on KPCA-SVM (Kernel Principal Component Analysis-Support Vector Machines) is proposed to achieve the detection and isolation of dark field partial discharge faults in GIS coaxial busbar. The main design steps are divided into three steps: firstly, the partial discharge fault area is divided into bright and dark areas, and the dark areas are further divided into edge dark areas, intermediate dark areas, and depth dark areas; secondly, the features of the test samples are extracted by KPCA method and the discharge phenomena occurring in the three sub-dark areas are classified by SVM method; then, based on these designs, the discharge diagnosis method of heuristic sequence comparison is constructed. Finally, the validity of these obtained results is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Virtual Power Plant Based on Stackelberg Game in the Context of “Electricity-Carbon-Green” Market
abstract: In order to promote the transformation to a new power system in the context of China's energy reform, a large number of distributed energy sources are integrated into the grid in the form of virtual power plants as aggregators, which poses a considerable challenge to the grid entities. In this paper, we design a “power-carbon-green” joint trading market framework and propose a Stackelberg game based on the optimal scheduling method of virtual power plant, with virtual power plants as the leader and load aggregators as the followers. The Nash equilibrium solution is obtained by iterative genetic algorithm. Finally, the algorithm is verified on the MATLAB platform by calling the CPLEX solver, the experimental results prove the effectiveness of the model, and both the virtual power plant and the load aggregator can obtain more benefits through this model.

articleTitle: Adaptive EKF Filtering Based on Model Feature Constraints
abstract: In the realm of state estimation for the majority of practical engineering applications, nonlinear systems have been prevalent. Traditional Kalman filtering, rooted in model feature constraint theory, exhibited limitations by being restricted to linear systems and proved inadequate for addressing nonlinear systems. In response to this challenge, this paper introduces a novel Nonlinear Adaptive Kalman Filtering approach that extends the application of model feature constraint theory to nonlinear systems. Firstly, the paper leverages the EKF filtering framework as a foundation and derives the optimal estimation theory for Gaussian noise statistical feature constraints (model parameter ratios) in nonlinear systems. A series of theoretical proofs are presented to verify the existence of Gaussian model parameter ratio features in nonlinear systems. Secondly, the paper combines model parameter ratios with covariance matching and introduces corresponding parameter estimation criteria for nonlinear systems. This approach transforms the adaptive filtering problem into an optimization problem with constraints. To obtain the optimal solution for estimating the system model, the Wild Horse Optimizer is employed to solve this optimization problem. Ultimately, by revealing and validating the existence of model parameter ratios in optimal nonlinear Kalman filtering, the feasibility of the proposed method is demonstrated. Experimental results further affirm the applicability of model feature constraint theory in nonlinear systems.

articleTitle: Research on Online Upgrade of DSP Application Program Based on Serial Communication
abstract: Digital Signal Process (DSP) is a MCU which could process control signal, and was often used in the implementation of control systems. With the improvement of user's requirements and the development of electronic technology, the application programs needed to be upgraded. Taking TMS320DSPF28335 as an example, this paper described a DSP program upgrade method that was separated from the JTAG port and implemented by serial port, which avoided exposing the equipment and transmission errors with long JTAG cable. Different from the common upgrade method, this method proposed in this paper could execute the application program when DSP was powered on. This satisfied the situation where the application program needed always executed when the device powered on, and also avoided the trouble of the users used the jump command to execute the application program. And the host computer software was designed to verify the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Steel Plate Surface Defect Detection Method - Based on Improved YOLO Algorithm
abstract: The steel industry is the bedrock of the national economy, and the inspection of surface defects in steel plate surface significantly impacts steel production efficiency and product quality. Due to the low accuracy, Low accuracy, slow detection speed, high hardware conditions of traditional steel plate surface defect detection methods under steel plate production environments, we propose an improved steel plate surface defect detection method using the YOLOv5 algorithm to enhance detection accuracy and speed. Firstly, an SE attention networks are added into the YOLOv5 backbone to improve the model's attention to defect targets. Then, the original SPPF is modified to an SPPFCSPC module to increase the model's feature processing capability. By comparing with Faster-RCNN, YOLOv3 and the original YOLOv5 algorithm, it can be founded that the improved YOLOv5 achieved a significant improvement in the average detection accuracy of defective targets on the surface of steel plates, reaching 91.4%, which is 13.6%, 8.9% and 4.2% higher than the other algorithms, respectively. In addition, the algorithm exhibited high real-time performance with a detection time of 10.4 ms for a single image frame. Thus, it provides important technical support for the accurate and real-time detection of the steel plate surface in the production of industrial steel plate.

articleTitle: Output Feedback Anti-Disturbance Control for Slow Sampled-Data Systems Combined with Model Predictive Control: An Alternating Predictive Observer Approach for Accelerating Sampling Rates
abstract: This paper investigates the combination of output feedback anti-disturbance control with model predictive control for slow-rate sampled-data systems with non-vanishing disturbances. The study focuses on a specific class of dual-rate systems, where the sensor samples output data at a slow rate, and the controller updates input data at a fast rate. To address the challenge of slow sampling, the paper introduces an observation method suitable for the anti-disturbance alternating predictive observer, utilizing only the measured output. To address the challenge of slow sampling, the paper introduces an observation method suitable for the anti-disturbance alternating predictive observer, utilizing only the measured output. By matching the observer's observation rate with the rapidly updated controller's rate, the sampling rate of the system can be improved. The proposed observer incorporates the estimated state and disturbance information into the output prediction. This information, combined with the control variable constraints in the resulting rolling horizon optimization problem, enables the design of a fast updating predictive control law. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed observer and the composite anti-disturbance control method under constrained control law, two sets of simulations are conducted on a dc-dc buck converter.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Segmentation Algorithm Based on Multi-scale Deep Learning Networks
abstract: Brain tumors seriously affect people's health, and the brain can be visualized by MRI, which provides the basis for physicians to accurately diagnose. Aiming at the problem that it is difficult to accurately segment brain tumors, a deep learning network is established to realize brain tumor segmentation. Firstly, according to the uncertainty of the region where the brain tumor is located, a multi-core convolutional model is constructed to obtain information at different scales. Then SP_Net is proposed, the constraint function is established and the brain tumor segmentation model is realized.

articleTitle: Active Distribution Network Optimization Based on Improved Tunicate Swarm Algorithm
abstract: As distributed power sources and power electronic equipment are continuously connected to the distribution network, the power electronics on the distribution network side are increasingly deepened. At the same time, unreasonable access to a large number of distributed power sources can negatively affect the radial distribution network. In this paper, we consider drop control to realize power distribution for the impact brought by power electronics on the distribution network, and on this basis, we consider the improved Tunicate Swarm algorithm(ISC-TSA) to conduct simulation experiments in IEEE-69 system to realize the optimal allocation of distributed power sources and compare the scenarios with and without considering the impact brought by power electronics respectively. The experimental results show that using drop control as a power allocation strategy will have an impact on power quality and active losses.

articleTitle: Compressed Video Enhancement with Spatio-Temporal Multi-Feature Extraction
abstract: Bandwidth limitations require transmitting the original video in a compressed format, leading to video artifacts and quality degradation. Therefore, compressed video enhancement is very important. In recent years, deep learning methods have gained prominence in compressed video enhancement due to their ability to efficiently restore lost details in specific frames by extracting features. Information extraction can be influenced by video artifacts in preceding and subsequent frames, even when techniques like optical flow estimation or quality-based frame selection are employed. To better capture artifact removal details, this paper introduces a spatiotemporal multi-feature extraction method for more accurate video reconstruction. The experimental results show that the peak Signal-To-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of the video enhanced by the method proposed in this paper is about 0.06 dB higher(QP37) on average when compared to the video enhanced by some other methods (e.g., MFQE2.0, MFQE1.0, DS-CNN).

articleTitle: Robust Human Upper Limbs Trajectory Predictor for Human-Robot Collaboration
abstract: Accurately sensing the human posture information of collaborators is the critical technology to achieve human-robot collaboration, which can effectively improve the security of collaborative tasks. However, the pose of the collaborator, especially the motion trajectory of the human upper limb has the characteristics of randomness and sudden change. To solve the instability of prediction probability caused by the sudden change of trajectory and improve the prediction accuracy, this paper proposes a novel motion trajectory predictor for the human upper limb (GMM-LSTM). The algorithm can be described as follows: (1) according to the statistical feature of Human Upper Limbs motion, a joint probability distribution is inferred as its cluster model. A human upper limbs trajectory dataset can be clustered using this distribution as a sub-dataset. (2) an improved long and short-term memory network is proposed to predicate the future motion in three directions under the spatial coordinate system conditioned on the observed motion. (3) in the end, one fuse the predicted values of the three directions to generate the future trajectories. The experimental results show that the algorithm's overall prediction error consistently falls within a range of 1cm, indicating a high degree of robustness.

Author Keywords: prediction of upper limb motion trajectory

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Based End-to-end Autonomous Obstacle Avoidance for Manipulators
abstract: In this paper, a simple end-to-end obstacle avoidance method is introded for manipulators. First of all, the 2D images in the workspace are used to uniformly describe the characteristics of obstacles in the 3D space. After that, a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm DrQ-v2 is used to train the obstacle avoidance strategy, which directly outputs the joint angles to avoid the obstacles autonomously and accurately in the joint space. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed end-to-end simple control method is more effective and convenient in handling obstacle avoidance tasks in complex dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Seismic Data Visualization System Based on Web Technology
abstract: A seismic data visualization system is constructed based on B/S architecture in JavaScript with Vue, ECharts and Baidu-map, so as to show data on the map intuitively and clearly. The system can be divided into four parts: parameter input, data processing, model calculation, and results output. The loading and rendering of the megascale data could be finished within 1–2 seconds since the system response has no correlation to the magnitude variable with the adoption of new development architecture.

articleTitle: Fractional Order Modeling for Hydraulic Cylinder System Controlled by Electro-Hydraulic Proportional Valve
abstract: The position control of hydraulic cylinder is the key to hydro forming. However, modeling is the prerequisite for system control. In this paper, the modeling for hydraulic system controlled by electro-hydraulic proportional valve is studied. First, by analyzing the mechanism of the system, an integer-order model is derived. Then, based on the measured data obtained from the test platform, a fractional order model of the hydraulic cylinder system controlled by electro-hydraulic proportional valve is identified by using the hybrid functions based collocation method. Experimental results and associated comparisons demonstrate that the fractional order model constructed by using the hybrid functions based identification method is more accurate for describing the hydraulic cylinder system controlled by electro-hydraulic proportional valve.

Author Keywords: Hydraulic cylinder system controlled by electro-hydraulic proportional valve

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Gesture Recognition System Based on STM32
abstract: Gesture recognition, as a form of human-computer interaction, is gaining increasing attention and importance. Currently, mainstream gesture recognition methods can identify fixed gestures through gesture recognition modules, but they lack flexibility. On the other hand, methods based on computer vision for gesture recognition have higher application requirements and are constrained by various conditions. In this paper, a modular design approach is adopted to create a low-cost, wearable, highly robust, and real-time detection gesture recognition intelligent system based on STM32. A flex sensor is used as the gesture recognition unit, maintaining a recognition rate of 70% or higher. This design effectively reduces system costs and environmental requirements while improving real-time performance. Additionally, the integration of voice broadcasting functionality with the gesture recognition system enhances the system's intelligence and user-friendliness, making it more convenient for users to interact with.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Adaptive Control of Pure-Feedback Nonlinear Systems with Matched and Mismatched Disturbances
abstract: This paper addresses the finite-time adaptive control problem for a class of pure-feedback nonlinear uncertain non-affine systems with both matched and mismatched disturbances. In the presence of uncertain parameters and unknown disturbances, radial basis function compensation is introduced to the subsequent adaptive tracking process and a suitable finite-time controller is designed to ensure stable tracking of the desired signal within a small tracking error. The construction of the state-feedback controller and the adaptive control laws is based on the combination of critical mathematical inequality and backstepping method. Finally, a simulation example is presented to illustrate the efficiency of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Inverse Kinematics Solution of Manipulator in Obstacle Environment
abstract: To tackle the challenge posed by an obstructed middle joint in the robotic arm, we introduce a novel approach to solving the inverse kinematic problem within the obstacle space. This method seamlessly integrates collision detection with a genetic algorithm. First, the process begins with a thorough kinematic analysis of a seven-degree-of-freedom robotic arm, employing the Denavit-Hartenberg (D-H) parameter method. For collision detection, we streamline the process by utilizing an enclosing box model to simplify the collision function. Next, leveraging a standard genetic algorithm, we guide the initial population generation within the search space using Gaussian functions. Simultaneously, we construct an adaptive degree function that incorporates both the collision function and the positional error function. This fusion enables us to efficiently pinpoint the optimal inverse kinematic solution while ensuring collision-free movement within the obstacle-laden environment. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are verified by MATLAB and Sawyer robotic arm.

articleTitle: V2VFusion: Multimodal Fusion for Enhanced Vehicle-to-Vehicle Cooperative Perception
abstract: Current vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) research mainly centers on either LiDAR or camera-based perception. Yet, combining data from multiple sensors offers a more complete and precise understanding of the environment. This paper presents V2VFusion, a multimodal perception framework that fuses Li-DAR and camera sensor inputs to improve the performance of V2V systems. Firstly, we implement a baseline system for multi-modal fusion in V2V scenarios, effectively integrating data from LiDAR and camera sensors. This baseline provides a comparable benchmark for subsequent research. Secondly, we explore different fusion strategies, including concatenation, element-wise summation, and transformer methods, to investigate their impact on fusion performance. Lastly, we conduct experiments and evaluation on the OPV2V dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the multimodal perception method achieves better performance and robustness in V2V tasks, providing more accurate object detection results, thereby improving the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive Finite-Time Control of Uncertain Mixed-Order Fully Actuated Nonlinear Systems with Parameter Estimations
abstract: The finite-time control (FTC) problem, in this paper, is investigated for uncertain mixed-order fully actuated nonlinear (UMOFAN) systems with parameter estimations. A new finite-time controller is proposed that can make the origin of the closed-loop system finite-time stable and make parameter estimations close to their real values at the same time. In the control design process, the requirement for the state derivative information is eliminated via filters. Furthermore, the parameter in the adaptive law is updated by utilizing past and concurrent data on the basis of concurrent learning, thereby alleviating the persistent exciting (PE) condition. The effectiveness and the practicability of proposed control method are illustrated on the basis of the application of the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM).

articleTitle: Optimization Study of Water Treatment Plant Surveillance Camera Arrangement
abstract: The use of video surveillance for real-time management of factories has become increasingly common. For traditional fixed surveillance cameras, selecting and arranging them properly is crucial for ensuring the smooth operation of water treatment plants. With complex facilities and various obstructions within the plant, a balance needs to be struck between monitoring scope and cost. Therefore, it is necessary to establish an effective digital plane model to optimize the layout of cameras in water treatment plants. By building an optimization model, it is possible to achieve full coverage of the entire monitoring area with the minimum number of cameras. This study takes a water treatment plant in Beijing as an example, where the optimization problem of camera placement is transformed into a minimum subset coverage problem. A greedy algorithm is utilized to solve the problem. And the satisfactory results demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Optimal Tracking Control for Nonlinear Game Systems Using Dynamic Event-Triggering Strategy
abstract: This paper investigates the optimal tracking control issue of nonlinear nonzero-sum game systems with partially unknown dynamics. An adaptive dynamic programming approach is presented on the basis of a dynamic event-triggering mechanism. This paper first introduces a discount coefficient and augmented vectors into the cost function, transforming the optimal tracking control into an optimal regulation control problem. Subsequently, a single critic neural network is proposed to seek for Nash equilibrium. By defining a dynamic variable, a dynamic event-triggering rule is devised with historical data, which causes the larger event-triggering intervals. Moreover, the uniform ultimate boundness properties of the neural network estimation error and the tracking error have been proved. Finally, a numerical simulation verifies the correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Lightweight YOLO V5 Method for Detecting Thermal Spot Defects in PV Panels in Infrared Images
abstract: As an important component of photovoltaic power generation, PV panels play a crucial role in the photovoltaic power generation industry. In order to overcome the current problem of low speed and accuracy in detecting hot spot faults of PV panels in photovoltaic power plants, this paper proposes a lightweight YOLO V5 model to realize the detection of hot spot defects of PV panels in infrared images. First, data enhancement is performed on the existing dataset so as to increase the number of samples i n the database and enhance the generalization ability of the model. Second, a lightweight network structure Shufflenet v2 is introduced to replace the YOLO V5 backbone network to enhance the speed of detection. Finally, the attention mechanism is combined with the neck network to enhance the extraction of hot spot features. It can effectively balance the network's speed and accuracy. The experimental results show that the improved network achieves recognition accuracy of 93.5% for hot spots, which is 4.4% higher compared to the original network.

articleTitle: Design of Integrated Smart Aquarium
abstract: With the increasing demand for spatial beauty and convenience of the home environment, home aquariums are not only sought after by ornamental fish lovers but also gradually join people's daily life as part of home decoration. To solve the problems of daily feeding and the short survival time of ornamental fish due to the inexperience of breeders, an integrated intelligent aquarium is designed to reduce the cost and effort of raising ornamental fish. The aquarium integrates a variety of functions necessary for raising ornamental fish, and is supplemented by machine vision technology to automatically identify the species and status of ornamental fish; the functions include the basic functions of raising ornamental fish such as automatic water filtration, oxygenation, and feeding, and the care functions such as detecting water temperature and analyzing the health status of ornamental fish.

articleTitle: Prioritized Path Planning for Multiple Robots Based on Theta* Plus with Known Dynamic Obstacles
abstract: This paper solves the problem that expanding nodes incompletely of pure theta* in dynamic environments. The theta* plus algorithm with known dynamic obstacles is proposed to plan feasible paths for multiple robots. It is a two-level algorithm. At the high-level, each robot is assigned a unique priority by prioritized planning. At the low-level, the theta* plus algorithm with known dynamic obstacles is proposed for each robot to plan the path while avoiding conflict with robots with higher priority. The results of the simulations show that the approach proposed can perform some multi-robot path planning problems well.

articleTitle: A Novel Model Based on Deep Convolutional Generation of Adversarial Networks Using Meta-Learning (MAML-DCGAN)
abstract: Aircraft fault diagnosis is the basis for fault-tolerant control of aircraft. Deep learning is an emerging data-based approach to fault diagnosis. Deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN) is a data augmentation model. Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) allows the model to obtain good initialization parameters, which produces better results. This study solves the problem of data augmentation through a data generation algorithm based on MAML and DCGAN. The algorithm uses the MAML model to optimize DCGAN so that DCGAN obtains the best initialization parameters to generate higher quality data. In this paper, vehicle failure data is used as the original data. Comparing the Fréchet inception distance score (FID) of the data generated by DCGAN and MAML-DCGAN, the experiments show that the data generated by the MAML-DCGAN is more similar to the original data and is more advantageous for fault diagnosis and analysis.

articleTitle: A Non-Angle-Regressed Rotating Object Detection Framework for Aerial Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Currently, the angle regression-based methods dominate the field of rotating object detection. However, this type of method faces two obvious limitations: i) The boundary problem caused by the angle prediction beyond the angle definition domain; and ii) the Intersection over Union (IoU) of two rotating rectangles is not derivable to the angle, which forms a bottleneck in the improvement of detection accuracy. Addressing above issues, this paper proposes a non-angle-regressed rotating object detection framework, and the core idea of which consists of two points: i) Introducing a rotating object representation that avoids angle to ensure that the regression parameter never cross the boundary, thus effectively solving the boundary problem; and ii) designing a simple and derivable loss function based on this representation that can replace the rotating IoU to a certain extent, which is capable of improving the detection accuracy. The proposed method is tested on a large-scale aerial remote sensing dataset. Without bells and whistles, it easily outperforms the state-of-the-art angle regression-based rotating object detection method, improving the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{mAP}_{50}$</tex> by 0.3%.

articleTitle: Attitude Measurement for Drilling Tools Based on Zonotopic Kalman Filter
abstract: In the field of oil exploitation, attitude parameters of drilling tools is of great importance, whose measurement is seriously affected by vibration disturbances and gyroscope noises. This paper proposes a state estimation method with state nonlinear constraints to solve the measurement problem. Firstly, the measurement system is modeled with measurement noises and parametric uncertainties which are unknown but bounded. Meanwhile, state nonlinear constraints are linearized as the additional system output, and the linearization error delimitation is utilized. Then, the gravitational components are estimated by a Zonotopic Kalman Filter (ZKF), and the inclination and the Toolface are obtained. Finally, the availability of the ZKF -based proposed method in attitude measurement are demonstrated by the results.

articleTitle: Design and Research of Curved Crawling Pipeline Robot
abstract: In industrial and agricultural production and daily life, the application of pipelines is diverse, ranging from natural gas pipelines to solid transportation, oil transportation, etc. Transportation pipelines, as an important means of material transportation, have a wide range of applications. The detection, maintenance, and repair of pipelines are particularly important. If they are not detected on time during the use of pipelines, they are prone to malfunctions and cause unnecessary losses. This article proposes an adaptive designed surface crawling robot that uses a miniaturized and integrated open-source platform. The robot integrates bluetooth, vision, and other components, carrying components such as inspection modules, cleaning modules, repair modules, etc. It can solve pipeline problems in a one-stop manner.

articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Fully Actuated System Approach for Free-Flying Space Manipulator
abstract: This study explores the trajectory tracking control problem of a free-flying space manipulator subject to parametric uncertainties, external disturbance, and actuator saturation. An adaptive control strategy, employing the fully actuated system (FAS) approach, is designed, wherein the radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) is incorporated to offset lumped uncertainties. As a result, a constant linear closed-loop system is obtained with an arbitrarily assigned eigenstructure. Then the parametric method is utilized for controller parameter selection. In the context of Lyapunov theory, the presented controller ensures robust convergence of position and velocity tracking errors to a small neighborhood of the origin. A numerical simulation is finally performed to validate the efficacy of the presented controllers.

articleTitle: Template Matching and Trend Feature Analysis-Based Data Pre-Processing Method for Seismic Wave Detection
abstract: In this paper, a template matching and trend feature analysis-based data pre-processing method for seismic wave detection is proposed with two stages. In the first stage, it involves extracting the rock physical parameters from seismic wave detection results using OCR (Optical Character Recognition) method, and extracting the original rock physical parameters from the raw rock property table using keyword matching method. Using the rock physical parameters as a template, a template matching approach is employed to eliminate abnormal values from the original rock physical parameters. In the next stage, a technique is proposed to extract trend features of rock physical parameters for conducting advanced geological forecasting, which considered the expertise of experts in interpreting seismic wave detection data. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the compared simulation results.

articleTitle: Legged Robot Locomotion via Hybrid Zero Dynamics and Model Predictive Control
abstract: During the motion of a quadruped robot, it may enter the underactuated state, such as when the legs are in the swinging phase of a trot gait. This underactuated state can lead to instability in the robot. In this paper, we present a nonlinear model predictive controller (MPC) to track periodic gaits generated by hybrid zero dynamics (HZD) for stabilizing legged robot locomotion, thereby ensuring stable periodic motion of the robot, particularly when a quadruped robot is in the underactuated state. Nonlinear optimization problem is designed based on HZD, considering the hybrid full-order dynamical model of the quadrupedal robot, which generates periodic trot gaits for the robot offline. The periodic trot gaits gurantee that the quadruped robot's state does not diverge, even when the robot is underactuated. We use a nonlinear MPC controller to track the desired periodic gait online. The MPC controller ensures that the constraints are satisfied during the tracking process. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed controller in achieving stable locomotion.

articleTitle: Cooperative Hunting Strategy with Multi-Pursuer and a Superior Evader
abstract: This paper considers a pursuit-evasion game involving multiple pursuers and a single superior evader with nonholonomic constraints. A novel cooperative pursuit strategy is proposed to capture a fast evader while minimizing the generation of escape gaps. First, based on the theory of Apollonius circles, the initial position distribution of pursuers required to ensure the capture of a fast evader is proposed. Second, based on the heading angle of the evader, the pursuers are assigned tasks to divide them into one hunter and multiple surrounders. Meanwhile, the surrounders are again divided into two groups to assist hunter in capturing the faster evader. Then, the strategy of the hunter is designed based on the concept of parallel guidance law. The strategy for the surrounders is proposed based on optimal control, taking into consideration the coverage angle between adjacent Apollonius circles and the distance to the evader. Finally, numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed cooperative hunting strategy.

articleTitle: A Novel Depth Map Restoration Strategy Based on Information Entropy-Guided
abstract: In order to effectively fill the holes in the depth map, especially to repair large holes, this paper proposes a new information entropy-guided strategy for depth inpainting. Firstly, the depth map and color image undergo preprocessing to obtain a connected hole map and grayscale image for subsequent steps. The filling priority of invalid points is then evaluated by introducing the concept of information entropy, which improves the intelligence of the filling priority evaluation results. Secondly, the depth value prediction for invalid points is guided by color and gradient information, which ensures the integrity of the overall depth data and enhances the precision of the restoration. Finally, a comparison experiment was conducted on the Middlebury dataset. The proposed method demonstrated better robustness and accuracy compared to other competing methods, providing new ideas for related research in the field of deep image processing.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Inspection of Damage Based on Damage Index Fusion for Detecting Complex Composite Structure
abstract: Reconstruction Algorithm for Probabilistic Inspection is a promising algorithm and widely used for active damage detection and localization. In this paper, the method based on multiple damage index fusion is used to verify its damage detection effect on complex composite structure with screw holes and hollow circular opening. This paper fuses two types of damage index, then sets up an inspection of the damage index to eliminate the small value of damage index, and finally sets a threshold to narrow the reconstructed false image range. Experimental results demonstrate the precision of the algorithm for detecting damage on complex composite structure and the effectiveness of fusion of damage index.

articleTitle: Double-layer Descriptors and High-dimensional Search Mechanisms for Partial Point Cloud Registration
abstract: Partial point cloud registration is an essential preprocessing technique to generate complete 3D shapes that aim to transform partial scans into a common coordinate system. Existing methods that utilize geometric alignment rarely combine local and global information, which results in many incorrect correspondences. In the paper, a two-layer descriptor and a high-dimension searching approach (DDHSM) are utilized to extract and select the correct correspondences. Firstly, in the first layer, the Fast Point Feature Histogram (FPFH) is used to describe the feature of every point with high-dimension information based on its robustness and fastness. Then a high-dimensional search is considered to extract the initial corresponding set. In the second layer, global information is introduced to find the correct correspondences. For each point pair in the initial corresponding set, the normal angles are compared for all remaining points that satisfy the distance requirement. Finally, the singular value decomposition (SVD) method is implemented to compute the rigid transformation based on the updated corresponding set. Experimental results and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of our approach.

articleTitle: Short-Term PV Power Interval Prediction Based on VMD and Deep Learning Model
abstract: At present, the short-term prediction of photovoltaic power generation is very important for the safe and stable operation of photovoltaic power generation system. Aiming at the problem that point prediction is difficult to describe the fluctuation of photovoltaic power generation, a method of PV power generation interval prediction based on variational mode decomposition and deep learning model is proposed. The original PV power sequence is decomposed into several different components by VMD decomposition, and the complexity of each component is described by sample entropy, and each component is reconstructed into high-frequency and low-frequency components. Then, the high frequency and low frequency sequences are taken as input respectively, and the bidirectional gated loop unit optimized by the gray Wolf optimization algorithm is used for prediction, and the prediction results of the two components are added to get the predicted values. Finally, the kernel density estimation method is used to describe the error distribution of the point prediction results, and the interval prediction results are obtained by combining the point prediction results. An example analysis shows that this method has good prediction effect.

articleTitle: Adapt Step-Size LMS Algorithm Based on Symmetrical Sigmoid for Loran-C Anti-Interference
abstract: This article proposes an Adapt Step-Size Least Mean Square Error method based on the Symmetric Sigmoid nonlinear function (ASS-LMS) to address the issue of instability and conflicting convergence speed in traditional Loran-C anti-interference methods that use fixed-step parameter filters, which do not allow for parameter adjustment to follow errors. By combining interference error with the update step-size, the ASS-LMS method improves the ability of the existing adaptive filter to align in low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) conditions and enhances its convergence speed in high SNR conditions. This article elaborates on how the step-size updating parameters of the ASS-LMS method affect the convergence and stability performance of the algorithm. Simulation experiments are conducted to verify the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method for anti-interference in Loran-C signals. The results demonstrate the efficacy and utility of the approach.

articleTitle: Parallel Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Transformer for Object Tracking
abstract: In recent years, the application of Transformer in the realm of object tracking has yielded promising results, enabling researchers to extract comprehensive global information from image features. Nonetheless, it has come to light that the current state-of-the-art Transformer networks exhibit limitations in acquiring pertinent local information from image features. To address this issue, this paper presents a novel framework, namely the parallel multi-scale feature fusion Transformer (PFOT). The primary contributions of this study can be summarized as follows: 1) the incorporation of parallel multi-scale feature fusion involving both Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Transformers, aimed at mitigating the deficiency of existing Transformer-based tracking networks in capturing local information; 2) the adoption of a progressive fusion approach to effectively reconcile the complexities arising from spatial disparities inherent in multi-scale features; 3) the pivotal role played by this fusion strategy in enhancing the network's overall performance. To evaluate the performance of our approach, extensive experiments have been conducted on three demanding datasets, attesting to the superiority of our PFOT network over state-of-the-art methods. Our experimental results on several benchmarks, including NFS, OTB100, and UAV123, demonstrate that PFOT achieves comparable performance to the state-of-the-art tracking algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-Branch Graph Neural Network Model for Hyperspectral Image Classification
abstract: Graph convolution can process non-Euclidean structural data and has some applications in hyperspectral image classification problems in recent years. However, existing Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) methods are generally conducted on the fixed neighborhood receptive. Thus, the multi-scale spatial information is not fully taken into account, which limits their classification performances on HSI data. To alleviate the above issue, in this paper, we propose to use the multiple GNN branches for HSI classification and develop multi-branch superpixel GNN (MBGNN) to carry out feature learning on different-scale irregular areas while using the convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the local receptive feature representation. Then, a fusion network structure of CNN and MBGNN is proposed. In our method, the multi-scale spatial information can be fully used to improve the information mining of the HSI images. Experiments on two widely used datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MBGNN for hyperspectral image classification tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Robot Map Merge Method Based on Prior Information in Logistics Environment
abstract: Due to the problems of low efficiency and low accuracy, single robot simultaneous localization and mapping(SLAM) technology has great limitations in practical applications.In the current large-scale and complex logistics environment, multi-robot simultaneous localization and mapping technology has greater advantages.This article studies the method of multi-robot map merge in the logistics environment using multiple robots with known prior information. Compared to traditional multi-robot map fusion algorithms, this method uses the location information and relative position relationships between multiple mobile robots as prior information to modify map merge. The experimental results demonstrate that this method improves mapping accuracy while retaining the speed of multi-robot mapping.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Graph-Based Approach for Predicting Railway Operational Hazards
abstract: Railway operational hazards may lead to other hazards and then may result in kinds of fatalities and injuries. In order to decrease fatalities and injuries, it is necessary to predict railway operational hazards in advance. In this paper, a new approach to predict railway operational hazards is proposed. Its originality is to apply the knowledge graph to railway operational hazards prediction. This paper takes the UK railway operational accidents as a case study. The results show that this approach can effectively predict railway operational hazards. This is of great significance to prevent the occurrence of hazards and decrease fatalities and injuries.

articleTitle: Multi-Sensor Fuzzy Interval Multi-Attribute Decision Fusion Method
abstract: For the increasingly complex information environment and changing target characteristics, most of the existing multi-sensor information fusion methods are “static”, and less consider the influence of sensor reliability change and the timeliness of the multi-dimensional feature index weight in the measurement process on the fusion results. To solve this problem, an information fusion method based on fuzzy theory and interval multi-attribute decision making is proposed. The method defines the information quality optimization degree from the consistency of the support degree of each sensor to fuzzy proposition, uses interval number and multi-attribute decision theory to define the comprehensive confidence degree of feature recognition, and objectively determines the fusion weight of the sensor from these two aspects, and solves the reasonable evaluation of the sensor information and target feature weight when it is fuzzy and uncertain. Therefore, an intelligent optimization decision level fusion recognition model is constructed. Finally, the experiment of target recognit-ion proves that this method has good accuracy.

articleTitle: Infrared and Visible Image Fusion Based on Multiscale Adaptive Transformer
abstract: In our study, we introduce an innovative Transformer-based approach that utilizes multiscale adaptivity for the fusion of infrared and visible images. First of all, we propose a three-branch network structure to extract multiscale differentiated features of source images, and a cross-modal feature interaction module is designed to realize the information interaction of infrared and visible images. And then, inspired by Swin Transformer, a novel adaptive Transformer fusion network is proposed to fuse multiscale features, which fully considers the global information preservation issue during the fusion process and could better integrate the differential and complementary features of infrared and visible images. Furthermore, we present a cross-correlation loss grounded in correlation coefficients to foster a more robust relationship between the fused output and the original images through cross-correlation. The concluding tests reveal that our method's fusion outcomes adeptly harmonize the complementary attributes of various source images, leading to enhanced visual quality and perception.

articleTitle: Target Capture of Space Manipulators Using Image Input Under Unknown Dynamics
abstract: With the development of space technology and artificial intelligence techniques, more and more research is dedicated to the application of reinforcement learning algorithms to space tasks. Since space manipulator play an increasingly important role in space missions, in this research, we work on the target capture task of free floating space manipulators(FFSM) using camera image as input under unknown dynamics. An algorithm combined model-based and model-free reinforcement learning is proposed to solve the problem of inefficient training of model-free algorithm. The algorithm introduces a model-based pretraining strategy based on model-free optimization, which improves the overall training efficiency while retaining the good asymptotic performance of model-free optimization. The experiment shows that our algorithm outperforms famous model-free reinforcement learning algorithm both in learning efficiency and final performance when dealing with the high dimensional input(camera image) capture task in the research.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Circuits Based on IHHO-MA1DCNN
abstract: Aiming at the problem of nonlinearity and tolerance in analog circuits, an analog circuit fault diagnosis method based on the improved Harris Hawk optimization algorithm and the multi-scale one-dimensional attentional convolutional neural network (IHHO-MA1DCNN) is proposed. Firstly, the MA1DCNN with three channels is built to extract the features of different receptive fields and enrich the feature information. Secondly, an attention mechanism is introduced to optimize feature weight allocation and enhance the expression of key features. Thirdly, the Harris Hawk optimization (HHO) algorithm is improved to optimize network parameters so as to build an optimal fault diagnosis model. This improvement results in an enhanced diagnostic capability for the MA1DCNN. Finally, two typical filter circuits, the Sallen-Key bandpass filter circuit and the double-T filter circuit, are chosen for fault diagnosis experiments. The results reveal that, in comparison to other models, the proposed method offers superior fault identification capability. The average fault diagnosis accuracy of the two circuits reaches 99.15%.

articleTitle: Multi-USV Formation Control and Obstacle Avoidance Under Virtual Leader
abstract: In recent years, Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) have been widely used in ocean transportation, search and rescue operations and other fields. This article focuses on the formation navigation problem of multi-USV clusters. We used deep reinforcement learning methods to establish a model for formation navigation and designed a reward function which guides each USV to its expected position while flexibly avoiding obstacles. By introducing a virtual leader, the multi-USV cluster successfully follow the expected path while maintaining formation and avoiding obstacles. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm in achieving both formation completion and formation navigation.

articleTitle: Debiased Recommendation Model Based on User Historical Behavior
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet, there is a widespread problem of highly imbalanced long tail distribution of user project interactions in most real-world application recommendation scenarios. This paper presents a novel approach for mitigating bias in the recommendation process of recommendation system models through the introduction of a debiased recommendation model that leverages user history behavior.
