The model models user click behavior on recommendation results and utilizes graph convolution operations to embed user and item representations, while incorporating recommendation ranking position information and item popularity information into the prediction inputs. Additionally, false positive signals are employed as post-processing to refine the model's prediction scores, resulting in improved item recommendation accuracy and enhanced personalized recommendation capabilities. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model exhibits a notable improvement in both precision and accuracy when compared to other baseline models mentioned in the paper.

articleTitle: Near-Nadir Wave-Induced Doppler Simulations and Analysis with GO Scattering Model
abstract: Sea surface Doppler is one of the important dynamic parameters of the ocean. The Doppler information obtained by radar monitoring can reflect the dynamic characteristics of the sea surface. Waves and currents are the main contributions to the sea surface Doppler measurements. In order to remove the wave-induced Doppler components and extract the current velocity from the sea surface Doppler, it is important to analyze the characteristics of the wave-induced Doppler. Due to the lack of measured data for near-nadir small-incidence Doppler radar at present, a Doppler frequency shift model based on the geometrical optics (GO) scattering model is proposed in this paper, and the radial Doppler velocity is calculated. Compared with the existing model, the proposed model has a simpler structure and fewer input parameters, and the reliability of the results is verified. Then, the analysis of wave-induced Doppler shows that Doppler shift has a strong dependence on the radar incidence, azimuth, and wind speed. In contrast, the radial Doppler velocity is not affected by the incidence at near-nadir. The Doppler frequency shift model and the analysis results of wave-induced Doppler characteristics presented in this paper can provide references for the application of wave-induced Doppler in ocean current inversion.

articleTitle: Assessment of Close Approaching Between ASO-S Satellite and Other Objects in Space
abstract: Advanced space-based solar observatory,short for ASO-S, has been in orbit for more than a half year. Most of the performance of ASO-S are demonstrated to be wholesome. Some achievements were reported in some academic journal or public media. In this paper, the space safety of ASO-S will be focused on. Based on cyber-accessible data set.the objects' orbits are simulated, further, the approaching events between ASO-S and other neighboring flying objects have been presented. The approaching objects are briefly introduced and discussed. Faced up with such a busy space traffic, emergency measures are proposed to prevent the ASO-S satellite from colliding with other neighboring flying objects in space.

articleTitle: Joint Photovoltaic and Battery Storage Multiple Objective Optimization Scheduling in Home Energy Management System
abstract: With the rapid development of renewable energy sources, the home energy management system shows an increasing importance in smart home. Therefore, this paper proposes a home energy management system architecture that integrates a photovoltaic system and an energy storage system. In this architecture, the household electricity load model, the photovoltaic generation model and the storage battery model are established. In addition, the electricity cost, user comfort and photovoltaic usage ratio are taken as the optimization objectives. For this multi-objective optimization problem, the control coordination strategy with time-of-use price and battery storage is proposed and solved by the NSGA-II algorithm. The simulation results show that the proposed scheduling strategy can complete the multi-objective optimization scheduling for the home energy management system and realize the coordination of photovoltaic source, household load and battery storage. Compared with the traditional control strategy, this strategy can reduce the loss of battery lifetime.

articleTitle: A Questionnaire Survey and Case Analysis on the Combination of 4P, 4C and 4R Theory and Neuromarketing
abstract: With the development of the world, the commodities must gradually enter the global stage, and traditional marketing is facing unprecedented impact and challenges. Neuromarketing is an emerging discipline that combines cognitive neuroscience and marketing, which can promote the development of the marketing. This study used case analysis and questionnaire survey methods to investigate the application of 4P, 4C and 4R theories in neuromarketing and the public acceptance of neuromarketing, with the aim of pointing out the direction for the development of neuromarketing and providing new marketing ideas for marketers.

articleTitle: Frequency Conversion Transformation and Control Strategy Optimization of Feed Pump
abstract: Feed water pump is an important auxiliary equipment in thermal power plant. It is of great significance to improve its investment, operation economy and reliability for power production. The feed water system of 300MW unit was reformed. The original three hydraulic coupler type electric feed water pumps were transformed into a feed water control system of two pump hydraulic coupling frequency conversion composite control and one pump hydraulic coupling scoop tube control. The hydraulic coupling frequency conversion composite control logic was added, the feed water system control logic was optimized, and the relevant protection settings and interlocks were improved. A period of operation shows that the unit operation economy and equipment reliability have been improved.

articleTitle: Time-Optimal Orbital Maneuvering for Bearings-Only Pursuit-Evasion Game
abstract: This paper studies the problem of impulse sequence design for time-optimal pursuit for a maneuverable evader only using line-of-sight (LOS) angles measurement. To obtain the evader's orbital information., an efficient recurrent iteration least square (RILS) algorithm is proposed to estimate the evader's position and velocity utilizing the LOS angles of the evader during a period of time. Based on the estimation information., two maneuver strategies for the pursuer are proposed respectively, one of which is the near time-optimal approaching strategy to approach the evader as soon as possible and the other is the observation-optimal strategy to enhance the estimation accuracy of the RILS algorithm. The two maneuver strategies are combined with different weights to enhance the pursuit performance. The numerical simulation is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed estimation algorithm and pursuit strategy.

articleTitle: Cooperative Search and Target Response Mission Planning for Multi-UAV Systems in Dangerous Environments
abstract: The planning of a multi-UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) system's search and target response mission in dangerous environments is the focus of this publication. Among the many studies that propose algorithms for mission planning with relation to search and target response, only few of them take into account the possibility of UAV damage and crashes during the mission. This article presents a solution by proposing a value game mission planning (VGMP) scheme based on game theory for multi-UAV systems, taking consideration that crashes have a substantial impact on the system's search and target response capabilities. This method considers the UAV system as a group of intelligent agents that collaborate to choose the exploration or target response action based on values. The approach accounts for the sunk cost of the target response while also considering the possible benefit of the search expedition. To forecast the likely reward of a given action, this method also makes use of a value prediction module. Through practical simulations on various maps, the effectiveness of these proposed algorithms is assessed.

articleTitle: Adaptive Path Following Control Algorithm Design for Spherical Robots in Surface Navigation
abstract: Aiming at the navigation control problem of surface spherical robots, we developed a navigation tracking control algorithm with dynamic curve tracking capabilities. Initially, a three-degree-of-freedom kinematics and dynamics model for the spherical robot was established. Subsequently, a path following controller was designed based on Adaptive Variable Distance guidance strategy. Finally, a heading tracking controller, with a dual loop control method driven by data of the system, was designed and stability analysis was performed on the inner loop controller. Field tests were conducted at sea for the entire designed algorithm, demonstrating that it could follow straight and curved paths with small errors under unknown wind and current conditions.

articleTitle: Fourier Single-Pixel Imaging Edge Detection in Arbitrary Directions
abstract: The standard edge detection method via fourier single-pixel imaging encodes the scene with Fourier patterns modulated by Sobel operators, which can directly reconstruct the object edges instead of the complete scene. This method is only sensitive to horizontal and vertical edge, which is not conducive to obtaining detailed edges because a natural image always have a variety of edge directions. However, as the number of directions increases, the sampling rate should be higher to improve the quality of edges. To trade-off low sampling rate and detailed edges, we propose an adaptive orientation and sampling number method, which can collect proper high-frequency information within a limited number of samples to accommodate the uncertainty of natural target edge orientation by introducing an arbitrary directional Sobel operator with spectral radial correlation. The simulation results show that the method in this paper has the highest image signal-to-noise ratio compared with the other two methods at 5%, 10% and 25% sampling rates. And it can reconstruct the edges of the image in any direction with high quality and reduce the reconstruction noise with a limited number of samples.

articleTitle: Design of Automatic Bobbin Packaging Production Line and Control System
abstract: In order to improve the packaging efficiency and quality of package yarn, design and realize the fully automatic package yarn packaging production line and its control system, and realize the automatic control of the whole package yarn packaging process, HMI on-site monitoring and centralized monitoring of the host computer. Improving the automation level of enterprises. According to the process flow of package yarn packaging in the enterprise and the modular design idea, the packaging production line is decomposed into package turnover, single yarn packaging shrinkage, buffer type alignment, woven bag packaging, automatic sewing and turning, automatic bundling, online weighing and labeling; the control management system based on Siemens S7-1200PLC, KTP1200 touch screen and remote host computer is designed, combined with PROFIBUS module and input and output module, the on-site monitoring of the running status of the production line is realized through the touch screen. The remote host computer is built to realize remote monitoring and management of the production line. It has been proved by operation that the automatic bobbin packaging production line runs stably and realizes local and remote control management. Compared with traditional manual packaging or low-level automation equipment, it has the advantages of strong stability and flexible configuration of system modules. Improve the packaging efficiency and automation level of spinning enterprises.

articleTitle: Fractional-Order Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control for Quadrotor UAV Under Actuator Saturation
abstract: In this study, a delicate fractional-order fast terminal sliding mode controller is proposed for the position and attitude tracking of a quadrotor UAV under actuator saturation. In this controller, the fractional order calculus is incorporated to the fast terminal sliding mode surface design, which can enhance the convergence speed of the controlled UAV system. Meanwhile, to solve the problem of actual control input limitation, a RBF-based estimator is designed to evaluate the error between the virtual control input and actual control output. The stability of the controlled system is proved by using Lyapunov theorem, where the validity and effectiveness of the proposed controllers and estimator are verified by a detailed numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Feature Point Extraction and Matching Based on Improved SURF Algorithm
abstract: To tackle the issues of slow searching and insufficient precision in feature detection and matching using the SURF algorithm, an improved image matching algorithm based on SURF algorithm has been proposed. Compared with SURF algorithm, by optimizing key components, this novel approach makes the feature detection and matching faster and more accurately. First, the conventional SURF algorithm is used to find the target image's feature points, and generate a 64-dimensional vector to represent the feature description of each point. Then, several nearest neighbors of each feature point are quickly found by building a KD- Tree. In order to optimize the feature points in both directions, the RANSAC algorithm is utilized to remove the set of incorrectly matched feature points. The findings of the experiments indicate that the improved algorithm suggested in this research enhances matching precision and speeding up feature point matching.

articleTitle: Confrontation-LSTM Network for stock trend prediction
abstract: The prediction of time series has a wide scope of applications in finance, however, for dynamic periodic patterns of the stock market, traditional forecasting methods cannot well capture the complex nonlinear dependencies among multiple time series. Also, compared to the standard static input learning approach, stock prices are subject to stochastic changes over time due to multiple market factors during the listing time, which is extremely challenging for model generalization. To address this problem, we design a new stock trend prediction algorithm CL-Net (Confrontation-LSTM Network), which makes the most of the “gate” structure in LSTM to solve the long-term dependency problem of previous RNN prediction methods. There are several issues with prediction caused by static features, we introduce an adversarial training model by adding perturbations to mimic the stochastic transformations of real stock price variables. The forecasting results of CL-Net on two real stock data show that it outperforms the state-of-art stock-prices trending forecasting schemes, and our model is more suitable for dealing with dynamic and volatile stock markets.

articleTitle: Similarity Registration Algorithm of 3D Point Clouds Based on Improved ICP
abstract: For the similarity registration problem of 3D point clouds data with a large amount of noise and outliers, this paper proposes a similarity registration algorithm of 3D point clouds based on improved iterative closest point (ICP). Firstly, a similarity registration optimization model of 3D point clouds is established by introducing the pseudo-Huber loss function, to obtain accuracy similarity registration of 3D point clouds. Secondly, the initial scale factor is solved according to the scale consistency criterion. Thus, the similarity registration problem is transformed into the corresponding rigid registration problem. Finally, the rigid transformation is solved for each scale factor according to the scale factor interval. By using alternating iterations, the optimal rigid transformation and scale factor can be obtained. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve high similarity registration accuracy by efficiently suppress the noise and outliers.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Co-evolution Algorithm for Multi-Constraints Electric Vehicle Routing Optimization
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are the primary means of transportation for urban logistics. The key of the EVs logistics distribution is to achieve the efficient routing optimization and charging arrangement. This paper considers an electric vehicle routing problem with time windows that takes the mileage cost and number of vehicles cost into account. An optimization algorithm based on the hybrid co-evolution mechanism is proposed to solve the problem. Specifically, the delivery scheme is initialized by the sand cat swarm optimization algorithm, and improved by discrete search and large neighborhood search. In addition, the elite individual migration mechanism is introduced to take advantage of the collaboration among the sand cat population, which improves the solution quality of the hybrid algorithm. Finally, the experiment results prove that the hybrid co-evolution algorithm has a better optimal solution to the multi-constrained electric vehicle routing problem.

articleTitle: Improved Integral Sliding Mode Control Strategy of PMLSM Based on Extended State Observer
abstract: A composite control strategy with an improved integral sliding mode controller (ISMC) and an extended state observer (ESO) is proposed for the permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMSLM) servo system that is easily affected by uncertainties such as parameter variations, load perturbations and friction. Firstly, a mathematical model of the permanent magnet linear synchronous motor considering the total disturbance is established; secondly, an improved integral sliding mode control strategy is proposed to design the speed controller and the stability is proved by Lyapunov, and in order to further enhance the anti-disturbance performance of the system, an extended state observer is introduced to estimate the system disturbances and apply them to feedforward compensation, and stability is proved for the system as a whole; finally, the feasibility of the proposed control method is verified by simulation, which can effectively improve the robustness and convergence speed of the system and reduce the chattering generated by the sliding mode surface.

articleTitle: Imitation Learning Method of Multi-quality Expert Data Based on GAIL
abstract: This paper focuses on the imitation learning methods of multi-quality expert data based on Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning (GAIL). The agent is able to acquire high-quality behavioral policies through GAIL by imitating actions from experts and learning the experience distribution instead of the reward function. Considering that multi-quality expert imitation learning can achieve the effect of data augmentation, a novel GAIL-based method named MT-GAIL is proposed for imitation learning. We first define the reliability coefficient of different expert data by calculating the accuracy of corresponding discriminator. Then the reliability coefficient is used as the weight to calculate the reward function that is defined as the sum of the products of the weights and the output of corresponding discriminator. The series of rewards, states and actions are finally fed into the experience pool to train the network of policy builder. We compare the GAIL method through experiments for the cases of single-expert and multi-quality expert trajectories, which shows that the proposed MT-GAIL method is capable of avoiding the worst expert data. The effects of different reward value calculation methods on multi-quality expert data are also conducted to illustrate the distinct advantage of our proposed discriminator output value weighting method.

articleTitle: Distributed Cooperative Decision-Making of Cross-Domain Swarm
abstract: This paper investigates a cooperative decision-making problem of the cross-domain swarm system involving unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Different from the distributed optimization of multi-agent systems, the cooperative decision-making problem considers the payoff functions that depend on the states of all agents. Each agent can only adjust its own state. To address the cooperative decision-making problem, a two-time scale system is constructed, where the fast model includes an average consensus for gradient estimation of the global function and the slow model incorporates a feedback control of all USVs and UAVs. By the Lyapunov analysis, the optimal solution is globally exponentially stable. Finally, a cooperative encirclement task is utilized to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Multi-strategy optimization of HHO algorithm for path planning of warehouse robots
abstract: Aimed at path planning of warehouse robots in a storage environment, this paper proposes a multi-strategy Harris Hawks Optimization algorithm (HHO). To better deal with the uneven population distribution caused by the high randomness of individual initialization, an escape energy updating mechanism was proposed to improve population information exchange. Considering that the global optimal individual was not chosen as the guide to update location in the searching process, a searching mechanism is designed based on the maximum and minimum of the individual location, which effectively improves the tightness in the searching process. The adaptive elastic factor is introduced to disturb the current local individual and realize the rapid escape from the local optimal. After the tests of 23 benchmark functions, the multi-strategy HHO algorithm is proved to be superior to HHO in convergence speed and accuracy. Lastly, the proposed HHO algorithm is applied to three different scale warehouse grid environments, which further verifies its applicability to the high-dimensional path planning problem, and effectively improves warehouse operation efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Improved A* Algorithm and Ant Colony Algorithm of Patrol Robot
abstract: In order to increase the robot's efficiency while patrolling, a method combining A * algorithm and ant colony algorithm was proposed. A * algorithm was used to build feasible and efficient paths among each two patrol points. To shorten the computing time of A * algorithm, a new heuristic function was designed. The experimental findings confirm that the traversed nodes and the computing time were reduced, especially in the environment with fewer obstacles, by using this method. Then, the generated paths were smoothed by testing the visibility between two nodes and removing redundant nodes, which compensated for the increase in path length caused by the redefined heuristic function. Finally, ant colony algorithm was used to search the shortest patrol sequence among various patrol points, and generate the final patrol path.

articleTitle: An Improved YOLOv5 Detection Algorithm with Pruning and OpenVINO Quantization
abstract: In order to address the problem of current object detection models being too large to be deployed on robot controllers, this paper proposes improvements to YOLOv5 for real-time detection. The YOLOv5s model is pruned at the Batch Normalization (BN) layer, and further optimized using the OpenVINO tool for quantization. The results demonstrate that our improvements effectively improve the model's inference speed while maintaining its accuracy. Compared to the original YOLOv5 model, the pruned model achieves the same accuracy without degradation, with a 36.6% reduction in parameter count and a 35% reduction in weight storage file size. Furthermore, after optimization with OpenVINO, the final model achieves a FPS of 56.

articleTitle: Further Improvements on Stability Analysis for Neural Networks with Traditional Delay and Leakage Delay
abstract: In neural networks (NNs), there exist two kinds of time delay, leakage delay (LD) and traditional delay (TD). Up to now, much effort has been done to the effect of TD on the stability of NNs while the effect of LD is always ignored. This paper aims at the stability problem for NNs considering both LD and TD by Lyapunov-Krasovskii approach. First, the model of NNs considering both TD and LD is established. A novel Lyapunov- Krasovskii functional (LKF) containing the information among TD, LD and system states is constructed. Then, the novel improved reciprocally convex inequality (NIRCI) is developed. It is employed to transform the stability conditions into the form of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). The proposed stability criteria can be utilized to check whether the neural network system is stable conveniently. Finally, two numerical examples are done to demonstrate the advantages of proposed criteria and the effectiveness is proved by the simulation experiment.

articleTitle: Optimization of Fuel Cell Air Supply System Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
abstract: Focusing on the maximum power point tracking for fuel cell systems (FCSs), this paper proposes the optimization of the fuel cell (FC) air supply systems based on the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. An air compressor and stack models were built based on the working mechanism, and the model's accuracy was verified through experimental data. Aiming at the maximum output power of the FCS, a PSO algorithm was designed to obtain the air supply system's working air mass flow and pressure. The power of the FCS was optimized at different current density points. Compared with the single optimized air mass flow and conventional fixed value methods, the system power increased by an average of 630 W and 380 W in self-defined operating conditions.

articleTitle: Homography-Based Visual Servoing of a Joint-Constrained Robotic Endoscope
abstract: In recent years, homography-based visual servoing (HBVS) under remote-center-of-motion (RCM) constraints has been successfully applied to minimally invasive surgery (MIS), which can ignore explicit image depth information. However, the existing HBVS control scheme fails to consider the joint constraints of the endoscopy robot and requires computing the Jacobian pseudo-inverse. To tackle these challenges, this article proposes an innovative HBVS control scheme that incorporates physical limits, RCM and HBVS constraints into a quadratic programming (QP) formulation. Subsequently, the QP problem can be solved by a gradient-based neural network (GNN). After that, simulations and experiments based on a robotic endoscope coupled with a Franka Emika Panda robot are conducted to validate the superiority of the proposed HBVS control scheme in achieving visual servoing.

articleTitle: Endo-SLAM:A Dense Endoscopic SLAM with Neural Implicit Representation
abstract: Accurate camera tracking and dense scene reconstruction are essential foundations for achieving automated surgical procedures. Many existing vision-based approaches struggle to address the prevalent specular reflections present in endoscopic videos. Moreover, the real-time reconstruction results from current methods often fail to provide reliable and precise geometric information for downstream tasks. This paper introduces a SLAM system tailored for endoscopic videos, based on neural implicit representation. Leveraging existing depth estimation models, we acquire geometric priors of the scene, facilitating a continuous and dense reconstruction of the surgical field. To mitigate the impacts of challenges like specular reflections on the system's performance, we employ neural radiance fields to model the intricate lighting conditions in the scene, thereby enhancing the precision of localization. The efficacy of our system is validated on both simulated datasets and real medical datasets.

articleTitle: Ascent Corridor Design Method for Combined Power Hypersonic Vehicles
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of air-breathing combined power vehicles with many constraints in the ascent stage and high precision requirements of terminal windows, a flight corridor design method based on the velocity-altitude profile is proposed. The velocity-altitude profile is used to describe the flight corridor, the relationship between constraints and velocity and altitude is analyzed, and the constraints contained in the upper and lower boundaries of the corridor are determined. Based on the analysis of the constraints, the angle of attack that satisfies the constraints and maximizes or minimizes the altitude at the current velocity is solved. A sample vehicle is used as an example to design and analyze the flight corridor in the ascent stage, and the calculation result shows that the method can be used for flight corridor design under multiple constraints in the ascent stage of the combined power vehicle.

articleTitle: Distributed Finite-Time Filtering of Switched Positive Systems with Communication Delays and Deception Attacks
abstract: This article investigates the design of secure finite-time distributed filters, for linear discrete-time switched positive systems in the presence of deception attacks and communication delays. Consider a set of sensors with communication interaction for measuring the output information of switched positive systems. In an interactive sensor network, in the event of a random failure in the interactive communication topology, sensor network based on a given interactive communication topology can share its measurement values with its neighboring nodes. In addition, considering the impact of deception attacks on the aggregated measurement information transmitted through communication networks, the aggregated measurement values of sensors will be compromised. Based on the above issues, the following solutions are proposed. Firstly, a sensor transmission model is proposed based on the effects of random communication link failures, deception attacks, and communication delays. Secondly, the network communication delay is considered Markov process related, and the filters is modeled as a Markov jump system using an augmented matrix. Thirdly, considering the target system switching based on the ADT rule, a sufficient condition for the finite time performance of distributed residual systems is obtained by constructing linear multiple co-positive Lyapunov functional, and a scheme is provided for the design of distributed filters for switched positive systems. Finally, explained the feasibility of the system implementation scheme was verified through numerical simulation.

articleTitle: A Refined Prediction Method of Short Wind Velocity Along High-Speed Rail Based on Transformer
abstract: To solve the problem of wind forecasting and early warning along high-speed railway, we proposed a short-term refined gale prediction method based on Transformer. Firstly, in order to distinguish the topography of different monitoring sites along the railway, we use K-means clustering algorithm to classify the data of different monitoring sites. Secondly, the Inverse Distance Weight (IDW) interpolation method is used to reduce the spatial scaling of meteorological forecast data. Finally, the trained Transformer model makes short-term refined gale prediction. Through the comparative experiment between prediction and observation data, the results show that the proposed method can achieve 67% wind speed prediction accuracy. The proposed algorithm is compared with LSTM and XGBoost, and evaluated by root-mean-square error, which shows that the proposed algorithm is obviously superior to other algorithms.

articleTitle: Study on Intelligent Allocation of Shipborne Weapons Air Defense Targets Considering Weapon Capability Constraints
abstract: Naval weapon air defense is a significant issue in the field of military operations, as it is crucial to allocate naval weapon systems effectively in order to protect ships from enemy threats. This paper introduces the Escape Adaptive Chaotic Particle Swarm Optimization (EACPSO) algorithm, which incorporates an escape strategy to address the Weapon Target Assignment (WTA) problem while considering weapon capability constraints. Firstly, a martial target assignment model is developed, incorporating the aforementioned constraints. Sub-sequently, the EACPSO algorithm is employed to optimize the solution, aiming to minimize both the failure probability of air defense strikes against naval targets and the sum of integrated failure probability and average strike time of each weapon. The simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed optimization algorithm in effectively resolving the shipborne weapon air defense target assignment problem.

articleTitle: Practical Finite-Time Average Consensus Tracking Algorithm for Multi-Agent Systems with Bounded and Continuous Input
abstract: For multi-agent systems, average consensus tracking (ACT) problem has gained much attention in recent years. In this paper, we consider the scenario that system subject to actuator saturation. By combining hyperbolic tangent function and local neighborhood relative state errors, a continuous-time distributed ACT algorithm is proposed, and the proposed algorithm achieves uniform bounded tracking in finite-time with adjustable tracking accuracy. What is more, the settling time and tracking accuracy of the proposed algorithm are estimated by using analytical Lyapunov method. Compared with existing ACT algorithms, the proposed algorithm not only has bounded and continuous control input, but also has practical finite-time stability. Finally, numerical simulations are provided to verify the effectiveness of our theoretical results.

articleTitle: Automatic Robotic Development through Collaborative Framework by Large Language Models
abstract: Despite the remarkable code generation abilities of large language models (LLMs), they still face challenges in complex task handling. Robot development, a highly intricate field, inherently demands human involvement in task allocation and collaborative teamwork[1]. To enhance robot development, we propose an innovative automated collaboration framework inspired by real-world robot developers. This framework employs multiple LLMs in distinct roles-analysts, programmers, and testers. Analysts delve deep into user requirements, enabling programmers to produce precise code, while testers fine-tune the parameters based on user feedback for practical robot application. Each LLM tackles diverse, critical tasks within the development process. Clear collaboration rules emulate real-world teamwork among LLMs. Analysts, programmers, and testers form a cohesive team overseeing strategy, code, and parameter adjustments [2]. Through this framework, we achieve complex robot development without requiring specialized knowledge, relying solely on non-experts' participation.

articleTitle: SOC Estimation of Lithium Battery Based on Improved Unscented Kalman Filter
abstract: An estimation approach based on adaptive unscented Kalman filter (AUKF) was presented to address the issue of low accuracy of state of charge (SOC) estimation of lithium battery with unscented Kalman filter (UKF) in the event of noise uncertainty and complex working conditions. The least squares method was employed to identify the parameters in the lithium battery's equation of state, which was created using the Thevenin equivalent circuit model. When data is gathered under experimental conditions and compared to traditional UKF, the estimation error may be kept around 4%, demonstrating the model's efficacy.

articleTitle: Distributed Interval Observer Design for a Discrete-Time LTI System
abstract: This paper introduces the investigation of distributed interval observers for discrete-time linear time-invariant systems in the presence of external disturbances and measure-ment noises. The focus is specifically on scenarios where only the boundary values of external disturbances and measurement noises are required to be known. Different gains were designed using the multi-hop decomposition method to cut down on the amount of information exchange needed to measure every agent state. The theoretical conclusions were validated through numerical simulation following careful design and analysis.

articleTitle: The Reservoir Topology of Echo State Network
abstract: Echo state network (ESN) has a unique reservoir topology and is widely used to solve a variety of problems. However, the relationship between the reservoir topology and the performance of the network is unclear. To address this problem, based on the small-world (SW) network and modularity theory, the small-world echo state network (SWESN) and modularity ESN are used to explore the relationship between the reservoir topology and the prediction performance of the network by experimental analysis. The experimental results show that the SW topology and random modularity topology of a reservoir play an important role in improving the prediction performance of the network. Moreover, the modularity echo state network with random topology (M-ESN) shows higher prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Control of Arm-Foot Robot Through Model Predictive Control and Whole Body Control
abstract: Improving the operational ability of quadruped robots by carrying a robotic arm is an important research direction for quadruped robots. In this paper, we first establish a dynamic model. On the basis of the dynamic model, the model predictive control is used to solve the ground reaction of the quadruped robot. The whole body control is used to unify the movement and operation tasks. The simple mobile grasping task of the quadruped robot is realized in Webots simulation software.

articleTitle: Security Control of Cyber-Physical System Under Continuous Collaborative Attacks
abstract: This paper mainly studied the state feedback control problem of Cyber-Physical System(CPS) with noise under the collaborative attacks of DoS and FDIAs. Firstly, by analyzing the impact of continuous collaborative attacks on different communication channels, a class of switched systems containing persistent collaborative network attacks, system noise and measurement noise are established according to different communication topologies. Secondly, by utilizing Lyapunov stability theory, sufficient conditions for the index stability of state feedback control is obtained, and a state feedback controller method based on Kalman filter estimation was provided based on linear matrix inequality technology. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the method were verified through a simulation example.

articleTitle: Design of Modular Embedded Micro Flywheel Automatic Testbed
abstract: As the torque actuator in the satellite attitude control system, the life of the micro flywheel is an important part in the working life of the satellite. Therefore, before the micro flywheel product is put into use, it is necessary to conduct factory testing on the performance and reliability of the complete micro flywheel machine. In order to solve the problems of a wide variety of flywheel product models, complex test procedures and high professional requirements for experimental operators, this article introduces a set of universal flywheels with strong versatility, high degree of automation, high test accuracy and simple operation. Automated testing platform. The platform adopts C/S (Client/Server) architecture to implement six-channel parallel testing, and is based on imx6ull and Qt (Qt Creator) software for software and hardware design and development. The hardware part integrates self-developed circuit modules and high-precision devices and adopts modular design to facilitate maintenance and expansion; the software part is based on object-oriented thinking to complete the research and development of the device interaction layer, human-computer interaction layer, business logic layer and data processing layer. The final developed test platform has been verified by experiments, and its function is perfect. It can be compatible with multi-type flywheel test. The test system has high stability, and the test accuracy and efficiency can meet the requirements.

articleTitle: Information Fusion Estimation for Nonlinear Systems with Multiplicative Noise
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed information fusion estimation problem for non-linear systems with multiplicative noise in multi-sensor systems. The paper uses virtual states with virtual process noise and designs one-step predictors and state update equations for the virtual conditions. An extended Kalman estimator with a forgetting factor is applied to optimize the valuation of each sensor for the non-linear system. matrix-weighted is used in the fusion process and compared to verify the optimization of the state valuation by adding the forgetting factor to the filtering process.

articleTitle: Fast Consensus of Discrete Multi-Agent Systems with Delay
abstract: This paper studied the fast consensus of discrete multi-agent systems (MASs) with time delay. A consensus protocol incorporating memory information is formulated to accelerate consensus. The necessary and sufficient conditions to reach average consensus are provided. Furthermore, an optimal design of the fast consensus for MASs with small delay is given, and the explicit solutions of the fastest convergence speed and corresponding optimal control gains are deduced. Finally, the theoretical findings are validated through numerical simulations, underscoring the effectiveness of the nronosed annroach.

articleTitle: Consensus of the General Second-Order MASs with Nonuniform Uncertain Time-Varying Communication Delays
abstract: This paper delves into the investigation of the consensus problem of general second-order multi-agent systems (MASs) with nonuniform uncertain time-varying communication delays. With the directed graph having a spanning tree, a distributed control protocol is proposed to achieve the consensus among all agents. By leveraging the Lyapunov-Krasovskii function and Jensen Inequality, the paper derives sufficient conditions for the consensus with communication delay. The algorithm also presents an upper bound for the admissible communication delay even in the presence of nonuniform uncertain and time-varying communication delays. The correctness is finally illustrated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-Path-Planning in Complex Intersection Based on Improved Hybrid A* and Minimum Jerk Optimization
abstract: Pre-definition of paths in intersections is an essential step in intersection management for autonomous vehicles, and it is difficult to ensure safety and smoothness of paths of all entry-exit pair of a complex intersection while obeying traffic rules. However, only a few researches cover this part and existing path/trajectory planning methods can hardly be implemented directly in the scenario, especially in terms of complex intersections. This paper is aimed to solve multi-path planning in complex intersection scenarios based on the improved hybrid A* - minimum jerk pipeline, which could adaptively generate collision-free, smooth and traffic-rule-complying paths for each entryexit pair in various complex intersections, ensuring safety and trackability. After single-path and multipath simulations in different intersections with comparison with two common path/trajectory generation methods, we tested the performance of our method and verified its feasibility and advantages.

articleTitle: Domain Adaptation for Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation
abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation has shown great potential recently, due to their independence from expensive depth labels. These methods perform well for images with the same distribution, but their prediction errors increase dramatically when encountering images with different distributions. Unfortunately, the process of capturing images is subject to various factors, leading to variations in the data distribution, which is challenging to predict accurate depth. In this paper, we propose a domain adaptation training strategy. This strategy utilizes datasets with different data distributions and adapts the ideal distribution to challenging distributions. We employ domain adaptation techniques to extract invariant depth features from these two domains, thereby effectively reducing the impact of challenging environments and improving the accuracy of depth estimation across different environments. Experiments prove the effectiveness and universality of the proposed method, and the performance is better than the baseline.

articleTitle: Plastic Content Detection Based on ResNet and Hyperspectrum
abstract: Plastic is a widely-utilized material that generates substantial waste and pollution due to its improper disposal and recycling. Therefore, it is crucial to identify and manage plastic waste. However, existing studies primarily focuses on identifying plastic waste categories, but lacks investigation into detecting plastic particle content. Hyperspectral imaging is an emerging technology that obtains spatial and critical spectral information from images, which is highly valuable for plastic detection and identification. Nonetheless, obtaining hyperspectral images is challenging, and labeling plastic particles is problematic. This study presents a methodology for data generation and a ResNet-based framework to identify the plastic content in mixed plastic hyperspectral imagery. The feasibility of this approach is demonstrated through experimentation.

articleTitle: Research on the Prediction of Cement Clinker Formation Heat Based on GA-SVM
abstract: The firing efficiency of rotary kiln reflects the heat utilization rate and firing quality of cement clinker firing process, and the clinker formation heat is the key part of the calculation of the firing efficiency of rotary kiln system, but the calculation of the clinker formation heat of cement has been relying on empirical formulas, which fails to realize the online monitoring, and there is a serious lag. To address this problem, this paper finds the input parameters related to the process and mechanism by analyzing the process and mechanism, and establishes a GA-SVM model to realize the prediction of the heat of clinker formation. After simulation, it was found that the method accurately predicts cement clinker formation heat, which has practical significance and guiding value for calculating the rotary kiln firing efficiency and the energy saving and emission reduction of the whole cement clinker firing process.

articleTitle: Path Planning Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning and Perturbed Fluids
abstract: Path planning is one of the fundamental components in autonomous navigation. Most existing works assume static and fixed environments. However, path planning is widely applied in random and dynamic environments, such as search and rescue, surveillance, and other scenarios. In this paper, we propose a method that combines deep reinforcement learning with dynamic disturbance fluid systems, enabling unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to perform navigation tasks in environments with randomness and dynamics. The method is based on the disturbance fluid algorithm and the twin-delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that this method enables UAVs to safely accomplish autonomous navigation tasks in multi-obstacle environments, showcasing its effectiveness. Moreover, compared to Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), this method exhibits superior generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: A New Assessment Method of Muscle Contraction: Video Myography
abstract: The assessment of muscle activity and contraction is significant in biomechanical research and clinical applications. Such information is commonly measured and characterized by electromyography, ultrasound imaging, and laser Doppler. In this paper, we propose a new method of Video Myography (VMG) that can be used to obtain muscle contraction information. The proposed VMG produces two results to measure muscle contraction: the Video Myogram (VMM) is used to obtain the strength of muscle contraction, and the Muscle Activity Vector-Field (MAV-F) is used to describe the two-dimensional displacement field of muscle contraction. Conventional muscle contraction measurement methods obtain a one-dimensional vibration signal of the muscle, where the contraction of muscle fibers induces a two-dimensional or even three-dimensional displacement field in the tissue, which cannot be properly quantified by these methods because they only provide a single scalar quantity. However, the Muscle Activity Vector (MAV) in the MAV-F quantifies the intensity and direction of the muscle contraction. To verify the validity of VMG, we compared the muscle activation and the signal amplitude of the VMM signal and the standard surface Electromyography (sEMG) measured by the skin electrodes. sEMG and VMM signals are simultaneously acquired and processed. The experimental results on nine participants show the validity of the VMG method.

articleTitle: Distance Based Prescribed Performance Switched Control for Spacecraft Flying Around Mission
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a distance based prescribed performance switching control for spacecraft flying around mission. The proposed control strategy investigates the chattering phenomenon and unreasonable prescribed performance function (PPF) problems in prescribed performance control (PPC) frame work. For the chattering phenomenon, a switch control strategy is designed and the control input is switched between the PPC and a nonlinear controller, then the chattering phenomenon can be avoided as the nonlinear controller doesn't contain the infinity term. As for the unreasonable PPF, an adaptive PPF is designed based on a second order system and the external input of the system is related to unattainable control force. Then the stability of the switched system is analysis based on the Lyapunov theory. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted and the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is illustrated.

articleTitle: The Lightweight Design of A Ship Object Detection Model for SAR Images
abstract: The utilization of deep learning in ship detection tasks for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images has attracted much attention. However, achieving real-time detection is a challenge due to the extensive model parameters of mainstream approaches and insufficient computing resources of embedded devices. To overcome this challenge, we propose SimBlock module and Lightweight Feature Pyramid Network (LFPN) to construct a novel detection model built upon the YOLOv5s. The proposed SimBlock modules replace the backbone network of YOLOv5s in a stacked manner. Moreover, the LFPN, which is constructed by utilizing depthwise separable convolution and G-bneck module, aims to decrease the number of parameters in the neck network of the detection model. Compared with YOLOv5s, our detection model reduces 90.2 % of parameters, while the model size is only 1.63 MB, and the mAP can achieve 94.5%.

articleTitle: Formation Outlier Formation Transformation Based on Virtual Robots
abstract: Aiming at the problem of robot swarming and the formation transformation and maintenance involved in multi-robot formation. In this paper, the formation control algorithm is based on the three principles of the Boids model, and under the framework of the pilot follower, simulates the flocking behavior of birds to realize the formation and formation maintenance of the multi-robot formation, and through the control of virtual robots to realize the individual robot's outlier control and formation transformation in the operation of multi-robot formations, and after completing the outlier, the other robots restore the original formation. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of this method are verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Design of Minimum Variance Controller for Strong Stabilization of Closed-loop Systems
abstract: Strong stabilization of the closed-loop system is desirable for the practical application, in which the controller is required to be stable. In this paper, a design method of the minimum variance (MV) controller is proposed for strong stabilization of minimum phase and non-minimum phase systems subject to stochastic output disturbances. The effectiveness of the proposed design method is illustrated by the numerical example. It shows that the output variance of the proposed minimum variance controller is closed to that of the original (unstable) one.

articleTitle: Spatial Cognition and Decision Model Based on Hippocampus-Prefrontal Cortex Interaction
abstract: Physiological experiments have shown that rats and other mammals can form neural representations of the spatial environment after exploring an unfamiliar environment, thus achieving goal-directed navigation. This spatial cognitive ability benefits from parallel processing of sensory information in rat brain networks, where the hippocampus structure is thought to be a key brain region for forming episodic memory and environmental cognition, while the prefrontal cortex receives reward information about spatiotemporal events and makes decisions. These two brain regions interact, ultimately producing goal-directed behavior and sequence planning. In order to simulate the cognitive and decision-making abilities of rats in a spatial environment, a model based on the interaction between the hippocampus and the prefrontal cortex is proposed. The model realizes goal-oriented navigation through reward propagation and forward replay mechanism. The experimental results show that the bionic navigation model can simulate the cognitive and decision-making ability of rats, which is consistent with the results of physiological studies. It provides a reference for understanding the operation mechanism of brain in cognitive process.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Cooperative Guidance Law With Impact Angle Constrained Based On Fixed-Time Convergent Error Dynamics
abstract: In this paper, three-dimensional cooperative guidance laws against stationary target are designed with both impact time and angle control. The guidance commands consist of tangential acceleration along line-of-sight (LOS) direction and normal acceleration perpendicular to LOS direction. First, the fixed-time convergent error dynamics is proposed, and the convergence time of error is related to the end time of the system. Subsequently, a fixed-time consensus protocol for multi-agent system is proposed based on the above fixed-time convergent error dynamics. Then, tangential acceleration command is designed based on the above consensus protocol. Moreover, normal acceleration commands are designed based on the predefined time global sliding mode face. The stability and convergence of the proposed cooperative guidance laws are rigorously proved. Finally, simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed guidance laws.

Author Keywords: predefined time global sliding mode face

articleTitle: Table Detection in Complex Layouts
abstract: Table detection is a critical component of document automation that has garnered increasing attention. However, accurately detecting tables with arbitrary styles presents a significant challenge. To address the problem, we propose a method to detect tables in complex layouts based on the YOLOV5 model. We introduce Deformable Convolutional Networks (DCN) into the backbone of the network to enhance table feature extraction capability from tables with arbitrary layouts. Additionally, We design a new residual module, ResDCN, which replaces the residual cell structure in the original algorithm. Additionally, we employ a Global Attention Mechanism(GAM) to efficiently exploit semantic information from channel and spatial features. Lastly, We merge Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) at the termination of the neck layer in the YOLOV5 model, promoting superior feature fusion across diverse scales. Our model shows exceptional performance in the ICDAR-2017POD table competition, with an F-measure(F1 score) of reaches 96.7%. Compared with the original YOLOV5 algorithm, our method improves the F1 score by 2.2% and attains a recall rate of 98% at a threshold of 0.6. 98% is state-of-the-art performance on the dataset. When evaluated at a higher threshold of 0.8, the F1 score reaches 96.4%, placing second in terms of the F1 score. Moreover, our model evaluates the TNCR dataset and achieves unparalleled performance, particularly in detecting complex wireless tables, where the F1 score improves by 2%. These noteworthy results show our model's proficiency in accurately detecting tables with diverse styles embedded in complex layouts.

articleTitle: Research on Decoupling Control Method for Feedwater System of Steam Generator in Nuclear Power Plant
abstract: The nuclear steam generator (SG) is an important component for nuclear power plant which transfers heat from the primary side coolant to the secondary side water. Water supply system is composed of water supply pump and feed water adjusting valve, and the water level of the steam generator is adjusted by the change of feed water flow rate. Changes in regulating valve opening and feed pump speed can both affect changes of feed water flow, and unrelated regulation of the two control variables will lead to mutual effects on the regulating effect, which makes the regulating time longer and the flow control deviation larger. In order to solve the coupling problem of feed pump and feed regulating valve of feed water system, the coupling characteristic of feed pump and feed regulating valve are studied in this paper. The paper analyzes the dynamic impact characteristics of feed pump speed on feed water flow rate and pressure difference of water supply adjusting valve, and also the dynamic impact characteristics of the opening of the water supply adjusting valve on feed water flow rate and pressure difference of water supply valve. A feedforward control scheme of water supply adjusting valve is further proposed for feedwater system decoupling, and the control simulation is conducted based on a flow rate step process. The simulation results show that the feed water flow response speed after decoupling is significantly improved, and the steady-state regulation time is shortened by more than 40%. Meanwhile, the maximum control difference of the feed water regulating valve is reduced by more than 60%.

articleTitle: Mixed-Flow Avoidance Control of Dynamically Reconfigurable Discrete Event Systems
abstract: Generally, in an epidemic, types and amounts of patients are always unpredictable. Therefore, doctors, medical facilities, and consulting rooms of hospitals needs be redeployed to ensure safety of diagnosing and treating environment. In this sense, a hospital can be considered as a dynamic reconfigurable discrete event system. How to avoid cross-infection among patients in a hospital during a period of epidemic is critical. The current work models the patient visiting process in a hospital by using a work flow net (WF-net), where patients are represented by tokens. On this application background, a new problem named mixed-flow relation in a WF-net is presented, which leads to cross-infection among patients. A detection method of the mixed-flow relation is developed and a mixed-flow avoidance controller is designed accordingly in the work. The effectiveness of the proposed method is illustrated by a group of experiments.

articleTitle: Nonlinear modeling between steering wheel angle and front wheel angle for unmanned vehicle
abstract: Unmanned vehicles have attracted notable attention in recent years. Trajectory control is one of the core problems of unmanned vehicles. It is meaningful to establish a precise model between the steering wheel angle and the wheel angle. This paper focus on the corresponding turning characteristics of the steering wheel angle and the front wheel angle for front-wheel steering vehicles. A novel nonlinear model with exponential terms and parameters is proposed. Base on measured data, the proposed nonlinear model has the minimal modeling error compared to other two linear models. The average absolute error is 0.1413°, which is a very small value. The simulation results illustrated the effectiveness of the proposed nonlinear model of the steering wheel angle and front wheel angle. This model can be applied to the trajectory control for unmanned vehicles.

articleTitle: Application of the Informer Long-Term Sequence Model in Agricultural Temperature Prediction
abstract: Long-term temperature prediction plays a pivotal role in agricultural production. While existing research has predominantly focused on short-term forecasts, this study delves into the realm of long-term predictions. Leveraging the power of the Informer model, this work successfully predicted the temperature for the upcoming month in the Shihezi region of Xinjiang, China, yielding highly satisfactory results with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 3.33 for the temperature prediction. Moreover, through empirical analysis, we showcase the practical applications of these prediction outcomes in agriculture. This study not only assesses the need for forecasting cold damage in the coming year but also provides guidance for agricultural production based on future temperature trends, underscoring the potential value of the research findings.

articleTitle: Shunting Route Search Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In recent years, with the application of advanced intelligent technology, the level of automation in station train operations has greatly improved. However, due to the complexity and high uncertainty of shunting operations, the challenge of the implementation of automation in shunting operations is attracting more and more attention. Moreover, the establishment of shunting routes lacks the support of advanced technology to enhance efficiency and accuracy. In order to improve the efficiency of shunting route search, which has a significant impact on route establishment, a shunting route search algorithm based on reinforcement learning, and more specifically, Q-learning is proposed. By analyzing the characteristics of shunting operations, two more specific scenarios that should be considered in shunting route search are proposed: time-conflict scenario and spatial-disturbance scenario. Experiments under ideal scenario and spatial-disturbance scenario are conducted to evaluate the performance of the Q-Iearning approach. The simulation results show the efficiency and effectiveness of the Q-learning method for shunting route search under both scenarios.

articleTitle: Defect Detection Method of PCB Small Target Based on Improved YOLOv5
abstract: In response to the problem of low detection accuracy in current PCB defect detection, this paper proposes a PCB defect detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv5. First, a GAM attention module is incorporated into the backbone network to enhance the model's feature extraction capability; Second, a small target detection layer is introduced to strengthen the fusion of deep semantic information with shallow semantics, thereby improving the detection performance of small target defects in PCBs; Finally, a new loss function SIoU was introduced in the YOLOv5 network model to replace the original CIoU loss function. SIOU smoothed the overlap between the predicted box and the true box, which is beneficial for the stability and convergence speed of the training process. Conduct a series of ablation and comparative experiments on the PCB defect dataset, and the experimental results indicate that that the improved YOLOv5 network model improves the mAP value from 95.4% to 99.0% compared with the original network, and the detection effect is better than the original network model and the traditional classical target detection network model.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Strategy of the Cascade Four-Switch Buck-Boost Converter
abstract: The cascaded four-switch Buck-Boost converter possesses a diverse range of operating modes and a straight-forward structure, making it well-suited for converting a wide range of input voltages. Traditional double-closed-loop control strategy is characterized by numerous PI parameters and complex control. In this paper, a proposed approach aims to address these challenges by introducing a model predictive control strategy (MPC) for Buck-Boost transformer control. On the basis of the three-mode control method, the model prediction control algorithm is used to predict the current, voltage and duty cycle of each working mode in the next cycle. According to the duty cycle prediction result of different working modes in the next control cycle, the most suitable working mode is selected for mode switching, and the response speed of the system is improved. In this paper, the model predictive control strategy and double closed-loop control of the cascaded four-switch Buck-Boost converter are compared and verified by the simulation results, and the simulation results show that the proposed control strategy can realize the smoother mode switching of the four-switch Buck-Boost converter and improve the dynamic response speed.

articleTitle: Q-Learning Design for Discrete-Time Stochastic Zero-Sum Games
abstract: This study explores the application of the model-free Q-Learning algorithm in discrete-time linear quadratic stochastic zero-sum games. The main contribution is two-fold: firstly, extending the zero-sum game concept to stochastic situation and resolving it through a model-based approach; secondly, introducing a model-free Q-Learning algorithm as an innovative method, differing from conventional policy iteration and value iteration. Detailed mathematical demonstrations are included, validating the model-free Q-Learning algorithm's convergence within this research. A numerical example is provided to demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on Hybrid Flow-Shop Scheduling Problem Based on Seeker Optimization Algorithm
abstract: When optimizing the hybrid flow shop scheduling problem with the objective of minimizing completion time, traditional intelligent optimization algorithms have limitations such as low solution accuracy, a propensity to converge to local optima, and slow convergence speeds. To address these issues, this paper introduces the Seeker Optimization Algorithm (SOA) to the shop scheduling problem. SOA possesses robust global search capabilities and a flexible local search function, which enables it to efficiently discover optimal solutions. This paper begins by comparing the performance of SOA with that of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) Algorithm in solving standard functions. Subsequently, SOA is applied to the hybrid flow shop scheduling problem. Experimental results are compared with traditional intelligent optimization algorithms, the convergence accuracy and speed of optimization is increased.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Gearbox Fault Diagnosis Based on Semi-Supervised Prototypical Network and Contrastive Learning
abstract: Due to the scarcity of labeled faulty data in industrial practice, fault diagnosis models often face challenges related to overfitting and limited accuracy. This article introduces a novel solution to tackle the problem—a fault diagnosis method that leverages a combination of a semi-supervised prototype network and contrastive learning. Firstly, a limited number of labeled samples is employed to construct pairs of positive and negative samples. And the training method of contrastive learning is used to provide appropriate initial parameters for the autoencoder. Secondly, the autoencoder is employed as a feature mapping function within the prototype network and obtains the prototype using a limited number of labeled samples. Finally, a prototype refinement method fine-tunes the prototype through unlabeled data, reducing the impact of anomalous data and obtaining a more stable and accurate prototype. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated using gearbox data as a validation dataset. Through comparative analysis with other methods, the results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: Abnormal Object Detection with an Improved YOLOv8 in the Transmission Lines
abstract: The abnormal objects hanging on the power transmission lines, such as nests, kites and balloons, can cause discharge faults which would endanger the safety of the power grid, especially under severe weather conditions. This paper proposes a power transmission line foreign object recognition algorithm based on the DnCNN network and YOLOv8 network. First, a denoising convolutional neural network (DnCNN) is applied for the image preprocessing to enhance the clarity of the images. Subsequently, the efficient multi-scale attention (EMA) network is applied in the backbone of YOLOv8 model to improve the channel description capability along with better pixel-level attention on the feature maps. At last, an image dataset is developed using the current inspection images and public datasets, and various scenes (such as foggy weather and heavy rainfall) are simulated via the blurring techniques with noises to diversify the dataset. Experiments have been performed to demonstrate that the proposed model can achieve high accuracy with an average precision (mAP) of 82.9%. Experiments have also been conducted in adverse weather conditions with comparison of the original YOLOv8 model to confirm the higher detection accuracy of the proposed object detection algorithm.

articleTitle: Multiple UAVs Formation Tracking and Monitoring Control for the Shearer*
abstract: The multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) cooperative tracking and monitoring control for the shearer is investigated via formation control technology. The trajectory of the shearer is designed by installing multiple rotation sensors. Then, formation controllers are designed for each UAV to tracking the promoted trajectory. Finally, the effectiveness of designing a formation controller was demonstrated based on simulation technology.

articleTitle: Gas Monitoring System for Underground Pipe Gallery Based on Fiber Optic Energy Information Sharing and ZigBee
abstract: The safety monitoring of underground pipe gallery is of great significance for practical applications, and gas monitoring is the main means of fire detection. ZigBee wireless sensor networks have the advantages of low cost, low power consumption, and large network capacity. Simultaneously utilizing optical fibers for energy supply and information transmission solves problems such as onsite energy supply difficulties, long-distance transmission, and the impact of complex environments on communication quality. The effective combination of ZigBee wireless sensor network and fiber optic energy information sharing provides high reliability for gas monitoring in underground pipe gallery.

articleTitle: Composite Detection Method for Subsurface Defects in Gas Gathering Station Pipelines Using Eddy Current and Ultrasonic Techniques
abstract: The gas gathering station is the first hub of the entire natural gas pipeline transmission. Some of the pipelines at the gas gathering station have wall thickness thinning, perforation and other damages, which affect the safe production operation of the gas gathering station. For a single pulse eddy current testing (ECT) or ultrasonic testing (UT) classification accuracy and detection range is limited and other problems, this paper investigates the ECT and UT composite detection method. In this paper, an optimized Dempster-Shafter(D-S) evidence fusion method based on fuzzy C-mean (FCM) clustering is proposed. First, the feature parameters of the ECT and UT response signals are extracted separately and the affiliation matrix is obtained by the FCM clustering method as the respective Basic probability assignment (BP A) of detection; Then, a solution to the problem of conflicting evidence in the composite process of heterogenous sensors is proposed to amend the ECT data by using the clustering centers obtained from the UT feature. Finally, effective classification of defects with different depths is achieved by fusing the BP As of ECT and UT using D-S evidence. The results show that compared with the traditional D-S evidence fusion method based on Bayes transform and single-sensor detection technique, the detection method proposed in this paper has improved the identification accuracy and detection range of subsurface defects.

articleTitle: Online Sparse Learning Object Tracking Based on Spatio-Temporal Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) has proven to be an effective tool for feature extraction in image processing of object tracking. However, its application in target tracking poses several challenges, including high computational complexity, insufficient training samples, limited spatiotemporal context(STC), difficulty with online learning, and more. In this work, we explore these key issues based on CNN theory and propose solutions to address them. Firstly, this study proposes an optimized spatiotemporal convolutional network that incorporates an online sparse learning method and an adaptive online sparse learning algorithm, which effectively leverages STC. Secondly, this study assesses the algorithm's effectiveness by measuring its precision and success rate against eight other known algorithms in six distinct interference scenarios using the OTB100 dataset. Finally, the comparison of experimental results on the dataset suggests that our enhanced algorithm, which is based on CNN, exhibits strong performance in terms of both tracking accuracy and realtime capabilities.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Production Forecasting Method Based on Hybrid Weighted Feature Selection and Neural Network with Recursive Units and Attention Mechanism
abstract: In the chemical production process, the production data are characterized by high dimensionality, high coupling, nonlinearity, and time-varying nature, which makes it difficult for traditional methods to evaluate and analyze effectively. Therefore, a novel production modeling method (Npmm) for complex processes based on a multivariate hybrid weighted feature selection method fused with gated recursive units with an attention mechanism is established in this paper. In this model, the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator(Lasso), Extreme Gradient Boosting(Xgboost), and Random Forest(RF) are used to select the feature variables to be selected, and then the correlation matrix mapping is established to select the key characteristic variables that affect production, and then the data are fed into the gated recursive unit with the introduction of the attention mechanism. After that, and a novel production prediction model for complex chemical processes was established. Finally, the model is applied to the production process of propylene to achieve high-dimensional, highly coupled, nonlinear, and time-varying data modeling, and compared with the mainstream modeling methods, it has a better effect under the evaluation indexes of MSE and RMSE, reaching 5.5432 and 2.3544, respectively, which indicates that the method has a better advantage in the complex chemical process, and it provides an effective technological solution for the modeling of complex chemical process data.

Author Keywords: multivariate hybrid weighted feature selection method

articleTitle: Towards Sustainable Urban Intersections: An Equitable Vehicle Emission-Based Traffic Signal Control System
abstract: The growing number of vehicles on roads has re-sulted in longer travel times, decreased mobility, and heightened environmental impact. In this paper, we present a framework for a traffic signal control system that utilizes vehicle emission measurements. The primary objective of this system is to effectively balance vehicle emissions across different approaches and ensure fairness for vehicles entering intersections. Initially, we determined the emission measurements for vehicles in each approach and subsequently selected the top priority approach. To further promote fairness, we introduced the concept of vehicle fairness and applied it to our traffic signal control system. Simulation results demonstrated the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

articleTitle: PCB Bare Board Defect Detection Based on Improved YOLOv7-Tiny
abstract: A PCB bare board defect detection model based on an improved YOLOv7-tiny is proposed in order to simplify computation, increase detection accuracy, and minimize the number of model parameters. The coordinate attention mechanism is introduced with the purpose of helping the network locate defects more precisely, and the SimCSPSPPF module is introduced to further improve the network's feature extraction powers. The RepGhostN et network is used as a new feature extraction network to boost the extraction of the features of images, reduce the computational complexity, capture richer semantic information, as well as improve the accuracy of detection. According to the results from the experiment, the number of parameters and computing effort in the modified model are correspondingly down from the original model by 33.3 % and 43.2 %, respectively, but instead the mAP (mean Average Precision) rises by 2.95%. The enhanced YOLOv7-tiny makes it possible to be implemented in edge devices by increasing detection accuracy and decreasing processing and parameter counts.

articleTitle: Research on Satellite Attitude Control Scheme with Multi-Source Disturbance Suppression
abstract: The problem of satellite attitude control under multiple disturbance sources is studied in this paper. Usually, satellites carry multiple payload devices, and each payload has different start-up times, operating hours, and motion characteristics during operation, resulting in various disturbances to the satellite's attitude. The paper first analyzes the motion characteristics under different loads and sorts out two typical disturbance torques. For the constant disturbance torque, a state observer based on satellite attitude dynamics is proposed to estimate the disturbance torque. Periodic disturbance signals are further divided into two categories. For periodic disturbance torques with known parameters, a disturbance torque fitting feedforward compensation method considering actuator delay is proposed. For periodic disturbance torques with unknown parameters, an adaptive disturbance suppression method based on Lyapunov principle is proposed that can identify parameters. The paper further proposes a solution for attitude control when the satellite is in orbit and subject to multiple sources of disturbance at the same time. Finally, mathematical simulation was conducted on a satellite, and the results showed that the proposed control scheme can effectively suppress various disturbances. After applying the proposed scheme, the suppression of disturbance effects exceeded 90%, verifying the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Handling Stability of the Chassis System of Intelligent Vehicles
abstract: The rapid development of intelligent vehicles has put forward higher requirements for chassis system architecture. A good chassis system is the determining factor for improving vehicle performance, driving experience, and passenger experience. Among them, the suspension in the chassis system is the key to ensuring the ride comfort and handling stability of intelligent vehicles.
