Therefore, in order to improve the ride comfort and handling stability of intelligent vehicles, this article focuses on the dynamic analysis of the chassis suspension system of intelligent vehicles. Firstly, a vehicle chassis system including passengers and suspension was established. Furthermore, based on parameters such as wheel speed, the ride comfort of intelligent vehicles was analyzed using Simulink in Matlab; On this basis, in order to ensure the handling stability of intelligent vehicles, the steering maneuverability of intelligent vehicles was mainly studied based on Simpack software, providing ideas for the development of intelligent vehicle chassis systems.

articleTitle: Research on Improved A* Path Planning Algorithm Based on Local Environment
abstract: Path planning is a key technology to realize autonomous navigation of mobile robots and intelligent vehicles, and how to make the robot search for an optimal global path in a complex and changing environment is a current technical challenge. In this paper, based on the classical A* algorithm, we firstly establish a hybrid neighborhood search switching mechanism to make the neighborhood traversal more flexible and reasonable, and then propose a new distance estimation model based on local environment and introduce an environmental gain to adjust the heuristic function weights adaptively, and finally use quasi-uniform B-spline curve to further optimize the generated path. The experimental data and results show that the overall performance of the improved A* algorithm is better than the original algorithm. The path length is reduced by more than 10% while that of the number of traversed nodes even reaches 70%, and the path smoothness is greatly improved and the overall optimization effect is remarkable.

articleTitle: Dissolved Gas Analysis for Transformer Fault Diagnosis Based on Capsule Network
abstract: To solve the limitations of current dissolved gas analysis based transformer fault diagnosis methods and further improve the diagnostic accuracy, this paper develops a novel transformer fault diagnosis approach based on the Capsule Network (CapsNet). By combining the unique capability of CapsNet to handle vectors and the characteristics of dissolved gases in transformer oil, our approach is able to accurately model the intricate nonlinear relationship between dissolved gases and fault types, realizing the automatic extraction of key features. The dynamic routing technique and backpropagation algorithm are used for training the diagnostic model. Case studies on the real DGA data from a power grid validate that our approach outperforms both SVM and DBN across three performance metrics, demonstrating its advantages in real-world transformer fault diagnosis applications.

articleTitle: Research on Customer Electricity Behaviour Based on K-Means Clustering Algorithm
abstract: With the State Grid Power Company paying great attention to customer service, it has carried out differentiated services for important and high-risk customers to improve the level of power supply services, for which it is necessary to analyze the set of influencing factors and the correlation or causal structure by using correlation mining technology. In this paper, firstly, K-means clustering algorithm, normalization algorithm and other statistical analysis methods are used to portray the characteristics of electricity users from the aspects of industry characteristics, customer value, electricity demand, etc., to excavate the hidden data and potential value of the user's electricity consumption data, and to derive the four types of typical user electricity load characteristic curves. And then establish the corresponding four types of typical user classifications, and get the results of the characteristics of the four types of electricity consumption behaviors, and through the result analysis The electricity consumption characteristics of the above users are derived. Finally, combined with the user clustering load curve diagram, the behavioral characteristics of the user's electricity consumption are analyzed to provide support for the refined management of the customer's electricity consumption and the provision of high-quality electricity consumption services.

articleTitle: Maneuvering Target Tracking of UAV in Urban Environment with PPO-MT
abstract: Tracking a maneuvering target using UAVs in an uncertain environment poses significant challenges. In order to solve the problem of maneuvering target tracking of UAV in urban environment, this paper proposes the proximal policy optimization with memory and transformer(PPO-MT) algorithm based on PPO algorithm. The PPO-MT algorithm uses a memory unit and transformer to make full use of the information from multiple time steps of the UAV and consider the importance weight of that information. Compared to the PPO algorithm, the PPO-MT algorithm demonstrated a remarkable increase of 41.7% in convergence speed and a notable improvement of 16.5% in success rate. Moreover, the average reward and maximum reward obtained by the PPO-MT algorithm during the training process are higher than the PPO algorithm.

articleTitle: Lane-Changing Decisions Making for Autonomous Vehicles via Behavior Cloning and Decision Tree
abstract: The use of behavior cloning technology for autonomous driving decision-making has become a research hot spot at home and abroad. Existing research methods are limited to existing data sets. The data is single and scarce, and the robustness of the algorithm cannot be verified interactively. The accuracy and convergence speed of the algorithm are limited. In this paper, we divide the lane-changing decision-making process of autonomous driving vehicles into two layers. The upper layer uses the decision tree algorithm to select tasks, selects lane-changing task or lane keeping task according to road conditions, subdivides traffic scenes, and simplifies the data space for behavior cloning. The lower layer uses end-to-end behavior cloning and outputs the steering wheel angle and the throttle angle control amount. Firstly, build the lane changing scene on the CARLA simulator, collect and preprocess the driving data, then use attribute reduction to filter appropriate attributes, and use decision tree algorithm to extract driving rules, finally the lane-changing task and the lane-keeping task are learned through the behavior cloning algorithm respectively. The training results are analyzed and simulated in CARLA. The results show that the accuracy and convergence speed of the behavior cloning algorithm are improved after the division of decision tree algorithm, the lane changing task loss is reduced by 6.25%, and the lane keeping task loss is reduced by 9.38%.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based Autonomous Aircraft Navigation with Potential-Based Reward Shaping
abstract: Autonomous navigation is essential to promoting the autonomy of the aircraft. While adjusting the velocity direction and altitude angles to navigate to the goal, aircraft must maintain speed to prevent losing height. In this research, a deep reinforcement learning method with a potential-based dense reward function is proposed to teach the agent to navigate independently. The method integrates the potential-based dense reward function to help the PPO algorithm with the navigation task. Experiments are conducted among three different reward functions: sparse reward, dense reward, and potential-based dense reward. The results show that the sparse reward can rarely guide the agent to navigate, whereas the rest can complete the assignment. Furthermore, the agent with the potential-based dense reward has a 15% greater task success rate than the agent with the dense reward. Finally, a validation experiment is carried out to see if the well-trained agent, which excels at navigating to a fixed target point, can track another aircraft that maintains a constant path and speed. It is inferred that the proposed method is capable of not only navigating to a fixed target location but also tracking another aircraft with consistent course and speed.

articleTitle: Robot Hand-Eye Calibration Method Based on Hunter-Prey Optimization
abstract: In order to solve problems of hand-eye calibration in robot vision systems, traditional methods are easy to be affected by noise in the calibration process, which leads to large errors. A new hand-eye calibration method based on hunter-prey optimization is proposed. The first step was to create the closed-loop mathematical model of robot hand-eye calibration, and error functions of the rotation part and the translation part of the hand-eye transformation matrix were respectively established by dual quaternion theory, and the constraint conditions were optimized by the outer point penalty function method. Then, the rotation optimization problem and the translation optimization problem were solved by the hunter-prey optimization algorithm. The problem of local optimal in the process of solving is avoided to the maximum extent. Finally, through numerical simulation and robot calibration experiments, the proposed method is compared with two traditional methods (classical two-step method Tsai and traditional dual quaternion method DQ). The results show that it has better solving accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Multiple Quasi-Proportional Resonant Control for Single-Phase Grid-Connected Inverters
abstract: This paper puts forward a more advanced control algorithm: fuzzy multiple proportional quasi-resonant control, which modifies the controller's parameters in response to input current mistake and the rate of alteration of the mistake. This algorithm combines fuzzy control and proportional resonant control in order to diminish the low harmonic components of the inverter's grid-connected current and suppress particular main frequency harmonics. The proposed control strategy's efficacy is confirmed by Matlab/Simulink simulation, which demonstrates that it can effectively diminish the low-order harmonic components of the input current, thereby enhancing dynamic performance and disturbance immunity to a certain degree. The effects of system disturbances and parameter uncertainties are either eradicated or lessened by it.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Management and Control System of Bionic Climbing Robot of Transmission Tower Based on Digital Twin
abstract: To achieve the goal of intelligent power infrastructure of transmission towers, introducing climbing robots into power grid engineering for maintenance and repair of transmission towers can improve inspection efficiency and reduce workers' labor intensity. In this paper, we solve the problem of difficult data interaction between transmission towers and climbing robots by designing a bio-inspired climbing robot as the research object. Using an innovative approach, we apply 3D modeling, robot control, communication and interaction technologies with Unity3D engine as the software platform to study the application of information and intelligence of the climbing robot on the transmission tower. We also designed a Unity3D-based data monitoring system. This study aims to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of maintenance and repair tasks on transmission towers through advanced technologies and data monitoring systems. In this study, we investigated 3D information modeling techniques in the initial setup of the system. We also used professional software for 3D modeling, data validation and optimization process, and finally realized the digital reconstruction of the climbing robot system.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of High Permeability Distribution Network Energy Storage System
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic permeability in the distribution network continues to increase. In order to improve the economic benefits of system operation and reduce the voltage fluctuation of the grid, this paper proposes a method to optimize the configuration and operation of energy storage power station on the basis of the cluster division of distributed photovoltaic. Firstly, the improved GN algorithm is used to cluster photovoltaic nodes, and energy storage power stations are set in different clusters, which can effectively reduce the calculation amount of the system. Then, on the basis of the partitioning results, several nodes are randomly selected within each cluster to set up energy storage power stations. Secondly, the multi-objective optimization model of energy storage power stations and systems is constructed by considering the investment and operation cost of energy storage power stations. Finally, taking the minimum economic cost of the distribution network system and the minimum voltage fluctuation of the grid as the optimization function, the improved NSGA-II algorithm is used to select the optimal configuration and operation strategy of the energy storage station. A 36-node system is used for simulation analysis, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Reducing the Impact of Communication Delay on Multi-AUVs Formation Control by a Predictive Compensation Method
abstract: This paper addresses the communication delay issue in the formation control of multiple autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) by utilizing a predictive compensation method. Firstly, the dynamic and kinematic models of the AUV s are established, and the formation control problem of the AUV s is transformed into a trajectory tracking problem based on the leader-follower algorithm. Subsequently, a formation controller is designed using the backstepping method. The mathematical model of the multi-AUVs formation control system with communication delay is analyzed. A predictive compensation method is proposed to solve the communication delay issue by utilizing the least squares and extended Kalman filter methods for delay compensation. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed method can reduce the relative position error compared to the motion without delay compensation.

articleTitle: Behavioral Cloning Based Model Generation Method for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) methods that train agents using simulation are well suited to solve behavioral decision-making problems. However, complex simulation platforms that have slow processing speed make RL time-consuming. It is therefore necessary to make full use of expert experience and historical simulation data to avoid training from scratch each time. Considering that the simulation data based on the expert experience are valuable, this paper proposes a new algorithm, which is derived from the behavioral cloning (BC) method, to generate the appropriate model for further RL. The proposed TD-BC algorithm is specifically designed to train policy network and value network simultaneously by using expert experience. We update the policy network by training the model output to be as consistent as possible with the given action of the expert. Then the difference between the value network output of the next moment state and the current moment state is used as the TD error to update the value network. Finally, the subsequent training tasks can be completed through simple fine-tuning with reducing the accumulation time of online learning data and improving the efficiency of the entire training process. The effectiveness of the proposed TD-BC algorithm is validated through the cases with single agent and multiple agents, respectively. In the simulation, we use behavior trees derived from expert experiences to generate historical data. The results show that the TD-BC algorithm can learn expert experience, which provides a high starting point for training and thus accelerate the process of RL.

articleTitle: A Prescribed-Instant Convergence Approach to Consensus of High-Order Multiagent Systems
abstract: Prescribed-time consensus of multiagent systems is known for its small conservativeness in settling time. Some studies even show that the consensus happens at a prescribed instant. However, the corresponding theoretical proof is not sufficient. In this work, a consensus control based on the backstepping method is designed for multiagent systems with high-order integrator dynamics. Two Lyapunov inequalities force the consensus to happen just at the prescribed instant (prescribed-instant consensus). One of the inequalities ensures the consensus happening not after the preassigned time instant (prescribed-time consensus). The other guarantees the consensus happens not before the prescribed time instant. In the numerical example, a five-node multiagent system simulation validates the proposed prescribed-instant consensus.

articleTitle: Hybrid Model for NOx Prediction in Cement Clinker Calcination Process
abstract: Accurate measurement of nitrogen oxide (NOx) concentration from cement clinker calcination process is of great importance for atmospheric environmental protection. However, the NOx concentration is difficult to measure by hardware sensors due to the harsh environment of the calcination process. In this paper, a hybrid model is developed for N Ox concentration prediction in the cement clinker calcination process. First, an improved attention mechanism is introduced into the hybrid model to improve the quality of the input signal. Then, an echo state network (ESN) is employed to develop a nonlinear model for NOx concentration prediction. Meanwhile, a regularization constraint is used to eliminate redundant information, which improves the generalization ability of ESN. The proposed hybrid model is applied to predict the NOx concentration from a real cement clinker calcination process. The experimental results show that the hybrid model is effective for NOx concentration prediction.

articleTitle: Construction Method of Partial Discharge Analog Signal Based on MATLAB
abstract: Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS), that is very significant to the stability of the whole power grid, has been widely used in Ultra High Voltage (UHV) power system. In order to truly reflect the function of the Ultra High Frequency (UHF) on-line monitoring device, the test pulse signal used for the inspecting device needs to be as realistic as possible. However, the real partial discharge (PD) pulse is difficult to obtain, and the parameters of pulse cannot be adjusted, which brings difficulties to the device inspection. In this paper a UHF PD analog signal generation system based on MATLAB is developed, the system composition, operation principle and application example are introduced. The application test shows that the PD pulse sequence generated by the simulation system is basically the same as the real PD pulse, and the output pulse amplitude, phase, time interval and other parameters can be adjusted as needed.

articleTitle: Design of Charging Station Load Forecasting Model Based on Image Classification
abstract: With the continuous popularity of electric vehicles, big data on car charging behavior has become a focus of attention. To fully explore the potential features of historical power load data and improve the prediction accuracy of short-term load prediction models, a prediction model combining RF-BIRCH, CNN-LSTM, and Bi-LSTM is proposed.This model takes the historical load, user ID, and predicted date characteristics of historical data as inputs. The historical data is divided into long-term and short-term users through RF-BIRCH, and then Bi-LSTM bidirectional short-term memory network is used to achieve charging prediction for short-term users; Using CNN-LSTM to achieve accurate prediction of long-term users; Combining long-term user load prediction results with short-term user load prediction results to achieve total load prediction of charging stations. The results show that the RMSE of the proposed model reaches 11.65%, and the MAE reaches 8.33%; This indicates that the proposed model has higher accuracy, robustness, and generalization ability compared to the comparative model

articleTitle: Offline Detection of Source-Network Coordination Performance with Generator Speed Control Excitation System
abstract: With the continuous expansion of power grid interconnection, the power grid's ability to optimize energy allocation has been greatly improved, and the safe and stable operation of the power system has been brought great pressure. Based on actual modeling, the accuracy of power grid stability analysis is getting higher and higher, and the actual power grid transmission capacity is getting closer and closer to the analysis and calculation limit. As the most important dynamic components, the generator set and its control system must give full play to its basic supporting role in the security and stability of the power grid. However, in recent years, a series of power grid disturbance events related to power plant control and protection defects/function imperfection have occurred, which have brought some hidden dangers and threats to the safe and stable operation of power grid. Generally speaking, on the one hand, the rapid development of power grid construction and the significant increase of transmission capacity have brought great pressure on the safe and stable operation of power system. On the other hand, as the basic support for the safety and stability of the power grid, the control and protection system of the conventional power station is still incompatible with the development of the current power system in many aspects, such as standards, detection methods and testing methods. In the face of these two problems, we need to change from passive to active, and actively study the performance index requirements of power plant control and protection system source network coordination, so as to make technical preparations for the revision and improvement of relevant standards. Research on off-line detection techniques for source and network coordination performance of power plant control and protection systems, implement standards and requirements, and ensure the safety and stability of power grid equipment quality. In addition, the prototype of off-line detection device which can be applied in power plant field is developed and trial-produced, which provides technical support for the popularization of off-line detection technology and the improvement of source network coordination performance of power plant control and protection system.

articleTitle: A Mobile Robot Indoor Positioning System Based on ArUco Array and Extended Kalman Filter
abstract: To improve the accuracy and robustness of indoor positioning of robots and avoid the use of high-cost sensors such as LiDAR and high-precision Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), a positioning method using an ArUco marker array as a manual marker and a camera as a global absolute positioning sensor is used. In addition, a fusion localization algorithm based on dynamic variance Extended Kalman filtering (EKF) is proposed to fuse visual information, wheel encoder information and IMU data, effectively improving the accuracy of indoor localization and reducing the influence of dynamic environment. Simulated experiments and indoor scene positioning tests are carried out to evaluate the viability of the positioning algorithm, and they are contrasted with the single sensor positioning approach. Experimental results show that the method can accurately localize indoor mobile robots.

articleTitle: FGTC Based Remaining Useful Life Prediction with Incomplete Bearing Dataset
abstract: Prognostics and health managemen is a vital technology for implementing the health management and predictive maintenance of rotating machinery. However, due to the lack of complete running data set of bearing, the practical application of life prediction is greatly restricted. Therefore, this paper proposes a feature generated time convolutional (FGTC) network framework, including coding layer time-convolutional network (TCN) and prediction layer bidirectional long short term memory attention mechanism (BiLSTM-AM), and decoding layer TCN network. Firstly, physical domain features are extracted from industrial equipment component sensor signals, and light gradient boosting machine is used to select more important features for fusion. The feature data is trend-decomposed using the complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise to construct a performance degradation feature set. Degradation states and points are determined through reconstruction features, and degradation modes are classified using degradation speed. Secondly, different degradation mode feature data are input to the TCN for encoding and the BiLSTM-AM is trained on the hidden output. Finally, decode the prediction result to realize life prediction and feature data generation. The study uses bearings as an example and compares the proposed FGTC network with commonly used deep learning methods, with the experimental results confirming its superiority and feasibility.

articleTitle: Dynamic Behavior Simulation and Model Predictive Control of Wave Energy Converter
abstract: In order to easily evaluate the effectiveness of the control strategy and the performance of the power generation system in a wave energy generation system, a simulation method for simulating the dynamic behavior of a wave energy conversion device (WEC) is proposed in this paper. The electric motor is used to simulate the real movement of WEC under the action of sea waves. In order to maximize the output energy, model predictive control is used to optimize the electromagnetic torque of the generator. The simulation was carried out in MATLAB/Simulink, and the results showed the effectiveness of the proposed wave energy conversion device motion simulation method and MPC control strategy, which provided a theoretical basis for the subsequent WEC semi-physical simulation experiment platform.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Digitally Controlled Current Source Circuit
abstract: With the development of laser-based sensing and communication technology, the application of semiconductor lasers in industrial production and scientific and technological research is becoming increasingly widespread. The driving accuracy requirements of lasers are becoming increasingly high. However, the sensitivity of the laser output optical signal to current changes is relatively high, which leads to a high-precision demand for the laser driving current. A digitally controlled current source circuit is proposed in this paper. This circuit consists of a controller, DAC, and voltage-controlled current source circuit, used to drive Finisar's S7500 laser. Parameter model of this circuit, which provides theoretical basis and practical references for digitally controlled current source circuit, is established. The output current accuracy of the circuit reaches 10uA level, and the results of prototype experiment prove the correctness and practicability of the circuit.

articleTitle: Reachability-Based Trajectory Design for Robot Walking
abstract: A biped robot is a hybrid system and developing trajectory designers and controllers is a challenging task. Current methods like Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) can't guarantee the safety and efficiency at the same time. Here, safety means avoiding collision on obstacles and keeping states stable. Efficiency means being capable of real-time performance. In our work, we use a semi-passive Spring-loaded Inverted Pendulum (SLIP) as a hybrid system and implement Reach-ability-based Trajectory Design (RTD) on this system to ensure safety and efficiency. RTD consists of an offline computation step, which finds a robot's Forward-Reachable Set (FRS), and an online identify step, which identifies all correct trajectories. Mathematical properties are presented and main elements of the hybrid system are defined. Through numerical simulations, RTD is validated to ensure the control safety in high-density obstacles.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Integrated Inertial Navigation Based on ESN Model
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) systems fail to achieve navigation positioning in thoroughfares, viaducts, urban canyons, and tunnel environments, where the navigation signal is lost due to the particular navigation position. Inertial navigation systems, in turn, can fail to achieve satisfactory accuracy due to errors generated by the inertial measurement unit (IMU). Therefore, improving the accuracy of inertial navigation algorithms remains a challenge. They were reporting new research findings. In this paper, we develop deeply integrated inertial navigation algorithms to model and compensate for IMU errors, thereby improving the accuracy of IMU positioning. To achieve this, we have added a modeling step to the inertial navigation algorithm to learn the IMU error model during integration. First, the errors generated by the inertial navigation algorithm are trained using an Echo State Network. Second, the completed training network is depredicted. Moreover, third, the predictions are compensated into the inertial navigation results, thus integrating the inertial navigation algorithm, deep learning network, and error compensation. The results show that our deeply integrated inertial navigation algorithm can achieve much higher accuracy than inertial navigation algorithms.

articleTitle: A Cross-Domain Information Modeling Method for Health Management of Aircraft Hydraulic Systems
abstract: Facing the development trend of airborne system integration, intelligence, and networking, in order to improve the level of airborne system health management and information interconnection, and solve the problems of data standardization description and cross-system integration, a cross-domain information modeling method for health management of aircraft hydraulic systems is proposed. The standardized representation of hydraulic component information is designed, the type definition and constraint rules of typical components are described, and the information model of a typical mainline aircraft hydraulic system is established. A320 aircraft braking system as an example to build the information model for verification, through the software tool to build the information model and generate XML files, developed a server to load the information model and use client access to realize the information model read and write, to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the information model.

articleTitle: A Parallel Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Turning Movement Flow Prediction
abstract: Accurately predicting the turning movement flow at intersections is crucial for optimizing traffic fluidity. Existing traffic flow prediction models primarily focus on segment-level traffic, leaving a gap in the study of turning movement flow at intersections. The challenge in turning prediction lies in handling the nonlinear patterns of intersection turning movement while meeting real-time requirements. In this context, we propose a novel Parallel Hybrid Deep Learning Model (PHDLM) for accurately predicting turning movement flow at intersections. This model synergistically integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), attention mechanisms, Deep Neural Networks (DNN), and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU) to capture complex temporal patterns in traffic data. Through extensive experiments on the “Milton Turning Movement Flow Dataset,” we demonstrate that PHDLM outperforms established benchmarks in terms of accuracy, stability, and generalization capability.

articleTitle: CoT-YOLOv8: Improved YOLOv8 for Aerial images Small Target Detection
abstract: Detecting small targets in aerial images using unmanned aerial vehicles is an important research direction in the field of object detection and a highly challenging task. However, existing object detection methods often suffer from high miss rates and false alarm rates in the task of detecting targets in aerial images. To address this issue, we propose an algorithm called CoT - YOLOv8 to improve small target detection in aerial images. Firstly, we add an additional detection layer to the YOLOv8 algorithm to enhance the detection capability for small target objects. Secondly, we insert multiple Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) into the Backbone network to focus more on useful information, thereby improving the detection capability in complex scenes. Additionally, we replace the standard convolutional network in the Backbone network with a Dynamic Convolution Module (DCN), enabling the model to better adapt to geometric variations of the targets. Finally, we introduce the Contextual Transformer module into the Head network, allowing the model to utilize contextual information to assist in object detection and further improve the detection accuracy. The improved algorithm shows an increase of 7.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, 7.2 %, and 8.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> in precision (P), recall rate (R), and average precision (IOU-O.5) respectively. This indicates that the CoT - YOLOv8 algorithm has better generalization capability and higher detection accuracy compared to the original YOLOv8 in aerial small target scenarios.

articleTitle: H_infty Performance Analysis and Controller Design for Data-Driven Dynamic Event-Triggered Systems
abstract: This article is concerned with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{H}_{\infty}$</tex> performance analysis and controller design for the dynamic event-triggered systems through noisy input-state data. A novel dynamic event-triggered scheme is proposed. Based on a data-driven representation, a new data-based analysis method for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{H}_{\infty}$</tex> performance of the dynamic event-triggered system is introduced by using Lyapunov stability theorem, which relies on the noisy data rather than the model parameters. Beyond that, a data-based method for co-designing the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{H}_{\infty}$</tex> controller and the event-triggering matrix is provided, through which the controller gain matrix can be optimized. Finally, a numerical example is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Event-Triggered Control of Markov Jump Systems Under Hybrid Network Attacks
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of adaptive event-triggered control for Markov jump systems under hybrid network attacks, which include deception attack and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. An adaptive-event-triggered scheme is adopted to alleviate the pressure of limited bandwidth. Under the proposed adaptive event-triggered control, a mode-dependent controller is designed for the stability of the networked Markov jump systems under hybrid network attacks. Additionally, sufficient conditions are formulated to guarantee exponential mean-square stability (EMSS) of the system. Finally, a numerical example is presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: An Underwater Bionic Palm-Like Tactile Sensor Based on Triboelectric Nanogenerator
abstract: In an environment with poor ocean light or severe noise disturbance, there are still marine organisms can rely on the sense of touch to perceive their surroundings. This is a non-acoustic, and non-optical perception method. By contrast, the current autonomous underwater vehicles (AUV) has not fully developed similar capabilities to achieve this perception. So, we designed a selfpowered underwater palm-like tactile sensor (UPTS) based on the triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG), it can collect information about the target object through direct contact. The structure of UPTS includes a flexible cover, five sensor units based on triboelectric nanogenerator, flexible support and fixed frame. The biomimetic neural structure that generates electricity acts as a tactile receptor to provide sensory signals to realize tactile perception functions. The tactile sensor is capable of detecting the external load magnitude independent of the contact frequency's influence. Additionally, UPTS exhibits high sensitivity, strong real-time performance and fast feedback. The experimental results show that UPTS enriches the tactile perception system of the AUV, follow-up may help AUV to complete underwater tasks better.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Cooperative Guidance Law with Multi-Constraint
abstract: To enhance the destructive capabilities of small air-to-surface missiles, it is necessary to address the challenges related to terminal attack angle constraints and multi-missile coordinated attacks, we propose a cooperative guidance law with multi-constraint based on deep reinforcement learning in this paper. Firstly, an intelligent control term is introduced into the biased proportional navigation law with angle constraints. Secondly, a reward function is designed to reduce terminal attack angle error and flight time error, ensuring that the missile successfully reaches the target within the expected flight time, while simultaneously converging the attack angle to the desired value. Finally, the deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is employed for the purpose of training and generating intelligent guidance instructions. Simulation results substantiate the efficacy of the devised guidance method in achieving accurate target strikes, both for individual missiles and in scenarios involving multiple missiles. And exhibiting better stability and guidance accuracy compared to the traditional biased proportional navigation law.

articleTitle: Image-Based Crystal Size Analysis for β- form L-Glutamic Acid Crystallization Via Deep Learning-Based Object Detection
abstract: For evaluating the quality properties of p-form L-glutamic acid (LGA) crystals during a crystallization process, an image analysis method with deep learning-based object detection is proposed to acquire the crystal classification and size measurement, based on the optimization of in-situ image quality. Firstly, the homomorphic filtering is adopted to enhance the contrast of snapshotted images and highlight the image contours of crystals. Secondly, the crystal images are classified according to the degree of blur, and meanwhile, YOLOv6 is utilized for model training to obtain the position of individual crystals in a snapshotted image. Thirdly, the size of non-adhesive crystal image with clearness is calculated by a boundary fitting algorithm to improve the measurement accuracy. The effectiveness of the proposed image analysis method is verified by numerical simulation and experiments on the β-form LGA crystallization process.

articleTitle: Spiking Cerebellar Network Model: Effects of Long-Term Synaptic Plasticity and its Application in Brain-Inspired Control
abstract: Brain-inspired computing is a novel computing paradigm to realize the advanced artificial intelligence which is inspired by the working mechanism of human brain. As an important part of human brain, the cerebellum plays an important role in motor control and motor learning, which can help us explore more intelligent robot control methods. The motor control function of cerebellum depends on the mechanism of long-term synaptic plasticity. This paper focuses on the dynamic effects of long-term synaptic plasticity on cerebellar networks. The synaptic plasticity in cerebellum exists in three groups of cell junctions, which are from granule cells to purkinje (PKJ) cells, from mossy fiber to deep cerebellar nuclei, and from PKJ to deep cerebellar nuclei. Based on this physiological observation, we investigate the effects of these three mechanisms of synaptic plasticity on the firing rate of PKJ cells. Furthermore, we study the effects of three mechanisms of synaptic plasticity on brain-inspired control performance by adjusting the ratio of long-term potentiation (LTP) to long-term depression (LTD). The results show that PKJ neurons will have higher firing rates when the ratio of LTP to LTD is higher. When the synaptic plasticity mechanism of LTP plays a dominant role in control process, it will produce better control performance in brain-inspired control process. This research can be applied to intelligent robots, unmanned systems, edge computing of Internet of Things and brain-computer interface.

articleTitle: Day-ahead two-stage optimal scheduling strategy of distribution network based on WSO
abstract: In the context of Low-carbon economy, a two-stage optimal dispatching strategy for distribution networks has been proposed to solve the problems such as increased network loss and node voltage deviation caused by the access of distributed generation to distribution networks. In the first stage, the comprehensive cost of power grid operation and the economic benefits of Carbon emission trading are comprehensively considered, and a dispatching model with the goal of economy and environmental protection is established. Then, the output size and purchasing power of each distributed power source are obtained by solving. Based on the results of the first stage, a reactive power optimization model is established with the objective function of minimizing network loss and voltage deviation. The White Shark Optimizer (WSO) algorithm is adopted to obtain the global optimal solution. The simulation was conducted on an IEEE33 node system. The test results of the example show that the proposed scheduling strategy can optimize the distribution of distributed power output, effectively reduce the total operating cost and active power loss of the distribution network, and improve the voltage level of each node. At the same time, it can also verify the superiority of WSO in solving complex scheduling problems such as reactive power optimization.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Long Short-Term Memory Modeling Under Dynamic Partial Least Squares Framework
abstract: To solve the problem that traditional feedforward neural networks (FNN s) lack of early information processing when identifying complex long-term dynamic processes, a model predictive control (MPC) method based on long short-term memory (LSTM) modeling under dynamic partial least squares (DPLS) framework was proposed. Firstly, the process input and output data of the control model are obtained, and the dynamic PLS framework is established by using the obtained data. Secondly, LSTM is used to establish the internal model in the latent variable space to obtain the accurate prediction model. Furthermore, MPC controller based on DPLS framework is designed, and fuzzy neural network model predictive control method is used to optimize the control quantity of each latent variable loop. Finally, the PH neutralization and titration process is used for experiments. The results show that the MPC model modeled by LSTM under DPLS framework has good control performance.

articleTitle: Adversarial Training Classifier for Imbalanced and Semi-Supervised Learning
abstract: The imbalanced learning research has made great progress due to the introduction of generative adversarial networks (GANs). However, most studies focus on combining GAN models with oversampling techniques which could potentially compromise the distribution of the original training dataset. This study presents a cost-sensitive classifier based on the adversarial training framework that can not only deal with imbalanced data distribution but also utilize the unlabeled sample sets for semi-supervised learning. Extensive experiments are carried out to compare the classification performance on imbalanced datasets with the resampling and balanced ensemble method, as well as class-imbalanced semi-supervised scenarios, to demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Semi-global cooperation of discrete-time multi-agent systems with saturated input and aperiodic intermittent control
abstract: In order to improve the process of accurate discretization for continuous physical system in real-world scene and reduce more communication burden between agents, this paper investigates the semi-global containment problem of discrete-time linear multi-agent systems with aperiodic intermittent communication. The saturated control protocol is proposed by using low-gain approach and discrete-time algebra Riccati equation. By the convergence analysis, some sufficient conditions are obtained, for that all the followers beginning from a bounded initial set can asymptotically enter into the convex hull spanned by the leaders. Intermittent semi-global leader-following consensus and containment control result are given. Finally, two numerical simulations are presented to reflect the validation of our research findings.

articleTitle: Deterioration Trend Prediction of Spalling Damage for Heavy-Haul Railway Based on PCA and TCN-Attention
abstract: This paper proposes a new prediction method for damages such as spalling and wear of heavy haul railways caused and deteriorated easily by the continuous rail-wheel contact during the high intensity and heavy load transportation. Based on the combined model of PCA and TCN-Attention, it is capable of accurately predicting the deterioration trend of spalling damage for heavy haul railways. Firstly, a feature set with high dimension is constructed with the features of time domain and frequency domain extracted from the original vibration signal of rail damage. Secondly, PCA is used to reduce the dimension of the high-dimensional feature set of rail damages. The first principal component is used as the health indicator of rail damages. Further, the TCN-Attention model is adopted to predict the deterioration trend of the rail spalling damage. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified by using the vibration data of the life cycle of a rail track, from normal working to damaged to failure, collected from a railway depot. The results of the proposed method are also compared with those of prediction models constructed by TCN, LSTM and GRU networks. The comparison shows that the proposed method has better performance and higher prediction accuracy. The proposed method can more accurately predict the deterioration trend of the rail spalling damage.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Active Distribution Network Based on Enhanced Honey Badger Optimization Algorithm
abstract: In today's distribution networks, there is an increasing proportion of power electronic devices and a large-scale integration of new energy generation, which has led to the emergence of the “double high” problem and transformed the distribution network into an active distribution network. The distribution network faces challenges such as the growing demand for load and the integration of renewable energy sources. In order to improve the reliability of the distribution network, reduce transmission losses, and promote the utilization of renewable energy, this paper introduces distributed generation (DG) and static compensator (SC) considering droop control strategy, and optimally configures them. Furthermore, the enhanced honey badger algorithm (EHBA) is applied for the first time in the simulation experiment using the IEEE 33 standard test system. The simulation results demonstrate that the DG units in the distribution network can operate stably and participate in power system regulation through the droop control strategy, thereby enhancing the system's reliability and flexibility.

articleTitle: An Improved Lightweight Yolov5 Algorithm for Strawberry Ripeness Detection
abstract: Strawberry ripeness detection is of great significance for evaluating fruit growth in strawberry orchards. However, the existing detection technology has challenges in mobile terminal deployment due to the large computing amount and large model size. Therefore, an improved lightweight Y010v5 algorithm for strawberry ripeness detection was proposed in this study. To reduces the calculated amount and model scale, Partial Convolution (PConv) is introduced to substitute the normal convolution, which is in the original C3(Cross Stage Partial Bottleneck with 3 convolutions.), and C3_Faster module is introduced to substitute the C3 module in yolov5. SIoU is used as the boundary box loss function to accelerate the regression prediction and improve the positioning accuracy of the object bounding box. Experiments on jetson nano on public dataset show that compared with the previous Y010v5 model, the mAP of the modified model is increased by 1.1%, FLOPs and params are decreased by 17.1% and 17.6%, respectively.

articleTitle: Shallow Binary Features Enhance the Robustness of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: It is known that small noise can mislead the deep convolutional neural networks and have them make misclassifications. The researchers have poured much effort to study the effective and efficient approaches to enhance the robustness of deep networks, among which, adversarial training is a popular one. However, adversarial training is time-consuming and resource-consuming properties, which limit its applicability. It is natural to ask: can we enhance the robustness of deep models without adversarial training? In this paper, motivated by the binary edge features of clean examples and adversarial examples, we propose a binary feature branch module (BFBM for short) for deep convolutional networks. This module consists two kinds of layers, one is called Sobel layer, and the other is called threshold layer. The effect of Sobel layer is to learn four parallel edge feature maps using horizontal edge detector, vertical edge detector, positive edge detector, and negative edge detector, respectively. The goal of threshold layer is to convert the edge features to the binary features. After finishing this, the binary features along with the conventional texture features are taken as the inputs for the fully connected layers to output logits. The module is lightweight, and can work with any existing backbone. The experiments on CIFAR-10 and MNIST show that the BFBM-VGG16 model and BFBM-ResNet34 model can achieve averagely 35% higher accuracy than the original ones under FGSM and PGD attacks.

articleTitle: Secure Formation Control for Unmanned Surface Vehicles Against False Data Injection Attacks
abstract: This paper studies the attack detection and controller design problem of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) formation control against false data injection attacks (FDIAs). A novel topology switching strategy based on attack detection result is proposed to ensure the stability of vehicles which are not attacked, while the attack-detection-based formation controller is designed to ensure the stability of USVs under FDIAs. Finally, the simulation example is introduced to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy and controller in preventing negative impact of the FDIAs on the USVs system.

articleTitle: An Accelerated Safety Probability Estimation Method for Control Policies of Autonomous Vehicles in Open Environments
abstract: One of the critical bottlenecks that influence the development and deployment of autonomous vehicles (AV) is the safety assessment for raised control policies, especially in the situation of taking sensing noise into account. Safety probability estimation is one of the useful tools to describe the performance of control policies. However, these evaluation metrics always require amounts of tests to obtain, especially in open environments, which brings high time costs, no matter with actual vehicles or high-fidelity models. This article proposes an accelerated safety probability estimation method based on multi-fidelity models and a scenario classification method. Our method can accelerate the safety probability estimation process and has a small error. In our test of a desert road scene, our method used 1/750 of the time of the Airsim with Unreal Engine 4 (UE4), and get less than 5% error in most cases.

articleTitle: PV Constant Voltage Control Strategy Based on Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control
abstract: The control strategy of photovoltaic (PV) system in DC Microgrid affects the overall microgrid stability performance. When there is excess power in the microgrid, the power generated by the PV system needs to be reduced and the PV system needs to be switched to the power-limited operation mode. At present, the commonly used power-limited operating mode is constant voltage (CV) control, about CV control is mainly based on PI controller, but PI control stability is poor, there are obvious overshoot and oscillation. This paper thus proposes the super-twisting sliding mode (STSMC) CV control algorithm, which is able to control the PV system stably. The PV CV control of STSMC is simulated on Matlab/Simulink software, and the simulation results are basically free of overshoot and oscillation, which verifies the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Research on Automated Testing Technology of Ground Test and Launch Control System Based on Configuration Files
abstract: In response to the requirements of short development cycle, high quality and automated testing of aerospace software, combined with the design concepts of high cohesion, low coupling, and reuse of software, an automated testing method based on configuration files was designed for ground test and launch control systems. By studying the business model of the test and launch control system and modularizing the test and launch control function, abstracting reusable modules such as human-computer interaction, data communication, flow driver, data interpretation, and log recording, independent modules are combined into a test and launch control software system with automated testing through the process driving module. Each module reads and parses its own configuration file to carry out business work, which improves system automated testing, reduces software design complexity, improves software reuse, and reduces software development and maintenance costs.

Author Keywords: ground test and launch control system

articleTitle: Multi-loop Adaptive Load Relief Control Technology for Launch Vehicle
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the shear wind interference makes the aerodynamic load larger when the new generation launch vehicle passes through the windy area, a multi-loop self-adaptive active load relief control method is proposed. Based on the overload feedback load relief method, the observer compensation loop is introduced, and the influence of the multi-loop joint load relief control method on the aerodynamic load and the control load is derived. An adaptive gain real-time scheduling algorithm based on aerodynamic estimation is designed. The simulation evaluation results show that the multi-loop adaptive load relief control method has better adaptability to shear wind interference than the overload feedback load relief control method, which can further improve the load relief ability.

articleTitle: A Novel Domain Adversarial Framework for Improving Cross-Subject Motor Imagery Classification
abstract: Motor imagery classification plays a crucial role in brain-computer interfaces by decoding electroencephalogram (EEG) signals associated with motor imagery and enabling control of external devices. Existing methods often face challenges in generalizing to new subjects due to variations in brain activity patterns. To address this issue, we propose a novel multi-domain adversarial framework that learns task-related representations while being unrelated of subject differences. Our framework incorporates multiple domain adversarial discriminators and introduces a unique adversarial training strategy to align feature distributions across subjects, thereby optimizing classification objectives. Through extensive cross-subject experiments on the widely used BCI Competition IV-2a dataset, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving an average improvement in classification accuracy. These findings indicate the potential of our framework to advance motor imagery classification, benefiting areas such as human-computer interaction, automatic control, and medical sports rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Economic Optimization Scheduling of Distribution Networks - Microgrids Considering Power Interaction between Microgrids
abstract: In order to improve the economy of microgrid group operation and increase the scheduling space of microgrids, a two-stage optimal scheduling model considering the power interaction behavior among microgrids is established. In the first stage, the power purchase and sale tariffs from the distribution grid to the microgrid are simulated based on the forecast data; in the second stage, the microgrids are optimally dispatched based on the tariffs passed over in the first stage with the goal of maximizing the revenue of the microgrid cluster, and the optimal scheduling process takes into account the inter-microgrid power interaction behavior. The model is simulated and analyzed on MATLAB platform. The results show that the proposed model not only improves the revenue of the microgrid cluster, but also improves the robustness and independence of the microgrid cluster.

articleTitle: Dynamic Residual Attention UNet for Precipitation Nowcasting Based on WGAN
abstract: In recent years, using radar echo maps for precipitation nowcasting has been a research hotspot. How to use deep learning methods to forecast precipitation is a challenge. Radar echo map contains rich temporal and spatial information, capturing the location distribution and intensity characteristics of radar echo is a key problem in precipitation prediction. To tackle these challenges, the paper presents a novel approach called the Dynamic Residual Attention UNet model(DRA-UNet). This model incorporates Decoupled Dynamic Filter(DDF) and Dynamic Residual Attention Modules(DRAM) while leveraging the Wasserstein GAN training strategy to perform generative adversarial training. A decoupled Dynamic Filter can adaptively adjust the convolution kernel in the feature extraction stage, effectively reducing blank areas in the feature maps. By exploring the correlation between residual paths and input image statistics, and appropriately weighting each residual path, the model's focus on precipitation positions is enhanced. Moreover, the utilization of the Wasserstein GAN(WGAN) strategy during model training enhances the image generation quality when facing the discriminator in adversarial training. This advancement ensures that the model's outputs closely approximate real results, leading to further improvements in overall model performance. We comprehensively evaluate the performance of our model on the KNMI dataset, and a large number of experimental results show that our method achieves remarkable results on the precipitation prediction task.

articleTitle: Feedback Control of Double-VSC DFIG by Sliding Mode
abstract: In order to improve the robustness of feedback linearization control scheme to parameter change in maximum wind energy extraction control, feedback decoupling combined sliding mode control is proposed for maximum power point tracking control of double-VSC DFIG system. The addition of sliding mode control negates the disadvantage of feedback linearization. Simulation results show that compared with the PI control based on feedback linearization, the proposed control scheme has stronger robustness.

articleTitle: Text Recognition for Station Equipment Troubleshooting Based on BERT-BiLSTM-CRF Models
abstract: The excessive length and high semantic complexity of station equipment fault handling report texts are addressed to the extent that effective text recognition is difficult to achieve. A station equipment fault handling dataset is formulated and a text recognition system for station fault reports based on the BERT-BiLSTM-CRF model is designed. The method first preprocesses the data using the BERT pre-trained language model to generate word vectors, which are then fed into BiLSTM to obtain the embedded contextual information, which is passed through the CRF model to obtain the global optimal solution, and finally outputs the textual results of the station equipment fault handling. The experimental results show that the model outperforms the other five comparative models by more than 2% in terms of precision, recall, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> value (checking accuracy) for intelligent recognition over the five entities predicted by the other five comparative models. This brings a new direction of thinking for the analysis of equipment troubleshooting texts in railway stations.

articleTitle: Study on Optimization of Vehicle Routing Problem by Improved Ant Colony Algorithm
abstract: This paper mainly studies the vehicle routing problem with path constraints, time window constraints and capacity constraints through the improvement of ant colony optimization algorithm to optimize the route of delivery vehicles to achieve the minimization of the total cost of the delivery route. The improvement is mainly carried out from three aspects: first, the insertion operation between nodes and paths is designed to avoid customer omission in the process of ant colony traveling and reduce the probability of generating infeasible solutions; second, the insertion operation between road sections is used instead of the traditional simple merger guides the search to minimize the cost of the route. Finally, the convergence speed of ant colony optimization is accelerated by rewarding only the pheromone of the route constructed by the global optimal solution obtained so far. Through two groups of experiments with the best known solution and the existing research results, the efficiency of the improved scheme in optimizing the vehicle routing problem with constraints is verified.

articleTitle: Internal Stability of One-Degree-of-Freedom and Two-Degree-of- Freedom Linear Time-Invariant Structural Vibration Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the internal stability of one-degree-of-freedom (l-DOF) and two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) linear time-invariant structural vibration systems. Five types of vibration systems are involved - systems with both boundaries fixed, systems with one boundary fixed, systems with no fixed boundary but the displacement of one boundary is restricted, systems with one boundary fixed and the other restricted, and systems with both boundaries restricted. The results give the necessary and sufficient conditions for the systems to be internally stable and can provide great convenience when one evaluates the internal stability of a vibration system.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Low-Light Image Enhancement Method Based on Generating Saturation-Corrected Reference Images
abstract: A two-step low-light image enhancement method is proposed to solve the problems of inadequate illumination enhancement and color information distortion of existing low-light images during illumination enhancement, and to achieve a well-lit, clear and color-informative finishing result. Saturation correction is used to correct the saturation component of the HSV color space. To obtain better photographs, we integrate the channel v with the modified channel V and the channel S. with the correctedly image serving as a reference image. According to the qualitative and quantitative test results, image can show better.

articleTitle: Thermoelectric coupling modeling of lithium-ion batteries operating under low-temperature domain
abstract: Accurate thermoelectric coupling model is essential to help to realize safe and reliable thermal management of lithium-ion batteries. In order to accurately estimate the temperature variation of lithiumion batteries operating under low-temperature domain, a lumped thermoelectric coupling model is established, which uses a second-order RC equivalent circuit model as the electrical model and a lumped mass model as the thermal model. By designing a hybrid pulse condition, the parameters of the electrical model are identified for different temperatures, C-rates, and SOCs. For the thermal parameters, the entropy heat coefficients at different temperatures and SOCs are identified using the potentiometric method, and a genetic algorithm is used to determine the specific heat capacity and convective heat transfer coefficient of the battery. To validate the efficacy of the proposed model, various pulse experiments are conducted under temperatures and C-rates. The maximum error in temperature is about 0.42°C for the 10C pulse condition at 0°C and 0.45°C for the 5C pulse condition at -20°C. Under the extreme low-temperature condition, i.e., at -40°C with 1C pulse rate, the average error obtained by the simulation is relatively only 1.59% when the temperature rise changes by only 1.2°C. These results fully demonstrate the accuracy and reliability of the modeling.

articleTitle: Parameter-Optimized Load Frequency Active Disturbance Rejection Control of Power System Based on Sine Cosine Algorithm
abstract: Load Frequency Control (LFC) is important to guarantee the stable, safe and continuous operation of power systems. In this paper, A parameter optimized load frequency active disturbance rejection control strategy is proposed. First, a two-area interconnected power system, which consists of thermal, hydro, and gas power generation units is established. Second, the Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Controller (LADRC) is used for the LFC task. Third, The Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA) is utilized to adaptively adjust parameters of the LADRC controllers. The performance of the proposed method has been evaluated using the integral of time multiplied absolute error (ITAE) cost function. Finally, a comparative experiment and analysis is carried out. The robustness of the proposed strategy is evaluated by adding the random load disturbances. Experiment results validate the superiority and effectiveness of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: integral of time multiplied absolute error

articleTitle: Mobile Robot Global Localization Using Unique Objects in Indoor Scenes
abstract: Localization or pose estimation is a fundamental capability for an autonomous mobile robot, especially in navigation tasks. With a known occupancy grid map, wheel encoder data, laser LiDAR data, and a particle filter localization framework, the mobile robot can localize itself in most indoor scenarios. However, the mobile robot will fail to localize when the environment has similar areas or few geometric structural features. To solve the problem, we propose to use an RGB-D camera to detect the unique object in each sub-region as a reference which is useful for assisting the localization task. The semantic object information will be associated with the grid map coordinate in the mapping stage. In the localization phase, the mobile robot moves to a suitable area to detect the unique object, then completes the global localization task based on the known object pose. The conducted experiment shows that the proposed method is effective while traditional laser-based particle filter always fails.

articleTitle: ML-SPNet: Real-Time Semantic Segmentation Network Based on Multi-Level Serial-Parallel Structure
abstract: Real-time semantic segmentation networks suffer from insufficient semantic information extraction, inadequate fusion of information from different branches, and high computational complexity, leading to a decline in segmentation accuracy and slow processing speed. To address these challenges, this paper proposes ML-SPNet, which leverages multi-level serial-parallel architecture to effectively extract contextual information at different scales and enhance the network's understanding of semantic features. Firstly, proposing a lightweight Adaptive Channel Enhancement Module (ACEM), which enhances the representation cap-ability and performance of deep learning models for image semantic information through channel weighting and multi-scale information fusion. Next, introducing the parallel connected channel attention and spatial attention module (P-CSAM) and utilizing channel compression techniques to enhance the network's perception of details and edges while reducing computational costs. Finally, the feature maps from parallel branches are fused in a serial manner to obtain feature outputs with abundant semantic information. Experimental results on the Cityscapes validation dataset demonstrate that ML-SPNet achieves 76.1%mIoU/ 177.3 FPS, exhibiting excellent segmentation accuracy and high processing efficiency. The study validates that the proposed model effectively balances accuracy and real-time performance in the context of autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Study on the Aging Service Performance of Fluorine Ether Rubber Sealing Rings for Aircraft Engines Considering Combined Operating Conditions
abstract: The failure mechanism and influencing factors were first analyzed in response to the aging problem of fluoroether rubber sealing rings used in high-performance aircraft engines under vibration, high temperature, pre-compression force, etc. Secondly, the performance characterization parameters were studied from various aspects such as rheological performance, medium resistance, heat resistance, cold resistance, and weather aging resistance. Performance degradation tests were designed considering combined operating conditions. Based on experimental data, the performance degradation law of fluoroether rubber sealing rings was analyzed. According to experimental data analysis, fluoroether rubber can meet the sealing performance requirements of aircraft engines under combined operating conditions, and compression set deformation can be used to characterize its aging performance degradation.

articleTitle: A Three-Step Approach for Influence Maximization in Social Networks
abstract: Scale-free property shows that complex networks tend to have a set of most influential key nodes. Influence maximization (IM) is a problem of identifying a set of most influential key nodes within a given network propagation model. However, most of the traditional IM algorithms cannot well balance the propagation range and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a three-step approach integrating the greedy, community detection and K-shell decomposition in order to solve the IM. The experimental results indicate that the proposed three-step approach is close to the greedy algorithm and better than several centrality-based approaches including degree, closeness, and the K-shell in terms of the propagation range, but runs several orders of magnitude faster than the greedy.

articleTitle: A Repetitive Motion Obstacle Avoidance Planning Scheme for Omnidirectional Mobile Manipulators with Noise Suppression Capability
abstract: Obstacle avoidance is essential for an omnidirectional mobile robotic arm (OMRA) to accomplish a given task in a complex environment. To make OMRA accomplish repetitive motion, obstacle avoidance, and trajectory tracking tasks in complex dynamic environments with the presence of obstacles and external disturbances, a new noise-suppressed repetitive motion obstacle avoidance (NSRMOA) scheme is proposed. As established previously many OMRA motion planning assumes that the simulation is noise free. However, noise interference may prevent OMRA from accomplishing repetitive motion, obstacle avoidance, and trajectory tracking tasks, which may lead to task failure. The proposed the NSRMOA scheme with intrinsic noise suppression can solve external noise interference, so that the OMRA can accomplish the repetitive motion, obstacle avoidance and trajectory tracking tasks in the presence of external noise interference. Finally, the optimal solution of the NSRMOA scheme can be effectively obtained by using recurrent neural network (RNN). The effectiveness and accuracy of the scheme are verified by examples and comparisons.

articleTitle: Vibration Control Method of Single Crystal Diamond Tool Grinding Based on FNN-IMC
abstract: In the grinding process of single crystal diamond tool, the tool vibration will directly affect the quality of the tool. Aiming at the vibration of the tool in the grinding process of single crystal diamond, this paper proposes a control method combining internal model ( IMC ) and fuzzy neural network ( FNN ) to control the vibration of the tool. By controlling the grinding load applied by the tool to the grinding disc, the quality of the tool is improved. The simulation and experimental results show that the control performance of this method is better than the traditional PID and internal model control methods. It has good dynamic performance of set value following and interference suppression, which can meet the actual needs of on-line control of tool vibration, improve the sharpness of the tool and reduce the surface roughness of the tool.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Feature Extraction and Autoregressive Prediction Based Wi-Fi Indoor Fingerprint Localization
abstract: Deep learning-based Wi-Fi fingerprint localization, which needs to receive signal strength (RSS) fingerprint for training, has been widely studied. Some inherent problems impact localization accuracy, such as device heterogeneity and effective feature extraction. Effective feature extraction and strict location estimation mechanisms can significantly improve the accuracy of localization. In this paper, we propose an indoor localization method based on multilevel feature extraction and autoregressive location estimation to further capture the intrinsic features of RSS (Received Signal Strength), and learn the approach of mapping fingerprint features to location information. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves higher localization accuracy compared with DNN and CNN-based fingerprint localization methods. In the multi-building scenario, the proposed method achieves higher localization accuracy than the compared baseline methods.

articleTitle: Object-Level Feature Memory and Aggregation for Live-Stream Video Object Detection
abstract: This paper proposes an object-level feature memory module that utilizes attention mechanisms to explore spatial and temporal contexts in videos. Compared to still-image object detectors, video object detectors consider features in the spatiotemporal dimensions, leading to higher accuracy. How-ever, previous video object detection methods often focused on memory and fusion at the feature map level when integrating features across different frames. These approaches not only introduce significant computational and memory burdens but also introduces considerable noise. To address these challenges, we introduce object-level feature memory, which not only retains features from previous frames but also reduces memory and computational overhead, resulting in a substantial improvement in the performance of video object detectors. The experiments conducted on the UA-DETRAC dataset validate the effectiveness of our approach in live-stream video object detection scenarios. Our method achieved 66.73% AP based on YOLOX-S, which is 4.0% more AP than the normal YOLOX-S. Our codes are released at https://github.com/Liyi4578/0FMA.

articleTitle: Towards Intelligent Manufacturing: An AI-Based Machine Vision Detection System
abstract: With the increasing maturity of deep learning, machine vision systems combined with AI deep learning algorithms is being widely applied. The AI-based intelligent detection system is to provide early warning to prevent defective products. Quality assurance testing could be carried out at early stages of the production, so as to avoid defective components going into the next process. Compared with manual inspections, AI-based machine vision detection brings higher efficiency and accuracy<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, and specific details and drawings of defective products can also be collected for analysis. The paper aims to propose an AI-based machine vision detection system, which may provide reference for intelligent quality testing in washing machine manufacturing.

articleTitle: Robust Stabilization of Nonlinear Delay System with Unknown Disturbance via Hamiltonian Method
abstract: Utilizing the Hamilton theorem, the paper give robust control results on nonlinear system with time delay under the disturbance observer. Firstly, a Hamiltonian isovalent form of primary equation is put forward and disturbance observer. Secondly, a robust stabilization result is given by dimension extension technique. In the end, several numerical simulations are applied to test the implement of robust stable controller on account of disturbance observer. A nonlinear system with time delay on unknown disturbances is studied in this paper.

articleTitle: Robust Predictive Pressure Control for the Wheel Cylinder with Switching Solenoid Valves
abstract: This paper presents a novel predictive control structure for the wheel cylinder with switching solenoid valves, which cancels the PWM generator module used in the classic PWM-based pressure regulator. On this basis, a robust predictive pressure controller with a finite control set is developed to handle the system's unmodeled dynamics, adjust the ON/OFF states of SSVs, and track the target pressure. Firstly, considering the limited ON/OFF states of the inlet valve and outlet valves, a new discrete mathematical model of the wheel cylinder hydraulic pressure regulation system with finite available control inputs is derived for controller synthesis. Then, a discrete time extended state observer is employed to estimate the lumped disturbance and the estimated result is used to calibrate the pressure prediction model. Finally, an extended state-observer-based predictive pressure control algorithm is designed to predict the future pressure, optimize the cost function, and directly obtain the optimal ON/OFF signals of switching solenoid valves. The joint simulation results based on MATLAB and AMESim verify the effectiveness of the newly proposed robust predictive pressure control strategy.

articleTitle: Robust and Efficient Indoor Crowd Visual SLAM Algorithm Based on RGBD
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping is an essential element of robot position perception and environmental reconstruction. However, many existing SLAM systems rely on the static environment assumption and have limited adaptability to dynamic crowd scenarios. This article suggests a dynamic SLAM approach that Visual odometry and keyframe improve-ments, respectively to enhance the efficiency and resilience of SLAM systems in dynamic crowds environments. Firstly, a crowd environment-based object detection module is proposed, mainly detecting moving people in the scene and performing dynamic segmentation. Secondly, an adaptive keypoint criterion is designed to achieve further dynamic point detection and improve camera pose. Finally, the pose estimation error is evaluated on TUM and Bonn dynamic datasets. Results show that, compared to ORB-SLAM2, the proposed method achieves the greatest improvement of up to 98.14% in the high dynamic sequence of the TUM dataset.
