The improvement on Bonn dynamic dataset is at least 95.05%. This suggests the suggested approach possesses strong accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: A Pose Association Method for Multi-Agent System Based on LiDAR Pointcloud Registration Algorithm
abstract: Pose association is an important problem in intelligent agents, especially in multi-agent systems, because the introduced supplementary pose information can help the localization algorithm and upper-layer modules to improve performances. This paper proposes a new method to build pose association with considerable accuracy and reliability into a multi-agent system. The proposed method utilizes LiDAR pointcloud registration to calculate the pose relationship and has good potential to be applied to most multi-agent systems as long as they are equipped with LiDAR. Modified on Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm, a stepwise registration strategy based on decreased thresholds called DT-ICP is proposed. It can significantly improve the performance of pointcloud registration. Furthermore, we design an additional confidence evaluation module to avoid counter-productive pose associations caused by unreliable registration. The method has been proven to perform well in both simulation test environments and real scenarios.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Fixed-Time Optimal Consensus for Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This paper develops a framework for solving the fixed-time optimal control problem of multi-agent systems (MASs) under dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM). To find the optimal control law, a critic-only adaptive dynamic programming (ADP) online learning algorithm is proposed to obtain the solution of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation within a fixed time. By the designed experience replay learning rule employing sufficiently rich recorded and current data, the critic weights are updated to approximate the value function and its gradient. The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems are adopted to verify the feasibility of the presented approach.

articleTitle: Bi-Level Iterative Optimization for Integrated Scheduling of Continuous Casting-Hot Rolling
abstract: The integrated scheduling for both continuous casting and hot rolling process (CC-HR) significantly affects productivity, product completion time and customer satisfaction of steel industry. Considering the parallel consistency with the actual production, the problem is formulated as a bi-level iterative optimization model in this study. The upper-level is a mixed-integer programming model with the objective function of minimizing the time difference between casting and rolling; the lower-level model is abstracted into a vehicle routing problem (VRP) with the objective function of minimizing the width, hardness and thickness jump penalty values for hot rolling batch planning (HRBP). In order to overcome the drawback that the optimization for the lower model is easy to fall into local optimality, a hybrid algorithm combining genetic algorithm (GA) with strong global search ability and improved variable neighborhood search (VNS) with strong local search ability is proposed in this study. Finally, the upper and lower models are iteratively solved to find the scheduling scheme with smaller time difference between casting and rolling while ensuring the optimality for each objective function. The experimental results demonstrate that the established bi-level iterative model and the proposed optimization algorithm are both effective, as well as having obvious advantages in reducing the slab off-line time compared with some common methods.

articleTitle: A Point Cloud Completion Method for Industrial Component Based on Multiple Encoders
abstract: In real-world scenarios, laser-scanned point clouds often suffer from missing data points due to occlusion and other factors, significantly impacting subsequent tasks. We propose a novel point cloud completion method based on self-attention mechanisms and multi-layer perceptrons to address this issue, building upon the PCN model. Our experimental evaluations on the PCN dataset demonstrate notable enhancements in the completion effectiveness and evaluation metrics compared to the baseline model. Additionally, focusing on the point cloud completion context for industrial components, we introduce an approach for constructing an industrial component point cloud dataset. This method leverages 3D mesh models to swiftly generate complete point clouds with uniform distribution and devoid of noise while simulating the incomplete point clouds obtained from real-world scanning scenarios. The final results fully exhibit the feasibility of this scheme, which is a strong candidate for future industrial component point cloud completion.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time/Preassigned-Time Synchronization of Multi-Layer Stochastic Complex Dynamic Networks with Intra-Layer Coupling Disturbance
abstract: This paper addresses the fixed-time and preassigned-time synchronization of multilayer stochastic complex dynamic networks with intra-layer coupling disturbances. In particular, the node number and topology of each layer can be varied to allow the model to stand for a vast amount of multilayer networks. Based on the Lyapunov stability theory, stochastic differential equations and their stability theory, non-chattering controllers are developed, and sufficient conditions for matrix inequalities are given to realize the fixed-time and preassigned-time synchronization. In addition, it is proved that the network under consideration can achieve synchronization in a pre-specified time, independent of the settling time of the fixed-time synchronization. Finally, the correctness of these theories is confirmed by the numerical simulation of a two-layer network.

articleTitle: Position Sensorless Algorithm for IPMSM Based on Extended Electromotive Force
abstract: A position sensorless algorithm based on extended electromotive force (EEMF) is proposed to address the issues of inconsistent models and complex switching algorithms in the traditional low speed and high speed position sensorless control of IPMSM. In the low speed range, signal injection is employed to enhance the amplitude of EEMF. Conversely, in the high speed range, the signal injection is halted, ensuring a sustained high signal to noise ratio for EEMF throughout the start up and medium to high speed ranges. A synchronous axis moving average filter is designed to effectively suppress harmonics in EEMF. Additionally, a position error fusion algorithm is proposed to avoid speed fluctuations caused by the switching of position error information. Simulation results demonstrate that the algorithm exhibits small position observation errors and speed fluctuations within the rated speed range, validating the feasibility of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Attentional Network for Point Cloud Processing
abstract: Multi-scale architectures have found extensive applications in convolutional neural networks, enabling the extraction of more powerful feature representations. However, point clouds are discrete sets of 3D spatial data composed of individual points, making it challenging to perform multi-scale feature extraction using different convolution kernels. In this paper, we propose a novel neural network module that addresses this issue and allows for the integration of multi-scale features in point clouds. To compensate for the inherent lack of topological information in point cloud data, the module adopts a dynamic graph construction approach to gather more point features. This module efficiently obtains multi-scale features without incurring additional overhead. Moreover, it leverages an attention-like mechanism to effectively fuse these features, resulting in a more comprehensive and accurate representation, overcoming the drawbacks of traditional point-wise MLP followed by pooling operations that may lose valuable information. Experimental results demonstrate that our network outperforms existing methods in point cloud classification tasks on common benchmark dataset, achieving higher classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Mechanical Fault Diagnosis Based on Multi-Scale IDCNN-LSTM
abstract: In order to solve the trouble of low fault diagnosis accuracy in complex industrial environment, where there are numerous types of mechanical equipment and complicated transmissions, and the performance variations brought on by malfunctions of various pieces of equipment, parts, and locations vary, in this paper, a novel approach for fault diagnosis is introduced, utilizing a combination of multi-scale one-dimensional convolutional neural network and long short-term memory neural network (MSIDCNN-LSTM). Firstly, based on a standard IDCNN network, from the original data, the process of extracting the fine data features is performed, and learned the features of the time series signals by multi-scale convolution layers and pooling layers. Secondly, the LSTM network explores the deep and refined features of the hidden time series are further extracted. Softmax is then used to achieve fault classification using the fully connected layer. The model has been verified, which has faster diagnostic classification effect and higher diagnostic accuracy, and the diagnostic accuracy can reach 98.32%, by comparing the proposed method with the experimental result of LSTM and IDCNN.

articleTitle: Indoor Localization System Based on WiFi RSSI using Wavelet-CNN Architecture
abstract: With the development of digitalization and informatization, the demand for location-based services has shown a significant growth trend. Indoor is the occasion where people stay the most, indoor localization based on WiFi RSSI is one of the most popular and efficient localization method. This paper proposed a WiFi indoor localization system, which combines convolutional neural network and wavelet transform. Specifically, we add wavelet transform to extract temporal features, and use one-dimensional convolutional neural network training fingerprint data to obtain localization result. In order to verify the effectiveness of the designed model, we set experiments on real fingerprint dataset. The experimental results show that the purpose system has great localization accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of PIES Considering Orderly Participation of EVs under Green Certificate-Step Carbon Trading Mechanisms
abstract: To reduce the economic cost and carbon emission of Park integrated energy system (PIES) and improve the consumption of renewable energy in the system, an optimal scheduling model of PIES considering the participation of electric vehicles (EVs) under the interaction mechanism of green certificate-step carbon trading is proposed. First, disordered EV charging is modeled based on Monte Carlo sampling, and this is used as the basis to establish an orderly EV charging model through time-sharing tariffs. Then, a PIES optimal dispatch model considering integrated demand response and EV participation is established, and a green certificate-step carbon trading interaction mechanism is introduced into the model to promote PIES carbon reduction and improve renewable energy consumption. Finally, the solver Cplex is invoked in MATLAB to solve the model with the objective function of minimizing the daily operating cost. The results of the algorithm show that the EV sequential charging synergistic green certificate-step carbon trading interaction mechanism can not only reduce the operating cost of the system, but also reduce the carbon emission of the system and increase the consumption of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and Analysis of Cable Climbing Robots Under Wind-Induced Cable Vibration
abstract: Wind is the leading cause of cable vibration, to enhance the adaptability of cable climbing robots in the cable vibration environment caused by different natural winds, this paper proposes a coupled wind-cable-robot dynamics modeling approach. Firstly, the effect of wind speed and direction on the amplitude and frequency of cable vibration is analyzed to establish a wind-cable coupled dynamics model. Then, this paper adopts a flying cable-climbing robot with a quadrotor drive mechanism consisting of four ducted-fans to provide climbing power as the research object to establish a flying robot-cable coupled dynamics model. Finally, the wind-cable-robot coupled dynamics model is developed based on the principle that the climbing of the flying robot triggers the forced vibration of the cable, and the vibration of the cable also has an effect on the climbing stability of the robot. The characteristics of the cable vibration under different wind speeds and the influence of the cable vibration on the climbing stability of the flying robots are analyzed through simulation.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization Configuration Method of Multiple Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
abstract: In order to meet the needs of electric vehicle charging station expansion planning under the “dual carbon” goal, renewable energy and electricity will be combined The com-bination of electric vehicle charging stations and the construction of integrated optical storage and charging stations have become the new development and research direction of electric vehicle charging stations in recent years. Photovoltaic power generation output and electric vehicle charging load are characterized by uncertainty and randomness. Based on the uncertainty modeling of both, this paper considers the lowest user charging cost as the objective function, and focuses on the optimization of the configuration of optical storage and charging integrated charging station to obtain better social and economic benefits.

Author Keywords: Integration of optical storage and charging

articleTitle: A Rulefit Based Model for Driving Intention Prediction at Intersections
abstract: Understanding the driving intentions of surrounding vehicles is crucial for safe decision-making and path planning in advanced driver assistance systems and automated vehicles. This paper presents a novel Rulefit-based model to predict driving intentions at intersections. The model comprises two parts. The first part contains three sub-tasks: judging whether the vehicle is more likely to turn left or go straight, turn right or go straight, and turn left or turn right with the Rulefit algorithm. Here, a rule set is introduced to fully use the experiences learned from the historical moments and increase the prediction accuracy. The second part uses hard voting to get the classification results. Simulations validate the model's performance using data in lankershim street from the NGSIM dataset. It shows that the proposed model is more accurate than typical model-based and neural-network-based methods on validation data when the distance between the vehicle and the intersection is less than 21 meters. Moreover, the proposed method can give the rules that play the most critical roles.

articleTitle: A Sensorless Force Estimation Algorithm for Robot Based on Model Compensation
abstract: Acquisition of external torque information is an important challenge for robot interaction with the environment. To avoid the high-cost problem associated with installing force sensors, a novel model-based sensorless interaction force estimation algorithm is proposed for accurate and fast estimation of interaction force and torque. To enhance the model's accuracy, the first step involves acquiring dynamics parameters through model identification, followed by conducting nonlinear friction compensation. Subsequently, an algorithm combining extended state observer (ESO) and generalized momentum is introduced to evaluate the system's interaction force and torque, which improves the rapidity and accuracy of the estimation. Ultimately, the proposed approach's efficacy was validated by conducting experiments on a six-degree-of-freedom robot as the primary testing platform.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning Algorithm of Manipulator in Small Space Based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The development of reinforcement learning has driven the progress of robot control technology. In recent years, reinforcement learning has become one of the highly concerned fields in the academic community, especially the control of robotic arms in the industrial field. In order to achieve intelligent and efficient production, the emphasis is on the research of obstacle avoidance motion planning of the manipulator. However, traditional trajectory planning algorithms have problems such as slow convergence speed, low intelligence, and difficulty in achieving optimization. In this regard, this research takes the six degrees of freedom manipulator PUMA550 as the research object, and focuses on the obstacle avoidance motion planning problem of the manipulator, studies the manipulator modeling based on the improved D-H parameter method, Rapidly-exploring Random Trees (RRT) algorithm, the Q-learning algorithm and the double Q network learning alzorithm.

articleTitle: High Resolution Remote Sensing Image Captioning Using Group Convolution and Attentional Mechanism
abstract: This paper proposes a remote sensing image description generation method based on group convolutional neural network and attention mechanism to address the problem of a single global feature extraction scale in the model for remote sensing image scene description generation. This method mainly applies grouping convolution modules to fuse the features of different network layers and global features at different scales in convolutional neural networks. To overcome the shortcomings of traditional convolutional neural networks in feature extraction, this paper proposes a remote sensing image description generation method based on the inverse bottleneck layer convolutional neural network and attention mechanism. This method significantly increases the global receptive field of convolutional neural networks by introducing inverse convolutional layers, grouped convolutions, and large-scale convolutional kernels. This method utilizes deep separable convolutional layers to further reduce network model parameters and model operations. The experimental results show that our method can generate more accurate text statements for describing remote sensing images.

articleTitle: Improved Sliding Mode Control of PMSM with Dead-Time Distortion Suppression
abstract: This study presents an improved super-twisting sliding mode (SSMC) control method for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) in a low-speed region. Considering the harmonics taken by dead-time of converters, a resonant-based extended state observer (RESO) based sliding mode control method is proposed to design the current regulator. Due to the salient features of RESO, the disturbances and harmonics are estimated. Then, the harmonics in current are suppressed and ripples in speed are eliminated simultaneously. The advantages of proposed method are that no extra harmonic extraction operations are required and the entire computational complexity is reduced. Finally, numerous simulation results are given to demonstrate the harmonic suppression performance of proposed approach.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of the Influence of Joule Heating on Single-Cell Electroporation Under 10Hz IRE Pulses
abstract: To study the influence of Joule heating caused by pulsed electric fields on cell electroporation, we constructed the spherical single-cell simulation models that included the EP model without Joule heating and EP+T model with Joule heating. Both models were subjected to continuous 8 irreversible electroporation pulses. By comparing the simulation results of the two models, we observed that in the EP+T model, Joule heating promoted cell electroporation, as evidenced by a faster transmembrane voltage at the anodic point on the cell membrane reaching the electroporation threshold (~1 V) and an increased peak pore density after accounting for Joule heating. In addition, the peak of transmembrane voltage in the EP+T model was higher during the first 7 pulses, indicating a possible increase in the probability of cell electroporation due to Joule heating. However, when the transmembrane voltage was lower than the threshold, there was little increase in the pore density in either model.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered Iterative Learning for Constrained UAV Attitude Control
abstract: This paper addresses the attitude control of quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with state constraints. We propose an event-triggered iterative learning control (ILC) scheme for quadrotor UAVs. The scheme effectively handles both parameter and non-parameter uncertainties in the UAV system through iterative learning laws. Additionally, an event-triggering mechanism is incorporated into the ILC design to reduce the update frequency of the final control signals, thereby reducing the signal transmission burden and control costs of the system. A barrier Lyapunov function is adopted to design the attitude control of the UAVs with state constraints. The convergence of the tracking error is analyzed using a constructed barrier composite energy function, ensuring that the prescribed constraints are not violated at each iteration. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed control scheme achieves accurate tracking performance and effectively alleviates the system burden, thereby verifying its effectiveness and feasibility.

articleTitle: Design of Proportional Integral Controller for a Class of Discrete Control System
abstract: This paper investigates the design of proportional integral (PI) controller for a class of discrete control system. By constructing new Lyapunov functions and Schur complementary derivatives, the parameters of single closed-loop PI controller for discrete control system are derived using LMI technology, where the controller used PI controller. The effectiveness of this method is verified through a simulation example of the primary temperature control system. The introduction of single closed-loop PI controller in discrete control system for the first time to regulate the stability performance of the system has important industrial production significance in practical industry.

articleTitle: Distributed Active Disturbance Rejection Control of Multiple Mobile Robots for Online Workload Partition
abstract: Considering the actual multi-agent coverage process, the motion trajectories are seriously affected by disturbances and noise. In this paper, a cooperative control method based on active disturbance rejection controller (ADRC) for multiple mecanum-wheeled robots (MWMR) is proposed to improve its robustness. In particular, to suppress the total disturbances during the running of each robot and reduce large computation and observation cost of high order ADRC, a reduced-order cascaded ADRC (RC-ADRC) is proposed. Moreover, distributed controller is proposed to track the expected trajectories of multiple mecanum-wheeled robots under disturbances. Compared with the proposed RC-ADRC based cooperative control scheme and PID based cooperative control one, the favorable motion trajectory tracking performance is obtained. Simulation results verify the superiority of the method.

articleTitle: Residual-Unet Generative Flow Model for Low-Light Image Enhancement
abstract: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) task based on deep learning learns the mapping from low-light image to normal exposure image by using supervised or unsupervised training. In the majority of current methods, the utilization of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) substantially constrains the network's capacity to assimilate comprehensive global information. Simultaneously, the reconstruction loss or adversarial loss commonly employed tends to inadequately gauge the visual disparity between predictions and targets, resulting in the emergence of blurred regions in the enhanced results. In this paper, we therefore propose a Residual-Unet Generative Flow Model for Low-light Image Enhancement (RUGF), which consist of a feature extraction module and a flow learning based reconstruction module. We first propose a residual-based Unet encoder during deep feature encoding in the feature extraction module, which can compensate for the shortcomings in global information processing and has advantages in processing depth information. In addition, our network adopts a negative logarithmic likelihood loss function, which can better constrain the model to learn the complex distribution of the reference image, thereby avoiding the local area blurring that exists in existing methods. We conducted extensive testing on two benchmark datasets, and the actual results confirmed the superiority and effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Prediction of State of Health Based on TCN-Attention Neural Network
abstract: A data-driven model based on Tem-poral Convolutional Network (TCN) is suggested to create the mapping link between battery charging curve and SOH in order to consistently and precisely predict the State of Health (SOH) of lithiumion batteries. Longer SOH data have their cross-time nonlinear characteristics extracted using TCN, and attention is added to highlight the significance of past temporal aspects in predicting SOH. The experimental findings demonstrate the high estimation accuracy and good battery type adaptation of the suggested TCN-based SOH estimation methodology.

articleTitle: Quality Evaluation Method of the DC Motor Based on VMD and MFCC
abstract: To address the challenges of inadequate feature extraction from acoustic signals and lower validness of machine learning methods, a DC motor quality evaluation method was proposed which combines Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC). Sound signals from DC motors of three classes are acquired and subjected to VMD decomposition, extracting Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). MFCC features are computed for each IMF. These features, along with time domain features, are combined into a feature matrix. Support Vector Machine (SVM) is then trained using the feature matrix for quality evaluation. From the experimental results, the following conclusion can be drawn: Compared to the MFCC-SVM model, the VMD-MFCC-SVM model exhibits an increase in classification accuracy from 90.2% to 97.9%. The method's validity and feasibility are confirmed through rigorous analysis of experimental data, providing a reliable approach for assessing DC motor quality based on acoustic signals.

articleTitle: The Influence of Flapping Hinge on Swashplatc-Less Rotor
abstract: We investigate the effect of the flapping hinge and its offset on the canted hinge swashplate-less rotor. By using helicopter rotor flapping analysis theory, we derive the kinematic and dynamic model of the swashplate-less rotor with flapping hinge. The theoretical calculation shows that adding the flapping hinge will increase the flapping range of blade, and its offset can provide additional hub torque to increase the maneuverability of UAVs. Finally, we conduct a test bench experiment to validate the results.

articleTitle: Design of Full-Mode Flight Control System for Tiltrotor Aircraft Based on Model Compensation Reduced-Order Active Disturbance Rejection Controller
abstract: In this paper, a flight control system based on a model compensation reduced-order active disturbance rejection controller (MCR-ADRC) is proposed for full-mode control of a tilt-rotor aircraft. Firstly, according to the characteristics of the conversion mode of the tilt-rotor, the manipulation allocation strategy and the control channel switching strategy are designed to lay the foundation for the subsequent design of the flight control system. Subsequently, MCR-ADRC is designed and compared with the conventional ADRC. Finally, the full-mode six degrees of freedom flight control system of the tilt-rotor is designed by using the MCR-ADRC, and the effectiveness of the designed flight control system is verified by simulation. The result indicates that the MCR-ADRC proposed in this paper has a better anti-disturbance effect than the canonical ADRC, and the flight control system could effectively complete the full-mode flight control of the tilt-rotor aircraft.

articleTitle: A Rigid Guide Rail Inspection Robot and Fault Detection Method for the Coal Mine Hoisting System
abstract: The coal mine hoisting system is responsible for the lifting and lowering tasks of underground workers, coal and equipment. As an important part of the hoisting system, the safety performance of rigid guide rail directly affects the safety of coal mine production. In order to solve the problem of low efficiency of manual inspection at present, this paper proposes a new rigid guide rail fault detection robot and detection method. First of all, based on our previous research, a new detection robot prototype is developed. Secondly, a method of detecting rail fault using robot attitude is proposed. Finally, the performance of the robot and the effectiveness of the detection method are verified by field experiments. At present, the robot proposed in this paper is the first robot tested onsite for fault detection of rigid guide rail of coal mine hoisting system. The detection robot system proposed in this paper can improve the intelligent and unmanned level of coal mines, and can also be extended to the detection of railway tracks and elevator guide rails in buildings.

articleTitle: Health Status Assessment of Aero-Engine Based on Multilayer Information Sharing and MOSE
abstract: As the heart of an aircraft, the complex structure of an aero-engine poses a considerable challenge for its maintenance. The traditional health status assessment includes two tasks of remaining useful life prediction and health status division, but this paper adds the study of reliability assessment of aero-engine operation process on its basis and proposes an aero-engine health status assessment method based on multilayer information sharing and MOSE. Firstly, a series of machine learning methods such as principal component analysis are used to preprocess the data, and a label construction method based on slope division is adopted. Secondly, the shared information in the sensor signal is extracted using the MOSE network module and the extracts task-specific information in the sensor signal is extracted by the BIGRU network module, and the weighted decision is realized by the gating network on the output of both, and the prediction output of each sub-task is performed by the sub-task module. Finally, experiments on the C-MPASS dataset show that the proposed method in this paper outperforms recent popular models.

articleTitle: Fixformer: Air Pollution Forecast in Fixed Time Interval without Sequence-to-Sequence Structure
abstract: The Transformer-based models have been successfully applied in time series forecasting tasks. However, most of these models retain the sequence-to-sequence structure, which is widely used in Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. In this paper, we aim to determine whether the sequence-to-sequence structure can be replaced. Thus, we designed the Fixformer model, which changes the sequence-to-sequence structure to an N-to-T structure. We applied this model to an air pollution forecasting task and selected the forecast time interval T using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis. The experimental results indicate that our Fixformer achieves an equivalent forecast accuracy to the Transformer, and the Fixformer requires less training time.

articleTitle: Analysis of Influence Factors of Model Predictive Control for Wave Energy Converters
abstract: Wave energy generation is an important renewable energy technology with great potential. In wave power generation systems, model predictive control is widely used to improve the efficiency and stability of the power converter system. The aim of this paper is to analyse the factors affecting the performance of the model predictive control of wave energy convetvers, and on this basis, to study in depth the optimisation of the model predictive control, which is of great significance to improve the control performance and power generation efficiency of wave energy converters.

articleTitle: Design of an Image Recognition Device for Electronic Water Meter Readings Based on Improved Threading Method
abstract: In view of the low success rate and efficiency of existing image recognition methods for electronic water meter readings, an image recognition method based on improved threading method has been developed, and the corresponding image recognition device has been designed. After segmentation, correction, and preprocessing of the water meter reading image, the improved threading method is used to accurately recognize the individual numerical characters segmented, which involves scanning from the midpoint of the upper boundary of the number from top to bottom, and then scanning from left to right from the 3/4 midpoint and 1/4 midpoint of the left boundary of the number. Based on the results of three scans, specific numbers are identified, and the cumulative flow indication of water meter is finally synthesized. This method only requires scanning 3 lines, greatly simplifying the image recognition algorithm, shortening the algorithm running time, and improving the quality of image recognition. After testing, the success rate of the image recognition device in recognizing seven segment LCD digits is higher than 99.9%.

articleTitle: Memory Mechanisms Based Few-Shot Continual Learning Railway Obstacle Detection
abstract: Efficient and accurate railway track obstacle detection is crucial for ensuring travel safety. In order to solve the problem of small amount of track obstacle data and variable types of obstacles, we introduce the concept of few-shot continual learning into the object detection algorithm. This paper introduces a novel memory mechanisms-based multi-Domain few-shot continual learning algorithm. By simulating working memory and long-term memory processes, our method combines few-shot learning with continual adaptation to varying obstacles. The proposed double-loop approach reduces catastrophic forgetting, enhances model generalization, and improves detection accuracy. This innovation holds promise for advancing railway safety through effective obstacle detection. The proposed method showcases remarkable efficiency and accuracy in the detection of railway obstacles. Our experimental results demonstrate significant improvements compared to other methods.

articleTitle: Robust Control for the Mixed Platoon with Polytopic Uncertainties, Delay and Packet Dropout
abstract: This paper proposes a controller for the mixed platoon with connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles (HDVs), which fully considers the functional differences between CAVs and HDVs. The delays and packet dropout of vehicles are also taken into account. To describe the uncertainties in vehicle parameters, a system with polytopic uncertainties is used to model the mixed platoon, and an adaptive robust gain-scheduling controller is designed to attenuate external disturbances. A sufficient condition is obtained so that the platoon system can be robust mean-square stable. Numerical simulation results confirm the validity of the proposed control scheme in stabilizing mixed platoon and suppressing disturbances.

articleTitle: Path Planning for Mobile Robot Based on Improved Artificial Potential Field Method
abstract: In this paper, an improved artificial potential field method is proposed to address the problems of excessive gravitational force, unachievable goal, and falling into concave obstacle regions in path planning for the mobile robot using the conventional artificial potential field method. Firstly, adding a dynamic adjustment coefficient to the gravitational field function of the conventional artificial potential field method to improve the problem of excessive gravitational force in the early stage, and adding the distance parameter to the repulsive field function to refrain from the goal unreachability problem resulted from the presence of obstacles near the goal point. Then, according to the distribution of obstacles, expanding the radius of influence of obstacles and setting a temporary goal point are used to realize the escape of the mobile robot in concave obstacle regions, respectively. Finally, the paths are optimized using B-spline. Simulation experiments are carried out for both the improved artificial potential field method and the conventional artificial potential field method. The results show that the improved artificial potential field method is smoother in path planning compared to the conventional artificial potential field method. It can effectively avoid the concave obstacle regions and complete the path planning.

articleTitle: Research on Ship Trajectory Tracking based on Nonsingular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control
abstract: To address the issues of chattering and slow convergence speed in traditional sliding mode control for underactuated ship trajectory tracking, this paper proposes a non-singular fast terminal sliding mode control method. Firstly, a virtual control law for lateral and longitudinal velocities is designed based on the lateral and longitudinal position errors of the ship. Then, an exponential reaching law is introduced to construct the non-singular fast terminal sliding mode controller, effectively solving the chattering problem in sliding mode control and improving the convergence speed of the system. Finally, the system's convergence within finite time is proved based on Lyapunov function and finite-time stability theory. Comparative simulation experiments demonstrate that the designed controller has good robustness and tracking performance, enabling the ship to quickly and accurately track the desired trajectory.

articleTitle: Anti-Disturbance Formation Control of Quadrotor UAVs Based on Terminal Sliding Mode Control
abstract: In this paper, the anti-disturbance formation flight control of quadrotor UAVs system is realized based on terminal sliding mode control. The generalized error state is designed for each quad-rotor UA V, based on which the formation control target is proposed. In order to achieve the goal of anti-disturbance formation control, a formation controller based on terminal sliding mode control is designed. Finally, the general error states of all quadrotor UAVs converge to zero to achieve the desired formation. Finally, a simulation example is given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: AM-GPD: Manipulator Grasping Pose Detector Based On Attention Mechanism In Dark Light Scene
abstract: To implement a competitive grasping pose detector in dark light scenes, an attention-based mechanism is proposed. The basic idea can be described as follows. First, the attention module is used to accurately identify the dark regions of the region of interest. By using an image brightness enhancement method, the brightness of the dark region is increased to the desired level. Subsequently, an efficient residual convolutional neural network model based on the attention mechanism is proposed to estimate the grasping pose of the target object in the visual field. An optimal object grasping pose is derived by using 640x480 RGB maps and depth maps as input to generate mass, angle and width maps. Simulations of the Cornell and Jacquard crawl datasets were performed in the dark light scene. The experimental results show that the detection accuracy of the proposed grasping pose model in this paper reaches 98 % and 92 %, respectively.

articleTitle: Fast Load Frequency Control for Power System Based on Fixed-Time Dynamic Surface Method
abstract: The inherent fluctuations of high penetrated renewables energy sources in power system results in larger and more sharp frequency deviation, which call for faster frequency response and fast load frequency control (LFC). This paper innovatively envisions LFC in power system with fixed-time dynamic surface method. Firstly, the virtual control law is designed through backstepping design to ensure the asymptotic stability of each subsystem. Additionally, dynamic surface control (DSC) is adopted to eliminate the influence by adding a first-order filter in the backstepping design. By using the fixed-time theory, the frequency of the LFC for power system reaches stability in a predetermined time. Finally, the simulation of the power system proves the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Unmanned Surface Vehicle Path Following Based on Model Predictive Control
abstract: To deal with the challenging problem of unmanned surface vehicle (USV) path following, a method based on model predictive control (MPC) is designed in this paper. An USV is a typical nonholonomic constrained and under-actuated system, and it has huge inertia while there is no effective brake system to control its drift. In order to follow a given path better, prediction based method should be used to take the future states into account. The kinetic model of USV has been established to simulate the prediction horizon while the inertia and hydrodynamic forces are considered. Numerical simulations are carried out and demonstrate that the controller can command the USV to follow a series of waypoints smoothly and accurately.

articleTitle: An Acceleration Inference Implementation of BEVFusion with MQBench on Xavier
abstract: The integration of sensor technology and deep learning has made multi-sensor fusion algorithms an essential component of autonomous driving perception. Among these algorithms, BEVFusion performs well in 3D perception tasks. However, its high computing cost presents challenges for deployment and application on the hardware. In this work, we propose a way that can trade off efficiency and performance to compress and deploy it on Jetson Xavier NX. We first decouple the model into three parts and then use MQBench to quantize the Fusion and Decoder of BEV in various ways. After that, we accelerate it on the hardware with the parameters of those schemes by utilizing TensorRt.By analyzing the mAP and inference time of the model in different quantization factors, we obtain the optimal schemes when using FP32 as scale, per-channel as granularity and EMAMinMax as calibration algorithm, whose accuracy only experiences a marginal drop of 0.12% while the execution speed witnesses a remarkable increase of 98.3% compared to the original model. The significant improvement makes the application of BEVFusion feasible for real-time autonomous driving perception.

articleTitle: Modeling of Throat Deposition Area of Solid Rocket Ramjet and Gas Flow Control
abstract: The slag produced during the operation of the burner of the solid rocket ramjet will deposit and fall off at the throat of the burner, resulting in a change in the effective throat area, thereby affecting the flow regulation accuracy. In this paper, the physical process of throat deposition and shedding is analyzed and modeled, and the equivalent deposition area of the throat is polynomially fitted with time as a variable, and a PID controller is designed to regulate the gas flow. The simulation results show that the designed controller can effectively suppress the drastic pressure change caused by the slag deposition and drop in the throat, which provides a reference for the controller design of the actual gas flow regulation system.

articleTitle: Fitness-Assisted Counting Based on Lightweight Pose Recognition Network and k-NN Classification
abstract: In this paper, propose a fitness assistance algorithm based on the combination of a lightweight network human posture detection model, BlazePose, and a k-NN classification algorithm for real-time counting on mobile devices. Firstly, the BlazePose model is used to predict the target pose on the given sample image, and the obtained Landmark is normalized to build the training set of the k-NN classifier. Then Pose Classification Colab classifies each sample by targeting the entire training set while excluding outliers and underrepresented categories. Finally, the implementation of the classifier itself can realize the real-time counting of fitness exercises. In this study, squats and push-ups, two of the most representative sports, are selected as the verification objects. The experimental results show that, with real-time and accuracy guaranteed This algorithm is capable of classifying and counting push-ups and squats at a rate of 30 frames on an ordinary mobile device.

articleTitle: Importance-Based DoS Attacks in Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: This work considers the security issue of the remote state estimation in a multi-process Cyber-physical system (CPS). Different from the existing works, we propose a novel Denial of Service (DoS) attack, which is called an importance-based DoS attack. The subsystem importance refers to the degree of the accuracy of the state estimation to the total decision-making for the system, and we employ the importance parameters to quantify that. These attacks are directed at the wireless communication channel between sensors and remote estimators. We employ the sum of terminal errors and the sum of average errors based on subsystem importance to quantify the impact of these attacks. We then investigate some scenarios and presented optimal attack strategies for specific scenarios. Finally, we provide numerical examples to illustrate our conclusions.

articleTitle: Counterfactual Negative Outcome Control for Required Navigation Performance
abstract: Output feedback control in flight relies on robust guidance commands. However, inevitable command deviations can result in excessive and adverse servo adjustments of the aircraft control surfaces. This paper presents a counterfactual negative outcome control (CNOC) method to restrain lateral and vertical errors for required navigation performance (RNP). Here the counterfactual responses are inferred to minimize the confounding effects between successive outcomes. Consequently, command and control with maximal causal effects between inputs and outputs can be applied to start or resume the appropriate aircraft servo actuators. Notably, conditioned flight control can reduce excessive and adverse servo actuation. Simulation results on guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) establish that the CNOC method permits a reduction in the loss probability of RNP capability on accuracy, integrity, and continuity.

articleTitle: PSO Based ADRC for Altitude Test Facility Intake Pressure Control
abstract: Significant disturbances are imposed on the altitude test facility pressure control system during the aeroengines' transition state tests, which degrades the control performance and subsequently reduces the accuracy and reliability of engine tests and evaluation. To tackle this problem, we propose the utilization of an active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) based controller. Additionally, we introduce a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to optimize and fine-tune the parameters of the ADRC controller for the simulation system of intake environmental pressure. Meanwhile, a component-level modeling approach is employed to establish a simulation platform for altitude test facility pressure, and proposed method is validated through experiments conducted on the platform. The results clearly indicate that the PSO-ADRC significantly improves the performance of pressure control.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Short Circuit Ratio Prediction Based on Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: The integration of renewable energy power significantly influences the voltage support strength of the power system. With the rapid increase in renewable energy generation capacity in recent years, the power system faces mounting pressure. The short circuit ratio (SCR), a key indicator of voltage support capability, plays a crucial role in the regulation of power systems. Therefore, we propose a renewable energy SCR Prediction model based on spiking neural networks (SNNs). Moreover, this model takes into consideration the correlation between wind power generation and SCR, enabling accurate multivariate prediction. The prediction results on real-world power system data from renewable energy wind farms in north-ern China demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed SNNs prediction model. And the SNNs model can be deployed on edge devices for low-power and efficient online prediction.

articleTitle: A Novel Two-Branch Convolutional Neural Network for EEG Decoding of Motor Imagery
abstract: In recent years, deep learning has been applied to the classification of motor imagery EEG, which can decode and classify EEG signals end-to-end. However, compared with picture datasets, EEG datasets are relative small and difficult to adapt to deeper networks. To solve this problem, we propose a shallow two-branch convolutional neural network (TBCNNet) to decode EEG information. More EEG information can be obtained by fusing the spatio-temporal features extracted from each single branch. Thus, the accuracy of EEG decoding can be improved without increasing the depth of the network. We tested this method on the BCI Competition IV-2a dataset, and the average decoding accuracy reached 86.59%, the average kappa value reached 0.82, and the average Fl-score reached 0.86. The results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the performance of motor imagery decoding.

articleTitle: Research of Position and Speed Detection Method Based on AD2S1210 for Permanent Magnet Motors
abstract: A method detecting position and speed based on AD2S1210 for permanent magnet motors is designed in this paper. The reluctance rotary transformer J37XU9732 is selected as the position and speed sensor, which need excitation signal provide by the decoding chip AD2S1210. And the feedback signal from rotary transformer should be decoded by the decoding chip. To achieve the above functions, the peripheral circuit of the decoding chip is designed. The Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) module of DSP28379 is used to visit AD2S1210 to obtain the binary code of the position and speed of the motor. The experimental results show that the design has good performance and can realize real-time monitoring of the position and speed of permanent magnet synchronous motor.

articleTitle: Research on Cock States Detection of Cock Oven Inspection Robot Based on YOLO-v3
abstract: The state switching of the coke oven gas pipeline exchange cock plays a vital role in the safe production of coking. This paper designs and manufactures a rail-type mobile robot applied to coke oven basement inspection tasks to troubleshoot coke oven heat exchange equipment. Three detection methods are proposed for the opening and closing state of the exchange cock. Each detection method is analyzed according to the actual production process and requirements. The cock images are collected by the robot and made into a dataset. YOLO-v3 is used to train models of three detection methods on the same experimental platform and compare them. Finally, the optimal detection model is selected and deployed on the inspection robot. The detection accuracy rate reaches 99.1%, which effectively reduces the accident rate and maintains the stability of the coking system.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of A Traction-Type Large-Load Cable-Stayed Inspection Robot
abstract: Stayed cables are important load-bearing structures of bridges, and their safety has always been the focus of attention. To solve the defects of traditional cable-stayed bridge cable inspection robots such as low load capacity and poor reliability. This paper presents a self-towing cable-stayed robot. First, an independent frame-type climbing mobile robot is designed as a heavy-duty mechanism. Furthermore, the self-traction mechanism, spring obstacle-surmounting mechanism, and self-locking structure including the winch drive is designed; Secondly, a dynamic model is established for the obstacle-over-obstacle module of the heavy-duty robot, and the superiority of the robot in the obstacle-over-obstacle process is analyzed; Thirdly, The kinematics and dynamics of the heavy-duty robot during the climbing process are analyzed, and then the stability of the robot is verified through the fuzzy variable gain PID control algorithm. Through the verification analysis, the heavy-duty robot can carry a payload of more than 45kg and climb stably on a cable with a diameter of 90mm under the vibration of the cable.

articleTitle: Direct Lift Backstepping Carrier Control Based on Prescribed Performance
abstract: A direct lift carrier landing controller is designed by combining prescribed performance with backstepping control. On the basis of the traditional backstepping control method, the comand amplitude limit and rate limiting of each loop is considered, and the compensation tracking error is analyzed by introducing a compensation system, and the prescribed performance method is used to improve the error's convergence ability. The designed carrier landing control can achieve decoupling of flight path, angle of attack, and speed in three channels. The pilot has little control burden, and can quickly correct glide slope errors, and the ship wake disturbance is suppressed well. Throughout the entire process, the angle of attack and velocity can be well maintained.

articleTitle: A Fault Detection Method Based on Clustering Algorithm for Internet of Things
abstract: In recent years, the Internet of Things (IoT) has experienced fast-paced technological advancements, connecting numerous smart devices and sensors and enabling seamless data exchange between them. However, due to software and hardware failures, it's inevitable that many sensors will fail, which can seriously affect the availability of IoT. To address this issue, we propose a fault detection method based on the clustering algorithm in this paper. This method divides sensors into different clusters, and the cluster head can determine the status of sensors based on data from neighboring sensors within the same group. Our simulation experiments demonstrate that this fault detection method has better performance in terms of detection accuracy and false positive rate.

articleTitle: Text Detection of Power Nameplate Based on Improved DBNet
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low efficiency and low accuracy of power nameplate text detection in natural scenarios, we propose a detection model based on improved DBNet. By introducing the MobileOne network, the feature extraction ability of the model is enhanced, while ensuring the real-time nature of the model, and the Feature Pyramid Network is improved, and the RepResBlock is introduced to control the amount of information in the previous layer, and at the same time, combined with the attention mechanism, improve the model's attention to text features, and strengthen the model's ability to integrate and express multi-scale features. Experimental results show that the model can maintain good detection results under small parameters. Compared with the original DBNet model, our model has significantly improved performance, achieving more accurate, more robust and faster power nameplate detection.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-Triggered Robust Output Feedback Model Predictive Control for a Class of Discrete Time-Varying Delay Systems
abstract: This article studies the dynamic output feedback robust model predictive control issue based on dynamic event-triggered mechanism and output feedback for a class of uncertain and delay systems with nonlinear disturbance. First, a mathematical model is constructed for uncertain system with time-varying delay, and an output feedback controller is proposed. Next, the dynamic event-triggered mechanism is introduced to determine whether current message needs to be transmitted or not. Based on the proposed cost function and Lyapunov stability theory, the robust model predictive control problem is turned into an online minimization optimization problem, and robust asymptotic stability conditions are given. In the end, the feasibility of this control scheme is validated through simulation examples.

articleTitle: Randomized Gradient-Free Mirror Descent Algorithm for Distributed Online Optimization
abstract: An online distributed optimization problem over a multi-agent system is concerned in this paper. Each agent can only evaluate the function value of its local objective function. A distributed zeroth-order mirror descent algorithm is proposed by adopting a two-point gradient estimator in the mirror descent scheme. Specifically, we employ gradient-free techniques to adapt the algorithm to scenarios in the absence of derivative information. The proposed algorithm utilizes a two-point gradient estimation technique, ensuring precise convergence to the optimal function value. It is proved that an average regularized regret of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(1/\sqrt{T})$</tex> convergence rate is achieved under the proposed algorithm, which is the best known T-rate of gradient-free algorithms in offline settings. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is validated through numerical experiments.

articleTitle: A Novel Model Predictive Control Algorithm with Rolling-Horizon Optimization for Three-Level NPC Rectifiers
abstract: Due to its simple structure and good performance, the model predictive control (MPC) algorithm has attracted a lot of research and applications, making it a promising control strategy. However, the traditional MPC algorithm selects the optimal space voltage vector based solely on one sampling period, which may not be optimal for subsequent periods. In order to enhance the control performance, a novel model predictive control algorithm with rolling-horizon optimization (RO-MPC) for three-level NPC (Neutral Point Clamped) rectifiers has been proposed in this article. The proposed algorithm takes into account the control performance of the next period as well. Based on this, it selects the optimal and suboptimal space voltage vectors at the k+1th time. Using these selected vectors, the algorithm predicts the system state at the k+2th time. And to reduce the computational burden of the system, adjacent candidate space voltage vectors are considered for the next period. Then, the optimal voltage vector that minimizes the cost function is selected. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified through simulation experiments, including the steady-state performance, the dynamic-state performance and the robustness under grid voltage fluctuation.

articleTitle: BTU-Net: Bidirectional Transformer U-Net for Buildings Segmentation
abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been employed in image segmentation more and more recently due to their ability to extract detailed properties from images. One of the most successful neural network frameworks for image segmentation among them is the encoder-decoder network structure. U-Net combines an encoder and a decoder to segment images at the pixel level for image segmentation tasks. U-Net uses multi-scale convolutional layers to extract visual information; nevertheless, these layers are unable to record long-distance correlations. In order to gather both local and global information about the image, this work proposes a bidirectional Transformer U-Net (BTU-Net) model, which draws inspiration from the Transformer concept. The BTU-Net structure has an encoder with five down-sampling layers and a decoder with five up-sampling levels. Two-way transformer hybrid convolution modules are used in the final three layers, whereas multi-scale convolution modules are used in the first two layers. With the addition of convolution layers and two-way convolution layers, the quadratic complexity of the traditional self-attention mechanism decreases linearly. The IoU, F1-score, accuracy, recall, and precision scores of our suggested model are 61.9%, 67.2%, 83.9%, 63.3%, and 84.3%, respectively, and experiments have shown that they are comparable to other network models.

articleTitle: A Multi-Channel K-Type Thermocouple Temperature Measurement System Based on LabVIEW
abstract: A multi-channel K-type thermocouple temperature measurement system based on LabVIEW was designed using virtual instrument technology for test objects that require multi-channel temperature testing. In order to reduce the complexity of hardware circuit design, a precision thermocouple digital converter with integrated cold junction compensation is used for temperature measurement circuit. This is combined with a communication circuit composed of MCU, RS485, and WIFI, forming the hardware system of the multi-channel temperature measurement system. The client software developed using LabVIEW allows users to select different communication methods to meet communication requirements at different distances. During the temperature measurement process, users can view real-time temperature rise curves of each measurement point and save the data locally. This system provides a reference for temperature acquisition and data transmission in practical production applications.

articleTitle: Research on Ship Pose Modeling Based on Wind Wave Current Ship Coupling
abstract: To study the Six degrees of freedom pose change of ships caused by wind, wave and current, and to facilitate the motion analysis of ships in complex marine environment, a ship motion model under the coupling of wind, wave and current was established. Firstly, the coupling relationship between wind and waves was established using the relationship between sea wind speed and wave wavelength, improving the matching degree between the calculated wind, wave, and current forces and the actual situation; Secondly, the fourth order Runge Kutta method is used to establish the Discretization ship motion model, which is convenient for the later discussion of the relationship between ship position and posture changes and wind, wave and current; Finally, according to the Discretization ship motion model, the ship Six degrees of freedom motion model under wind wave current coupling is established. The simulation results indicate that the above model has certain rationality and reference value.

articleTitle: Vehicle and Vehicle Distance Detection Based on Improved YOLOv5
abstract: Vehicle detection is one of the important applications of target detection in the field of autonomous driving. In response to the shortcomings of vehicle model recognition and low detection accuracy in existing vehicle target detection methods, an improved vehicle and distance detection method based on YOLOv5. By designing the adjacent feature layer correlation module in the feature pyramid structure, the advantages of adjacent feature layers with different receptive fields are used to provide more accurate spatial position signals, thereby improving the detection accuracy. To solve the problem of non-fixed output feature map size in the SPP module, a spatial pyramid pooling module with average pooling and residual edges is designed to comprehensively improve the overall performance. Finally, the vehicle distance detection module is designed by combining the RealSense D415 depth camera to add distance measurement display to the detection header, achieving vehicle detection and distance measurement simultaneously. Through experimental horizontal comparison with other algorithms, vertical comparison before and after improvement, the results show that the precision, recall rate, and average precision have increased by 5.17%, 7.92% and 4.25% respectively after improvement, fully verifying the feasibility of the algorithm improvement. The corresponding camera distance measurement error experiment is designed, and the distance measurement error results are all within 3%, indicating practical value.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fixed-Time Tracking Control for Nonholonomic Wheeled Mobile Robot with External Disturbances
abstract: In this paper, the fixed-time tracking control problem for a nonholonomic wheeled mobile robot (NWMR) with external disturbances is studied. Firstly, a fixed-time kinematic controller is crafted through the application of linear transfor-mation and the fixed-time theory method, that is, a designed auxiliary linear and angular velocity enables NWMR to track the trajectory of the virtual leader in a fixed time. Then, a continuous adaptive fixed-time tracking controller is designed for NWMR with external disturbances such that the NWMR is able to track the auxiliary velocity in a fixed time. So it can realize the position tracking control of the robot in a fixed time. ultimately, the numerical simulations are presented to show the effectiveness of the controller.

articleTitle: Enhanced Short-Term Wind Speed Prediction by ICEEMDAN and Feature Engineering
abstract: Accurate wind speed prediction are essential for ensuring the safety of marine engineering, fishing, and other offshore operations. Due to the nonlinear properties of wind speed, however, it is often difficult for conventional prediction models to produce accurate prediction. This paper proposes a hybrid prediction model that combines the ICEEMDAN decomposition algorithm and feature engineering to solve this problem. This model decomposes the original wind speed series into subsequences with different frequencies and then eliminates the high-frequency subsequences that contain white noise. In addition, current research on wind speed prediction focuses primarily on the wind speed series itself. Using feature engineering, this paper extracts the statistical features within the sliding window and combines them with the time series to generate the characteristic time series input for training the LSTM model. The short-term wind speed predictions of this fusion model are more accurate than those of traditional models.

articleTitle: Build General Pansharpening Model Through a Simple Sensor-Specific Model Selection Strategy
abstract: Deep-learning-based pansharpening methods have become a hot field in the remote sensing community. However, most existing deep learning pansharpening methods are conducted in a sensor-specific and supervised way. That is, pairs of panchromatic (Pan) and multispectral (MS) images acquired from a given sensor are fed into networks. The trained model can achieve a satisfactory fusion result only if the images are fused from the same sensor as the training images. The trained model from one sensor cannot be transferred to another. How to train a general model suitable for different sensors is a challenging problem. In this context, we propose a simple sensor-type detecting strategy, which can be integrated with any sensor-specific pansharpening methods and result in a general fusion framework across different sensors. More specifically, for a given deep-learning-based pansharpening method, sufficient Pan and MS image pairs from multiple sensors are fed into the network respectively, and models from multiple sensors are obtained to construct a model pool. Thereafter, a pair of local patches of MS and Pan from the test images are fed into existing sensor-specific models in the pool respectively. The pansharpening quality of outputs are evaluated with multiple fusing indices, such as quality without reference index (QNR). The model that achieves the best performance in terms of index is selected as the candidate model and further employs the images over the whole scene. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, WSDFNet, a state-of-the-art pansharpening method was trained with GaoFen-1, QuickBird, and WorldView-3 datasets respectively. The QNR index is the optimal index for predicting the sensor type. With 100 images from three datasets as testing images, the correct accuracy rate of the statistical QNR index on sensor differentiation performance is 86, 69, and 62, respectively, which indicates this model is promising for distinguishing the sensor type. This proposed prediction strategy is simple and flexible, and it can be combined with existing deep-learning methods to form a complete fusion process without distinguishing the sensor type.

articleTitle: Tracking Accuracy Improvement Algorithm for Underwater Moving Target Based on DKF and AUKF
abstract: During the detection and tracking of a moving target by an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV), sonar detection suffers from delayed updating of 3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> position data and low updating frequency, which may degrade the tracking accuracy of the AUV on the moving target. Therefore, this paper proposes a delayed-adaptive unscented Kalman filter (D-AUKF) algorithm based on the delayed Kalman filter (DKF) and the adaptive unscented Kalman filter (AUKF) that is based on observation noise covariance. First, when the detection data is updated, the D-AUKF algorithm is used to compensate for the data update delay and improve the accuracy of the position data. Then, during this detection cycle, the D-AUKF algorithm is used to predict the position of the moving target several times based on the delay-compensated position data to improve the AUV's tracking accuracy on the moving target. The simulation results show that the D-AUKF algorithm performs better in improving the tracking accuracy of the AUV on the moving target than the EKF.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Model-Based Imitation Learning for In-between Motion Synthesis
abstract: Motion in-between problem is the key to solve the issue of long-term motion synthesis, which are widely applied in animation production, virtual reality, video games and film industry. Motion in-between can be defined as a process generating transitions between previous motion and future motion. Previous researchers focus on motion sequence generation, which omits the interaction with environment and can cause foot-sliding problem. In this work we present a novel, generic system based on imitation learning for motion in-between problem. This hierarchical system contains two parts: first part is motion primitives, which utilize reference motion to learn general knowledge of human motion; second part is policy controller, which uses multiple primitives to generate natural human motion. The primitives are controlled by the combine weights generated by policy controller. Experiment shows that our method can effectively improve motion quality and reduce the amount of reference motion data.

articleTitle: A Method of Using a Thruster to Ensure the Stability of Attitude Control and Improve the Efficiency of Orbit Control
abstract: Aiming at the gap of the prior art, the technical problem to be sloved in this paper is a method of using the thruster to improve the efficiency of orbit control, which can make the attitude control jet output in time, reduce the attitude control delay on board, ensure the stability of the satellite plarform, and make the orbit control jet effective output, save the orbit control time and improve the orbit control accuracy.

articleTitle: Research of Oxygen Excess Ratio Control Methods for PEMFC Air Supply Systems
abstract: The control problem of its oxygen excess ratio for a proton exchange membrane fuel cell air supply system is addressed. First, a fourth-order nonlinear dynamic model is developed for the control of the PEMFC system; next, feedforward PID, feedforward fuzzy PID and ANFIS controllers are designed to control the air compressor voltage so that it can track the optimum OER by changing the output flow rate of the air compressor when the fuel cell load current changes. The results indicate that the ANFIS control has the best dynamic performance and no overshoot when the stack load current changes, while the feedforward PID control and feedforward fuzzy PID control have a faster response time, but take longer to reach the optimal OER, and show fluctuations and overshoot. The ANFIS control has the shortest average regulation time, which is 38.4 % and 52.9 % shorter than the feedforward PID control and feedforward fuzzy PID control respectively.

articleTitle: Underwater Asymmetric Hysteresis Modeling and Compensation of Flexible Structure Actuated by Macro Fiber Composites
abstract: Macro fiber composite (MFC) is widely used in vibration control due to its fast response and large actuating force. However, the underwater asymmetric hysteresis behavior of an flexible structure actuated by MFC actuator greatly affects the accuracy of vibration control. In this paper, to improve the control accuracy of the underwater MFC-actuated flexible structure, a hybrid hysteresis model is proposed to describe the asymmetric hysteresis behavior of the underwater MFC-actuated flexible structures. In the hybrid hysteresis model, we take full advantage of the curve-fitting capabilities of polynomial models to form a hybrid model cascading a classical Prandtl-Ishlinskii (CPI) model. The model fitting results show that the modified PI (MPI) model based on experimental input and output values has a better performance than the pure PI model having a symmetrical parallel quadrilateral structure, and the modeling error is reduced by 81%. Then, the tracking control experiment is performed to prove the effectiveness of feedforward compensation control for the underwater MFC-actuated flexible structure.

articleTitle: An Obstacle Avoidance Path Planning Algorithm for Manipulator in Deep Crate Grasping
abstract: The deep crate grasping problem is a major challenge for manipulator in industrial applications. In order to solve the issue of deep crate grasping and ensure the path quality of the algorithm, this paper proposes a new hybrid obstacle avoidance planning algorithm based on goal-biased rapidly exploring random tree and improved artificial potential field (RRT-APF). Initially, the algorithm strategizes an efficient trajectory for the working element within the operational area. Subsequently, it dissects this trajectory through sampling, creating a sequence of sub-target points. These points serve as the basis for obstacle avoidance planning within the manipulator's configuration space, mitigating planning complexities. Moreover, the RRT algorithm is employed to address the challenge of local optima within the artificial potential field method. The stochastic nature of the RRT algorithm plays a crucial role in enabling the APF algorithm to break free from local optima. Ultimately, the efficacy of the algorithm is demonstrated through the planning of a path for obstacle avoidance on the DOBOT CR5 manipulator using MATLAB.

articleTitle: Formation Control of Coupled Harmonic Oscillators Based on Bearing-Measurement
abstract: This article examines formation control issue of coupled harmonic oscillators by using bearing-measurement among agents. Two control protocols are proposed for followers under the case without disturbance and the case with the bounded disturbance to achieve the desired formation pattern. Then, by algebraic graph theory and matrix theory, we present some conditions on bearing network structure to ensure the convergence of both followers and leaders towards the desired formation pattern. Lastly, numerical simulations are performed to validate the findings presented in this study.

articleTitle: Adaptive Prescribed Performance Backstepping Control of PMSM
abstract: The nonlinear behaviors in the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM), for instance, parameters uncertainties, chaos oscillation and disturbances can make a serious menace to the system stability and even deteriorate system performance. The analog circuit of PMSM is constructed, which provides a basic theoretical basis for the construction of its actual circuit. To handle these nonlinear behaviors, an adaptive prescribed performance backstepping controller integrated with the hyperbolic tangent tracking differentiator (HTTD), radial basis function (RBF) neural network, Nussbaum function and prescribed performance function (PPF) is designed. The stability analysis fully proves that all signals of the PMSM system are uniformly ultimately bounded. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the designed controller.
